english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy vines but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are special crops that generate their own leaf-building nitrogen in the soil. If you plant them in soil that already has high nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves rather than forming flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni feɔ nitrogen yɛ amɛbaai ni feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji oodu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen fa yɛ nɔ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight cups and stop growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck the juices from young shoots, spreading viral diseases as they feed. Protecting plants early with insect traps or simple soapy sprays keeps these sap-sucking insects away.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwaa be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ mra Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants get weaker and produce smaller fruits when I plant them on the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot year after year drains specific soil nutrients and lets plant-specific diseases build up in the soil. Moving your tomato crop to a new spot each season breaks the disease cycle and lets the soil recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tomato tsei ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he hee yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: The very first rainfall often only wets the surface layer of soil while the deep soil remains hot and dry. If a short dry spell follows that first rain, young seeds will germinate and quickly dry out before the regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbi. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo ko yɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui bibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon heat even when the ground felt damp in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull moisture out of the earth. Covering the bare ground around your plants with dried grass or leaves helps trap moisture in the dirt and keeps roots cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain accumulates around their roots in heavy soil without good drainage, allowing underground fungi to attack the wet skin. Planting yams on raised mounds lets excess water flow away safely.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ atutua hewolo ni efɔ lɛ. Atomɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does seed maize bought from the agricultural office yield bigger cobs than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seed maize is carefully bred by scientists to combine strong traits that resist local pests and produce uniform, big cobs. When you save seeds from your own farm, those strong combined traits break down, resulting in smaller cobs in the next generation.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛ sui ni mli wa ni teɔ shi woɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ awo mli ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛji obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli Nakai kuu sui ni mli wa lɛ baakumɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying during the hot sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without protection, the strong sun causes them to lose water faster than they can absorb it, leading to wilting and death.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ abuuu amɛhe Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ. Ekɛ shwiemɔ kɛ gbele baa.

english: How does intense sunshine affect the growth of newly planted cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa kookoo ni adu ehee lɛ dalɛ he?

english: While mature cocoa trees need sunlight to produce pods, young cocoa seedlings suffer under direct sun, which scorches their soft leaves, slows down their growth, and makes them wither.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛwo ŋmeii moŋ, shi cacao dumɔwui bibii lɛ baaná amanehulu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. shweremɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ

english: If cocoa seedlings receive too much sun, their green leaves will start yellowing, curling at the edges, drooping downward, or turning brown and crispy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Ebaai eŋɔlii lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ, amɛbaagbee shi, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What helps young cocoa seedlings survive and grow strongly during their first year?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees thrive when they are sheltered by temporary shade crops like plantains, which keep the surrounding air cool, protect the leaves from sunburn, and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ omanye kɛ tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do many farmers plant plantains in the same field with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping young cocoa plants cool while they are establishing roots.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha amɛmli ajɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Will planting plantains alongside my cocoa steal water and nutrients from the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo lɛ masɛi lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: No, when planted with proper spacing, plantains act as helpful companion plants that shelter cocoa from heat stress while also giving you food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu kɛ gbɛ ni sa. Dumɔwui lɛ baatsu nii akɛ nanemɛi tso ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Do plantain trees need to stay on my farm permanently next to the cocoa?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni plantains ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ kookoo masɛi?

english: No, plantains are temporary nurse crops. Once the cocoa trees grow larger and develop their own thick leafy branches, the plantains can gradually be removed.
ga: Dabi, plantains ji tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da ni eyɛ niji kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie Plantains lɛ fiofio.

english: Why is it important to plant shade crops before or at the same time as my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ dani loo yɛ be kome too mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ mli lɛ, ehe miihia waa.

english: Planting shade crops early ensures that when your young, sensitive cocoa seedlings go into the soil, they are immediately sheltered from harsh direct sun.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ adumɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɛ́ adu o-cocoa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nuɔ he waa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abuɔ amɛhe amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise using a straight string or thread when laying out my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ kpãa loo kpãa ni ja atsu nii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ?

english: Using a measuring line helps you plant in straight, properly spaced rows so that both your cocoa and plantains have enough room to grow without crowding each other.
ga: Kɛ okɛ susumɔ line tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni eha kookoo kɛ plantain fɛɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkafee amɛhe nɔ ko.

english: Is it better to clear all the natural plant cover off my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie adebɔɔ mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: Clearing the land completely leaves the bare soil exposed to burning heat and dry winds, which damages young cocoa. It is better to keep or plant protective shade plants like plantains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kwraa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ feɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ Esa akɛ obua tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa loo odu.

english: Why do some of the new seeds from the agricultural store have a special coating or color on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei komɛi ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ yɛ nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe loo kɔla ko yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: That coating is a seed treatment that contains nutrients like iron or protective chemicals. It shields the seed from insects and soil diseases while giving the young plant an extra boost of nutrients right as it starts to grow.
ga: Nɔ ni fata he ji ni akɛ niyenii tamɔ dade loo tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu dumɔwui ahe nii. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi kɛ helai ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii krokomɛi hu kɛji amɛbɔi dalɛ pɛ.

english: How can planting a specific type of seed help prevent sickness and weak blood in my family?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ko ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hela kɛ lá ni bɛ hewalɛ naa yɛ miweku lɛ mli?

english: Some improved seeds are biofortified, meaning they are bred to grow crops packed with essential vitamins and minerals like iron. When your family eats these crops, it builds up their blood and boosts their immune system against common illnesses.
ga: Akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, atsɔse amɛ koni amɛdu tsei ni vitamini kɛ mineral ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ dade babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛji oweku lɛ ye nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ, Ehaa lá tswaa ni ehaa amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Can treating my seeds before planting really stop my crops from getting diseases later in the season?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaná hela yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, seed treatments create a protective shield around the seed. This prevents harmful fungi and bacteria in the soil from attacking the seed when it is most vulnerable, ensuring a healthy plant that can resist early diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ahe tsofafeemɔi haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: What actually happens inside a dry seed after I plant it in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A dry seed acts like a sponge, drinking in soil water to wake up the dormant baby plant inside. Once it absorbs enough water, the seed coat bursts open, sending roots down into the dirt and a sprout up toward the sky.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛte tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ashi. Kɛji akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miimɔ Dumɔwu lɛ he atade lɛ baafo. Ha shishifãi lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: How much water does a seed need to sprout, and can too much water rot it?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa dumɔwui? Ni ani nu babaoo baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akpɔtɔ?

english: Seeds need moist soil to trigger growth, but if the soil is soaked with too much water, the seed cannot get air. Without oxygen, the seed suffocates and rots in the ground instead of sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni ekanya amɛdalɛ. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ, amɛmuɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do plant shoots turn green only after they push out of the soil into the sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Underground shoots stay pale because they are living on stored seed energy. Once they hit sunlight, the plant creates chlorophyll—the green substance that allows leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ahewalɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ klorofil. Enɛ ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What are plant nutrients like iron, and why do my crops need them to grow well?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei amli niyenii tamɔ dade, ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Just like humans need vitamins to stay strong, crops need micro-nutrients like iron to produce green leaf pigments, process food from sunlight, and build strong stems that resist disease.
ga: Taakɛ vitamini he hiaa adesai koni gbɔmɔtso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii nibii bibii, tamɔ dade hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛfee baai lɛ ahe sui. Niyenii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli ni afeɔ tsei ni wa ni baatsi helai anaa

english: Why do some crops fall over during heavy rains while others stand firm in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ekrokomɛi hu damɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Crops stand firm when they have deep roots and strong stalks nourished by good soil nutrients. Weak plants often lack essential minerals or were planted too close together, making their stems thin and easily knocked over by wind or heavy rain.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ́ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni nine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ minerals ni he hiaa loo aduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi feɔ mlɛo ni egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop shoots turning yellow instead of a healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the young plant is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil and cannot pull food from the earth properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen loo dade. Aloo shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is there really a big difference between planting certified improved seeds and using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ kpele ko yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli, ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adumɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, certified seeds are tested to ensure high germination rates, disease protection, and strong vigor, whereas saved seeds often lose their strength over time, resulting in lower yields and weaker plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, akaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Helai atsimɔ kɛ hewalɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce flowers before any fruits start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Fruit trees like mangoes must produce flowers first because the flower contains the natural parts needed to create fruit. Once the flower gets visited by insects and fertilized, the petals fall off and the tiny fruit begins to grow in its place.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango lɛ afɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji kooloi bibii basara fɔfɔi ni amɛbɔi gbalashihilɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ ahe fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni aduawai bibii baafee. Ebɔi dalɛ moŋ.

english: Do all tree crops like mangoes and oranges have to flower before they can give fruit?
ga: Ani esa akɛ tsei fɛɛ, tamɔ mango kɛ akutu dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, almost all fruit-bearing trees must bloom first. Flowering is the tree's way of preparing to reproduce, and a fruit cannot form unless a flower develops and gets pollinated first.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii lɛ esa akɛ amɛfɔ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. Fɔfɔii ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛsaa amɛhe kɛha fɔmɔ. Ni aduawai nyɛŋ afee ja fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi shweremɔ ni awo amɛ pollen klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my citrus trees bloom at a different time of the year compared to my mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli kɛ akɛto mi-mango tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Different trees react to weather changes like rainfall and temperature in their own way. For example, mango trees usually flower after a period of dry weather, while many citrus trees flower after the main rains begin.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso henɔ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa he nii yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ nɔ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsei babaoo fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ wulu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are so many bees gathering around my orange trees when they start blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo ebua amɛhe naa nɛkɛ? Mi orange tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi?

english: Bees come to your orange trees because the flowers produce sweet nectar and pollen that bees use for food. As bees fly from flower to flower, they help the tree turn those blossoms into actual oranges.
ga: Wuobii baa o-orange tso lɛ he ejaakɛ fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ pollen ni wuobii kɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ amli efeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Should I chase away bees when I see them flying around my flowering crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashwie ŋmeii lɛ kɛ mina amɛ ni amɛmiibɔle mi fɔfɔi tsei lɛ ahe?

english: No, you should welcome bees on your farm. Bees are friendly helpers that pollinate your flowers; without them, many of your tree flowers will not turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ohere ŋmeii atuu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Wuobii ji yelikɛbualɔi ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su ni yeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛwoɔ ofɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ amɛbɛ Otso lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo tsakeŋ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do flowers on my fruit trees produce such a strong sweet smell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ he muji waa nɛkɛ?

english: The sweet scent is a natural signal produced by the tree to attract beneficial insects like bees from far away, guiding them directly to the nectar so pollination can happen.
ga: Nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsei feɔ koni amɛkɛgbala kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kudɔ amɛ kɛya nektar lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ koni pollination aba.

english: How can I encourage more bees to visit my farm to help my trees yield better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmeii babaoo hewalɛ ni amɛbasara miŋmɔ lɛ koni eye ebua mitsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: You can bring more bees to your land by planting a mixture of flowering trees and plants, keeping some flowering weeds nearby, and avoiding spraying harmful chemicals while your crops are blooming.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei kɛ tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛfutu mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahi ohe. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ he.

english: How does planting different types of trees together on my farm help my crop production?
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Te Sharing My Farm yeɔ ebuaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Growing different trees ensures there are flowers blooming at different times of the year. This keeps bees and other helpful insects living on your farm year-round so they are ready to pollinate your main crops when they flower.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔii ni fɔɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Hii oŋmɔ lɛ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaafee pollination yɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do many of my mango flowers fall off without ever turning into mango fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when they fail to get pollinated by insects like bees, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather, pests, or poor soil nutrients. Ensuring good pollination and proper water helps keep flowers on the tree.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee amɛ pollin, loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Pollination kpakpa kɛ nu ni sa baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some tree flowers drop to the ground even after bees have visited them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe fɔfɔii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ebasara amɛ po lɛ?

english: A fruit tree naturally produces far more flowers than it can feed. Even if bees visit every flower, the tree will shed excess blossoms so it can focus its food and water on growing a manageable number of strong fruits.
ga: Yibii tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii saraa fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi moŋ Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi babaoo lolo. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii kɛ nu nɔ koni ekɛdu aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and soil moisture to help the young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sun. Getting plenty of sunlight allows the plant to produce more energy, which makes the yam tuber inside the ground grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts that can burn and damage the plant's stem and soft roots if applied directly against them. It is safer to place fertilizer in a small ring or hole a few inches away from the plant stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo buji ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why is it good to leave dry plant leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi tsei ahe baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ kpakpa.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket. It prevents hot sun from drying out the soil too quickly, stops weeds from growing, and breaks down over time to feed the soil.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Tsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that like that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs to grow green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baa ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. High heat stops the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ amɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does cassava become hard and woody if I leave it buried in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ tso lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs for the plant. As the plant gets older, the root fibers harden to support the growing plant above ground, making the root tough and less pleasant to eat.
ga: Kasava shishifã ji tso lɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ eda lɛ Shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔji lɛ mli wa koni eye ebua tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the real rains begin. If you plant too early, your seeds might sprout and then wither and die from lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: These worms are usually Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs inside the leaf funnel of young maize plants, and the newly hatched caterpillars hide inside the funnel eating the fresh young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii heei.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree usually take before it starts giving me good pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees usually take about 3 to 5 years after planting to start bearing good fruit, depending on the variety you planted and how well you keep weeds away, provide shade, and nourish the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 beni adu cacao tsei lɛ dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ kɛ bɔ ni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ohaa hulutsoo, ni ohaa sũ lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready to dig up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground around the stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi efuuɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the open sunlight so their leaves can catch light and make energy; without stakes, the leaves sit on the damp ground where they rot, resulting in very small yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baata shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni miifite lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Yellow bottom leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. When there is not enough food in the dirt, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or the soil stays dry for too long. The heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by small whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry up so fast during the Harmattan season even if I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: The dry, dusty Harmattan winds suck moisture out of plant leaves much faster than usual, causing the leaves to lose water quicker than the roots can drink it from the wet soil.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do so many small shoot stems grow around my main plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo lɛ ji Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Midumɔwu titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Those extra shoots are suckers that steal food and water from the main tree. You should cut most of them away, leaving only one or two healthy ones, so your main tree can grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ ji ŋmeii ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofo mli babaoo. Tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛ ni baaha otso titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: If I take good care of my cocoa farm, can the trees keep producing pods for many years?
ga: Kɛ mikwɛ kookoo abɔɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ani tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii afii babaoo?

english: Yes, if you prune them regularly, control pests like capsids, and protect the soil, cocoa trees can stay healthy and keep producing good yield for 20 to 30 years or more.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ofoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa. Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ nɔyeli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hebuu nɔ lɛ, cacao tsei baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii afii 20 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why do weeds sprout up so much faster on my cleared land right after the first heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dry and sleeping in the topsoil for months. The first heavy rain softens their seed coats and waters the soil, triggering thousands of weed seeds to wake up and sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu. Ewoɔ jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ hewalɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃.

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is major food for the plant. Maize takes whatever nitrogen it has left in its older, bottom leaves and moves it up to the young growing leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri kɛha tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ yɛ baai ni eda kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛyaa baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts together with my maize will make my soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ mɔ ko akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of crops called legumes that pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in the ground. This extra food stays in the soil to feed the maize growing beside or after it.
ga: Peanuts fata ŋmeii akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he. ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ Niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass or cocoa leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo baai aha he ni gbɛ yɔɔ ni ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating in the hot sun, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into natural manure as it rots.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other to get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When cassava is crowded, the roots stay thin and small instead of swelling into big tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli beni ŋmei mli eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛfuu ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it good to cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, because if there are too many young shoots, the mother plantain tree has to share its food with all of them, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ plantain nyɛ lɛ aja niyenii lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi ebaafee ŋmeii bibii. Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ koni plantains lɛ ahi shi agbo ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed by full sun and hot, dry winds. Dropping leaves is the tree's defense to save water and keep its main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ tso lɛ he koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkpaa?

english: Cassava tubers rot mainly when heavy rainwater sits in the soil without draining away. Excess water suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases to enter and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii helai hewalɛ koni amɛye nɔ ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as intense heat, dry soil, or sudden lack of water. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive the harsh weather.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the tender leaves of my young maize right after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like the Fall Armyworm lay eggs that hatch rapidly right after rains. The tiny caterpillars quickly feed on the young, soft leaves inside the center of the maize plant.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni fɔɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kplukai bibii yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ oya.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my crops even when there is enough rain for everything?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the hidden plant food and nutrients out of the soil. Even with plenty of rain, your crops will stay stunted because the weeds are starving them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi miiha hɔmɔ miiye amɛ.

english: When crops lack enough plant food, their growth slows down, stems stay thin, and leaves often turn light green or yellow instead of remaining dark green.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer around my maize plants so it does not wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ? Abɛi tsei koni amɛkaho?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a gentle rain, placing it a few centimeters away from the plant stem and covering it with soil so heavy rains do not wash it down the farm.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Akɛ amɛ toɔ he ko ni kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi, ni akɛ sũ haa nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I calculate how much fertilizer or seed I need for my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui ni he hiaa mi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: First, measure your field size in acres or hectares, then check the recommended bag rate per acre for your crop; using exact measurements prevents wasting money on too much fertilizer or burning your crops.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, susumɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ he yɛ acre loo hectares mli. No sɛɛ lɛ kwɛmɔ baagi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo acre kome mli kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ susumɔi ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he loo akashã oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I space them out instead of planting seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijara amɛmli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced properly, their roots do not fight each other underground for nutrients and soil water, and their leaves get enough sunlight and breeze to grow strong.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ yɛ he ni sa Amɛshishifãi lɛ ewuuuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ebaai lɛ baaná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow first when a plant runs out of nitrogen in the soil, forcing the crop to pull stored food from its older leaves to feed its new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and fall off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry spells to reduce the amount of water lost through leaf pores, protecting the main trunk from completely drying out until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Buu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage, which stops the flower from turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi bibii efite tso lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi afee aduawai.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and what is causing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: Holes in leaves are usually made by small caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant leaves during the night or cool morning hours to help themselves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai gbɛkɛ loo leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli koni eye ebua amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ koni amɛfɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with groundnuts on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, groundnuts actually capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which helps feed neighboring plants like cassava while giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ niyenii, yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ nibii enyɔ hu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Maize plants need a key food from the soil called nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals the nutrient from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Abɛi biɔ niyenii ko ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen. Koni tsei afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. This damages the leaves and stops the plant from growing tall and bearing good peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ adara ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa aba.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and light to grow thick, strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of water. Without steady moisture and moderate temperatures, the flowers dry up and fall off before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping the air cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do small green insects gather on the stems and pods of my cowpeas during the dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are called aphids, and they multiply quickly in warm, dry weather because they feed on the sweet sap inside the stems and pods. Sucking this sap weakens the cowpea plant and reduces pod growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akɛ aphids. Ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɛkɛ nu nɛɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa pod lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the maize I plant next season yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to catch nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts and leave the roots to decay, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmeii ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot when heavy rain floods my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When soil is flooded for long periods, water pushes out all the air, causing the tubers to suffocate and decay due to waterlogging and soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows their leaves to capture sunlight efficiently while staying off the damp soil. Sunlight helps the leaves produce food to swell the underground tuber, and keeping vines off the ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfuuɔ. Ni wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi foliary helai anaa.

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings grow very slowly when weeds surround the base of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni jwɛi ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer away from young oil palms. Clearing weeds around the base ensures that all the nutrients and water in the soil go directly into growing the palm tree.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ mu tsei bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Konui lɛ kwɛɔ koni akɛ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkwɛ ŋmei tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves make food. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow a lot of leafy green stems but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil. If you add too much artificial nitrogen fertilizer, the plant gets confused and spends all its energy growing big leaves instead of flowering and producing pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ artificial nitrogen fertilizer babaoo fata he lɛ Tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods baa lɛ

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand easily. If the soil is too hard, compacted, or full of stones, the tuber struggles to push through and ends up bent, small, or deformed.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaagbe naa akɛ amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaafee bibioo, loo amɛbaafee nɔ ni efite.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Too much shade and poor ventilation trap moisture on the pods, allowing the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Shade babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and drying out at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. They can also transfer viruses that permanently stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie helai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa daa lɛ hu.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes and small dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ? yɛ kɔni lɛ mli

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day, chewing on the young leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oooye dani amɛje kpo kwraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. If it gets too hot during the day, the flowers cannot set fruit and simply drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Extra suckers steal water, light, and food from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack as the thick tubers expand beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bare trunk left kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing tall and flowering instead of forming a tight, hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eefee fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages head best in cooler weather. If temperatures get too hot or water is inconsistent, the plant thinks its life cycle is ending and skips forming a head to focus on producing flowers and seeds.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tso lɛ susuɔ akɛ ewala be lɛ miiba naagbee ni efoɔ bulbs ni efeɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the healthy-looking branches from my cocoa or fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi cacao loo aduawai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so the plant does not waste energy maintaining them. This allows the tree to focus its nutrients on growing bigger, healthier pods and fruits instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ nakai niji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting cassava stems into specific lengths before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli kɛyashɛ he ko dani adu lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need to be about 20 to 30 centimeters long with several buds so they have enough stored food and energy to sprout strong roots and leaves before relying entirely on the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ afee aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni ehiɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Enɛ ji koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa dani ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to support a good maize crop this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil feels soft and dark, holds moisture without becoming overly waterlogged, and crumbles easily in your hand. If crops previously grew dark green and strong in that soil, it likely contains adequate nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ su ni tsuɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli tsɔ. ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ eyɛ nine mli Kɛji tso lɛ tsutsu lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa baahi mli.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the ground is too dry or completely flooded, or if soil insects damage them. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in moist, loose soil gives them the best chance to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu lɛ mli eyi tsɔ. aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite nii Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do many farmers plant cassava and maize together in the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together maximizes space and time. Maize grows fast and is harvested within a few months, leaving the slow-growing cassava behind to take over the land and yield tubers later.
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa he kɛ be babaoo yaa hiɛ. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmei aba sɛɛ mli.

english: Young crop seedlings cannot compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to build strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that excessive water around the roots is suffocating the plant. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme weather conditions, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen in the soil. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants struggle against each other for light, water, and ground nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants with small yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant's sap or transmitting viruses. Protecting young plants from pests keeps the foliage healthy and growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe feɔ fɛo ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. Heavy rains in Ghana often wash this nutrient deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach it, or the soil itself may just be exhausted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ sũ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baaho.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and greener when I plant cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen food straight out of the air and put it into the soil. When planted together, the maize feeds on this extra soil food provided by the cowpeas.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu Abɛi yɛ he kome lɛ, Abɛi baaye niyenii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsina ŋmeii kɛhaa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die so easily if I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ? Kɛji mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn quickly in strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist so the cocoa plants can survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before any pods can start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of plant nutrients, or insect attack. If the tree feels it does not have enough water or food to feed a pod, it sheds the flower to save its own life.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ ni bɛ Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ e-pods lɛ, Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up on sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ miniji lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows the big tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and allows maximum sunlight to reach every leaf.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ ahi mli lɛ. ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ baa fɛɛ baa he

english: Why do my cassava roots turn woody and hard to cook if I leave them in the dry ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewa akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When the soil gets dry, the cassava plant uses up the soft starch stored in its roots to stay alive. As it drains the starch, the roots fill up with tough wood fibers to protect against total water loss.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi. Beni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Koni nu fɛɛ akafite

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: You can tell groundnuts are ready when the leaves of the plant start turning yellow and dry up. Pulling up one test plant should show dark brown or black inner linings inside the shells, which means the seeds inside are fully ripe.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmeii efee klalo beni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ kaa tso kome ni agbalaa lɛ aná mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually a reaction to extreme heat, uneven watering, or small sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a virus. The plant curls its leaves to try to reduce water loss under stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ yɛ haomɔ shishi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and bushy but fail to produce any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants grow lots of leaves and tall stems, but tricks the plant into 'forgetting' to make flowers and fruit. Excessive heat can also cause flowers to fall off before peppers form.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ aná baai babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Shi elakaa tso lɛ ni ‘ehiɛ kpaa nɔ’ ni ewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Dɔlɛ babaoo baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow thin and weak while others grow thick and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Suckers that sprout directly from the mother plant's main root system share food and grow thick and strong. Narrow suckers with thin leaves often grow from shallow, weak points with little access to the main plant's food stash.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ jaa niyenii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni tso titri lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my pawpaw tree producing plenty of flowers but never growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees have different sexes. Male pawpaw trees produce many flowers on long stems but will never bear fruit; only female and hermaphrodite trees are capable of growing pawpaw fruits.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ bɔlɛnamɔi srɔtoi. Pawpaw tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ. Shi ewoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. Yei kɛ tsei ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii pɛ baanyɛ akwɛ pawpaw aduawai.

english: How do groundnuts form under the soil when the flowers grow above the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After the groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it grows a long stem-like peg that pushes down into the soil, where the tip swells up underground to form the peanut pod.
ga: Beni ashɛre ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eshishigbɛ lɛ fũuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni efeɔ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my maize plant have powdery tops and hair on the side, and do they help make the corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ayiteŋ tamɔ powder kɛ yitsɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ? Ni ani eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ ŋmãa feemɔ mli loo eyeee ebuaaa?

english: The powdery top (tassel) releases pollen, while the hair (silk) catches it. Each individual silk thread connects to a single grain on the cob, so proper pollination is needed to fill out the whole corn cob.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni tamɔ powder (tassel) lɛ jieɔ pollen. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii (silki) lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ dumɔwu kome ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aná pollination ni sa koni akɛwo ŋmãa muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do small plantain shoots keep growing at the root of my main plantain tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii miida yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: These shoots are called suckers and they compete with the main tree for soil nutrients. Removing most of them and leaving only one strong shoot allows the main tree to produce larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ suckers ni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain panicles ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines on sticks helps the leaves catch more sunlight to feed the growing yam tubers underground while keeping leaves off the damp ground to protect them from disease.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ekɛhaa sweet potato tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akamɔ bo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, carried by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from catching light properly, which leads to weak plants and small cassava roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Akɛni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ hela nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ shɛɛɛ la he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, which prevents the flowers from successfully developing into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ aye omanye ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly dry up and die even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden drying is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot in the soil, which damages the root system so severely that the plant can no longer draw up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ waa aahu akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the young leaves on my cocoa trees turn brown and burn when planted in an open sun field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and light. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa leaves until the tree is mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my tall maize stalks fall flat to the ground right when the corn cobs are getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minɔ lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli tsii pɛ?

english: Maize falls over when root systems are shallow, damaged by insects, or when excess nitrogen makes the stem tall and thin, making it too weak to support heavy ears in strong winds.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni kooloi bibii efiteɔ Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ shwiili ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi toi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do the new, tender leaves on my cocoa tree turn reddish-brown before changing to green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii heei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This reddish color stage is a normal process called a 'flush.' The young leaves produce reddish pigments to protect themselves from intense sunlight until they mature, harden, and turn green to produce plant food.
ga: Nɛkɛ fã tsuru nɛɛ ji gbɛjianɔtoo ni ale lɛ akɛ 'flush'. Baai bibii lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsuru ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshwereɔ, amɛwaa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival defense cocoa trees use to reduce water loss through their foliage when the air and soil become dry. Mulching around the base helps preserve soil moisture during this period.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala hebuu gbɛ ni cacao tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to survive their first two to three years before they build resilience.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli dani amɛto shifimɔ shishi.

english: Why are the small green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, shaded conditions. Clearing heavy shade, removing infected pods, and improving air circulation around the trunk helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Shade ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ Tsu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ehe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods develop tiny dark puncture marks and stop growing during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ? ni ekpaa shweremɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli

english: These punctures are usually caused by mirid insects (capsids) sucking sap from the pods. Timely spraying with approved control methods during peak pest seasons protects the pods from destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirid kooloi (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsii lɛ be mli lɛ, ebaabu tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce fewer pods when I leave all the wild side branches to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mihaa koo lɛ mli niji lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When a tree supports too many useless branches and suckers, it spends its energy maintaining leaves rather than forming flowers and pods. Regular pruning directs nutrients directly into pod development.
ga: Kɛ tso ko fiɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni he ehiaaa lɛ asɛɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi daa lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa pod lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do moss and lichens grow on the bark of my old cocoa trees, and does it hurt the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani eyeɔ tso lɛ awui?

english: Moss and lichens grow on tree bark when there is high humidity and low sunlight reaching the trunk. While they do not directly feed on the tree, heavy growth can hide pests or trap moisture that encourages disease.
ga: Moss kɛ lichens kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛ tso lɛ shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyeee tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ, shi shweremɔ ni tsii baanyɛ ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ato loo ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ hela he hewalɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth and improves grain size.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my food crops produce better when I plant cowpeas or beans together with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ du tsina loo ŋmeii?

english: Legume crops like beans take nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and nourishes neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa tsei ahe nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so the beans inside are mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: A pod is fully mature when its husk turns completely yellow or orange, depending on the variety. Picking pods while they are still fully green results in flat, poor-quality beans that do not ferment properly.
