ga: Pods lɛ daraa kwraa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ, ebaaha kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa, ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main food they need to build green leaves, or the soil has too much water around the roots after heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni ebɔle ehe Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ

english: What are those bushy, feather-like tops growing on my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those top structures are called tassels, and they drop pollen onto the lower silks of the plant so that the kernels can grow on the cob.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋwɛi fãi nɛɛ akɛ tassels. Ni amɛshwieɔ pollen yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ siliki lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tight like straws during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural survival trick to shield itself from extreme sun and prevent water from evaporating out of its leaves.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ekɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my corn seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the corn plants to fight over sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la, sũ mli niyenii, kɛ nu bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii waa.

english: Why do weeds in my field slow down the growth of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crop, leaving your plants starving and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil between my crops with dry straw or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping the hot sun from drying it out, while also suppressing weeds.
ga: Mulching, loo mulching, haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ jwɛi hu.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my corn leaves and powdery brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei amli lɛ amli

english: This is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the central leaves of the plant to feed on the tender young growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni amɛye gbekɛbii ni dara lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans in my field after harvesting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds the soil and prepares it for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni esaa lɛ kɛha onibii ni obaakpa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know that my corn crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is mature when the outer husks turn completely dry and brown, the silks turn dark, and the kernels inside become hard.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi kwraa. Siliki lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa

english: Why does my stored corn develop small holes and tiny insects after a few months in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli buji bibii kɛ kooloi bibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those insects are grain weevils that hatch and multiply inside stored corn if the grain was not dried completely before storage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni fɔɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa seedling on my farm to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 3 to 5 years to produce their first pods, while improved hybrid varieties can start bearing fruit in as little as 18 to 24 months if well cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi 24 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep shade trees like plantains near my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain lɛ ahi mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Shade plants like plantains provide shelter, hold moisture in the soil, and protect young cocoa from harsh heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ haa wɔɔhe. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: How many cocoa pods can I reasonably expect one healthy tree to produce during a main harvest season?
ga: Pods enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mafee kɛjɛ cacao tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli?

english: A healthy, mature cocoa tree under good care usually produces between 20 to 50 pods per year, though yields can vary depending on soil richiness, water, and tree age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii 20 kɛyashi 50 daa afi, eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii, nu kɛ afii ni tso lɛ eye lɛ naa moŋ.

english: Why do many small flowers fall off my cocoa tree without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. It is natural for the tree to shed unpollinated flowers so it can save energy for the pods that actually set.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Eji adebɔɔ naa nɔ akɛ tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha fɔfɔi diɛŋtsɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some tiny young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This natural process is called 'cherelle wilt.' The cocoa tree often produces more young pods than it can feed, so it naturally drops the extra ones to allow the remaining healthy pods to grow big.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle wilted’ bei pii lɛ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni darako tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aye. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ adara.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest a cocoa pod from my tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ mitso lɛ mli?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color; green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. You should also hear a slight hollow sound when you tap a ripe pod, showing the beans inside have detached from the outer shell.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Esa akɛ onu gbee ko ni hoɔ fioo kɛji ota pod ni ahoo lɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ejɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crop if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long without harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa amɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the seeds inside to start germinating or rotting. Overripe pods also attract pests like squirrels and pod borers and can spread diseases to healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ pod borers. ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the growing pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in wet, humid weather. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent moisture build-up that feeds the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abua naa akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose so many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo miifite yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, cocoa trees naturally drop older leaves to prevent losing moisture through evaporation. This helps the tree survive the water shortage until the rains return.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai momoi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nu ni faaa mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes small bugs to cluster on the young shoots and pods of my cocoa tree, and are they dangerous?
ga: Nɔ ni feɔ kooloi bibii ni abua naa yɛ kookoo tso lɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni ani eyɛ oshara?

english: These are often mirids (capsids) or mealybugs that suck sap from young leaves and pods. They weaken the tree, stunt pod growth, and can spread diseases, so they need to be managed through field sanitation or approved treatments.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji mirids (capsids) loo mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Dwarf pod dalɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwa No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ loo tsofafeemɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ nɔ.

english: You should not plant after the very first rain shower because the soil underneath might still be dry. Wait until the rain falls steadily for a few days so the ground holds enough deep moisture to help your seeds sprout and keep growing continuously.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: If the rains stop suddenly right after I finish planting, what will happen to my seeds?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni adu nii agbe naa lɛ Mɛni baaba wɔdumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: Young seeds and sprouts need continuous water to build roots. If a dry spell occurs immediately after planting, the tender shoots will dry out and die before they can establish themselves.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui kɛ tsei bibii daa koni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ he okadii ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shi.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster during the rainy season compared to the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves nutrients stored in the soil so plant roots can easily drink them up. Constant moisture allows crops to make food efficiently, helping them grow bigger and greener very quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni ato yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ mlɛo. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli oya.

english: Why do my crops seem to need even more water when they start producing flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai shishi lɛ?

english: Flowering and fruiting require huge amounts of energy and liquid to build sweet produce or grains. If water drops during this stage, the flowers will fall off, and your crop yield will be very poor.
ga: Fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo biɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo koni akɛfee nibii loo ŋmaa ni ŋɔɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ ba shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi Ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my plants curling up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve moisture inside when the heat is extreme.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa waa.

english: How can I keep my soil wet for a longer time when the weather stays dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: You can cover the bare ground around your plants with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching. This blanket shields the soil from direct sunlight and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Can too much water damage my crops even if they need rain to grow?
ga: Ani nu babaoo baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Yes, excessive water fills all the small air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, roots rot, leaves turn yellow, and the plant dies despite being surrounded by water.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni tsei baagboi kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe po.

english: Should I plant my crops on raised mounds or flat land when preparing for the rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ kɛ́ miisaa mihe kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ?

english: Creating raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from root zones so crops don't get waterlogged. Flat land works better in drier zones where you want to trap every drop of moisture.
ga: Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akabote nu mli Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni egbi ni oosumɔ ni okɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fɛɛ awo mli lɛ.

english: How does water availability throughout the year affect when I can harvest my crops?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ saa be ni manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need a specific amount of water to reach maturity on schedule. Adequate rain keeps their growth cycle on track so you can harvest on time, whereas water shortages delay maturity.
ga: Tsei biɔ nu abɔ pɔtɛɛ ko koni amɛdara yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ baaha shweremɔ be lɛ aya nɔ taakɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni nyɛkpa nii yɛ be naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni faaa lɛ baaha dalɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: How do I know which crops need constant water and which ones can survive dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni nu he hiaa amɛ daa lɛ? Ni mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Crops like maize, rice, and leafy vegetables require steady moisture throughout their life. Root crops like cassava or grains like millet store water in deep roots or tough stalks, helping them withstand dry periods better.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmei toɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ bei anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it wrong to just dump my mixed fertilizer in one big pile at the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mashɛrɛ mi-fertilizer ni mikɛfutu lɛ ashwie ŋmei agbo kome mli yɛ kookoo tso ko shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is concentrated chemical or organic food for plants. Dumping it in a single pile near the trunk creates a heavy chemical concentration that can burn the roots and kill the tree; spreading it evenly in a ring around the tree canopy allows roots to feed safely.
ga: Fertilizer ji tsofa loo niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa tsei. Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ ashwie ŋtayaa kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tsofai babaoo ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ baa. Jajemɔ ni yeɔ egbɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii shweshweeshwe.

english: How does leaving dry fallen leaves around my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Baai ni egboi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ ajiemɔ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry leaves act as a natural blanket called mulch. They block direct sunlight from heating up the soil, hold moisture in the ground much longer, and slowly turn into nutrient-rich organic manure as they decay.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni fiofio lɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that lose moisture faster than they can draw water from the soil. They need shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains during their first few years to protect them from direct sun heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni ji nurse ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ amli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight underground for water and nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. This competition results in thin, weak stems and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to prune or cut away extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches that suck energy away from pod production. It also lets sunlight and air pass through the tree canopy, which keeps the tree dry and prevents fungal diseases from building up.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ pod feemɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food rather than water. It indicates that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bolɔɔ amɛbiɔ niyenii moŋ fe nu. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which travels in water droplets and thrives in damp, dark, and cool conditions. Excessive shade and poor airflow in the farm allow the wet fungi to multiply quickly on the pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efãa gbɛ yɛ nu mli ŋmɔtɔi amli ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Shade babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ faa oya yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without turning into fruit during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be kuku mli lɛ?

english: When crops face a shortage of water, they go into survival mode. Dropping their flowers reduces the energy and water the plant needs, allowing it to keep itself alive rather than feeding developing fruits.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni faaa kpe lɛ Amɛyaa wala shihilɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii ni miida.

english: Is it good practice to plant cassava directly inside my young cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Cassava has aggressive, deep roots that consume huge amounts of water and soil nutrients, often starving young cocoa plants. Plantains or bananas are better intercrops because they offer shade without overpowering the young cocoa trees.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ cacao tsei bibii. Plantains loo banana ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛtsĩii kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops produce smaller pods and harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tso titri lɛ naa ŋmeii bibii ni ekpaa nii lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal the fertilizers, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. When weeds take over, your crops do not get enough nutrients to develop large, heavy pods or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii loo aduawai.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds instead of just re-using seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee amɛ ehee lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to grow stronger, yield more food, and withstand common local pests and dry spells better than older seeds, which naturally lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛhe awa. woɔ yibii babaoo ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ, ni amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety will actually sell well in my local market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko baajara jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Traders and buyers look for crops that have good color, firm texture, great taste, and don't spoil easily during transport. Breeders test new varieties with local market women and buyers before releasing them.
ga: Jarayelɔi kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ su kpakpa, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni ŋɔɔ, ni efiteee oya kɛji akɛ akɛyaa he kroko. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ kaa kooloi srɔtoi heei amɛkwɛɔ yɛ yei anɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei kɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛ kpo.

english: Vegetables spoil quickly due to heat, rough handling, and high moisture content. Planting varieties bred for long shelf life and keeping harvested produce in cool, shaded spaces helps them stay fresh much longer.
ga: Aduawai fiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. rough handling and has high humidity Nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ okpamɔ lɛ ni oooha ehi he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does planting a crop with a long shelf life help me make more money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo?

english: Crops that last longer without spoiling give you extra time to transport them to bigger city markets and allow you to wait for market prices to go up instead of selling in a rush at cheap prices.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee lɛ haa onáa be babaoo ni okɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji wuji amli lɛ. ni ehaa omɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara lɛ aya hiɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ oya kɛha jara ni waaa.

english: Is there a way to store my harvested yams for months without them rotting?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee?

english: Yes, selecting varieties known for long storage and keeping them in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn off the bare ground protects them from heat and pests, preserving them for many months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ohala sweet potato henɔi ni ale akɛ amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ni okɛto sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛtsɔ nyɔji babaoo ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do men and women in our community sometimes prefer different crop traits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ wɔ akutsei lɛ amli lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sui srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Men often focus on field performance like high yield and fast market sale, while women who process and cook food often care more about taste, easy peeling, and how long the food stays good in the kitchen.
ga: Hii sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nitsumɔ lɛ mli, tamɔ nibii ni anáa babaoo kɛ jarayeli ni yaa oya lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, yei ni tsuɔ niyenii ahe nii ni amɛhooɔ lɛ susuɔ niyenii lɛ ŋɔɔ, bɔ ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ mli, kɛ be abɔ ni niyenii lɛ baahi shĩa lɛ he fe fɛɛ.

english: If I plant a new high-yielding crop, will it still taste as good as our traditional variety?
ga: Kɛ midu tso hee ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ Ani ebaahi lolo tamɔ wɔ shishijee tso lɛ?

english: Yes, modern plant breeders specifically select new varieties that keep the rich, traditional taste and cooking quality that your family and local buyers love while still giving you higher yields in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei akwɛlɔi halaa tsei srɔtoi heei pɔtɛɛ ni haa shishijee ŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii he sui ni oweku lɛ kɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ ahiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo hu yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: What does it mean when a crop variety gives dual benefits to a farm household?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ko kɛ sɛɛnamɔi enyɔ ba ŋmɔ mli shiabii anɔ?

english: A dual-benefit crop satisfies two major needs at once—such as providing high cash income in the market for the farmer while also offering great taste and long kitchen storage for home cooking.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni sɛɛnamɔi enyɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ hiamɔ nii titrii enyɔ ahe nii shikome tamɔ jarayeli shika babaoo ni anáa kɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa kɛ pantry nitoohe kakadaŋŋ hu haa kɛha shia niyenii.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive dry spells better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ wala yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant crop varieties are bred to grow deeper roots that reach underground water and have leaves that naturally conserve moisture during dry weather.
ga: Afɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛ baai ni haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow while the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have weak root systems and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to trap moisture and protect them until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition causes the plants to grow tall, weak, and thin, resulting in very small yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green crops turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are lacking essential nutrients in the soil, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water and suffocating the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the farm open for the slower-growing cassava to expand and mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmei lɛ ada blɛoo, egbɛ eshwa ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I trim branches off my cocoa trees when they seem to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji lɛ? He ni kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ?

english: Trimming extra or diseased branches helps the tree direct its energy and food into growing big, healthy pods rather than wasting strength on unnecessary leaves and stems.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei ahe ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just replanting seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests often produce weaker plants that get sick easily and yield less food. Certified seeds are specially bred to fight diseases and produce higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ oya ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkɛ helai awuu ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my land produce less food when I grow the same crop on it every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly removes the same specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural food supply for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet environments. Clearing weeds and trimming shade trees lets air and sunlight in to dry the farm and keep the fungus away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ fe nine ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: How do I know if the first rainy day of the year means it is time to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ afi lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: You should wait until the rains become consistent before planting. Sowing after just one early rain can cause the seeds to sprout and then die quickly when the hot sun returns for several dry days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa dani odu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛgboi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or flood the roots so they cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ eyi kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Cowpeas and beans have small bumps on their roots filled with friendly microbes. These microbes take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting like a free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni bɔɔ nii bibii ni feɔ naanyo eyi mli obɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ bɔɔ nii bibii nɛɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose to protect itself when water is scarce. By shedding leaves, the plant loses less water through evaporation and saves its energy underground to keep the roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe kɛji nu bɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu fioo kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli. ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by excessive afternoon heat, severe dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops the flowers to save energy so the main plant can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fa fe nine lɛ hao amɛ. hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide inside the center of my maize plants instead of staying outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms crawl into the tight center roll of tender leaves because it gives them soft food to eat while protecting them from the hot sun, rain, and predators like birds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhaa amɛ niyenii ni mli jɔ ni amɛyeɔ, ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a sickness, or by the plant trying to roll up its leaves to prevent water loss during very dry and hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfo amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu akafite yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and reach upward as fast as possible. Because all their energy goes into growing tall to beat their neighbors, they don't have enough food left to produce big fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawu amɛha hulu la lɛ ni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tee hiɛ waa koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important to pull out weeds while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak, short roots. If weeds grow next to them, the weeds will steal the water, sunlight, and soil food first, causing your young crops to become stunted and weak.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred in a lab for high yields, but their offspring do not keep those good traits. If you plant saved hybrid seeds, the new plants will grow unevenly and produce very small cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛshwiei lɛ hiɛɛɛ nakai sui kpakpai lɛ amli. Kɛji odu hybrid dumɔwui ni ato lɛ Tsei heei daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their skin color completely changes from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting at this time ensures the seeds inside have fully developed the right oils and flavors for fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhewolo nɔ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ená fɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔlɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize often mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the root zone. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer can help the crop turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers around here plant cassava together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ biɛ lɛ duɔ ŋmãa kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space later. Planting them together helps you get two crops from one piece of land and keeps weeds down.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa mra. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, edaa fiofio ni sɛɛ mli lɛ eŋɔ jɛmɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onáa nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ, ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny green insects curling the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miibɔle mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: These insects are aphids that suck juice from the plant leaves, causing them to curl up. Spraying them early with neem oil or recommended insecticides stops them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji aphids ni nuɔ tsei ahe baai amli nu, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite onibii.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves curl up in strong afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing water. It is a natural way the plant survives hot sunshine until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. When it is too hot, the pollen dries up and fruits cannot form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni aduawai nyɛɛɛ afee.

english: What happens if I plant my yam seeds too close to each other in the heap?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋtayaa mli?

english: Planting yams too close makes the roots compete for nutrients and sunlight. This results in many small, thin tubers instead of big, heavy yams.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa anáa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land is ready and healthy enough to plant vegetables without synthetic chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels soft when moist, breaks easily in your hands, and contains living things like earthworms and decomposed leaf litter.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo kɛ́ edɔ Efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ hu yɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage seedlings look weak and flat on the ground after I move them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes root shock because they are used to shade and regular care. Protecting them with fresh palm leaves for a few days helps them adjust to the sun and stand firm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ daa kwɛmɔ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei ahe gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu lɛ mli ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my millet crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-millet tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to harsh soil conditions, so they wake up quickly and grab sunlight and water faster than cultivated crops like millet.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛteɔ shi mra ni amɛheɔ hulu la kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does my groundnut crop harvest with many empty shells that have no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpaa mi-peanut tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods usually happen when the soil lacks calcium during the time the pods are expanding underground. Adding agricultural lime to the soil prevents empty pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that protects the seedlings and keeps the soil moist until the trees are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so long to produce fruits compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow slowly when too many suckers grow around a single parent stem, competing for food and water. Removing excess suckers so that only two or three strong stems remain per stand allows the plant to put its energy into growing big fruit bunches quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa fiofio kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he ni miitswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ lɛ fa babaoo. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii ni wa enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ woɔ aduawai wuji ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli oya.

english: Pepper blossoms fall off when the plants experience severe heat stress or lack water. Adding dry grass or leaf mulch around the base of the plant keeps the root area cool and moist, allowing the flowers to stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in maize fields. Spraying approved treatments or applying crushed neem leaf liquid early in the morning into the center leaf funnels stops them from destroying the growing leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni atswa lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baa ni miiya hiɛ lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to develop black spots and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads easily in cool, damp, and overly shady conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight reach the trees and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm to stop the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, edɔ, kɛ shade tsɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni helai akpa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when there is enough water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi trukaa ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This wilting is usually caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt that blocks water from traveling up the plant stem. Planting tomatoes in a fresh piece of land where peppers or eggplants have not grown recently prevents the disease from attacking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacterial wilt ni tsiɔ nu gbɛ koni ekaya tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ loo eggplant ekwɛ̃ko nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akatutua bo.

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores the soil nutrients so the crop can produce large ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná toi wuji.

english: How do I keep my cassava roots from rotting inside the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long without draining away. Planting cassava stems on top of high raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is too hard, stony, or compacted for the tuber to push through easily. Building deep, soft mounds mixed with organic compost gives the tubers space to expand smoothly and draw food.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ abote mli mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ ni afee lɛ baaha tuber he lɛ mli alɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ejie niyenii kɛjɛ mli.

english: Planting maize on the same soil every season drains specific nutrients and allows pests to settle in the land permanently. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas returns good nutrients to the soil and starves maize pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii kpakpai kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmei mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for crop growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant stay green and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eshishifã lɛ hu aná hewalɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally in dry weather to reduce water loss and protect its root tubers underground. As soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ ni tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why does my okro crop grow plenty of large leaves but fails to grow many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ekwɛɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages the okro plant to focus energy on growing leaves rather than flowers. Using balanced nutrients or higher phosphorus encourages the plant to set more pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ okra tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nɔ ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo awo mli.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil, so they absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing essential food from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on leaf sap. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate pesticides controls these pests before they stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot directly on the branches?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet environments. Pruning excess shade trees and removing infected pods helps keep air circulating and protects healthy pods.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Shade kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebu ŋmeii ni wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent moisture at the soil base helps the plant retain flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to leave proper spacing between my yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Giving yam mounds enough distance ensures each plant gets adequate sunlight and room for root tubers to expand large underground without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato ni ato lɛ to he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. kɛ he ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellowish-brown and the inner walls of the harvested shells show dark brown veins instead of a pale white color.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli gbogboi lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ waa yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops take a very long time to produce fruit while others grow so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daa oya waa lɛ?

english: Different plant varieties have different natural lifespans. Some varieties invest time into building strong root systems to produce high yields later, while fast-growing varieties like suckers quickly produce stems and leaves to yield fruit sooner.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi heɔ be dani amɛmaa shishifãi ni mli wa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai oya koni amɛwo yibii oya.

english: Should I plant crop varieties that produce quickly or varieties that take longer but yield well?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei ni woɔ yibii oya loo tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ shi amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: It depends on your farm goals. Fast-growing types give you quick food and early cash flow, while longer-term varieties often yield heavier crops over time. Many farmers plant a mixture of both to balance quick income with long-term harvests.
ga: Edamɔ otii ni okɛma ohiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Henɔi ni daa oya lɛ baaha oná niyenii oya kɛ shika ni baa oya. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo ni tsii waa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ efutu koni amɛha shika ni amɛnáa oya kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbaakpa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ afee ekome.

english: What is a plant sucker, and why do other farmers prefer planting them?
ga: Mɛni ji tso sucker? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi sumɔɔ ni amɛdu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ?

english: A sucker is a new young shoot that sprouts from the base of an established mother plant, such as a plantain or banana. Farmers plant them because they already have strong growth energy, helping them establish faster than starting from tiny seeds.
ga: Tso ji tso hee ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso ko ni ato ama shi, tamɔ plantain loo banana shishi. Okwaafoi duɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ dalɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa momo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduɔ oya fe ni ajeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli.

english: How can I get my young plantain suckers to grow very big and strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha midumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa?

english: To get big suckers, plant them in nutrient-rich soil mixed with compost, keep the base free from weeds, ensure good watering, and remove excess small shoots so all the energy goes into one or two strong suckers.
ga: koni ona ŋmeii wuji Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi akafee shishitoo lɛ, nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni ojie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ bɔni afee ni hewalɛ fɛɛ aya tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to grow big after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Slow growth happens when young suckers lack soil nutrients, compete with weeds, or are planted in hard, dry soil. Adding organic manure and mulching around the plant holds moisture and speeds up growth.
ga: Dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ jwɛi akaŋ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ awo mli Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha amɛdara.

english: Why does my main plantain tree start dying off after I harvest the fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ beni mikpa aduawai akui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That main tree is called the mother plant. Its main life purpose is to bear that single bunch of fruit. Once harvested, its natural cycle ends so it can make room for the young suckers at its base to take over.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tso lɛ akɛ nyɛ tso. Yiŋtoo titri ni yɔɔ shihilɛ sɛɛ ji ni ewo yibii kome. Kɛji akpa lɛ Ebɔɔ su lɛ baa naagbee koni eha gbɛ aha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ koni amɛye nɔ.

english: Do I need to buy new seeds every time I harvest a bunch of plantains?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe dumɔwui heei be fɛɛ be ni makpa plantain ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, you do not need new seeds. Before the mother plant finishes fruiting, it produces new suckers from its base which will grow into the next generation of fruit-producing plants automatically.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui heei he ehiaaa bo. Dani tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baagbe yibiiwoo naa Ebaajie ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ shishigbɛ ni baada kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛbatsɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ayinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Is it good to leave all the small shoots that sprout around the main plant?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooshi ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso titri lɛ he?

english: No, leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving you with small plants and thin bunches. Prune away weaker shoots and leave only the strongest one or two.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni oshi tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome loo enyɔ pɛ.

english: What should I do with the stem of the main plant after cutting down the fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ beni mifo aduawai akui lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After harvesting, cut down the old stem near the base. Chop up the old leaves and stem to use as mulch around the new suckers, which feeds the soil and protects the young plants.
ga: Yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Kpɔ̃ɔ tso momo lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai momoi kɛ tsei lɛ ni okɛtsu nii akɛ mulch ni bɔleɔ tsei heei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Does the dying mother plant help the new young shoots growing next to it?
ga: Ani tso ni ji nyɛ ni miigbo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi?

english: Yes, as the mother plant finishes its cycle, it transfers its remaining moisture and stored nutrients down to the root system, giving the emerging suckers a strong boost to start their own growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ gbeɔ esɛɛkuu lɛ naa lɛ. Ebaajie ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso ni miiba lɛ náa hewalɛ waa koni ebɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the roots are drowning in too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn dark green and grow vigorously.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifã ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open from the growing tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji yɔɔ mli? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the growing center of the maize plant to feed, and applying recommended insecticides or neem extracts early in the morning or late evening helps clear them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye niyenii. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the blossoms just drop off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the air gets extremely hot, when the soil experiences sudden dry spells, or if you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to build leaves instead of holding onto its fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tso lɛ mli, ni no nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or plant leaves on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo madu baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the dirt so you water less, protects crop roots from heat, stops weeds from growing, and gradually rots into natural fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli shii abɔ. Ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam leaves need as much direct sunlight as possible to produce energy. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground away from diseases and exposes the leaves to the sun, which helps the plant store energy and build large tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ, kɛjɛɔ helai ahe ni ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same farm plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot rapidly drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni ayaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abɛi lɛ mli lɛ baa shi oya. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or recommended sprays prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour heavy buckets of water directly over freshly planted seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ baagi ni tsii shwieɔ shi lɛ? Kɛya dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Pouring heavy streams of water washes small seeds out of their soil beds, buries them too deep under heavy mud, or creates a hard crust on top of the soil that fragile young shoots cannot push through.
ga: Nu babaoo ni oooshwie lɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni ebaafu amɛ tsɔ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. aloo efee ŋmei ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ abote mli.

english: Why do people say I should keep big trees on my cocoa farm when planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli beni miduɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Big trees provide shade to cool down young cocoa plants, protect them from harsh scorching sun, and keep the soil moist during hot weather so the crops do not dry up.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni haa kokoo tsei bibii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akagbi.

english: When cocoa trees get too much sun, their leaves turn yellow or brown at the edges, dry up, and drop off early, leaving bare branches that struggle to grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ asɛɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Egbi ni egbee shi oya Enɛ haa tsei niji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni miitao amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baa.

english: Can having too many big shade trees on my farm actually harm my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-kokoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, if shade is too thick, it blocks sunshine that cocoa needs to make pods, keeps the farm too wet, and encourages diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ hulutsoo lɛ mli wa tsɔ Ebaatsi hulu la ni he hiaa kookoo lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni oha helai srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Does it matter what kind of tree I allow to grow alongside my cocoa crop?
ga: Ani tsei ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, some trees attract cocoa pests or choke cocoa roots, while recommended shade trees like Emire or Framo provide light shade and improve soil quality without harming cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi gbalaa kookoo kooloi loo amɛtsiɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ anaa. yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ Emir loo Framo he ŋaa lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni eyeee kookoo lɛ awui.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Kookoo ni adu ehee?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, shielding young cocoa while providing early food and income for your family.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu kookoo bibii ahe Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji niyenii kɛ shika hu jɛɛhe kɛha oweku lɛ.

english: Can I plant heavy food crops like cassava or yam together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ani abaanyɛ akɛfata kookoo tsei bibii ahe?

english: It is best to avoid heavy tubers like cassava near young cocoa because their aggressive roots steal water and food from cocoa, and harvesting them damages fragile young cocoa roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo mli. Ni kpamɔ lɛ baafite kookoo shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ.

english: Why is the changing weather making my cocoa trees behave differently these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ miiha mi cacao tsei lɛ miifee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Unpredictable rainfall and rising temperatures stress cocoa plants, causing them to shed leaves early, flower at unexpected times, or produce smaller pods than they used to.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi mra. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ mli loo ewoɔ fɔfɔii bibii fe tsutsu lɛ

english: How do shade trees help keep water in the soil during a long dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Shade tree roots draw water from deep underground, and their canopy blocks direct sun rays from evaporating surface moisture, while fallen leaves act as a mulch blanket over the dirt.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishifãi gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni amɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are extension officers encouraging shade trees now when farmers used to clear all trees in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ amrɔ nɛɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ miitswa shade tsei ahe adafi lɛ? Be ko ni eho lɛ, okwaafoi shwieɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: In the past, summers were cooler and rainfall was reliable. Today, temperatures are hotter and dry seasons are longer, so shade trees are now needed to save cocoa from heat drying.
ga: Be ko ni eho lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ waa ni abuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ akɛ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Ŋmɛnɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amrɔ nɛɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ he miihia koni eye ebua ni abu kookoo lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: If I cut down all the large trees on my land, will my cocoa grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ Ani mikoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya?

english: While young cocoa without shade grows fast at first, full exposure to sun makes the trees age quickly, lose leaf health, and die off much earlier than shade-protected cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ mli moŋ, shi shishijee lɛ, kookoo bibioo lɛ daa oya. Shi hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔ oya. Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni laajeɔ Ni egboɔ oya kwraa fe kookoo ni nine shɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has too much water, suffocating the roots. Adding manure or fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce food for the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they feel stressed by harsh dry weather, lack of shade, or insect attacks. The tree sheds its flowers to save energy and water so it can survive the difficult conditions.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open on the bush right before I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ dani mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when sudden heavy rain follows a dry spell. The inside of the tomato absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit to burst.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni no haa aduawai lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die early when the hot sun comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves lose water quickly under intense heat. If the soil does not have enough moisture or organic mulch to cover it, the vine shuts down early to keep the tuber underground alive.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo organic mulch ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wein tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ mra koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Cassava roots rot in soggy ground because standing water stops air from reaching the roots. Without air, the roots weaken and fungal diseases easily attack and rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and keeping the crop small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee tso lɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the top of the soil. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, or if small soil pests weaken the roots, strong winds can pull the whole tree down easily.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ baa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei muu fɛɛ kɛba shi mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay weak even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil meant for your plants. If weeds are not cleared early, your crops will be starved and stay small.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛbaafee bibioo.

english: Why do officers ask us to plant cowpea or groundnuts before planting other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ biɔ ni wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap air and turn it into natural soil food (nitrogen). When the plant leaves decay, they leave rich food in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) beni tso lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni jara wa yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin without yielding fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight for light. They put all their energy into growing tall to beat their neighbors to the sun, leaving no energy left to bear fruits or seeds.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawuu amɛha la lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim yɛ hulu la mli. Hewalɛ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha ewo yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK early in the growing season helps keep the leaves green and boosts grain yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa.
