Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my farmland become hard and dry quickly even after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard soil lacks organic matter, which acts like a natural sponge to soak up and hold moisture. Adding compost, animal manure, or mulching your farm with dry grass helps the soil retain rainwater and stay soft longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni ehiɛɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo jwɛi wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli ni ehi shi blɛoo be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing raw fertilizer directly against a plant stem can scorch or 'burn' the plant roots due to concentrated salts. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring or band a few inches away from the stem where feeder roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã loo ‘eshã’ tsei lɛ ashishifãi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ mli. ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme dry heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Watering regularly during dry periods and using balanced plant food helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tso niyenii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show light yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and patterned leaves on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early helps protect your farm.
ga: Baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits rotting while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ ashishi miifite be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, which happens when plants cannot get enough calcium due to irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist through mulching and proper watering helps prevent the fruit bottoms from turning black and rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ashishi akatsɔ ediŋŋ ni ekafite.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are attacking my maize early in the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall armyworms miitutua mi-corn lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Fall armyworms leave ragged holes in the central young leaves (the funnel) of the maize plant along with brown saw-dust like droppings. Inspecting your field weekly allows you to spot them early and apply neem oil or recommended insecticides before severe damage occurs.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ shĩɔ bu ni mli ewo muji yɛ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii (cones) lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmãa. Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ daa otsi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. Ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii dani nɔ ko ni fiteɔ nii waa aba.

english: Why should I rotate my maize with cowpeas or groundnuts instead of planting maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ cowpeas loo peanuts atsake ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ

english: Planting maize continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets soil pests build up. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts add natural nitrogen back into the soil, keeping the land fertile and breaking pest and disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shi be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my bean plants produce many leaves and long vines but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai kakadaji kɛ wain tsei babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages bean plants to grow lush foliage instead of flowers and pods. Since legumes make their own nitrogen, avoid applying high-nitrogen fertilizer so the plant can focus on pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the yam tubers grow big underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by fungal leaf diseases or when exposed to extreme dry heat. Staking the vines properly off the ground improves airflow and keeps leaves dry, allowing the plant to stay healthy long enough to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal leaf lɛ emɔ amɛ loo kɛ́ amɛtee hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa mli. Kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient in the soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like beans in the field can help restore the soil's nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather. Pruning shade trees and excess cocoa branches lets air and sunlight in, which keeps the pods dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically from dry to wet. Watering your crop regularly at the base early in the morning can keep the plants stable.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu daa yɛ shishigbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the sap under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects. Spraying neem seed extract or appropriate pest treatment early can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Neem dumɔwui amli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa. baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects around them in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. Cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and naturally put it back into the soil, which feeds your maize plants, while also shading the ground to keep weeds from growing.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ji niyenii kɛha o-corn tsei lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the crop roots and out of the field before the plants have time to drink it in, leading to wasted money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli dani tsei lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can struggle to hold up heavy fruit bunches during strong winds, or nematodes in the soil might be damaging the roots. Propping the stems up with sturdy wooden poles (staking) supports the heavy trees.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni baanyɛ akpɛtɛ aduawai ni tsii ahe Ewa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Aloo nematodes ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ tsei ni wa (stakes) afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni akɛfi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and becoming soft while in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams start sprouting when stored in hot, bright places because they react to heat and light as a signal to grow again. Keeping harvested yams in a cool, well-ventilated, and shaded yam barn slows down sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ la he akɛ okadi ni haa amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ. Sweet potato ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ ni mli ejɔ mli Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical pest treatments on my crop leaves during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying in the hot afternoon heat causes the liquid chemical to evaporate too fast to work properly, and the combination of hot sun and chemical liquid can scorch and burn your crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ tsofa mli nu baanyɛ ashã ni ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo hee nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa, while also providing you with fast food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛ shika haa dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How does growing plantains help my farm income while waiting for cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Te plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni maná shika yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees take three to five years to start bearing fruit, but plantains yield fruit within a year. Intercropping allows you to harvest and sell plantains to support your family while your main cocoa crop matures.
ga: Eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi plantains baawo yibii yɛ afi kome mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa plantains ni ohɔ̃ɔ koni okɛkwɛ oweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni o-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: If I spot plants with a little bit of disease while clearing my farm, what should I do with them?
ga: Kɛji mina tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ fioo beni mijieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee nakai tsei lɛ?

english: You must sort and separate infected plants from healthy ones immediately. Leaving diseased branches near healthy plants allows pests and fungi to spread across the entire farm.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ogbala amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to cut down and remove diseased crops instead of leaving them to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajie amɛ moŋ fe ni aaaha amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Once a crop is infected with a serious disease, it acts as a permanent breeding ground for pathogens. Cutting down and burning or isolating the sick plant protects the surrounding healthy crops from catching the infection.
ga: Kɛji helai ni naa wa ba tsei anɔ lɛ Ebaatsu nii akɛ he ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ daa. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ashãa loo agbalaa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I leave diseased branches lying on the ground after I clear them off my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fungal spores and pests can live on dead plant tissue lying on the ground. Rain droplets or wind can easily splash these spores from the ground back onto healthy standing plants.
ga: Fungal spores kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi tso mli fãji ni egboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ashɛrɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ oya.

english: Can a crop that has become sick cure itself and return to how it was before?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsa ehe ni eku esɛɛ kɛba bɔ ni eyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Severe crop diseases, such as cocoa swollen shoot virus or advanced fungal infections, cannot heal on their own once established. Once damaged, the plant tissue remains infected and must be managed or removed.
ga: Tsei ahe helai ni naa wa tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efuu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni etee hiɛ waa lɛ Enyɛŋ etsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛji eba pɛ. Kɛji tso mli fãji fite lɛ Tso mli fãji lɛ baakã he ahi hela mli ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ loo ajie.

english: How can I tell if a plant on my farm is just starting to get sick versus being totally ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ emɔ hela kɛkɛ ni amɛfite kwraa?

english: Early disease shows as small leaf spots, mild yellowing, or slight wilting on a few stems, whereas a totally ruined plant has black stems, rotten pods, dying roots, or completely dried leaves.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, hela lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ baai bibii. ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbo fioo yɛ tsei komɛi anɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni efite kwraa lɛ baaná tsei diji, ŋmeii ni egboi, shishifãi ni egboi, loo baai ni egbi kwraa.

english: If disease affects only one part of my farm, do I need to destroy my whole farm?
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ ye miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome pɛ nɔ lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni makpãtã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ?

english: No, you do not need to destroy the whole farm if the disease is localized. You can create a buffer zone by cutting down infected plants and a few healthy boundary plants around them to contain the spread, saving the rest of your farm.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ofite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji hela lɛ yɛ he kome. Obaanyɛ ofee buffer zone kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni husui kpakpai ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Ajie nakai tsei lɛ koni akɛtsi hela lɛ gbɛɛmɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant new cocoa trees on land where crops were previously destroyed by disease?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela kpata tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, it is safe if you properly clear and destroy all infected plant residues first and allow the land a resting period or use disease-resistant crop varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ atsu nii.

english: What steps can I take to build confidence that my farm will recover after losing crops to sickness?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hela efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can rebuild your farm successfully by following proper extension advice: sorting diseased plants during land preparation, planting protective shade crops like plantains, and using improved, disease-resistant crop varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma oŋmɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ omanyeyeli mli kɛtsɔ ŋaawoi ni sa ni kɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oootsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo buɔ mɔ he, tamɔ plantains, kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni afee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my okro growing very tall with plenty of leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshishifãi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes okro plants to put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa okra tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather when there is too much shade and dampness.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli beni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves dry up and die long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ egbi ni egbo be saŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Premature leaf drying in yam is often caused by fungal leaf spot diseases like anthracnose, which attack the foliage and reduce the crop's ability to feed the growing tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot diseases, tamɔ anthracnose, ni tutuaa baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and allowing fungal rots to develop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my watermelons turning dark and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering patterns.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Legumes like beans put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots, restoring fertility that heavy-feeding crops like maize take away.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ. Bɔni afee ni aku sɛɛ aha fɔmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ.

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or pests like weevils damage their root system, weakening the tree's anchor in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii fite shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ osɛɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves using sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch full sunlight and stay free of ground diseases, resulting in much bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot easily hold the weight of heavy fruit bunches, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden prop keeps the tree standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo, titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential soil food. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color and form strong cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot uses up all the nutrients in the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up. Rotating your field with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts goodness back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ehaa abele pɔtɛɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa kpakpafeemɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the roots of my cassava rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, suffocating the plant. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots remain dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛhe awa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mixture of soapy water or neem extract helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla efutu mli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other like crowded children for light, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper space lets each plant grow thick stems and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli tamɔ gbekɛbii ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso feɔ tsitsi ni mli tse kɛ tsitsi agbo.

english: How do I know the soil is ready for planting right after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The very first light rain usually only wets the top layer of dirt, which will dry out quickly under the sun and kill young seeds. It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked deep into the ground before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ baagbi oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni ebaagbe dumɔwui ni edako lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is lacking, or when there are no insects around to move pollen within the flower. Regular watering and planting at the right time of year help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛ́ nu faaa, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe. koni ekɛ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ aya Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are very sensitive. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them provides living cover, keeping the air moist and protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa kwraa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni ooodu yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaye abua ni okɛ oshihilɛ ato. tsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: What happens to my cassava crops if I plant the stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight for space, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin leaves and produce very small tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa bibii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot quickly when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. High humidity and splashing rainwater spread the fungal spores easily from infected pods to healthy ones.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya.

english: Why is my maize crop covered in small green caterpillars that eat the leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the plant canopy during the hot day and come out at night to feed on soft young maize leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye ŋmãa baai bibii

english: Why is it important for me to wear protective clothing when spraying chemical medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Agricultural chemicals can pass through your skin or be inhaled into your lungs, causing sickness or long-term health issues. Protective gear keeps the spray safely away from your body while you treat your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ hewolo lɛ mli loo ashɛre kɛya fɛ̃i mli. Ekɛ hela loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Nibii ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akaje ogbɔmɔtso lɛ he shweshweeshwe be mli ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before they can grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or dry, or when the soil lacks enough moisture and nutrients to support fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra water shoots growing around the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nu mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, known as chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk. Removing them helps the tree focus its energy on producing healthy leaves and pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How do weeds lower my crop yield if I leave them growing in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi? Kɛji miha ekwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, leaving your crops weak and producing smaller harvests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are lacking food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: If maize leaves start turning pale yellow from the middle tips backward in a V-shape, or if the stalks stay short and thin, the soil is low in nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ amɛteŋgbɛ kɛtee amɛsɛɛ, ni amɛfee V su Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishifã lɛ yɛ kuku ni eyɛ mlɛo lolo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmãa awo mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of insects and fine powder while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ sũ bibii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils attack maize if the grains are not dried completely before storage or if the storage space has moisture, allowing pests to multiply inside the cobs.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. aloo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ Enɛ baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: When is the best month for me to clear my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo?

english: The best time to clear your land for cocoa is during the early dry season, specifically around January or February. Clearing during these months gives the weeds and cut brush enough time to dry so you can prepare the field before the first rains start.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni akɛdu kookoo ji yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli. Titri lɛ, yɛ January loo February mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ nyɔji nɛɛ amli lɛ haa jwɛi kɛ brɔshi ni afo lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ osaa he lɛ dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi.

english: What happens if I start clearing my farm late after the rains have already begun?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mibɔi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: If you start clearing after the rains begin, the soil becomes muddy and difficult to work on. Weeds will also grow back very quickly, forcing you to spend extra labor and money clearing the land again before planting.
ga: Kɛji obɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ bafeɔ muji ni ewaa akɛ ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi baakwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni otsu nii waa ni ofite shika ni okɛjie jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ dani odu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I clear my farmland during the peak of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing land during heavy rains makes the soil muddy, hard to work on, and causes heavy soil erosion. It also makes it impossible to dry and clear cut weeds easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ muji, ewaa akɛ aaatsu he nii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa. Ehaaa anyɛ agbi ni ajie jwɛi lɛ hu mlɛo.

english: Why does cocoa farming require specific timing for each farm activity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ biɔ be pɔtɛɛ ko kɛha ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ nitsumɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to weather patterns like rainfall and dry spells. Performing tasks like land clearing, planting, or weeding at the right time ensures the trees receive the water and nutrients they need to grow strong and produce good pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei. Nifeemɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ, dumɔ loo jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii kpakpai aba.

english: What happens to my crops if I miss the main planting season?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo be titri ni miduɔ nii lɛ mli?

english: If you plant out of season, your crops may not get enough rainfall during their critical growth stage. This leads to stunted growth, weak roots, low yield, or even the complete loss of your crops.
ga: Kɛji odu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Ekolɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa, shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Does every crop have a specific month when work on it must begin?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko ni esa akɛ eje nitsumɔ shishi yɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops rely heavily on local weather and rain cycles. Starting field preparation and planting in the correct months ensures early growth matches the rainy season for optimal crop development.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii damɔ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. He ni abaaje lɛ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mra be mli dalɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kpãa gbee koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does it feel like there is no work to do on the farm during certain months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ enuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni nitsumɔ ko bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi lɛ?

english: Farm work follows seasonal natural cycles. During parts of the dry season or between planting and harvesting windows, crops are either resting or growing on their own, meaning major field activities naturally pause until the next season begins.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli be mli nibii asɛɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fãi komɛi amli loo yɛ dumɔ kɛ kpamɔ samfɛji lɛ ateŋ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi titrii lɛ Ebaakpa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees seem to slow down their growth during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally conserve water and energy when moisture levels are low. During dry periods, growth slows down to help the tree survive until the rainy season returns to trigger new leaves and flowering.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ buɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa ni ekɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei baa.

english: Why is timing so critical when preparing land for long-term crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be he hiaa waa kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Long-term crops like cocoa need strong root establishment in their first year. Preparing the land early in the dry months ensures you can plant right at the onset of the rains, giving seedlings the maximum amount of moisture to survive the next dry season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ kookoo lɛ he miihia shishitoo ni wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu babaoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is seasonal planning so important for a farmer in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be he gbɛjianɔtoo he hiaa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Agriculture in Ghana relies heavily on rain cycles. Planning your clearing, planting, and harvesting according to wet and dry seasons ensures crops get natural water when needed and prevents wasted labor when conditions are unsuitable.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha tsei lɛ ajiemɔ, dumɔwui, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli nu kɛ́ ehe miihia. ni atsĩ nitsumɔ ni baafite lɛ naa kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ esaaa.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize start turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baa lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: When soil lacks nitrogen, maize plants move the remaining nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the young upper leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil when harvested.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ akpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava shed most of its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself; without leaves, the plant loses very little moisture to the hot air and can survive in the soil until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ŋmei he. Kɛ́ baai bɛ lɛ, nu fioo ko pɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out tomato pollen, preventing flowers from getting fertilized, which causes the plant to drop the useless flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ nii Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa amɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain shoots give me very small bunches if I let all the young stems grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ woɔ niji bibii waa kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ tsei bibii gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many young suckers compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, stealing the food needed to make a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee plantain ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small if I plant my cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji mikɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their underground roots fight each other for root space and soil food, preventing any single plant from forming thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmei tsei lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear away all the large trees in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight; they require taller shade plants like plantain or trees to shelter them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need strong tall stakes to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy required to send food down to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛ niyenii aya shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling instead of growing flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the underside of tender young leaves, distorting their growth as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ashishi. ni efiteɔ dalɛ beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why does lowland rice grow well in flooded mud while my maize rots and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that carry oxygen from their leaves down to their flooded roots, whereas maize roots suffocate and drown without air in wet soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I put fertilizer on my corn farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer gives corn crops essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, helping the plants grow strong, stay green, and yield larger, heavier cobs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa, amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli?

english: The best practice is to apply the first batch of fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after planting when the seedlings emerge, followed by a second application when the corn reaches knee height.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ lɛ.

english: Can putting too much chemical fertilizer burn or damage my crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo baanyɛ ashã loo efite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer at once can scorch the roots and leaves of your corn, stunt plant growth, and waste your hard-earned money.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã o-abele lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. ehaa tsei adalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ shika ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa lɛ

english: Why is it important for me to buy my farm inputs from a licensed chemical shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mahe ŋmɔ mli nibii kɛjɛ tsofafeemɔ shwapo ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Licensed chemical shops sell genuine, unadulterated fertilizers and pesticides, and the shopkeepers are trained to give you correct instructions on safety and dosage.
ga: Tsofa shwapoi ni yɔɔ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo lɛ hɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ, ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi. Ni atsɔɔ shwapoi anɔtsɛmɛi koni amɛwo ŋaa ni ja yɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ he.

english: How do I know which specific chemical or fertilizer my crops actually need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mitsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can determine crop needs by observing leaf color and growth signs, or by describing your crop's current stage to an extension officer or agrochemical dealer who can recommend the right product.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole nɔ ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛtsɔ baa lɛ su kɛ dalɛ he okadii ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mlitsɔɔmɔ nɔ aha extension official loo agrochemical jarayelɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nibii ni sa kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I calculate how many bags of fertilizer or chemical containers to buy for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: The required quantity depends on the total acreage of your farm and crop spacing, so measuring your field size allows agro-dealers to tell you the exact amount needed.
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ osusu oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ ni ekɛɛ bo shika pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your corn lacks sufficient nitrogen in the soil, which can be fixed by applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does corn show faster growth after chemical fertilizer application compared to organic manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ wo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa oya kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers dissolve quickly in soil moisture, providing nutrients that corn roots can absorb immediately for rapid leaf and stalk development.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ sũ mli nu mli. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ŋmãa shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why is my corn growing very tall in some parts of the farm but staying short in other areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi ebɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when soil fertility or moisture varies across your land, which you can balance by spreading fertilizer evenly throughout the whole farm.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ afee ekome kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaajara pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do if insects start eating the leaves of my growing corn?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji kooloi bɔi mi-abele baai ni miida lɛ yeli?

english: You should immediately visit an agrochemical shop for a recommended crop protection spray and apply it early before the pests damage the growing point of the corn stalk.
ga: Esa akɛ oya agrochemical shwapo ko mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni oyahe tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ. ni okɛtsu nii kɛjɛ shishijee Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does locally grown rice in Ghana taste and behave differently from the imported rice I buy at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ŋɔɔ ni efeɔ enii yɛ srɔto fe ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Local Ghanaian rice is often harvested fresh and retains more natural nutrients and aroma, whereas imported rice is heavily polished and stored for long periods, which removes some natural flavor and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akpaa Ghana maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ ehee ni ehiɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ ehenumɔ babaoo mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ashɛreɔ ŋmãa ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ waa ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Where can a beginner farmer like me get good quality rice seeds to start planting?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafonyo hee tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛdu?

english: You can get certified seeds from your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office, registered seed dealers, or local farmers' cooperatives that work with organizations promoting Ghanaian rice.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔhe lɛ, dumɔwui jarayelɔ ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ. loo maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akui ni kɛ Ghana Omɔ He Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do rice crops require so much water on the field compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are adapted to grow in wet conditions where their shallow roots can easily absorb nutrients, and keeping water on the field prevents unwanted weeds from growing and competing with the rice.
ga: Atsake omɔ tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akabɔ akaŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to level my land flat before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Leveling the land ensures that water spreads evenly across the entire field, preventing some plants from drowning in deep water while others dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei komɛi abote nu ni mli kwɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant rice seeds directly into the main field or start them in a small nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery and transplanting seedlings gives the young plants a head start to grow strong against weeds, though direct planting saves labor if your land is clean.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ ji nitsumɔ ni baa shi kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse moŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that the field has poor drainage, which can be fixed by applying the right fertilizer like Urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ urea ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and are extremely tough; heavy rains activate them instantly to compete with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhe wa waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsirɛɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How can I protect my rice grains from birds when the crop starts producing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe kɛji tsei lɛ bɔi dumɔwui amli yaa?

english: Birds target rice when the grains are soft and milky; you can protect them by using scarecrows, bird-scaring ribbons, or by clearing nearby bushes where birds rest.
ga: Okpoi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ su tamɔ mliki. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he gbeyei, tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ okpoi, loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ he ni okpoi jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ lɛ ni oootsi amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time my rice is fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ baashɛ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grain heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color and feel hard when you bite or press them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. ni enuɔ he waa kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ lɛ loo anyɛ enɔ

english: Why do I need to dry my rice immediately after cutting it from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmãa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Drying reduces the moisture inside the grains so they do not rot, smell, or grow mold, ensuring the rice stays good for storage and milling.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, egboŋ, eŋɔɔɔ loo ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni akɛto kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my crops failing to grow on land that was previously used for illegal mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shika tsuru ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil where plants feed and often leaves behind toxic chemicals or hard mud. Without good topsoil and clean water, crop roots cannot breathe or absorb the nutrients they need to survive.
ga: Sũ ni akuɔ mli lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa ni haa tsei niyenii lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, eshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo muji ni wa yɛ esɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ nu ni mli tse bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Burning destroys essential soil nutrients, kills friendly soil organisms that feed your plants, and dries out the ground. Leaving plant remains to rot naturally builds richer soil for future harvests.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ ahiɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ kpamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. It indicates your soil nutrients are exhausted and need organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ etã, ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil is too hard or compacted by heavy work on the land, tubers cannot expand underground. Cassava needs loose, deep soil so its roots can swell and grow large.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitsumɔ ni tsii ni atsuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tubers nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse he hia cassava koni eha eshishifãi lɛ afuu ni amɛdara.

english: How does using muddy, polluted river water affect my vegetable farm?
ga: Te faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni mli ewo muji lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dirty or chemically polluted water coats the soil with harmful waste, suffocates roots, and can introduce toxins that weaken or kill your vegetables instead of nourishing them.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo tsofai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshara haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ tsofai fɔji ni haa o-vegetables lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo egbeɔ amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops rot and die when water sits on my farm for days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to live just like humans do. Flooded soil blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to drown and rot underground.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods after all the big forest trees around my farm are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo komɛi beni tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ eda lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Afo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees need shade and protection from harsh sunlight and drying winds. Without large shade trees, the hot sun stresses the cocoa plants, causing leaves to dry and reducing fruit production.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ nɔ mi waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do shade trees on my farm help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Shade trees drop leaves that cover and protect the soil, keeping it cool and holding moisture much longer so your crops do not dry out quickly during heat waves.
ga: Shade tsei lɛ jieɔ baai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ he lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiɛɛ oya tamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant different types of crops on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and attracts pests that feed on that specific crop. Rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and naturally reduces pest problems.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that adapt easily to poor conditions and quickly steal water and nutrients from the soil before your planted crops have a chance to take them in.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa amli oya. ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my healthy cocoa trees when they are growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This helps prevent diseases and allows the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, hela emɔmɔ amɛ, loo ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to start trimming my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mi-cacao tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: It is best to prune your cocoa trees right before the rainy season or early in the main crop season, as this prepares the trees to produce strong leaves and flowers for the coming harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba loo yɛ be titri ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ baasaa tso lɛ koni ewo baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha kpamɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: I see tiny flowers growing directly on the trunk of my cocoa tree; is that normal?
ga: Minaa fɔfɔi bibioo ko ni Miida yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa?

english: Yes, cocoa trees naturally produce flowers directly on their main trunk and thick branches rather than at the tips of twigs. These flower spots are where your cocoa pods will form.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔmɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ kɛ eniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ naagbee lɛ Nɛkɛ fɔfɔi ahe hei nɛɛ ji he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated quickly, or if the tree lacks water, shade, or soil nutrients. Climate stress can also cause the tree to drop flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ashɛɛɛ amɛhe oya. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ baanyɛ aha tsei ajie fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ.

english: How long does it take for a small cocoa flower to grow into a pod ready for harvest?
ga: kookoo fɔfɔi bibii Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Once a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about 5 to 6 months to grow from a tiny cherelle into a fully mature cocoa pod.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani ejɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibioo ko mli edaa. kɛyashi kookoo ŋmɔji ni edara kwraa lɛ anɔ

english: What is cocoa pollination, and how does it happen on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ebaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pollination happens when tiny insects carry pollen from one flower to another. This transfer triggers the flower to stop dropping and start developing into a cocoa pod.
ga: Pollination baa kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko mli. Nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpa gbee ni amɛje shishi amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Can I pollinate cocoa flowers myself by hand, and will it help my harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ miniji awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli? Ni ani ebaaye ebua yɛ nikpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, hand pollination involves manually transferring pollen between flowers using small tools. Doing this can greatly increase the number of pods on your trees compared to relying only on natural insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ biɔ ni akɛ niji atsɔ fɔfɔi ateŋ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ nibii bibii anɔ. Enɛ feemɔ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli kooloi pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he

english: What simple practices can I do on my farm to get more pods this flowering season?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni maná pods babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can increase your yield by neatly pruning your trees to let in light, keeping the farm clear of weeds, protecting natural pollinating insects, and practicing hand pollination during flowering.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha nibii ni afeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni oookpa amɛ fɛfɛo koni amɛha la lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahe kɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he nifeemɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Are there insects on my farm that actually help my cocoa flowers instead of destroying them?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakpãtã amɛhiɛ?

english: Yes, tiny insects called midges live in damp leaf litter on your farm and are vital because they pollinate your cocoa flowers so they can become pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ hiɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni amɛhe hiaa waa ejaakɛ amɛhaa o-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will spraying chemicals on my flowering cocoa trees hurt my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Spraying harsh insecticides while flowers are open can kill beneficial insects like midges that pollinate the crop, leading to fewer pods forming on your trees.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwie shi yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miikwɛ lolo lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges ni haa tsei lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa pods fioo pɛ baa otso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive their early growth stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ shishijee fãi ni edara lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good to plant plantains in the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade to protect the cocoa from direct sun heat, while also giving you food and quick income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii ni oná shika oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without forming pods due to a lack of tiny pollinating midges, prolonged dry weather, or insect attacks. Proper moisture and pest management help flowers develop into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ yɛ Fɛ̃i kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for my cocoa pods to turn yellow before picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani mikɛto?

english: Harvesting cocoa pods when they are still green means the beans inside are not fully developed. Waiting until they turn yellow or orange ensures maximum bean size, good weight, and high quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eshɛko he jogbaŋŋ lolo. Mɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ dalɛ fa fe fɛɛ, amɛtsiimɔ hi, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the Harmattan dry season lasts very long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need regular moisture to form and keep pods. Extended dry weather forces the tree to drop flowers and small pods to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee amɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ni amɛkɛto. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ nu ato ni oha ohe ahi wala mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they get mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly humid conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning excess branches for sunlight, and removing infected pods helps stop the spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. weeding Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do the young shoots on my cocoa trees look dried up as if fire burned them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi tamɔ nɔ ni la miitswa amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by mirids (capsids), tiny insects that suck sap from young stems and leaves, injecting toxic saliva that causes the shoots to dry up and die back.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ. Spray toxic saliva ni haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant my cocoa trees too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close makes them compete for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. It also prevents air movement, creating damp conditions that promote fungal diseases.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ, hulu la kɛ nu yɔɔ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa.

english: Extra shoots, known as chupons, suck away nutrients and energy that the tree needs to produce cocoa pods. Removing them helps the main tree stay strong and yield more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, shwieɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm needs fertilizer for my crops to produce well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa trees have pale yellow leaves, grow very slowly, or produce small and few pods despite getting enough rain, the soil is likely low in nutrients and needs specialized cocoa fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa po sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu fɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo, ni ebiɔ ni akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi awo mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. The plant naturally moves the small amount of food it has to its newest top leaves so it can keep growing, showing you that the soil needs organic compost or fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛji nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baajie niyenii fioo ko kɛya baai heei lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eya nɔ eda. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. The plant protects itself during heat stress by dropping blossoms so it does not waste valuable water and energy trying to feed fruits it cannot support.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Tsei buɔ amɛhe he yɛ dɔlɛ be mli kɛtsɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee nu kɛ hewalɛ ni jara wa ni okɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ aduawai ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ aye niyenii.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same farm without them stealing food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛjuuu niyenii kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them because maize and cassava grow at different speeds and feed at different soil depths. Maize grows quickly and uses the topsoil, while cassava grows slower and sends its roots deeper later, allowing you to harvest maize early without damaging the cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ amɛteŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi daa oya ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa sɛɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa ŋmãa oya ni efiteee ŋmãa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of spreading out. Because the plant uses all its energy to grow tall to reach light, it does not have enough energy left to form heavy branches and produce peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛná la. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshwɛɛɛ ni akɛbaafee tsei niji ni tsii ni akɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep producing good yields if I take proper care of it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ kookoo tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A well-managed cocoa tree can produce good yields for 25 to 30 years or more. It usually starts bearing pods after 3 to 4 years, reaches peak production around 10 years, and continues yielding well if kept pruned, shaded, and free of pests.
ga: Cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Bei pii lɛ, amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ pods yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ aaafee afii 10 mli, ni amɛbaatsa nɔ amɛwo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ, awo amɛ shade ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on my farm before or alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani loo yɛ cocoa plantains bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does cutting off the top tip of my pepper plant make it produce more fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo pepper tso lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming the top tip stops the plant from growing straight up and signals it to grow side branches. A bushier plant creates more stems, which leads to more flowers and ultimately a higher harvest of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ, ni etsɔɔ niji lɛ koni amɛdara. Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi babaoo lɛ woɔ tsei babaoo. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii babaoo baa, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a natural self-defense mechanism to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through evaporation and stays alive underground until the rains return to trigger fresh growth.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ eba koni ewo shweremɔ hee he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow curved and branched instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ niji moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil beneath them is too hard or rocky. The growing tuber cannot easily push through hard ground, so it splits and branches into soft pockets of soil, which is why making high, soft earth mounds helps yams grow long and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi. Bulbs ni miida lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. mlɛo No hewɔ lɛ, ejaraa ni egbɛɔ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season cause my harvest to drop each year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?
