english: Maize consumes specific nutrients from the upper layer of soil every growing cycle. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot exhausts those specific nutrients, leaving the soil drained unless you rotate crops or plant leguminous crops like beans to restore the ground.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã fɛɛ fã mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Dalɛ He Gbɛjianɔtoo Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo odu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the roots will give the plants the food they need to stay green and grow heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when the plant is stressed by hot dry weather or infected by tiny insects like whiteflies that pass diseases to the plant. Giving your plants regular water at the base and spraying neem water can protect them from heat and pests.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hao tso lɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ hela eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ emɔ tso lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa ni akɛ neem nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel too hot, don't get steady water, or lack nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil around the roots moist with mulch and feeding the plant with compost helps the flowers turn into strong pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni anáaa daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Shishifãi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baawo mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods off the farm helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ mli lɛ kɛ cocoa pods diji baa. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni afolɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do my orange trees drop small green fruits on the ground before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani eda?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they run out of water during dry spells or when fruit flies pierce the skin. Mulching around the tree base to hold moisture and using fruit fly traps will help the oranges stay on the tree until harvest.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji nu bɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii tsɔ amɛhewolo nɔ. Mulching ni akɛbaabɔle Tsei lɛ ashishi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛtswaa ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni citrus lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in tall, thin plants with small harvests. Proper spacing gives every seed enough room to build thick stems and full yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ hu faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil without proper drainage, suffocating the tubers. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong rain and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots near the soil surface and get top-heavy when carrying fruit bunches. Supporting fruiting stems with strong wooden prop poles prevents wind from pushing the trees over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛmiiwo aduawai akui. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating large holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on cabbage leaves that hatch into hungry caterpillars that feed on the crop. Checking under leaves regularly and spraying natural neem leaf extract kills young caterpillars before they ruin the head.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baa lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink up the groundwater and fertilizer meant for your crops while blocking sunlight. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure all soil nutrients go straight into feeding your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛwoɔ onibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa otsei titrii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I dump all my fertilizer on my maize crop at once instead of spreading it out over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ shikome moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: If you apply all the fertilizer at once, heavy rains will wash most of it away before the plant can absorb it, wasting your money. Giving fertilizer in split doses allows the crop to use what it needs as it grows.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛyaa dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ atsu nii be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary for me to walk through my farm regularly after I have already added fertilizer?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ ewo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, regular monitoring is essential. If you leave crops unwatched, pests and diseases can take over and destroy them, turning your initial investment into waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii amli kwɛmɔ daa he miihia. Kɛji oshi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni otsuuu he nii Kooloi srɔtoi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai Amɛ nyɛ amɛye nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni amɛfite amɛ. Enɛ haa shika ni okɛwo mli shishijee lɛ yaa yaka.

english: Do my crops feed on soil nutrients and light all day and night, or only at specific times?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ la gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ, gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ, loo yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi pɛ amli?

english: Crops mainly produce and absorb food during daylight hours using sunlight. At night, their processes slow down as they rest and use that stored energy to build plant tissue.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛwoɔ niyenii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. gbɛkɛ Amɛ nifeemɔ lɛ baa shi be mli ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei amli fãji.

english: Why do my crops seem slow to respond when I give them cold water early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛ kpaaa nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ha amɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Early in the morning, soil temperatures are cool and the plant's pores are just beginning to open. Crops take up water slowly until the morning sun warms up the environment.
ga: Leebi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ miije shishi amɛmiigbele kɛkɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nu blɛoo. Kɛyashi leebi hulu lɛ ha shihilɛ lɛ mli dɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season around December and January?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ December kɛyashi January mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural survival behavior. Shedding leaves prevents the plant from losing water through evaporation during dry months, allowing it to preserve its energy until the rains return.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ subaŋ. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaje nu kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: If I give my crops extra food and fertilizer, will it guarantee double the yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ niyenii ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ Ani ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shii enyɔ?

english: No, crops can only absorb a limited amount of nutrients at a given time. Extra fertilizer beyond what the plant can eat will simply sit unused in the soil or harm the roots.
ga: Dabi, tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe bɔ ni tsei baanyɛ aye lɛ baaha akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akatsu nii loo ebaaye shishifãi lɛ awui.

english: Why shouldn't I spray liquid fertilizer on my crop leaves late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ?

english: Leaf pores close up as daylight fades and temperatures drop, meaning the plant won't absorb the fertilizer. Leaving wet chemicals on leaves overnight can also invite fungal diseases.
ga: Baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe beni hulu la lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Tsofai ni mli efɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why does fertilizer fail to work when my soil is very cold and waterlogged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii beni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: In cold, waterlogged soil, roots cannot breathe properly and slow down their activity. They leave the nutrient 'food' untouched in the cold mud, which can lead to root rot.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ ni enɛ haa amɛnitsumɔ lɛ baa shi. Amɛshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ‘niyenii’ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he yɛ muji ni mli ejɔ ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in midday heat is a self-defense mechanism. The plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the strong sun to prevent losing precious water.
ga: Abuɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ akɛ eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ni jara wa lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my young pepper plants looking yellow even though I gave them good plant food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ tsei niyenii kpakpa moŋ?

english: If weeds are growing around your pepper plants, they are stealing the nutrients and water from the soil. The weeds consume the food intended for your crops, leaving them undernourished.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, no lɛ amɛmiiju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi yeɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: My elders taught me to leave all shade trees standing on my farm, but modern advice says to trim them. Why should I change how we used to do it?
ga: Mi onukpai lɛ tsɔɔ mi akɛ mashi tsei fɛɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaawoo kɛɛ akɛ, afolɔ nakai tsei lɛ. Mɛni he je nɛ e sa nɛ ma tsake bɔ nɛ wa peeɔ níhi ha a?

english: Trimming extra shade trees allows just enough sunlight to reach your cocoa, helping the pods grow bigger and ripen faster, while still keeping enough shade to protect the soil from drying out.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɔ kookoo lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa pods lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi.

english: Are modern cocoa farming methods really better at helping trees produce fruit earlier than traditional ways?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ kookoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya fe blema gbɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, modern practices like strategic pruning, weed control, and timely fertilization give cocoa trees direct access to more nutrients, allowing them to flower and yield ripe pods earlier in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ. jwɛi nɔyeli Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛŋmɔji lɛ shwereɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: What farm practices can I do so that my cocoa trees mature and yield fruit earlier in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ okwaayeli mafee koni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Removing dead branches, clearing weeds under the canopy, and applying fertilizer right before the rainy season gives the cocoa trees the energy they need to produce pods sooner.
ga: Niji ni egboi ni ajieɔ Ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ shishi lɛ amli Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: How can I easily tell when a cocoa pod on my tree is fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods change color when ripe. Green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange. Picking them at full color change ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ oootsi ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛ fɛɛ amɛtsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop if I delay harvesting my ripe cocoa pods and leave them on the tree?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ be ni mikɛkpaa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni mishi amɛ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to sprout or rot, and attracts pests like rodents, which ruins the quality of your harvest and lowers your income.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. ni egbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, ni baanyɛ afite nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni eha shika ni onáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds under my cocoa trees before the harvesting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ dani nikpamɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and food from the soil that your cocoa trees need. Clearing them ensures the tree gets full nutrition to develop healthy, heavy pods before harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ sũ ni o-cacao tsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ená ŋmeii ni wa ni tsii dani akpa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by lack of nutrients, water shortages, or pest attacks. Proper pruning, regular weed control, and pest management help keep flowers attached until pods form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. nu ni faaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Akpamɔ ni sa Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii baa.

english: How often should I prune my cocoa trees, and what happens if I don't do it?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ? Ni mɛni baaba kɛji okɛkpaaa lɛ?

english: Pruning should be done at least once or twice a year to remove unnecessary branches. Unpruned trees become too bushy, blocking sunlight and trapping moisture, which leads to fewer pods and more disease.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ afo tsei lɛ shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli koni ajie tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara fe nine. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa pods fioo pɛ baa kɛ helai babaoo.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in heavy moisture and dark shade. Pruning branches to let air and light flow through the farm helps prevent the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ duŋ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield a huge harvest one year, but very few pods the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Producing a large crop exhausts the tree's energy and nutrients. Without feeding the tree with fertilizer and proper care after a big harvest, it takes time to recover before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa haaa tso lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Eheɔ be dani ehiɛɔ shi dani ekɛ yibii ni tsii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing usually shows that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key food it needs to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like beans can restore the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo adu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: During the dry Harmattan season, young cocoa plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the dry ground. The tree sheds its leaves to protect itself from completely drying out and dying.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun heat or lack of water in the soil. When it gets too hot, the plant discards its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa mli loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves but leaves small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing top leaves instead of expanding its roots into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ ewo yitsei ni mli tse mli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I give them tall sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa amɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Staking holds the vines up so every leaf catches sunlight instead of rotting or staying shaded on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite loo amɛaahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to prune the small extra shoots around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni bɔle mi-plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing them allows all the nutrients to go into making one large, healthy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tsoi bibii krokomɛi loo tsei bibii juɔ nu, tso niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ehe koni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and quickly steal fertilizer, root space, and sunlight from your plants, leaving your crop starved even if water is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables get burnt or scorched after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ahe lɛ ashãa loo shãa lɛ?

english: Leaf burning happens when liquid chemicals are mixed too strong, sprayed under intense afternoon heat, or applied incorrectly. Spraying in the cool early morning gives the plant time to absorb treatment safely.
ga: Baai shãa baa kɛji akɛ tsofai ni ji nu futu mli waa tsɔ. Okɛ la ni mli wa afɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli. loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi maŋkpa ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa be koni amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my stored maize grains develop tiny insects and holes after a few months in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii kɛ buji lɛ? Eba mli beni awo baagi lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ?

english: Weevils often lay microscopic eggs inside the grain while it is still standing in the field. If the harvested grain is not dried completely until it is hard before storage, those eggs hatch inside the warm bags and eat the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛwui bibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛdamɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ egbiko kwraa ni ewaaa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: My cocoa farm land seems weak and poor, so why are my cocoa trees not growing well?
ga: Mi kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need rich nutrients from the soil to grow strong and produce healthy pods. When soil becomes exhausted over time, trees become starved of essential food, leading to stunted growth, pale leaves, and poor harvests.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ hu ehiii.

english: Can I use chicken manure from local poultry farms to improve my cocoa soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi alɛɛhe lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛha mi-kokoo shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, poultry manure is very rich in nitrogen and organic matter that revives tired soil. Applying well-composted chicken waste supplies missing nutrients to the cocoa trees, helping them grow stronger and yield more pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ fa babaoo yɛ kooloi aŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina loo ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha cacao tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for fresh poultry manure to dry or rot before spreading it near my cocoa roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni kooloi afɔfɔi heei lɛ agbi loo amɛgboi dani mikɛshwie mi-kokoo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fresh poultry waste releases high heat and strong ammonia as it breaks down, which can burn tender cocoa roots. Allowing it to compost safely transforms the raw manure into gentle, nutrient-rich plant food.
ga: Kooloi ahe jwɛi heei jieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ammonia ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tso niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ adu kookoo dɔŋŋ?

english: Signs of poor soil include slow tree growth, leaves turning yellowish even when it rains, small pod sizes, and trees easily dropping their flowers before pods can form.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ he ji: Tsei lɛ daa blɛoo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po. Pods lɛ ji bibii. Ni tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up under heavy sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to shelter them from scorching sun while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ niyenii anɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa trees too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting trees too close makes them compete with each other for water and nutrients in the soil. Overcrowding also blocks sunlight and airflow, which reduces pod growth and encourages plant diseases.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa pod lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ tsei ahelai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa branches need to be pruned when the trees get too bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ amli be mli ni tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive or extra branches so the tree directs its energy into producing pods rather than excess leaves. It also lets in light and fresh air to keep the crop healthy.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni wooo yibii loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers fall off when trees suffer from stress caused by weak soil, lack of water, or lack of pollinating insects. Restoring soil fertility helps the tree retain its flowers until pods develop.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ naa haomɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akuɔ sɛɛ akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔji lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and excess moisture create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread. High humidity combined with thick canopy shade keeps the pods damp and speeds up decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli edɔ fataa he lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do cocoa trees in one part of my farm yield big pods while trees in another part produce tiny pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ he kroko lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Soil quality often varies across a farm. Areas with richer soil and better moisture yield larger pods, while patches with poor, depleted soil cause cocoa trees to produce small, underdeveloped fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha pod lɛ agbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni efite lɛ baawo kookoo tsei bibii ni ekwɛko nɔ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my maize crops too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo loo fioo miiha mi-abele lɛ?

english: Curling leaves usually mean the maize is thirsty and needs water, while yellowing leaves and soggy soil mean the roots are drowning from overwatering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye ŋmãa ni nu he miihia lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli.

english: Watering in the early morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the heat of the day, whereas afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can scorch hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha etsɔ la oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very bushy with lots of leaves but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ tomato fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers; switching to fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium encourages fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally put nitrogen back into the soil, which restores the nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize take away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi aniyenii waa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting too closely causes peppers to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin plants that produce smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ aduawai bibii baa.

english: Why are my okra seeds taking so long to sprout after I buried them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too deep struggle to reach sunlight and air, which causes slow germination or causes the seed to rot underground before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are there strange holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. Akɛtee tso lɛ shishi?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars; early application of approved organic or chemical sprays, or putting neem extract in the plant whirls, helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ; Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra loo ni akɛ neem mli nu baafata tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my yam leaves developing dark brown spots and dying off early before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is usually yam anthracnose disease caused by excessive dampness and fungus; proper staking improves airflow around the leaves and reduces moisture buildup.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa. Staking ni sa baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ. baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa lɛ baa shi

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water and protect their roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Extreme heat, sudden drought, or lack of soil nutrients causes the plant stress, making it drop its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Ha egbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing cocoa trees with the shade and moist air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture plenty of sunlight to feed the tuber underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akafite tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small even though the stem and leaves above ground look very big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves on top instead of storing starch in the tubers below the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering stress tomato plants, causing them to shed their flowers to survive. Keeping the soil steadily moist and protecting plants from harsh winds helps them turn flowers into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛbai lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight balls and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, which distorts their shape as they grow.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly show up in the centers of my maize plants right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on fresh, soft leaves that sprout right after the early rain. When these eggs hatch into caterpillars like fall armyworms, they feed on the tender young leaves inside the center funnel.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii heei ni jeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nɛkɛ wɔji nɛɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ. Ebaaye baai bibii ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the dirt. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water until the heat drops in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stems turn brown and drop their lower leaves during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry, dusty harmattan season, plants reduce water loss by shedding older leaves to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ waa ni sũ hu yɔɔ mli. Tsei haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ baai momoi ni amɛfoɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava shows it is mature when its lower leaves naturally drop off, the plant stops growing tall, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem from tubers swelling underneath.
ga: Kasava tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, tso lɛ kpa shweremɔ, ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ panicles bibii waa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Plantains require a constant supply of water and nutrients to form big bunches. During dry seasons, lack of soil moisture slows down fruit development, resulting in smaller bunches unless irrigation or heavy mulching is used.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii he miihia plantains daa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ jwɛi wuji. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ shweremɔ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni shwereɔ fioo. Ja akɛ nu ni tsii loo mulching tsu nii.

english: Why do all plantain farms in my village seem to mature at the exact same time, causing market oversupply?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni plantain ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ miida yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayelihe lɛ nibii ni fa fe nine?

english: Plantains depend heavily on seasonal rainfall patterns. When farmers plant at the start of the major rainy season, the crops follow the same growth calendar and mature simultaneously, leading to a temporary glut in the market.
ga: Plantains damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ nɔ waa. Beni okwaafoi duɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa yɛ dalɛ kalanda kome nɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa fe nine yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds when heavy bunches are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing bunch. Using bamboo or wooden props to support fruit-bearing trunks prevents wind damage and protects your yield.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni eda lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei tsu nii kɛfi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite nii ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantains so they do not spoil before buyers arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mi-plantains lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ekafite dani mɔ ni heɔ lɛ aba?

english: Harvest plantains when the fingers are full and plump but still completely green. If you wait until they begin turning yellow on the tree, they ripen too quickly during transit and lose market value.
ga: Kpaa plantains be mli ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ shi amɛji eŋɔli lolo. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ, ni amɛjara wa waa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: What is the best way to store harvested plantains on my farm while waiting for buyers?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ toɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Keep harvested green plantains in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded shed away from direct sunlight. Avoid stacking them too high, as bruising accelerates ripening and damages fruit quality.
ga: Kɛ plantains eŋɔli ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Ha hulu la akashɛ ohe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ amɛhe ni oooto he tsɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ atswa lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ oya, ni ebaafite aduawai lɛ ahe fɛo.

english: Does the size and appearance of my plantain bunch affect the price buyers give me?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikuu lɛ da ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ saa jara ni hɔlɔ lɛ kɛhaa mi lɛ he?

english: Yes, buyers prefer large, clean, undamaged plantain fingers with full shapes. Good post-harvest handling and proper plant care lead to premium-grade bunches that command higher prices.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ nineshi niji agboi, ni he tse, ni efiteee ni yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ ni sa Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni biɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce so many suckers, and should I cut some of them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii babaoo nɛkɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo ekomɛi amli?

english: Plantains naturally produce multiple shoot suckers, but leaving too many forces them to compete for light, water, and nutrients. Pruning to leave only one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small sucker ensures large bunches.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, plantains woɔ ŋmeii babaoo. Shi shi ŋmeii babaoo ni miitswa akaŋ kɛha la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso titri kome pɛ, tso bibioo kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome koni efee kuu agbo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves can be caused by nutrient deficiency, natural aging, or leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka. Removing yellowed leaves keeps the farm clean and prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Ekolɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ loo baa mli helai tamɔ Sigatoka. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What kind of fertilizer or soil care works best to keep my plantains fruiting well every year?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yeɔ ebuaa mi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai daa afi?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that need high amounts of potassium and nitrogen. Applying well-rotted manure, compost, or balanced fertilizer around the base of the plant maintains healthy soil and continuous high yield.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen babaoo. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii kɛbɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Can I grow plantains alongside cocoa trees to get food while waiting for the cocoa to produce?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe koni maná niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa provides essential shade that protects young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while giving you edible food and extra income in the early years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo dumɔwui duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni ayeɔ kɛ shika kroko hu yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade, often provided by fast-growing plantain trees, to keep them cool and moist while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ plantain tso ni daa oya lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Elevating the leaves on stakes keeps them exposed to light while protecting them from soil-borne diseases and rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ náa la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Yellowing at the bottom of maize plants is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a key nutrient for green leaf growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to its newer, top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize make my maize grow stronger next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli waa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut harvest is over, those roots decay and leave natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeikpamɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why does leaving my land unplanted for a year or two make crops grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi kome loo afii enyɔ ni miduko nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving land to fallow gives the soil time to rest and naturally restore nutrients, moisture, and organic matter that previous crops depleted.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsei efite tsutsu lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny, invisible pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the plant's sap and spreading viruses, which prevents healthy leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɔ ni anaaa, tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. ni tsiɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I do not harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Over-mature cassava tubers absorb excessive water from the soil, causing their starch to break down and making them vulnerable to soil fungi and bacteria that rot the root.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ, ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nɔ waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when water is unstable, as heat stress prevents the flower from pollinating itself properly.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot without them killing each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni agbeee amɛhe?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly during that time. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava has plenty of space and time to fill out the farm.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmã daa blɛoo yɛ nakai be lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa lɛ, Cassava baaná he ko kɛ be babaoo ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: The first rain often creates a hot, humid soil environment followed by dry days, which heats up seeds and dries out their tender young roots before they can establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Gbii ni mli egbi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ gĩɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is 'dead' and cannot grow crops well anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ ‘egbo’ ni ewooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Dead or exhausted land usually looks pale, bakes hard under the sun, and causes crops to stay small, weak, and yellowish. Adding organic matter like animal manure helps bring life and nutrients back into the soil so crops can thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbo loo nɔ ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Charred yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wala kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant crops immediately on poor land, or do I need to fix the soil first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo ehe miihia ni mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is always better to fix and nourish poor soil before planting. Treating tired land with compost or manure revives the ground first, giving your seeds a healthy environment to grow strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni aha lɛ niyenii dani adu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ hei ni efite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ afee amɛ ekoŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ shihilɛ kpakpa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: What should I do if my crops always stay stunted on a specific part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ bei pii lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi?

english: Stunted growth usually means that specific area lacks nutrients or has damaged soil. Working organic soil improvers or poultry manure into that spot before planting will revive the soil and fix the growth issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko loo shikpɔŋ lɛ efite. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ wo he lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni esaa naagbai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What makes farm soil 'alive' and ready to feed my crops?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ‘hiɛ kã’ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Soil stays alive when it contains organic matter, such as decomposed chicken manure or crop waste. This organic matter feeds beneficial organisms in the ground and holds moisture, making plant food easily available to roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ wuɔ ŋmei ni egbo loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi yɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ehaa tsei aniyenii shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe mlɛo

english: Is chicken dung good for my crops, and how does it help them grow?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa?

english: Chicken manure is a very rich organic fertilizer. It restores weak soil by adding essential nutrients like nitrogen, which helps crops grow dark green leaves and produce better yields.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni ekɛfataa he lɛ nɔ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How will my crops react if I put chicken manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee amɛnii amɛha tɛŋŋ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu?

english: Crops planted in soil treated with chicken manure generally sprout faster, build stronger stems, and stay green longer because the soil retains moisture and food much better.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ wuɔ ŋmei ewo mli lɛ fɔɔ kwɛ̃mɔ oya. Bɔɔ tso ni mli wa ni ohi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I apply organic manure to my field before planting seeds or after they sprout?
ga: Ani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔji amli dani miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ loo beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply organic manure to the land before planting. This allows the manure to mix into the soil and revive it, ensuring nutrients are ready as soon as the seeds sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ futuɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: How does poultry waste help soil that gets dry and hard easily?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashwiemɔ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbiɔ ni ewaa oya?

english: Poultry manure adds organic material that breaks up hard soil structure. It acts like a sponge, helping the ground hold onto water longer so crop roots do not dry out quickly.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ fataa he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ egbiɛɛ oya.

english: Should I try a new organic fertilizer on my whole farm at once or start on a small patch?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ makwɛ shikome loo mabɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii?

english: You should always test a small amount of any new input on a small section of your land first. Once you see that it works well and yields good results, you can safely apply it to the rest of your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ oka saji heei fioo komɛi okwɛ yɛ he ko bibioo. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ Kɛ́ ona akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai. Obaanyɛ okɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it risky to buy a large amount of new soil treatment without testing it first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ ooohe shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakemɔi heei babaoo ni okaaa amɛ okwɛɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Testing a small quantity first protects your money and farm. It allows you to observe how your specific crops respond without taking a big risk on your whole season's harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oka shika fioo ko okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oshika kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he. Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa ni okɛ onibii ni akpaa lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy green growth, or that excess water around the roots is preventing nutrient uptake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔle Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava shed its leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water and protect itself from drought, and it will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains growing beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná tso kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that scorch easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide vital shade and humidity to help them survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Curled or wrinkled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the sap, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ latex lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Removing extra suckers stops the offspring from competing for water and food, allowing the main plantain stem to direct all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa seshibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eda ni etsɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight to produce energy, which directly feeds and enlarges the tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aye nii tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the roots and leaves to compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants with poor yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally enriching the soil with food for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and soil moisture, leaving the crop plants weak and incapable of producing full yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ Ehaa tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or leave the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing long and thin instead of fat and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ fɔmɔ nii kɛ agbo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand easily. If your soil is hard or compacted, the tubers struggle to swell. Also, using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow lots of leaves while leaving the tuber under developed.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ewa akɛ yitso lɛ baafu. Kɛfata he lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ náa baai babaoo yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shweremɔ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plants don't get water consistently, or when tiny pests like thrips attack the blossom stems, causing the plant to shed them before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei, ni no haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning light green with tiny white insects under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with tiny insects underneath mean your field has whiteflies, which spread the cassava mosaic virus. These pests suck nutrients from the leaves and stop the cassava plant from making food.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ. ni gbɛɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛhaa ŋmei tso lɛ feɔ niyenii.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by tiny black beetles after a few weeks in the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii ebɔle mi-abele nikpamɔ lɛ he lɛ? Ani oyeɔ lɛ beni okɛ otsii fioo komɛi ehi shwapo lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Those tiny beetles are maize weevils. They often lay eggs inside the grain while it is still drying in the field. If the maize is not dried completely before storage, the eggs hatch and the insects multiply quickly.
ga: Nakai ladybugs bibii lɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa mli be mli ni egbi lolo yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni kooloi bibii lɛ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun and dry winds. Leaving taller trees like plantains or forest trees gives them necessary shade and keeps the air moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do seeds I save from my last hybrid maize harvest yield much less than the seeds I bought from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one season of high performance. The grain saved from that harvest loses those special traits, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and much lower yields if planted again.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sunshine causes pepper leaves to lose water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. As long as the plants bounce back and look fresh by evening, this afternoon wilting is a normal defense against extreme heat.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni he ejɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ. Gbɛ ni ŋmɛnɛ shwane nɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hu ji gbɛ ni afɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is my maize crop producing cobs with missing kernels and empty spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bɛ mli kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty spaces on maize cobs happen when dry winds or drought hit during the flowering period. If the silks dry up before catching pollen from the tassels, those specific grains will not form.
ga: He ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo hɔmɔ ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ siliki lɛ gĩ dani ajie pollen lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, Nakai dumɔwui pɔtɛɛi lɛ efeŋ.

english: How can I tell if the agrochemicals or fertilizers I am buying at the market are genuine and good quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ agrochemicals loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Always look for an official approval label and registration number from regulators like the FDA or EPA on the container. Genuine products have sealed tops, clear manufacture dates, and should only be bought from accredited input dealers.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ wolo ni tsɔɔ akɛ akpɛlɛɔ nɔ kɛ nɔmba ni aŋmalaa awoɔ wolo nɔ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhe ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ FDA loo EPA lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Akɛ nibii ni ji anɔkwale lɛ ewo nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ gbi ni afee lɛ ni esa akɛ ahe kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɛ adɛŋ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so adding manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does dried chicken manure help my crop farm compared to chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te tsina ŋmei ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ he?

english: Chicken manure feeds the crop slowly while also softening the soil so it can hold rainwater longer. Chemical fertilizers feed the plant very fast, but they do not improve the soil structure like animal manure does.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã haa tsei lɛ niyenii fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya waa. Shi ehaaa sũ lɛ mli nibii lɛ aya hiɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. Spraying the leaves early with neem seed water or recommended insect medicine can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem dumɔwui nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naa

english: Why do my tomatoes develop black rotten spots on the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or water while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil constantly moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cassava sticks after clearing the land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time to plant cassava is right after the first steady rains begin when the ground is soft and wet. This allows the cassava stem to sprout roots quickly before any dry spell comes.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa.

english: Watering in the cool morning is best because the plant gets to drink before the sun rises high. If you water in the hot afternoon, much of the water turns to steam and evaporates before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baanu nu dani hulu lɛ ateshi. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Nu lɛ fa ko tsɔɔ lasu ni etsɔɔ lasu dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally stronger at pulling food and water from the soil than domestic crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light and food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛjieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe shia tsei. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoots to plant in a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which are shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. These grow into stronger plantain trees with larger bunches than shoots that already have broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli tseee, tamɔ akpɔlɔi, ni amɛshishi lɛ mli kwɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ plantains ni wa ni fɔfɔii lɛ dara fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when I store them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they were bruised during harvest or if the storage barn is hot and lacks fresh air. Storing uninjured yams off the ground on raised wooden racks in a cool, shady barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni pilaaa lɛ to shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from the high-yielding maize I bought and harvested to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ato kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni miheɔ ni mikpaa lɛ mli koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted hybrid maize seeds from a shop, saving those seeds will result in a much smaller harvest next season. It is best to buy fresh certified seeds every season for maximum yield.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni oookɛto lɛ baaha ŋmãa bibioo kwraa aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi koni oná yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know which cassava stems are strong enough to cut and plant for my next farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Look for healthy, mature stems from plants that are 10 to 18 months old. Choosing thick stems without pest damage or spots gives your crop the stored energy it needs to sprout quickly and produce heavy tubers.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 18 lɛ amli tsei ni eda ni amɛhe wa. Halamɔ tsei ni mli tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli. Ebaaha onibii lɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo bulbs ni tsii.

english: Does the weight or size of the seed yam I plant affect how big the new yams will grow?
ga: Ani ŋmeii dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ amli tsiimɔ loo amɛdalɛ saa ŋmeii heei ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, larger seed yam pieces (weighing around 200 to 300 grams) contain more stored food reserves for the sprouting shoot, helping the vine grow strong early on and yield bigger tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii wuji (ni tsiimɔ aaafee gram 200 kɛyashi 300) yɛ niyenii babaoo ni ato aha ŋmeii ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Ye obua wain tso lɛ ni ehiɛ wa mra. ni oha yitso ni da fe no

english: Why should I pick suckers from the base of my pineapple plant rather than planting the top leafy crown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala ŋmeii ni jɛ pineapple tso shishi lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Base suckers are more developed and mature than top crowns. Planting suckers allows the pineapple crop to flower and fruit much faster (in about 12 to 14 months) compared to crowns, which take up to two years.
ga: Base sucker lɛ etsɔ hiɛ ni eda fe ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Shikpɔŋhosomɔi ni aduɔ lɛ haa pineapple lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii oya (yɛ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 14 mli) kɛ akɛto akɔɔblei ni aduɔ lɛ he, ni baanyɛ ahé afii enyɔ.

english: How can I tell that my pepper seedlings in the nursery are mature enough to move to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Pepper seedlings are ready for transplanting when they are about 4 to 6 weeks old, roughly finger-length high, and have developed 4 to 6 strong, healthy true leaves.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ ekoŋŋ beni amɛye aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6, ni ji aaafee tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ. ni eyɛ baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni wa, ni ji anɔkwale.

english: How long does a hybrid cocoa tree take before it is mature enough to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ daa ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees mature quickly and usually begin flowering and bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, marked by branching out and forming flower cushions on the main trunk.
ga: Cacao tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ daa oya ni bei pii lɛ amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ, ni amɛwoɔ niji amli ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔii akutsei yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the right plantain sucker from an old mat to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker kɛjɛ mat momo mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have a broad bulb at the base and narrow, spear-like leaves. These mature faster and produce heavier bunches than 'water suckers' which have broad leaves and weak stems.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni hiɛ yitso ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ panicles ni tsii fe ‘nu mli ŋmeii’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks moisture, which stress the plant and disrupt its natural transition into the fruiting stage.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ kɛmiiya yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep growing leaves and vines without producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen or excessive water, they stay in a continuous vegetative state, spending energy on foliage rather than shifting into flowering and pod production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baaya nɔ ehiɛ dalɛ shihilɛ mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeetsake lɛ ewo fɔfɔii amli ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the smallest maize grains left over after selling my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui bibii fe fɛɛ ni eshwɛ beni mihɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Small or weak grains lack sufficient stored energy reserves. Planting large, heavy, high-quality seed grains ensures strong germination, fast early growth, and higher yields.
ga: Nibii bibii loo ni bɛ hewalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui wuji, ni tsii, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa. shweremɔ oya kɛ nibii ni anáa babaoo

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce empty fruit bunches while others have thick palm nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni mli tse.
