english: Young or poorly pollinated oil palms fail to set kernels properly. Trees need sufficient maturity, good nutrition, and pollinating insects to consistently form full, high-oil nuts.
ga: Mu tsei bibii loo ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ. Tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa. niyenii kpakpa kɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are small and leaves are fragile. They need shade crops like plantain planted beside them to shield them from high heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛbaai lɛ hu waaa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni sũ lɛ akadɔ fe nine ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start producing many flowers right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees store energy during the dry season, and the sudden moisture from the first rain signals to the tree that conditions are right to reproduce, causing a fast burst of flowering.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ni hulutsoo ni jɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli baa trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ leɔ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ sa kɛha fɔmɔ. Ekɛ fɔfɔi baa oya

english: Why should I cut off the small extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Mɛni eshwɛ yɛ mi koko tso lɛ he?

english: Removing extra branches stops the tree from wasting energy on leaves that do not produce fruit, allowing it to direct all its food toward growing bigger and healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and pale green even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛhe tseee yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Maize plants turn pale green and stay small when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need for green leaves and fast growth. Adding manure or the right fertilizer gives them the strength to grow tall.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni biɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdara.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if my crop plants are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo moŋ.

english: Even if your crops are taller, weeds underground steal water and plant nutrients directly from the soil, leaving your crops hungry and reducing your final harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ po Shi shikpɔŋ shishi jwɛi lɛ hu juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni oha onaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du tsina ŋmã lɛ, ehaa mi-ŋmã lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, effectively feeding natural fertilizer directly to the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I harvest more cassava roots?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani makpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your total harvest because the plants fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow large tubers instead of many thin, useless roots.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Akɛni tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni he ehiaaa yɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when watering is uneven. Keeping moisture steady in the soil and providing shade helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo awo lɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids that suck the juice out of young leaves and spread plant sicknesses, which stunts the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ kpaa.

english: Excess rain and darkness create high moisture, which allows a fungus called Black Pod disease to spread quickly; pruning shade trees to let sunlight and wind reach the trees helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ duŋ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their green color and boosts yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, prevents rainwater from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When cassava gets too much leaf-building nutrient (nitrogen) or is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing top leaves instead of storing food in the roots to make big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii ni haa baai feɔ baa lɛ nɔ babaoo tsɔ (nitrogen) loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms so they can develop into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, leaving plenty of space and light for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ eda sɛɛ mli.

english: It is safest to wait until the ground receives two or three steady, deep rains that soak thoroughly into the soil, rather than planting right after the very first light shower which can leave seeds stranded in dry dirt.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se, nɛ lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ dumɔwu ɔmɛ maa hi zu nɛ egbi ɔ mi.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the center whorl of the plant. Applying recommended biological or chemical controls directly into the leaf whorl helps manage them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa yɛ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛkudɔɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akwɛ enɛɛmɛi anɔ.

english: Weeds act like competing neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops hungry, stunted, and less able to fight off diseases.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi helai.

english: Why are the stems and leaves on my cassava plants twisting and curling up instead of growing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stem twisting usually happen when tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies feed on the plant or spread a virus. It can also occur when the crop suffers from severe heat or drought stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifã kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ yeɔ tsei loo amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haomɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks bend over and fall so easily before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks bend or fall over (a condition called lodging) when the crop has weak roots, lacks proper soil nutrients like potassium, or is exposed to strong winds without enough soil ridging to support the stem base.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ ebɔle loo amɛmiigbee shi. (shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy) beni tso lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing with strange, bent shapes instead of smooth and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ bangs kɛ sɛɛtsɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yam tubers twist and deform when the soil is too hard, stony, or clay-heavy. Loose, well-tilled mounds or ridges give the tubers space to grow smooth and long without resistance.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo. Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa bulbs ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa lɛ naa hei kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves fold inward and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during peak afternoon sun to prevent water loss and protect themselves from burning heat. If they recover by evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from drought stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ koni nu akafite ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji amɛhe wa amɛ gbɛkɛ Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ hɔmɔ ni baa lɛ he haomɔ lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow during the rainy season when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off air, making it impossible for roots to absorb nutrients. This root stress turns leaves yellow even when water is abundant.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ahe haomɔ nɛɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ po.

english: Why are my crops growing so slowly and remaining stunted even though I planted them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth happens when soil lacks necessary nutrients like nitrogen, or when hard soil prevents roots from spreading outward to find food and moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ koni amɛyana niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it fine for me to transfer my young pepper seedlings from the nursery to the field in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛya ŋmɔ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Moving seedlings during intense heat causes severe shock because they lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Transplanting is safest early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ ni naa wa baa ejaakɛ amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ aaawo tso lɛ mli yɛ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt completely after I move them to a new bed even when I water them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa beni mikɛ amɛ tee saatso hee nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused when fine root hairs are damaged during the move. Minimizing root disturbance and shading young plants for a few days helps them recover smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ amli haomɔ ni aba shi kɛ tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe shade mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ baaye abua ni amɛná hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a disease starting on just one crop spread so fast to neighboring plants across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela ko ni tso kome kɛbaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant diseases spread rapidly through wind, splashing rain, contaminated farm tools, or insects moving from one plant to another. Removing sick plants early helps stop the spread.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good enough to support crops before I invest money to clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu nii yɛ nɔ? Dani oookɛ shika awo mli koni okɛjie mli

english: Good agricultural land usually has dark, rich topsoil that drains water easily after rain and holds deep vegetation without signs of extreme erosion or hardened rock layers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛ okwaayeli tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. ni ehiɛɔ tsei ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli ni nɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tɛsaa lɛ mli ewo wu waa loo ewa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for light, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have ragged holes and dark dirt in the centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm infestation. The caterpillars feed deep inside the central leaf whorl of the maize plant, which damages the leaves and can reduce your harvest if not treated early.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela ko eba. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmaa lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why does my rice field need standing water during the growing stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Water helps keep the soil consistently wet for the rice roots while naturally choking out weeds that would otherwise steal light and nutrients from your crop.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and small cracks appear in the soil right around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo miikwɛ̃ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when exposed to direct heat, high humidity, or if they were bruised during harvest. Storing them on raised wooden racks in a cool, well-ventilated area prevents rot and delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli, loo kɛji akɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso ni awo nɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off when plants experience extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of bees to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Aloo ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves and transmitting plant viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni egbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ baai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops turning pale yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the new top leaves, leaving the older lower leaves without enough nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during hot afternoons even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, leaves lose moisture faster through evaporation than the roots can suck up from the ground. Adding dry grass or straw as mulch around the plants keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating too fast.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi baafata he akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I prepare and nourish my soil well before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mawo lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When soil is well-prepared and rich in nutrients, crops do not struggle to find food. Healthy soil allows plant roots to easily absorb nourishment in one place, helping the plant grow bigger, stronger, and produce higher yields.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ asaa jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛna niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ he kome. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa, amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How does applying fertilizer close to the root zone help my plant grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitso lɛ ni eda?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base of the crop allows the roots to absorb essential nutrients directly without spreading out far or competing with weeds, leading to faster and bigger crop growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãaa shɔŋŋ loo amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ yeee akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa oya ni amɛdaraa.

english: Should I apply disease prevention treatments to my crops even if I do not see any pests on my farm yet?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ minako tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo moŋ?

english: Yes, preventive crop protection acts like a vaccine. Treating seeds or young plants early prevents invisible disease spores and pests from attacking your crops before they can cause damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ hela naa. Dumɔwui loo tsei bibii ahe nitsumɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa lɛ akatutua onibii dani amɛfite nii.

english: Why do some improved crop varieties survive diseases better than the traditional seeds I use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtsuɔ nii ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred with natural resistance to common diseases, giving them a strong internal defense system that keeps them healthy even when disease is present in the area.
ga: Afɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni adebɔɔ mli nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa mligbɛ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛji hela ba jɛmɛ po.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds away from my crops even when the plants are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji tsei lɛ dara momo po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients and water meant for your crops, and they also harbor dangerous insects and plant diseases that can easily spread to your main harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛhiɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli oya lɛ hu.

english: Why should I find out where my planting seeds or cassava suckers came from before buying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mana he ni mi-cassava dumɔwui loo mi-suckers lɛ jɛɔ dani mahe lɛ?

english: Knowing the source and history of your planting materials ensures you are not unknowingly introducing seed-borne diseases or weak plant strains from another farm onto your land.
ga: Kɛ́ ole he ni odumɔ nii lɛ jɛ kɛ yinɔsane lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa loo tsei srɔtoi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli ni baanyɛ atswa mɔ lɛ baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni oleee nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest sometimes produce smaller yields than certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over multiple generations gradually lose their vigor and may carry hidden diseases from previous seasons, whereas certified seeds are carefully bred for high quality and uniform growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Amɛhewalɛ baa shi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara daa lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a plant's natural defense behavior to conserve moisture during dry periods. By shedding leaves, the crop reduces water loss and survives until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli su ni tsei buɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ, ebaaha nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops wilt and die when rain water sits on my field for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate, rot, and lead to the plant dying.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha he ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ mumɔ, egboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight. The plants stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the light, making their stems thin and weak instead of thick and sturdy.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ waa. Tso lɛ baajie ehe kpo oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is hungry for nitrogen. The maize plant moves the limited food it has from its old, lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ niyenii fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very bushy with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When soil has too much animal manure or excess nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ebaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and fall off when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mifo tso agbo ko yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Tall trees act as natural umbrellas to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ amɛhe.

english: Pepper plants roll up their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water in the heat. It is their way of sweating less until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji ni ajie latsaa fioo kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant corn on the exact same spot on my farm three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting corn on the same land every year drains all the specific nutrients corn loves and gives corn pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi sumɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ayi fa babaoo kɛya naanɔ.

english: Yam vines need sticks so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight. Sunlight acts as sunlight food, helping the plant build bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ niji koni amɛba lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ hulu la niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small ragged holes suddenly showing up inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe lɛ eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in the center leaves are a clear sign of caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the warm center leaf roll and chew the fresh growth.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which usually occurs when watering is irregular during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or when insects fail to visit and transfer pollen between the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ayasara ni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off dry leaves and extra shoots from my plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ plantain ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming dry leaves removes hiding spots for pests, while removing excess shoots ensures the main plantain stem gets all the food and water to bear large bunches.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa plantain tsei titri lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni baaye abua jwɛi agbo ko.

english: Why do my rice crops die when rain water sits flat on the land without moving for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni etsiii ehe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the air to breathe. When water sits on the field without draining or moving, it starves the roots of air, causing them to rot and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ta ŋmɔ ko nɔ ni nu hoɔ loo enyiɛɛɛ. Hɔmɔ baaye kɔɔyɔɔ mli shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to make my field land flat and level before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Leveling your land ensures that water spreads out evenly to all plants. On uneven land, water gathers in low spots and drowns some crops while leaving high spots dry and thirsty.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ jaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. yɛ he ko ni bɛ ŋwɛi Nu shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwieɔ nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kumai yeɔ amɛ.

english: How can I lead heavy rainwater away from my maize field so my crops do not get washed away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaho?

english: You can dig small, shallow drainage channels along the edge of your field to guide excess water away softly. Placing small grass barriers or stones slows the water down so it leaves without taking topsoil and crops with it.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ mli bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ koni okɛjie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ blɛoo. Jwɛi loo tɛi bibii ni akɛwoɔ mli Ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya.

english: How does controlling the water height in my farm field help my rice stalks grow tall and strong?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa?

english: Keeping water at a steady, controlled depth stops weeds from growing while giving rice stalks the support they need. Too much water drowns young shoots, but a controlled level nourishes the roots properly.
ga: Nu lɛ mlihilɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ emlibotemɔ nɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Nu babaoo baaha tsei bibii lɛ agbo. Shi bɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow during the heaviest period of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water in the soil washes away nutrients like nitrogen from the roots. Cassava roots also dislike waterlogged ground, which stresses the plant and stops it from making green leaves.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Cassava shishifãi sumɔɔɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow better when the soil is just moist instead of flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni nu aaawo mli lɛ?

english: Tomato roots are very sensitive to losing air. Moist soil gives the roots the exact balance of water to drink and air space to breathe, whereas flooded soil breeds fungal diseases and causes the plant to wilt.
ga: Tomato shishifãi lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ he waa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni anuɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛmuɔ lɛ teŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can quick floodwaters damage my young pepper seedlings even if the water drains away fast?
ga: Ani nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ akpata mi-pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahiɛ kɛji nu lɛ ho oya po?

english: Yes, even fast floodwaters can bend or snap fragile stems and coat the leaves in heavy mud. Mud on the leaves blocks sunlight, which stops the young plant from making food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu afua ni hoɔ oya po baanyɛ abɔle loo akumɔ tsei ni waaa lɛ ni ekɛ muji ni tsii aha baai lɛ ahe. Muji ni yɔɔ baai anɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii.

english: Why do sugarcane crops grow well near riverbanks where water moves constantly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ faai anaa he ni nu hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Sugarcane needs plenty of water, but moving water constantly brings fresh oxygen to the roots. Unlike standing water, flowing water keeps soil healthy and prevents root rot.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia shɛ̃. Shi nu ni hoɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hee baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa. Esoro nu ni hoɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he, ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my vegetable plants if dirty river water with leaves and trash enters my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa lɛ mli ni baai kɛ jwɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ bote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Debris and trash can block water flow, choke young stems, and harbor plant diseases. Filtering water through a simple mesh screen keeps the water clean so your crops receive clean moisture without infection.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Nu ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni eji tsei ahe helai ashia Nu lɛ ni akɛ tsɔne ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ he tseɔ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nu ni he tse ni hela ko bɛ mli.

english: How does muddy water settling on plant leaves slow down the growth of my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni mli ewo muji ni shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Leaves act like solar panels that catch sunlight to create food for the crop. When muddy water coats the leaves, it blocks the sun, forcing the plant to stop growing until rain washes the mud off.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, emɔɔ hulu la koni efee niyenii kɛha dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ha baai lɛ anɔ Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ muji lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense to save water. When the sun is too hot, the maize plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, preventing moisture from escaping.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli.

english: Why does my maize crop dry out so quickly in the field as soon as the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: When the rains stop, strong sunshine and dry winds like the Harmattan pull moisture out of both the soil and the plant leaves rapidly, causing the crop to stop growing and mature or dry out fast.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, hulu ni naa wa kɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ amli oya. Ehaa tsei kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛdaraa loo amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why is my maize producing flowers and tassels when the plants are still very short and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo ni eyɛ bibioo?

english: When crops experience heat or water stress early in their life, they feel threatened and try to reproduce quickly before dying. This causes them to flower early on short stalks.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra lɛ Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfɔ oya dani amɛgboi. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ tsei kukuji anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the crop is lacking water or nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nutrients it has from its older, lower leaves up to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does soil dry out faster around my maize plants than under dense patches of grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe jwɛi ni mli edɔ shishi.

english: Grass forms a thick mat that shades the ground like a blanket, keeping soil cool and moist. Young maize foliage is open, leaving exposed soil to dry out rapidly under direct sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji mama ni mli tse ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kuntu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Ashiɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi.

english: If I plant fodder grass for my animals, will it keep growing straight through the dry season without rain?
ga: Kɛji midu niyenii jwɛi kɛha mikooloi lɛ Ani ebaakwɛ̃ shi jaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Deep-rooted forage grasses can survive long dry spells by pulling water from deep underground, but their leaf growth will slow down significantly until the rains return or water is applied.
ga: Niyenii jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi baai lɛ adalɛ baafee mlɛo waa kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ loo abaaha amɛ nu ekoŋŋ.

english: If I cut green grass or maize stalks to feed my cows, will the plants sprout back from the roots?
ga: Kɛji mifo jwɛi eŋɔli loo ŋmãa tsei koni mikɛha tsinai lɛ Ani tso ko baakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Grasses have growing points near the ground level, so cutting them allows fresh leaves to regrow. However, maize plants have a single main growing tip and will not regrow once cut down completely.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ hei ni edaa yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni baai heei akwɛ̃. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmãa tsei yɛ dalɛ he titri kome pɛ. ni ekwɛŋ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ afo lɛ kwraa.

english: Can I harvest my green maize stalks before they dry out and store them together with grass to use later in the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dani amɛgbi ni mikɛto jwɛi he koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, chopping fresh green maize together with grass and packing it tightly away from air allows it to ferment into 'pillat' or silage. This keeps the feed juicy and nutritious for months into the dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ hee ni akɛ jwɛi feɔ ekome ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afee ‘pillat’ loo ŋmãa. Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ hewalɛ nyɔji babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if it is already too late in the rainy season to plant a new crop of maize?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ ni obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa hee?

english: Maize needs steady water for about 60 to 90 days to produce food. If the rainy season usually ends before your seed variety has enough time to mature, the crop will dry up before producing full ears.
ga: Abɛi biɔ aaafee gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 ni nu yɔɔ mli daa koni enyɛ ená niyenii. Kɛji akɛ bei pii lɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee dani odumɔwui lɛ ná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, Nibii ni adu lɛ baagbi dani ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaje kpo.

english: Why do some farmers plant leguminous crops like cowpeas together with maize in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas capture natural food (nitrogen) from the air and feed it into the soil to help the maize grow, while the strong maize stalks give the trailing cowpea plants a solid frame to climb on.
ga: Cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni wa haa tsina tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ náa ŋmãa ni wa ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ.

english: How can I know if my farm soil has enough moisture for planting maize just by squeezing it in my hand?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makɛ minine bibioo ko pɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Squeezing a handful of soil is a quick test. If the soil forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water, it is ready for planting; if it crumbles immediately, it is too dry, and if water drips out, it is too wet.
ga: Shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni aaamɔ lɛ ji kaa ni afeɔ oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ. Kɛji efo trukaa lɛ Egbi tsɔ. Ni kɛji nu ho kɛjɛ mli lɛ Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil when we receive heavy rains for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause waterlogging, which removes air from the soil. Without oxygen around the roots, rot-causing fungi and bacteria grow rapidly and cause the yams to decompose underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. ni jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop during intense afternoon sun to reduce leaf surface exposure. This helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from drying out until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Yucca baakpã ni ebaagbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli koni ekɛba shi ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some vegetable plants stay small while others right next to them grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yɛ bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ kɛlɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plants compete directly for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. If seeds are planted too close together, stronger plants absorb most of the resources, leaving neighboring weaker plants stunted.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaŋɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing proper pollination. When temperature stress is too high, the plant sheds its flowers to preserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be mli haomɔ lɛ fa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster on my farm than the pepper crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with aggressive root systems built to absorb nutrients and water rapidly. Farm crops like peppers require more time and care, making it easy for weeds to outgrow them if not cleared.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ama koni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya. Okwaafoi adumɔi tamɔ ŋmeii biɔ be babaoo kɛ saamɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji ajieee amɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by direct sunlight. They need partial shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to protect their leaves and keep the surrounding air humid.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is ripe enough to harvest without cutting down the whole plant early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mifolɔko tso muu lɛ fɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: As plantains mature, the sharp ridges on the sides of individual fruits become rounded and plump. When the fruits lose their flat sides and feel firm and full, the plantain bunch is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Beni plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afãi lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii. Beni aduawai lɛ sɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Plantain tsei lɛ akui lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize field so suddenly and eat up the leaves within a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ trukaa ni amɛye baai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs on leaf undersides at one time. When the caterpillars hatch all at once, they begin feeding aggressively on the crop leaves simultaneously, causing fast damage.
ga: Autumn caterpillar ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ shikome yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fee ekome lɛ Amɛbaabɔi tsei ahe baai yeli kɛ mlifu yɛ be kome mli. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya

english: Why do black spots spread so quickly from one cocoa pod to another during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black spot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that travels in water. Raindrops splash fungal spores from infected pods or soil onto healthy pods, spreading the disease rapidly throughout the farm during wet weather.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni nyiɛɔ nu mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and burn when exposed to too much direct sunlight and wind. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby shields young trees from harsh sun until they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo shɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow instead of remaining deep green while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, waterlogged soil, or a shortage of essential nutrients during the early flowering phase.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishijee bei amli

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and rot quickly during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain keeps the soil wet and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungal diseases, which attack tomato root systems and cause sudden wilting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ. Enɛ tutuaa tomato shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ trukaa.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining small and thin even after growing for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot swell if the soil is packed too tightly or lacks potassium, which is the main nutrient roots need to store starch and expand.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛkɛ ŋmeii ato ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my yam vines produce many thick leaves but yield very small tubers beneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai ni mli wa waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages the yam plant to spend its energy producing leafy top growth instead of directing nutrients down into building large underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: When seeds are planted too densely, the young plants stretch upward competing for sunlight, resulting in weak stems and poor harvests as their roots crowd each other for food.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ beni amɛshishifãi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa kɛhaa niyenii lɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds weeks before planting help my crops grow better than clearing on planting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ otsii babaoo dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing early gives the weeds time to decompose into organic matter that enriches the soil, while planting immediately after clearing leaves soil dry and nutrient-poor.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ náa be ni ekɛfiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie lɛ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling with yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread between plants by tiny insects called whiteflies when they feed on plant sap.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi ateŋ ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ beni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my maize crop is ready to harvest for fresh eating?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni aye ehee?

english: Maize is ready for fresh consumption when the silks turn dark brown and puncturing a grain releases a milky fluid; if the fluid is clear, it is too early, and if solid, it is ready for dry grain.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha niyenii hee beni siliki lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ jieɔ nu ni tamɔ mliki kpo lɛ. Kɛji nu lɛ mli tse lɛ, no lɛ eyaa oya tsɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ ewa lɛ, efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui ni egbi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. They need shade from companion plants like plantains or shade trees during their first few years to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso ni eshwɛ lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow healthy green leaves and big ears. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure fixes this shortage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ toi wuji lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni aye nɛkɛ shweremɔ nɛɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new shoots and roots to struggle and grow in the wrong direction, severely reducing your harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi heei lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves brown dirt inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that eats the growing tip of maize plants. Spraying recommended control products or applying neem extract early when damage starts helps protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ yitsei lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo ni akɛ neem mli nu tsuɔ nii mra. Kɛ́ efite lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot and drop their flowers when water collects around them after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu shwie shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have sensitive roots that drown and rot easily in waterlogged soil, which stops flower development and damages the plant. Planting peppers on raised soil beds or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Pepper tsei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ nu mli oya ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daamɔ kpaa ni efiteɔ tso lɛ. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in direct sunlight to feed the tubers growing underground. Raising the vines on poles keeps the foliage off damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why is my harvest getting smaller every season when I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow slow and weak if I wait until the weeds are tall before removing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji mimɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ shwere dani mijie amɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with young crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early—within the first three to four weeks after planting—ensures your crops get all the food they need during their critical growing phase.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tightly into small rolls during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe bibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to reduce water loss during hot, dry weather, or as a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. Watering properly and controlling whiteflies keeps the foliage open and healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ shi. aloo nɔ ni jɛɔ bɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ mli baa. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua ni baai lɛ agbele ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers lay dry grass or palm fronds on top of the soil around their vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei baai fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Placing dry grass or palm fronds on the soil is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that stops soil water from evaporating in the sun, keeps the root zone cool, and blocks weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is clay or loamy soil, and which one is better for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji shikpɔŋ loo sũ? Ni mɛɛ shikpɔŋ hi kɛha tsei akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Clay soil feels sticky when wet, hardens like brick when dry, and holds a lot of water. Loamy soil feels dark, soft, and crumbly in your hand. Loamy soil is generally better for most crops because it holds nutrients well while letting roots breathe and drain water easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ baanyɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji edɔ. Ewaa tamɔ brikii kɛ́ egbi. ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu babaoo Loam nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ enine mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ejaakɛ ehiɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhoɔ nu oya.

english: What are the clear signs I can look for to know if my land is in good condition for planting food crops?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni manyɛ matao koni mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli kɛha niyenii ŋmɔ?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hands, contains earthworms, and grows dark green weeds naturally. If your soil stays light-colored, crumbles into fine dust, or cracks heavily in the dry season, it needs organic material to restore its health.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ su ni tsuɔ, ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ sũ bibioo loo egbɛɔ eshwaa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli koni ekɛha ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: My farm land has heavy clay soil that stays soaked with water; how can I help my crops grow without rotting?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee?

english: You can improve heavy clay soil by mixing in organic compost, dried manure, or decaying leaves. Building raised soil mounds or digging small drainage channels also helps move excess water away so crop roots do not drown.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi, loo baai ni egbo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ maa loo nu homɔ gbɛ bibioo ko ni atsaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Koni tso shishifãi akabote nu mli

english: Can I successfully plant cassava in an urban area like Accra, or does it only yield well in rural areas?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ maŋtiase ko tamɔ Accra mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli? Aloo ebaawo yibii kpakpai yɛ akrowai amli pɛ?

english: Cassava can grow very well in urban areas like Accra provided the soil is loose, well-drained, and receives adequate sunlight. It is a resilient crop that adapts well to various soil types across different locations.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ maji wuji amli tamɔ Accra kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni oná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Eji tso ko ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ hei srɔtoi

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 8 to 12 months after planting. You can check readiness when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, or by carefully digging around one stem to inspect the thickness of the tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo baahi shi aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fã kome ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ mli wa ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava start rotting so quickly after I dig it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots deteriorate quickly after harvest because they lose moisture rapidly and suffer internal chemical changes once severed from the main stem, usually spoiling within 2 to 3 days if untreated.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Enɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ oya kɛ tsofai ni tsakeɔ yɛ mli lɛ amli kɛ́ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, egboɔ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How should I clean and arrange my harvested cassava so buyers in the market will pay a good price?
ga: Te esa akɛ atsu ŋmei ni akpa lɛ he nii aha tɛŋŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo bɔni afee ni aná jara kpakpa aha mɛi ni heɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: To make cassava attractive to buyers, brush off excess soil without peeling the skin, leave a small stub of the stalk attached to slow down spoiling, and sort the tubers neatly by size.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ afee nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ Okɛ sũ ni fa fe nine lɛ afɔ shi ni okɛ ŋmei lɛ akajie. Shĩ tso bibioo lɛ oshwie. Kɛto koni ekɛha fitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo. ni oto yitsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ ji lɛ naa

english: What kind of assistance can I get from government agriculture officers for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ maná kɛjɛ mimaŋ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Government extension officers offer free guidance on best planting practices, advice on controlling pests and crop diseases, access to subsidized farm inputs, and training on crop processing.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ haa ŋaawoo ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ ahe. Ŋaawoi kɛha tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai akudɔmɔ Hegbɛ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ mli

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with plenty of leaves but producing very thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or planting stems too close together causes cassava to spend its energy growing tall foliage instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine yɛ sũ loo tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Will my cassava crop survive if rain does not fall for a few weeks during the growing period?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tso lɛ baahi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Cassava is naturally drought-tolerant. During dry spells, the plant drops its leaves to conserve water and goes dormant, then sprouts fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, baai heei jeɔ kpo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Which part of the cassava plant do I cut to plant for my next crop, and how should I plant it?
ga: Mɛɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo koni mikɛdu yɛ mi-tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli? Ni te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ madu lɛ?

english: Use healthy, mature woody stems cut into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long. Plant them horizontally or slanting into the soil with the growth buds pointing upward.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni eda ni mli wa atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30. Dumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi.

english: What can I do with my harvested cassava if I cannot sell it all fresh on market day?
ga: Mɛni mikɛ mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ ehee yɛ jarayeli gbi lɛ nɔ hu?

english: If you cannot sell cassava fresh, you can process it into longer-lasting products like gari, dried cassava chips (konkonte), or high-quality cassava flour to preserve its value.
ga: Kɛji onyɛɛɛ ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmei hee Obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii ni ofee nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ gari, ŋmei woji ni egbi (konkonte) loo ŋmei ashikiŋsha ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni ehiɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Is cassava a good crop for both feeding my family and earning extra income?
ga: Ani ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nii kpakpa ni akɛyeɔ weku ko ni anáa shika kroko?

english: Yes, cassava is an ideal dual-purpose crop. It provides a stable home food source and any extra harvest can easily be sold in local markets or to food processors for steady cash.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nibii babaoo he nii. Eji niyenii jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shia ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ahɔ̃ɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi fɛɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ loo niyenii afeelɔi lɛ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full tropical sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil moist and protecting them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu he kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa duɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This added nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize crop, improving growth and soil health.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni akɛfata he nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shweremɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize stalks indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and grow; applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore the green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when water supply to the plant is inconsistent during fruit development. Mulching and maintaining steady soil moisture helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are caterpillars eating into the central funnels of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye nii kɛmiiya mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the growing point of maize. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late in the evening directly into the leaf funnels helps suppress them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: Cassava root rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil and fungal growth during heavy rain seasons. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi fiteɔ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy upper foliage with fruit bunches. Using strong wooden or bamboo props to support heavy bunches and controlling banana root pests keeps the stems stable against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋwɛi baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ aduawai akui. Kɛ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa tsu nii koni akɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ ni akudɔ banana shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to produce the food required to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to sunlight and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, prolonged dry weather, or poor nutrient intake. Providing overhead shade and retaining soil moisture helps the trees hold their flowers to form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ Shade ni akɛhaa yɛ yiteŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why do seeds saved from my hybrid maize produce smaller yields when I replant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ mikɛwo ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for a single generation of high yield. Replanting saved seeds from a hybrid harvest results in loss of vigor, producing uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from their roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts restores the soil's health and prevents soil pests from building up.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabote shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Tall trees provide essential shade and keep the soil moist, acting like natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa ni ewaa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baanyɛ aná tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn plants roll up into tight straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?
