english: Corn leaves roll up as a natural protective defense to trap moisture and reduce water loss through evaporation during extreme heat. Once the sun goes down and temperatures drop, the leaves unroll.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi ni eha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. Beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Baai lɛ jieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why is my plantain tree growing tall leaves but failing to produce a fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ baai kakadaji shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of potassium and steady moisture to push out a flower stem. If the soil lacks key nutrients or suffers from dry spells, the tree focuses only on leaf growth and delays fruiting.
ga: Plantains he miihia potassium babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛtsi fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa loo hɔmɔ shihilɛi miipiŋ lɛ Tso lɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ waa pɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or sap-sucking insects. Ensuring regular watering and keeping pests away allows the flowers to stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oooha nu daa ni okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and feeling hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking sap from underneath the leaves. Spraying early with neem water or recommended pest treatments stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water gets trapped in flat, heavy soil for long periods, suffocating the root system. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni tsii lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and ground water, resulting in thin, weak stems and small yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei titrii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and greedily steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛkɛ hiɛjoomɔ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade from plantain trees during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ biɔ ni dumɔwu lɛ aná hulutsoo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, preserving soil moisture and giving young cocoa the shade it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and resources to grow large tuber roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some of the seeds I sow in the soil fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry or completely waterlogged, or if soil insects and birds eat them before they can break through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ kwraa. aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye amɛ dani amɛbote nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaafɔse tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ ashwie tsei ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain strong salts that draw water out of the plant tissue, causing chemical burns on tender stems and roots. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring or line a few inches away from the plant stem.
ga: Nuŋtɛi ni mli eyi obɔ ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Ehaa tsofa shãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ shishifãi. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, reduces water loss through evaporation, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: How do weeds actually lower the amount of crop yield I harvest from my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by competing directly with your crops for plant food, groundwater, and sunlight. This leaves your crops starved, stunted, and unable to produce full harvests.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná tsei aniyenii, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛshɛɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu he.

english: Why should I trim off some of the side stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming excess leaves and side branches keeps the tomato plant from wasting energy on leafy growth, directing that energy into growing larger fruits. It also improves air flow, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tso lɛ ni efiteee hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nakai hewalɛ lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai ni da fe tsutsu lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni no haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell before steady rains begin. If seeds sprout during that first rain and experience dry days afterward, the delicate young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni amɛna hulutsoo yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade to keep cool and retain moisture until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Why is it important to establish shade on my land before planting cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee hulutsoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Setting up shade early ensures that fragile cocoa seedlings are shielded from direct heat from day one, preventing high plant loss and saving money on replanting.
ga: Ni akɛ hulutsoo baaha mra Enɛ haa abuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi tsei wuji ni laajeɔ lɛ naa ni okɛ shika ato tsei heei ni aduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do cocoa trees yield better pods when grown under moderate shade rather than direct open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Moderate shade reduces heat stress, keeps humidity levels ideal for flowering, and prevents soil moisture from evaporating too quickly, helping the trees produce healthy pods.
ga: Shade ni sa baaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be ni sa kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi. ni etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain on the same farm field as young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛduɔ kookoo bibii lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain grows fast and has wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing broad shade and cool soil conditions that young cocoa plants need to survive.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa cacao tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees no longer need plantain shade and are ready to stand on their own?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-koko tso lɛ he ehiaaa hulutsoo dɔŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaadamɔ shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: When cocoa trees grow thick trunks and create a full leaves canopy that overlaps with neighboring trees (usually around 3 to 5 years), they shade themselves and plantains can be gradually reduced.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ feɔ ekome (bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli lɛ), amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baa shi fiofio.

english: What other temporary crops besides plantain can I plant to protect my young cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi manyɛ madu kɛfata plantain he koni mikɛbu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ he?

english: Crops like cocoyam and banana grow quickly with broad leaves, making them great temporary companion crops to shield cocoa from scorching sun during its early growth.
ga: Tsei tamɔ kookoo kɛ banana daa oya kɛji amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ be kukuoo ko ni buɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ eshishijee be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops alongside young cocoa, or will they steal all the nutrients from the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ kookoo bibii ahe? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Food crops can be grown with young cocoa if spaced properly; they protect the cocoa from direct sun while giving you harvestable food from the same land.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ kookoo bibii adu niyenii tsei kɛji akɛ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Amɛbuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa niyenii ni abaanyɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does growing plantains with young cocoa help me financially while waiting for cocoa to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantains yield fruit within a year, providing quick food and farm income while you wait several years for the cocoa trees to grow and produce their first harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii yɛ afi kome mli. Feemɔ niyenii oya ni okɛ shika aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni omɛɛɔ afii babaoo koni cacao tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ.

english: What happens to soil fertility when I mix shade crops like plantain with cocoa?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ shade tsei tamɔ plantains futu cocoa?

english: Fallen plantain leaves and organic shade cover decay on the ground, creating natural mulch that feeds the soil and protects it from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Plantain baai ni egbee shi kɛ bɔɔ nii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli sũ ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ ni haaa efo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How do shade crops help protect young cocoa trees from severe weather like strong winds and heavy rainfall?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall shade crops break the force of heavy winds that break cocoa branches and shield the topsoil from being washed away by heavy torrential rain.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ gbálaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ kookoo niji lɛ amli, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains before putting young cocoa trees in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu kookoo tsei dani madu kookoo tsei bibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, which results in weak stems and very small tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce larger yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulbs bibii waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ babaoo.

english: Why do small holes appear on my vegetable leaves, and does it stop them from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ Ni ani etsĩɔ hewalɛ dalɛ naa?

english: Holes are usually made by insects like caterpillars eating the leaves. Since plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food, damaged leaves slow down the plant's growth and reduce your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Ejaakɛ tsei kɛ amɛbai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛna hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ baai ni efite lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ baa shi.

english: Flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat, dry soil from lack of rain, or a lack of specific soil nutrients like potassium needed to support fruit development.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ. aloo sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to turn soft and rotten while they are still underground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Underground rot is caused by soil fungi and bacteria that thrive when the soil stays too wet and lacks proper drainage, or when tiny worms in the soil damage the skin of the yam.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ jɛɔ sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lolo ni nu hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpata ŋmeii ahewolo lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds come up faster and stronger than my main crop right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive roots that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to grow rapidly when water is available.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya yɛ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I planted fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the soil, if the ground was too dry or too flooded, or if the seeds were old and damaged by insects during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni kooloi efite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing tall when we experience a long period without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ beni wɔnaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water acts like the transport system that carries food from the soil into the crop. Without enough rain, the plant stops expanding to save energy and water so it can stay alive.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo ni kɛ niyenii jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛhe shweremɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell by looking at the soil on my farm if it will support a good crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly, holds moisture without turning into heavy mud, and contains living earthworms or decaying organic matter like rotting leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji waa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Larger shade trees or plantain plants act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from intense heat and conserving moisture until their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baadara

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ma sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to create energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which keeps the plant healthy and causes the underground tuber to grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: The extra shoots, known as suckers, steal water and soil nutrients from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree has enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves to keep its newer top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋwɛi baai heei.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work together with helpful bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Look closely at the leaf buds along the stem cutting; they should always point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stem cuttings upside down delays sprouting and leads to poor tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo ni ebaaha tuber yibii ni ehiii aba.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the leaf sap, or by viruses carried by these insects that stunt leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes with powder-like waste inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ sũ bibii ni tamɔ sũ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides deep inside the funnel of the maize plant and feeds on the soft growing leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat gets too high or when soil moisture is unstable. Extreme heat causes stress that prevents flowers from properly pollinating into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkafee pollen jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee aduawai baa.

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to soak up water before the sun gets intense, preventing water from evaporating too quickly in the afternoon heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ mli waa. Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to put fertilizer right at the base of my crops instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base puts nutrients directly where the feeder roots can reach them easily, preventing weeds from stealing the food and keeping rain from washing it away.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii lɛ yaa he ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Enɛ haaa jwɛi aju niyenii, ni ehaa nugbɔ hu shwieɔ niyenii kɛyaa.

english: When is the best time during the year to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli?

english: The best time is at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist, allowing the roots to easily absorb dissolved nutrients without the heat burning the plant.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni mli tse yɛ nu mli oya ni amɛkɛ dɔlɛ tsuuu nii kɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor get a much bigger cocoa harvest than I do from the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da kwraa fe mi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Higher yields depend on good soil nutrients, proper tree pruning, shade management, and early control of pests and diseases, not just the size of the farm.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai anɔ. Tsoi ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ shishijee mli. Jeee ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ pɛ he ewieɔ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers advise us to prune branches from cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unwanted branches so air and sunlight can reach the tree, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the plant to use its strength to make more cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ataooo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How can I get more crop yield if my farmland is very small and cannot be expanded?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa kwraa ni anyɛɛɛ alɛɛ mli?

english: You can maximize a small plot by practicing intercropping, using improved high-yield crop seeds, and applying proper soil nutrients to grow more crops in a smaller space.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibioo ko aya hiɛ babaoo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsei dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni atsake lɛ tsuɔ nii ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa tsuɔ nii koni akɛdu tsei babaoo yɛ he bibioo ko.

english: What happens to my soil if I keep growing the same crop on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop drains specific nutrients from the soil over time, making crops weaker and yields lower unless you restore soil fertility with fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ku sɛɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do crop roots actually absorb food and water from the ground?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops have small feeder roots near the top of the soil that soak up water and dissolved nutrients like tiny drinking straws, sending food up to nourish leaves, stems, and fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji tamɔ jwɛi bibioo ni anuɔ Enitsumɔ ji ni ekɛ niyenii amaje koni ekɛha baai, ŋmeii, kɛ aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What signs show that my cocoa trees are hungry and need extra plant food?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛmiitao tsei niyenii babaoo?

english: When cocoa trees lack food, their leaves turn yellowish, their growth slows down, and they produce very few pods or shed young pods prematurely.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. edaa blɛoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo eshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii oya

english: What is the proper way to handle my harvested cocoa so I get the best quality beans?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ koni maná kɔfi ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Harvesting only ripe pods, fermenting the beans properly in plantain leaves for about six days, and drying them thoroughly on raised platforms ensures high-quality beans that buyers prefer.
ga: Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ momo lɛ pɛ ni akpaa. Beans ni yɔɔ plantain baa mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii enumɔ. Ni kɛ́ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokui ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ lɛ.

english: What quick-growing food crops can I plant alongside my young cocoa trees to make money while waiting for the cocoa to yield?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao lɛ awo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops like plantain, cassava, and maize grow quickly to provide food and income while also offering helpful shade to protect young cocoa plants as they grow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains, cassava kɛ ŋmãa miiya hiɛ oya kɛha niyenii kɛ shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food element in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves the soil too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need partial shade from faster-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves and keep the soil cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year make my harvest smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the ground a chance to recover. It also allows specific pests and soil diseases that target maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi ni ŋmãa kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hu feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does sickness move from one diseased cocoa tree to healthy trees nearby?
ga: Te hela tsɔɔ tɛŋŋ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Crop diseases often spread through tiny insects like mealybugs, which carry viruses from sick trees to healthy ones, or through fungal spores carried by wind, rain splashes, and uncleaned farm tools.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni he tseee lɛ kɛyaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains make the soil hold too much water for too long, suffocating the roots, or when fungal diseases infect the stem cuttings used during planting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko gbɛ eshwa tsei ni afolɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are insects eating big holes in the leaves of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects and caterpillars feed on green leaves because the leaves contain the sugars and moisture they need to survive. If too many leaves are eaten, the plant cannot make enough food for itself to grow strong.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ejaakɛ sugar kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli. Kɛji oye baai babaoo lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha hewalɛnamɔ nɔ dalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is a strong storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil rather than anchor deep down. Because the stem and heavy fruit bunches are top-heavy, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the wet ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Akɛni tso lɛ shishi kɛ etsitsii lɛ tsii hewɔ lɛ, aduawai lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni tsii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants fold their leaves and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plants curl or droop their leaves in high heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them save water. As long as the roots have moisture, the leaves usually stand back up once the weather cools in the evening.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ loo amɛbaagbe amɛbaai lɛ anaa yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni baaye abua ni akɛ nu akafite Be fɛɛ be ni shishifãi lɛ mli efɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ beni gbɛkɛ hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, water, root space, and sunlight away from your main crops, leaving your plants with less energy to grow big and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ fioo koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist—such as right after a light rain or early in the morning—so the roots can absorb it easily. Avoid applying it during dry heat, which can burn the roots, or during heavy downpours that wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. koni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ mli oya Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. aloo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantain bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living shade that protects the delicate young leaves from intense heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer growth at the top, which means you need to apply nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he.

english: Why are the small flowers on my watermelon vines dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ watermelon tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants grow both male and female flowers. Male flowers bloom first to attract pollinators and naturally drop off after releasing pollen, while only the female flowers with tiny fruits at their base will grow into full watermelons.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Fɔfɔi hii fɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛgbala pollinators. ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ejie pollen lɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi yei lɛ yɛ aduawai bibii Yɛ shishigbɛ pɛ ebaada ni etsɔ watermelon ni eyi obɔ.

english: Tomato leaves curl upward in extreme heat to reduce their surface area and prevent water from evaporating too quickly. As long as the plant gets enough water at the root level, the leaves usually uncurl when temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛgbala kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Yes, leaving too many sucker shoots forces them to compete with the main tree for soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one or two young suckers gives you healthier plants and larger plantains.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi feɔ efolo. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots decay, that natural nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshishifãi lɛ egbo. Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, pepper plants drop their blossoms as a survival tactic to preserve moisture and energy. Providing adequate watering at the base helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form peppers.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ shihilɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛbu hulutsoo kɛ hewalɛ he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Planting maize too close together forces individual plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to tall, thin stems that fall over easily and produce small, poorly filled cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to grow upward so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, reducing the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ adara babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away, or the soil may simply need manure or fertilizer to help the plant build healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ kɛya. Aloo ekolɛ ŋmɔtɔ he baahia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, they leave that extra food behind in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Amɛbaashi nakai niyenii ni fa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create necessary shade and keep the air cool around the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. If the soil goes from very dry to soaked, or if temperatures get too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa mli loo kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa tsɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the dirt quickly. It keeps the soil moist longer, prevents weeds from sprouting, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha muji lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft and rotting inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil for too long, especially during heavy rains on flat land. The roots need oxygen from the air, and too much standing water suffocates them and invites fungal decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ taoɔ shishifãi lɛ. Ni nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of young leaves, or passing a virus to the plant. This stunts the leaf growth and prevents the plant from expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsei Enɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do weeds make my crop plants look thin, tall, and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɔ, ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and steal the plant's drinking water, soil fertilizer, and sunlight. Your crops stretch thin trying to reach the light over the taller weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ tsei lɛ nu ni amɛnuɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la. Okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpã mli fioo ni obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha la abote jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do tiny holes appear all over my cabbage leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Small caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, hide under the cabbage leaves and chew small holes into them. These pests reproduce faster in hot, dry weather.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ cabbage baai ashishi ni amɛyeɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How do I know which direction to face a coconut when planting it in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ otsɔ nɔ okɛ ŋmei akpee kɛji oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: A coconut has three soft spots or 'eyes' at one end. Plant the coconut on its side or with the eye-end slightly tilted upwards so the sprout can easily push through and grow toward the sunlight.
ga: Kokoo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii etɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ yɛ enaagbee kome. Dumɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ esɛɛ loo tsɔ ŋmei lɛ naa fioo koni tso bibioo lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni eda kɛya hulu la lɛ he.

english: How deep do I need to dig the hole when planting a seed coconut?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ, te esa akɛ otsa bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Dig a hole deep enough so that about half to two-thirds of the coconut nut is buried in the soil, leaving the top portion uncovered so the shoot can grow freely without rotting.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni okɛfutu aaafee ŋmei lɛ fã kɛyashi mlijaa enyɔ mli ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ashiɔ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ ni agbeleɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkafite.

english: How do I choose the best ripe coconut to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select a mature, brown coconut that feels heavy and still has water sloshing inside when you shake it. The internal water provides the nutrients required for the sprout to grow.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ tsii ni kɛ́ otsi lɛ lɛ, eyɛ nu lolo yɛ emli. Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I put sawdust at the bottom of the planting hole for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii awo midumɔ bui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Adding sawdust at the base of a planting hole acts like a sponge, helping to trap water and keep the root area moist so young plants can establish roots and thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ sawdust wo dumɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni amɛdara.

english: Can I use fresh sawdust from a nearby carpenter shop directly in my crop hole?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ahe ŋmɔtɔ hee ni jɛ kapintɛfonyo shwapo ni bɛŋkɛ midumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is best to use aged or decomposed sawdust. Fresh sawdust can break down rapidly in the soil and temporarily rob nitrogen from your young plant's roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbɔ loo ni egbo atsu nii. Sawdust hee baanyɛ afite oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejie nitrogen ni yɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I help my young tree seedlings survive during hot, dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli?

english: Mixing organic material like decayed sawdust, compost, or dry husks into the base of the planting hole holds moisture near the roots, protecting the plant from drying out.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmãa ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ dumɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ amɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Koni akɛbu tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi

english: Where exactly on a coconut does the new shoot sprout from?
ga: Nɛgbɛ pɔtɛɛ ji he ni ŋmeii heei lɛ jɛɔ?

english: The sprout always emerges from one of the three dark circular spots, known as the 'eyes,' located at the top end of the coconut shell.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, tso bibioo lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ hei etɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘buds’ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ ateŋ ekome mli.

english: Why does a coconut nut sprout even before it is planted in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akoobii kwɛ̃ɔ dani aduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Coconuts carry their own food and water supply inside the hard husk, allowing the plant embryo to germinate naturally inside the nut as long as it stays warm and moist.
ga: Kokooi kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛ nu baa amɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni edɔɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I ensure my newly planted crops thrive instead of wilting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni tsei ni midu ehee lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagboi?

english: Provide good root support by digging loose soil holes, adding moisture-retaining material like compost or old sawdust at the base, and watering consistently after planting.
ga: Ha shishifãi yelikɛbuamɔ kpakpa kɛtsɔ bu ni oootse yɛ sũ ni mli tse mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛ nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii momo afata shishigbɛ lɛ he. kɛ nu daa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ

english: How do I know if my newly sprouted coconut seedling is healthy and growing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmei tso ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni eedara?

english: A healthy coconut sprout will produce firm, bright green fronds and develop thick, sturdy white roots growing out from the base of the nut into the soil.
ga: Kokooshi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛ shishifãi yɛŋ ni mli wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ shishi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes the branches and leaves of my cocoa trees to swell up and change color?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi cacao tso lɛ niji kɛ baai lɛ miifu ni amɛmiitsake amɛhe su?

english: This swelling is a primary symptom of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. It is caused by a virus transmitted by insects, which weakens the tree, reduces pod production, and eventually kills the plant if not managed.
ga: Nɛkɛ fuumɔ nɛɛ ji Cocoa Fumɔ Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi titri. Virus ko ni koolooi gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tso lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees growing unusually small and deformed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Abnormally small or misshapen pods are often a sign that the cocoa tree is infected with a viral disease like Swollen Shoot, which blocks nutrients from reaching the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo amɛhe ni ehiii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu, ni no haaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ayashɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: How do tiny insects like mealybugs harm my cocoa trees?
ga: Te kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs baanyɛ aye mi-cocoa tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mealybugs feed on cocoa sap and act as carriers for the Swollen Shoot virus. As they move from plant to plant to feed, they transmit the virus from sick cocoa trees to healthy ones.
ga: Mealybugs yeɔ kookoo nu ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ mɛi ni kɛ bud swelling hela lɛ baa. Beni amɛshiɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ koni amɛyatao niyenii lɛ, Amɛjieɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise cutting down infected cocoa trees instead of just spraying them with chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ tsofai baashwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Because Swollen Shoot is caused by a virus living inside the plant's tissue, chemical sprays cannot cure it. Cutting out infected trees and nearby contact trees is the only reliable way to stop the virus from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji akɛ muawai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ fãji amli lɛ kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ fuumɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Can a cocoa tree recover on its own after showing signs of swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ aná hewalɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ beni amɛjie ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ he okadii akpo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, a cocoa tree cannot cure itself of the Swollen Shoot virus. Once infected, the tree's health will continuously decline over two to three years until it completely dies.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei nyɛŋ atsa amɛhe kɛjɛ Swollen Shoot hela lɛ mli kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ amɛ pɛ. Tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ baaya nɔ aba shi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛyashi ebaagbo kwraa.

english: How long should I wait before planting new cocoa seedlings on land where infected trees were recently cut down?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: You should ensure all old roots and infected stumps are completely dead and wait a few months until the mealybug population dies off before replanting with clean, healthy seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei akutsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ egbo kwraa. Ni mɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi mealybug lɛ ayibɔ baagbo dani odu dumɔwui ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can swollen shoot disease spread from my neighbor's cocoa farm to my farm?
ga: Ani bud swollen hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects carrying the virus can crawl across farm boundaries or be carried by wind and ants from an infected neighboring farm to your healthy trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni hiɛ hela lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ anɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii aŋɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Are there specific cocoa varieties in Ghana that can withstand swollen shoot disease better than older varieties?
ga: Ani kookoo henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ Ghana ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ bud swollen hela nɔ fe henɔi ni eda lɛ?

english: Yes, research institutions in Ghana have developed hybrid cocoa seeds and seedlings that possess higher resistance and tolerance to viral diseases compared to older varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ efee kookoo yibii kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa lɛ, ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ amli kɛ akɛto kookooi srɔtoi ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ ahe.

english: Can my cutlass or pruning tools spread diseases from one cocoa tree to another?
ga: Ani mi-kpoo loo nibii ni mikɛfoɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ?

english: Yes, tools that carry sap from an infected tree can transfer pathogens to healthy trees. Cleaning and disinfecting your farm tools regularly helps prevent disease transfer.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɛŋdadei ni hiɛɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ otsumɔ oŋmɔ mli nibii amli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ helai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How does planting permanent shade trees help protect my cocoa crop from getting sick?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe koni hela akamɔ amɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees reduce heat stress on cocoa plants and create a cooler microclimate. Healthy, unstressed cocoa trees have better natural strength to endure pest attacks and environmental hardship.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni baa kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ baa. Kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ adamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shihilɛ mli naagbai anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside them provides shade and retains soil moisture, protecting the seedlings while they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli waa.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Blossom drop in tomatoes happens when plants suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Providing consistent water and mulching helps keep the roots cool and prevents flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with sticky dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? ni muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves during the day and eat the tender growth, requiring early detection and proper treatment to save the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ mli ni atsa lɛ mra. koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Root rot in cassava is caused by fungal diseases that multiply in heavy, waterlogged soils. Improving soil drainage or planting on raised mounds prevents water from standing around the roots.
ga: Hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni abaafee jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak without giving good harvest when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ mli tseee ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo kpakpa baaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, underground water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves for maximum food production.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ená niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when many young shoots are growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) steal water and nutrients from the main parent plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant yields big, healthy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I grow maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients and lets soil pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ bii. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why should I wait for rain or wet soil before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Dry soil cannot break down solid fertilizer, which means plant roots cannot take it in. Soil moisture dissolves the fertilizer so the roots can safely absorb the nutrients without burning the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛŋ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ abote mli. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe ni eshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest grow as well this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are special varieties bred for one generation of high performance. Saving and planting seeds from that harvest causes the next generation to lose those strong traits, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni akwɛɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ni abuɔ he ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa yinɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat dry spell. If your seeds germinate and the rains stop for two weeks, the tender young seedlings will dry up and die before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii enyɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shɛɔ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the earth. This naturally feeds the soil so your next crop has free fertilizer to grow strong.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas lɛ yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant sends down to grow a much larger tuber.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them, the hot sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture in the surrounding soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduuu tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ he yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaashã amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their blossoms without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo yibii ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when daytime temperatures get too hot or when they do not get enough water. High heat stresses the plant, preventing the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Heavy, waterlogged soil suffocates the roots and breeds fungi, so planting on raised ridges helps excess water run off.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii fɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves growing very big and green, but the fruits and tubers remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee eŋɔli lɛ? Shi aduawai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kwraa.

english: This usually means your soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen builds big leaves, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to grow tubers, grains, and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ feɔ baai wuji. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛkwɛ bulb, dumɔwui, kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are my maize stalks falling over and showing small holes chewed through the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani oootsɔ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like stem borers or fall armyworms. They bore inside the stalk and chew the leaves, weakening the main stem until the wind easily blows the plant over.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms. Amɛboteɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ, ni amɛhaa tso lɛ shishi fã titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ oya.

english: Curling leaves are caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of new growth, or by viruses they spread. This prevents the leaves from expanding and weakens the entire plant.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa baa lɛ mli alɛɛ ni egbɔjɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is already plenty of sunlight in the field for all plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha tsei fɛɛ?

english: Weeds do not just block sun; they aggressively steal water and plant food directly from the soil beneath your crops. Even with sunlight, your crops will starve because weeds are taking their nutrients.
ga: Jeee akɛ jwɛi tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa kɛkɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la yɛ moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii po baaye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ jwɛi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and leafy. When soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to the new leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why is my okra plant growing very tall with big leaves but no fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji shi aduawai bɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich chicken manure, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and thick green leaves instead of making flowers. The plant needs fertilizers richer in phosphorus to encourage it to stop branching out and start fruiting.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsei he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli koni amɛkafee niji ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by heat, dry winds, or a lack of moisture in the soil. The tree naturally drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying when weather conditions get too harsh.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu tsɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a defense trick to protect themselves from losing water through the sun's heat. If the leaves unroll again in the cool evening, the crop is fine, but if they stay rolled in the early morning, it means the plant desperately needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, Tsei ni miida lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi. Shi kɛji akɛ efoɔ lolo leebi maŋkpa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia tsei.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just like human lungs do. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the plant for too long, the roots drown, starve of oxygen, and rot from fungal attacks.
ga: Tamɔ gbɔmɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ, ha nu lɛ ahi ohe. Kɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagboi, amɛnaŋ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni amɛbaafite kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni baatutua amɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their leaves when the dry sun season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce the amount of water evaporating from their bodies. Giving them consistent water at their roots early in the morning prevents them from dropping leaves in self-defense.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbɔmɔtsei amli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa leebi lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and growing small and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a plant sickness called leaf curl virus. Once the virus gets inside, it distorts leaf growth and slows down fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, ni ji tso hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf curl virus lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. Kɛji hela lɛ bote mli Efiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are insects eating the blossoms off my cowpea plants before any pods appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms produce sweet nectar that attracts pests like flower thrips, which chew through the delicate flower parts. Without healthy flowers, the plant cannot get pollinated to form bean pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ. ni shwieɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ Kɛji fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollination ni amɛfee bean pods.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting shoots long before the rainy season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ be saŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from their resting period after a few months, especially if stored in a room that is warm or humid. Keeping them in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn slows down this natural inner clock so they don't sprout too early.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ, titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni ekakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, weak root systems that stay near the surface of the soil. When the heavy bunch adds weight to the top, strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you support the stem with a sturdy wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsii lɛ, okɛ muji afata he yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient crops need to grow strong green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants recover their healthy green color and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When too much rain collects in the soil without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows fungal rots to grow, destroying the tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ adara. Kpata bulb lɛ hiɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting them under shade trees or alongside fast-growing plantain trees acts like an umbrella, shielding the cocoa from harsh heat while keeping the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi loo yɛ dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it naturally into the soil through their roots. When the cowpeas finish growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free plant food for crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji tsina ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay attached and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?
