english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that live on the underside of the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or appropriate organic washes stops the insects before they stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ loo nibii ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa dani amɛfeɔ tsei ni shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if the seed yam I bought is healthy enough to sprout properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A good seed yam feels firm when you press it, shows clean skin without soft decay, and has visible small bumps or 'eyes' near the head, which show that new shoots are ready to break out.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji onyɛ amɛnɔ. Ejieɔ hewolo ni he tse ni fiteee lɛ kpo. ni ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ yɛ yitso lɛ masɛi ni anaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii heei efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaje kpo.

english: Why do some of my vegetable seeds fail to shoot up even after I water the nursery bed daily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ nu ewo ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ daa gbi po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were stored in bad conditions, are too old, or were buried too deep in the dirt where oxygen cannot reach them. Planting clean seeds at a shallow depth in moist, loose soil yields the best sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ehiii, amɛgbɔ tsɔ, loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni mli ewo muji nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the wind blows during rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the top of the soil. When heavy rain softens the earth and heavy bunches grow on top, strong winds can push the whole plant down unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni jwɛi ni mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei muu fɛɛ kɛba shi. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop produce extra shoots coming out from just one planted seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ shwereɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally spread by producing extra stems called tillers. Giving each plant enough spacing, adequate water, and early fertilizer encourages it to produce many strong tillers, leading to much larger harvests per seed.
ga: Omɔ tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ spades lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni oookwɛ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ bɔ ni sa Ha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi Ebaaha tso lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa babaoo baa yɛ dumɔwu kome mli.

english: The very first rain after a dry season often warms up the dry topsoil without soaking deep into the ground. If a dry spell follows right after, the germinating seed dries out and dies before it can push through the soil. It is safer to wait for steady rains before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli agbala. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani odu.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest because there are more plants on my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ejaakɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei babaoo yɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Instead of getting more produce, you will end up with many weak, thin plants that yield very small ears or fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona yibii babaoo Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ toi loo aduawai bibii waa.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food for growth. When nitrogen runs low in the soil, the plant pulls it from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa. Kɛji nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge leaves but produce small tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or when there is heavy rain, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems up top instead of storing food below in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii kɛyaa ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I cut down all the plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifo dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? kookoo tso muu fɛɛ

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to survive full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before they turn into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or when the soil gets too dry. When the plant experiences heat stress, it drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the inner leaves of my young maize wilting and drying up while the outer leaves still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ egbo ni egbi yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: This drying is usually caused by stem borer worms that hatch inside the stalk. The small caterpillars eat the soft growing core of the plant from the inside out, causing the center leaves to die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii lɛ yeɔ tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. ha baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ gboi

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and die during the afternoon even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli beni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is a sign of root rot or bacterial wilt from the soil. When soil stays soaked with bad drainage, the roots cannot breathe and rot away, causing the plant to wilt because broken roots cannot suck up water.
ga: Enɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛgboi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni ekumɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why does the maize seed I saved from my own harvest yield much less than the certified seed I bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to give maximum yield only for the first planting. If you save and replant those seeds, the new plants lose their vigor and give smaller, uneven yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu lɛ Tsei heei lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ ni amɛbaawo yibii ni baa shi daa.

english: Weeds are wild local plants naturally adapted to your soil and weather. Their roots grow fast and grab water and plant food much quicker than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee yɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ niyenii oya kwraa fe shia tsei.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside your cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the cocoa from intense sun and keep the soil moist while the tree grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa o-cocoa lɛ náa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your farm early and spraying recommended insecticides or a neem leaf mixture directly into the central stem funnel can stop them from destroying your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are small brown insects eating holes in my stored maize months after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa ni ato nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that multiply in stored crops. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is bone-dry and storing it in airtight bags or using approved grain storage dust prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni fɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi egbɔ ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo okɛ dumɔwui ahe sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekashwere.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellowish-green instead of staying flat and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects or infected stems. You can prevent this by obtaining certified, disease-free stems for planting instead of using stem cuttings from sick plants.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela bɛ mli ni aŋmala he odaseyeli akɛ ooodu lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why are my healthy-looking tomato plants drooping and dying suddenly even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving up the stem. Rotating your crops so you do not plant tomatoes, peppers, or eggplants in the same soil every season helps clear the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii koni akadu tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, loo eggplant yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hela lɛ kɛya.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and when the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy. Supporting the main stalk with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole gives it the balance needed to withstand high winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Akɛ tsei loo ŋmei tsei ni wa fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji lɛ? No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tso ko ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that feeds the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground using poles allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, leading to larger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant will restore its green color and help it grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛbaafata he Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaha tso lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to put chemical fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied early in the morning or late in the evening when the soil is moist after rain. Putting fertilizer on dry soil under hot sun can burn plant roots and waste nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough rain for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ enɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked deep into the ground—at least up to the depth of your middle finger—before planting. Planting in dry or barely damp soil causes seeds to dry out and fail to sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ—kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛyashi oteŋgbɛ nine lɛ nɔ—dani okɛdu. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Yellow leaves, especially starting from the bottom of the plant, usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient or the ground is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the specific soil nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil, resulting in lower yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and small even when the leaves on top look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy top leaves instead of pushing roots deep to expand into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai ni tsii lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo tsi sisifã ɔmɛ kɛ ya shɔkɔ konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why is it important to leave specific spaces between my cassava stems when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ oodu lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives each cassava plant enough sunlight for its leaves and enough room underground for its tubers to spread without competing with nearby plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa yucca tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ebaai lɛ. Ni he ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juices, or by viral diseases spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely during the flowering stage, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients like calcium.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but end up with empty pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Empty pods occur when sap-sucking insects attack the young developing pods early on, eating the tiny seeds inside before they have a chance to grow full and dry.
ga: Pods ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua gbekɛbii, ni amɛmiifee pods mra. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui bibii ni ayeɔ yɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight so they can make more food for the plant, keeps leaves away from wet soil diseases, and ultimately produces much larger yam tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Buu baai ahe kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ obaaná sweet potato tuber ni da fe no kwraa.

english: Why must I clear weeds while my crop seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and easily choked out by weeds; clearing weeds early ensures young crop roots get all the water, sunlight, and nutrients without competing.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up quickly whenever the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: If maize seeds are planted too shallowly or in hard, unplowed soil, the roots remain near the surface and cannot reach the deeper soil moisture needed during dry spells.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and thin when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plants are like people sharing a small plate of food. When planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none with enough nourishment to grow thick and healthy. Proper spacing gives each plant room to feed.
ga: Tsei tamɔ gbɔmɛi ni miija niyenii tsɛnsii bibii. Kɛji adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛbɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara ni amɛhe awa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsu fɛɛ tsu náa niyenii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for their tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant direct its energy into growing larger yams underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdu ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant cannot catch sunlight efficiently, causing its growth to slow down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. haa dalɛ baa shi

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring the soil's strength for future crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater collects around the roots without draining away, it drowns the roots and encourages fungi to grow, causing the cassava tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu babaoo buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Ha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo dani okpa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off before producing fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms to save water and protect themselves. Mulching the soil around the plant and keeping it moist helps protect the blossoms so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo tso lɛ he ni oha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees or plantain plants act like living umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from harsh heat and keeping the surrounding air and soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why should I cut off some of the young suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Too many young suckers growing from the same stem will steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Pruning the extra suckers allows the main tree to put all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tsei bibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating deep inside the leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye nii kɛmiiya mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the center funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early allows you to apply recommended pest control methods before they destroy the growing point of the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Ehaa okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery patches appear on the leaves of my vegetables when the weather is warm and humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: The white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which thrives in high humidity and crowded foliage. Giving your plants good spacing improves airflow and helps keep the leaves dry, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ tsei ahe tsei babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ he jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akagbi. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: My cocoa trees have stopped producing pods for a while; does this mean my trees are dying?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ kpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ be fioo. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mitso lɛ miigbo?

english: No, cocoa trees naturally go through resting periods. During and after these resting periods, the tree re-energizes itself to produce fresh flowers and bear new fruit.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli. Yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be mli kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ Abaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni ewo fɔfɔi heei kɛ aduawai heei.

english: Does a cocoa tree produce flowers and fruit continuously all year long?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally take resting periods. After a rest period, the tree blooms with flowers and forms fruit, depending on how well the farm is maintained.
ga: Cocoa tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be. yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi ni ebaawo yibii. Edamɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there tiny insects flying around my cocoa flowers when they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii ni fɔ̃ɔ amɛhe kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe beni amɛwo fɔfɔii lɛ?

english: Those small insects, such as midges, are pollinators. They visit the blooming flowers to feed and, in doing so, carry pollen from flower to flower, which allows the tree to set pods.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii. Amɛsaraa fɔfɔi ni miikwɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Ni yɛ nakai feemɔ mli lɛ esa akɛ ajie Pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ etsitsii lɛ toɔ.

english: How do insects help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Te kooloi bibii yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects transfer pollen between flowers as they move around your farm. Without this pollen transfer, cocoa flowers dry up and fall off instead of developing into cocoa pods.
ga: Kplukai kɛ pollen yaa fɔfɔi ateŋ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛbɔleɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ. Kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: What can I do on my farm to attract more beneficial insects to my cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛgbala kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛba mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ?

english: Keeping moist leaf litter, plant residues, and moderate shade on the ground creates an ideal breeding environment for tiny pollinators like midges so they stay on your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni mli efɔ, tsei amli sũi, kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges lɛ baanyɛ afɔ yɛ koni amɛhi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated by small insects very soon after opening. If pollinators do not visit them within that short window, the unpollinated flowers naturally drop off.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni fɔfɔi lɛ egbele amɛhe lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ eyasaraaa amɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi ni ŋmeii shwieee amɛnɔ lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk of the tree instead of just on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ, shi jeee yɛ baai lɛ pɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on their main trunk and thick branches—a trait called cauliflory—which makes it easier for small ground-dwelling pollinators to reach the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ kɛ amɛniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛshɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What signals my cocoa trees to start blooming during the year?
ga: Mɛni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa flowering is usually triggered by changes in weather, particularly the onset of light rains after a dry spell, which tells the tree it has enough moisture to support flower growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ kookoo fɔfɔi baa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ fioo. yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Can cocoa trees that were planted decades ago by my parents still yield good pods?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni mifɔlɔi du afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Yes, older cocoa trees can remain productive for many decades if they receive proper pruning, protection from pests, adequate soil nutrients, and have good pollinator activity around them.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa Niyenii nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ŋmeii kpakpai yɛ ni bɔleɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if an old cocoa tree should be pruned or completely replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mafo cacao tso momo ko loo matsake kwraa?

english: If an old tree still flowers well and has healthy bark, good pruning and care can restore its yield. If it is severely diseased or no longer produces flowers despite good weather, replanting may be necessary.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ egbɔ lɛ ewoɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ hela ko ni naa wa loo ewooo fɔfɔi dɔŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi yɛ lɛ, Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is keeping moderate shade trees on my cocoa farm good for flower production?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha fɔfɔii afeemɔ lɛ?

english: Shade trees keep the air humid and the soil cool, protecting delicate cocoa flowers from drying out in harsh sunlight and preserving the moist conditions pollinators need.
ga: Tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. ni ekwɛ hulutsoo shihilɛ ni kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ taoɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees seem healthier when there are diverse plants growing around the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ waa yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: A varied environment supports a steady population of helpful insects and maintains good soil moisture, which helps cocoa trees flower consistently and resist environmental stress.
ga: Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi daa ni ekɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi kpeɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to push my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' on the cassava stem. They must point upward toward the sky so the new branches grow smoothly above ground instead of pushing down into the earth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni niji heei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Rainwater often washes nutrients out of the soil, so feeding the plants with the right fertilizer helps them green up and make food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nu hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can easily burn the tender stem and delicate roots of your plant. Placing it a few centimeters away in a ring lets the roots reach out safely to drink up the nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe shweshweeshwe koni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground, so they droop to save moisture. Once the sun goes down and cools off, the leaves stand straight again.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egboɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ te shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of friendly insects like bees to pollinate them. Keeping the soil damp helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii ni baahã amɛfɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the middle leaf funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm hiding inside the leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnel gets rid of them before they eat the main growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛye ŋmei titri ni miida lɛ.

english: How do weeds damage my crops if I leave them growing in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ efite miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds steal vital drinking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops' roots, while also providing safe hiding places for farm pests and diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni anuɔ ni he hiaa waa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam leaves and vines onto tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he?

english: Yam vines naturally climb up high to expose maximum leaves to sunlight so the plant can produce food to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie amɛhe tsei lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii lɛ, abaanyɛ adu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully grown and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Sample your groundnuts by digging up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brownish markings and the nuts fill out the skin tightly, your crop is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Bua ŋmei he nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa kɛtsɔ tso ko ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ egbɔ ni esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow and stop growing if I delay my weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young maize for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeding is delayed, the weeds choke the maize and absorb the essential nitrogen needed to keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi lɛ ashwiemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Balancing soil nutrients encourages the crop to set flowers and produce healthy pods.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so it does not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. When lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, digging up one sample root allows you to check if the roots are starch-filled and ready before harvesting the full plot.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Kɛ́ otsa shishifã kome he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ebaaha okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ eyɛ starch ni amɛfee klalo dani okpa shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What happens to my okra plants if I leave the pods on the stem for too long without picking them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi okra tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ?

english: Leaving okra pods on the stem too long causes them to become hard and woody, which signals the plant to stop producing new flowers. Regular harvesting every few days encourages the plant to keep bearing fresh pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi okra ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee tamɔ tso. Enɛ ji okadi kɛha tso lɛ akɛ ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ. Nikpamɔ daa daa Gbii fioo komɛi baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eha eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi ehee.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking plant juices, or by viral infections. Early spraying with organic neem oil or recommended insecticides helps protect fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ mli Akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in overly dark, damp, and crowded farm conditions. Pruning excess cocoa leaves and clearing undergrowth allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees and prevent fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ duŋ, fɛ̃i, kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo mli. Cocoa baai ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ kɛ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why is it important for me to rotate crops like yam with groundnuts instead of planting yam every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmeii daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yam continuously in the same soil depletes specific nutrients and allows yam pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts fixes nitrogen naturally back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa sweet potato tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap loose soil around the base of my groundnut plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔle muji ni etse ehe lɛ he lɛ? Peanut tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni edaa lɛ

english: Groundnut flowers produce stems called pegs that must push down into the ground to form nuts underground. Earthing up soft soil around the stem makes it easy for pegs to enter the earth and expand into full nuts.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni esa akɛ atswa shikpɔŋ koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ tsa lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmei lɛ baabote sũ lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into small fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Extreme heat causes stress that prevents proper pollination, leading tomato blossoms to drop off unfertilized. Consistent watering at the root level and maintaining good plant spacing helps reduce heat shock.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ pollination naa baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni akɛ fɔmɔ nii wooo mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ gbɛ kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves wither and dry up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and wide leaves that lose water rapidly in dry, hot weather. Mulching with dried leaves or grass around the base helps conserve soil moisture and keeps roots cool.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni ebɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Is cassava a good crop for me to plant if I want to avoid crop failure?
ga: Ani ŋmei ji tso kpakpa kɛha mi kɛji miisumɔ ni matsi mihe kɛjɛ tso ni fiteɔ lɛ he?

english: Cassava is a very tough crop that survives dry conditions and poor soils well. It produces high yields and rarely fails completely, making it a reliable choice for farmers.
ga: Cassava ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa waa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli jogbaŋŋ. Yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko baaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛhaa okwaafoi.

english: Why does cassava yield more food compared to many other root crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei woɔ yibii fe tuber ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava is highly efficient at converting sunlight and soil nutrients into starch stored in its roots, allowing it to yield heavily even in basic farm conditions.
ga: Cassava tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsakemɔ mli ewoɔ ŋmeii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli po.

english: What happens to my cassava crop if dry weather sets in before harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi dani akpa?

english: Cassava responds to dry weather by shedding leaves to save moisture, resting underground until rains return, which keeps the crop from dying easily.
ga: Cassava tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ebaai ni eshwieɔ shi koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ nɔ. Hii shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo oya.

english: How many months does it take for cassava to mature before I can harvest it?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmei?

english: Most common cassava varieties take about nine to twelve months to reach full maturity, depending on the rainfall and soil type.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ babaoo lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji nɛɛhu kɛyashi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant my cassava early in the year, when should I expect to harvest?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa?

english: If you plant around March at the start of the rains, a nine-month variety will be ready for harvest in December towards the start of the dry season.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ March he, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni eye nyɔji 9 lɛ baafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa yɛ December mli, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Can I leave my cassava roots in the soil if I am not ready to harvest them immediately?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afeee klalo akɛ abaakpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ani abaanyɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava roots can stay safely underground for several months after maturing, acting as a natural storage until you are ready to harvest and market them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa amɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my cassava long past its maturity date?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe be ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the ground too long can cause the roots to become tough and woody, reducing the quality and weight of usable starch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee tso. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ashikiŋsha ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ emli tsiimɔ baa shi.

english: What type of soil is best for growing big cassava roots?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ni sa kɛha ŋmei shishifãi wuji akwɛmɔ?

english: Cassava prefers loose, well-drained soil where roots can easily expand underground without getting waterlogged or trapped in hard clay.
ga: Cassava sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni ekɛ nu akamɔ shi loo ekɛ ehe akawo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa mli.

english: Does the variety of cassava I grow affect the quality of food I make from it?
ga: Ani ŋmeii srɔtoi ni miduɔ lɛ saa niyenii ni mikɛ ŋmeii feɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, high-starch varieties produce better texture and quality when processed into foods like gari, flour, or baked cakes.
ga: Hɛɛ, starch henɔi ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ afee niyenii tamɔ gari, ashikiŋsha loo keeki ni ashã.

english: What food products can I process my cassava tubers into after harvesting?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii manyɛ mafee ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvested cassava roots can be processed into gari, high-quality cassava flour for baking, starch, or traditional doughs like fufu and kokonte.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa lɛ afee ŋmei ashikishaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shãa, ashikishaŋ loo blema ashikiŋsha tamɔ fufu kɛ coconte.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or they are getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer early helps them turn green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. loo enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my plant has a disease before it completely dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ mitso lɛ dani egbo kwraa?

english: Check your plants regularly for early signs like unusual leaf spots, stunted growth, or curling leaves. Catching disease symptoms early allows you to treat the plant before the problem spreads across your whole field.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ daa kɛha mra be mli okadii tamɔ baa hei ni esaaa, dalɛ ni egbɔjɔ, loo baai ni ebɔle amɛhe. Helai okadii ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tsei dani naagba lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young corn leaves. You can protect your crop by inspecting the funnels of the plants early and applying safe pesticides or local remedies.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ otsei lɛ agbɛi ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo maŋ lɛ mli tsofai atsu nii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate insecticide clears the pests and lets new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi lɛ ni eye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings fail to sprout if they are planted upside down, if the stems used were too old and dry, or if the soil lacked enough moisture during the first few days.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Tsoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni egbi. aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli

english: Yams need loose, soft soil on mounds or ridges to grow big and long. Hard or stony soil prevents the tuber from expanding easily, leading to small or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛdara. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my farm ground needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, look pale, or produce small leaves and weak harvests despite getting rain, your soil is likely low on essential plant food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ baai bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in heavy shade and excess moisture. Pruning your cocoa trees to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kookoo tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa mɔ nɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit heads. Planting them deep enough in rich soil and mounding dirt high around the base gives them better support against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ayitsei ni tsii. Dumɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my corn farm early when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ mra be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeding early removes competition so your young corn plants do not have to fight weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, allowing them to grow strong and yield higher harvests.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni o-baby corn tsei lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I plant my corn seeds in straight lines with clear spacing instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ mli ka shi faŋŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each corn plant gets enough room to grow roots and leaves without crowding, while straight rows make weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi kɛ baai akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe ebɔko he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ haa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do improved seed varieties help my farm perform better than using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Certified improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry weather, and produce larger, uniform crops compared to grain saved from older harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da, ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmaa ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ blema ŋmaakpamɔi amli lɛ he.

english: Where can I get high-quality seeds for planting this season?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni madu yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Quality certified seeds can be obtained from registered agro-dealers, local agricultural extension officers, or at official agricultural events and fairs organized for farmers.
ga: Abaanyɛ ana dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Kuu lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi loo kɛjɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kɛ jarayeli nifeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha okwaafoi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly into tubes on very sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural way of saving water during heat stress. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to stop moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ dɔlɛ be mli. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akaho oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my corn field is lacking nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your corn leaves start turning pale green or yellow—especially starting from the tip down the center of the leaf—it is a sign that the soil is low on nitrogen and needs fertilization.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-corn baa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse—titri lɛ kɛjɛ baa lɛ shishi kɛyashi teŋgbɛ lɛ—eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I keep my corn clean and good quality when I am shelling and processing it after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ŋmãa lɛ he atse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie ŋmãa lɛ ni atsu he nii yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Shell your corn on clean tarpaulins rather than on the bare dirt to keep out stones and dust, and sort out broken or moldy kernels to prevent spoilage and maintain high market value.
ga: Okɛ o-corn lɛ awo tarp ni he tse nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ koni obu he kɛjɛ tɛi kɛ sũ he. kɛ dumɔwui ni ekumɔ loo ni efite lɛ mligbalamɔ koni akafite ni eha jara ni nɔ kwɔ ahi jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my corn is completely dry and ready for safe storage in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli shweshweeshwe?

english: Corn is ready for storage when the kernels are hard, cannot be marked with a fingernail, and make a sharp cracking sound when bitten or rattled together.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha nitoo kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli wa. Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ eniji atswa ni ekɛ gbɛɛmɔ ni naa wa aba kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ loo akpokpo lɛ ekome

english: How can listening to local agricultural radio programs help me manage my crop farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he redio nɔ nifeemɔi atoiboo baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Farmer radio broadcasts give timely updates on seasonal weather changes, pest outbreaks, step-by-step planting guidance, and current market prices directly from agricultural experts.
ga: Okwaafoi redio adafitswaa haa be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Pest outbreak Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ dumɔ he kɛ jarayeli jara ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nilelɔi adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What should I do if I notice unusual pest damage starting to spread across my corn crop?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ miibɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ?

english: Inspect the field immediately to check under the leaves and inside the growing shoots, then contact your local extension officer for advice on safe biological or chemical controls before the pests spread further.
ga: Kwɛmɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ona baai lɛ ashishi kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ oakutso lɛ mli nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ agba sane koni ewo bo ŋaa yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he. Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baagbɛ ashwã

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living cover to protect them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ebaaha amɛhe ahi nɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crop plants use to grow strong leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and keeps the plant growing healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but produce tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are planted too close together, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in its roots. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients help the plant focus on growing bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas and maize together in the same field without harming my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, cowpeas actually take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for neighboring maize plants while giving you two different harvests from the same land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ nibii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems near the surface of the soil rather than deep taproots. Heap up extra soil around the base of the stem and support heavy fruit bunches with strong bamboo or wooden poles to keep them upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Okɛ muji krokomɛi abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni fiɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa ni akɛbaakwɛ nɔ ni ekɛma shi shiŋŋ.

english: The first rain after a long dry spell usually only wets the top layer of soil, which dries out fast and traps seeds in hot, humid ground where fungus thrives. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures the subsoil is damp enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Egbiɔ oya ni emɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central fold of young maize plants where it is moist. Spraying approved organic or chemical treatments directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ateŋ he ni ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani efite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in full sunlight to create energy for building heavy underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant produce much larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist with grass mulch and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ daa ni okɛ tso ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why is my maize crop yielding less grain even though I plant on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ yibiiwoo faaa eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same spot every season wears out specific soil nutrients and lets plant-specific pests and diseases build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or soybeans breaks disease cycles and naturally restores soil power.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo soybeans atsake ŋmãa. Efoɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food they need to build green leaves. This often happens if the soil is weak or if heavy rains have washed nutrients away, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts next to my maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special micro-bugs in their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the groundnut plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your maize crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he ni eyɛ kooloi bibii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ gbo lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmei lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, which gives them more light and protects them from rot and diseases caused by wet dirt.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa la babaoo baa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: The mother plantain tree shares all its food and water with every sucker growing next to it. By pruning away extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones, you allow the mother plant to focus all its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ jaa eniyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni eeefo ni ehiɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu plantains ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ he nii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can actually feed, so dropping flowers is normal. However, if almost all flowers drop, it means the tree is stressed by dry weather or there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi, kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo laaje lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Aloo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and turning tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or aphids sucking the sap out of the young leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these tiny bugs early using neem oil spray helps new leaves grow back healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Black, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is growing fast. Watering your plants regularly and avoiding dry spells helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato ni yɔɔ shishi diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium awo tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli.

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves in your farm because their roots grow fast and drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's food and sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava cuttings sprout quickly while others just rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings rot if they are planted upside down or placed in waterlogged soil during heavy rains. Planting the cutting right-side up with the buds pointing toward the sky in well-drained soil helps roots grow quickly.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ninejurɔgbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ oya he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my small seeds fail to come up when I bury them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ bibii nakai lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ edaaa kɛji mifu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A small seed has only a tiny packet of stored food energy inside it to push its first sprout out of the ground. If planted too deep, the sprout uses up all its energy before reaching the surface and dies in the soil.
ga: dumɔwui bibii Paketi bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ. ni hiɛɔ niyenii hewalɛ yɛ mli koni ekɛtsi klɛŋklɛŋ tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji adu lɛ mli tsɔ tsei bibii yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant soybeans in the same field alongside my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu soybean yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Soybeans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This feeds the soil naturally, helping your corn grow stronger and saving you money on commercial chemical fertilizers.
ga: Soybeans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni okɛ shika ato jarayeli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: How does growing more than one crop like corn and soybean protect my money?
ga: Nibii ni fe ekome ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ soybeans Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mishika he?

english: Growing different crops creates a financial safety net. If bad weather or pests ruin one crop, the other crop may survive, ensuring you still have produce to sell and income to support your family.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Ehaa shika he shweshweeshwefeemɔ baa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko hiɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi. Obaanyɛ oná hekɛnɔfɔɔ akɛ oyɛ nibii ni okɛbaahɔ̃ɔ lolo, ni oyɛ shika ni okɛbaakwɛ oweku lɛ.

english: Why do my young corn leaves have small holes in them during the early growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the plant. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmã tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmã baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How will attending modern farming training sessions help my yield improve?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ mli ni mikɛ mihe aaawo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Training sessions teach you updated techniques like proper row spacing, fertilizer timing, and weed management, which help you harvest much more grain from the exact same size of land.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ bei tsɔɔ ŋaai heei, tamɔ gbɛ ni sa ni ato yɛ lii ​​amli. be ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa dumɔwui babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my soybean leaves turn yellow and drop off right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at maturity are normal for soybeans. The plant is sending all its remaining food and energy directly into the pod seeds to make them dry and ready for harvesting.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ soybeans mli. Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ majeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: What is the benefit of planting my corn in straight rows instead of scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: Planting in straight, measured rows gives every plant equal space to catch sunlight and soil food, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your field.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛ gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni onyiɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my corn plants so they grow big?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli koni amɛdara?

english: Corn needs food twice: a small dose right at planting to build strong roots, and a second dose when the plant is knee-high so it has energy to build large, heavy cobs.
ga: Niyenii enyɔ he miihia ŋmãa: tsofa bibioo ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa; kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni amɛha hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What happens to my soil if I plant only corn on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi?

english: Planting corn continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating your field with soybeans cleans the soil and restores nutrient levels.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Soybeans ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsakemɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up like tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up as a defense mechanism to hide from direct sunlight, reducing water loss through evaporation until the heat passes and moisture stays inside the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ hoɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my harvested corn is dry enough to store without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni efiteee?

english: Corn is dry enough when the grain is hard, cannot be easily scratched with a fingernail, and makes a sharp cracking sound when rattled together, which prevents mold and insects from ruining stored grain.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ mli wa. Niji ahe tsɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ mlɛo. ni efee gbee ni naa wa waa kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ ekome Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa shoots burn easily under the harsh tropical sun. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight over nutrients in the soil and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This lack of food and light makes the leaves lose their green color.
