ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Niyenii kɛ la ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight. This is a survival trick that helps the plant conserve water by preventing it from evaporating too fast.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛtsiɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a blossom cannot produce seeds, the plant drops it to save energy rather than waste resources on fruit that will not grow.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ awo fɔ Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui. Tsei baashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ aduawai ni baakwɛ̃ŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before harvest after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbala dani kpamɔ lɛ ba yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When cabbages get a sudden surge of water after a dry spell, the inner leaves absorb water very fast and grow quicker than the outer leaves can stretch, forcing the head to burst open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cabbage nine shɛ nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mligbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛdaraa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. ha yitso lɛ mli agbala

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, deep soil to push downward smoothly. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the tuber struggles to penetrate the ground and turns bent or stunted.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛbaakoto loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Excess rain fills up all the tiny air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, the living tissues in the roots die, allowing soil fungi to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Faji ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baagboi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop growing and develop tiny, crinkled leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa shweremɔ kɛ baai bibii ni ejieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɔɔ?

english: Tiny insects like thrips or aphids feed on the sap of young pepper leaves and spread plant viruses. This sap-sucking and viral infection damages the plant leaves, causing them to curl up and stunt overall growth.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa bibii amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ. Sap ni anuɔ kɛ hela ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ baai. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ dalɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall with thin stems and small cobs when I apply too much chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Beni akɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ mli lɛ

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend almost all its energy producing leaves and stems, leaving very little strength or nutrients to build thick stalks or large, heavy cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii. Hewalɛ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ ni baanyɛ afee ŋmeii ni mli tse loo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cowpea pods dry up at different times on the same plant instead of ripening all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ tso kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ shikome lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants produce blossoms continuously over a period of weeks rather than all at once. Because the flowers appear at different times, the seed pods mature and dry out in stages.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ yɛ otsii babaoo amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafɔ shikome Enɛ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi jeɔ kpo yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, intense sunlight. Without shade from companion trees like plantains, the hot sun dries out the tender leaves, causing them to scorch and turn yellow or brown.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli kɛ ekãa nɛkɛ lɛ adɛŋ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo asarasu.

english: Why are my young maize leaves full of tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by early-stage pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant's leaves during the rainy season and eat the tender growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mra, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni eyeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable stems rot faster when I plant them very close together in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close together stops air from flowing between the plants. During the rains, moisture stays trapped around the stems, creating a wet space where fungal rot grows easily.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaaaa kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ abɔle tso lɛ he, ni eha he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ jɛmɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much chemical fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to build tall stems and green leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow better after I leave my field to rest for a season without planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be ko ni miduuu nii lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow lets decaying plants and natural organisms rebuild the soil's organic matter and nutrients, giving the earth time to recharge for future crops.
ga: Ha tsei kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni miifite lɛ ama nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni aha je lɛ be ni ekɛwo wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the soil grow better food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ mi-ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When planted alongside maize, they feed nitrogen into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛhaa nitrogen boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five maize seeds into the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one spot forces the young plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ lɛ baa.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your plants before their roots can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli dani amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by sudden extreme heat, long dry spells, or sudden heavy downpours during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because it might be a false start and the heat will destroy your seeds. Wait until the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days after regular rain starts before sowing your maize.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ ebaafee amale shishijee ni latsaa lɛ baagbe odumɔwui lɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ koni okɛdu ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from bigger plants like plantain or cassava. Without shade, direct sunlight scorches the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and fall off to protect the plant from losing water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo cassava adɛŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava grow lots of green leaves instead of feeding the underground roots. Using manure or fertilizer rich in potassium helps the plant direct its energy into growing big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat. Protecting young plants and controlling sucking insects stops these viruses from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Tsei bibii ahe ni obuɔ kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ haaa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good because beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally nourishes the maize and helps both crops produce better yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight, air, and soil water, making them weak. Proper spacing allows air to flow through, which prevents fungal diseases and gives each plant room to bear heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ehaa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu woɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds take the soil food, your crops starve and cannot make enough energy in their leaves, causing them to turn pale.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi ba koni amɛbaye niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni tsuɔ

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to save water and keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Abɛi haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai ni efoɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔlɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I pluck off the first set of flowers on my young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing the first flowers forces the young plant to spend its energy building strong roots and stems first. Once the plant is bigger and stronger, it will produce many more healthy flowers and larger peppers.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso bibioo lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni ehe wa lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why can't I just take seeds from the maize I harvested last season and plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested high-yield hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation, leading to smaller harvests and weaker plants. Using fresh certified seeds every season guarantees strong plants and better yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa be lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle direct heat. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living cover that protects the young cocoa trees from drying out under intense sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni yɔɔ wala mli ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the primary nutrient maize needs to stay green and build big cobs. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot every year lead to smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Growing maize on the same soil every season continuously drains the exact same nutrients without giving the soil time to recover. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the land and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efo tso helai lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause waterlogging without proper drainage, water displaces the oxygen in the soil, allowing rot-causing organisms to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make the food required to grow big underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi baai helai anaa.

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when weather temperatures get extremely hot or when watering is inconsistent. High heat stresses the plant, forcing it to shed flowers to conserve water and survive rather than setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stunt the plant's growth?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying mild soap-and-water solutions helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How do I know which suckers to cut away from my main plantain tree to get larger fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmeii ni esa akɛ mafo dumɔwu titri lɛ mli koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: A plantain mother plant shares food and water with every shoot growing around its base. Leaving only one main stem and one strong follower shoot directs maximum nutrients into producing a single, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Mae Kla tso lɛ kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ jaa niyenii kɛ nu. Tsobii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni baaha aná plantains kuu kome ni tsii.

english: How does spreading dry grass and leaves around the base of my crops help them during dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct heat, keeps the soil cool, and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni egbi woɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akaho oya

english: When is the safest time to apply fertilizer so that rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already damp after a light rain or early in the morning before gentle watering. Applying fertilizer right before heavy rain causes the nutrients to wash off the farm before roots can absorb them.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Aloo leebi dani okɛ nu awo mli fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and dry out quickly. Leaving taller shade trees creates a cool umbrella that protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crops turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to grow green. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe baai lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the vines on my yam farm need wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and air, which leads to much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ kɛ yitso ni da kwraa baa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell before the continuous rains begin. Planting too early can cause delicate seedlings to dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be Dumɔ mra tsɔ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I leave them past maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji miha amɛdara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers reach full maturity, heavy soil moisture causes them to absorb too much water, inviting soil fungi and bacteria that cause the roots to soften and rot.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha amɛŋɔ nu babaoo. Efɔ̃ɔ sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ nine.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that drain sap from leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents severe leaf damage and plant stunting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ waa kɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant lacks sufficient moisture or when tiny pollinating insects are absent. Maintaining moisture through mulch and shade helps keep flowers on the tree to turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up maize pests. Rotating with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa abɛi amli. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the seeds I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from crowding out your crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Okɛ ohe aaawo mli mra Ebaatsi otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my mature tomato fruits crack open right on the plant before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ tso lɛ shishi dani mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split open when they receive a sudden surge of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack.
ga: Tomatoi baatswa kɛji amɛná nu ni fa trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds, pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and air, and spraying approved fungicides can save your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. weeding Afolɔ tsei ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: What makes the stems of my cocoa trees swell up and the leaves turn yellow with red veins?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo lɛ tsei lɛ miifu ni baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD), which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Affected trees produce fewer pods and eventually die, so infected trees must be removed to protect the healthy ones on your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (CSSVD) he okadi, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baaná ŋmeii fioo ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni abu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: What are these tiny bugs making dark spots on my cocoa stems, and how do I protect my farm from them?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: These are likely mirids, also known as capsids. They suck sap from cocoa shoots and pods, causing the branches to dry out. Spraying recommended insecticides at the right time of year keeps their population down.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji myrids, ni ale amɛ hu akɛ capsids. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. dry the branches Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ baaha gbɔmɛi ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Is it better to clear all big trees off my land or leave some when planting cocoa?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mashi ekomɛi kɛ́ midu kookoo?

english: You should leave some large trees for shade. Cocoa plants naturally prefer partial shade, which protects young leaves from strong sunlight, keeps the soil moist, and prevents heat stress.
ga: Esa akɛ ashi tsei wuji koni amɛná hulutsoo. Taakɛ eji lɛ, kookoo tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he

english: How far apart should I plant my new cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa seedlings are best planted 3 meters by 3 meters apart (about 10 feet by 10 feet). Proper spacing ensures every tree gets enough light, water, and nutrients without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10 kɛ ninetalɔi 10) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce many flowers, but very few of them actually grow into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Many flowers drop off naturally because the tree cannot support all of them, or because tiny insects damage the flowers. Good soil nutrition, proper pruning, and pest management help more flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ hewɔ. proper pruning Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer for my cocoa trees to produce well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo kookoo tsei kpakpai?

english: If your trees grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves, or produce very small pods, the soil may lack nutrients like nitrogen or potassium. Applying cocoa-specific fertilizer at the start of the rainy season boosts growth and yield.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔ kookoo he lɛ wo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adaramɔ kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad to leave ripe cocoa pods hanging on the tree for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to germinate or rot, reducing their quality. It also attracts insects and fungal diseases that can spread to nearby healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi Egbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ hu.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves wilt and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds remove moisture from the soil and air, forcing cocoa trees to drop leaves to save water. Planting permanent shade trees and leaving organic mulch around the tree roots helps hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe. Tso shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do weeds harm my young cocoa trees more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ awui fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow rapidly in the rain and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young cocoa trees. Regular weeding keeps the soil nutrients available for your cocoa and removes hiding spots for pests.
ga: Jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ mli ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛhaa o-cocoa lɛ, ni ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: How do I know if the sandy soil on my land is good for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Sandy soil drains water very quickly and loses nutrients easily. While crops like cassava or sweet potatoes can tolerate lighter soils, adding organic matter like compost or animal manure helps sandy soil retain moisture and nutrients so vegetables and maize can grow better.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ oya waa ni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ oya. Dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmei loo atomo baanyɛ akpɛlɛ shikpɔŋ ni su yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ, moŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli. Koni aduawai kɛ ŋmãa akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: What can I do if my farmland soil gets too hard and baked by the sun for seeds to sprout?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃?

english: Hard soil stops plant roots from spreading and prevents water from soaking in. You can loosen hard soil by tilling it and spreading organic compost or mulching with dry crop leaves, which keeps the ground soft, cool, and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa haa tsei ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaaa, ni ehaaa nu abote mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsu he nii ni okɛ organic compost loo tso baai ni egbi ni oookɛwo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, edɔɔ, ni edɔɔ.

english: How does adding dried leaves and animal dung into my land help my crops produce more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfataa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Dried leaves and animal dung break down into organic matter, acting like a natural sponge that traps rain water in the soil and slowly releases essential food nutrients to your crops throughout the growing season.
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hot middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves tightly as a natural defense to reduce water loss through evaporation when the sun is hot. It is a signal that the plant is under water stress and would benefit from soil mulching to keep moisture in the ground.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi, ni ebaaná he sɛɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ mulching wo nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning yellow while the top ones are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish new growth at the top, which means you need to add nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost to your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ afata oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very big and leafy but fail to produce flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of setting flowers. Using balanced nutrients with more phosphorus helps the plants switch from growing leaves to producing abundant fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ fɔfɔii anɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja babaoo kɛ fɔsfɔs babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ amli kɛyaa aduawai babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds on my farm grow much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to local soils and harsh weather conditions in Ghana. Because they steal water, light, and nutrients quickly, clearing them early gives your cultivated crops the space they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aná he ko ni he hiaa lɛ koni eda.

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close, their roots compete heavily with each other underground for nutrients and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Which food crops are best to plant on my farm when the rainy season is short?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa akɛ adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli?

english: Fast-maturing crops like cowpeas, millet, sorghum, and early-maturing maize varieties are best for short rainy seasons. They require less total rainfall and finish producing food before the dry weather arrives.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kwraa lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛgbe niyenii feemɔ naa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers encourage farmers to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food, naturally fertilizing the neighboring maize crop while protecting the soil from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ sũ lɛ he koni nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa lɛ akahole lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop even matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient they need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't rot on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Bɔni afee ni akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the green husks turn dry and brown like paper, and the silks at the top turn dark brown. You can also press a grain with your thumbnail; if no milky juice comes out, it is mature.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ wolo. ni siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ oshishifã lɛ hu anyɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji mliki ko ejeee kpo lɛ, no lɛ ahoo.

english: Why do caterpillars keep eating the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hide in the cool, moist center roll of young maize leaves because it protects them from the sun while giving them soft, tender leaves to eat.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ ateŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa amɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ hu.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden heat stress combined with dry soil. The plant drops the flowers to save its own energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fata he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to turn black and soft at the bottom while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil goes from very dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes soften and rot so quickly before buyers arrive at my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya dani mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baashɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if harvested in the hot sun or packed tightly in deep wooden crates, which crushes the fruits at the bottom and generates heat that speeds up spoilage.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ ni haa efiteɔ oya lɛ baa.

english: Why is my okra growing very tall with large leaves, but producing very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi okra ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much manure or nitrogen fertilizer makes the okra plant put all its energy into growing tall stems and big leaves instead of flowering and producing pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ehaa okra tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods baa lɛ

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and tough to cut when I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ abaakpa kɛji mikɛto lɛ?

english: Okra pods grow very quickly and become woody if left on the plant too long. You should harvest them every two to three days while they are still small, tender, and snap easily off the stem.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Esa akɛ okpa gbii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ be mli ni eji bibioo lolo, ni eyɛ blɛoo ni ejɛɔ tso lɛ shishi oya.

english: Is it safe for me to plant maize and okra on the same bed together?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ okra yɛ saatso kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and okra together works well because maize grows tall and upright while okra branches out lower, allowing both crops to share sunlight and soil nutrients without crowding each other out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ okra ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa ni ekwɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni okra niji lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ jaa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Why does the soil around my crops dry up so fast during the dry season even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ?

english: Direct sunlight bakes bare soil and makes water evaporate into the air quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ kpo ni eha nu lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft stems and shallow roots that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees planted alongside young cocoa provide shade and keep moisture in the soil, helping the young cocoa plants survive until their canopy develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmei ko baa.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking due to the expanding tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin without producing big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɛɛ toi wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and light to grow strong stems and produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ dumɔwui akutsei lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants and feed on them, but early application of recommended insecticides or neem extract can effectively control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing. Applying it about two to three weeks after seedlings sprout—and again when flowers start forming—helps the roots absorb the nutrients easily.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ tsofa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal water and food from the main mother plant. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough nutrients to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil damp with mulch and applying balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛkɛduɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni akɛtsi foliar helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and getting dark spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high dampness that encourages fungal diseases like blight to spread on tomato leaves. Mulching the soil prevents mud from splashing onto the leaves, and spraying approved fungicides protects them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa tomato baai anɔ. Mulching baatsi muji ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves on the soil surface is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under hot sunshine, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and breaks down into natural compost over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: That damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the young leaves (the whorl) of maize plants and feeds on them, which can severely reduce crop yield if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii (rings) amli ni eyeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which usually happens when the soil lacks enough calcium or when the soil moisture changes too drastically between dry and wet conditions.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves are a common sign that your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their green color and helps them grow big leaves.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai wuji.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is weak without paying for a expensive test?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni miwooo kaai ni jara wa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: You can spot weak soil if your crops look stunted, turn yellowish early, or if wild weeds grow very thin and weak on the land compared to nearby fertile areas.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya Aloo kɛji koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a open field with full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun; they require shade from crops like plantains or temporary shade trees during their first two years to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Removing excess suckers ensures that water and soil nutrients are concentrated on the main plant stem, allowing it to produce a larger, healthier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ plantains akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting them in the field?
ga: Kɛji oodu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, teŋ jɛkɛmɔ enyiɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋmei niji lɛ ateŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should generally be spaced about 1 meter apart from each other so the roots have plenty of space underground to expand into large tubers.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the leaves to generate more food energy that goes straight into swelling the tuber below ground.
ga: Staking baaye abua ni ewó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo. ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ fũuɔ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing naturally nearby?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil food away from your crops, effectively starving your plants and providing a hiding spot for destructive pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni eha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aná he ko ni amɛhi.

english: How do I know if it is safe to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until two or three steady rains have fallen so that the soil holds enough deep moisture to sustain the germinating seeds if a short dry period follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer for hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during extreme heat to protect themselves and reduce the amount of water escaping from their leaves into the dry air.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato blossoms, which prevents the flowers from forming fruit and causes them to drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the soil when the rainy season is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots, allowing water rot and soil fungi to destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpataa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear and spread quickly on my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The heavy rains and damp air create the perfect conditions for a fungus to grow and spread Black Pod disease across your cocoa trees.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baaha ŋmei lɛ adara ni egbɛ black pod hela lɛ eshwa o-cocoa tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs if I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak even after I apply chemical fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ewo ŋmɔji lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer and water out of the soil before your main crops have a chance to drink them in.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ náa hegbɛ enuɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield less than the certified seeds I buy from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases, whereas certified seeds are specially bred to resist pests and produce higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting buds in the barn before it is time to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout early when stored in warm or humid conditions because the heat signals to the tuber that it is time to wake up and grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo he ko ni mli edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛdu wain tsei heei.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when I leave them under the hot sun before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and generate heat. Direct sunlight speeds up water loss and bacterial growth, causing tomatoes to soften and rot rapidly, whereas keeping them in a cool, shaded place slows down this decay.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni helatsɛmɛi amli helai hu daa. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tomato to he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha efitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How can I keep my harvested leafy vegetables fresh when transporting them to distant markets like Accra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni akpa lɛ ahi shi ehee beni mikɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tamɔ Accra lɛ?

english: Leafy greens lose water rapidly after being cut. Keeping them moist, packing them loosely in ventilated crates, and covering them with cool, damp cloths slows down water loss and keeps them crisp during long journeys.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji afo amɛ. keeping hydrated loosely packed Yɛ adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli Ni okɛ mama ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ aha nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee mlɛo, ni ebaaha ohe ajɔ bo yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and rotting within just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a protective skin, so oxygen enters cuts made during harvesting and triggers rapid internal deterioration. Processing or keeping them cool immediately after harvest delays this spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli ni ehaa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya. Nibii ni atsuɔ he nii loo ni akɛtoɔ fɛ̃i mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How do I prevent my delicate crops like garden eggs and ripe peppers from getting crushed during long-distance transport?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ amɛ yaa he ko shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Overpacking produce in soft sacks causes heavy pressure that crushes delicate items at the bottom. Using rigid, stackable plastic crates distributes weight evenly and prevents bruising during long journeys.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ blɛoo amli fe nine lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa baa nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Plastic adekai ni wa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ jaa pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits split open on the farm right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelon skin splits when the plant absorbs a sudden surplus of water after a dry period, causing the inner flesh to expand much faster than the outer rind can stretch.
ga: Watermelon hewolo lɛ mli gbalaa kɛji tso lɛ ŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa loo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a natural protection mechanism where the plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from its tissues.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ ji koni nu akajɛ fãji lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn yellow and dry up when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi beni amɛji gbekɛbii bibii lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt, a natural self-thinning response where the cocoa tree drops extra young pods it cannot support due to water stress, nutrient shortages, or excessive sunlight exposure.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherelle wilt, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni nyɛɛɛ aye abua amɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ lɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo

english: Why do buyers pay more for certain varieties of maize over others in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer specific maize varieties based on their end use, such as grain hardness for long storage, resistance to weevils, or high starch content for local food preparation like kenkey and banku.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ abele henɔi pɔtɛɛ ni damɔ amɛ naagbee nitsumɔ nɔ, tamɔ ŋmaa ni wa kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ. Moth nyɛɔ eshiɔ loo eyɛ starch babaoo ni akɛsaa maŋ niyenii tamɔ kenkey kɛ banku.

english: Why do some of my stored maize grains get attacked by weevils while others stay clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ ekomɛi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu he tseɔ lɛ?

english: Maize varieties with tight, long husk covers naturally protect the cob from insects in the field, whereas open-husk varieties allow pests and moisture to enter much faster.
ga: Abele henɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi ni buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi ni agbele naa lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli oya babaoo.

english: Why do my okra plants produce plenty of flowers but very few actual okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi okra ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Okra flowers require insect pollinators like bees to set fruit, and using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow leaves instead of holding onto its fruit pods.
ga: Rosella biɔ nibii ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛwo yibii, ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ atsɔ baai moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out the soil around their roots. Keeping taller trees or planting plantains around them creates shade and holds moisture in the ground.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛdara loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to keep leaves green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plants green up and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When maize grows near groundnuts, it feeds on this extra nitrogen, naturally enriching the soil.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop rows with dry leaves or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni gboi loo tsei ahe tsei aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow easily, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot days.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi hulu la lɛ naa. Ehaa jwɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving plants proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough food and space to thrive.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots deteriorate rapidly within 2 to 3 days of harvesting because injuries during digging allow air inside, triggering natural spoilage. It is best to leave cassava in the soil until you are ready to use or sell it.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ pilamɔi ni baa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. kɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ baa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii loo okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture as much sunlight as possible. Exposure to light helps the leaves create energy, which flows down to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. La ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to preserve water and stay alive. Regular watering and mulching around the plant base lowers soil temperature and helps hold flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my tomatoes turn black and rotten before the fruit ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black tips on tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which occurs when roots cannot draw enough calcium from dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows steady calcium uptake.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni calcium lɛ shwereɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are fall armyworms, pests that lay eggs on young leaves. The larvae crawl into the growing tip of the maize to feed, which damages future growth if not managed early.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Lala lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ najiaŋ koni amɛyaye nii. Enɛ fiteɔ wɔsɛɛ be mli dalɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is yielding less because the trees are old or because they are sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo yibii fioo ejaakɛ tsei lɛ egbɔ loo hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Old trees gradually reduce their yields over many years, whereas a disease usually causes a sudden, dramatic drop in harvest or visible damage like dying leaves, swollen stems, or rotten pods regardless of the tree's age.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baafee fiofio Nibii ni anáa lɛ eba shi yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ hela haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi trukaa loo efiteɔ nibii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni miigboi, tsei ni efuu, loo tsei ni fiteɔ, ekɔɔɔ afii ni tso lɛ eye lɛ he.

english: Can very young cocoa trees also catch severe diseases, or do diseases only attack old trees?
ga: Ani helai ni naa wa baanyɛ amɔ kookoo tsei bibii waa lɛ? Aloo tsei ni egbɔ pɛ hela lɛ baatutua amɛ?

english: Diseases do not care about the age of the crop; even young trees that are only 2 or 3 years old can catch viral or fungal diseases if they are exposed to infected nearby plants or insect pests.
ga: Helai susuuu afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye lɛ he. Tsei bibii ni eye afii 2 loo 3 pɛ lɛ po baanyɛ aná helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai amli kɛji amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kpe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods even when they still look tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ ekpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni ekwɛɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Certain diseases attack the reproductive parts or inner vessels of the tree, stopping fruit formation and pod growth long before the tree actually dies or loses its leaves.
ga: Helai komɛi tutuaa tso lɛ fɔmɔ hei loo lá fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai kɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kpaa dani tso lɛ gboɔ diɛŋtsɛ loo ebaa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If one cocoa tree on my farm gets sick, should I cut it down immediately to protect the others?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni mabu tsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe?

english: For incurable viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, removing the infected tree along with neighboring trees is necessary because insects can easily carry the disease to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Kɛha helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni anyɛɛɛ atsa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii baanyɛ amɛkɛ helai aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Will applying more fertilizer cure my cocoa trees if they have a disease?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baahere kookoo tso lɛ yiwala kɛji hela yɛ enɔ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food to help healthy plants grow, but it cannot destroy viruses or fungi; using fertilizer on a diseased tree will not cure the infection and cannot restore your lost yield.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa. Shi enyɛŋ efite helai loo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ, etsaŋ hela lɛ, ni ebaahaa nibii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How long can a healthy cocoa tree continue to produce good yields?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kpakpai?

english: With good soil care, proper shade, and protection from pests and diseases, a cocoa tree can remain productive for 25 to 30 years or more.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛhaa hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe lɛ nɔ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: How many years after planting should I expect my young cocoa trees to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, provided they receive adequate water, light shade, and disease protection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛná nu, hulutsoo, kɛ helai ahebuu ni sa.

english: How can I tell when it is time to cut down my old farm and plant new cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni madu kookoo tsei heei?

english: When trees are around 30 years old and harvest yields remain consistently low despite good weed control and weather, the farm is aging out and should be cut down and replanted with improved seed varieties.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ eye aaafee afii 30 ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be yɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai fɛɛ sɛɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ hu miigbɔ ni esa akɛ afo mli ni akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How do plant diseases move from one cocoa farm to another in our village?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread across farms through airborne fungal spores, insects like mealybugs that carry viruses, unwashed pruning tools used on infected plants, or movement of infected pod husks.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni ji ŋmeii tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛ hela lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo pod shells ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ

english: What causes the leaves on cocoa trees to turn yellow and fall off before harvest season?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa?

english: Early leaf drop is often caused by sap-sucking pests, root diseases, or viral infections that cut off nutrient supply, rather than natural leaf shedding.
