ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ, shishifãi ahe hela, loo hela ko ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli ni fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ mra. fe adebɔɔ mli baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: What does cocoa rehabilitation actually mean, and why should I cut down my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo ni anáa lɛ tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei momoi lɛ?

english: Cocoa rehabilitation means replacing old, diseased, or unproductive cocoa trees with healthy new seedlings. Old trees yield very few pods and spread diseases, so removing them helps clear the farm so fresh, high-yielding cocoa trees can grow.
ga: Cocoa sɛɛkuu tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baatsake cocoa tsei ni egbɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akwɛ kookoo tsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade plants like plantains nearby to shield them from heat stress until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the stems on some of my cocoa trees swelling and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees stop producing pods and will eventually die, so they must be cut out to protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baakpa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ koni akɛbu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Removing infected pods and pruning the farm to let in air helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni afolɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Pruning removes unnecessary, weak, or dead branches so the tree can send its energy directly into growing strong cocoa pods. It also lets light and air pass through, keeping pests away.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni he ehiaaa, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo ni egboi lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ awo kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin trees that produce very few pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree lacks water or soil nutrients, or if beneficial insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping the soil healthy and managing pests helps more flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yes, planting plantain with young cocoa is recommended because the plantains provide vital shade for the cocoa while giving your family food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu plantains kɛ kookoo bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains haa kookoo lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: The best time to plant cocoa in Ghana is at the beginning of the major rainy season, around May or June. This gives the young plants plenty of water to establish deep roots before the dry season comes.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ kookoo yɛ Ghana ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Aaafee May loo June mli Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu babaoo koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How do I know if my farm's soil lacks the right nutrients for cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha kookoo?

english: If your cocoa trees grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produce very small pods, the soil is likely low in nutrients and may need fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa tso lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ. aloo amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii hu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees or food crops like plantains protect young cocoa from harsh sun and keep the soil moist so the roots can grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots compete for soil food and water, and their tops block sunlight from each other, resulting in skinny trees that bear very few pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni kookoo tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa branches turning dry and brown like they were burnt by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by tiny pests called mirids or capsids that bite the stems and suck out the plant's sap. Protecting the trees with proper pest control prevents this drying effect.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids, ni amɛkɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli baa lɛ naa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which thrives in wet and humid conditions. Keeping the farm clear of heavy weeds and trimming thick foliage lets airflow in to dry out the pods.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Kɛ́ jwɛi babaoo bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ baai ni mli tse ni afolɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Why is a different kind of green plant growing directly on my cocoa tree branches and causing them to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miida yɛ mi-kokoo niji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmiiha kookoo tso lɛ miigbi lɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that attaches itself to cocoa branches and steals water and nutrients directly from the tree. Removing these green parasites regularly keeps the cocoa tree strong.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: A cocoa tree has limited energy. Removing non-producing or overgrown branches ensures that the food the tree makes goes directly into producing big, healthy cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ he. Niji ni wooo yibii loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni tso lɛ feɔ lɛ yaa koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees give me fewer pods now than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past twenty years, their stems become weak and produce fewer pods naturally. Heavy pruning or grafting new shoots onto old trunks can help old trees regain their productivity.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye fe afii 20 lɛ, eshishifã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ekɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ. Tso momo lɛ he tsei ni afolɔ waa loo ni akɛwoɔ tsei heei amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso momo lɛ ni ená yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do many tiny flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo babaoo ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen so pods can form. Keeping organic leaf litter on the farm floor gives these beneficial insects a place to live and multiply.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen yaa koni efee pods. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni abua naa yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are hungry for plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye kookoo tso ko kɛha tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If cocoa leaves turn pale yellow instead of deep green, or if the tree produces very few, small pods, the soil lacks nutrients and needs cocoa-specific fertilizer to restore growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo, kɛji tso lɛ woɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo ko lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko awo mli koni ekɛha ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my cocoa trees grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa plants. Clearing weeds regularly allows cocoa roots to absorb all available food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my field's soil turn hard like stone after it rains and dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbiɔ lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil lacks organic matter like compost or dead leaves. Adding animal manure or decomposed plant matter improves soil structure, helping it retain moisture and preventing it from baking into a hard crust under the sun.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo tsei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa etsɔ ŋmei ni wa yɛ hulu la shishi.

english: Why do we make high soil mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: High mounds create loose, deep soil that allows yam tubers to expand easily into large, healthy roots. Mounds also keep water from pooling around the tubers, which prevents them from rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ shishifãi wuji ni wa. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa egbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of laying them flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni makã shikpɔŋ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanted angle encourages the roots to grow deeper and spread out evenly. This produces bigger roots and gives the plant a stronger anchor so wind cannot knock it over.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa ni ehaa tso lɛ naa shi waa. No hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atswa lɛ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting plantain suckers too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows all of them to grow strong and produce large bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la he. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tsei ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo jwɛi babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I see small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest in Ghana. They hide in the center whorl of the maize plant where leaves are soft. Applying recommended organic or chemical controls early in the morning or late evening targets them effectively.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbaatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatswa amɛ ojo jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that enters through the roots and blocks water transport inside the stem. Rotating your crops with non-vegetables like maize helps clear the disease from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni efiteɔ nu ni akɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni jeee aduawai tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does allowing weeds to grow around my crops reduce my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha mi naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aba shi tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. They also harbor destructive insects and diseases, which weaken your main crops and reduce the total amount of food they produce.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai hu jɛɛhe. Enɛ haa onibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni amɛha niyenii fɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants face heat stress, extreme dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Supplying adequate water during dry periods and feeding the plants balanced nutrients helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do rice plants require so much standing water compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa tsei kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally suited for flooded conditions, which help protect them from competing weeds and provide a steady supply of moisture required to fill out high-yielding grain heads.
ga: Omɔ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ titri. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ahe. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛwo dumɔwui ayitsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why are some of my crops ready for harvest while others on the exact same plot are just starting to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ekomɛi eshɛ nikpamɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: Uneven growth usually happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when soil nutrients are uneven across the field, or when mixed seed varieties are used. Ensuring equal planting depth and using single-variety certified seeds helps crops grow at the same pace.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi. Be mli ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo be mli ni akɛ dumɔwui ni efutu miitsu nii Kwɛmɔ ni adu lɛ mlibotemɔ kome kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ srɔto kome ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ adara yɛ oyaiyeli kome mli.

english: How can I get all my crops to mature at the same time so I can harvest everything once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli koni manyɛ makpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome?

english: To get a uniform harvest, buy certified seeds of a single variety, plant them on the same day at uniform depth and spacing, and distribute fertilizer evenly across the entire field.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná ŋmaa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ Hemɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi kome ni awo he odaseyeli pɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ gbi kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ kɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ ekome. ni amɛgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amɛshwã hei fɛɛ

english: Why do some plants on my farm take longer to flower while neighboring plants right next to them are already fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ? Ani eewo yibii momo?

english: Differences in localized soil moisture, shade from nearby trees, or slight variations in seed quality can cause neighboring plants to enter their flowering stage at different times.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ Shade ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli loo dumɔwui ahe su ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ abote fɔfɔii afeemɔ mli yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why is harvesting my field in stages costing me so much more money than harvesting all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli lɛ heɔ mi shika babaoo fe ni akpa amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Staggered harvesting forces you to hire and pay laborers multiple times over weeks or months instead of paying for one quick operation, which increases your total spending on food, wages, and transportation.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ onɔ ni oŋɔ nitsulɔi ni owo amɛ nyɔmɔ shii abɔ yɛ otsii loo nyɔji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo oyaiyeli opireshɛn kome pɛ he nyɔmɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shika fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ yɛ niyenii, nyɔmɔwoo, kɛ gbɛfaa he lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does harvesting my crop selectively take up so much more time and physical effort?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akpamɔ biɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Selective harvesting requires workers to walk through the entire farm searching for mature plants while taking care not to crush or damage the younger plants still growing around them.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni ahalaa lɛ biɔ ni nitsulɔi anyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛyatao tsei ni edara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsei bibii ni miida lolo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ akafite loo okafite.

english: Why does an extended harvest period increase my risk of getting into farm debt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo he oshara lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: A long, drawn-out harvest spreads your income into small, irregular amounts, while forcing you to spend money continuously on daily labor and farm care without receiving a single large payout to settle your main expenses.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baagbɛ oshika ni onáa lɛ eshwa shika bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, enyɛɔ onɔ koni oya nɔ okɛ shika atsu daa gbi nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ he nii ni onine shɛɛɛ shika babaoo kome po nɔ ni okɛwoɔ shika titri ni ofiteɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Why do buyers offer me lower prices when my crops mature in small batches instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee fɛɛ shikome

english: Produce buyers and market women prefer purchasing large bulk quantities to save on their transport costs. When you can only sell small quantities at a time, your bargaining power drops.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi ni feɔ nibii kɛ jarayeli yei sumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii babaoo koni amɛkɛ shika ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ akafite. Be mli ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ shika fioo pɛ yɛ be kome mli Ohewalɛ ni okɛbaajara nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from my own harvest give me uneven growth compared to buying new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa midalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ he lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their genetic purity and vigor over time and may carry hidden diseases. Certified seeds are specially produced under strict conditions to guarantee high, uniform growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa shishi koni ekɛha amɛdalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops perform so well on a nursery or seed plot but struggle once planted out in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ shi amɛnaa amanehulu kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seed plots and nurseries provide ideal shelter, rich soil, and careful watering. In the main field, plants face harsh direct sun, tougher soil, and competition from weeds and pests, which tests their strength.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei kɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ji hei ni sa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni naa wa waa. shikpɔŋ ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi awuiyelɔi adɛŋ. ni ji amɛhewalɛ he kaa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds that look healthy in the bag give weak or patchy crops after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ kotoku mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds can look fine on the outside but still have low germination power if they were stored in hot conditions, are too old, or carry seed-borne diseases that only express themselves after absorbing moisture in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ afee fɛo kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo mli ni edɔ tsɔ, amɛgbɔ tsɔ, loo amɛyɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa ni jieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ be mli ni amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are very tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates a canopy that shields the cocoa from heat and keeps the soil moist until the trees are old enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ darako kwraa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the plant will help restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he lɛ he. Tsei baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw water out of plant tissues, which can burn or kill the stem and roots if touched directly. Placing the fertilizer in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients through the soil.
ga: Nuŋtɛi ni mli eyi obɔ ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. ni baanyɛ ashã loo efite tsei ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ ŋwɛibɔfoi bibii amli Loo okɛwo tso lɛ he inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight balls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids that feed on the sap beneath the leaves. Spraying the plants early with neem oil or a recommended insecticidal soap gets rid of these pests and lets new, healthy leaves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ tsei anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Fall Armyworms leave small ragged holes in the leaves and leave behind tiny light-brown droppings that look like sawdust inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early when the holes first appear makes them much easier to control.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ shĩɔ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso teŋgbɛ Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Beni bu lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ewaaa kwraa akɛ abaakwɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly, which stresses the plant. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long and starves the roots of air. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers safe and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha yitso lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni egbi.

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil, causing them to temporarily droop. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will bounce back once the afternoon sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ be mli ni shwane hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the ground, fertilizing the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do tiny black insects eat up my harvested maize grains while stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miiye mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils, and they multiply rapidly if maize is put into storage while it still contains too much moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until the kernels are hard before bagging them stops weevils from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii. Ni amɛbaafa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to be mli ni edɔ tsɔ lolo lɛ. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plant turn yellow and die while the cob is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: The plant prioritizes its growing cob over its older leaves. When food or water is limited, the plant naturally pulls stored nutrients out of its lower leaves and sends them straight to the cob, causing the old leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Tso lɛ sumɔɔ cob dalɛ fe baai ni egbɔ. Kɛ niyenii loo nu faaa lɛ Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. ni akɛmajeɔ ŋmei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy green leaves and branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves consume a lot of the food that the plant makes. By trimming extra leaves, you stop the plant from wasting energy on foliage and force it to direct all its food into growing bigger and heavier tomato fruits.
ga: Baai yeɔ niyenii ni tsei woɔ lɛ babaoo. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ anyɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye amɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tomato lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my cassava tubers to stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients and light. They take up the food in the soil first, leaving very little energy for your cassava plant to store underground in its tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eha o-cassava tso lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are young pods dropping off my cocoa tree before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree will automatically shed young pods if it realizes it does not have enough food or water to feed all of them. It drops a few pods so it can save enough energy to fully grow the remaining ones.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe kɛji niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Ekɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi shwie shi bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara kwraa.

english: If I plant my yam mounds very close together, won't I get more harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces the yams to fight one another for limited sunlight and soil nutrients. Because each plant receives less food, you will end up with many tiny, weak tubers instead of large, high-value yams.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ awuu yɛ amɛteŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii fioo nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, obaagbe naa kɛ bulb bibii babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ji ngma agbo nɛ e he jua wa wawɛɛ.

english: How do the green leaves on my crop actually feed the plant to make tubers and fruits grow?
ga: Te baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii koni bulbs kɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Leaves act like small kitchens for the plant. They take in sunlight, air, and water brought up by the roots to make food, which is then sent through the stem to feed growing fruits, seeds, and underground tubers.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso lɛ shĩa bibioo lɛ. Amɛheɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ jieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Atsuɔ amɛ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi koni amɛyaye aduawai, dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the hot, dry season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: During extreme heat, the plant goes into survival mode. It drops its flowers to save its limited water and nutrients for keeping the main stem and roots alive instead of spending energy on new peppers.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaya wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ nɔ. Akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ akahi shi. Koni akɛbu tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii heei ahe lɛ

english: Why is it important to feed my crop fertilizer early before it begins to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ? Ehe miihia dani amɛfɔ̃.

english: Crops need to build strong roots and healthy leaves early so they can manufacture plenty of food. If the plant is well-fed early on, it will have enough stored energy ready to nourish big flowers and heavy fruits.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ niyenii babaoo aba Kɛji onine shɛ niyenii kpakpa nɔ mra Hewalɛ ni abua naa ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi wuji kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know that my groundnut crop has finished feeding and is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanut tsei lɛ egbe niyenii naa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: When the leaves start turning yellow and drying up, the plant has stopped making new food and has sent all remaining energy down into the nuts, signaling that the crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii hee feemɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eda ni esa kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths drawing food away from the main mother plant. Removing them ensures all the nutrients flow into the main stem so it can produce a full, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ fãi krokomɛi, ni amɛgbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni aná plantains ni eyi obɔ ni tsii

english: How do I test if my maize seeds are healthy enough to sprout before I plant them on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can test your seeds by placing a small sample, like 10 seeds, in a wet cloth for three to four days. If eight or nine of them sprout shoots, your seeds are healthy and good for field planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii kpaanyɔ loo nɛɛhu kwɛ̃ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ehi kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why are my seeds failing to sprout even after rain has fallen on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the soil, damaged by storage pests, or if the soil became flooded with water and suffocated the seed.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ efite Aloo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I prevent ants and birds from eating my corn seeds right after I put them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ okpoi anaa koni amɛkaye mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can treat your dried maize seeds with approved protective seed-dressing powders before planting. The smell and taste keep insects and birds away while the seed is sprouting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ahe tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ahe nii dani okɛdu. Ehe muji kɛ ehiɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ haa kooloi kɛ okpoi kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do people say that starting a new cocoa farm takes much more effort than other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishijee biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and need constant care for several years. You have to provide shade, clear weeds regularly, protect them from harsh sun, and shield them from pests before they start producing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ daa afii babaoo. Esa akɛ okɛ hulutsoo aha. Tsumɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe daa. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe dani amɛje ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ shishi.

english: Why do I need to prepare shade on my field before transplanting my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo dani mawo kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantain or leaving selected forest trees keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the seedlings survive their early years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo ashi koo mli tsei ni ahala lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my trees shriveling up and turning black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by cherelle wilt, where the cocoa tree naturally sheds extra young pods it cannot feed due to dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cherelle lɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ, ni anyɛɛɛ atsu he nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ni miigba onaa.

english: What basic steps should I follow when preparing land for a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: You need to clear unwanted brush while saving good shade trees, mark out straight rows with proper distance between holes, and ensure the soil is loosened so the roots can spread easily.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei bibii ni ataooo lɛ yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ hulutsoo. Kadimɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja kɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ bu lɛ teŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Is it better to plant my corn in straight rows or scatter the seeds like my elders used to do?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli loo ooofɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ofeɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows with measured spacing gives every corn plant enough light, air, and water, while making it much easier for you to weed and apply fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni asusuɔ he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa náa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves need. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure will give the corn its green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei taoɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant corn inside my young cocoa farm, or will the corn spoil the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli? Aloo ŋmãa lɛ baaha kookoo lɛ afite?

english: You can plant corn between young cocoa trees in the first season because the tall corn gives temporary shade. However, you must keep enough distance so the corn does not steal water and food from the cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ kookoo lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I put double the fertilizer on my maize to make it grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe shii enyɔ woɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ oya lɛ?

english: Applying extra fertilizer to rush growth can burn the crop's roots and ruin the soil. Crops need steady, gradual nutrients to grow strong stalks and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he koni eha amɛdara lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei he miihia ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yaa nɔ fiofio koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to harvest my cassava early just because I want quick cash?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaakpa ŋmei mra kɛha oyaiyeli shika kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting cassava before it fully matures results in small, watery roots with low starch content. Waiting for the proper maturation time allows the tubers to swell fully and fetch a much better market price.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii ni nu kɛ ŋmei fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Be ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ koni amɛdara lɛ mɛmɔ baaha bulb lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa ni ekɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba jara nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I force my young cocoa trees to fruit as early as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ minyɛɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ koni amɛwo yibii oya bɔ ni manyɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need time to build a strong root system and sturdy branches first. Rushing early production weakens the tree and reduces the total pods it can produce over its long life.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ. Nibii ni afee lɛ oya kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha tso lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ. ni ehaa pods fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ afee yɛ wala be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I pick off the first flowers on my young pepper plants instead of letting them turn into peppers immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso bibioo ko nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Removing the earliest flowers encourages the young plant to direct its energy into building stronger roots and foliage, which allows it to produce a much larger harvest later.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ fɔfɔi ni jeɔ shishi mra lɛ, ewoɔ tso bibioo lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa kpamɔ babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What goes wrong if I cover my planted seeds hastily with too much soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ oyaiyeli ha midumɔwui ni midu lɛ ahe sũ babaoo?

english: Covering seeds too deeply or unevenly makes it difficult for delicate sprouts to break through to the surface, leading to weak germination or seeds rotting underground.
ga: Kɛ́ ooha dumɔwui ahe tsɔ loo ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Will crowding more crops into my field help me get a bigger harvest quickly?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo oya?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding results in thin, sickly plants that produce smaller overall yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant my crops right away without clearing all the weeds first if I am in a hurry?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji mikɛ oyaiyeli miitsu nii?

english: Leaving weeds in the field when planting means the weeds will steal valuable moisture and nutrients from your young seedlings, causing your crops to be stunted from the very start.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni oduɔ nii lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaaju ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ odumɔwui bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee.

english: If I receive new seed varieties as a gift or grant, should I plant them across my entire farm right away?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ dumɔwui heei anɔ akɛ nikeenii loo shika Ani Esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to be cautious and test new seeds on a small test plot first. This allows you to observe how the variety handles your local soil and weather before risking your main field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ ohe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oka dumɔwui heei okwɛ yɛ kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ daa lɛ. Te otsuɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he nii ohaa tɛŋŋ? Dani okɛ oŋmɔ titri lɛ baawo oshara mli

english: Why shouldn't I pour a large amount of water on my young crops all at once to speed up their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo shwieɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ shikome koni amɛdara oya lɛ?

english: Drowning young plants with heavy watering suffocates the roots and washes away valuable topsoil. Crops grow best with consistent, moderate moisture rather than sudden flooding.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo wo tsei bibii amli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaafɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa, ni mli ejɔ. Yɛ nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why does building healthy soil take time instead of giving an instant result?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni aaama lɛ heɔ be moŋ fe nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil health relies on organic matter breaking down slowly over time. While quick chemical fixes give a brief boost, building rich soil creates long-term fertility that protects your crops during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ damɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ fiofio lɛ anɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii oya lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni afee lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baabu onibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and turn yellow when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like infants—their tender leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts as an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and protecting the young trees from hot sun until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are there small eaten holes all over the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Tiny holes on young maize leaves are typically caused by early attacks from pests like fall armyworms feeding on tender growth. Catching this early is important because if the worms reach the growing center of the plant, the maize stem will stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa mra. Emɔmɔ mra Enɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ shɛ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ, Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ baakpa dalɛ.

english: How can I know if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a tall stem, and small cracks begin appearing in the soil around the base of the plant where expanding tubers are pushing upward.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Tso kakadaŋŋ ashi ni ŋmeii bibii bɔi baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishi, ni yɔɔ yitso ni elɛɛ lɛ, tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow even though it rains regularly on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which provides green leaf color. Heavy rains can wash essential soil nutrients deeper into the ground away from roots, so plants still need added compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe kɛya sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lolo.

english: Why are my plantain bunches small when I let all the small shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the mother plant. Pruning away excess shoots and keeping only one or two stems ensures all the soil food goes into making large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam plants need their leaves lifted high into the sunlight to manufacture the food required to grow big underground tubers. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, protecting them from soil-borne rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ sũ mli nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat waves, uneven watering, or getting too much chemical fertilizer at once. Keeping the soil steadily moist helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be kome mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my green tomato fruits develop flat black spots as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when growing tomatoes do not get enough calcium from the soil. Irregular watering prevents roots from taking up calcium, so keeping soil moisture steady prevents the fruit tips from turning black.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato ni adu lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa amɛná calcium. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my field make the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural helpers in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the legume crop finishes, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as natural fertilizer for maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay alive during long dry spells while my maize dries up and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep taproots that reach far underground to extract hidden groundwater, and it can drop its leaves to save water. Maize has shallow roots and large leaves that lose moisture rapidly into dry air.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifã ko ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ejie shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai ashwie shi koni ekɛhere nu Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season keeps the leaves green and leads to bigger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha ŋmei toi lɛ afee wuji.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same food from the soil and allows specific pests and soil diseases to multiply. Switching your field to beans, groundnuts, or cassava breaks pest cycles and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni amɛshwereɔ. Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni atsakeɔ lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii Efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe.

english: How do plants like cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen fertilizer directly from the air and put it into the ground. When the leaves and roots decay after harvest, they leave natural plant food behind for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a freshly cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbele mli ehee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside your young cocoa creates living shade that cools the seedlings and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cocoa tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need to reach as much sunlight as possible to make food for the plant. Staking holds the leaves high off the hot ground so the plant can use that solar energy to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ nakai hulu hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together make them grow tall and thin with small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kukuji ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and food. Giving plants proper space between rows ensures each plant gets enough light and root space to grow thick, healthy, and high-yielding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃, ewa ni ewo yibii.

english: Excess water trapped in heavy soil cuts off air to the roots, causing cassava tubers to drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ajɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from baking moisture out of the earth. It keeps crop roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛ́ egbo.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking plant sap and passing on a virus. Clearing surrounding weeds and using simple sprays like mild soap solution or neem oil helps keep insects away so leaves stay flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ atsu nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi akaboteɔ jɛmɛ Baai lɛ amli tseɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or a lack of soil food. Watering steadily and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into full pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hao tso lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ ebatsɔ pepper aduawai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right through the center of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide or a natural mix like neem leaf extract early in the morning can stop them before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai nɛɛ akpa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out, or when the plant gets too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil damp with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crops when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Instead of planting on a fixed calendar date, wait until the first heavy rain thoroughly wets the soil deep down. Planting into soil that is still dry causes seeds to dry up and fail.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomato seedlings very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each tomato plant room to breathe, preventing leaf diseases and producing larger fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tomato tso fɛɛ tso muɔ. Tsi baa helai anaa ni oha aduawai lɛ afee agbo.

english: Why do people tell me not to plant maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same place every year uses up the same nutrients and allows crop pests to build up in the soil. Alternating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts goodness back into the ground naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ebaaha ekpakpafeemɔ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer without sending it to a lab?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛmajeee laboratori?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale or yellowish leaves, or give smaller yields than in previous years, your soil is exhausted. Adding compost, animal manure, or inorganic fertilizer will restore those missing nutrients.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ etee. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ wala mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living canopy that shelters the young seedlings until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why does leaving weeds around my cassava plants make the tubers stay small?
ga: Mɛni Hewɔ ni Ashiɔ Jwɛi yɛ Mi-cassava tso lɛ he lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunshine, and fertilizer that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure all the nutrients in the soil go straight into making large cassava tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi wuji baa.

english: If I have a large piece of farmland, should I plant crops on the whole field at once or clear and plant it in smaller sections over time?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ agbo Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mafo mli ni madu yɛ he bibioo ko? Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: It is usually better for a single farmer to plant in manageable sections. Planting a huge acreage all at once requires a lot of labor for weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting at the exact same time, which can overwhelm you and lead to crop loss if resources are tight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okwaafonyo kome baadu yɛ hei ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ wulu ko ni aaakwɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo koni akɛjie jwɛi, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa nii yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ohe ajɔ bo ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii afite kɛji nibii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa.

english: How long does a cocoa tree take to start bearing fruit, and for how many years can it keep producing?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso woɔ yibii? Ni afii enyiɛ ebaanyɛ ewo yibii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting. With good care, pruning, and soil maintenance, a cocoa tree can continue producing healthy pods for 30 to 40 years or more.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔkwɛmɔ Cacao tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, tomato plants experience heat stress. High heat dries out the pollen, preventing pollination, which causes the plant to drop its flowers to save energy until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha pollen lɛ agbi. Tsi pollination naa Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and making the plant look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Sprayers use neem oil or insecticides to control these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Mɛi ni shwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant plantains on the same land where we plant young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔduɔ kookoo bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Is it helpful to plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows tall quickly and is harvested in about 3 to 4 months, while cassava grows slower and stays in the ground longer. This allows you to harvest two different crops from the same land without them competing for space at the same time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe awo he ko he akaŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is soft and deep enough to grow large yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, well-drained soil so they can push downward easily as they grow. If your soil is heavy clay or full of rocks, the yam tubers will grow short, bent, or small because they cannot easily penetrate the hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni anyɛ ashɛre lɛ kɛya shi mlɛo beni edaa lɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ Sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ kuku, ebɔle, loo eyɛ bibioo ejaakɛ enyɛŋ ebote shikpɔŋ ni wa mli mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my crop seedlings after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds naturally lie dormant in the soil in huge numbers and are adapted to sprout instantly at the first drop of water. Crops often need a little more time for their root systems to settle before they take off.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo ni ebaatsake ehe koni ekwɛ̃ kɛji nu klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwie shi pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná be fioo ko dani amɛshishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ dani amɛgbee shi.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so it does not rot or become woody in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni ekafite loo etsɔ tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. Leaving cassava in the ground past its maturity can make the tubers fibrous, woody, or prone to rot during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmei, tso, loo ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get more corn harvested from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to thin, weak stalks with small or missing ears. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce a high yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii loo ni bɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them alone in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikome too midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily and lose water fast under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them provides shelter and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ hulutsoo tsei lɛ, ebaaha aná wɔɔhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants after I touch or shake them roughly while walking through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ beni mikɛ yiwalɛ eta amɛhe loo miwoso amɛ beni mitsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rough handling disturbs fragile flower stalks, causing the blossoms to fall off before forming fruits. Additionally, handling infected plants and then healthy ones can spread crop diseases directly through your hands.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni mli wa baagba fɔfɔi tsei ni waaa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oootsu he nii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ oniji anɔ agbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour water over the leaves of my vegetable plants in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ nu awoɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under strong afternoon sun causes water drops on leaves to act like tiny magnifying glasses, scorching the foliage. Heat also makes the water evaporate quickly into the air before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni haa baai lɛ shãa Dɔlɛ hu haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need for healthy green foliage. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ hia baai ni mli wa, eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings burn and die when I place chemical fertilizer right against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that burn delicate plant stems and roots upon direct contact. Always place fertilizer in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo, be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cut off side branches from my tomato plants when they look so leafy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛji baai ni amɛhe wa waa lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots (suckers) forces the plant to send its food and energy into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on useless extra leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ aha aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants look like they are wilting right after I weed around them with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi yucca tso lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmei jie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Weeding too deeply damages shallow feeder roots near the soil surface. Hoeing gently around the base clears weeds without tearing the vital roots that pull water into the crop.
