ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli tsɔ lɛ baafite niyenii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ shishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi lɛ ni efiteee shishifãi ni he hiaa ni gbalaa nu kɛboteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes produce smaller harvests when I plant them in the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly in one spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases targeting that crop to build up. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts refreshes the soil and starves pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ajɔ ni hɔmɔ baagbe kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do pests like armyworms destroy my entire maize farm so much faster when I plant only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ oya fe tsutsu lɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa pɛ lɛ?

english: Fields with only one crop give armyworms an uninterrupted food supply, allowing them to multiply rapidly. Intercropping maize with crops like cassava or cowpeas confuses pests and limits their spread.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei duɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ futuɔ amɛhe ni ehaaa amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi.

english: Why do some seeds need extra warmth inside a box to start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi he hiaa ni hulutsoo babaoo aba adeka lɛ mli koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Trapped warmth tricks seeds into thinking the rainy season has started. Providing steady heat softens the hard outer shell of the seed and speeds up sprouting so the seedlings emerge faster and stronger.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ lakaa mɛi ni amɛsusuɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi. Kɛ́ edɔ po lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ fã ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ adara oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do farmers start delicate seeds inside a wooden box instead of planting them directly in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi bɔi dumɔwui ni waaa ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a controlled box protects delicate young sprouts from harsh weather, hungry pests, and heavy rain, while holding in the heat and moisture they need for a strong start.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ adeka ni akudɔɔ mli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛhiɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kɛha shishijee kpakpa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it helpful to keep my seedboxes covered during the early days of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aha dumɔwui adeka lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? ni ji dumɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ

english: Covering the box traps warmth and moisture inside, creating a warm mini-climate that keeps the soil consistently damp without needing constant watering, which encourages the seeds to break open quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ha adeka lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ lɛ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo nɔ nu daa. Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ agbele oya.

english: Can using a warm light bulb inside a nursery box really help my seeds germinate faster?
ga: Ani kanei ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Yes, standard heat-emitting light bulbs provide continuous, gentle warmth that keeps soil temperatures high enough for heat-loving seeds to sprout even during cool nights or cloudy days.
ga: Hɛɛ, kanei ni jieɔ dɔlɛ haa blɛoo, dɔlɛ daa. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui ni sumɔɔ latsaa lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli loo gbii ni atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ po mli.

english: How can I tell if the heat around my young nursery seedlings is becoming too high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dɔlɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ mli edɔ? Ani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ?

english: If seedlings receive too much heat, their leaves will droop, turn yellow, or show scorched tips. You should reduce the heat source or open the container slightly to let cool air circulate.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo dɔlɛ babaoo mli lɛ, baai lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ. loo etsɔɔ naagbee ni shãa Esa akɛ ajie latsaa jɛɛhe lɛ shi loo agbele tsɛnsi lɛ mli fioo koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my stored seed tubers need heat and humidity before I plant them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atswa dumɔwui ayitsei ni ato lɛ awo la mli ni afee amɛ fɛ̃i dani adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warmth and humidity signal to stored tubers that the growing season has begun, forcing the hidden buds to sprout evenly so you plant active, living crops.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i tsɔɔ bulbs ni ato lɛ akɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ eje shishi. Nyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ daa koni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka.

english: Why should I slowly increase inputs like water and light as my seedlings grow bigger in the box?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ lɛ blɛoo? Ha nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ nu kɛ kane aya hiɛ. Beni mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa yɛ adekai amli lɛ

english: As seedlings grow, their root systems demand more nourishment step-by-step; gradually increasing care prevents shocking the young plants while building their strength for the open farm.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ daraa Amɛshishifãi lɛ biɔ niyenii babaoo fiofio. Kwɛmɔ ni yaa hiɛ fiofio lɛ tsiɔ tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkafee shoo yɛ be mli ni ewajeɔ ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds take so long to wake up and shoot out their first stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Some seeds enter a resting state after harvest and require specific conditions—like sustained heat and moisture—to trigger the internal hormones that tell the plant to wake up and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi boteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Ni ebiɔ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa. Koni ekanya mligbɛ tsofai ni kɛɔ tsei ni amɛte shi ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: How do I know when my sprouted seeds inside the box are ready to be moved into nursery bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ adeka lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie awo grow bag mli?

english: Once the seeds shoot out their first visible green stems or roots above the soil, they need direct light and more space, meaning it is time to move them into individual nursery bags.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwu ko kwɛ̃ lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ tso loo shishifãi ni anaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. La ni tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo kɛ he ko babaoo he miihia amɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ aŋɔ amɛ awo grow bags sɔrɔtoi amli.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers say I must prepare my boxed seedlings before putting them under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ehe miihia ni masaa dumɔwui ni akɛwo adeka mli lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ awo hulu lɛ mli?

english: This process involves gradually exposing indoor seedlings to hotter outdoors conditions over a few days so they build resistance and do not wither when transplanted to the open farm.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ biɔ ni ajie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shĩa mli lɛ awo kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli fiofio gbii fioo komɛi koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkagbo kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa mli.

english: Why are my mango trees dropping their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers mainly because of sudden dry spells or diseases like powdery mildew and anthracnose. Giving the tree enough water during flowering and spraying appropriate organic or chemical fungicides helps flowers set into proper fruit.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ trukaa hulutsoo be loo helai tamɔ powdery mildew kɛ anthracnose hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a grafted mango tree produce fruit faster than one I grow directly from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe nɔ ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A seed grows a brand-new young plant that takes 7 to 10 years to mature. A grafted tree uses a branch from an already mature fruit-bearing tree, so it skips the juvenile years and can start producing fruit in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ tsei heei ni heɔ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛdaraa. Tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ewo yibii momo lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, efoɔ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be lɛ mli ni ebɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my sweet potatoes on raised soil mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu sweet potatoes yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Sweet potatoes need soft, loose soil so their roots can expand easily into big tubers. Mounds and ridges keep the soil loose, improve water drainage, and stop the tubers from rotting in heavy rain.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse. koni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ bulb agboi oya. Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akafiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa

english: How far apart am I supposed to plant my young mango trees in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mango tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Mango trees grow very large, so they need about 8 to 10 meters of space between each tree. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and airflow, which keeps them healthy and prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Mango tso lɛ da waa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ afee aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines have plenty of green leaves but tiny potatoes under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow big green leaves on top instead of developing tubers underneath. Sweet potatoes need balanced fertilizers with more potassium to grow large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni baa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Sweet potatoes he miihia ŋmeii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to grow food crops without adding chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ niyenii ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well without staying soggy, and breaks apart easily in your hands. If wild weeds grow thick and green on the land, it usually means the soil has good natural nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa. ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ eyɛ nine mli Kɛji koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell that my sweet potatoes are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready 3 to 4 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, or by carefully digging up one mound to check if the tubers are full-sized.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu sweet potato lɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋtayaa lɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋtayaai lɛ eshɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my sweet potatoes to rot quickly in the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: When water sits in the field for too long, it chokes the soil and starves the tubers of air. Bacteria and fungi thrive in this wet environment, causing the sweet potatoes to rot quickly before harvest.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Muawai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Ha sweet potatoes lɛ agbo oya dani akpa.

english: Can I plant sweet potatoes under the shade of my large mango trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mango tso agbo ko shishi?

english: Sweet potatoes need full sunshine for at least 6 hours a day to make food and grow big tubers. Under heavy tree shade, they will produce long leafy vines but very small or no tubers.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, hulutsoo be fɛɛ he miihia sweet potatoes ŋmɛlɛtswai 6 daa gbi koni enyɛ ehoo ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs agboi. Yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi Amɛwoɔ wain tsei ni baai kakadaji yɔɔ mli shi amɛhe bɛ bibioo kwraa loo amɛbɛ ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Why do heavy rains during the flowering season cause my mango crop to fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa mango lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Rain washes away pollen from the flowers so insect pollinators cannot do their work. The moisture also encourages fungal diseases that cause the flower clusters to rot and fall off.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ fɔfɔii amli muji. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Fɛ̃i hu woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major nutrient crops need to grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure gives the plant its healthy green color and growth back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade trees nearby during hot seasons helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ duɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and direct sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop full-sized leaves and fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa kɛ aduawai ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to full direct sunlight and high heat. Keeping mature shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains provides the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ baaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when we receive heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause water to pool in flat soil, suffocating the roots and allowing fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the tuberous roots healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ tɛtrɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni oha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ waa

english: Why does my farmland produce less harvest every year even though I plant cassava on it every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ daa be mli?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same land repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops with beans or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ awo mli koni nugbɔ lɛ akaŋɔ lɛ kɛya?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is damp but not during heavy downpours. Applying it a few inches away from the plant stem and covering it lightly with soil prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Okɛtsu nii inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Koni nugbɔ lɛ akashwie lɛ

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide in the growing point of the plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays directly into the funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it ruins the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani tso lɛ afite.

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and quickly consume the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's lifecycle gives your main plants the head start they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛyeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala be mli lɛ haa otso titri lɛ yitso ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce less than the new seeds I buy in sealed packets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni mihe yɛ wolo kotoku ko ni akɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Packet seeds are usually certified hybrids bred for maximum yield and disease resistance. The seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose those special traits in the next generation, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ paketii amli lɛ ji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When soil lacks enough nitrogen, the maize plant steals it from its older lower leaves to feed the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Abele juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the young leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these insects. The feeding damages leaf cells, causing them to distort as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii kpataa baa mli wala yibii lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa baa mli wala yibii lɛ feɔ srɔtoi beni amɛmli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to pour water directly onto my vegetable leaves in the middle of a hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ahe tsei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Water droplets sitting on hot leaves can burn leaf tissue under intense heat, and wet leaves combined with high temperature create the ideal humid environment for destructive fungal diseases to spread quickly.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baa ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baa lɛ mli fãji yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Ni baai ni mli efɔ ni akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa fata he lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is scarce. Heat stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination, causing it to drop flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni akɛto hewalɛ he.

english: Groundnut pods develop underground. Once the flower above ground is pollinated, the stem automatically grows downward into the soil—a process called pegging—so the nut can safely form in the dark earth.
ga: Bean pods lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo pollin lɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pinning. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ jeŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods when I give them too much animal manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ naa baai eŋɔli babaoo shi enáa ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ha lɛ lɛ?

english: Animal manure contains high amounts of nitrogen. While nitrogen helps grow leaves, too much of it tricks the plant into focusing entirely on growing foliage instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ kooloi aŋmɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa moŋ, shi nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ lakaa tsei koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui akutsei.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Multiple suckers compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and light. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ koni tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the air and sun, improving photosynthesis and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fotosintɛsis yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ foliar helai anaa.

english: Why do my maize plants give me tiny cobs when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the roots and leaves to fight for limited light, water, and food. This extreme competition weakens every plant in the hole, leading to small, poorly filled cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi kɛ baai ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ kɛha la, nu kɛ niyenii lɛ naa wa. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, cob tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when there is heavy rainfall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Excess standing water suffocates the roots and promotes water-loving soil fungi that infect and decay the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu ni yeɔ bulb lɛ hela ni amɛfiteɔ dani akpaa lɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily get scorched by intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stems and large ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient in the soil that helps plants stay green and produce food. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged after heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu.

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water from their leaves through evaporation faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. As long as the soil is moist, they usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the air gets too hot or dry, or if the plant suffers from irregular watering. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Aloo kɛji akɛ afɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu be fɛɛ be Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't dry out fast in the heat. It also keeps the soil cool and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ekɛwo la mli lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific soil nutrients every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ daa be mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose their leaves to direct sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and helps the plant capture more light to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Staking haa tso lɛ baa lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ la babaoo koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the funnel) of maize plants and eat the tender growing leaves, which can reduce your yield if not treated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting since they are hidden underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ be mli ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the base of the main stem swells and cracks slightly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miikwɛ̃ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ shishi baafu ni ebaagbala fioo.

english: How do I know if my maize leaves are turning yellow because of too much rain or lack of food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmãa baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean either issue. If the yellowing starts from the tips of the bottom leaves and forms a V-shape along the middle, the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer. If the entire field looks pale and weak after heavy rain, the soil is likely waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Kaadi ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ naagbai enyɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni efeɔ V su yɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Why is it bad to throw chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashɛrɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ ashwie tsei ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes 'fertilizer burn.' The concentrated salts pull water out of the plant tissue, damaging the stem and roots, which can stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ 'ŋmɔshi nibii shãa' baa. Nu ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli fãji amli. efiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbo.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Shade plants like plantains or shade trees keep the air humid, protect leaves from scorching, and keep the soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle before planting my cassava cuttings instead of planting in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani odu ŋmei tsei moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need moist soil to sprout roots and buds. In dry soil, the heat bakes and dries out the stems before roots can form, leading to poor germination and dead crops.
ga: Yucca tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, la ni tsoɔ lɛ shãa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii gboiɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the maize to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small cobs or empty heads.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa bibii loo yitsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on leaf sap, or by a viral disease spread by whiteflies. Controlling these small insects early stops the leaves from crumpling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. ŋmeii bibii akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black sunken spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or experiences uneven watering, making it difficult for the plant to move water and nutrients into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than many crops. They steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil, effectively starving your crops and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni oha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the base of the main stem swells, and cracks appear in the soil around the plant stem, usually 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishitso lɛ baafu. ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli, bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my harvested maize inside the barn even after I dried them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ migbi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the grain while the maize is still in the field. If the grain is not dried completely to a hard state or treated with safe grain storage protectants, the eggs hatch inside your barn and eat the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmaa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa ni amɛhe wa loo akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii. Wɔɔji lɛ baafɔ yɛ otsu lɛ mli ni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural food source for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nodes krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade trees or plantains alongside them acts like an umbrella, keeping them cool and maintaining soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa shade loo tsei bibii ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I spend money on certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength and yield lower amounts each year. Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases, handle heat better, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ yibii fioo daa afi. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baa

english: Why do my cassava roots go bad if I leave them in wet ground for too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mature cassava tubers continue to absorb excess water from wet soil. This extra moisture causes fungal diseases and rot to set in underground, spoiling the crop before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ baaya nɔ agbala nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming any fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather is extremely hot and dry, tomato plants experience heat stress and drop their flowers to conserve water and energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tomato tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water in the soil. Pruning extra suckers allows the main tree to grow bigger and produce larger bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni edara ni ewoɔ kui wuji.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the wet ground, exposing them to more sunlight so the plant can make more food for the tubers while preventing leaves from rotting due to damp soil.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na hulu la babaoo Koni tso lɛ afee niyenii babaoo aha ŋmei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ wulu ko baanɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash the fertilizer away from the soil surface before the roots have time to suck it up, which wastes your money and damages nearby water streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaafite nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and produce small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, light, and water from the soil that your crops need to grow strong. Cleared fields allow your crops to get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele naa lɛ haa onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my mango tree without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mango tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often drop due to poor pollination, sudden changes in water levels, or attack by tiny pests like thrips and fungal diseases like anthracnose. Ensuring balanced watering during flowering and managing pests helps the tree hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi tsakeɔ trukaa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose lɛ tutuamɔi. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How long will it take after planting my oil palm seedlings before I can start harvesting palm nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ adu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani aje palm ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ shishi?

english: Hybrid oil palm seedlings usually start producing their first fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after field planting, provided they receive adequate sunlight, water, weed control, and regular feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni ji hybrid oil palm dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii akui lɛ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛna hulu la, nu, kɛ jwɛi akudɔmɔ. kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ daa

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dying from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often signal a lack of essential nutrients in the soil, particularly potassium, or an infection like Lethal Yellowing disease. Applying compost or potassium-rich fertilizer around the base of the palm can help nourish the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. titri lɛ potassium loo hela ni baa mɔ nɔ, tamɔ hela ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ gboiɔ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo potassium ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning shade trees to allow sunshine in and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is short on phosphorus or that wet, cold soil is preventing the roots from taking up phosphorus properly. As the soil warms up and drains, or with phosphorus fertilizer added, the leaves will turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni eho nu loo akɛ phosphorus ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: My cassava plants have grown very tall with plenty of big leaves, so why are the roots underneath so small?
ga: Mi-cassava tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai wuji waa. Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing leafy branches instead of tubers. Using soil with balanced nutrients ensures energy goes into enlarging the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei niji kɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha hewalɛ ni ekɛbaagbɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Should I leave all the young shoots growing around my plantain tree or cut some off?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii komɛi ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ loo mifolɔ ekomɛi?

english: You should prune away extra suckers and keep only one or two strong ones alongside the main plant. If you leave too many suckers, they will compete for water and plant food, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi tso titri lɛ masɛi. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, Amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist and the sun is gentle. Applying fertilizer under a strong mid-day sun can heat up the chemical and burn the crop roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai lɛ adɔ ni amɛshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so quickly on my farm even after I clear them with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dade jie lɛ moŋ

english: Cutting weeds with a cutlass only removes the top leaves while leaving roots and buried seeds unharmed in the soil. Uprooting weeds by their roots or covering the soil with mulch prevents sunshine from reaching new weed seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie jwɛi lɛ, ebaajie baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ashiɔ shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui ni afu yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeee amɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui heei ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up into tight cups during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss from evaporation. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled, it may need watering or treatment for tiny insects like mites.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hi, shi kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ nu awo mli loo okwɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: What is the main difference between organic fertilizer and chemical fertilizer for my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mikoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer comes from natural plant or animal matter, while chemical fertilizer is factory-made. Organic options break down naturally in the soil, improving the ground's health and feeding your cocoa trees gradually over a longer period.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii jɛɔ tsei loo kooloi amli kɛbaa diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhei. Organic nibii ni ahala lɛ baafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ Ni okɛ niyenii haa o-cacao tsei lɛ fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do some extension officers recommend organic fertilizers like Tatahwema for cocoa trees in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ Tatahwema atsu nii kɛha kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Organic fertilizers like Tatahwema are specially made to break down smoothly in tropical soils. They release steady nutrients over time, which improves cocoa tree strength and protects the long-term fertility of Ghanaian soil.
ga: Afee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ Tatahwema lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛfite jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ebuɔ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni baa nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Why would a fertilizer that feeds cocoa trees slowly be better than one that acts immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa kookoo tsei lɛ blɛoo lɛ? Ani ehi fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Slow-release fertilizers break down gradually so the cocoa roots get a steady, continuous supply of food over many months. This prevents heavy rains from washing all the plant food away before the crop can use it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ blɛoo lɛ baafite fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ aha kookoo shishifãi lɛ nyɔji babaoo. Bɔni afee ni nugbɔ akanɛ waa lɛ, afɔ tso niyenii lɛ fɛɛ he dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: If your cocoa leaves turn yellow, growth seems slow, or your trees are producing fewer pods than usual, it usually means the soil has run out of nutrients and needs plant food to recover.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Dalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo loo otso lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe bɔ ni efeɔ daa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni ana tsei aniyenii koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when an officer says a fertilizer 'breaks down well' in the soil?
ga: Beni onukpa lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Mɛni ji ‘ni efite jogbaŋŋ’ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ shishi?

english: When fertilizer breaks down well, soil microbes easily digest it and convert it into tiny nutrients that cocoa roots can easily drink up, without leaving harsh chemicals or damaging the earth.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii bibii. Cocoa shishifã lɛ numɔ waaa. Ni eshiŋ tsofai ni mli wa yɛ esɛɛ loo efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How does adding fertilizer to my cocoa soil actually help me harvest more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cocoa shikpɔŋ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food like nitrogen and potassium that cocoa trees need to build strong leaves, grow healthy flowers, and fill up heavy pods with rich beans.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium jɛɛhe. ni cacao tso lɛ he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni mli wa Ekwɛ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Is organic fertilizer good for old, mature cocoa trees or is it only used for young trees?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha kookoo tsei ni eda loo tsei bibii pɛ?

english: Organic fertilizer is great for both. On young trees, it builds strong roots, and on mature trees, it keeps the soil rich enough to sustain high pod production year after year.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sa kɛha amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, efeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa. kɛ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ pod yibiiwoo ni fa nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away some fertilizers, and how can I prevent that on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kɛyaa lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Heavy rains easily wash away light chemical powders before roots can grab them. Using organic fertilizers that break down slowly helps nutrients stay bonded to the soil longer during rainy seasons.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai ni waaa lɛ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ blɛoo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Can using a gradual organic fertilizer prevent my cocoa soil from growing weak over time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fiofio lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mi-kokoo shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, gradual organic fertilizers nourish beneficial organisms in the ground while feeding the tree. This keeps the soil soft, moist, and fertile so it doesn't get worn out after many harvest seasons.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, fiofio lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa bɔɔ nii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, edɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee yɛ nikpamɔ be babaoo sɛɛ.

english: Will applying fertilizer to my cocoa trees make them more resistant to dry weather?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, well-fed cocoa trees build deeper, stronger root systems and healthier leaves, which helps them survive long dry seasons much better than nutrient-starved trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tso ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni mli wa, kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shaded environments. Pruning excessive shade trees and clearing underbrush helps air flow around the trees and reduces the wetness that spreads the disease.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo fe nine ni afoɔ kɛ tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ agbala helai ashwã lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my pepper plants, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Small holes are typically caused by chewing pests like flea beetles or caterpillars. Planting repellent flowers like marigolds nearby or spraying a natural neem seed mixture can keep these insects away without harming the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ mɛi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu fɔfɔi ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ marigolds yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ loo akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he ni eyeee tso lɛ awui.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs fertilizer or if the soil is still rich?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo?

english: You can tell by looking at your crops: pale yellow leaves, thin stems, and slow growth usually mean the soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen. If your harvest yields keep dropping year after year, your soil needs added organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, kɛ dalɛ blɛoo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛji akɛ okpamɔ lɛ miiba shi afi fɛɛ afi. Ehe miihia ni okɛ humus loo humus afata oshikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows rapidly and is harvested early within a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space later. Planting them together allows you to harvest two different crops from the same piece of land without them competing for space at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe awo he ko he akaŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so much faster than my planted crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant deep in the soil for years and sprout rapidly as soon as sunlight hits bare earth. Covering the bare ground around your crops with mulch, such as dried leaves or straw, blocks sunlight and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ he. Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and dry wind, preventing it from losing moisture too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he yɛ dɔlɛ bei amli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya tsɔ naa

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruit. Regular watering and using balanced fertilizers during flowering can help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to prune the extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive wood so the tree directs its energy and water into developing healthy cocoa pods. It also opens up the tree canopy to let in light and air, which keeps damp-loving diseases away.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni mli wa. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ hu koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela kɛjɛɔ suɔmɔ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ naa

english: Why do my nursery seedlings grow tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out and become tall, thin, and weak when they are reaching for sunlight in a overly shaded nursery. Giving them partial, balanced sunlight encourages them to grow thick, sturdy stems that survive transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tsɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulu la ni sa lɛ fioo lɛ, ebaawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ atsake amɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to heap fresh cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato kookoo yibii heei ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Covering the beans with plantain leaves creates heat that ferments the cocoa pulp. Fermentation destroys the seed's bitter taste, prevents it from sprouting, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color required by buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ baa koni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fɛ̃i fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa lɛ. Tsi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni oná tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cover my harvested cocoa beans with banana leaves for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ banana baai haa kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermenting cocoa beans under banana leaves helps develop the rich chocolate flavor and deep brown color that makes Ghanaian cocoa premium and highly valued around the world.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ banana baai ashishi lɛ haa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni mli kwɔ baa. Enɛ haa Ghana kookoo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ejara wa waa yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he.

english: Drying cocoa beans on the bare ground allows dirt, stones, and mold to mix with the beans, which ruins their quality and reduces the market price you can sell them for.
ga: Kookoo yibii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha muji, tɛi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ afutu kɔfe yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe baa shi, ni ehaa jara ni obaanyɛ okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and wilting under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Intercropping them with fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living shade to keep the soil moist and leaves cool.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains du lɛ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ hu afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra wild branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches that waste the tree's energy, allowing light and air to circulate while directing more nutrients into growing healthy, larger pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii ni haa tso lɛ he waaa lɛ. Ehaa kane kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa niyenii mli hewalɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdara.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When trees are overcrowded, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants, smaller yields, and a higher risk of fungal diseases spreading.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo Ni oshara babaoo yɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from extreme heat, lack of soil nutrients, or when there are not enough beneficial insects like midges present to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ midges, ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ faaa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high moisture and excessive shade where rainwater stays trapped on the leaves and pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine. ni nugbɔ nu ekpɛtɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe

english: How do wild weeds around my crops prevent them from growing big and healthy?
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkadara ni amɛhe wa?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal essential water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight directly from the soil, effectively starving your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ. fertilizer nutrients kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops from dying during the long dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ harmatta be kakadaŋŋ ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli?

english: Mulching by placing dry leaves or straw around the base of your plants keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly and protects roots from severe dry heat.
ga: Mulching kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ he

english: Why should I consider replacing my old cocoa trees with improved hybrid varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu kookoo tsei momo ni mikɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsake lɛ he?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees are developed to produce pods much faster—often within two to three years—and yield more pods while being stronger against common crop diseases.
ga: Afee cacao tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii oya kwraa—bei pii lɛ yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli—ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: What is pollination, and why do my crop flowers need bees or insects to make fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ mifɔfɔi lɛ ahe hiaa ŋmeii loo kooloi koni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pollination is how plants reproduce. Bees and wind carry pollen from flower to flower so the plant can form healthy fruits and seeds. Without pollinators, many crop flowers will simply drop off without growing into usable food.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii. Wuobii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ fɔfɔi amli fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ Tsei fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi kɛkɛ ni niyenii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ko kwraa bɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when they are not properly pollinated, or when the plant is stressed by severe heat or drought. If insects or wind do not shake the pollen inside the flower, the plant aborts the flower to save its energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa miihao tsei. Kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ etswaaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baafo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What causes my garden egg fruits to grow in strange, bent shapes instead of full, healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni haa eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ, ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ?

english: Deformed garden eggs often happen because of poor pollination. When insects only deliver pollen to one side of the flower, only part of the fruit develops fully, leading to twisted or misshapen produce that fetches a low market price.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni efite yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Beni kooloi bibii kɛ pollen lɛ yaa fɔfɔi lɛ afã kome lɛ, tso yibii lɛ fã ko pɛ ji nɔ ni edara kwraa. Ekɛ nibii ni efite loo amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baa ni no haa jarayeli jara baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the roots standing in waterlogged soil for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ loo kɛ́ ashi shishifãi ni damɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why does my pepper plant have so many big leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ baa lɛ dara shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing lush stem and leaf foliage rather than flowers and fruit. Balancing your fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set more fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ Kɛ́ okɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to o-fertilizer lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo aduawai babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and watery inside even when the plant grows tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Tall, bushy growth with poor roots usually means the crop received plenty of water early on but suffered from poor soil aeration or poor nutrient balance later. Excess nitrogen encourages top-leaf growth while starving the starch storage in the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛlɛ, ni shishifãi bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ná nu babaoo yɛ shishijee mli. Shi sɛɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ amanehulu. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa baa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmei ni ato yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Will spraying chemicals to kill insects harm my crops while they are blooming with flowers?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Spraying strong insecticides during peak flowering hours can kill beneficial insects like bees that pollinate your crop. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when bees are not actively visiting flowers.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he wa ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ ayasara fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: This is usually Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning excess tree branches improves airflow and helps keep the remaining pods safe and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I pay extra for certified seeds from a shop instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo nyɔmɔ babaoo koni manyɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ shwapo ko mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are bred to resist local diseases, tolerate drought, and produce uniform high yields. Saved seeds from hybrid crops often lose their strength in the next generation, producing smaller and less consistent harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli mli kɛha maŋ lɛ mli helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai. Enyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa ni eyaaa nɔ daa.

english: Plants suffering from drought wilt during the heat of the day and have dry, crunchy leaves. Plants suffering from excess water have soft, droopy, yellowing leaves and sour-smelling soil around soggy, rotten roots.
ga: Tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛbaana baai ni egbi ni amɛkpãtã. Tsei ni nu ni fa fe nine yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni shwieɔ shi, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe. Shishifãi ni efɔ ni egboi

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips inward, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen to the younger top leaves to survive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su kɛjɛ mligbɛ naagbee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa baai bibii lɛ amli amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato leaves curl up in extreme heat to protect themselves from losing water. It is a natural defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when water availability changes suddenly. Extreme heat stops effective pollination, causing the plant to shed the flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollination kpaa. Ha tsei ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more food the plant produces to send underground to grow a larger yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni ekɛmaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to fight with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, leading to bigger and heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tsei akuu ko ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow strong with less reliance on expensive fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmãa ni jara wa nɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool in hot weather and stops moisture from evaporating quickly. It also blocks sunlight so weeds cannot easily grow and compete with your crops.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Etsĩɔ hulu lɛ hu naa. Jwɛi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ mlɛo ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔ akaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi bibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers during dry spells to protect themselves from dying of thirst. Dropping flowers reduces the amount of water the tree needs until the rains return.
ga: Kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he. Kɛ́ oshi fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaha nu ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without draining. Waterlogged soil cuts off air to the roots, allowing harmful water fungi to grow and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani ahum aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away surface fertilizer before the crop roots can drink it in. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil after rain, so the roots absorb the nutrients directly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth, or that heavy rains have flooded the root zone and prevented the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is sick from a disease or just suffering from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ hela loo edɔ fe nine kɛkɛ?

english: Heat-stressed cassava will wilt slightly during the dry afternoon but recover by morning, whereas diseased cassava shows distorted, curled, or yellow-spotted leaves that remain damaged regardless of water.
ga: Cassava ni dɔlɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ shwieɔ fioo yɛ shwane mli ni nu egbi lɛ. Shi ebaatsa lɛ leebi. Shi ŋmei ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ baaná baai ni etsake, ni ebɔle ehe, loo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baaya nɔ efite ni nu kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to build mounds when planting root crops like yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔma gɔji beni wɔduɔ tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potato lɛ?

english: Building mounds creates loose, aerated soil that allows tubers to expand freely and prevents excess water from collecting around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Gɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ehe. ni etsĩ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efite

english: Why should I plant legumes like cowpeas alongside my corn field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko masɛi lɛ?
