english: Legumes pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, which helps feed neighboring crops like corn without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruit when the afternoon becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa be mli ni shwane lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from pollinating successfully and forcing the plant to drop the flowers to conserve moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Enɛ haaa anyɛ afee pollination yɛ omanyeyeli mli. kɛ tsei ni anyɛɔ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he

english: Why does fall armyworm attack my maize crops more severely during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather speeds up the hatching cycle of armyworm eggs, while thirsty maize plants become too weak to naturally resist insect feeding.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa cutworm wuji lɛ fɔɔ oya. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi niyenii yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is the difference between planting certified hybrid seeds and saving seeds from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield and disease resistance in their first generation, whereas saved seeds lose those special traits and produce weaker plants in the second year.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature faster than the traditional seeds my parents used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni mifɔlɔi kɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Early-maturing crop varieties have been selected by plant breeders to complete their life cycle in fewer days, helping them produce yields before short rainy seasons end.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ehala tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa nibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Why does picking green peppers early cause the plant to produce more peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akpa chili ŋmɔji mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ woɔ chili babaoo?

english: Harvesting mature fruit tricks the plant into thinking it hasn't finished its job of reproducing, prompting it to grow new flowers and produce another batch of peppers.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ egbeko fɔmɔ naa. Enɛ haa anáa fɔfɔii heei, ni anáa ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he.

english: Why is it important to ferment cocoa beans in banana leaves right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee cocoa ŋmeii awo banana baai amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans, killing the seed embryo to prevent sprouting while unlocking the rich chocolate flavor and changing the bean color from purple to dark brown.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ. Egbeɔ dumɔwui amli fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbeleɔ tsokolate ni mli wa lɛ naa. ni otsake ŋmeii lɛ ahe su kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that excessive rainfall has flooded the roots and prevented them from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ niyenii.

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil, while legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, refreshing the soil naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce so many green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When yam plants receive too much shade or too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall vines and leaves on top instead of storing food in the root tuber below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo be babaoo loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Ebaakɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni miida lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the leaves and stalks of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Holes in your corn plants are typically caused by pests like stem borers or fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the plant's funnel or leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms kɛ bu ni baa ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ baa. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi loo amɛbaai amli lɛ amli.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This black pod condition is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in high humidity and wet weather when rainwater lingers on the pods without good airflow through the trees.
ga: Nɛkɛ black pod shihilɛ nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi tsei lɛ amli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ko tsɔɔɛɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the sap underneath the leaf, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, often due to poor drainage or planting in low areas where heavy rains collect without draining away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo dumɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa buaa ehe naa ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture suddenly jumps from very dry to very wet, which shocks the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. ni haa tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei lɛ

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves until the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe kɛyashi be mli ni edɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the sun gets very hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ ohe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, delicate leaves that cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees beside them protects the young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps moisture in the soil while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko yɛ amɛmasɛi. Kakao tso lɛ buɔ kakao tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni eshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. This happens when the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash the soil's food away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii lɛ jeɔ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: Why do small caterpillars suddenly appear inside the central leaves of my corn plants and eat them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant where it is cool and moist to feed on the fresh green growth before the plant can produce corn.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛye tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, especially in heavy rain. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to make food that grows the big tuber underground. Climbing a stake spreads the leaves out in the air and keeps them off the wet ground where plant diseases spread easily.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, he ni tso helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests now than it did three years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food nutrients out of the earth every time they grow. If you plant the same piece of land continuously without adding manure or organic fertilizer, or without letting the soil rest, the soil becomes tired and runs out of food for new crops.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji oya nɔ odu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ebɛ niyenii kɛha tsei heei.

english: Will planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize help or hurt my crop yield?
ga: Ani ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Planting groundnuts or beans alongside maize helps your crops. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting like a natural food supply that feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if the very first rain of the year is enough water for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi?

english: The first rain often only wets the surface and can dry up quickly, which kills newly planted seeds. It is best to wait until the rain penetrates the soil to a depth equal to the length of your hand, ensuring sustained moisture for root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbi oya. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ agboi. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ onine lɛ kɛlɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Koni aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have thick wooden roots like trees, so heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden prop stick prevents wind and weight from pulling the plant out of the soil.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli tse tamɔ tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ni atswa amɛ awo kui amli lɛ tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fi tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji naa koni ekagbala tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop bringing out fresh flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi heei anaa koni amɛkaje kpo lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on tomatoes are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the plant juice and spread plant diseases. Protecting young plants and keeping weeds away stops these insects from attacking your tomato crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tso helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ obu tsei bibii ahe ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akatutua o-tomato tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I keep my harvested rice separate from my neighbor's rice instead of mixing them all together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ ato mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ fɛɛ afutu yɛ he kome lɛ.

english: Mixing different farmers' harvests can spoil your good rice if someone else's grain is damp or infested with insects. Keeping your harvest separate protects your grain quality, ensures you get paid fairly for your work, and helps buyers know exactly where good quality rice came from.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo anibii ni amɛfutuɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ efite o-ŋmãa kpakpa lɛ kɛji mɛi krokomɛi aŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ loo ŋmeii ebɔle he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he kroko lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmaa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ ni awo bo nyɔmɔ ni sa yɛ onitsumɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ni amɛleɔ he pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jɛɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves, and why are the leaves rolling up?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on tender leaves inside the plant stalk. The leaves roll up because the plant is stressed and trying to protect itself from drying out in the sun while insects eat it from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ miihao ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni miigbi lɛ he yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii yeɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Young cocoa trees act like human babies—their leaves burn easily and lose water faster than their small roots can absorb from the soil. Leaving bigger trees or planting plantains nearby provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni nu fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing thin and hard like wood instead of big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa tamɔ tso lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni etsii?

english: Cassava roots become thin and woody when the soil is packed too hard, lacks proper plant food, or goes through long dry spells without water. Loose, well-drained soil allows the tubers to expand easily and store water, making them large and soft.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Tso niyenii ni sa ni bɛ loo ni esa akɛ atsɔ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nu bɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni etse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Ha efee agbo ni efee blɛoo.

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain tree, they fight with the main plant for food, light, and water. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant, resulting in much larger and heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) daraa yɛ dumɔwu kome he. Amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ko ni da ni tsii kwraa baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn brown and look burnt after I put chemical fertilizer right next to the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that suck moisture out of plant tissues if placed directly against the stem. To feed the plant safely, fertilizer should always be buried a short distance away in moist soil where the roots can reach it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii shweshweeshwe Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ

english: Why is it better for me to buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du wuhi nɛ i he kɛ je nyagbe kpami be ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time and often carry diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially cleaned and treated to germinate evenly, resist pests, and produce much higher yields than old seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, ni bei pii lɛ, ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa. Atsuɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe nii krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be. Enyɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui momoi lɛ

english: How do weeds growing near my crops make my maize plants stay thin and short?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kuku?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the food they need to grow tall and produce strong cobs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience sudden shock, such as very high heat, dry soil, or too much standing water around their roots. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants during intense heat helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ tswa trukaa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tso lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow and droop when water stands still on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Even though rice loves water, plant roots still need oxygen from air to survive. When water sits completely still without flowing or draining, it starves the roots of air, turning the leaves yellow and slowing down plant growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi tso shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ lolo koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu lɛ efee dioo kwraa ni ehooo loo efooo. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: How deep into the soil should I place small seeds like maize or chili pepper when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui bibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds generally need to be planted at a shallow depth of about two centimeters or one inch. Burying them too deep wastes the seed's energy before the shoot can reach sunlight, while planting too shallow causes them to dry out or be eaten by birds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ aaafee sɛntimitai enyɔ loo inchi kome. Dumɔwui ni afuɔ amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: How do I know if the hole I dug for my young crop seedling is too deep?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji bu ni mifoɔ kɛhaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ?

english: The hole is too deep if the stem of the seedling gets buried under the field soil. You should dig the hole to match the height of the soil ball around the seedling's roots, so the top of the root ball sits level with the farm ground.
ga: Bu lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ otsa bu lɛ koni ekɛ muji ni bɔle dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ akpã gbee. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yiteŋ kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I push them very deep into the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need both air and sunlight energy to sprout successfully. When buried deeper than an inch or two, the soil blocks air from reaching the seed, and the young shoot dies underwater or underground before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe inchi kome loo enyɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ nu shishi loo shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yes, you must ensure the growth buds on the stem point upwards toward the sky. Planting cassava sticks upside down forces the shoots to bend awkwardly, which slows down growth and leads to poor tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kasava ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa tuber lɛ wooo jogbaŋŋ.

english: When placing a nursery seedling into the ground, why must the growing shoot point straight up?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmeii ni adu lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Plants naturally grow toward sunlight. Placing the shoot so it points straight up helps the seedling direct all its energy into growing tall immediately, rather than wasting energy unbending itself from the soil.
ga: Tsei daa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oookotoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Which way should the roots point when I am putting a young cocoa tree into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ kɛji mikɛ cacao tso bibioo ko du shikpɔŋ?

english: The roots must point straight down into the hole. If roots are bent sideways or upward during planting, the tree cannot absorb water deeply from the soil and may dry out and die during the dry season.
ga: Esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛya bu lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ shwie shi kɛtee afã loo kɛtee ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die immediately after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when their tender roots are damaged or left exposed to dry air. Keeping soil attached to the roots and moving them gently protects them from shock so they can establish quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ loo ashiɔ amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni otsi amɛ blɛoo lɛ, ebaabu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni tswaa amɛ lɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛma shi oya.

english: How big or tall should my nursery seedlings be before they are ready to be transplanted?
ga: Te esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ adara loo amɛkwɔ aha tɛŋŋ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for the field when they reach a height of a few inches and have developed 3 to 4 strong leaves. At this stage, their stem and root system are sturdy enough to survive open field conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛji amɛshɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 kɛyashi 4. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli tse mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to plant my young crop seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui bibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: It is best to plant late in the afternoon or early in the morning when the sun is gentle. Planting during the hottest part of the day causes young seedlings to lose water rapidly and wilt before their roots can settle.
ga: Esa akɛ adu shwane loo leebi maŋkpa beni hulu la ni tsoɔ fioo lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afite oya ni ebaagbɔjɔ dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: How firmly should I press the soil around a seedling after placing it in the hole?
ga: Te esa akɛ mamɔ sũ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ mli waa tɛŋŋ beni mikɛwo bu lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: You should press the soil gently around the base of the seedling to remove large air pockets, but do not pack it too tightly. Gentle firming holds the plant upright and keeps roots in contact with moist soil without crushing them.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ atswa shi. light seedling base ni akɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui wuji Shi kaahã eyi mli obɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afee tso lɛ blɛoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpaa gbee ni ekɛ amɛ ekpãaa shi.

english: Yams grow deep under the ground and need soft, loose earth to expand into large tubers. Mounds give the tubers space to grow easily without fighting hard, packed soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee.

english: Does it matter which direction I point my cassava stem when planting it in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni otsɔɔ gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting a cassava stem upside down will prevent it from sprouting properly. You must ensure the small buds or nodes on the stick are pointing upwards toward the sky so the roots and shoots grow in the right direction.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaaa amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Osumɔɔ ni okwɛ koni ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Yɛ tso nine ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ Bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then die from thirst when the rain stops; it is safer to wait until the rains become regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni kumai gbeɔ amɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and produce tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow big ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ toi wuji.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an important food in the soil. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves become green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my farm soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take food from the air and store it in their roots in the soil. When the plant dies, that food stays in the ground, making the soil richer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Excess rainy weather and dark shade create humid conditions where a fungus called Black Pod thrives. Trimming excess branches lets sunlight and air in to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ duŋ haa hulutsoo baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects sucking the juices from the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil water can get rid of these insects and protect new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nuu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ nu shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu baai heei ahe.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Regular watering and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo mli daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the flowers on my crops rotting and falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower rot is usually caused by tiny fungal organisms that thrive in cool, damp conditions. Rain alone doesn't cause the decay—the water allows fungi to infect delicate blossoms, making them turn black and drop prematurely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ fɔfɔi fitemɔ baa. No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔ pɛ kɛ fitemɔ baaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ diŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi mra.

english: Is heavy rain the only reason my crop blossoms turn soft and dark during the rainy season?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ duŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: No, rain creates the wet environment, but living fungus spores actually cause the disease. High moisture lets these microscopic fungi grow quickly and destroy flower tissues.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Shi fungal spores ni hiɛ ka lɛ kɛ hela baa diɛŋtsɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ daraa oya ni amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔi ahe fãji.

english: Why do my cocoa and vegetable blossoms turn black when the air gets very humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Humid weather traps moisture around delicate flower parts, creating perfect conditions for fungal diseases to break down the blossom tissues before fruit can set.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ fɛ̃i ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. delicate flower parts Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baafite fɔfɔi lɛ amli fãji dani aduawai lɛ baa.

english: What can I do to stop my crop flowers from decaying before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mitsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ akafite dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can protect flower blossoms by spraying recommended preventive fungicides before humid peak seasons start and pruning excess leaves to allow sunlight and breeze to dry off the plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu fɔfɔi ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ dani hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ aje shishi. Ni ŋmɔmɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tsei lɛ agbi.

english: What is a fungicide, and how is it different from other farm sprays?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai krokomɛi ahe?

english: A fungicide is a specific crop medicine made to prevent or kill fungal diseases like flower rot and leaf mildew, whereas insect sprays (insecticides) only target insect pests.
ga: Fungicides ji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe ni afee koni akɛtsi loo agbe fungal helai tamɔ fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ (tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi) lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui pɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know which chemical medicine to buy for my sick crops instead of just buying any spray at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni ji tsofa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe spray yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Different plant problems require different treatments. You must identify whether your crops suffer from insects, fungi, or poor soil, and consult an extension officer to choose the right targeted medicine instead of random chemicals.
ga: Tso he naagba fɛɛ naagba biɔ tsamɔi srɔtoi. Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji kooloi, ŋmeii, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ egba onibii ahe. ni okɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ agba sane koni amɛhala tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii trukaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous to buy unlabelled or re-packaged chemical liquids from informal market sellers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ ooohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Unlabelled chemicals may contain banned, highly toxic substances that can burn your crops, poison your soil, or cause severe health problems for your family.
ga: Tsofai ni aŋmalako nɔ ko lɛ baanyɛ ahi nibii ni agu ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Poison ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni mli wa aba oweku lɛ nɔ.

english: Can spraying farm chemicals near my house harm my children or family?
ga: Tsofai ni okɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara aha obii lɛ. loo miweku lɛ?

english: Yes, improper or harsh chemicals can cause dangerous poisoning, breathing troubles, or toxic reactions in children. Crop protection products should always be handled carefully and stored safely away from homes.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni esaaa loo ni mli wa baanyɛ aha mɔ ko aná tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara. mumɔ mli naagbai loo nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa gbekɛbii amli Esa akɛ akwɛ nibii ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto he ko ni kɛ shia lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: What safety body protection should I wear when spraying chemical medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he nibii esa akɛ mawo kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should wear protective long sleeves, trousers, rubber boots, gloves, and a nose mask to prevent chemical liquids and fumes from touching your skin or entering your lungs.
ga: Esa akɛ owo atadei ni niji kɛlɛ, trɔsa kakadaŋŋ, rɔbɔt atadei, glɔvs kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa hiɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsofai kɛ lasu akashɛ hewolo lɛ he loo akabote fɛ̃i lɛ mli.

english: How do I safely mix and spray chemicals with a knapsack machine without contaminating myself?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofai afutu ni mikɛshwie sɛɛkuu nɔ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Check your knapsack sprayer for leaks, mix chemicals outside in open air using protective gear, stand upwind while spraying, and thoroughly wash your hands, body, and clothes immediately after finishing.
ga: Kwɛmɔ osɛɛgbɛ sprayer lɛ mli kɛji nu miiho. Okɛ tsofai afutu kpo nɔ yɛ kpo nɔ kɛtsɔ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ nɔ. Damɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, ni ofɔ oniji, ogbɔmɔtso, kɛ otadei ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛji ogbe naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are so many farmers in my area planting maize specifically to sell to poultry farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkɛhɔ̃ɔ kooloi alɛɛhei lɛ?

english: Poultry farming is growing rapidly in Ghana, creating a constant demand for chicken feed, which is made mostly from grains like maize and soybeans.
ga: Kooloi akwɛmɔ miiya hiɛ oya yɛ Ghana. Enɛ haa abiɔ tsina niyenii be fɛɛ be. Akɛ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ soybeans feɔ amɛ babaoo.

english: Is there any difference between the maize I grow for my family to eat and the maize used for chicken feed?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ mihaa miweku lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛhaa mikooloi lɛ niyenii lɛ teŋ?

english: While chickens can eat regular white maize, feed producers often prefer specific yellow maize varieties because they are rich in nutrients that help chickens grow faster and make egg yolks bright yellow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi baanyɛ aye daa ŋmãa yɛŋ moŋ. Shi mɛi ni feɔ kooloi aniyenii lɛ sumɔɔ abele ŋmɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ. Niyenii babaoo yɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛdaraa oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do prices for grains like maize drop so drastically right after the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jara baa shi waa yɛ nikpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During harvest time, many farmers try to sell their produce at once, causing a huge market supply that drives prices down until grain becomes scarce again later in the year.
ga: yɛ kpamɔ be mli Okwaafoi babaoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ. ni kɛ nibii babaoo baa jara nɔ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, jara ba shi aahu kɛyashi ŋmaa ni faaa ekoŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to save moisture; by rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat, slowing down water loss.
ga: Baai lɛ akumɔ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛbu nu mli. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Ha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: What causes my young maize plants to have large, ragged holes eaten through their leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ná buji wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide during the hot day and feed heavily on plant leaves at night when temperatures cool down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ tsei ahe baai babaoo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stay small when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots compete fiercely for the limited water and soil nutrients available, causing the plants to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my harvested grain turn moldy and spoil so quickly in storage before I can sell it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains hidden moisture inside; if it is not dried properly under the sun before storing, trapped moisture creates ideal conditions for mold and fungi to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same plot of land without harming either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee tso lɛ eko kwraa awui?

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, leaving plenty of space and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ abele daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ daa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting legumes like soybeans on a field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa, tamɔ soybeans yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu ŋmãa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soybeans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground so the next crop of maize has richer soil to grow in.
ga: Soya jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛha shweremɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer when my crop is small instead of waiting until it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii beni midumɔ nii lɛ darako lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni ebɔi fɔmɔ?

english: Young plants need early nutrients to build strong roots and thick stems; feeding them too late when flowering begins cannot make up for early missed growth.
ga: Niyenii he miihia tsei bibii mra. Koni afee shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli wa Ni ayeɔ amɛ niyenii yɛ sɛɛ mli tsɔ beni fɔfɔii lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ atsu dalɛ ni elaaje lɛ he nii mra.

english: Why does my cocoa crop take so many years before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ lɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa focus their energy during the first few years on developing strong roots and thick trunks. Once their structure is strong enough to support heavy pods, they begin producing full harvests.
ga: Tso tsei tamɔ kookoo kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Beni tsɔne lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua pod ni tsii Amɛbɔi nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ feemɔ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil food can stress pepper plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save its own energy until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops start wilting so quickly when the rain stops for just a short period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Crops with shallow root systems can only absorb water near the surface. When dry spells hit, surface moisture disappears fast, causing the plant to dry out if the soil is not mulched to trap water.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba lɛ Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni nu ahi mli.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my farm more during the hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry weather weakens plants because of water stress, making them defenseless against pests. Warm temperatures also cause many crop-damaging insects to hatch and multiply much faster.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ abu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. He ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi babaoo ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Why is my farm producing less harvest every year even though I put in the same hard work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi, eyɛ mli akɛ mi hu mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop every season takes away the same nutrients from the soil repeatedly. Without adding organic manure or rotating crops, the soil becomes tired and loses its fertile power.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fataaa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil food needed for healthy growth, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Aloo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it better for me to grow cassava and maize together on the same land instead of just maize alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Mixing crops helps protect your income. If dry weather hurts the fast-growing maize, the hardy cassava can still survive, ensuring you do not lose all your food and money.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ buɔ shika ni onáa lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ebaana ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo. Cassava ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu baanyɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haaa ofite oniyenii kɛ oshika fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my tomato plants when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra stems allows air and sunlight to reach the inner plant, preventing fungal diseases and forcing the plant to feed fruits instead of growing extra leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye aduawai moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ baai krokomɛi.

english: Why do the seeds I save from last season's harvest give me lower yield than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni baa shi fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can carry hidden diseases and lose vigor over time. Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to grow uniform plants that resist pests and produce bigger yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛhewalɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni akɛdu tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Healthy soil feels soft, holds moisture well after rain, and has a dark color. If you see earthworms and decaying leaves mixed in, it means the soil has living nutrients to feed your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, ni eyɛ su ni tsuɔ. Kɛji ona shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni egboi ni efutu mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni hiɛ ka ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What can I put on my land to make the soil rich again without buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can mix decomposed animal manure, dry leaves, and leftover crop stalks into the ground. This natural compost feeds the soil slowly and helps it hold onto water during dry periods.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egboi, baai ni egboi, kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii fiofio. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Why should I avoid burning all the cleared weeds and bushes on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys the natural cover that keeps the ground cool and moist. Leaving cleared weeds to rot on the soil protects it from scorching heat and slowly turns into free food for your next crop.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni fiofio lɛ, ehaa efeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha onibii ni obaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or that weeds are stealing its food. Adding compost or weeded soil around the base gives the plant the nourishment it needs to turn green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo jwɛi lɛ miiju niyenii lɛ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ baafata he koni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani etsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flower dropping happens when the plant gets stressed, usually by extreme heat, too little water, or sudden pest attacks. Giving them steady water at the roots and protecting them from strong winds helps the flowers stay on to become fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. nu fioo tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa trukaa Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and survive even when there is no rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and energy inside its thick underground tubers and drops some of its top leaves during dry spells to save moisture. This allows it to survive heat until the rains return.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni mli tse lɛ amli. ni okɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ekomɛi ashwie yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni hulutsoo akahi shi. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ latsaa lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do some of my crops produce large green leaves but very small fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi aduawai loo bulbs bibii waa lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen from raw manure or wrong fertilizers, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of sending food down into their fruits or roots.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii baa shi kɛya aduawai loo shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat lines instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in lines gives every crop its own space to catch sunlight and gather soil nutrients. It also makes it much easier for you and your laborers to walk through, weed, and harvest without damaging young plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo kɛ onitsulɔi lɛ hu akɛ nyɛbaatsɔ mli, nyɛjie jwɛi, ni nyɛkpaa nii. ni efiteee dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why is it bad to let weeds grow big before clearing them from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mahã jwɛi lɛ adara dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny ensures your crops get all the food they need to start strong.
ga: Jwɛi wuji juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are usually caused by a moisture-loving fungal disease called Black Pod. Excess shade and wet air make it spread quickly, so pruning overhead tree branches helps air flow through and keep the pods dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ baa. Shade babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, niji ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rainfall washes away soil nutrients or leaves the roots flooded and unable to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest so they don't rot in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. Leaving tubers in the ground too long, especially during heavy rains, makes them woody, watery, or prone to rotting.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Ni aaashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei, nu loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers when they face stress from heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate them. Providing adequate shade trees helps keep the soil cool and preserves flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi titri lɛ kɛ́ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni ehiii Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is my young oil palm tree producing only male flowers and no fruit bunches yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Young oil palm trees naturally produce male flowers first when they are still developing or experiencing stress. As the palm matures and receives sufficient water and balanced nutrients, it will start producing female flowers that grow into heavy oil palm bunches.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛmiiya hiɛ lolo loo amɛmiina haomɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da kwraa lɛ, enine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ. Ebaaje shishi ená fɔfɔi yei ni daa ni amɛfeɔ mu tsei ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when midday temperatures get too hot or dry, which damages the pollen inside the flower. Watering your plants consistently around the root area and mulching the soil with dry grass helps lower heat stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Enɛ baafite pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yɛ Root hei lɛ ahe kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo he haomɔ aba shi.

english: What is causing tiny holes and brown waste inside the center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Applying biopesticides or neem-based sprays directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning destroys the caterpillars before severe damage occurs.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji neem loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Why do my pepper crops droop and wilt in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, pepper leaves lose water faster through heat evaporation than the roots can pull up from warm soil. Covering the bare earth around the base of the plants with dry leaves or straw cools the ground and keeps water in the soil longer.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni dɔlɛ shwieɔ shi. Efa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young plantain suckers to grow around my main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? mi tso titri lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to steal water and food from the main plant, resulting in very small plantain bunches. Pruning back excess shoots so you keep only one main stem, one medium sucker, and one small shoot gives you the largest bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii waa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ fɛɛ bɔni afee ni okɛ tso lɛ yitso titri kome pɛ ahi shi. Ha tso 1 ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ tso bibioo 1 ni afee bouquet ni da fe fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber. Keeping the leaves off the damp soil also prevents fungal diseases and leads to much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What makes the leaves on my garden eggs roll up tightly and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by a plant virus spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids. Removing severely stunted plants immediately and controlling sap-sucking insects using neem oil or soapy water sprays stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni egbɔjɔ waa lɛ oya, ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Rain can wash nutrients out of topsoil, so adding organic manure or targeted fertilizer replenishes the soil and allows the leaves to regain their green color for healthy growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli eyi ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to spoil and turn dark just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛfee diŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots contain a lot of water and continue breathing heavily once dug up from the earth. When separated from the main stalk, natural internal changes cause rapid breakdown, which is why cassava needs to be eaten, sold, or processed into dry forms like gari or flour shortly after harvesting.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ cassava shishifãi amli. kɛ mumɔ ni wa kɛji atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he Adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔi ni baa mli lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ aye ŋmãa, ahɔ̃ɔ loo afee lɛ nɔ ko ni egbi, tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ, yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from excessive heat or dry soil. When the weather gets too hot, the plant discards flowers to conserve its remaining water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as temporary natural shade, keeping the young cocoa moist and protected during its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade be kukuoo ko. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli fũuɔ ni ebuɔ ehe yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my vegetables keep the soil damp for longer during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, forms a protective blanket over the soil that shields it from direct heat. This blocks the sun from evaporating water out of the ground, helping the soil stay cool and moist for longer periods.
ga: Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wooden stakes while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei akwɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and absorb as much sunlight as possible, which feeds the growing tuber under the ground. Elevating the vines off the ground also keeps leaves dry and prevents damp fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli edɔ baa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating large holes through my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye buji wuji kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs underneath cabbage leaves that hatch into hungry caterpillars. These caterpillars feed continuously on the leaves to gain energy for growth, requiring early detection or natural sprays like neem extract to control them.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ kaabaji baai ni efo lɛ ashishi lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ baai be fɛɛ be koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdara. Esa akɛ ana lɛ mra. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko tamɔ neem mli nu atsu nii. koni eye amɛnɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my field better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial microorganisms in their root nodes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the legume crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop.
ga: Nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap underneath the leaves. As these insects feed, they weaken the leaves and can spread plant viruses that cause the wrinkling pattern.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye niyenii lɛ Baai lɛ hu baa shi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tso lɛ mli hela ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I avoid putting too many seeds together into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ he?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the growing seedlings to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds out properly gives every individual plant enough room to build strong roots and yield larger crops.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni miida lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves will start to roll inward, turn pale, or curl during the hottest parts of the day when they lack water. Checking if the soil two inches below the surface feels dry is a clear sign your crop needs watering.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ baabɔi shwiemɔ kɛya mli. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli beni nu efo mli lɛ Kɛ́ okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji inchi enyɔ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi lɛ, eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia otso lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the water reaches the root zone before the heat causes high evaporation, keeping the plants strong and hydrated throughout the hot day.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani latsaa lɛ haa hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow when I water them too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns the crop roots by pushing out air in the soil. Without air, the roots cannot take up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni eeetsi kɛya he kroko lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if the irrigation water I use contains too much salt?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli ŋmei fa tsɔ?

english: Salty water creates a mineral buildup in the soil that burns plant roots and makes it difficult for crops to absorb water, leading to stunted growth and lower yields.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ haa sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu Ehaa amɛdaramɔ baa shi ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot days, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can drink it up. This causes temporary midday wilting, but the plant usually recovers by late evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko aaafee shwane fintiŋŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers mainly due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are wilting from heat or from a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ latsaa loo tso hela hewɔ?

english: Heat wilting occurs during the hottest afternoon hours and recovers by evening or after watering. Disease wilting remains constant even at night and is often accompanied by yellowing, spots, or rotting stems.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. ni ebaatsa lɛ gbɛkɛ loo yɛ nu ni eha lɛ sɛɛ Wilt hela lɛ yaa nɔ daa gbɛkɛ po. Ni bei pii lɛ, okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egboi lɛ ahe okadii baa.

english: How can I keep my soil moist for longer without spending extra money on water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni miwooo nu babaoo he nyɔmɔ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a process called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, lowers soil temperature, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching—tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: How does strong sunlight affect the growth and tuber size of my cassava crop?
ga: Te hulu la ni naa wa lɛ saa mi-cassava lɛ dalɛ kɛ e-tuber lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to produce energy through its leaves, which is then stored as starch in the roots to make large, healthy tubers under the ground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia Cassava koni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli akɛ starch koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do legumes like beans need less water than leafy vegetables like cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii biɔ nu fioo fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kaabɛji lɛ?

english: Leafy crops like cabbage have broad leaves that lose moisture quickly, whereas beans have deeper roots and leaf features that allow them to pull moisture from deep in the soil and withstand dry conditions better.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai, tamɔ kaabɛji, yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I dig deep to test my soil before planting new crops instead of just looking at the topsoil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni maka shikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani madu tsei heei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Testing soil below the surface gives you true assurance of its health. Deep soil testing shows nutrient levels, hardpans, and root-zone moisture that topsoil alone cannot reveal, helping you choose the right fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ni oooka lɛ haa onáa nɔmimaa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ehewalɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni mli kwɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, pans ni wa, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ ajie lɛ kpo lɛ kpo. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants have lush green leaves on top, but the tubers underground are small and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛmiifite?

english: Looking at surface leaves isn't enough to check crop health. Hidden soil pests, waterlogging, or poor root-zone aeration can destroy tubers beneath the ground even when the plant looks healthy above.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa ni akɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, nu ni damɔ shi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why do I need to inspect underneath the leaves of my pepper plants when the farm looks fine from afar?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ makwɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso ko baai ashishi kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ?

english: Harmful pests like aphids and whiteflies hide on the undersides of leaves long before damage shows on the top. Inspecting closely helps you spot and treat problems early before crops are destroyed.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ashishi be kakadaŋŋ dani nɔ ni efite lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa naagbai lɛ mra ni osaa amɛ. dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why is my stored yam rotting inside even though the skin looked completely healthy when I harvested it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miifite yɛ mli lɛ? Ni hewolo lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lolo kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: Rot-causing fungi and microscopic insects often enter through tiny invisible cracks made during harvest. Inspecting and curing yams properly in a dry, ventilated shade prevents hidden decay from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ naa gbɛ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. nibii ni anaaa ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Sweet potatoes lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsamɔ yɛ he ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees regularly even if they are growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ daa eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Regular pruning opens up the canopy so sunlight and air reach deep inside the tree. This prevents black pod disease and ensures the tree directs its strength into pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli daa lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ black pod hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa pod lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: Why is it important to weed my maize farm continuously as the season goes on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds grow constantly over time and steal nutrients, light, and water from your maize. Keeping up with regular weeding ensures your crop gets the full benefit of fertilizer and rain throughout its growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ o-corn lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow after heavy rains fall over several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As time passes and heavy rains continue, water washes essential nitrogen deep into the ground beyond the roots' reach. Applying fertilizer after prolonged heavy rain restores missing nutrients.
