ga: Beni be hoɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ biɔ nitrogen ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Extreme temperature changes stress crops, causing them to drop flowers to survive heat. Adding organic mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist during hot spells.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔii agbee shi koni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to water my garden deeply a few times a week rather than lightly every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi fe nu ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ha lɛ nu blɛuu daa leebi.

english: Light surface watering keeps roots near the top where they quickly dry out. Watering deeply encourages roots to grow far into the soil, securing deep moisture and making plants stronger during dry periods.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ, he ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ahi shi ni oha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli

english: Why should I space my plantain suckers far apart when setting up a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala plantain tsei lɛ amli beni miito shikpɔŋ hee he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures roots do not fight each other underground for food and water as they grow over time, leading to thicker stems and larger fruit bunches.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe akatswaa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as a natural umbrella, protecting the young cocoa trees from the heat while providing food and extra income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil where they could rot or catch diseases, and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs agboi ni daraa. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ. ni egbɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help bring back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with heavy leaves but produce tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni tsii shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or too much shade, it puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves on top instead of building tubers underground. Cassava needs full sunlight and balanced soil nutrients to direct energy downward.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo loo shade babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ, Cassava he miihia hulu la ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa koni ekɛha ehewalɛ lɛ aya shi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap. Spraying early with recommended treatments or organic neem extract helps protect the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii mra Loo organic neem mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei ahe.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my maize farm for just a few weeks cause my crop yield to drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your maize for the fertilizer, water, and sunlight in the soil. If weeds are allowed to grow alongside your crop early on, they steal the food meant for the maize, leading to weak plants and small cobs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-corn lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛfata onibii ahe mra. Nakai jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees turn dry and brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees lose water very quickly through their leaves when dry winds blow during the Harmattan. Having shade trees interplanted on the farm helps shield the cocoa leaves from excessive heat and slows down water loss from the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa yɛ harmattan be mli. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heat spell before the real rains arrive. If the seeds soak up initial water to start germinating but the soil dries out completely afterward, the seeds die underground and decompose.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ shwie nu shishijee mli koni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ shi shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How long does a cocoa tree actually take from planting until I can harvest my first pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ko kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni mikpaa mi klɛŋklɛŋ pod lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, though newer hybrid varieties developed in Ghana can start fruiting in about 2 to 3 years with proper care and good weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ Afee cocoa henɔi heei ni akɛfee ekome yɛ Ghana moŋ, shi ebaaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai ba.

english: Is there any safe way to make my cocoa trees produce pods faster than normal?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii oya fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: While you cannot force a plant to mature unnaturally fast, using recommended hybrid seeds, applying the right fertilizer at the right time, and keeping the farm weed-free can significantly speed up growth and early pod production.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ onyɛɛɛ onyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛdara oya yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli Kɛ ŋmɔ ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baanyɛ aha amɛdaramɔ kɛ pod feemɔ aya hiɛ waa.

english: What is the difference between the old cocoa trees my grandfather planted and the new hybrid cocoa seeds available today?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei momo ni mitsɛkwɛ̃ du lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Older cocoa varieties take longer to yield and grow very tall, whereas modern hybrid varieties produce pods much earlier, yield more pods per tree, and stay at a manageable height for easier harvesting.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ni amɛdaraa waa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ woɔ pods oya fe tsutsu lɛ. Ewoɔ yibii fe pods yɛ tso kome mli. kɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ koni ŋmaakpamɔ afee mlɛo.

english: My neighbor uses a different farming trick than what I was taught; is it safe for me to combine his method with mine?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ okwaayeli he ŋaa kroko tsuɔ nii fe nɔ ni mitsɔɔ lɛ. Ani ebaafee shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ gbɛi ni etsɔɔ nɔ etsuɔ ​​nii lɛ kɛ mi nɔ lɛ baafata he?

english: Combining different farming methods without knowing how they interact can harm your crops or waste money. It is best to test new ideas on a small patch of land first or ask an extension officer before applying them across your entire farm.
ga: Okwaayeli gbɛi srɔtoi ni okɛaafee ekome ni oleee bɔ ni nakai gbɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eye onibii awui loo efee shika fitemɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni aka susumɔi heei akwɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ, loo bi o-extension officer lɛ dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Are local traditional farming methods worse than the new scientific methods recommended by extension officers?
ga: Ani akutsoŋbii akusum nifeemɔi ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ ehiii kwraa fe jeŋ nilee gbɛi heei ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Traditional methods often protect the soil naturally, but modern extension practices use tested science to increase yield and control diseases faster. The best results often come from combining reliable local knowledge with proven scientific techniques.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Bei pii lɛ, blema gbɛi lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ fɔmɔ nifeemɔi kɛ jeŋ nilee ni aka akwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ ni ekɛkudɔ helai oya. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli nilee ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ jeŋ nilee mli ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli ni akɛaafata he lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers in my community get much higher cocoa yields even when we share the same soil type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ naa kookoo babaoo babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ wɔkɛ shikpɔŋ kome tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Higher yields are usually due to better farm management timing—such as pruning regular shade branches, weeding on schedule, and applying pest control before insects damage the young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ jɛɔ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nii, tamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni afoɔ daa lɛ hewɔ. Akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli dani kooloi bibii lɛ akpãtãa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop often happens when the tree lacks nutrients, water, or light, or when small insects attack the blossoms. Proper pruning to allow sunlight through and applying recommended cocoa fertilizers help the tree hold its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, nu loo la, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Tso lɛ he tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la atsɔ mli kɛ kookoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Do full-grown cocoa trees need full sunlight or do they still need shade trees around them?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ aloo amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lolo ni ebɔle amɛhe?

english: Mature cocoa trees prefer partial, filtered sunlight. Too much direct sun dries out the soil and stresses the tree, while too much shade traps moisture that causes fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ sumɔɔ hulu la ni mli tse fioo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha tso lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning low branches to improve air circulation and harvesting mature pods quickly helps control the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Ni aaafolɔ tsei lɛ amli fioo koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni akpa tsei ni eda lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling from poor soil nutrients rather than just lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ hewɔ? Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: If plant leaves turn yellow, pale, or stunted even during rainy weather, the soil is missing key nutrients. If the leaves only wilt during the hot afternoon and bounce back at night, the issue is lack of water.
ga: Kɛji tso baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli pɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa gbɛkɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ naagba lɛ ji nu ni bɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps them turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally restores nutrients to the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting virus-resistant stem cuttings recommended by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ŋmei baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Niji ni nyɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew holes in my maize leaves right at the center where new leaves open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli yɛ teŋgbɛ he ni baai heei lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs inside the central funnel of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved organic or chemical sprays into the leaf funnel stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic spray loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ awo baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving them steady moisture and balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my okra leaves wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: On very hot days, okra leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting. They usually recover in the evening once the sun goes down and temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Okra baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take longer to produce pods when they are planted in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fe be mli ni akwɛɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed under harsh full sun, which dries out their leaves and roots. Shade trees lower the temperature and keep moisture in the soil, allowing cocoa trees to grow steadily without getting burnt.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni ashãaa amɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my tomato seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, weak stems and small fruits. Dense leaves also trap moisture, making fungal diseases spread quickly.
ga: Beni Aduɔ Tomato He ni Ebɛŋkɛ Tsɔ Tomato kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomato yɛ tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii. Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How does placing dry grass around my yam mounds help the yam tubers grow bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi sweet potato pile lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering yam mounds with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture in the ground, and stops weeds from taking away the food your yam tubers need to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ha ŋmeii ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii ni he hiaa o-sweet potato shishifãi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh shoots growing at the bottom trunk of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso shishi lɛ?

english: Those shoots, called chupons or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main cocoa tree without producing many pods. Removing them ensures the tree puts all its energy into growing big pods on the main trunk.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons, loo suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baaa. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: How do I know which way is up when I plant cassava stems in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ odu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look at the small buds where leaves used to grow on the stem; those buds should point upwards towards the sky so the shoots can sprout easily above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. He ni baai lɛ daa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Which kind of plantain shoot should I dig up from my old farm to plant a new one?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni madu ehee?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers' that have thin, needle-like leaves and a broad bulb at the bottom, because they grow into stronger plants than 'water suckers' which have wide leaves early on.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘Sword Bud’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ yitso ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Ejaakɛ edaa ni etsɔɔ tso ni he wa fe ‘nu tso’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee bei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows corn pests to multiply in the dirt, leading to smaller harvests each time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni faaa pɛ akpaa be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green, or that the ground is too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight; without shade crops like plantain or trees to protect them, direct sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make energy, and lifting the foliage off the damp soil stops diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. Ni kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akafite tsei lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry, when the plant receives inconsistent water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: What causes small green worms to eat the inner leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the sweet central leaves of young corn plants.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Why do people spread dry grass on top of the soil around pepper plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Pepper tso yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Spreading dry grass keeps the soil cool, traps moisture in the ground so it doesn't dry out fast in the sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni hulu lɛ akagbi oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my vegetable leaves get dark spots when I pour water on them late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ afɔ nu awo mli gbɛkɛ lɛ, aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ diji lɛ?

english: Leaving water on leaves overnight creates wet conditions where fungal diseases grow easily, leading to leaf spots and rotting.
ga: Nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa oya. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do you recommend that I plant groundnuts or beans after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛji akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the ground, but plants like groundnuts and beans put natural nitrogen back into the dirt, making the soil healthy again for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in small roots. Proper spacing gives the tubers room to swell and grow big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha yitso lɛ adara ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are small worms eating the middle of my young corn plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the growing center of the corn. Catching them early and applying approved treatments or neem oil prevents them from destroying the field.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔji.

english: How does covering the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass help them during dry weather?
ga: Te sũ ni akɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a blanket (called mulch) that shades the dirt from the sun, trapping moisture in the soil longer and preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch) ni tsiɔ muji naa kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer immediately when I plant my seeds or wait a few weeks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ oodu dumɔwui loo ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: It is usually best to wait a week or two after the seed sprouts, as the plant needs to develop initial roots strong enough to actually absorb and use the fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ ehi akɛ omɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná shishijee shishifãi ni mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I keep planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii fioo yɛ be mli ni miyaa nɔ miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose vigor over time and carry diseases from previous seasons. Fresh certified seeds are selected to resist pests and produce higher yields under local conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ekɛ helai ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ aba. Ahalaa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does burning my land before planting cause my soil to dry out faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ haa egbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial organisms that keep the soil soft and spongy. Leaving cleared vegetation to decay naturally helps the soil hold water much better.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I pinch off the tiny extra stems growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso bibioo lɛ? Extra ni miida yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Removing those extra side shoots directs all the plant's energy and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa tso yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each maize plant its own space allows the roots to grow deep and produce larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my field before I plant young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the tender cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Okɛ ŋmɔlɔ awo koko tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil around the roots is holding too much water, which starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds helps extra water drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ efo. Shishifãi lɛ toɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with neem oil or insect solution helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiitsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops every year even though I clear and plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miduɔ nii yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the exact same field year after year removes all the specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops—such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize—puts good food back into the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. lɛ baaha niyenii kpakpa aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ

english: How do I know if my crop field needs animal manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia kooloi ashikpɔŋ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: If your plant leaves look pale green instead of dark green and grow very slowly, the soil lacks nutrients. Animal manure builds long-term soil life and holds moisture, while fertilizer gives plants an instant boost of food.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do worms always hide deep inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The center funnel contains the newest, tenderest leaves that are easy for pests like fall armyworms to chew. Hiding deep inside also protects the worms from hot sun and birds.
ga: Baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe fɛɛ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ oya lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ ekɛ ehe tee mli shɔŋŋ lɛ hu buɔ ŋmei lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rainwater collects around them in low ground or when tiny pests in the soil make cuts in the skin. Making high ridges keeps the tubers out of standing water.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye hewolo lɛ awui. Gbɛjegbɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haaa yitso lɛ akabote nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look healthy above ground but produce empty shells with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi eewo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty shells happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are forming underground. Adding wood ash or lime to the soil gives the pods the strength they need to fill up with nuts.
ga: Husks ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni pods lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, intense sunlight when they are small. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a natural umbrella, protecting the soft cocoa leaves until the tree is mature enough to withstand heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: The main plantain tree shares all its food and water with every sucker growing around it. Removing the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main tree to keep enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain wulu lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa eniyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ toɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest produce weaker plants than the seeds I originally bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni mihe shishijee lɛ?

english: Many modern crop seeds are specially bred hybrids designed to grow strong only in their first planting. Saving seeds from that harvest causes the next generation of crops to lose their strength, disease protection, and high yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei dumɔwui babaoo ji tsei ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ haa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe waaa. Helai atsimɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they spend all their energy growing upward to fight for sunlight instead of using that energy to build broad stems and large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ peeɔ ngma tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ ngma a bumi nguahi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light green and yellow before it even forms corn ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ dani etsɔ toi po lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen in the soil, which frequently happens after heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil becomes exhausted from continuous farming.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year give me smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water sitting in the soil for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi rapidly cause them to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Extreme weather heat or irregular watering stresses the tomato plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy and survive rather than spending resources on producing fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshɛrɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛwo yibii

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if my plants are taller than the weeds?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and fertilizer from underground long before they grow tall enough to block sunlight, effectively starving your crop's roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the inside funnel of my young maize leaves, and how does it affect the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miitutua mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli gbɛi lɛ? Ni te enaa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm target the tender growing center of young maize because it is soft and nutritious, which destroys the plant's ability to form new leaves and properly grow corn ears.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ niyenii kpakpa Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo baai heei kɛ ŋmãa toi ni sa lɛ.

english: If I put more fertilizer on my maize, will it make the crops grow faster and produce more food?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ani ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Adding extra fertilizer beyond what the plant needs does not mean more yield. Over-feeding crops can burn their roots, cause them to grow excessive leaves instead of grain, and waste your money on inputs you do not need.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli fe bɔ ni ehe hiaa lɛ lɛ, etsɔɔɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo. Tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshishifãi lɛ ashã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa babaoo tsɔ yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. kɛ shika ni ofiteɔ yɛ nibii ni afee ni he ehiaaa bo lɛ ahe

english: Why is my tomato plant growing very tall with big green leaves, but it is not producing any flowers or tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo tomato ko bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: When a plant receives too much food or nitrogen, it puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves rather than making fruit. Over-nourishing the crop causes it to put on weight without giving you an actual harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná niyenii loo nitrogen babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Kɛ́ ahã ŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii fe nine lɛ, ebaaha egbɔjɔ ni enáaa yibiiwoo diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Is it better to feed my crops fertilizer every single week or only at specific growth times?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii daa otsi loo yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli pɛ?

english: Crops only need nutrients at specific stages of their life. Feeding them continuously every week wastes fertilizer and overloads the soil, causing crop health issues rather than better growth.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛshihilɛ be pɔtɛɛ mli pɛ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be daa otsi lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii fe nine. Ekɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai baa tsei amli moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cassava stems bend and fall over easily after I add extra manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi efata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too much manure causes cassava plants to grow top-heavy stems very quickly. This rapid growth makes the stems weak and heavy, causing them to fall over in weak winds and damaging the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ amɛhe ŋmeii ni tsii fe nine. Nɛkɛ dalɛ ni yaa oya nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni etsiiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, egbee kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei fitemɔ baa

english: Can giving my cocoa trees too much manure actually cause them to die?
ga: Ani ŋmeii babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ agbe kookoo tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, over-applying manure or chemical fertilizer creates a high salt buildup in the soil that damages the tree's roots, preventing them from taking up water and potentially killing the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni fiteɔ tsei shishifãi Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu ni baanyɛ agbe tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow even though I give them plenty of water every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants water every day when they do not need it suffocates their roots. Just like overeating, overwatering creates unhealthy conditions in the soil that cause root rot and leaf yellowing.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu ha otso lɛ daa gbi be mli ni ehe ehiaaa lɛ lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ fe nine lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛi ni ehiii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Will watering my vegetable crop constantly during the dry season guarantee a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani Mi-Aduawai lɛ Ahe Nu ni Miaaya Nɔ Yɛ Hɔmɔ Be lɛ Mli lɛ Baaha Makpa Nikpamɔ Kpeteŋkpele?

english: Watering too much can wash away soil nutrients and drown the root system. Crops need balanced watering; excessive moisture leads to disease and poor fruit development.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli. Nu ni sa he miihia tso lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ helai kɛ aduawai ni ehiii baa.

english: Why am I spending so much money on farm inputs but not seeing any extra profit during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ shika babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe shi minaaa sɛɛnamɔ kroko ni fata he lɛ? Nikpamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Buying and applying more fertilizer or chemicals than your crop can handle creates unnecessary debt. Over-applying inputs increases your farm expenses without increasing your yields, leaving you with less profit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai babaoo ni okɛbaatsu nii fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii lɛ kɛ nyɔmɔ ni he ehiaaa baa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔmɔwoo yaa hiɛ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sɛɛnamɔ fioo pɛ obaaná.

english: Will spraying my cabbage farm with insect chemicals every week keep it safe and give me more yield?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa otsi lɛ, ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ebaaha yibii babaoo aba?

english: Spraying chemicals constantly when pests are not present builds up heavy financial debt from buying chemicals without adding any extra value to your crop harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ lɛ kɛ shika he nyɔmɔ babaoo baa kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni aheɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko fataaa onibii ahe.

english: If I plant my yam seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm plot?
ga: Kɛ midu sweet potatoes yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for the same soil food and water. This competition means every plant gets overloaded trying to survive, leading to small tubers and poor yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa nitsumɔhei fɛɛ tsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leaves above ground look bushy and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? He ni baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves on top instead of pushing food down into the tubers. Loosening the soil and using balanced soil nutrients helps the roots grow thick.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsi niyenii kɛya shi kɛya ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmei ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ mli ni akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants compete with each other for food, water, and sunlight. This makes them grow tall and weak, resulting in smaller cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo ko baa loo eko kwraa bɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as natural shields, protecting the tender cocoa leaves from sun damage and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot or the ground lacks moisture, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from dying, which stops fruit from forming.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Enɛ baatsi yibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look limp and tired in the afternoon sun, but wake up in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni etɔ lɛ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ? Shi te shi leebi?

english: In intense heat, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the dirt. Drooping is their natural way of minimizing sun exposure until the air cools down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ohiŋmɛii ni oootsi kɛjɛ ohe lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ oha hulu ni okɛkpeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee fɛ̃i.

english: Tiny holes are a sign that insects or caterpillars are eating your plants. Spraying natural solutions like neem water or recommended pest treatments deters insects before they destroy the whole leaf.
ga: Buji bibii ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii miiye otsei lɛ. Akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kooloi bibii anaa dani amɛfite baa muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to swap and plant different crops on my field every new season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa be hee lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously lets pests and diseases that prefer that crop multiply in the dirt. Changing crops starves those pests and allows the soil to rebuild missing nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aya nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ama ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot shortly after I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bafee bɔdɔɔ ni egbo beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get bruised during digging or are stored in warm places without air blowing through. Storing them in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn keeps them firm and fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ amɛ loo akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni loo lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni efee ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is fully ready to be cut down from the tree?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ plantain ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Plantains are ready when the fingers become plump and round, losing their sharp side edges, and the top leaves of the plant start turning yellow naturally.
ga: Dare baafee klalo beni oniji lɛ egbɔ ni efee kokroo lɛ. Ha sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ aje ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ aje shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries up the soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves on maize usually means the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Applying the right fertilizer early in the season helps the plant maintain healthy green leaves to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baa ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni wa aba.

english: What happens to my cassava crop if I plant the cuttings very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni he akafite?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin while producing very small tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and getting yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases, or by excessive heat and dry conditions. Controlling insect pests early and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be mli Mra Be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from too little water, too much water, or extreme heat. Maintaining consistent soil moisture with mulching helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu fioo tsɔ, nu babaoo, loo latsaa babaoo hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it bad for my farmland if I burn all the cleared bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei bibii ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush destroys useful organic matter in the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms like earthworms. Letting cleared plant material decompose naturally enriches the soil and retains moisture for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. Harvesting too early yields soft, watery tubers that spoil quickly during storage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ kɛ wain tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa bulbs ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last harvest fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were damaged by insects like weevils, stored in damp places, or taken from hybrid plants. Storing dry seeds in airtight containers or using certified seeds ensures high germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii fite amɛ. Kɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. loo ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome mli Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, known as water sprouts or chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk and branches. Removing them encourages the cocoa tree to direct its energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ water shoots loo chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ewoɔ cacao tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ awo ŋmeii ni mli wa amli.

english: Why shouldn't I just cut my big harvested yams into small pieces for seeds like my father taught me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli bibii bibii? Ni odu dumɔwui tamɔ bɔ ni Ataa tsɔɔ bo lɛ?

english: Cutting big yams creates open wounds that easily catch soil diseases, causing the seed to rot before it can sprout. Using whole, clean seed yams or improved seedling methods gives the plant a healthier start without rots.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ, ehaa pilamɔi ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni he tse, ni eye emuu loo dumɔwui ahe gbɛi ni atsake lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: How can tiny yam seedlings raised in a nursery grow into big yams underground?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso bibioo ko ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli lɛ aaatsɔ ŋmei tso agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Nursery seedlings start with strong, clean roots that are free from soil diseases. Once planted in good soil, their leaves catch sunlight to produce energy, which the plant stores underground to form a large tuber.
ga: Nursery dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni he tse ni hela bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do yams need high soil mounds instead of being planted on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil so the tuber can expand easily without resistance. High mounds also allow excess rainwater to drain away, stopping the roots and tubers from sitting in water and rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote nu mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yams on the exact same piece of farmland every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yams repeatedly on the same land drains the specific soil nutrients yams need and allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Adumɔ ŋmɔtɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do yam plants grow bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mihaa wain tso lɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the tuber grow bigger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ baa hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulb lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Why are my yam plants growing plenty of leafy green vines but producing small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei babaoo ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer or planting in overly rich soil forces the yam to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of building up starch in the tuber below.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei loo amɛdumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo nɔ Enɛ baaha sweet potatoes kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee starch yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do young crop seedlings dry up and die if I plant them in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes young leaves to lose water faster than their small, newly planted roots can absorb it from the soil, leading to severe heat stress and death.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ tsei ni adu ehee lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa kɛ gbele baa.

english: Why is it important to separate damaged yams from healthy ones right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmeii ni efite kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Rot and fungal diseases on damaged yams can quickly spread to healthy ones in the barn through contact, ruining a large portion of your stored harvest.
ga: Rot kɛ fungus ni yɔɔ sweet potatoes ni efite lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛya mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛaashɛ he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ nibii ni okɛto lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting white shoots in the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii yɛŋ shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from resting after a few months. Storage warmth triggers them to use their stored energy to grow new shoots for the next season.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn yellow and dry up towards the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean the plant has finished making food and has moved all its energy into the underground tuber. It is a natural sign that the yam is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe nihoomɔ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi akɛ atomo eda ni esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Can I plant other food crops under my coconut trees, or will the coconut roots choke them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmei tso shishi? Aloo ani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ?

english: You can safely grow crops like cassava, plantain, or cocoyam under coconut trees because coconut roots go deep while leafy crops feed mainly near the surface. Planting compatible crops together maximizes your land without harming your coconut trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei tamɔ ŋmei, plantain, loo kookoo yɛ ŋmei tsei ashishi shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ nu lɛ hiɛ titri. Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni efiteee ŋmei tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct harsh sunlight and hot winds. Keeping large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields tender leaves from burning and keeps soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil or lacks water. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and build big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa lɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ mli. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ni mli tse ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ toi wuji.

english: When heavy rain creates standing water, cassava roots suffocate from a lack of air in the soil and rot. Building high soil mounds or raised ridges allows excess water to drain away quickly so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ekɛ nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi baa. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ fitemɔ hewɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces them to steal food and water from the main mother tree. Cutting away all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, no haa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, which catches more light and prevents fungal rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa la babaoo boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or attack by microscopic insect pests. Watering regularly and spraying safe pest controls keeps the flowers attached so they can grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from drying up in the heat, and stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients from your tomatoes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa be mli. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tomato mli

english: Why do dark spots start forming on the bottom leaves of my tomato plants after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Rain splashes soil containing microscopic fungal spores onto lower leaves, causing spot diseases. Trimming the lowest leaves and avoiding splashing water directly on leaves keeps the plant dry and disease-free.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ hela baa hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajie nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbi ni helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my farm soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have friendly microbes on their roots that trap nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop leaves when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiiho amɛhe yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high temperatures. Without shade crops like plantains or forest trees to shield them, intense sun burns their soft leaves and drains their moisture, causing the leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on all their leaves to manufacture food for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking lifts the vine into the sunlight and protects the leaves from rots and soil-borne diseases that spread on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa ni gbɛɔ eshwaa sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing starting from the middle tip of older maize leaves usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow leaves, so when it runs out, the plant starves from the bottom leaves upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting cowpeas or groundnuts helps my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi-ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume crop dies, that stored nitrogen remains behind as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei gboi Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ baaya nɔ afee niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots or suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: A plantain root system has limited food and water. If too many suckers grow at once, they steal nutrients from the main stem, resulting in smaller bunches; keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ plantain shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: How do I know if my cassava stem cuttings are healthy enough to sprout well after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava ni afo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Good cassava planting stems should come from mature, disease-free plants, be firm, and leak a milky sap immediately when cut. Stems that are dry, brittle, or full of tiny insect holes inside will rot or fail to sprout shoots.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpai ajɛ tsei ni eda jogbaŋŋ, ni hela bɛ mli, ni yɔɔ loo ni wa kɛ nu ni hoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji afo lɛ amli. Tsoi ni egbi, ni shwieɔ shi, loo ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli Enyɛŋ egbo loo ekwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from under the soft young leaves. As the damaged leaf tries to grow, it twists and curls up tightly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni baai ni efite lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara lɛ Etsɔ ehe ni ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and flat before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually because of irregular water supply. When the soil swings from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot move calcium to the tip of the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil if I plant right after the very first small rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first shower often leaves the deeper soil hot and dry underneath. If no more rain falls immediately after, the seed absorbs just enough moisture to start sprouting, but then dries out and rots in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ eshishi. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is like dry salt—plants cannot drink or eat dry powders directly through their roots. Soil moisture is required to dissolve the fertilizer so root hairs can absorb it, and without moisture, concentrated dry fertilizer can actually burn root tips.
ga: Fertilizer tamɔ ŋmei ni egbi. Tsei nyɛŋ anu loo amɛye powda ni egbi lɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mli ewo muji lɛ hu baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi.

english: When the bottom leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the tips, it means the plant is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will feed the crop and restore green growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have natural nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next maize crop naturally.
