ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their young leaves dry out and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains next to young cocoa creates protective shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ he lɛ haa shade ni buɔ mɔ he baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni cocoa shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high heat or inconsistent watering. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating successfully, so keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch enough sunlight for making food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ahe hewalɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow around a single plantain stem causes them to compete for water and soil nutrients. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one strong replacement shoot, ensuring the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain tso kome pɛ he lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ feɔ ŋmei agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the plant from becoming permanently stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi daa.

english: Ragged holes and tiny green droppings inside the central shoot of maize are clear signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying an recommended control product early into the central funnel will stop them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ afɔse mra. Yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekpaa dani efoɔ he ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable leaves during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ oooha aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ nu yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Watering in full sun causes rapid evaporation, so water dries up before reaching the roots. Additionally, droplets left on leaves can magnify sunlight and scorch tender plant tissue, so watering early morning or late evening is best.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la oya. No hewɔ lɛ, nu gbiɔ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni eshã tso lɛ mli fãji. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause standing water and poor drainage, oxygen is cut off from the roots, allowing soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to protect them and keep the ground moist until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Wet and humid weather causes a fungus to attack cocoa pods, leading to Black Pod disease. Pruning tree branches lets sunlight and air in, and removing infected pods stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ black pod hela aba. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the middle tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downwards when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like NPK or Urea early in the growth stage helps the plant turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni edɔ waa.

english: Why are there small ragged holes and dark dirt inside the centers of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii ni etse ehe kɛ muji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center funnel of corn plants are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the fresh leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide into the central funnel kills the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft and rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater pools around them in flat or heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which flows down to build larger, heavier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Enɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, water supply is irregular, or the soil lacks nutrients. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizer keep the soil stable so flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii bɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ tomato.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves, or by viruses they spread. Spraying early with recommended treatments protects the fresh shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Mra ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ abu ŋmeii heei ahe.

english: Too many extra shoots steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only the main tree, one medium shoot, and one small shoot ensures large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain wulu lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii Tso titri lɛ pɛ, teŋgbɛ tso 1 kɛ tso bibioo 1 ji nɔ ni eshwɛ, ni ehaa yibii wuji baa.

english: Why are my cowpea plants flowering while they are still very small and low to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni amɛji bibii waa ni amɛba shi kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas flower too early if they experience drought or heat stress as a survival response. Adequate moisture and planting at the start of the rain season allow the plant to grow enough leaves before producing pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo lɛ, cowpea baawo fɔfɔi oya tsɔ kɛji ekɛ hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe. Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná baai ni fa bɔ ni sa dani ŋmeii lɛ aje kpo.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off due to stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks. Proper soil care, maintaining shade, and protecting flowers from harmful bugs help them stay on the tree to turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haomɔ hewɔ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ahebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do cocoa flowers actually turn into pods on the tree?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Tiny beneficial insects called midges visit the small blossoms on the trunk and branches to pollinate them. Once pollinated, the flower fertilizes and gradually expands into a cocoa pod over several months.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baasara fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. yɛ tsei akui kɛ tsei aniji anɔ kɛha pollination Beni pollination Fɔfɔi lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ni fiofio lɛ Egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the main trunk instead of just the top branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ moŋ fe niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on old wood and trunks so the heavy cocoa pods can hang securely without snapping thin branches, making it easier for ground insects to reach and pollinate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsei momoi kɛ tsei akutsei anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni tsii lɛ afɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni akumɔɔɔ niji bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ baanyɛ aya jɛmɛ ni amɛfee pollin.

english: What causes my cocoa trees to produce hundreds of blossoms but almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ shi eshwɛ fioo ni ebaawo fɔfɔi?

english: This usually happens when there are not enough pollinators like midges around, or when the tree lacks water and plant food to feed all the blossoms. Keeping natural shade and organic matter on the farm encourages pollinators and feeds the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi, tamɔ midges lɛ faaa, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ efo. Adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ kooloi ahewalɛ koni amɛwo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛha amɛ niyenii.

english: Is it safe to spray natural leaf or herbal teas on my cocoa trees when they begin to blossom?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tii baai anɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ?

english: Yes, mild organic solutions made from natural plants like lemon grass or neem can act as safe repellents against harmful bugs without damaging delicate blossoms or harming beneficial pollinators.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei tamɔ lemongrass loo neem fee lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni efiteee fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ loo efiteee pollinators ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui.

english: How does dry weather affect the flowers on my cocoa trees during the harmattan season?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Hot, dry air dries out the stems of the blossoms, causing the tree to shed its flowers to save water. Mulching the soil around the tree roots helps hold moisture so the flowers can survive the dry period.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Ha tsei ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my cocoa trees as soon as flowering starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni kookoo tso lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi kɛji efɔ fɔfɔi pɛ.

english: Weeds compete with cocoa trees for water and soil food during a time when the tree needs extra energy to feed its blossoms. Clearing weeds ensures all nutrients go directly to growing strong pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ he hiaa hewalɛ kroko koni amɛkɛye amɛbua fɔfɔi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: What are those tiny flies hovering around my cocoa blossoms, and should I kill them?
ga: ŋmeii bibii Mɛni ji nakai nibii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ? mi kokoo fɔfɔi Ni ani esa akɛ magbe amɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are usually cocoa midges, which are essential friends to the farmer. They pollinate the blossoms so pods can grow, so you should avoid spraying strong chemicals that kill them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji kookoo ŋmeii akui. ni ji okwaafoi anaanyo ko ni he hiaa Amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okpa tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ.

english: When is the safest time to spray my farm so I do not ruin the flower blossoms?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekawo fɔfɔi?

english: It is best to avoid heavy chemical spraying during full flowering periods, especially in the early morning when pollinators are active. If you must spray for pests, aim for late afternoon or use gentle, non-chemical options.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he. Yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ waa lɛ Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ. Kɛ ehe bahia ni okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ koni ojie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Aim kɛha shwane mli. Aloo okɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsofa bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need extra fertilizer to keep their blossoms alive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If leaves look pale yellow and blossoms fall off in large numbers despite good rainfall, the tree lacks nutrients. Adding organic compost or appropriate cocoa fertilizers gives the tree strength to retain its flowers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fɔfɔi babaoo efo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ. tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crop field early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil absorbs the moisture before the hot afternoon heat can evaporate it, giving the plant roots water to survive the day.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi náa nu yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my bean plants start wilting and turning yellow when the ground gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Bean plants have shallow roots and need regular moisture to take up nutrients from the soil. When the soil dries out, the plant cannot absorb food, causing its leaves to turn yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii kpakpai. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on the soil around my young crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi mashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɔle mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so it does not evaporate quickly in the heat, and prevents weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, giving them the cool environment they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: What will happen if I plant my crop seeds very close to one another in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce very small harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haa yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the upper leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an important plant food. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help your maize stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow very quickly and steal the nutrients, water, and space meant for your crops, leaving your plants weak and starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ he ko ni okɛbaakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my crop leaves, and how does it hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai anɔ Ni te eyeɔ tsei awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles eating the foliage. Leaves act as the plant's food factory, so damaged leaves reduce the crop's ability to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. No hewɔ lɛ, baai ni efite lɛ haaa tso lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Can I plant the white beans I bought for cooking from the local market on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛŋ ni miheɔ kɛha nihoomɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Market beans are usually meant for cooking and may not sprout properly or resist local plant diseases. It is better to use certified planting seeds from agricultural extension stores for a reliable harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ jarayeli ŋmeii lɛ koni akɛhoo nii ni ekolɛ amɛkwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli tsei ahe helai anɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni adu ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ shwapoi amli lɛ baatsu nii kɛha ŋmaa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: How do I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well after I plant on the same farm land for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every season. Over time, the soil loses these essential nutrients and becomes weak, which causes plants to produce smaller yields unless the nutrients are replaced.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ laajeɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ wooo yibii fioo ja akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsake.

english: What should I do if my crops are failing on my current piece of land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ nɔ bianɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can either clear and move to a new piece of fertile land or stay on the current land and add soil improvers like manure, compost, or fertilizers to restore the strength of the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi ohe ni oya shikpɔŋ hee ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Aloo hi shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What can I add to my soil to help my crops grow strong and healthy?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata mishikpɔŋ lɛ he koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: You can add organic matter like animal manure and decomposed plant waste, or chemical fertilizers. These materials feed the soil with nutrients that plants need to build strong roots and good yields.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi aŋmei kɛ tsei ni egboi ni etse amɛhe lɛ afata he. loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli Nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some crops grow very well on one part of my farm but struggle on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi amɛnaa amanehulu yɛ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil context changes across different areas. One part of your land may naturally have rich plant food and moisture, while another section may lack key nutrients needed by that specific crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ tsakeɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi. Ekolɛ tsei aniyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ekolɛ fã kroko hu bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha nakai ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I improve poor soil so that it can support crops that normally refuse to grow there?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni bei pii lɛ amɛkpooɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, by adding the specific plant foods and organic material that the soil is missing, you can transform weak soil into a healthy environment that supports demanding crops.
ga: Anáa enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ otsake shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ofee shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni fiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How can I know if my soil has enough nutrients before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: You can have an extension officer take a soil sample for testing. A laboratory analysis shows exactly what nutrients are present in your soil so you know what is missing before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha extension nitsulɔ ko abua shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko naa koni ekɛka lɛ akwɛ. Laboratory mlipɛimɔ tsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli faŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ole nɔ ni elaaje dani odu.

english: Why is it useful to do a soil test instead of just buying any fertilizer from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ moŋ fe ni ooohe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil testing tells you the exact nutrient levels in your farm land. This prevents you from wasting money on fertilizers your soil does not need and helps you buy only what will actually help your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ baatsi shika ni okɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ naa. Ni ehaa oheɔ nibii ni baaye abua onibii diɛŋtsɛ pɛ.

english: How do nutrients in the earth affect how fast my vegetables mature?
ga: Te niyenii ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni aduawai daa oya lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When soil contains balanced plant food, crop roots easily absorb the nourishment they need, allowing the plants to grow continuously, stay green, and yield on time.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tsei aniyenii ni sa Tse shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa daa. Ha ohe afee ŋmɔŋ ni ofee nibii yɛ be naa

english: What causes my crops to turn light green or yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the soil is hungry and lacks essential plant foods like nitrogen, meaning the crop is starving even if it has plenty of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ.

english: How will knowing my soil's nutrient levels help my farm in the long run?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni mile lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Understanding your soil allows you to plan crop rotations and fertilizer use properly every year, keeping your land productive season after season without degrading the earth.
ga: Kɛ́ onu oshikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa otoɔ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ afi fɛɛ afi. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ofiteee shibɔlemɔ ŋulami lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans before maize make my soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the maize is planted afterwards, it uses that trapped nitrogen to grow much faster.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni abaadu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli Ekɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ oya babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under the full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and cool moisture, protecting the cocoa while it establishes roots.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he yɛ be mli ni etswaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving them proper space ensures each crop gets enough resources to grow big fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and increasing tuber size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How many suckers should I leave attached to one plantain stand?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ yɛ plantain tso kome nɔ?

english: It is best to leave only three shoots: the main fruiting parent stem, one medium sucker, and one small shoot. Leaving too many suckers causes them to share food, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii etɛ pɛ: tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ. Sucker kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ ŋmei bibioo kome Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛja niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get steady water. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant keep its flowers and set fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets light and air in to dry the pods and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck juices from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Using organic neem oil or recommended sprays helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I wait too long to harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water during heavy rains makes the soil too wet and suffocates the cassava roots, causing underground rot. It is best to harvest mature cassava before the rain peak.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa ŋmei ni eda lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ ayashɛ he ni fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I write down my farm expenses and harvest yields when I can just remember them in my head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ he saji lɛ? Be ni mikaiɔ yɛ miyitsoŋ lɛ?

english: Keeping simple records on paper helps you track whether you are making a profit or a loss at the end of the season. It also helps you see patterns year after year so you know which practices make you money and where you are losing income.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Yɛ wolo nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ kɛji oná sɛɛnamɔ loo ofite nɔ ko yɛ be lɛ naagbee. Eyeɔ ebua bo hu ni onaa nɔkwɛmɔnii afi fɛɛ afi. No hewɔ lɛ ole nifeemɔi ni haa onáa shika kɛ he ni ofiteɔ shika yɛ.

english: Why do buyers pay me so much less money when my harvested rice has broken grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo kwraa yɛ be mli ni mikpamɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii efo lɛ?

english: Buyers pay less for broken rice because market customers prefer whole grains, which cook better and look nicer. Broken grains also spoil faster during storage, so traders lower the price to cover their own financial risk.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni akumɔ he nyɔmɔ fioo ejaakɛ jara nɔ jarayelɔi lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ yɔɔ fɛo. Nibii ni akumɔ lɛ hu fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jarayelɔi baa jara nɔ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshika he naagbai lɛ aba mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice field so the grains stay strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the crop heads turn a golden color. Leaving rice in the field for too long under the hot sun makes the grains dry out completely and become brittle, which causes them to shatter and break when milled.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa kɛ́ atsɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, egbɛɔ ni efoɔ.

english: Why do my rice grains crack when I dry them in direct sun after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛji akɛ amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When damp rice is exposed to intense mid-day sun, the outside of the grain dries much faster than the inside, causing heat stress cracks inside the kernel. Drying grains gradually on a tarpaulin and turning them regularly prevents this cracking.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ wo hulu la ni naa wa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa fe emligbɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo haomɔ mli fãa yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ gbi blɛoo yɛ tarp nɔ ni otsake lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi ŋmãa lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my grain is dry enough for market without using expensive machines?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ni tsɔnei ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: A simple way is the 'salt test' or the 'bite test'. If you bite a grain and it snaps cleanly with a sharp sound, it is dry. If it feels soft or flattens between your teeth, it still holds water and needs more drying.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ji 'ŋoo kaa' loo 'ŋmei kaa'. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔ dumɔwu ko mli ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwie mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaagbi. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nu lolo ni ehe miihia ni agbi babaoo.

english: What causes my bagged crops to go bad or change quality while sitting in storage?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ fiteɔ loo etsakeɔ amɛhe beni mitaraa nitoohe lɛ?

english: High moisture and lack of airflow are the main causes. If grain is bagged while still slightly damp, mold grows and heat builds up inside the bag, which ruins the color, smell, and market value of the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni amɛmli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ, Mold daa ni dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe su, amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ kɛ jarayeli jara.

english: What can I do to stop my harvested crops from getting ruined when transporting them to the market buyer?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikpamɔ lɛ akafite beni mikɛyaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Pack your produce tightly in strong, clean bags, load them on flat surfaces without over-stacking, and cover them with a canvas tarp. This protects the crop from heat, rain, and physical crushing during transit along bumpy roads.
ga: Okɛ o-fruits kɛ vegetables lɛ awo kotokui ni mli wa ni he tse mli jogbaŋŋ. Okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni ekɛ nɔ ko akafee nɔ ko. ni akɛ tarpaulin haa nɔ Enɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ shoofeemɔ he beni akɛ amɛ yaa gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it hard to sell my farm produce if I leave damaged or discolored grains mixed with good ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ minibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni efite loo ni amɛhe su etsake ni dumɔwui kpakpai yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie shi lɛ?

english: Traders want uniform and clean produce because it sells faster to customers. A few discolored or broken grains make the whole batch look bad, giving the buyer a reason to demand a big discount or reject the load entirely.
ga: Jarayelɔi miitao nibii ni amɛfeɔ daa, ni he tse ejaakɛ amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ oya. Nibii ni etsake fioo loo ni ekumɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ naa yiŋtoo ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛbi ni ajie amɛ jara babaoo loo amɛkpoo jatsu lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do insects attack my harvested grain more easily when the grains are already broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ kooloi bibii baatutua ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ kɛji ejara mli pɛ lɛ?

english: The hard outer shell of a whole grain acts like a protective skin against insects. When a grain is broken or cracked, the soft starch inside is exposed, making it easy for pests to feed, multiply, and ruin the store.
ga: Ŋmaa lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe. Beni ŋmaa lɛ mli gbala loo egbala lɛ Abaagbele ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛaaye nii, amɛshwere, ni amɛfite shwapoi.

english: Why does my rice turn into powder or small broken pieces when I take it to the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice lɛ tsɔɔ powda loo bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛya tsɔne ni akɛfeɔ pɛnte lɛ mli?

english: Excessive breakage during milling happens when the grain was either dried unevenly, harvested too late, or milled when it was too hot. Ensuring proper field drying and letting grain cool before milling protects the kernel strength.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji ŋmaa lɛ gĩ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. akpa sɛɛ tsɔ loo kɔla beni edɔ waa Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni edɔ dani ashɛreɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmaa lɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I plant my crops at specific distances so their leaves eventually touch each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fioo koni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When neighboring crop leaves grow close enough to meet and touch overhead, they create a shade canopy. This canopy blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, which stops weeds from growing and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kɛ tso baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni sa ni amɛkpe ni amɛta amɛyiteŋ lɛ Nakai baai lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛitsu nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow better when the branches of neighboring trees meet overhead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aniji kpe yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees thrive when their tops touch to form a soft canopy. This protective layer shields fragile flowers from dry winds, traps beneficial humidity, and prevents sunlight from burning young cocoa pods.
ga: Kokoo tsei daa kɛji amɛyitsei lɛ ta amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ buɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashã kookoo tsei bibii

english: Why should I remove or pull out extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main stem. By pulling away all but one strong sucker, your main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ja tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kome pɛ nɔ. Otso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava plants split into two main stems as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ mli gbalaa ewoɔ ŋmeii titrii enyɔ mli beni edaa lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally splits its stem into two or three branches as it matures to produce more leaves for catching sunlight. This branching is a healthy sign that the plant is building food reserves to grow large roots underground.
ga: Yucca baajara etso lɛ mli ewo niji enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni edara lɛ koni ekɛ baai babaoo aha ni ekɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Nɛkɛ niji ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitswa niyenii ni ekɛto koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines split into different branches, and why should I guide them onto wood stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli gbalaa ewoɔ niji srɔtoi amli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛma tso nɔ?

english: Yam vines split naturally to spread their leaves out for sunlight. Training these divided vines up wooden stakes keeps them off the wet ground, preventing rot and helping the plant produce big, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛhere hulu la lɛ atuu. Wein tsei ni aja mli nɛɛ ni aaatsɔse amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni wein tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How does trimming away side branches help my tomato plants produce bigger fruits?
ga: Te niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-tomato tso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji tɛŋŋ?

english: When a plant has too many extra branches, it wastes energy feeding unnecessary leaves instead of fruits. Removing excess side branches directs all the plant's energy into making larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Ebaafite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaaye baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ, ni ehaa tomato lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant crops directly inside the footpaths that run through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛ ni tsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Footpaths are where people and farm animals walk, which packs the soil down too hard for plant roots to breathe and absorb nutrients. Keeping crops off pathways also prevents them from getting trampled.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi asɛɛ ji he ni gbɔmɛi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi nyiɛɔ yɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ gbɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa koni akanyiɛ amɛnɔ.

english: How do clear walking paths across my farm field help my crops produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Clear pathways allow you to walk through your farm easily to weed, spray, and inspect crops without damaging young plants or compacting the soil around root systems.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya koni oyajie jwɛi, okɛ tsofa afɔ shi ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. ni efiteee tso bibioo lɛ loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ebɔle ehe

english: How do I split a water stream so it waters two separate crop beds evenly?
ga: Majara faa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni mawo ŋmɔji enyɔ ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amli nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can dig small side trenches or open water gates to divide one main water flow into two smaller streams. This distributes water evenly so all your crops get hydrated without flooding one specific area.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu bibioo ko. Nu shinaa ko ni yɔɔ afã loo nu lɛ mli lɛ jaa nu ni hoɔ titri kome mli ewoɔ faai bibii enyɔ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ jaa pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu awo onibii fɛɛ amli ni nu akashwie he pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: Why do crops planted in low spots where farm pathways cross tend to rot and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ŋmɔ mli gbɛi yɔɔ lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Water often collects in low junctions or pathways during heavy rains. When water stands around plant roots for too long, it cuts off oxygen, causing the roots to rot and the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu fɔɔ buamɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni gbɛjegbɛi lɛ kpeɔ yɛ nɔ loo gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ nu hi tso shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that maize needs to create green chlorophyll and grow healthy stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ klorofil eŋɔli aba ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause heat stress in tomatoes, which prevents proper pollination and causes the plant to shed flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. ni ehaa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whitefly insects that slows plant growth and reduces root size.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi bibii amli ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong direct sunlight; they require shade from taller trees or plantains to keep their leaves from scorching and to maintain soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛkashã baai lɛ, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during high winds even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that hold heavy fruit bunches; if rain softens the soil or pests weaken the roots, strong winds can easily push the heavy plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hiɛɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa tsei ni tsii lɛ ashwie shi mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, creating conditions for fungal diseases to multiply and decay the underground tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baafa babaoo ni ekpãtã shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ahiɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do I need to put dry leaves and straw on top of my yam mounds after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi woɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mulching yam mounds keeps the soil cool under hot sun, traps moisture in the earth, and prevents heavy downpours from washing away the soil protecting the seed yam.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni abua naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ sũ ni buɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning rather than during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Morning watering allows roots to absorb water before sunlight evaporates it, whereas watering under hot afternoon sun leads to rapid evaporation and can shock hot plant leaves.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ akpokpo.

english: Why are small caterpillars burrowing into the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifo mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the tender leaf funnel to eat growing leaves, which prevents the maize plant from forming healthy ears if not controlled early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli koni amɛye baai ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa tso lɛ afee toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require a large amount of water to stay healthy. During dry spells without irrigation, their broad leaves lose moisture very quickly, causing the leaves to dry up and wither to help the plant conserve water.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, nu shwieee nɔ. Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu akafite.

english: How can I keep my plantain crops alive when there is no river or water source near my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantain lɛ ahi shi? Akɛni faa loo nu jɛɛhe ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ.

english: You can use mulching by covering the soil around the base of the plantains with dry leaves, straw, or farm waste. This traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and reduces water loss from direct sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain shishi lɛ he lɛ ni okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔ mli jwɛi baaha nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi

english: How can I tell if my plantain plants are suffering from severe water shortage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia mi plantain lɛ waa?

english: When plantains lack water, their leaves will droop, turn brown from the tips inward, lose their firmness, and the main stem may become soft and weak.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ plantains lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. Mligbɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. efiteɔ shifimɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ baanyɛ afee blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Is it a good idea to plant plantain and cocoa together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu plantain kɛ cocoa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantain alongside young cocoa is beneficial because the plantain provides essential shade and extra income while the cocoa trees are young and vulnerable.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ plantains ni akɛ cocoa tsei bibii duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ekɛ shika kroko baa. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ,.

english: What happens to my plantain plants when my cocoa trees start growing bigger and taller?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ beni mi cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees mature, their wide tops block out the sunlight and their deep roots take up most of the soil nutrients and water, naturally causing the shaded plantains to weaken and yield less.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do cocoa trees seem to grow stronger and take over the farm after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔji anɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop with a deep root system and a wide leaf cover, allowing it to control the land's space, sunlight, and nutrients better than plantains as it matures.
ga: Kookoo ji tso ni yeɔ daa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baa ni mli kwɔ ha nɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui lɛ kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa.

english: When is the right time to stop growing plantains alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: You should gradually remove plantains around the third or fourth year when the cocoa canopy closes together, so the cocoa trees can get full sunlight and space to produce pods.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie plantains lɛ fiofio yɛ afi ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ he beni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do young cocoa plants die so easily during their first dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out rapidly when exposed to hot sun and dry winds without enough soil moisture or protective shade.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does soil on an open farm dry out so fast even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Without shade trees or ground cover, direct sunlight bakes the soil surface and causes rainwater to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo lɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How can starting a cocoa farm help me build long-term income for my family?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kookoo ŋmɔ ni ogbeleɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha oweku lɛ aná shika be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa is a high-value cash crop that produces harvests for several decades once established, giving farmers a reliable seasonal income to reinvest in their farm and family.
ga: Cocoa ji shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa ni ekɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ewo yibii kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, okwaafoi yɛ be mli shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni amɛkɛbaawo amɛŋmɔji kɛ amɛwekui amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or isn't getting enough water, which prevents the plant from producing food and growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants keep falling off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too hot, when watering is irregular, or when insects aren't pollinating the blossoms during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kooloi bibii efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi anɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy fruit stems, so strong winds can easily blow them down if you do not support the main trunk with strong wooden prop stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai tsei ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa lɛ shi oya kɛji akɛ okɛ tso ni wa fioo ko fiii tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the branch before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excess wetness and shade; clearing surrounding weeds and pruning extra branches helps sunlight dry out the pods and stops the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni etsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: What is causing all these small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young corn crops?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Enɛɛmɛi ji mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai.

english: Ragged holes inside young corn leaf shoots are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of the crop and eat the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛyeɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks into the ground next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ Sweet potato tsei ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need tall sticks to climb upward so their leaves can catch full sunlight, which helps the crop build energy to form large tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni biɔ niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ feɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower stem leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do some of the crop seeds I plant in the soil fail to sprout into green shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to grow if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the soil dries out completely after planting, or if heavy rain causes the seeds to rot before they can break through the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool under the bright sun, holds moisture in the dirt longer, and prevents unwanted weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and acts as free food for crops like maize planted nearby.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni efeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to grow safely. Direct, harsh sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil, so planting them under temporary shade crops like plantain protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo fioo koni amɛdara shweshweeshwe. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Small holes in the central whorl of maize leaves are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning or late in the evening targets the caterpillars when they come out to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshishifãi lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage with poor tuber growth happens when soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, causing the plant to put all its energy into leaf growth instead of storing starch underground.
ga: Foji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Flower drop occurs when the plants experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus, which prevents successful pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛhaa sũ lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni tsiɔ sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to pare or trim the bottom of my plantain suckers before putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo mafo mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishi dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming the dark root base of fresh plantain suckers removes hidden pests like weevil larvae and parasitic nematodes, ensuring only clean, healthy plant material goes into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ plantain tsei heei lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ahe nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is dry or after a heavy rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after rain because crop roots need water to dissolve and absorb the nutrients; applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso shishifãi lɛ taoɔ nu koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves into the air so they can absorb maximum sunlight to produce energy, while keeping the foliage off wet ground to prevent fungal foliage diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha sweet potato baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafee fungal leaf helai.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper bushes twisting into tight, wrinkled clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Twisted and wrinkled leaves are often a sign of damage from tiny insects like thrips or mites, or a plant virus transmitted by sap-sucking insects that stunts normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsake ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii efite. loo tsei amli helai ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa ni haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmei kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving behind natural nitrogen fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating too fast in the sun, suppresses weeds, and decomposes into rich organic food for plants.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛha tsei.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight because their leaf leaves dry out easily. Leaving larger shade trees creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps soil moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ

english: When maize plants are placed too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and nutrition to grow strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu shwɛɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for green leaves and leafy growth. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the plant so leaves stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni haa baai eŋɔli kɛ baai lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps leaves flat and allows fruit to develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plantain stem for water and nutrients. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing the main tree to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when plants suffer from sudden dry spells or extreme heat, or if pollinators like insects are missing. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo latsaa ni naa wa waa ba tso lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kooloi bibii bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas first make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need their leaves exposed to maximum sunlight to produce energy, which is stored in the ground to grow large tubers. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where they might rot or catch diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ koni bulb agboi akwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ akatara hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to apply granular fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji oshara be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can actually drink. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil concentrates chemical salts around the roots, which can burn the roots and kill the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu diɛŋtsɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ afee ekome kɛbɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni efite tsei

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct hot sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the moisture in the soil. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living umbrella shade and keeps the young trees cool until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua tsei bibii lɛ. Eha ejɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee eŋɔli ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water drowns the root system and encourages fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy winds when the fruit bunch appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akutsei lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them unbalanced. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy, fork-shaped wooden pole (propping) prevents wind from knocking the tree down before harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. unbalance Tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ fɔk (braces) ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa tso lɛ shi dani akpa tso lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering. Watering your crop regularly at the base and putting dry grass on the soil around the plant keeps the roots cool and reduces flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Okɛ nu awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa yɛ shishigbɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. tsei koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi.

english: Weeds have hardy wild seeds already buried in the soil that naturally absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing light, food, and water from your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp earth, giving them light and preventing soil-borne fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa la kpɛɔ ni etsiɔ baa helai ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves. Spraying the leaves with neem leaf extract mixed with soapy water helps control these insects so healthy new leaves can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso mli nu ni akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ efutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ koni baai heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does covering the bare ground around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mikɛ jwɛi haa mi-vegetables lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) blocks hot sunlight from drying out the earth, keeping moisture in the root zone much longer. As the dry grass rots over time, it also turns into natural soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ fite yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ E hu ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why has my old mango tree stopped bearing plenty of fruits even though it has big green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango momo lɛ kpaɔ yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When a tree grows too dense with branches, sunlight cannot reach the inside parts where new flower buds form. Pruning away old, dead, or crowded inner branches allows sunlight and air to flow through, triggering fresh flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da ni eyɛ niji babaoo lɛ Hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii heei amli. Niji ni yɔɔ mli ni egbɔ, ni egboi, loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ni afoɔ. Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni kɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei baa

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight. If they do not have enough shade from companion plants like plantains, the harsh sun burns their leaves and turns them yellow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tsei ni amɛjaraa lɛ amli lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?
