english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juice from the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Controlling these small insects stops the damage from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa nɛɛ amli Kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli haa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: On hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves from heat, but usually recover as the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Does it mean my cassava is ready to harvest as soon as the stems start producing flowers?
ga: Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji eshishifãi lɛ je shishi amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: No, flowering is just a natural stage of growth and does not mean tubers are mature. Cassava tubers usually need between 9 to 12 months underground to grow big enough for harvest.
ga: Dabi, fɔfɔii afeemɔ ji adebɔɔ mli dalɛ shihilɛ ko kɛkɛ. Ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ yitso lɛ baada kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to use tall sticks to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji duɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture more food, which is stored underground to make bigger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Staking Wo sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni onine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Will leaving weeds around my crops reduce the amount of food I get at harvest?
ga: releasing weeds around Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, weeds act like extra mouths to feed; they steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to yield well.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabui krɛdɛɛi kɛha niyenii. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: That damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl of the plant. Applying early treatments like recommended insecticides or neem extract can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ahe ŋmeii amli lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually because of irregular watering during fruit formation.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ feɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do extension officers always tell me to use a rope to plant my crop in straight lines instead of just scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ mikɛ kpãa adu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines with a rope ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. It prevents crowding, allows plants to grow strong roots, and makes weeding and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Boxwood ni akɛkwɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii anaa Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa. Ni ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo babaoo kɛhaa bo.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. The plants stretch upward quickly to search for light, resulting in tall, weak stalks that fall over easily in wind and produce smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe oya koni etao la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei bibii bibii lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into large tubers. Leaving about 1 meter between plants gives the roots enough room to swell fully and stops neighboring plants from stealing each other's nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ ashi aaafee mita kome yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. ni amɛtsi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju amɛhe niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant plantains near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong sunlight. Taller crops like plantain grow quickly and act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and cool moisture cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting stressed from heat before they completely die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ hulutsoo be mli dani amɛgboi kwraa?

english: Crops show heat stress early by curling or rolling their leaves inward during the hottest hours of the day, or by looking dull green instead of shiny and bright. This is their way of reducing water loss.
ga: Tsei jieɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpo mra. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaakpã mli loo aaakpã mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tseee ni oookwɛ yɛ nɔ ni kpɛɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Naa bɔ ni aaafee aha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: When plants lack water or soil nutrients like nitrogen, they move resources from older leaves to keep young growing leaves alive. Yellowing lower leaves show that the crop is starving for food or moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛjieɔ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the ground around my crop with dry leaves or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔhamɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmei baai baadu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Covering the soil around plants keeps the ground cool under the sun, prevents soil moisture from evaporating, and blocks sunlight from reaching weeds so they cannot grow and choke your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Etsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni otsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe Enɛ ji koni amɛkakwɛ ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive tough conditions, so their roots quickly grab water, light, and fertilizer before your planted crop can establish itself. Removing them early gives your crop the advantage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ama shi shiŋŋ. Ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop rows straight down a sloping hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting straight down a hill creates channels for heavy rain to wash away topsoil and fertilizers. Planting across the hill traps water in the ground and protects the nutrients your crops need.
ga: dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi Abaafee nugbɔshiimɔ ko kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni baaha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie. Kɛ́ odu yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ebuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra side shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie sɛɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Extra branches pull food and water away from main fruits. Trimming extra shoots helps the plant direct all its energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of unnecessary stems and leaves.
ga: Niji krɛdɛɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ aduawai titri lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsei kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when heavy rains wash away nitrogen from the topsoil or when waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea once excess water drains will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he kɛ́ nu lɛ ho babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the main stem becomes woody. You can also carefully dig up one plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso titri lɛ bafeɔ tso. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome hu he nii koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli ewo wu ni eyɛ shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face heat stress, long dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning excess branches to let light and air into the farm, along with removing infected pods quickly, stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli Agbɛnɛ hu Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense sun, tomato leaves lose water faster than the roots can take it up, causing temporary wilting. If the plant recovers by morning, it is just heat stress; if it stays wilted, it may be root rot or a bacterial disease.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ leebi lɛ Eji heat stress kɛkɛ. Kɛji egbo lolo lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee shishifãi ni egbo loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli.

english: Why does my yam crop need wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out toward sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the vines on stakes helps the plant catch more sunlight, which feeds the roots and results in much larger yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awo wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings shade each other and fight for light, causing them to stretch upward and grow thin stems. Proper plant spacing ensures every stem receives enough sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛnáa shishifãi bibii. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits crack open on the farm before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack when a dry period is followed by sudden heavy rain or overwatering. The inside of the fruit takes in water rapidly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ babaoo nyiɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow thick green leaves but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Using fertilizers rich in phosphorus instead of nitrogen encourages the plant to produce more pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii yɛ nitrogen najiaŋ lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my plantain suckers are strong enough to transplant to a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu awo ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Healthy plantain suckers for planting should be about two to three feet tall with narrow, spear-shaped leaves. This shows the sucker has a strong base bulb with enough stored food to survive being moved and take root fast.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ ashɛ aaafee ninetalɔi 2-3 ni amɛhiɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ lance. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmei ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ basal bulb ni mli wa ni niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli ni baaha enyɛ efã ni ekɛ shishifãi awo oya.

english: Can I plant cassava stems upside down, or does it matter which direction the buds point?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava tso ni mikɛ mihe awo mli? Aloo gbɛ ni hiŋmɛii lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Cassava stems must always be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the roots to grow upwards first before bending down, which weakens the plant and greatly reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei be fɛɛ be ni amɛshishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara klɛŋklɛŋ dani amɛkotoɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before planting my maize instead of planting right after the very first rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often tricks farmers because the deeper soil stays hot and dry. Planting immediately means seeds might sprout, but if the rains pause for a week, the young seedlings dry up and die. Waiting for steady rains ensures enough soil moisture for roots to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under intense, direct sunlight during the Harmattan dry season. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy that cools the soil and retains humidity.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eeeha ejɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create energy for underground tuber growth. Staking lifts the foliage into the air so leaves capture maximum sunlight and stay off damp soil where fungal diseases and crawling pests can destroy them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛha hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni baai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ lɛ he.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun. It traps moisture so you water less often, keeps soil cool, suppresses weeds, and breaks down over time into natural manure.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow while the stalks are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually indicate a shortage of nitrogen in the soil, often caused by poor soil or heavy rains washing away nutrients. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure restores green leaf color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil naturally. Intercropping them with maize feeds the soil with natural fertilizer while giving you two crops to harvest from one piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni obaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting during the continuous rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a common disease caused by tiny fungi that spread quickly in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning tree branches to let sunlight and wind into the farm, clearing weeds, and picking off infected pods stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience severe water stress or extreme heat. Inconsistent watering stops the plant from feeding the blossoms. Watering deeply and consistently at the base helps flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaha fɔfɔi niyenii. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni afeɔ daa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or whiteflies feeding on young leaves and spreading plant viruses. Protecting plants early with safe neem-based sprays prevents these insects from damaging the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Neem tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot drink water fast enough in full sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, the hot sun dries out the soil and burns the leaves before the plant can get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi latsaa ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai lɛ dani tso lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and fresh air, which encourages the plant to direct its energy down into growing a bigger root tuber.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛaaha amɛná la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya shi koni shishifãi wuji lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the soil stays too soggy for the roots to breathe.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why is it good for my field if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil and uses up its nutrients. Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring field fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when there are lots of weeds around them, even if I put fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ woɔ mli moŋ

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that drink up the water and gobble up the fertilizer meant for your crops. They also block sunlight from reaching your plants, leaving your crops weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya ni baanu nu ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la hu naa koni ekashɛ otsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ bo.

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains waterlog the ground and water sits without draining, the roots drown and soil organisms cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni nu damɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry break before the main rains begin. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout, but the hot dry days right after will scorch and kill the delicate new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi gbii ni mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baashã ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, every seedling competes with its neighbors for the same small amount of water, sunlight, and soil food. None of the plants get enough to grow full-sized fruits or tubers.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu kɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso ko bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai loo bulbs ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects like bees to shake pollen inside the blossom. Without pollination and stable water, the plant cannot make fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hosoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ daa lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called Fall Armyworms, hide inside the rolled center leaves of corn plants because it is soft, hidden from predators, and easy to chew. Left untreated, they destroy the plant's growing point and stop it from producing corn ears.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooye Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa yɛ lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ anaa.

english: Is it too late for me to start planting maize if the major rainy season has already started?
ga: Ani etsɛ tsɔ akɛ abaaje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ eje shishi momo?

english: No, it is not too late, but you should select early-maturing maize varieties. These varieties grow and produce grain quickly before the rains stop, protecting your harvest from dry spells.
ga: Dabi, etsɛko tsɔ. Shi esa akɛ ohala ŋmãa henɔi ni shwereɔ oya. Nɛkɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi nɛɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui oya dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he.

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in a warm or damp place, or damaged by insects like weevils. Storing seed in cool, dry, airtight containers keeps them healthy for the next season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. loo ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii efite lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and yellowish even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients like nitrogen from the soil to grow tall and green. Water alone is not enough; adding organic manure or fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to grow strong.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee eŋɔli. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ he kome yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When yam seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight for space, light, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow large, healthy tubers instead of small ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná he ko, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa trees cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does leaving weeds around my pepper plants affect how much harvest I will get?
ga: jwɛi ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Ani mi-pepper tso lɛ saa bɔ ni mikpaa nii lɛ he?

english: Yes, weeds steal water, light, and food from the soil that your pepper plants need. Clearing weeds early allows your pepper plants to produce more flowers and larger fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa o-pepper tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-chili tsei lɛ akwɛ babaoo ni amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally in dry weather to save water and survive the heat. As long as the stem stays green, the plant is still alive and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ ji eŋɔli lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry or the air becomes extremely hot. Keeping the soil moist by spreading dry grass around the roots helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up into tight little balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects spreading a disease or by severe heat stress. Protecting the plants with pest control methods or shade keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ helai ashwãa loo hulutsoo ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hulutsoo he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes under the ground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Sweet potatoes show they are ready when their vines and leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can also dig up one tuber at the edge of the row to check if it has reached full size.
ga: Akɛɛ akɛ sweet potatoes efee klalo beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tuber kome hu atsu nii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ naa koni ona kɛji eshɛ elɛɛmɔ he.

english: Is there a chemical I can spray on my farm that will kill the weeds without destroying my maize?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛgbe jwɛi ni mifiteee mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, there are selective weed killers specially designed for maize farms. These chemicals destroy unwanted weeds while leaving your maize plants completely unharmed.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo yɛ ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afee krɛdɛɛ aha ŋmãa ŋmɔji. Tsofai nɛɛ kpataaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa o-corn tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhe kwraa.

english: Why does spraying chemical weed killers sometimes burn my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shãa mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ?

english: Some weed killers are non-selective, meaning they burn every green plant they touch. To protect your crops, you must use a chemical specifically safe for the exact crop you are growing.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ halaaa mɔ ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaashã tso fɛɛ tso ni eŋɔli ni amɛbaashɛ he lɛ. koni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe pɔtɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do selective weed killers destroy weeds without harming my maize plant?
ga: Te tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ agbe jwɛi ni egbeee mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ?

english: Maize plants absorb and process certain chemicals differently than broadleaf weeds and grasses do. The chemical targets biological features unique to the weeds, burning them while the maize safely survives.
ga: Abɛi tsei ŋmɛɔ tsofai komɛi ni amɛtsuɔ he nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ. Tsofai lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi lɛ wala yibii ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ amɛshãa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ wala mli shweshweeshwe lolo lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I accidentally spray the wrong weed killer on it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ejaaa lɛ shwie amɛnɔ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Using a non-selective chemical will burn and kill your maize just like a weed, which is why it is critical to confirm the spray type before applying it to your field.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni halaaa mɔ lɛ baashã ŋmãa ni egbe lɛ tamɔ jwɛi. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni oma nɔ mi akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji dani okɛwo oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Can I feed my crops and kill weeds on my land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni mafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi yɛ be kome too mli?

english: Yes, there are specialized agricultural products that reduce weed growth while simultaneously feeding nutrients to your crops so they can thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni haa jwɛi lɛ shweremɔ baa shi, yɛ be mli ni ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ. ekomefeemɔ koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my maize crops need fertilizer even after I have cleared all the weeds from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Clearing weeds stops them from stealing food, but the soil itself may still lack essential nutrients. Fertilizer provides the extra nutrition your maize needs to grow strong and produce heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ tsi he ko lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii. Shi ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa o-ŋmã lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii aba.

english: Why do weeds make my maize crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds crowd your crops, the maize starves and cannot develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye ŋmãa lɛ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and stronger on my farm than the crop seeds I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants adapted to soak up water and soil nutrients very quickly, which is why active weed control is needed to give your crops the advantage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni atsu jwɛi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná he sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I harvest very few maize cobs when I leave grass growing inside my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmãa fioo ko pɛ beni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grasses compete aggressively for the same root space and nutrients your maize needs. Uncontrolled grass starves the maize during its crucial growing stage, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ baaha ŋmã aye hɔmɔ yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: How do I choose the right chemical for my farm when there are so many different bottles in the store?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofai ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Beni tsɛnsii srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ

english: Always select a chemical based on your specific crop type and weed problem. Look for crop-safe herbicides, like maize-selective sprays, so you protect your yield while clearing the weeds.
ga: Halamɔ tsofai ni damɔ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi pɔtɛɛ naagba lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Taomɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when there is not enough, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when there is too much or too little water. High heat stops the flowers from pollinating properly, causing the plant to drop them to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu babaoo loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Ha tsei agbo koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava leaves dry up and drop during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry weather as a survival trick to save water. The plant goes to sleep above ground while keeping its roots alive under the soil until the rain returns.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the harmattan wind blows hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan wind sucks moisture out of the leaves and soil very fast. This stress causes the cocoa tree to wilt, shed leaves, and stop forming new flowers or pods to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ shi, ebaa, ni ekpaa fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii heei feemɔ koni ekɛbu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites living under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. They suck the juices out of the plant, causing the leaf to twist as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo virus ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ lɛ kɛbaa Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do the stems of my tomato plants turn black and rot near the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates very wet soil, which lets microscopic soil fungi grow fast and attack wet plant stems. This rot cuts off food and water to the rest of the plant, making it collapse.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ daa oya ni amɛtutuaa tsei ni efɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ŋmɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛyaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ. ha efo mli

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I plant three or four seeds in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil food. Because no single plant gets enough nutrients, none of them can grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ agboi wuji.

english: Why are my young plantain suckers leaning toward one side instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miiku amɛhe amɛmiiwo he kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi jaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers naturally bend towards sunlight. If tall trees or other plants are blocking light from one direction, the plantain will lean toward the open sky to get the light it needs to grow.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Kɛji tso lɛ kwɔ loo tsei krokomɛi Tsĩɔ la naa kɛjɛɔ he kome Plantains shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ koni amɛná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Yam tubers grow bent when the soil underneath them is too hard, rocky, or poorly tilled. The growing root cannot easily push through hard earth, so it bends around obstacles.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baakɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi ni miida lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, ebɔleɔ gbɛtsii nii ahe.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight for long hours. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out their shallow roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ bɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil, or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu yɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing—usually a few weeks after germination—so roots can easily soak up nutrients without burning.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida waa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why do I need to keep some big trees on my farm when growing young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei wuji anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun; shade trees act like large umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and protecting delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight and dry winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant make food to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects in poorly drained soil for too long, creating conditions for root-rot fungi to attack the tubers during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baatutua ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or damp places lose their vitality quickly, or small insects like weevils damage the internal seed embryo during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ hei ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi oya. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baafite dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or when there is too little water in the soil during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛ́ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli.

english: Plantain stems are made of tightly packed leaf sheaths rather than solid wood, making them top-heavy; strong winds can easily tip them over unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Akɛ baai ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ moŋ fe tso ni wa. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi oya ja akɛ tso fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Yes, planting legumes like beans with maize helps the soil because legumes draw nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt, feeding the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce hardy seeds that stay dormant in the soil and are naturally adapted to sprout immediately after the slightest rain, competing with your planted crops for water and food.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni etsake ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. koni okɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ

english: Why is my young mango tree dropping all its flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Young fruit trees often shed their blossoms in their early years because the tree structure and root system are not yet strong enough to support heavy fruit. As the tree grows deeper roots and matures over a few seasons, it will naturally hold the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfi yibii ni tsii lɛ anɔ lolo. Kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni eda yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli lɛ, ebaahiɛ eyibii lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the main trunk instead of on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally flowers on the thick trunk and main branches so that tiny pollinating insects can reach the flowers easily, and to ensure the heavy pods can hang securely without breaking thin stems.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ niji wuji anɔ. kɛha kooloi bibii ni amɛfee pollination Ebaanyɛ eshɛ fɔfɔi ahe oya ni bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkuuu ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: How do I stop my cassava roots from rotting under the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them in heavy soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers using sunlight on their leaves. Climbing tall poles spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight, which direct more energy into growing large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsoi ni kwɔlɔ ni akwɔɔ lɛ gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ yaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaves. Adding fertilizer or planting crops like beans on the land before maize helps restore soil nitrogen.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli loo ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after I planted them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to wake up and begin growing. If planted in dry soil without water, the seed remains asleep (dormant) or can spoil before it gets the moisture it needs to germinate.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi (dormant) loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi dani amɛná nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. You can prevent them from falling by propping up the main stem with strong, forked wooden poles tied securely near the top bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni no haa ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ otsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛtsɔ tso ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmeii lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ ni oookɛfi amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from drying out quickly, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich natural manure as it breaks down.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii kɛji efite.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas naturally refreshes the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and looking shiny even after watering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves. While watering helps dry soil, you need to apply an organic spray like neem oil to clear the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi moŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ organic spray tamɔ neem fɔ afɔ nɔ koni ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to protect their delicate leaves from heat and to keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers yield smaller bunches when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients in the soil, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall stalks but produce very small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsei kakadaji shi ewoɔ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize needs enough balanced nutrients, especially nitrogen, to fill out corn cobs. If the soil lacks nutrients, the plant uses its energy to grow leaves and stalks instead of healthy corn ears.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa. titri lɛ nitrogen ni akɛbaafata ŋmãa ŋmãa he Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. Planting too early means the seeds might sprout and then dry up and die before the main rains arrive consistently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba daa.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to attack my young maize leaves more than mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn baai bibii lɛ fe baai ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are tender, soft, and easy for armyworm caterpillars to chew and digest, whereas mature leaves are tough and harder for pests to eat.
ga: Abɛi bibii ahe baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii akɛ amɛaaye ni amɛye. Beni baai lɛ daraa lɛ, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ewaa kɛhaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛaada.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and changing color to light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do I need to heap loose soil into mounds before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabu shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ naa awo gɔŋ ko mli dani madu sweet potatoes kuu ko?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil so their tubers can expand underground without hitting hard earth, which helps them grow large, smooth tubers.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni wa etswaaa amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa amɛyitsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without growing into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to conserve water and energy rather than trying to support fruit growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Mohu ɔ, bɔɔ mɔde kaa o maa ye bua tso yiblii ɔ wami.

english: Why do my groundnut plants need to be weeded and banked with loose soil around the stem while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-peanut tso lɛ mli ni awo sũ ni ebɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, small stems grow downward to push the nuts into the soil. Loose soil makes it easy for the pegs to enter the ground and grow pods.
ga: Beni ashɛre ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbaa shi koni amɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ hu.

english: Why does my land still become hard and dry even after I put commercial fertilizer on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds the crop, but it does not fix hard soil structure. Adding organic material like decomposed animal manure or dead plant leaves keeps the soil soft and helps it hold water.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shi enyɛŋ etsake bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egbo loo tsei ahe baai ni egboi fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua ni ehiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads rapidly in heavy shade and high humidity when rainwater sits on the pods for too long.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen food in the soil, or the ground is flooded with water, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and dry out during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water in extreme heat, or because tiny insects like whiteflies are feeding on them and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies miiye amɛ ni amɛmiigbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their blossoms to save energy and water, preventing fruit from setting until the weather becomes milder.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Tsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baadɔ.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops every time I plant on the same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Crops continuously pull nutrients out of the earth as they grow. Without adding compost, manure, or alternating with leguminous crops like beans, the soil becomes depleted and tired.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing grains and empty patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ okadii ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Missing grains occur when dry weather or strong winds prevent pollen from reaching all the silks on the ear during the flowering stage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo kɔɔyɔɔ tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekashɛ siliki ni yɔɔ toi lɛ nɔ lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Cassava roots cannot expand easily if the soil is too hard or compacted, or if the soil lacks potassium, which causes the plant to spend its energy surviving instead of storing food in the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up completely before the harvest season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miije shishi amɛgbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam vines is usually caused by leaf spot fungi or microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes attacking the root system, cutting off water supply to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. ni efo nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do worms appear inside the middle of my maize leaves even when the leaves look healthy on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on the leaves at night, and once hatched, young pests like fall armyworms crawl deep into the central funnel of the plant to hide while feeding on the growing leaves.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ Ni kɛ́ efo lɛ Kooloi bibii tamɔ cutworms lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatee amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do some new cassava varieties mature in six months while our older varieties take more than a year to yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni wɔ ŋmeii momo lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties have been bred by agricultural scientists to grow tubers faster and fight off common plant diseases early, whereas older varieties naturally take a longer time to build up starch in their roots.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efee ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ adara oya ni amɛwu amɛshi tsei amli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei henɔi ni egbɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbuaa ŋmeii anaa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor nutrients, which leaves the plant without enough energy to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo niyenii ni esaaa Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. The plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the new leaves at the top to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa hee lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot, dry periods as a natural defense to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from burning under direct sunlight.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ be mli ni edɔ, be mli ni egbi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting on their own in the barn even when I have not planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy right after harvest. Once this sleep period naturally ends after a few months, warm air and light trigger the tuber to sprout in preparation for a new planting season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Beni nɛkɛ wɔɔhe nɛɛ baa naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ la baawo ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ be hee lɛ.

english: Why do my root crops grow better and produce bigger yields when I plant them on raised mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds and ridges break up hard soil so roots can spread easily, allow excess water from heavy rains to drain away, and keep the soil soft so tubers can expand underground without pushback.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ha nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ ehe wooo sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight one another for light, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward trying to capture sunlight, leaving them weak and without enough energy to build large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ shwie ŋwɛi, ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help make the soil richer for next season's crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial microbes in the soil to capture nitrogen gas from the air and lock it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil when the plant leaves and roots decay.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa from intense heat, cool the air, and prevent soil moisture from drying out too quickly.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ

english: Why do I see holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hidden deep inside the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii amli ni akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central funnel of the maize plant because it is dark, safe from predators, and filled with soft, fresh leaves for them to eat.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ duŋ, ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. ni akɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ eyi mli obɔ koni amɛye.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nutrients like nitrogen or are getting too much water around their roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving water drainage in the field will help them turn green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he loo aha ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Curling leaves with yellow spots are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Blackening pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads easily during wet and humid weather. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly will help protect healthy pods.
ga: Black pods hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily by harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller or empty ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. ni ŋmãa toi lɛ ji bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground so the soil stays wet longer during dry spells and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is it better to plant my crops at the very start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting with the first rains allows young crop roots to grow deep while the soil is full of moisture, giving the plants strength to survive unexpected dry breaks later in the season.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛjeɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my plantains are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the fruit looks plump, loses its sharp angular edges, and the dried flower tips fall off easily, even while the skin is still green.
ga: Plantains efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ. Elaajeɔ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be mli ni hewolo lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo po.

english: Why do my stored grains get spoiled by insects so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kooloi ahewɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil and attract insects when they are stored while still holding moisture. Drying your harvested grains thoroughly under the sun before storing them keeps pests away and prevents rot.
ga: Nibii amli ŋmaa fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi dani akɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings look weak and wilted when planted directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have soft leaves and small root systems that lose water quickly in direct sun. They need temporary shade to protect them from heat stress while their roots grow deeper into the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to leave wide spaces between trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving enough space between trees ensures that each tree gets enough sunlight, underground room for root growth, and a fair share of soil water and nutrients without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Cellar kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni sa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How does leaving cleared weeds and dry leaves on top of my soil help my planted crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajie kɛ baai ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with cleared weeds and organic matter acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and decays over time to release natural food into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni ajie kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ejie adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs help to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni ehe miihia yelikɛbuamɔ koni akwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Signs of tired soil include crops turning yellow early, slow or stunted plant growth, thin stems, and poor harvest yields even when there is enough rainfall.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miifite lɛ he ji: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.
