english: Why do tree crops take a few years to bear fruit while crops like maize produce in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heɔ afii fioo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Trees spend their first few years building a deep root system and a strong trunk to support heavy branches, while short-term crops like maize focus all their energy on quick stem growth and seed production in a single season.
ga: Tso lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni ekɛmaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifã ni mli wa ni baaye abua niji ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmãa ni yaa hiɛ oya kɛ dumɔwui ni anáa yɛ be kome mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up or droop during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where plants reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun to cut down on water loss during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ baaha he ni amɛbaai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to prune or cut away lower branches from my growing trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo majie tso ni miida lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Removing dead or unnecessary lower branches directs the tree's energy toward growing a strong main trunk, forming a healthy upper canopy, and producing better flowers and fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ gbɛ koni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri ko ni mli wa ada. Bɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni eha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my young tree seedlings after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have aggressive root systems adapted to quickly grab surface water and nutrients right after rain, whereas young trees direct energy into deeper root establishment first.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsake amɛhe koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: Can planting beans or groundnuts around my main crops help improve my soil?
ga: Beans loo peanuts ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi tsei titrii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather stresses crops and weakens their natural defenses, making them softer targets for sap-sucking insects that thrive and multiply rapidly in warm, dry conditions.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni shwereɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their foliage and quickly dries out the moisture in the soil. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, protecting them until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu nakai tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Extra suckers steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from the main mother plant. Removing excess suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring the main plant grows a larger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná plantains babaoo ni tsii fe no.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is a vital food for leafy green growth. Adding compost or proper fertilizer gives the soil the nitrogen needed to restore green leaves and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛbaa baai eŋɔli lɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni aduɔ yɛ mi-corn lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds the nearby maize. At the same time, the tall maize plants provide support and shelter for the ground crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ wɔɔhe.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my maize after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer about two to three weeks after the seeds sprout, once roots are developed enough to drink up nutrients. Always ensure the soil is moist when applying fertilizer so it dissolves safely into the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee otsii 2-3 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ koni enyɛ etsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves full of waste in the funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ kɛ baai ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hoppers lɛ amli lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant to eat the soft leaves. Spotting them early and applying safe neem oil or recommended extension sprays protects the stem before the entire plant is ruined.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ yitso lɛ he dani efite kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant's juices and spreading sickness. Controlling these insects early with proper soapy sprays or natural barriers prevents the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Emuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ samla ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, suffocating the roots and attracting fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to support my climbing yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make energy. Staking the vines keeps leaves away from ground diseases and helps the plant produce much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara babaoo.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Keeping the soil consistently moist using grass mulch protects the flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ tomatoi.

english: Yellow leaves on lower maize stalks usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key plant food, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily, meaning they cannot handle direct, intense sunlight without shade plants protecting them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, cacao tsei nyɛŋ akpee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ bɛ ni buɔ amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant doesn't receive regular water, which causes the plant stress and forces it to drop its flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbee shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space for cassava to grow bigger later.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are fully established before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ kwraa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Maize seeds need continuous moisture to sprout and grow strong roots, so planting too early during dry spells can cause the seeds to dry up and rot in the soil.
ga: Abele dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my tubers if I build my yam mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa miyitso nɔ kɛji mima ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Placing yam mounds too close together forces the plants to fight for soil nutrients and sunlight, which leaves less energy for the roots and produces smaller yams.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato ni abua naa lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and showing yellowish patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and patchy leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies that weakens the plant and reduces tuber growth.
ga: Baai ni atsɔ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi Yɛ ŋmei nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my crop plants after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems designed to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains end up with small holes and powdery dust in the bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: Small holes and dust in stored grain are caused by tiny insects called weevils that eat the inside of the grain, especially if the maize was not dried completely before storage.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii amli. Atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei ni yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my groundnuts from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying up, and the inside of the harvested pods shows dark brown markings.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ baaná okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain crops yield so much fruit around September to November compared to other months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ September kɛyashi November lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nyɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ

english: Plantains yield heavily late in the year because their growth responds to the major rainy season earlier in the year. The ample water from April to August allows the plant to flower and build large, heavy bunches that mature right around September to November.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee ejaakɛ amɛdalɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ hetoo. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáa kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashi August lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji ni tsii, ni amɛdaraa yɛ September kɛ November teŋ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant new plantain suckers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant is at the start of the major rainy season, usually between April and May. Planting during this time gives the young suckers enough soil moisture to build deep roots before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛ May teŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do prices for crops like plantains drop so drastically during the late months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains jara eba shi waa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Prices drop because of a market glut, which happens when many farmers harvest the same crop at the exact same time. Because fresh produce spoils quickly, farmers lower their prices to sell everything before it rots.
ga: Jara ba shi yɛ nibii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okwaafoi babaoo kpa ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ aduawai ni afee ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya. Okwaafoi baa jara shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ dani egbo.

english: Why do small plantain shoots grow around my main plant, and should I leave all of them to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains bibii No hewɔ lɛ edaa yɛ mitso titri lɛ he Ni ani esa akɛ maha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: These shoots are called suckers and are how plantain plants naturally multiply. You should not leave all of them because they steal nutrients from the main plant; leave only one strong sucker to take over after you harvest the main plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ŋmeii ni amɛji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii. Esaaa akɛ oshɛrɛɔ fɛɛ oshwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha sucker ni he wa kome pɛ aye nɔ beni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves dry up to save water when the soil gets dry. Plantains have large leaves and shallow roots, so they lose water very fast when rain stops, causing the leaves to dry out to protect the main stem.
ga: Agbiɔ plantain baai lɛ koni nu akafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Plantains yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya waa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Ha baai lɛ agbi koni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees sometimes fall over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over mainly because small underground pests like stem borers or nematodes weaken their roots. Without a firm root system, the tree cannot support the heavy weight of a growing plantain bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛji shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop my plantains from ripening and going soft too quickly after harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantains lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains ripen quickly because they release a natural gas called ethylene after being cut. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded place away from direct sunlight slows down this process.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwereɔ oya ejaakɛ ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo kɛ́ afolɔ mli. Okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo be aba, ni hulu la akashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: What can I do with surplus plantains when I cannot sell all of them fresh at the market?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ plantains ni fa fe nine lɛ beni minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ ehee yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: You can process surplus plantains into flour or dried chips. Turning fresh plantains into dried products extends their shelf life from a few days to several months, allowing you to sell them later when prices go back up.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain ni fa fe nine lɛ afee ashikishaŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Kɛ́ atsake plantains heei awo nibii ni egbi mli lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi kɛjɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛyaa nyɔji babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ jara lɛ ku esɛɛ etee ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or cassava on the same plot as my plantain trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, you can grow short-term crops like maize alongside young plantains in their first year. This intercropping makes efficient use of your farm space and gives you food while waiting for the plantains to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ plantains bibii lɛ ahe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli nɛɛ kɛ oŋmɔ mli he lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛha bo niyenii be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni plantains lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough nutrients to produce big plantain bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha plantains wuji akwɛ?

english: Good soil for plantains is dark, rich in decayed leaves or compost, and holds moisture without staying flooded. If your plantains grow very slowly with thin stems and yellowish leaves, the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium and nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha plantains lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee enɔ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo waa ni amɛhe tsei bibii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in open sunlight without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shelter and moisture while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha oná wɔɔhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb toward the sunlight so their leaves can process light into food. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, increases light exposure, and allows the plant to build large underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ atsu la lɛ he nii ni etsɔ niyenii. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, la baaya hiɛ, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow better when flooded with shallow water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flatland ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water controls competing weeds and keeps the root zone consistently moist, allowing rice plants to absorb the heavy amounts of soil nutrients required to form full grains.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kudɔɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tso lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ aba lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the tips usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires substantial nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed manure to maintain green leaves and develop large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji aba.

english: Will planting beans or groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Ani ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ baaye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which enriches the land and helps feed neighboring maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ haa niyenii.

english: Allowing too many shoots, or suckers, to grow from one plantain plant forces them to compete for water and soil nutrients. Pruning down to two or three strong suckers ensures bigger and healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo ni shwereɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: How long can I leave mature cassava tubers in the soil before harvesting them?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifãi momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa?

english: Cassava tubers can remain stored underground in the soil for 12 to 24 months after maturing, but leaving them too long will cause the tubers to turn woody, watery, and lose starch content.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 24 beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei, nu ni amɛmli starch lɛ hu baaje mli.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid, and overly wet conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches opens up the canopy, letting air and sunlight in to dry out the pods and prevent rot.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baagbele ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ naa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la agbi ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Tight leaf curling on tomatoes is frequently caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant, or by extreme heat and drought stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat or water stress. When soil dries out completely, the plant sheds its blossoms to conserve water and survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my maize crops dry up and fail when I plant them immediately after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. Planting too early before the rainy season fully settles means young seeds germinate but then scorch and dry up in the hot soil, wasting your seeds and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ shi kwraa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui bibii baakwɛ̃. Shi kɛkɛ lɛ, eshã ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Efiteɔ odumɔwui kɛ onitsumɔ.

english: How can I harvest crops two times in a single year on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: You can take advantage of Ghana's major and minor rainy seasons by planting fast-maturing crops like early maize or cowpeas during the major season, and immediately following with vegetables or legumes as the minor rains begin.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii anyiɛ sɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ fioo pɛ.

english: How does putting dry leaves or wood dust around my crops help them survive the heat?
ga: Baai ni egbi loo tso sũ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, straw, or sawdust acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool during scorching hot days, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo ŋmei shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii.

english: Can I save money by taking stem cuttings from my old crops instead of buying fresh seeds every season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ shika ato kɛtsɔ mitsei momo lɛ amli ŋmeii ni mafolɔ mli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui heei daa afi?

english: Crops like cassava, yam, and plantain grow very well using stem cuttings, tubers, or suckers from your existing farm. However, for crops like hybrid maize or tomatoes, buying certified seeds gives you much better yields and disease resistance.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ plantains tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii, bulbs, loo ŋmeii ni jɛ oŋmɔ ni oyɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii. Shi, kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ hybrid corn loo tomato lɛ, Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hemɔ baaha oná yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ bo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops onto my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and air to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of vital nutrients like nitrogen, or water is sitting around the roots because of poor drainage, causing the roots to choke and fail to feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha niyenii.

english: Why do insects attack and eat my crops much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa ni amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, green vegetation is scarce, so farm insects flock to your crops for moisture and food. Heavy rains also naturally wash insects off plants and create damp conditions that keep pest populations down.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa. Okwaafoi amli kooloi shwereɔ kɛbaa onibii amli koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Weeds are native wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions and steal nutrients quickly. If you do not clear them early, they rob your crops of food, water, and sunlight, leading to stunted plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya. Kɛji ojieee amɛ mra lɛ, Amɛbaaju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ odɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved directly into bright, hot sunlight. Moving them late in the afternoon or on cloudy days, watering them immediately, and providing light shade helps them adjust smoothly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaná piŋmɔ kɛjɛ tsakemɔ mli kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ oya kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves surrounding the cob turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard. Harvesting too early leads to mold, while leaving it too long exposes the ears to insects and birds.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Abɛi lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha toi lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ okpoi baanyɛ aná.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize crop so it grows well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ awo mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at specific growth stages—first about two weeks after sprouting to build strong roots, and again at knee-height to help the plant form large, full ears.
ga: Abele biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ koni efee shishifãi ni wa. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ etsitsi nɔ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ená toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my cassava stems too close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too closely, the plants compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and small tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Will trimming small side stems off my tomato plants help them produce bigger fruit?
ga: Tso lɛ fã bibioo lɛ ni aaafo Ani kɛ́ mijie kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi-tomato lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji?

english: Yes, removing small side shoots forces the plant to send its food and energy into developing larger, healthier tomatoes instead of extra stems and leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ amaje koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ a ngɔ tso ɔmɛ kɛ tso ɔmɛ kpahi kɛ piɛɛ he.

english: What happens to my tomato crop if heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off oxygen, leading to root rot, wilting, and fungal diseases that can kill the plants quickly.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbe tsei oya.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during dry spells or sudden weather changes to conserve energy and water, or as a result of insect pest attack.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. aloo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli baa.

english: How do weeds growing around my young crops reduce my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi dumɔwui lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ aha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crop, causing your crops to remain weak and produce smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by pest caterpillars feeding on the crop, which weakens the plant's ability to use sunlight for food and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ hulu la atsu nii kɛha niyenii kɛ dalɛ.

english: Why does mixing dried animal manure into my farm soil help crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Animal manure enriches the soil with organic matter, improving its ability to hold moisture during dry periods while slowly feeding crop roots over time.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, Ha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens to my maize grain quality if I harvest the cobs too early before they dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ dani amɛgbi?

english: Harvesting early leaves high moisture inside the grain, making it soft, lighter in sale weight, and very prone to mold growth during storage.
ga: Nikpamɔ mra lɛ kɛ dumɔwui amli nu ni fa babaoo baa. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ Nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ amli tsiimɔ waaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Should I plant all my crop seeds directly into the main field or use a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔji atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Crops with tiny, delicate seeds like tomatoes, peppers, and cabbage do best in a nursery bed where you can protect them from heat and heavy rain. Stronger crops like maize, beans, and cassava can be planted directly into your main farm field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kaabe yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I prepare a simple nursery bed to help my crop seeds sprout well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baaye abua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: To make a good nursery bed, clear the area, break the soil into fine loose pieces, mix in organic manure, and raise the bed slightly off the ground so rain doesn't wash away your seeds. Keep it moist and build a simple shade using palm fronds.
ga: Koni afee ŋmɔ mli saatso kpakpa Tsumɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Jaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bibii bibii. Mix organic fertilizer No sɛɛ lɛ, wo saatso lɛ nɔ fioo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ lɛ akashwie dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni okɛ tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ palm baai lɛ afee shade ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I protect my tender young crop seedlings from getting scorched by the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Young crop sprouts need partial shade while their roots are developing. You can build light shades above them using palm branches or sticks, or plant fast-growing shade plants nearby to filter the strong sunlight.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tso niji loo tsei niji afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛhe. Aloo dumɔ tsei ni shwereɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Koni ajie hulu la ni naa wa lɛ

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a good balance of moisture, warmth, and air to break open and sprout. If the soil is too dry, buried too deep, or packed too hard, the seeds will take longer to sprout or might rot underneath.
ga: Ehe miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ aná fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, afu lɛ mli tsɔ, loo ewa tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crop seedlings suddenly fall over and die just a few days after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by seedling rot (damping-off disease) when the soil stays too wet and cloudy weather prevents drying. It rots the tender stem right at ground level. Keeping soil damp—but not soaked—helps avoid this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egboi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Damping-off hela (damping-off hela) baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni atatu haaa egbi. Egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ efɔɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee naagba nɛɛ.

english: How deep should I plant my seeds so they sprout easily?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: A good rule of thumb is to bury a seed at a depth equal to twice its size. Small seeds need to be placed shallowly near the surface so they have enough energy to reach the sunlight, while larger seeds can go slightly deeper.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni esa akɛ atsu he nii ji ni afu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ yeɔ egbɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ awo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui wuji baanyɛ abote mli fioo.

english: Why do I see so many ants around my young crop seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Ants are drawn to soft soil, moisture, or tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids that feed on young crop shoots. While ants themselves don't always eat the plant, their presence usually signals that other small pests are attacking your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli bɔdɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ jeee be fɛɛ be ŋmeii yeɔ tsei moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi miitutua oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do insects attack my crop leaves right when they start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Freshly sprouted leaves are soft, full of water, and easy for insects to chew through compared to tough, older leaves. Checking your farm early in the morning allows you to catch and manage these pests early.
ga: Baai ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ mli mlɛo kɛ akɛto baai ni wa ni egbɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni otsa amɛ mra.

english: Does planting crops near a farm pond or wet area make them grow faster?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nubu loo he ko ni nu yɔɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha amɛdara oya?

english: Plentiful soil moisture helps crop roots drink up plant food easily, which speeds up growth. However, if the ground stays completely waterlogged, roots can drown from a lack of air, so balance is key.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ babaoo lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaaye tsei niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyaa hiɛ oya. Shi, kɛji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ-feemɔ he miihia.

english: How can I store water on my farm to keep my vegetables growing during dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛdu mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can dig a small catchment pond or farm reservoir ('kuba') at a low point on your land to collect rainwater runoff. This stored water can then be used to bucket-water or irrigate your crops when the rains stop.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu bibioo ko loo ŋmɔ mli nubu (‘kuba’) yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni okɛbu nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni ato nɛɛ awo onibii amli nu loo okɛshwie nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why does maize grow so well in places like Northern Ghana and Brong-Ahafo compared to wetter forest areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei tamɔ Ghana Kooyigbɛ kɛ Brong-Ahafo lɛ? Kɛ akɛto kooi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ahe

english: Northern Ghana and Brong-Ahafo have expansive savannah and transition lands with well-drained soils and direct sun that cereal crops like maize need, whereas heavy forest soils can hold too much water and rot corn roots.
ga: Ghana Kooyigbɛ kɛ Brong-Ahafo yɛ ŋmɔji wuji kɛ tsakemɔ hei ni shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa biɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu babaoo mli ni eha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Can I plant the exact same corn seed variety in the Volta Region that my family uses in Northern Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi ni miweku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Ghana Kooyigbɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ Volta kpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: It is better to choose seeds suited to your local environment; Northern varieties are bred for shorter rainy seasons and drier savannah soil, while the Volta Region often needs varieties adapted to different rainfall patterns and coastal or riverland soils.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Akwɛɔ kooyigbɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo kɛ savannah shikpɔji ni egbi. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ Volta kpokpaa lɛ biɔ tsei srɔtoi ni kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi kɛ ŋshɔnaa loo faa shikpɔji lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why do I see corn plants growing by the roadside without anyone watering or feeding them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he ni mɔ ko mɔ ko wooo amɛ nu loo ehaaa amɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Corn seeds accidentally drop from transport trucks and take root because roadside soil catches rainwater runoff, but without field management, these wild-growing plants produce small and poor-quality ears.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwu ko gbee shi kɛjɛ lɔle lɛ mli yɛ oshara mli ni etswa shishifãi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ ji he ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ bɛ Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi nɛɛ amli lɛ woɔ toi bibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants curl up tightly during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the crop's natural defense mechanism to save water; by shrinking its leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni abaatsi shi koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ enɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs only half-filled with grains when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fã pɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Incomplete cobs usually happen if the plant suffered from dry weather or lack of nutrients during pollination, which stops the wind from successfully carrying pollen from the tassels to the silks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aná pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛya siliki lɛ mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Yellow leaves indicate that your crops are starving for nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away nutrients beyond the reach of the young roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller corn yields when I plant corn on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients, so rotating corn with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ nitrogen-fixing nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa baatsake ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my corn seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, causing the stalks to grow thin and weak with small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds early before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni adu tsei.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will steal sunlight, soil moisture, and fertilizer, preventing your seeds from getting a strong start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju hulu la. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni haaa odumɔwui lɛ aná shishijee ni mli wa

english: What is eating holes in the leaves of my young corn before the plant even flowers?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ shwereɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the central funnel of the plant to feed on tender new leaves as they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ beni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom, it usually means the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The plant automatically moves the few nutrients it has up to the young top leaves to stay alive, leaving the older bottom leaves to wither.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the earth. It shades the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps root temperatures cool so crops can survive longer between rains.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eha shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i ahi shi Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak without big fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni aduawai wuji bɛ mli beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops need sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to build fruit. When planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight and stretch upward instead of spending energy on growing thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, moŋ lɛ amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers using sunlight on their leaves. Lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to catch maximum sunlight and prevents damp leaves from rotting on the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from the parent tree. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the ground without draining away, root rot fungi multiply and cause the tubers to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni ejeee kpo lɛ Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign of tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the leaf sap and transmitting viruses, which distort normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ he okadi. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: This issue, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by inconsistent watering while the fruit is developing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiya hiɛ oya lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to move pollen from flower to flower. If weather conditions are too dry or insects are absent, unpollinated flowers drop off naturally without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kooloi bibii bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize seeds into dry soil before the rains fully start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to swell up and germinate. If sown into dry, hot soil, seeds may heat up and die, or sprout weakly with the first light sprinkle and wither before the real rains come.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛfuu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ adɔ fe nine ni amɛgboi. Aloo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli ni amɛgbiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and small if I keep planting cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji midu cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: When you plant the same crop on the same land every season, it drains the specific nutrients it needs, leaving the soil exhausted. Rotating cassava with crops like beans or cowpeas helps put fresh nitrogen back into the dirt and breaks the cycle of soil diseases.
ga: Beni oduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be mli lɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa pɛ kɛyaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen hee baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni ekpa helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize seeds when the rainy season first starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should not plant right after the very first rain shower because the ground is still dry underneath and the intense heat can scorch the seeds. Wait until you get a few steady days of rainfall so the soil stays deep moist, which allows the seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oduɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ shishigbɛ. Ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and overwhelm my young crops even after I cleared the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping in the soil until clearing exposes them to rain and sunlight. Covering the bare dirt around your plants with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ hulu la baa amɛnɔ. Ale shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la akashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why does chicken manure sometimes help my crops grow better than the fertilizer bags I buy from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tsina ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei kotokui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost of food, but chicken manure feeds the plants slowly while also improving the structure of your soil so it can hold water longer during hot days.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii oya. Shi tsina ŋmɔtɔ haa tsei niyenii fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: What causes tiny worms to suddenly appear and eat big holes through my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa ni amɛyeɔ buji wuji kɛtsɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli?

english: These are pests like fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on crop leaves by moths during warm weather. Checking your farm early in the morning helps you spot these caterpillars early before they destroy the middle growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ tsei ahe baa nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii nɛɛ mra. dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ dalɛ he ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing big green leaves but dropping all their blossoms without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Extreme heat or lack of water can also stress the tomato plant, causing its delicate blossoms to fall off.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When yam seeds are planted too close to each other, their roots fight underground for water, air, and plant food. Spacing them out gives each tuber enough room and nutrients to grow big and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ tsei aniyenii. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa bulb fɛɛ bulb naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains nearby creates a protective shield of shade and keeps the air humid around the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo aduɔ kookoo tso ko yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaafee gãimlibii ni baabu he kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli fũuɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get damaged by small insects and rot when I store it in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects and mold thrive on moisture inside stored crops. If maize is not dried completely under the sun until the grains are hard before storage, the trapped wetness attracts dark weevils and causes the grain to rot.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye kɛji ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmãa ni hiɛ su diŋ lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck the plant juice and spread a virus, rather than a simple lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nu baaje emli kɛkɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary canopy protection, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender seedlings until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why should I cut back weeds around my crop roots before adding fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi ahe dani mawo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water and nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds around the base ensures that the crop receives the full benefit of the fertilizer rather than sharing it with unwanted grass.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛha onibii. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe sɛɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ baaja

english: Yellow lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy plant color and yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage me to intercrop cowpeas or groundnuts with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi hewalɛ koni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This feeds the neighboring maize crops naturally and improves overall soil fertility without extra fertilizer cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni ŋmãa kroko fataaa he.

english: Why does harvesting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year lower my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikpaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting one single crop drains specific nutrients from the soil while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating different crops restores balanced soil nutrients and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tso kome ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil food. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and small maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy stems above ground but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava to direct its energy into growing thick stems and leafy foliage instead of roots. Balancing soil nutrients with potassium helps redirect energy back down to produce larger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei tsɔɔ ehewalɛ mli kɛyaa tsei ni mli eyi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Midumɔwui ni yɔɔ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Covering soil with dried plant matter, called mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It retains moisture during dry spells, keeps soil temperatures cool, and prevents topsoil from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if armyworms are attacking my maize early in the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ parasaiti miitutua mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Check the central funnel of young maize plants for ragged, torn holes in the leaves and fine, powdery droppings. Early detection allows you to treat the central funnel before the pest destroys the growing tip.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛji buji ni etse yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni akɛ powda fee lɛ yɛ mli. Nibii ni anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I prune off excessive branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning thick or dead branches allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy. Good ventilation lowers humidity around pods, which significantly prevents fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni mli tse loo ni egboi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ yiteŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni no tsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa waa.

english: Why do I see small worms inside my maize stalks eating the plants from within?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ni yeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ?

english: Those worms are stem borers. They hatch from eggs laid by moths and bore into the stem to feed, which blocks water and nutrients from reaching the top of your crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli. Amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akutsei amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Enɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ayashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my yam leaves to wither suddenly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: This usually happens when tiny worms called nematodes or root beetles are attacking the tuber and roots underground. Damaged roots cannot drink water, causing the leaves above ground to dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi lɛ tutua ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more during the rainy season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: The damp, warm weather of the rainy season creates ideal breeding conditions for insects, and fresh green leaves give them plenty of food to grow quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi lɛ náa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfɔɔ. Ni baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I cut off and throw away cocoa pods that have black spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ni mashɛrɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ ashwie?

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal disease called black pod. Removing infected pods prevents rainy weather from splashing the fungal spores onto healthy pods nearby.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods kɛ helai diji baa. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be naa koni ekashwie fungal spores lɛ nɔ yɛ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does rot spread so quickly from one vegetable plant to the next in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ aduawai tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rot is caused by germs that spread through soil, splash water, or farm tools. When crops are planted too close together, the disease moves easily from an infected leaf to a healthy one.
ga: Hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ sũ, nu ni shwieɔ shi, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Hela lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is under stress, often from pests sucking its juices or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops its lower leaves to conserve energy for new growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baashi baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha dalɛ hee.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces its exposure to the hot sun to save moisture and prevent itself from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei baa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to spray crop medicine early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ tsei anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon heat can cause chemical sprays to evaporate too fast or burn tender leaves. Morning and evening hours are cooler, allowing the plant to safely absorb the treatment.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eshã baai bibii. Leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why must I repeat spraying my infected crops over several days instead of just doing it once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbii babaoo mli moŋ fe shikome pɛ?

english: A single treatment usually kills adult pests but leaves behind eggs. Repeating the treatment over a set number of days ensures you kill the new pests as they hatch before they can reproduce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa kome pɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda lɛ shi eshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Tĩi tsofafeemɔ lɛ mli gbii ayibɔ ni he hiaa lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ogbe kooloi heei beni amɛfɔɔ lɛ dani amɛfɔ bii.

english: Will applying extra crop medicine help my sick plants heal much faster?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ ni etsa oya kwraa?

english: No, using more medicine than recommended can burn the roots and leaves, killing the crop. Plants need the exact recommended dosage to recover safely without damage.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni gboiɔ. Tsei lɛ he miihia tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before they even grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Applying fertilizer like NPK or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients the maize needs to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my crops perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni mikɛ mi-corn lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer. This feeds the neighboring maize plants and leaves the soil richer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does hard, packed soil cause my groundnut crops to produce very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa mi-peanut tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need to push their flower stems underground to form nuts. Hard soil makes it difficult for the stems to penetrate and expand, so loosening the soil before planting helps the roots and nuts grow freely.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii ashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashishi kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi dani odu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and refusing to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended insecticides protects the leaves so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding lime or poultry manure helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime loo kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have ragged holes and powdery dust inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ sũ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant. Applying recommended treatments directly into the central funnel of the plant early in the morning helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the soil when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but standing water smothers them and leads to rotting. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my yam plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist during hot days while preventing weeds from growing and taking nutrients from your yams.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot support with water and food, but extreme heat or lack of insect pollinators can make it worse. Keeping soil moist with shade trees and avoiding unnecessary chemical sprays helps more flowers become pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii ni aha amɛ nu. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo pollinators ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela lɛ he okadii lɛ aya hiɛ.
