Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to steal food, light, and water from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers so that only two or three remain results in much larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Afoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Enɛ haa plantain ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa ni etsiiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops make the plants grow so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Clearing them ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need without sharing.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ amɛ aha.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sun. They need shade trees to act as natural umbrellas to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni amɛbu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Excess water fills up the air spaces in the soil, preventing the cassava roots from breathing. This stagnant water creates conditions for fungal rot to attack the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Nu ni damɔ shi nɛɛ haa shihilɛi baa ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baatutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat up the middle leaves of my maize plants at night?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which hide inside the central whorl of the plant during the hot day and feed at night. Putting a little clean sand or neem powder inside the leaf whorl can help control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo loo neem powda fata baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with insecticidal soap or neem extract keeps the new leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in the same small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the roots fight each other for food and water, resulting in weak, thin stalks that produce very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber, while preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Multiple suckers steal water and nutrients from the mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two shoots, ensuring the main plant yields a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ baaná plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant crops in straight lines instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔɔgbɛ dumɔwui wɔshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every plant gets equal space, air, and sunlight. It also makes it much easier to walk through the field to clear weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging the crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni tamɔ amɛhe. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa hu akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okpa ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear all the wild bush and weeds before planting my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Weeds and wild bushes steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil. Clearing them before planting ensures your cassava stem cuttings get all the nutrients they need to grow strong roots quickly.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei niji lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot survive intense heat. Direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out root moisture, which is why temporary shade crops like plantains are needed to shelter them.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ he hiaa koni amɛha hulutsoo lɛ aha lɛ.

english: Why do plantain suckers take so long to sprout during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need moisture to wake up their root systems. During harmattan, the soil dries out completely, causing the plant to stop active growth until rain returns.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni ekɛte shishifãi lɛ ashi. Yɛ Harmatta beaŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural defense mechanism. It reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, helping the maize plant trap moisture inside and survive the intense heat of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: How does mixing dried animal manure into the soil help my crops stay green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil. It improves soil structure so that the ground holds onto rainwater for longer periods, keeping crop roots fed and hydrated even when rain stops for a few days.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ náa niyenii ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my yam setts too deep inside the soil mound?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Planting yam setts too deep forces the young shoots to expend too much energy struggling to reach the surface sunlight. This weakens the vine and leads to smaller tubers at harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni amɛkɛwuu kɛha hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji akpa.

english: Why do cassava tubers grow bigger and longer in loose, tilled soil than in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ fe sũ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need soft soil to expand outwards easily. Hard, unbroken soil squeezes the growing roots, preventing them from swelling into full-sized tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ekumɔko lɛ baatsi shishifãi ni miida lɛ amli. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafuu ni amɛfee bulbs ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani etsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, kɛji akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, renewing land fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight or severe dry heat. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the intense sun and retain air moisture, their leaves scorch, turn yellow, and dry up.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo la ni mli egbi waa lɛ naa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he Koni atsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Abaashã baai lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I let all the young shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one parent plant, they all compete for the same nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing excess shoots leaves only two or three, allowing the main plant to get enough food to produce big, healthy plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii daraa kɛbɔleɔ Nyɛ tso kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Tsobii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kome mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha baai enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji ni wa.

english: Why should I use tall wooden stakes to hold up my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ atsu nii kɛmɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves into the sunlight and improves airflow. Sunlit leaves produce more food for the plant, which leads to bigger yam tubers underground and prevents the leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Baai ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii babaoo aba. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Why do I see tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants and eating holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ekɛ ehe tee mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni eyeɔ bu yɛ mli.

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the growing center of maize. They feed on young leaves from the inside, which can ruin the crop's development if not caught and managed early.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ ni atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and making the whole plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ekpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the plant, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. This damage stunts the plant's growth and stops fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa ni ekpaa aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Without steady moisture and mild heat, the flowers fail to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil. When the plant roots decay, they leave this natural fertilizer behind for future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the heavy rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ tsei lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. Applying it a few weeks after planting and lightly covering it with soil near the plant stems helps the roots absorb it before rain sweeps it away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli ji otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ ashwie lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for long periods, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing waterborne rot-causing organisms to infect them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná hela.

english: Why does my swamp rice turn pale and grow poorly if the water level stays too deep for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-marsh rice lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji nu lɛ mli tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Although swamp rice likes wet soil, submerging young plants in deep water blocks sunlight and oxygen from reaching the stalks, causing the leaves to turn yellow and delaying crop growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ moŋ Shi tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ nu ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build green leaves. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to the newer top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to fade and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Excess rain fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the cassava roots due to lack of oxygen. This overly wet environment encourages harmful soil fungi to multiply and attack the swollen tubers, turning them soft and rotten.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ fe nine nɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛtutua ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high off the damp ground so every leaf can catch direct sunlight and stay safe from fungal diseases lurking in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai feɔ niyenii, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When crops are crowded, they grow thin, weak, and produce smaller yields than properly spaced plants that have room to feed and expand.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ he ko ni amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ.

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or irregular water supply. When the plant gets stressed by hot afternoon sun or dry soil, it drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli. Kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tsei hao lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick plants use to save water. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to direct heat and harsh sunlight, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant beans or cowpeas alongside my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. This enriches the soil and helps nearby crops grow better without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ mli efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ he ehiaaa amɛ babaoo.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests or diseases that feed on that crop to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi loo helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa helai lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crop yield even after I have already applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔji amli po sɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than normal crops and will aggressively drink up the water and fertilizer you applied before your crops can reach it. Leaving weeds in your farm starves your main crop of the nourishment it needs to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ, ni amɛbaanu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anaaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to prune away the small sucker branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Pruning removes useless extra branches that waste the tree's food and energy without producing pods. Clearing these shoots also opens up the tree canopy to let in fresh air and sunlight, which keeps harmful insects and black pod disease away.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ hu haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ black pod hela lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Is it really possible to grow a whole yam plant using just a single leaf instead of burying a heavy tuber?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ baa kome pɛ atsu nii ni akɛdu sweet potato tso muu fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaafu ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Yes, under special nursery or lab conditions, scientists and technicians can grow a full yam plant from just a leaf cutting. While regular field farming uses tuber pieces, leaf propagation allows quick production of clean seed yams without wasting heavy food tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe loo laboratori krɛdɛɛ ko mli lɛ shishi. Jeŋ nilelɔi kɛ ŋaalɔi enyɛ amɛdu sweet potato tsei ni kɛlɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛfoɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii tsuɔ nii moŋ, shi Leaf propagation haa anáa ŋmeii ni he tse oya ni ŋmeii ni tsii ni haa niyenii lɛ fiteee.

english: If I cut a leaf from my yam plant and push it directly into my farm soil, will it grow into a yam?
ga: Kɛji mifo sweet potato tso ko baa ni mikɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ani ebaada ni etsɔ ŋmei?

english: No, planting a leaf directly into normal field soil will cause it to dry out and rot. Leaf propagation requires a clean, high-moisture nursery environment with special nutrient media so fragile roots can form before the plant goes into field soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu baai tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. Baai lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ biɔ shihilɛ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛfata niyenii krɛdɛɛi ahe lɛ Enɛ ji koni shishifãi ni waaa lɛ anyɛ afee dani tso lɛ aya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How can I get more seed yams to plant without saving half of my harvest every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sweet potato dumɔwui babaoo ni madu ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã etooo daa afi?

english: You can use rapid multiplication methods like leaf or vine cuttings in a nursery setting. Taking small cuttings every few weeks from one mother plant allows you to produce dozens of new seed plants while keeping your big yams to sell at the market.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashwereɔ oya tamɔ baai ni afolɔ loo wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. niji bibii ni afoɔ Kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso kome pɛ mli Otsii fioo komɛi baaha oná tsei heei srɔtoi srɔtoi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, mikɔlɔ yam tso agbo ko ni miyahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Can a single yam plant give me enough cuttings to create many new plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ sweet potato tso kome mli ŋmeii ni mikɛfee tsei heei babaoo?

english: Yes, a healthy yam plant produces new shoots continually. In a protected nursery, you can take small leaf or stem cuttings every three to four weeks from one mother plant to raise many new plantlets throughout the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei daa. Yɛ ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he mli Obaanyɛ ofolɔ baai bibii loo ŋmeii. Kɛjɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ nɔ daa otsii 3-4 kɛyashi tsei heei akwɛ̃ɔ. babaoo yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: How long does it usually take for a young yam plant to start producing new leaves after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ baai heei akwɛmɔ shishi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Under warm, moist, and healthy conditions, a young yam sprout or cutting typically takes about three to four weeks (one month) to start producing a strong set of new green leaves.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ hewalɛ shishi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ (nyɔŋ kome) dani sweet potato bibii ni afolɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I need so many healthy green leaves on my yam vine if the yam grows under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi ni maná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be ni yams kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam leaves act like tiny food factories. They catch sunlight and convert it into energy, which the plant then sends down underground to swell up and build the actual yam tuber that you harvest.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ hei bibii. Amɛ mɔɔ hulu la ni amɛ tsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Akɛ enɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efu ni efee sweet potato ŋmeii ni okpaa lɛ.

english: How often does a healthy yam vine produce new leaves during the growing season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ wein tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ji sweet potato lɛ baajie baai heei yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When a yam plant has sufficient water and soil nutrients, it grows rapidly, regularly expanding its vine and producing new flushes of leaves every three to four weeks.
ga: Beni sweet potato tsei lɛ ná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaakwɛ̃ oya. Wein tso lɛ baagbɛ eshwa daa. Ni baai heei jeɔ kpo daa otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ.

english: What is the benefit of buying seed yams that were started in a lab or specialized nursery?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ sweet potatoes ni adu yɛ laboratori loo ŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ ko mli lɛ hemɔ he?

english: Lab-grown seed yams are raised in sterile, clean materials. This means they are completely free from hidden soil diseases, worms, and rot, leading to healthier crops and higher yields on your farm.
ga: Aduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ Lab lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni he tse, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers use special clear liquid or gel mixtures in containers instead of normal farm dirt to grow young plant cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ nu ni mli tse loo gel ni akɛfutuɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ najiaŋ koni amɛkɛdu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Normal farm soil contains tiny pests, weeds, and rot-causing germs that easily kill weak young cuttings. A clean, nutrient-rich growth gel or medium gives delicate new plants a safe, disease-free environment to sprout roots fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli sũ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, jwɛi, kɛ helai ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ yɔɔ mli. ni gbeɔ tsei niji bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo Gel loo nɔ ni haa tsei heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni hela bɛ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara oya.

english: Why do my seed yams sometimes rot in the ground before they even sprout leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ewoɔ baai lɛ?

english: Seed tubers cut from old harvests often carry hidden fungal infections or pest damage from the previous season. When buried in damp soil, these diseases spread quickly and destroy the tuber before it can shoot up leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei ni afo kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛji akɛ afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfeɔ baai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, hot sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over once they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top becomes too heavy for the roots to hold, especially during wind. Supporting the stem with a bamboo fork or wooden prop prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsii lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green, healthy leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves with little green powder inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ powda bibioo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and feeds on young leaves. Early checking of fields and applying appropriate control measures into the central whorl can save the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles in heavy soil without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi to attack them, causing root rot. Planting on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu gbee shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atutua amɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni okɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which travels down to swell the tuber underground. If weeds cover the vines or there are no stakes, the leaves cannot capture enough light to grow big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛji jwɛi ha wain tsei lɛ anɔ loo tsei komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or sudden heavy watering. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni mli wa trukaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛha amɛhi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites that hide under leaves and suck out sap. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to distort and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Spreading dry plant material around crops is called mulching. It shields the soil from hot sunshine, reducing water loss through evaporation, keeping soil temperatures cool, and preventing weed seeds from receiving light to germinate.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away granular fertilizer off the field or buries it too deep before crop roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer when soil is moist—but not during heavy storms—ensures the plant drinks the nutrients effectively.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe loo efuɔ amɛ tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ—shi jeee yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ—baaha tsei lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to protect them, the sun burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture needed for their survival.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni baabu he lɛ bɛ Hulu la lɛ shãa ebaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down underground to expand and swell the yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eyakwɛ̃ ni egbɛ eshwa ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Why shouldn't I plant many maize seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ oduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Leaving too many small shoots forces the main plantain tree to share its water and food. Removing extra suckers directs energy into the main plant so it can produce bigger plantain bunches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ fa tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa tso titri lɛ mli. Koni enyɛ ekɛ dumɔwui wuji aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn light yellow after a period of heavy, continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots and preventing them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which turns leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit mainly due to extreme heat, uneven watering, or attack by tiny pests like thrips that damage the flower stems.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii, titri lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so root systems can absorb it safely. Applying concentrated dry fertilizer to bone-dry soil burns the roots and kills the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mli wa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts helps improve my soil for the next crop season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by these insects that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa ni haa tsei kpaɔ amɛdalɛ

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest under the ground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and visible cracks appear in the soil at the base of the plant from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ shwereɔ kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that shield the delicate leaves from sunburn and keep the surrounding air and soil cool and moist while the young cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they all fight for the same soil food, water, and sunlight. Pruning away the weaker shoots leaves only the mother plant and one or two strong suckers, allowing the main plant to put all its energy into growing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. When food in the soil is low, the plant pulls available nitrogen out of its older, bottom leaves to keep its newer, top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce a lower harvest the year after I use heavy chemical fertilizers without adding animal manure or compost?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo faaa yɛ afi ni mikɛ tsofa ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji fataaa he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give plants a quick boost of food, but they do not nourish the living organisms in the soil that create lasting soil health. Over time, relying only on chemical inputs hardens the soil, making it hold less water and organic nutrients for future crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii oya. Shi ehaaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa sũ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ niyenii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ faaa.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts in my maize field makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut roots stay in the soil after harvest, they release this natural plant food for the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmei shishifãi yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: High heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from fertilizing properly. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally sheds the blossoms to conserve its water and energy until temperatures drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baafite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing the inside hearts of my young maize plants right after a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ atsui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛgbi be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Warm, dry spells allow pests like the Fall Armyworm to hatch rapidly and seek shelter inside the moist center leaves of young maize plants. Inspecting the field early during dry periods helps catch them before they destroy the plant's growing tip.
ga: Be ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni amɛfɔɔ oya ni amɛnaa abobaahe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers rot quickly in the ground if heavy rain falls right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall fills the small air spaces in the soil with water, cutting off oxygen to the cassava roots. Waterlogged soil creates ideal conditions for rot fungi to attack mature tubers before they can be dug up.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmei ni egbo lɛ koni etutua ŋmeii ni eda lɛ dani abaanyɛ atsa amɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden sticks instead of spreading across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight, allowing them to capture energy and produce food for the underground tuber. Keeping the foliage off the damp ground also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases from wet soil.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkanáa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from last year's high-yielding hybrid crop produce weak and uneven plants when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwu ni mikɛto nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli tso ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ, kɛ́ midu lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing two specific parent plants to get maximum strength in the first generation. The second generation of seeds loses that special combination, resulting in mixed plant heights, smaller ears, and unpredictable yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni anyɛ ana hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite nakai nibii krɛdɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni amɛhe lɛ futuɔ, toi bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa.

english: What tiny insects help pollinate my cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloo bibioo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers are pollinated mainly by tiny flies called midges. They live in damp leaf litter on the farm floor and move pollen between cocoa flowers so pods can grow.
ga: Fɔlɔi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji. Amɛhiɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ pollen yɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Hand pollination is when you use tiny tools to manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another. It helps create more cocoa pods when natural insects like midges are scarce on your farm.
ga: Nine mli pollination ji be mli ni okɛ nibii bibii tsuɔ nii. koni okɛ onine ajie pollen kɛjɛ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ Ye obua ni ofee kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo beni adebɔɔ mli kooloi, tamɔ ŋmeii, faaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce so many flowers but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo lɛ?

english: This happens mainly because of poor pollination. If there are not enough midges to transfer pollen, or if flowers dry up from heat or chemical damage, the flowers drop without forming pods.
ga: Enɛ baa mli titri yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ midges ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollinate lɛ bɛ, loo kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ egbi yɛ dɔlɛ loo tsofai ni efite lɛ hewɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemicals when my cocoa trees are in full bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he beni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Spraying during full bloom damages delicate open flowers and kills the helpful midges doing pollination work, which destroys your chances of getting a good pod yield.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni agbele lɛ. ni egbeɔ yelikɛbualɔi ni feɔ pollin lɛ. Enɛ baafite hegbɛ ni oyɔɔ akɛ obaaná pod yibiiwoo kpakpa lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day to spray my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ tsofa?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler and pollinating insects are less active, preventing chemical burn on flowers and protecting good insects.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. kɛ kooloi ni feɔ pollinating lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ Etsiɔ tsofai ni shãa fɔfɔi lɛ anaa ni ebuɔ kooloi kpakpai ahe.

english: Can the chemicals I spray on my cocoa trees kill beneficial insects?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, strong pesticides can kill friendly insects like midges and bees along with pests. When good insects are killed, your cocoa flowers cannot get pollinated naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he wa lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, kɛ agbɛnɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kɛ agbe kooloi kpakpai O-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollin yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do cocoa flowers drop off right after I spray chemical insecticide on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: High-concentration chemicals or spraying directly onto open flowers can burn the delicate flower parts and drive away or kill midges, causing unpollinated flowers to die and fall off.
ga: Tsofai ni fa babaoo loo ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni agbele nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ejie ŋmei lɛ loo egbe lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How does a cocoa flower turn into a full cocoa pod?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ?

english: A cocoa flower turns into a pod after a tiny insect transfers pollen into the center of the flower. Once pollinated, the flower petals fall off, and the center swells into a tiny pod.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ kooloi bibii asɛɛ. Okɛ pollen lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollinated Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbee shi. ni yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo

english: Can spraying cocoa trees at the wrong time lower my final harvest yield?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, timing is critical. Spraying during peak flowering or pollination periods destroys the flowers and kills pollinating insects, leading to fewer pods and a smaller harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, be he miihia. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii loo pollination be mli lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔii lɛ ni ebaagbe fɔfɔii ni fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa pods fioo pɛ baa, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Is hand pollination harmful to my cocoa flowers or trees?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yeɔ mi kokoo fɔfɔi loo tso lɛ awui?

english: No, hand pollination is completely safe for your cocoa trees when done carefully. It simply assists nature by placing pollen on the flowers without using any chemicals.
ga: Dabi, nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha cacao tsei kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ye obua adebɔɔ kɛkɛ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ pollen ni okɛ tsofa ko tsuuu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantain on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight can dry them out and kill them. Plantain grows quickly and provides broad leaves to shield young cocoa trees from the harsh sun while giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe amɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Will planting plantains too close to my cocoa trees harm the growth of the cocoa?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ tsɔ lɛ baaná kookoo lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: If planted too closely, plantains can compete with cocoa for water and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows plantains to provide helpful shade without starving the young cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Plantains baanyɛ ekɛ cocoa atswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hɔmɔ yeee kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Does a mature cocoa tree still need shade trees around it like when it was young?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulu tamɔ bɔ ni amɛji beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ lolo?

english: Mature cocoa trees need much less shade than young ones. While a few tall trees help protect the farm from harsh winds and extreme heat, too much shade on mature cocoa causes damp conditions that encourage diseases like black pod.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo fioo kwraa fe tsei bibii. Shi kɛlɛ, tsei fioo komɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Shi ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ kookoo ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ baa.

english: Why would government officers come to cut down my cocoa trees with a machine if the trees are still standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mli onukpai kɛ tsɔnei miifo mi kokoo tsei lɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ damɔ shi lolo lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees get infected with viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, there is no cure. Cutting down the infected trees completely is the only way to stop the virus from spreading and destroying the rest of your farm and neighboring farms.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela ko tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ bote kookoo tsei lɛ, tsamɔ ko bɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ ni efite oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: How can I tell early on if my cocoa trees are getting sick and starting to fail?
ga: Kulɛ mana mra. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ aná hela ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ?

english: Early warning signs of disease include swollen stems, yellow patterns or pale spots on the leaves, pods changing color prematurely, or branches dying back from the tips.
ga: Hela lɛ he kɔkɔbɔɔ mra okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Pods tsakeɔ amɛhe su oya loo nine lɛ gboɔ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ

english: What kind of support can I get from the government if my farm gets infected by cocoa diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ maná kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ dɛŋ kɛji akɛ kookoo hela ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Government organizations like COCOBOD often assist farmers by inspecting farms, helping cut down infected trees safely, and supplying disease-resistant cocoa seedlings to restart the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ COCOBOD yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi yɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ mli. Ye obua ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe. kɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ koni akɛje okwaayeli nitsumɔi shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: If my old cocoa trees are cut down, can I plant new cocoa immediately on the exact same spot?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo mi-kokoo tso momo lɛ Ani manyɛ madu kookoo hee amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: You can replant on the same land, but you must first clear out all old diseased roots, let the soil rest, and plant temporary shade crops like plantain to make the field favorable for new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie shishifãi fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. ni amɛdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni eha jɛmɛ afee he ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui heei.

english: Why are my newly planted cocoa trees struggling to grow on land where cocoa was previously planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni midu ehee lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ aduɔ kookoo yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Older cocoa trees exhaust specific nutrients from the soil over time. Replanting on old cocoa land without replenishing nutrients through organic manure or fertilizers makes it hard for new seedlings to thrive.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ laajeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kookoo shikpɔŋ momo ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ ni akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui heei ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Why does cocoa farming require continuous labor even after the trees are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ biɔ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require ongoing attention like pruning branches to let in light, clearing weeds that steal soil food, and harvesting ripe pods regularly to prevent diseases from spreading.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ amɛfolɔ amɛhe koni amɛná la. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ni kpamɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping leaves and failing to produce pods during certain months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees react strongly to water stress during long dry periods. Without adequate moisture, the tree sheds leaves to save water, which stops it from flowering or holding onto young pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa yɛ nu he haomɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha ekawo fɔfɔi loo ekɛ ehe akakpɛtɛ ŋmeii bibii ahe.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time will restore healthy green leaves and improve crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide necessary shade, cool the soil, and maintain moisture for the delicate cocoa plants during their early development.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Cassava tuber rot happens when water accumulates around the roots due to poor soil drainage or heavy rainfall. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, preventing fungal rots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture through regular watering and mulching helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices. Applying neem oil solution or approved insecticidal soap controls these insects and allows new, healthy leaves to expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over in strong winds before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Heavy fruit bunches make plantain plants top-heavy, and weak root systems struggle to support them. Supporting the stem with strong wooden Y-props and mounding extra soil around the base keeps the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Yibii akui ni tsii lɛ tsiɔ plantain lɛ nɔ. Ni shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfi amɛsɛɛ. Akɛ nibii ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tsei ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ muji krokomɛi ni abua naa ni ebɔle he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Is it really necessary to clear tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ajie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves off the ground toward sunlight so the plant can produce more energy. Vines left trailing on hot ground are more prone to diseases and produce significantly smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking tsiɔ sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo. Wein tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya, ni amɛbaaná ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why are insects swarming and damaging my cowpea plants as soon as they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwereɔ ni amɛfiteɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms are naturally attractive to flower thrips and pod borers seeking sweet nectar. Spraying recommended botanical extracts like neem seed juice during early flowering protects the buds so pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers ni biɔ nectar lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ waa. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso mli tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ mra lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Aduawai kɛ jwɛi

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It holds moisture in the ground during hot dry spells, reduces the need for frequent watering, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔɔ. Ehaa nu ni afɔɔ he hiamɔ baa shi. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are wild weeds growing so much faster than my rice seedlings in the valley field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardier and compete aggressively with rice for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Maintaining a shallow, continuous layer of controlled water in the rice field smothers young weeds while allowing the rice to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛmɔ koni akɛkudɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What actually happens to my cocoa pods if I leave them on the tree too long after they turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ sɛɛ?

english: When cocoa pods overripe on the tree, the seeds inside begin to germinate or rot. This damages the quality of the cocoa beans, making them unsuitable for sale and reducing your harvest income.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ loo amɛbaafite. Enɛ baafite kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. ni ehaa esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ni ehaa shika ni onáa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: It is best to harvest every 2 to 3 weeks during peak season. Harvesting regularly prevents pods from overripening, stops pests from attacking mature fruits, and keeps fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa amɛ daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ. Nibii ni akpaa daa lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ fe nine. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why are some of the green cocoa pods on my farm turning black and rotting before they even get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa po lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by high humidity and excess shade. Removing infected pods early and clearing weeds helps stop the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo be ni fa kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛbaa. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: I see bushy green plants growing directly out of my cocoa branches. Are they harming my trees?
ga: Mina tsei eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miida kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ani amɛmiiye mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, those are parasitic plants commonly called mistletoes. They tap directly into your cocoa tree's branches to steal water and nutrients, which eventually weakens the tree and reduces pod production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, amɛji tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni afɔɔ amɛ gbɛi akɛ mistletoe. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kookoo niji amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ naagbee, ni ebaaha pod ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend that I cut away some of the healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mifo mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm. This reduces fungal diseases like Black Pod and directs the tree’s energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I remove the long fresh shoots growing straight up from the bottom of my cocoa stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ehee ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishi lɛ?

english: These fresh shoots, called suckers or chupons, consume a lot of water and nutrients from the tree's roots. Removing them ensures that all food goes toward pod production on the main branches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii heei nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupon. Eheɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ fɛɛ aya nɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tso lɛ nine wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to plant plantain trees next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide temporary shade and moisture, helping young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i be kukuoo ko. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and look weak during the dry season while my neighbor's farm stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Thick weeds compete with cocoa trees for groundwater during dry spells. Clearing weeds regularly and leaving dry leaves on the soil as mulch helps retain ground moisture so trees withstand dry weather.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ mulch lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa.

english: My cocoa trees produce so many small flowers, but why do most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small portion get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Stress from drought or lack of soil nutrients can also cause the tree to drop unused flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashwie fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: My farm used to yield many bags of cocoa, but now the older trees produce very few pods. What causes this drop?
ga: Kulɛ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo kotokui babaoo. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Mɛni kɛ shigbeemɔ nɛɛ ba?

english: As cocoa trees age, they continuously draw nutrients out of the soil. Without replenishing the soil with organic matter or appropriate fertilizers, the soil loses its fertility, leading to lower crop yields.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da Amɛbaagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense sunlight and drought. When exposed to direct sun without protection, their leaves dry out faster than the roots can supply water, causing them to curl, turn yellow, and burn.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni abuuu he lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji curling Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshã

english: Why does my main plantain stem grow so slowly when there are many small shoots growing at its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ? Nibii babaoo ni miida yɛ eshishigbɛ?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients directly from the main plant. Cutting away most of the extra suckers allows the main plant to keep all the food and produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ toɔ eniyenii fɛɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch as much direct sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which travels down to grow large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyadu ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my cabbage plants look weak and wilted during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, cabbage leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water, and it usually bounces back once the sun sets and the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, Kaabaji baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light green and yellow starting from the lower leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji eŋɔli kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leafy growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the upper leaves, turning the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie emli nibii fioo kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make the soil better for the crop I plant next?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots have tiny nodules that suck nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. No yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen gas lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I tell if my cassava plants are growing thick roots underground rather than just big leafy stems?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe tso lɛ shishifãi agbo ko kɛkɛ?

english: A healthy cassava plant putting food into root tubers will have firm, thick stems with leaf joints spaced closely together. If the plant grows tall and leafy too quickly with wide gaps between leaves, it usually means it has too much nitrogen and is focusing on leaves instead of tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa. Kɛji tso lɛ da ni eshi oya tsɔ ni gbɛ babaoo kã baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ema baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe bulbs lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when rainfall is unpredictable. Extreme heat destroys the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming a tomato seed, so the plant sheds the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ tomato dumɔwui anaa koni ekafee. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants wrinkle up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaf. They suck out the plant sap and sometimes spread viruses that deform the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni bei komɛi lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why does stored maize get hot and rot when I bag it right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?
