english: Freshly harvested maize still contains high moisture. When bagged too soon, the grains continue to breathe and trap moisture and heat inside the bag, which encourages mold growth and insect infestation. Grains must be completely sun-dried before storage.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lolo. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli oya tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ amɛmu ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ kɛ kooloi bibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto.

english: Why is the rain still falling in December when the weather on my farm is supposed to be dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji December lolo be mli ni esa akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli agbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Changing climate patterns in Ghana are causing rainfall seasons to shift and extend into normally dry months like December. Farmers need to adjust their harvesting schedules and watch out for fungal diseases caused by the unexpected wet weather.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ eha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ etsake ni ekɛtee nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa tamɔ December mli, ni enɛ enyɛ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛtsake ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hulutsoo be ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: What happens to my crops when the rains delay for several months during the normal planting season?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Delayed rains cause soil to stay dry, which prevents seeds from germinating and causes young plants to dry up and die because they cannot take up nutrients without moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná niyenii kpakpa kɛji nu bɛ mli.

english: Is heavy rainfall always good for my crops, or can too much rain harm them?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi kɛha midumɔ nii be fɛɛ be. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii awui?

english: While crops need rain, extremely heavy rainfall can wash away topsoil nutrients, flood root systems so plants cannot breathe, and create damp conditions that cause diseases.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hoɔ nu aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba lɛ baa

english: I keep hearing about special high-yield cocoa varieties; how are they different from the traditional cocoa on my farm?
ga: Miyaa nɔ minuɔ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro nɛkɛ kookoo nɛɛ yɛ blema kookoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to grow faster, bear pods within two to three years instead of five, produce higher yields, and withstand tough weather conditions better than traditional cocoa.
ga: Akwɛ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee hybrid koni amɛdara oya. Ha pods yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli yɛ afii enumɔ najiaŋ. Ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa fe tsutsu kookoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the rain suddenly stops for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from heat stress, as they do not have enough moisture to support fruit development.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why is my electricity bill so high when I use an electric pump to water my crops, and how can I manage it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi srawa hewalɛ nyɔmɔwoo lɛ fa babaoo beni mikɛ srawa hewalɛ pɔmp tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ nu lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu he nii?

english: Electric water pumps draw a lot of power when running continuously during dry periods. You can lower costs by using drip irrigation systems that focus water directly on roots or by watering early in the morning to reduce evaporation.
ga: Nu pɔmpii ni akɛ la tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ́ amɛmiitsu nii be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi lɛ nɔ

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil so my crops don't die when the rain stops unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii akagboi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves, grass, or plant remains—known as mulching—blocks sunlight from drying out the ground and keeps moisture in the soil for much longer.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo tso ni eshwɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha onibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I wait for heavy rains to start before planting my seeds, or should I plant early in dry soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa dani madu dumɔwui? Aloo esa akɛ madu mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: It is best to plant right after the first steady rains begin so the soil is moist enough for seeds to sprout, but not so soaked that seeds rot or get washed away by heavy downpours.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi jeee ni edɔ waa bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baagboi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the rains continue late into the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ enɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Continuous late-season rain creates cold, humid conditions that allow the fungus responsible for Black Pod disease to thrive and spread quickly across your cocoa farm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ kɛ fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: What should I do on my farm when heavy rain leaves standing water on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water starves plant roots of air, causing them to rot. Digging simple drainage pathways across your field allows excess rainwater to flow away cleanly.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye tsei shishifãi lɛ hɔmɔ. ha egbo Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni ahaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa hetsemɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is vital for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps leaves turn dark green so the plant can make energy and yield larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why did the store-bought fertilizer end up burning my crops instead of helping them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very concentrated. Applying too much at once, placing it directly against plant stems, or applying it to dry soil without water causes chemical burn on roots and leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii babaoo. Ni akɛ babaoo baatsu nii shikome Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni akɛaawo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu bɛ mli Enɛ baaha tsofa ashã shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow much better when I plant beans in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This provides a natural food source that helps neighboring crops like maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense sun, plants sweat out water from leaves faster than their roots can drink from the soil. Placing dried leaves or grass on the soil around the plants (mulching) keeps the roots cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. Keeping soil moisture consistent and planting flowers nearby to attract pollinators helps fruit form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni baahã ŋmɔtɔ aba lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni agbala ŋmɔtɔbii lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with huge leaves, but giving me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put its energy into growing lush stems and leaves rather than storage roots. Balancing soil nutrients directs the plant to store energy in big tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ fɛo moŋ fe ni ekɛ shishifãi baato. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtoɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji amli.

english: Why are my young orange trees dropping green fruits before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso bibioo lɛ woɔ yibii eŋɔli dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees shed fruit early if they experience water stress during dry spells, nutrient shortages, or attack by pests like fruit flies. Steady watering and pest control during early fruiting prevent early drop.
ga: Citrus tsei baawo yibii mra kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ naa.

english: Why did the chemical weedkiller I sprayed kill my crops along with the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Some weedkillers are non-selective, meaning they kill any plant leaf they touch. To keep your crops safe, you must use a crop-specific selective weedkiller or shield crop leaves while spraying.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ halaaa mɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛgbeɔ tsei ni amɛtaa he lɛ ahe baai. Bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ atsu nii loo obu tsei ahe baai ahe beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why did the packaged seed I bought from the farm shop fail to sprout in my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo mli ni mihe yɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Improved seeds often require specific planting depths and damp soil to germinate. If buried too deep, planted in hot dry soil, or exposed to rain that washes them away, the seeds will fail to sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ko ba ni shwie dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Yam rot is caused by small soil pests, bacteria, or fungi that thrive in waterlogged soil. Planting on raised mounds that drain excess water well and choosing rot-free seed yams keeps the harvest clean.
ga: Sweet potato fitemɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii, helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni sweet potatoes ni fiteee lɛ ni ooohala lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse aba.

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and loose soil to stretch and grow big without resistance. Mounding loose soil gives the tuber space to expand downward easily and protects it from waterlogging during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni ekɛgbala ni edara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi enaa. Shikpɔŋ ni ato lɛ haa tuber he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shishi oya, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither if I clear away all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji mijie cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees protect the young plants from extreme heat and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: You should wait until the major rains start consistently, usually after two or three deep rains that thoroughly soak the soil. Planting after just one small rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if rain stops for weeks.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ baaje shishi eba daa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ 2-3 sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is sitting in too much water. Nitrogen acts like food for green leaf growth, so applying fertilizer like NPK or animal manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing lots of big green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy making leaves instead of fruits. Switching to balanced nutrients rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set peppers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium fata he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my tomato plants falling off before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when insects disturb them. Keeping the soil moist evenly with mulch helps the plant retain its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii gbaa mɔ naa Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no hewɔ lɛ ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed tightly, their roots compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving them proper distance allows each plant to spread its leaves fully and produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa ebaa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while naturally suppressing weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What makes the leaves on my cassava plant curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Removing and destroying the twisted plants early stops the sickness from spreading to healthy crops nearby.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei ni efite lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Weeds produce thousands of hardy seeds that stay hidden in the soil for years. When rain falls, these seeds shoot up quickly because they are adapted to survive tough conditions much better than domesticated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ejaakɛ amɛhe esa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shia lɛ.

english: How old does a hybrid cocoa tree need to be before it starts producing pods?
ga: Esa akɛ cacao tso ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ aye afii enyiɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing their first pods around 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crops are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem will start to crack as tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted oil palm seedling to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani oil palm dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: High-yielding oil palm varieties (like Tenera) generally begin producing their first fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo (tamɔ Tenera) lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii akui lɛ ashishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How many months after planting hot pepper should I expect to pick my first harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ esa akɛ makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ gbɛ?

english: Pepper plants usually begin flowering about 2 months after transplanting and will yield mature, harvestable fruits between 3 and 4 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi aaafee nyɔji 2 sɛɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ. Ni aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Flower drop in tomatoes is often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of natural pollinators like bees. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer helps.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua.

english: Why do my watermelon vines produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any melons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ eda ni etsɔ melon lɛ?

english: Watermelons produce male flowers first before female flowers appear. If female flowers drop without fruiting, it usually means insects are not pollinating them, or the plant is stressed from drought.
ga: Watermelon woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ dani fɔfɔi yei jeɔ kpo. Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo hɔmɔ haa tsei haoɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall without forming any corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni amɛwooo ŋmãa ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Maize plants often grow tall without cobs if they are planted too close together, receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, or lack adequate sunlight and water during the critical flowering stage.
ga: Abɛi sumɔɔ ni eda ni ŋmeii bɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anáa loo hulu la kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli.

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to maximum sunlight for food production, lifts the foliage off hot, humid soil to prevent leaf diseases, and encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni akaye baai lɛ ahe hela. ni ehaa yitsei wuji lɛ daraa

english: Yellow leaves on young plantains usually point to a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, root damage from pests like nematodes, or waterlogging in poor-draining soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ plantain bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, loo nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: At what age or height should I prune my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ afii loo bɔ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: You should begin light pruning when the cocoa tree forms its first jorquette (forking point), usually around 1.5 to 2 years old, to remove low side-shoots (chupons) and keep the tree at an accessible height.
ga: Esa akɛ oje tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ shishi fioo beni kookoo tso lɛ feɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ jorquet (junction), ni bei pii lɛ eyeɔ aaafee afii 1.5 kɛyashi 2 lɛ, koni ojie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ (chupon) lɛ ni oha tso lɛ ahi he ko ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their roots are not deep enough yet. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living cover that protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ wala ato ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow and staying small even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil. When maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen, which helps the plant stay green and grow tall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight with each other underground for space, water, and soil food. This causes the plant to produce thin, small cassava roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Heat stress prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, causing the plant to shed the flowers to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or by a virus carried by those insects that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy weight, especially during high winds. Supporting the stem with strong wooden stakes helps hold up the heavy fruit bunch until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi tsɔne ni tsii ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow thick stems and leaves instead of flowers. The plant spends all its energy on leaf growth rather than producing the flowers needed to form pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up towards the sun so their leaves can trap light and make food. Lifting the leaves off the ground allows the plant to send more energy down into growing a bigger tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu la mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná la ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the center funnel of the young maize plant to feed on tender new leaves before they open up.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai heei dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In hot weather, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Wilting is a natural way for the plant to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun to protect itself until temperatures cool down.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa he ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves growing so big and bushy, but the tubers underground remain tiny when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ dara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi tubers lɛ ji bibii kɛ́ mikpa amɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth isn't managed, the cassava plant spends all its energy making green leaves on top instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ a pee zugba a sisi tsɔwi nɛ mi wa.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce food. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows the leaves to trap maximum light and air, which feeds the growing tuber below and prevents leaves from rotting on damp ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni haa bulbs ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ niyenii. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Those shoots, called suckers, act like extra mouths to feed. They steal water and plant food from the main mother plant, which leads to small plantain bunches if you don't remove all but one or two strong ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ suckers. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛyeɔ nii Amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. ni baaha plantains bibii aba Kɛji ojieee tsei fɛɛ shi kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ,.

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom leaves is a sign of hunger, specifically a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left up to the new leaves at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Yellow jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishi akɛ hɔmɔ he okadi. Titri lɛ, nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my corn in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plant dies, that trapped food stays in the earth to feed your next crop of corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni emɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye o-abele ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease. It spreads in wet, shady weather when water drops stay on the pods for too long, allowing microscopic germs to enter and spoil the fruit.
ga: Fungal tutuamɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛ́ nu mli nui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa helai bibii waa boteɔ mli ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the underside of new leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ woɔ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers on the ground without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. The plant drops the flowers to save water and keep itself alive instead of trying to feed fruit.
ga: Tomato baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔ ni jɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ kpe. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye aduawai.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots under the ground are mature enough to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the bottom leaves naturally dry up and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground right around the main stem starts to swell and crack open.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efuuɔ ni ejaraa.

english: When maize plants grow too close, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching neighboring stalks. This causes weak, tall stems that fall easily and yield smaller ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu kɛ niyenii. ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya ni ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from sunlight and wind protection to survive. Leaving large trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain creates a cooler environment that protects the delicate young leaves from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the soil, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Propping them up with wooden poles supports the weight and prevents the wind from blowing them down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii baaha tso lɛ atsii waa. Tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfi muji lɛ sɛɛ ni akɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛba shi lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava tubers rot mainly when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, allowing fungi to attack the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the light, keeps them away from soil diseases, and prevents overcrowding.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa la lɛ he. Etsiɔ helai anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the plant gets either too much or too little water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo loo fioo nɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil extract or insecticidal soap kills these pests and keeps leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of crops called legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil. This natural food feeds the nearby maize and keeps the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Cowpeas fata ŋmeii akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific soil nutrients year after year and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plant roots are actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting. Applying it during heavy rains washes the food away, while applying during dry spells can burn the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi miida. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii shwieɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the growing top leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps keep the whole plant green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest them, they leave behind enriched soil that helps heavy-feeding crops like maize or cassava grow better in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dried plant materials, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops heat from the sun from drying out the soil, retains water longer, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly rots to add nutrients back into the land.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines into the light and keeps the leaves off damp ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni akɛbaakwɛ bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the center of the maize plant where leaves unroll and eats the soft green parts. Checking plants early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem leaf extract can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛheɔ fã ni ji eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a plant virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these tiny insects early with insecticidal soap or neem oil prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni whiteflies hiɛɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked in water for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots dry enough to avoid rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛkagboi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when plants don't get regular water, or if the soil lacks key nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching to keep root areas cool encourages the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i Ebaaye ebua ni ekanya fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch before main rains begin. If seeds sprout after the first rain, the dry spell that follows can dry up and kill the tender seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains are regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Hɔmɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up towards sunlight to grow large, healthy leaves. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and leads to larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ baai wuji ni mli wa. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and chewed patches at the top of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ diski ni atsɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize and eat the tender growth, which can ruin the crop if not caught early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ, ni baanyɛ afite ŋmãa lɛ kɛji amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly collapse and die right at ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbee shi trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which happens when seeds are planted too close together in overly wet soil. Spacing seeds out and reducing excess water prevents the fungus from killing tender stems.
ga: Fungal shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping out kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui lɛ amli ni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shi lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: How does planting groundnuts make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural nitrogen stays behind in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean young cocoa trees are getting too much harsh, direct sunlight or lack proper nutrients. Adding shade plants and applying compost or manure helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso bibioo lɛ ená hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo niyenii ni sa bɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo fata tsei ahe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my developing green tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli ni miiya hiɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which occurs when plants do not get enough calcium or face irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding lime or wood ash helps protect young tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛkɛ nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kpeɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni abu tomato bibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or drought stress. Watering them regularly during dry spells and providing light shade during peak heat prevents flower loss.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haomɔ kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow steals vital nutrients and water from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main stem to produce larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tso lɛ yibii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ awo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that lose water quickly in direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects seedlings from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants energy to grow green leaves; adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using certified disease-free stem cuttings when planting prevents the disease from taking over your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni afolɔ ni hela bɛ mli ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli tsu nii beni oduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, but crops like groundnuts and beans trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Rotating them naturally restores soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and nutrients directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when water supply drops suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rains before sowing my seeds instead of planting at the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: First rains are often followed by hot dry spells that dry out seeds before they can establish roots. Waiting for consistent rainfall ensures seeds have continuous moisture to germinate and grow safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe.

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops usually results in lower yields and weaker plants in the second year. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season guarantees strong germination and high yield potential.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when I store them in a enclosed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily when kept in warm, damp places without good airflow. Storing yams off the ground in a well-ventilated, shaded barn prevents moisture buildup and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa, ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops growing differently this year compared to last year even though I planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Crops react constantly to small changes in weather, rainfall timing, and sunshine hours, which are never exactly the same from one year to the next. Even a short dry spell during a key growth phase can change how fast the crop matures and how much yield it produces.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ tsakemɔi bibii ni baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli, nugbɔshiimɔ bei, kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ahe nii be fɛɛ be. Ebaafee nɔ ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ daa afi. Be kuku ni nu bɛ mli po Yɛ shweremɔ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsake bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ amɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller heads of grain when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close to one another, their roots fight under the soil for nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. This competition starves the crop, causing it to produce smaller, lighter grains.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii ni waaa baa.

english: How can I tell that my rice crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the individual grains at the base of the head feel hard rather than soft or milky when squeezed.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmãa yitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Ni dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo loo amɛfee tamɔ mliki kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛ.

english: What happens to rice grains if I cut them down too early while the stalks are still green?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ oya tsɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Immature rice grains contain soft starch and too much moisture. When processed in a milling machine, these soft grains break easily into tiny pieces, reducing your usable grain quantity and lowering market value.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa bibii lɛ yɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ atsu he nii yɛ tsɔne ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ nii amli lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ fãa bibii bibii oya, ni no haa ŋmãa ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ baa shi. ni ekɛ jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi

english: Why does my harvested rice spoil or develop mold if I store it immediately after cutting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikɛto beni mifo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly cut grains contain high levels of moisture trapped inside. Storing wet grain prevents airflow, causing moisture to build up and create warm conditions where mold and rot thrive.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo ni emɔ emli. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekabɔle he. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do grains shrink and lose weight after I leave them out in the sun to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ beni migbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain is filled with water. As the sun warms the grain, that water evaporates into the air, making the individual seeds harder, slightly smaller, lighter, and safe for long-term storage.
ga: Nu woɔ dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ hulu la lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔ lɛ Nu lɛ baaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ nɔ ni wa. Amɛ yɛ bibioo fioo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ.

english: Why does the inside of my grain pile feel hot when I stick my hand into it after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛ minine wo mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested grains are living tissues that continue to breathe. When grains are stored with extra moisture, their respiration generates heat, which traps steam and accelerates spoilage if the grain is not spread out to dry.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ. Kɛji akɛ ato ŋmaa ni mli edɔ babaoo lɛ Mumɔ haa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu mli lasu ni ehaa efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ agbɛɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwãaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How do small insects get inside my grain bags even when I tie the sacks very tightly?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko bote miŋmaa kotoku lɛ mli? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi waa moŋ

english: Insects like weevils often lay microscopic eggs on the crop while it is still growing out in the field. Once the grain is bagged, the warm conditions inside cause those eggs to hatch into bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwuji bibii ni anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lolo lɛ. Beni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ kotoku mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ mli lɛ haa nakai ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii.

english: Why do processing mill operators prefer grains that have been thoroughly dried before milling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmaa ni egbi kwraa dani ashɛreɔ lɛ?

english: Well-dried grains have a hard outer shell that separates cleanly from the inner seed during milling. Wet grains remain rubbery, which clogs milling machinery and causes the seeds to crush instead of shell cleanly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa ni gbalaa ehe kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ tamɔ rɔba. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ naa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeefo amɛhe.

english: Why do buyers pay less for my harvested grain if it contains a mix of large and small seed sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji dumɔwui wuji kɛ bibii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ?

english: Processing machines are set to handle uniform grain sizes. When mixed grain sizes go into a milling machine, smaller seeds miss the hulling blades while larger seeds get crushed into dust.
ga: Ato tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni etsu ŋmaa dalɛi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ahe nii. Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni dalɛi srɔtoi efutu mli lɛ awo pɛnte tsɔne lɛ mli Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui wuji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ sũ.

english: Why is it best for me to start planting my maize in April or May instead of earlier in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ April loo May mli moŋ fe afi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: In Ghana, the major rainy season usually begins around April or May. Planting during this window ensures your seeds receive consistent rainfall needed to germinate and grow strong without dying from early drought.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi aaafee April loo May. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ naa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛgbooo yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa mra lɛ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. They require shelter from shade crops like plantains or shade trees to retain soil moisture and protect their young leaves during their early growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao he ko ni amɛhi kɛjɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ahe. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu baai bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that it is experiencing stress from too little water or pest damage. Adding organic manure or fertilizer can help restore their green health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo ekɛ haomɔ miikpe kɛjɛ nu fioo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sun, which slows down water loss and protects it from drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Tsei baa baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination by insects. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding chemical sprays while flowers open helps tomatoes set fruit successfully.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni bɛ pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? ni akɛtee mli

english: Ragged holes in young maize are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on the tender growing leaves inside the central shoot, which slows down plant growth if not treated early with proper pest control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai ni miida ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. When weeds are allowed to grow around your crops, they consume the food and water meant for your crops, causing stunted growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛji aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛbɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop relies on and encourages crop-specific pests to live permanently in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like cowpea restores nitrogen and keeps soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ hiɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baafite be fɛɛ be. ni ewo tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits continuously around the roots without draining away, it smothers them and creates damp conditions where soil fungi thrive and cause tuber rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be ni nu shwieee lɛ Nu lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many seeds very close together so that I can harvest more food from a small field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade each other from sunlight and fight for nutrients in the soil. Spacing seeds properly ensures every individual plant gets enough light, air, and soil nutrition to grow big yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh direct sunlight and hot winds. Leaving larger trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does it matter which way I push my cassava stems into the dirt when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, ani bɔ ni aaafee atsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds or 'eyes' pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the roots struggle to develop and the plant yields very little.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa naagba yɛ amɛshweremɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up the weight of heavy fruit bunches during high winds. Supporting the stalk with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants dropping off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off when the plants experience water stress from hot, dry weather or from applying too much chemical fertilizer at once. Consistent watering helps plants keep their flowers and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be kome mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are there ragged holes and soft waste inside the tops of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf whorls of young maize. Catching them early and applying organic treatments like neem oil or approved pesticides can stop the damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, prevents the sun from drying out the soil quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps root zones cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to the light, preventing disease from wet soil contact and improving tuber yields.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli. Tsi hela naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. ni eha tuber feemɔ aya hiɛ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and bear small fruits when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing lets each plant get what it needs to produce a full harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer on my field right before a huge downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafɔse ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away fertilizer before the roots can absorb it, wasting your investment. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but no heavy storm is expected immediately.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi be mli ni akpaaa ahum ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How often should I apply fertilizer to my crops to make them grow faster?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Applying fertilizer every 30 days during the main growing period gives crops a steady boost of nutrients, allowing them to grow rapidly and produce healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli daa gbii 30 yɛ be titri ni tso lɛ daa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does weeding every month help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa nyɔɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing weeds every 30 days stops wild plants from stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from your crops, keeping them growing at a fast pace.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa gbii 30 lɛ baaye abua ni koo mli tsei akaju hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Ha amɛdara oya

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very slowly this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Slow growth usually happens when crops lack nutrients or water, or when underground pests eat the roots, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛ́ amɛbɛ niyenii loo nu. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ shishifãi lɛ Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are insect pests damaging my crop leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai oya nɛkɛ?

english: Insects feed aggressively when temperatures are warm, and if left unchecked, a small group of pests can quickly multiply and ruin your crop yield within weeks.
ga: Kplukai taoɔ niyenii waa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa. Ni kɛji oshi lɛ Kuu bibioo ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwere oya ni amɛfite onibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and drop off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded farms, so pruning excess foliage helps air flow and protects the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Spacing maize seeds properly gives each plant enough space for roots to spread, preventing them from competing with each other for water and sunlight.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ hulu la he yɛ amɛteŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough richness for growing tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tomato nɔ?

english: Rich soil is usually dark, holds moisture without staying soggy, and breaks apart easily, providing the ideal condition for strong root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ feɔ duŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ehiɛɛɛ mli. ni efiteɔ oya No hewɔ lɛ, eji shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi ni wa ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm every single day or wait a few days?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu daa gbi loo ooomɛ gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Watering deeply every few days is better than light daily watering because it encourages plant roots to grow deep into the soil where moisture stays longer.
ga: Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa Gbii fioo lɛ hi fe nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo daa gbi ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How many main branches should I leave on my pepper plants for the best yield?
ga: Niji titrii enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Leaving around 5 to 8 main branches allows the pepper plant to balance its energy between healthy leaf growth and producing large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji titrii 5 kɛyashi 8 ni etseɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, pepper tso lɛ baanyɛ aha ehewalɛ lɛ afee ekome yɛ baai ni wa ni edaa kɛ aduawai wuji ni wa ni ewoɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees take longer to produce fruits compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains delay fruiting if the soil lacks sufficient organic matter or if weeds around the base steal water during the early stages of growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛji jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Cones ju nu yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the cocoa seedlings with shade and moisture until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnaa hulu la fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough room and food to produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.
