english: Why is it important to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei kakadaji awo mli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to capture sunlight and turn it into food, which gets stored underground to form big tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, spreading the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight and preventing them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulb agboi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Gbalamɔ baai lɛ amli koni onine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. ni otsi enaa koni ekafite.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, leaving the plant unable to make green leaves and slowing its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo baai eŋɔli ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why is planting beans or groundnuts in my field good for the crop I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes, which means they take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. After you harvest them, they leave behind naturally fertile soil that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ Amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season to settle before sowing my corn seeds in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Corn seeds need steady moisture to sprout and build deep roots. Sowing seeds in dry soil or after just one early rain can cause the seeds to dry out and die before they can grow into strong plants.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots underground are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the top stem stops growing rapidly, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ oya. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that grow faster than crop roots, stealing the soil nutrients and water meant for your crops. Even with abundant rain, weeds rob your plants of the food they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe tsei shishifãi. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ ni oooju lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi jwɛi hu juɔ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and irregular watering. The curling damages the leaves, preventing the plant from making enough food to grow good fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli Curling baafite baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside of my maize stalks and causing the leaves at the top to wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ni amɛhaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: These worms are young pests, such as stem borers or fall armyworms, that hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. They tunnel into the center of the stalk to feed on the soft tissue, blocking water and food from reaching the top of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms, ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛ buɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋ koni amɛ ye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii ayashɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa plants the cool shade and moist soil they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni cacao ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa efeee lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather or high heat, or when there are no tiny insects like midgets around to pollinate the flowers. Keeping shade trees on your farm helps keep the air humid so insects can pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa ha tso lɛ miihao. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ midges bɛ he fɛɛ he koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kooloi bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and bushy. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I get smaller maize harvests when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil water and food, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Proper spacing gives every plant enough light, water, and soil room to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, nu kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing plenty of tall stems and broad leaves but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into top leaves instead of underground tubers when the soil has too much leaf-building nutrients or when the earth is packed too hard. Loose soil allows the plant to send its food downward to swell the tubers.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii babaoo ni feɔ baai. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Loamy shikpɔŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni eha bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines start turning brown and dying off when it gets close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miije shishi amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi be mli ni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry up at the end of the season because the plant has finished its main growing cycle. It transfers all the energy left in the leaves down into the ground to complete the growth of the heavy yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee be mli ni tsei lɛ egbe amɛdalɛ be titri lɛ naa lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they feel stressed by hot afternoon heat or lack of soil water. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy so it can survive until water and weather conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nu kɛ shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from baking moisture out of the soil. It keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and keeps rain from splashing soil diseases onto tomato leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akashã ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tomato baai lɛ anɔ

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant cowpeas on the same land where I planted maize before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miidu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmãa nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of crops that take natural food from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea roots rot in the ground, they enrich the soil with free nitrogen fertilizer that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni heɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aná nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after putting them in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the dirt where air cannot reach them, if the soil is too packed down, or if the seeds were saved for too long and lost their life inside.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ mli.

english: If I already put good fertilizer on my farm, why do I still need to spray insecticides?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: Fertilizer only feeds the plant to help it grow big and strong, but it cannot stop insects from eating the leaves and fruits. Insecticides are needed to kill or drive away pests so your fertilized crops can actually survive and yield food.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii pɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ená hewalɛ. Shi enyɛŋ etsĩ kooloi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye baai kɛ aduawai lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ahe miihia koni akɛgbe loo ashwie kooloi bibii koni onibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Will applying more fertilizer help my crops fight off insect attacks on its own?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwu amɛshi kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer does not kill or repel bugs. In fact, lush and fast-growing plants fed with fertilizer can attract even more insects, making proper pest spraying essential to protect them.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii egbeee kooloi loo eshwieee amɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, Lush, tsei ni daa oya ni nine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi bibii babaoo kɛba amɛŋɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa waa koni akɛbu amɛhe.

english: Can insects ruin my crop harvest even if my plants look strong and full of potential right now?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ nyɛmɔi amrɔ nɛɛ moŋ?

english: Yes, even very healthy crops with high yield potential can be completely destroyed in a short time if insect pests attack the leaves, flowers, or young pods before you harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akpata ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo lɛ po ahiɛ kwraa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua baai, fɔfɔii, loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani okpa

english: What causes a farm with good soil and healthy plants to still give a poor harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔji ni shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lolo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: A farm can look promising early on, but if you ignore pest control, insects will destroy the crop before harvest time. Feeding the plant is not enough if you do not protect it from pests.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔ lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni shiwoo yɔɔ mli mra. Shi kɛji oku ohiɛ ofɔ̃ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani kpamɔ be baashɛ. Tsei ni oooha amɛ niyenii lɛ faaa kɛji obuuu amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are bugs able to cause so much trouble on a farm that has very fertile soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ amɛkɛ naagbai babaoo aba ŋmɔji ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii waa yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects feed directly on the plant's leaves, stems, and fruits. Even if the soil gives the plant nutrients, bugs destroy the parts of the plant needed to make food and grow fruit.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ tsei ahe baai, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛyibii tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ haa tsei niyenii moŋ Shi kooloi bibii fiteɔ fãi komɛi. Yɛ tsei ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ he.

english: How do I know if my crop needs insecticide spraying or if it needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ loo ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: You use fertilizer when plants grow slowly or have yellow leaves due to poor soil. You use insecticides when you see actual bugs, holes chewed into leaves, or damaged fruits on your farm.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii kɛ́ tso lɛ miida blɛoo loo eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi tsuɔ nii kɛ́ ona kooloi diɛŋtsɛ. Akɛ buji shwieɔ baai anɔ. loo aduawai ni efite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: What does it mean to use a quality insecticide spray on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: A quality spray means using an approved, effective chemical designed specifically for the pests on your crop, mixed in the correct proportion with clean water so it kills pests without damaging the plant.
ga: Quality spray tsɔɔ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Afee amɛ pɔtɛɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu ni mli tse ni akɛfutuɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ. Koni egbe kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: Is spraying my crops with insecticides safe for the plants themselves?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, as long as you follow the correct instructions for mixing and application. Using the right spray at the right time protects the plant from damage without harming its growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii kɛ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa wo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he ni efiteee edalɛ.

english: Should I wait until bugs destroy my crop leaves before I start spraying insecticides?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni kooloi bibii efite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ dani mabɔi tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: No, you should inspect your farm regularly and spray at the first sign of pest activity. Waiting too long allows bugs to multiply and cause damage that cannot be fixed.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ kɛji ona klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eba. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli ni ekɛ nibii ni anyɛɛɛ asaa aba.

english: I just took over an existing farm; what is the most important step to safeguard the crop's yield?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni miŋɔ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ. Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afee koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Along with basic weeding and feeding the soil, you must immediately inspect the crops for pests and protect them with quality insecticide spraying so pests do not ruin the farm's potential.
ga: Kɛfata shishijee jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he lɛ, Esa akɛ Okwɛ otsei lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii yɛ mli ni obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni oookɛshwie amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite nyɛmɔi ni ŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips inward, it usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and helps them grow strong; adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ mligbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my farm if I plant cowpea in the same bed where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikpaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, while cowpea leaves and roots actually fix nitrogen back into the soil. Rotating cowpea after maize acts like a natural soil restorer, making the land richer for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni tsina ŋmei lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the plant from growing big roots, so affected plants should be removed, and you should plant mosaic-resistant cassava stems next season.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei akaná shishifãi wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni esa akɛ odu yucca tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ mosaic lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa pods on my trees turn dark brown or black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches and removing infected pods quickly allows air and sunlight to keep the remaining pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating holes inside the top leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying recommended neem extracts or target treatments early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and twisting upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with neem oil solution or soapy water helps clear these pests so normal leaf growth can return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni etsɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. Koni ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when wind blows after they produce a fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa beni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when bearing fruit. Removing excess suckers around the main stem and supporting the fruiting plant with a bamboo or wooden prop pole prevents the stem from snapping under heavy weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ fiɔ tsei lɛ ashishi wulu kɛ aduawai lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ shishi koni ekafo yɛ muji ni tsii shishi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the air temperature gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry soil conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and using dry leaves as mulch keeps the roots cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ baai ni egbi ni oooha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and dying early before the tubers are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miije shishi amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry prematurely when fungal leaf spot diseases attack them or when they lie directly on hot soil. Staking yam vines onto wooden poles keeps the foliage elevated, dry, and healthy enough to keep feeding the growing underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ fungal leaf spot lɛ tutua amɛ loo kɛ́ amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Sweet potato wain tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look wilted in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Vegetable leaves wilt temporarily in strong midday sun because water evaporates from their leaves faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. As long as they bounce back in the cool evening, it is normal, but putting dry grass around the plant base keeps soil moisture from escaping.
ga: Aduawai ahe baai baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, no lɛ ehi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ akaje mli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or diseases such as Cassava Mosaic Disease. Planting disease-resistant varieties released by agricultural research centers and using proper control methods stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo helai tamɔ yucca mosaic lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yucca baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ odu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Agricultural Research Centers lɛ jie lɛ kpo lɛ, ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ hela lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to use the same crop medicine on all my different crops when insects attack?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tso tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kooloi bibii batutua mi?

english: No, different farm chemicals are specially made for specific crops and specific pests. Using the wrong medicine can burn your crop leaves, fail to destroy the pest, or leave harmful chemical residues on food crops.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso baai lɛ ashã. nyɛŋ akpata kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahiɛ loo eshi tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa trees are like young human babies—they burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting food crops like plantains next to them creates living shade that protects the cocoa and keeps the soil moist until the trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii, tamɔ abifabii, shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ he waa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin stalks and very small, poor-quality cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: If I apply extra chemical fertilizer to my farm, will it make my crops grow faster and produce more?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Too much fertilizer can burn plant roots and damage your soil quality over time. Crops only need specific amounts at key growth stages, so following correct measurement guidelines protects your crop investment.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ susumɔ he lɛ ni ooonyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni obu onibii ni okɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn purple when there is too much water standing on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ purple kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents roots from getting air, which stops the plant from absorbing essential nutrients like phosphorus. Good farm drainage helps roots breathe so the plants stay green and grow well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ. Tsei lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before they produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from intense heat, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Maintaining steady watering and feeding the soil helps the plant keep its flowers so they turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Koni ebatsɔ chili ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants that quickly drink up rain and soil nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early removes this competition so your crops get all the sunlight and food they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hulu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety recommended by research officers will do well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei ni minitaomɔ nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Research institutes breed improved seeds to withstand drought, resist local pests, or yield more harvest. Testing a small plot first allows you to see how well the new seed grows in your specific soil and climate.
ga: Dumɔwui afɔmɔ he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhe kɛha hɔmɔ shitee-kɛ-woo Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ehaa babaoo Small plot test Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa bɔ ni dumɔwui heei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of insects even after I dry it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii beni mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Sun-drying may not remove all hidden moisture inside the grain, which attracts insects like weevils during storage. Storing fully dried grain in airtight bags protects your harvest from insects and damp air.
ga: Ekolɛ hulu ni egbiɔ lɛ ejieee ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baagbala kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ he.

english: Why is my farm producing far fewer bags of crop now than it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ faaa kwraa fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Soil loses its food nutrients every time crops harvest from it without getting manure or fertilizer put back. Just like a human gets weak without food, exhausted soil cannot feed plants to give big yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa tso ko ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ akɛbaa. Taakɛ bɔ ni adesai gbɔjɔɔ kɛ niyenii bɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ miifite ni ehe miihia yelikɛbuamɔ?

english: Tired soil turns light in color, becomes hard like rock when dry, washes away easily during rain, and grows weak crops with thin stems and pale yellow leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ewa tamɔ tɛ kɛji egbi Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaafɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni odu tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does burning the bush on my land before planting cause any harm to my farm?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ awui?

english: Yes, burning destroys the rotten leaves and natural plant food in the ground that hold moisture. While burning clears the land fast, it leaves the soil hot, dried out, and poor after a few seasons.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shãa fiteɔ baai ni egboi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ zugba a mi dɔɔ, e gbiɔ, nɛ e fiɛɔ ngɛ be bɔɔ komɛ a se.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's way of protecting itself from losing water in hot sun. If the soil has water, the leaves open back up, but if leaf-rolling happens every day, the plant is thirsty and growth will stop.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi daa gbi lɛ, kumai baaye tso lɛ ni edalɛ baakpa.

english: Why are my crops producing flowers, but the flowers fall off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun, lack of water, insect attacks, or lack of soil food. The plant drops its flowers because it lacks the energy to grow them into full fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, nu bɛ, koolooi tutuaa lɛ, loo niyenii bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara kwraa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my old crop trees yield less fruit compared to when I first planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso momo lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ akɛto be mli ni midu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: As trees get very old, their wood hardens, their roots struggle to pull water, and they build up diseases. Trimming old branches or replacing old trees with fresh seedlings brings strong yields back.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ Etso lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni ekɛ helai baa Tsei niji momoi ni afolɔ loo tsei momoi ni akɛ dumɔwui heei baatsake lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni mli wa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving crops proper space allows each plant to grow big and bear many healthy fruits.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it bad to plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Yes, planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up. Switching crops each season keeps soil balanced and pests away.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa jɛmɛ.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii aba shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the food and fertilizer from the soil before your crop roots can reach it. Even with rain, weeds choke your plants and reduce your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ haa otsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow while the veins stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni fãji lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is usually a sign of plant hunger, showing the soil is missing specific plant foods like iron or nitrogen, or that the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji tso hɔmɔ he okadi. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii komɛi tamɔ dade loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves, or that heavy rainfall has washed the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaa eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans on their farmland before planting their main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii titri lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans capture food from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them first naturally fertilizes and enriches the ground for whatever main crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii aba ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ aba jɛmɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wuji fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why should I avoid planting my cocoa seedlings in full, open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kookoo dumɔwui adumɔ he yɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and can easily get scorched by intense heat. They need shade trees over them to trap moisture and protect their leaves until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can spread out and capture maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the power to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a small bunch even when I plant it in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ po.

english: If you allow too many sucker shoots to grow around the base of one main plantain stem, they steal the food and water from the mother plant, leaving less energy to make a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, Plantain shishitoo titri kome Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi ni akɛfee kuu agbo.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing on the main stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Cutting off unwanted shoots, known as chupons, keeps the tree from wasting food on useless stems and directs all its energy into producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo, ni atsɛɔ lɛ chupons lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa efite niyenii yɛ tso lɛ yibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: The first rain after a long dry season is often followed by a hot, dry period that dries out the topsoil, which can scorch and kill newly germinated seeds before the main rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, be ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why are tiny insects causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects suck the liquid sap out of the soft young leaves, causing the leaves to dry up, curl, and stop the plant from bearing healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ, ni no haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛkpãa shi ni amɛhaaa tso lɛ awo pepper yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil or their roots are choking from waterlogged ground. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green so they can make food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he loo amɛshishifãi lɛ miihoso kɛmiijɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni enyɛ ehoo nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller cassava roots when I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava on the same field every year drains specific soil nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and gives the land a chance to recover.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee ehee ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat spikes, lack of water, or receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer during flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and reducing nitrogen application once flowers appear helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔtsemɔ kɛji fɔfɔii je kpo lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai shwereɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and crooked even when the vines on top grow bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato bulbs lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand properly. If the soil underneath is hard or stony, the tubers cannot swell and will bend, so making tall, soft mounds or ridges gives them space to grow large and straight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ Yitso lɛ efuuu ni efoŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ooofee lɛ baaha oná hegbɛ ni oda ni oda shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong sunlight and dry winds. Leaving large trees or planting plantains beside them creates a canopy of shade and keeps the air humid, protecting the tender seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛ baa da bɔ ni sa ni amɛ damɔ dɔlɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens if I plant three or four maize seeds together in one small hole instead of spreading them out?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo ko mli? Bu kome moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa

english: When multiple seeds grow out of a single hole, the plants compete closely for water, sunlight, and food. This struggle leaves all of them with thin, weak stems and tiny cobs instead of strong stems with full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo jɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii. Ta nɛɛ haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛhiɛɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ tso ni mli wa ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if the spotty marks on my leaves are caused by insects or by a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe helai ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibaai lɛ anɔ lɛ ba?

english: Insects usually leave physical bite holes, chewed edges, or sticky liquid on leaves, and you can often see them or their webs underneath. Disease symptoms usually look like spreading brown spots, powdery patches, or soft rotten areas without any visible chewing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ, ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ, loo nu ni shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ ona amɛ loo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ he okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛ eshwa, ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ blɛoo ni anaaa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and twisting like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by the plant protecting itself during extreme sun heat. Checking under the leaves for tiny white flies will tell you if an insect treatment is needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni buɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i bibii yɛŋ ni anaa Baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ bo kɛji ehe miihia ni akpata kooloi bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stunt so quickly compared to when the crops are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miigbɔjɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, making them too weak to compete with fast-growing weeds for soil moisture and sunlight. Once crops grow tall and cast shade on the ground, they can naturally suppress weeds better.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo lɛ Amɛhe esa waa yɛ jwɛi ni amɛtsiɔ naa lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does putting dry bush grass around the base of my crops help them stay healthy in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks hot sunlight from drying out the earth. It keeps the root area cool and traps moisture in the soil far longer after watering or rainfall.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu loo nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that create a living canopy, offering shade and keeping the soil cool and moist while cocoa roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant plantain and cocoa trees so they do not choke each other?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain kɛ cocoa tsei kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni mitsi mihe kɛjɛ he?

english: Planting plantains about 3 meters apart gives cocoa seedlings enough shade without forcing them to fight too hard for light and soil nutrients as both crops grow.
ga: Kɛ́ adu plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 lɛ, ebaaha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná hulutsoo ni sa. Enɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛwuu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la babaoo he beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Will planting plantain with cocoa delay when my cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Ani plantains ni akɛ cocoa duɔ lɛ baahe sɛɛ kɛji mi-cocoa tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ pɛ?

english: No, plantains actually help young cocoa grow healthier by protecting them from sun stress, while providing you with food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Dabi, plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anáa hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhebuu kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Is it good to cut down old plantain leaves and stalks and leave them on the ground near my cocoa?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ plantain baai kɛ eshishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ amli? Ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi koko lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cut plantain leaves and stalks around cocoa plants acts as mulch. This covers the ground to hold moisture, slow down weed growth, and turn into natural manure as it rots.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain baai kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afolɔ Kɛ́ ajie kookoo tsei lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulch koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo

english: What visual signs should I look for to know if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii ni anaa esa akɛ matao koni mana kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo?

english: If cocoa leaves start turning yellow, drying up at the tips, or looking burnt, the plants are getting too much direct sun and need shade plants like plantain to cover them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ egbi loo eshã. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, he miihia amɛ koni amɛkɛha amɛhe nɔ

english: What should I do if I see plantain trees falling over near my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina dumɔwui ni miigbee mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Fallen plantains can damage young cocoa or attract pests. You should prop up heavy fruiting stems and chop fallen stalks into mulch away from the bases of the cocoa stems.
ga: Plantains ni egbee shi lɛ baanyɛ afite kookoo bibii loo egbala tsɛŋemɔ helai. Esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii awo mli. Ni ofolɔ tsei ni egbee shi lɛ amli owo mulch mli kɛjɛ kookoo shishitoo lɛ he.

english: How long do I need to keep plantain trees providing shade for my cocoa farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ plantains lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo?

english: Plantains are usually kept for 3 to 5 years until the cocoa trees grow tall and broad enough to form their own leaf canopy to shade the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ plantains toɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛlɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ baai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe hulutsoo.

english: Should I clear all the big wild trees from my land before planting cocoa and plantain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo kɛ plantains?

english: No, leaving some selected tall forest trees alongside your plantains helps protect the farm from harsh winds and extreme dry-season sun.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi koo ni ahala lɛ mli tsei kakadaji lɛ yɛ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu ni naa wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How often should I clear the weeds around my young plantain and cocoa suckers?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Clearing weeds every 2 to 3 months ensures that aggressive weeds do not steal water, fertilizer, and light from your young crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ akaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the best time of the year to plant plantain suckers for my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: It is best to plant plantain suckers right at the start of the major rainy season so they catch enough water to establish leaves before the dry period begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ aba dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why does the weed killer I bought not work when I just pour it on the weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mihe lɛ tsuuu nii be mli ni mikɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When you pour weed killer directly, most of it drips off or runs straight into the dirt without staying on the leaves long enough to penetrate. Spraying creates a fine mist of droplets that stick to the leaves so the weed can fully absorb the chemical.
ga: Kɛji okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Mɛi babaoo baafo loo amɛbaajo foi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbote mli. Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa afua kpakpa ko baa ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni jwɛi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ tsofai lɛ kwraa.

english: Is it really necessary to use a knapsack sprayer, or can I just pour the chemical from a bottle onto my weeds?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ akɛ akɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ atsu nii? Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ tɔ mli lɛ afɔse jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Pouring wastes a lot of chemical because large streams of liquid bounce off the leaves and soak uselessly into the soil. A knapsack sprayer breaks the liquid into tiny drops that coat the plant evenly, ensuring the plant actually absorbs the chemical.
ga: Muji ni ashwieɔ lɛ biɔ tsofai babaoo ejaakɛ nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he. Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baagi lɛ nɔ lɛ gbálaa nu lɛ mli bibii bibii. Koni akɛwo tsei lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ koni tsei lɛ aŋɔ tsofai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How do I know if I am applying my farm chemicals correctly so I do not waste my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, mifiteee shika?

english: Proper application means using a sprayer to produce an even mist over the leaves without over-soaking them. If you see liquid heavily dripping off the leaves onto the bare ground, you are applying too much and the plant is failing to absorb the excess.
ga: Ni akɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ nii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee afua kome pɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni akɛwooo mli fe nine. Kɛji ona nu ni miiho waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ babaoo miitsu nii ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: If I pour weedicide on sandy ground where weeds are growing, will it still kill them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie ŋã ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani ebaagbe amɛ lolo?

english: Sandy soil lets liquid drain away into the ground very quickly before the chemical can soak into the weed roots. You must spray the chemical directly onto the green leaves of the weeds rather than pouring it onto the sand.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsofai baanyɛ abote jwɛi shishifãi amli. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ jwɛi lɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofɔse yɛ ŋã lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why does my weed chemical work well on my dark soil farm but fails on my sandy farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? shi eyeee omanye yɛ mi ŋã ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Sandy soil does not hold onto liquids well, letting chemicals wash straight down past the roots before they can penetrate. Darker soil holds moisture near the surface longer, giving the weeds and soil enough time to absorb the chemical properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani amɛboteɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ kɛ sũ lɛ naa be koni amɛŋɔ tsofai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does chemical poured directly onto the ground stay in the soil to stop future weeds from growing?
ga: Ani tsofai ni afɔseɔ ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baakã he ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ wɔsɛɛ?

english: No, pouring chemical onto bare soil allows most of it to wash deep into the earth where it cannot reach weed seeds or roots. Most farm chemicals need to be sprayed directly on plant leaves to be absorbed effectively.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛteŋ babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni jwɛi dumɔwui loo shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo afɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ eshɛre mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the weeds on my farm still alive even after I put chemical on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai efata he lɛ?

english: Weeds have a tough outer layer on their leaves that prevents full chemical penetration if the liquid is applied in large drops or at the wrong time of day. Fine spraying helps the chemical stay on the leaf long enough to break through and destroy the weed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni haaa tsofai lɛ abote mli kwraa kɛji akɛ akɛ nu lɛ wo mli babaoo loo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ebote jwɛi lɛ amli ni efite.

english: How can I make sure the chemical reaches all the small weeds hiding under big crop leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofai lɛ baashɛ jwɛi bibii lɛ ahe? Akɛtee tsei agboi ashishi

english: Chemicals only penetrate what they touch directly because they cannot pass through top leaves to reach lower ones. You need to adjust your spraying technique and angle so the fine mist reaches under the main leaves to coat the smaller weeds.
ga: Tsofai baanyɛ abote nibii ni amɛkɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ pɛ amli. Ejaakɛ enyɛŋ ebote baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli ni eshɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ otsake gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ okɛ tsofa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ he ni okɛshwieɔ shi lɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ ashɛ baai titrii lɛ ashishi koni ekɛha jwɛi bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: If I pour extra chemical on tough weeds, will it kill them faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai wo jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ Ani ebaagbe amɛ oya?

english: Pouring extra liquid does not mean the plant absorbs more; the excess simply runs off into the ground and wastes your money. Spraying the recommended amount evenly gives the best coverage so the maximum amount of chemical penetrates the leaves.
ga: Nu babaoo ni oooshwie lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baaŋɔ nu babaoo. Nɔ ni fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ ni efiteɔ oshika. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ shwie nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba. koni tsofai lɛ anyɛ abote baai lɛ amli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ

english: What happens to the chemical if rain falls right after I apply it to my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa tsofai lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the leaves and into the soil before the plant has time to absorb it. For the chemical to penetrate and work properly, it usually needs a few dry, sunny hours on the plant leaves after application.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai kɛjɛɔ baai amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ tsofai lɛ. koni tsofai lɛ abote mli ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ, be ni akɛgbiɔ nii kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa yɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my corn immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant immediately, the seeds may sprout but then dry up and die in the hot soil before the regular rains actually begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow strong and green. It can also happen when heavy rain washes the nutrients deep out of the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Can I put wood ash from my kitchen fire on my pepper farm, and will it help?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ ni jɛ shĩa la mli lɛ awo mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni ani ebaaye ebua?

english: Yes, wood ash contains natural potassium and calcium which help crops like peppers grow strong stems and produce good fruit. It also helps sweeten soil that has become too sour.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ mli potassium kɛ calcium yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ chili ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by a fungal sickness called black pod disease. High humidity, heavy rain, and too much shade allow water to sit on the pods, which lets the fungus grow and spread quickly.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baanyɛ aha nu akpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: What makes my pepper leaves curl up into tight little balls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu bibii? ni mli wa ni ekpaa dalɛ

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, or by a virus transmitted by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot daytime temperatures, lack of regular watering, or soil that lacks essential nutrients during flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa. Nu ni akɛhaa daa loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ bɛ mli

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the roots. Staking lifts the vines off the ground where it is damp and crowded, helping the leaves get sun and preventing ground diseases so the tubers grow larger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha bulb lɛ afee wuji.

english: Does leaving weeds between my crops really harm them, or can I just leave them until harvest?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ loo manyɛ mashi amɛ yɛ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ be?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow. If you leave weeds in your farm, your crops will get weak and your final harvest will be very small.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛji oshi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni naagbee ŋmaa lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully grown and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, the main stems turn woody and thick, and the soil right around the base of the plant starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ bafeɔ tso ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Cassava plants curl or droop their leaves during peak heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is a natural survival trick that helps the plant save moisture until the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out suddenly, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Young cocoa trees have thin roots and sensitive leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the sun, the heat scorches the leaves and drains moisture from the seedling.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la naa lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaajie nu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant roots decay, they leave behind free natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛye tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very thin with tiny cobs even though the plants are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa bibii ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ

english: Tall, thin maize stalks usually mean the crop lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen during its early growth stage. The plant stretches upward searching for light, but without enough food in the soil, it cannot produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Shi kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enyɛŋ ewo cob yɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also prevents fungal diseases from rotting the foliage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra young suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, sunlight, and soil water. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the mother plant has enough food to grow large, heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does planting my seeds too close together reduce the size of my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Overcrowded plants grow weak and small, yielding far less than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii. Enɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and dark dirt inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day, chewing the fresh leaves and leaving behind dark waste pellets.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ. Okɛ baai heei lɛ atsu nii ni oshi jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Weeds have faster-growing root systems that steal the water and fertilizer meant for your crops. If you do not clear weeds early, they consume most of the soil nutrients before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Nakai jwɛi lɛ baafite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ.

english: Officer, why is it a good idea to plant different vegetables like peppers and cabbages together on the same plot?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kaabii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting different crops together, known as intercropping, helps naturally confuse pests, improves soil health, and ensures you still have food to harvest even if one crop suffers from bad weather or disease.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome Ale lɛ hu akɛ intercropping. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai futuɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oyɛ niyenii ni obaakpa lolo. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela ko ye ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ po.

english: How close together should I plant different crops so they do not fight for nutrients?
ga: Te esa akɛ mabɛŋkɛ mihe tɛŋŋ koni madu tsei srɔtoi koni amɛkaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: Every crop needs its own space to spread roots and leaves. Proper spacing ensures taller plants do not block light from smaller ones and prevents roots from competing for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiii tsei bibii lɛ akana naa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ he akaŋ

english: What are screen plants, and how do they help protect my main crops?
ga: Mɛni ji filta tso? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe?

english: Screen plants are taller or dense plants grown around or between main crops to act as natural windbreaks, provide partial shade, and form a green wall that stops insect pests from easily finding your delicate vegetables.
ga: Filter tsei ji tsei ni kɛlɛ loo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei wuji ahe loo amɛteŋ koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ. Ha hulutsoo fioo ni ofee gbogbo eŋɔli ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa o-vegetables ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do delicate crops like cauliflower need shade from the strong afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kɔliflawa he hiaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables like cauliflower are sensitive to high heat. Direct midday sun can burn their leaves and prevent them from forming tight, healthy heads, so giving them light shade keeps the soil cool and preserves moisture.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ kɔliflawa nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha yitso lɛ akadara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe awa. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Can exotic vegetables like cabbage and cauliflower grow well in warm areas like Kumasi?
ga: Ani aduawai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi tamɔ kaabe kɛ kɔliflower baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Kumasi?

english: Yes, they can grow well in warm regions if you plant heat-tolerant varieties, enrich the soil with plenty of organic manure, and ensure they get regular water during hot dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ kɛji odu henɔi ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni amɛná nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but refusing to form solid heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ehaaa mi yitso ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form heads when soil temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil which forces the plant to grow big leaves instead of tight heads.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do my chili pepper flowers keep falling off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Chili pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a shortage of key nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Do chili pepper plants need full sunlight all day to yield well?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be fɛɛ he miihia chili tsei lɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Chili peppers love sun to make fruit, but extreme afternoon heat can stress them. Planting them near taller plants that cast light shade during the hottest part of the day can actually protect the flowers and boost your yield.
ga: Peppers sumɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ aduawai. Shi latsaa ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhao. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ ni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why can water plants like lotus survive in flooded soil while my pepper plants rot in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu mli tsei tamɔ nu mli tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be mli ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifite yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water plants have hollow spaces in their stems and roots that send oxygen down underwater, whereas dryland crops like peppers need air in the soil and will suffocate and rot if their roots stay underwater for too long.
ga: Nu mli tsei yɛ hei ni bu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yaa nu shishi. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ, tamɔ chili lɛ, he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ebaagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough to grow leafy vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai ni yɔɔ baai?

english: Good soil for leafy vegetables should be rich in dark organic matter, drain excess water easily without becoming soggy mud, and stay soft so delicate crop roots can spread quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ afee nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ waa yɔɔ mli babaoo. Ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ efeee. ni ehiɔ shi blɛoo bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do imported seeds from neighboring countries like Nigeria grow differently than our local Ghanaian seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ tamɔ Nigeria lɛ amli lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe wɔ Ghana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds adapt over time to the specific weather, rain patterns, and soil of where they are grown. Seeds brought from other places may react differently to Ghana's conditions, requiring different care or timing to grow well.
ga: Dumɔwui baatsake amɛhe yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔshiimɔi, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ hei krokomɛi kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ Ghana shihilɛi ahe. Amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ loo be srɔtoi bɔni afee ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will foreign seeds from outside West Africa produce good yields in Ghanaian soil?
ga: Ani maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Foreign seeds can produce high yields, but they are often bred for cooler or different climates. In Ghana, they might need extra shade, more frequent watering, or special fertilizers to produce as well as they do overseas.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo. Shi bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ amɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛbi hulutsoo babaoo. Nu shii abɔ Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko afata nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tamɔ yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ.

english: Does using local Ghanaian seeds guarantee that my crops will survive bad weather better?
ga: Ani Ghana maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Local seeds usually have a natural resistance to local heat and irregular rains because they have adapted to the environment over many generations, making them generally sturdier against local climate stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋ dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ akutsoŋ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ yinɔi babaoo mli. Enɛ haa amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from a harvest of foreign crop varieties to plant again next season?
