ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Many foreign or hybrid seeds lose their strength, productivity, and pest resistance after the first generation. Replanting saved foreign seeds often leads to weaker plants and lower harvests in the second year.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui loo hybrid dumɔwui babaoo fiteɔ hewalɛ, yibiiwoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties require so much more labor and effort to cultivate than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo dani adu fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: High-yielding or non-local crop varieties often lack natural defenses against local pests and weeds. They need more frequent spraying, extra weeding, and careful soil preparation compared to traditional crops that grow easily on their own.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni jeee maŋbii lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ maŋbii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi ahe. Amɛbiɔ ni afɔ amɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ akɛto blema tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do certain crops get attacked by pests more easily than other varieties on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Some imported or new seed varieties have sweeter tissue or thinner leaves that local insects love to eat, while local varieties have often developed natural scents, tough skins, or bitter tastes that deter local bugs.
ga: Henɔi komɛi ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ loo ehee lɛ yɛ fãji ni ŋɔɔ loo baai ni mli tseee ni maŋ lɛ mli kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛye. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ, amɛhewolo ni wa, loo ŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ jɛmɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why is soil preparation harder for some seed varieties compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa kɛha dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi lɛ wa waa kɛ akɛto ekrokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Crops with small or delicate seeds need very finely tilled soil so their fragile young roots can penetrate the ground. Hardier, larger seeds can push through rougher, unplowed soil easily.
ga: Tsei ni dumɔwui bibii loo amɛhe waaa lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ anyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni wa, ni dara lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do some seed types fail to sprout even when I plant them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ po lɛ?

english: Different seeds need specific levels of moisture and soil temperature to break their resting state. Sensitive or foreign seeds will remain dormant or rot if the soil conditions aren't exactly right for them.
ga: Dumɔwui henɔ fɛɛ henɔ biɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa koni ekɛfo dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ loo maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. loo egbo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ esaaa nakai dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why do some crop varieties take much longer to mature than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Ani adu nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Every seed variety has its own natural growing clock. Early-maturing varieties focus on producing fruit quickly, while late-maturing varieties spend more time building strong roots and leaves before fruiting.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni baa oya lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does where my seeds come from affect how much fertilizer I need to apply?
ga: Te he ni midumɔwui lɛ jɛɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: High-performing foreign seeds are bred to consume large amounts of nutrients to produce heavy crops. If you don't give them extra fertilizer, they may perform worse than local seeds that are used to growing in poorer soils.
ga: Atsɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ koni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi haaa Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni tsutsu lɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient that helps plants grow strong and leafy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps restore their green color and growth energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛnáa baai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Plants lose water through their leaves in intense sun. Cassava plants curl their leaves to save moisture and protect themselves from burning, and they will usually bounce back once the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Tsei laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: When temperatures get too high or the soil gets too dry, pepper plants drop their flowers to preserve their energy for survival instead of spending it on making fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite lɛ kɛfee aduawai

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and thin, producing smaller cobs overall.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli lɛ, cob fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal the sunlight, water, and food from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Should I trim off some of the bottom leaves from my tomato plants as they grow taller?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing the lower leaves helps the tomato plant send its energy upwards into growing big fruits rather than wasting energy keeping old, shaded leaves alive near the dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ehaa tomato tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ewo yibii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahi shi lɛ, amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kpaakpa.

english: Why does my farm produce fewer crops each year when I plant maize on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the earth every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil's strength, so rotating your plot with cowpea or beans helps naturally build the soil back up.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ he waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and crooked instead of long and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ agbo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Hard or stony soil blocks yam roots from expanding easily underground. Digging deep, loose mounds gives tubers the soft space they need to stretch out and grow big.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni akuɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it better to start my tomato seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them straight into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaaje tomato dumɔwui ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Young tomato seedlings are very delicate and easily killed by hot sun, heavy rains, or insects. A sheltered nursery keeps them safe until they are strong enough to survive in the big field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi gbeɔ amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ gbekɛbii yɛ lɛ baaha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do pests like armyworms attack young maize shoots much more than older maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ armyworms lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa bibii babaoo fe ŋmãa tsei momo lɛ?

english: Young maize plants are soft, tender, and easy for worms to chew through quickly, whereas older plants have tougher stems and leaves that make it harder for pests to eat.
ga: Abɛi bibii tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya. Shi tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa ni haa ewaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yeɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct, intense sunlight. Cutting down large shade trees exposes the cocoa to severe heat stress, causing the leaves to burn, turn yellow, and fall off to protect the trunk from losing water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni shãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ yitso lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he.

english: Planting maize too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stems and small cobs, resulting in a lower harvest overall.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my corn grow bigger next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die after harvest, they leave this natural fertilizer in the ground for the next corn crop to feed on.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the tender leaves hidden inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests, often called Fall Armyworms, hide inside the center funnel of the maize because the inner leaves are soft to eat and protect them from dry heat and predators. If left untreated, they can destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ emli baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ayeɔ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground when heavy rains stay on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the ground for days without draining, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi and bacteria to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of blossoms, but the flowers drop off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, so the plant drops the flower to conserve its remaining strength.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants roll up tightly like tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to defend against heat and save water. Rolling the leaves hides the pores on the leaf surface from the hot sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha nu akafite. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Yams need their leaves lifted high into the sunlight to produce the food needed for growing big underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia ni amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why should I cut away the small plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: When too many shoots, or suckers, grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main mother tree. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring you get large bunches of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha oná plantains babaoo.

english: Why do green weeds sprout back up on my land so fast right after I clear the ground with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi eŋɔlii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ ŋmei shwie jɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping deep under the soil for a long time. When you hoe the soil, you turn it over and bring hidden seeds up to the top where sunlight and rain awaken them to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji ootsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ Ebaabi ni otsɔ mli ni okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aba ŋwɛi. Hulu kɛ nugbɔ baaha eda oya.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to grow big roots. Giving plants proper space allows each one to feed well and produce larger, high-quality yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃. Tso he gbɛ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso yeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to cultivate a smaller plot and care for it well than to clear a huge farm I cannot maintain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mi akɛ matsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mafolɔ ŋmɔ agbo ko ni minyɛɛɛ makwɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need regular weeding, water, and plant food to thrive. A smaller, well-tended farm yields healthier, bigger crops that buyers prefer, whereas a neglected large farm often loses most of its harvest to weeds, pests, and poor growth.
ga: Tsei hia jwɛi, nu, kɛ tsei niyenii daa koni amɛshwere. Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni da ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ lɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji wuji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ jwɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ amɛshweremɔ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ.

english: If I put fertilizer on my maize plants, why do they still stay short and yellow when the farm is full of weeds?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ wo ŋmãa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo beni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal fertilizer and water meant for your crops. If weeds surround your maize, they drink up the plant food first, causing your crops to starve even if you applied fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni he wa waa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi bɔle o-ŋmã lɛ he Ebaanu tsei niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by lack of water, extreme heat, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve its own life when it senses it cannot feed the growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ nu ni bɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ kɛ́ amɛnu he akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with many leaves but give me very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and leaves instead of flowers. Crops need balanced plant food and full sunlight to switch from leaf growth to fruit production.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsei he miihia tso niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛtsake kɛjɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛya aduawai afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do market women reject my tomatoes even when I bring a large quantity to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei kpooɔ mi-tomato lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihɔ̃ɔ amɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Buyers look for firm, bright, and undamaged fruits rather than large quantities of weak or damaged produce. Crops that receive consistent water, shade, and pest protection grow uniform and attractive, making them sell much faster.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ aduawai ni wa, ni kpɛɔ ni efiteee. Mohu ɔ, mo hla yiblii babauu nɛ a he wami loo a puɛ. Tsei ni nu, hulutsoo, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe daa lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛbaafee fɛo. Ehaa jarayeli yaa oya

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get full of tiny holes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cabbage leaves attract pests like caterpillars and beetles, especially when the weather is warm and dry. These insects eat the leaves to get moisture and food, so inspecting leaves early and applying proper plant protection keeps the harvest clean and marketable.
ga: Kaabeji baai lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra. Ni tsei ahe ni abuɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmaa lɛ mli tseɔ ni anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when the soil stays waterlogged or when underground pests puncture the skin, allowing water and disease to enter. Soil needs good drainage and properly built mounds so excess water flows away from the roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bote hewolo lɛ mli. Ehaa nu kɛ helai boteɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nu kpakpa kɛ gɔŋ ni ama jogbaŋŋ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my garden egg plant wither and dry up suddenly while the rest of the farm looks green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho trukaa yɛ be mli ni tso ni eshwɛ lɛ miigbo lɛ? Ani ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli?

english: Sudden wilting is often caused by soil diseases or tiny worms damaging the roots hidden underground. When the roots are destroyed, the plant can no longer draw water from the soil, causing it to collapse quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. ni kɛ gbee shi oya baa

english: Why do my bean plants turn yellow and stop growing if rain stands on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like human beings. When heavy rain leaves standing water on your field, the soaked soil drowns the roots, preventing them from taking in air and nutrients, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do I need to provide wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa niji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need as much direct sunlight as possible to make energy, which it sends down to grow big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing disease and helping the plant capture light efficiently.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. ni abaamaje shi koni ayadu shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and form good cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni efeɔ ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that trapped plant food stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Tse niyenii ni akɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Does it matter which direction I push a cassava stem cutting into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ashɛre ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pushing the cassava stem upside down forces the young buds to grow downwards into the dirt before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy and results in weak growth and smaller tubers. The buds should always point upwards toward the sky.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ otsi ŋmei tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛtsɔ amɛhe. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraaa ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni bulb bibii hu baa. Esa akɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other underground for soil food and water, while their leaves block light from each other. Giving each seed enough space ensures every plant grows full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso atsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plant before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress or prolonged dry spells. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural defense to save water and energy so it can stay alive during tough weather.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kpe. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli

english: Why do the bottoms of my young green tomatoes turn black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This soft black rot happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or water while the fruit is forming. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding compost or lime prevents the fruit bottoms from spoiling.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ baa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ fataa he lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot faster during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by tiny fungal spores that thrive in cool, damp shade. Heavy rain splashes these spores from the wet ground onto low pods, and dense foliage traps moisture that helps the rot spread rapidly.
ga: Fungal spores bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No daa yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and fibrous if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu kɛ fiber kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava passes its full maturity, the plant begins consuming the starch stored in its roots to feed new stems and stay alive through dry seasons, leaving the roots woody, watery, and poor for eating.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔi ŋmei ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yeli koni amɛkɛye ŋmeii heei ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shi shishifãi lɛ afee tso, nu ni ayeee.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots break down, they release free fertilizer into the soil that nearby maize can feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ fã Ejieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ mli.

english: Why is my cowpea plant growing lots of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas have too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant focuses all its energy on making leaves instead of flowers and pods. Reducing heavy nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to set fruit.
ga: Beni cowpea yɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai feemɔ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔtsemɔ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam plants need sunlight to make food that builds big underground tubers. Staking lifts the vine leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight without rotting.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni efiteee.

english: Should I remove the small suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi. ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain lɛ shishigbɛ?

english: Yes, leave only one or two strong suckers and prune the rest. Too many suckers will steal water and nutrients from the main tree, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ofolɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why should I spread dry grass on the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry grass or dry leaves keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, holds moisture in the ground longer, and blocks weeds from growing around your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It usually happens when the soil dries out completely between waterings, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if tiny pollinating midges cannot reach them, if the tree suffers from drought stress, or if pests damage the flower stems before fruit can set.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen lɛ fee nakai. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he Kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Poor drainage allows soil fungi to infect and decay the roots underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Officer, why is it so difficult for me to harvest cassava when it starts raining heavily?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ makpã ŋmei kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain falls, the soil becomes wet, heavy, and muddy, which makes it physically harder to pull the cassava tubers out of the ground without breaking them or getting trapped in muddy farm tracks.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, eyɛ tsii ni efeɔ muji. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ewa akɛ abaajie ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akumɔɔɔ loo ekɛ ehe wooo ŋmɔ mli gbɛi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: What is the best weather condition for me to go and dig up my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛni ji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mafo mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to harvest cassava during clear, dry weather when the soil is slightly damp but not muddy, making digging easier and preventing bad weather from spoiling your harvested roots on the path back.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa ŋmei be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse ni edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo shi ebɛ muji. Ehaa shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni akpa yɛ gbɛ ni akuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does making fufu from cassava require so much more time and effort compared to other uses?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo koni akɛfee fufu kɛjɛ ŋmei mli kɛ akɛto gbɛi krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Fufu requires freshly harvested cassava roots that must be boiled and pounded heavily while hot, which demands immediate, strong physical labor on the same day you harvest.
ga: Fufu biɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa ehee, ni esa akɛ ahoo ni atswa waa be mli ni edɔ lɛ. Enɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni mli wa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi ni okpaa nii lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: If I am too busy to cook my fresh cassava right away, what else can I turn it into?
ga: Kɛji mibɛ deka tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mahoo ŋmei hee amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ani manyɛ matsɔ nɔ kroko?

english: You can process your cassava into gari by grating, fermenting, and roasting it, which allows you to preserve the crop for months without worrying about it spoiling quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei atsu nii ni okɛfee gari kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni oookɛwo mli, ni ooofee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmei ni oooshã lɛ nɔ, ni no haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo ni ohaooo akɛ ebaafite oya.

english: Why do many farmers in our community prefer turning their cassava into gari instead of selling it fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtsake ŋmei amɛfee curry lɛ? yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahɔ ehee

english: Gari processing transforms a quick-spoiling tuber into a dry, long-lasting food product that is easier to store, handle, and sell over time whenever you have free hours.
ga: Gari ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efite oya lɛ feɔ niyenii ni egbi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oookɛto, okwɛ nɔ, ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni oyɔɔ be fɛɛ be ni obaaná hejɔɔmɔ be.

english: Is cassava a good crop for me to harvest on days when I have very little free time?
ga: Ani ŋmei ji tso kpakpa ni esa akɛ makpa yɛ gbii ni mibɛ hejɔɔmɔ be fioo ko pɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: No, harvesting cassava is labor-intensive because it requires clearing, digging, uprooting, and carrying heavy tubers, so it is better done when you have a full, dedicated day.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ni akpaa lɛ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo ejaakɛ ebiɔ ni ajie, atsa, ajie, ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ aya he fɛɛ he ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ oyɛ gbi ni okɛ ohe fɛɛ baaha lɛ.

english: How does sudden rain affect my ability to transport harvested crops from the bush back to my house?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ baaku sɛɛ kɛba mishia lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain makes unpaved farm roads slippery and full of mud, making it extremely difficult to carry heavy loads like cassava baskets on foot or by vehicle from the farm.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ ha ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi ni atswako nɔ lɛ nɔ sũ kɛ muji. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaajie nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei tsɛnsii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nane loo tsɔne nɔ.

english: Does harvesting cassava right after heavy rain affect the quality of the root for pounding fufu?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ baaná shishifãi ni akɛfeɔ fufu lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, cassava harvested from waterlogged soil absorbs extra water, which can make the tubers soft or watery, giving your fufu a poor, soggy texture when pounded.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaŋɔ nu kroko ni fata he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ loo amɛfee nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, o-bulbs ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa, ni kɛ́ atswa amɛ lɛ, amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my fresh cassava roots spoil so quickly if I leave them sitting on the farm for a couple of days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi heei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji miha amɛtara ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots begin to deteriorate within 48 hours of being pulled from the ground because exposure to air and warmth causes rapid biological decay once separated from the plant stem.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ latsaa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: What can I do on my farm if rain catches me before I finish digging up my cassava field?
ga: Mɛni mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ dani migbe mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbee naa?

english: It is safest to stop digging and leave the remaining cassava unharvested in the ground, as living roots stay fresh inside the soil until the weather clears and you are ready to process them.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ji ni akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ ni ashi ŋmei ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akpaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee klalo ni ofee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is deep enough to plant oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ mu tsei?

english: You can check by digging a test pit or driving a sharp rod into the ground to see if you have at least 1.5 to 2 meters of loose soil before hitting solid rock. Oil palms need this depth so their thick root bases can establish properly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ kaa bu ko ni oootsi loo tso ni mli wa ni oootsɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni ona kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ, oyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 dani otswa tɛ ni wa. Mu tsei biɔ nɛkɛ mlibotemɔ nɛɛ bɔni afee ni anyɛ ama shishitoo ni mli tse jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant palm trees on land that has big rocks under the topsoil?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tɛŋ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ?

english: It is not recommended if solid rock sits close to the surface. Palm trees need clear soil for at least 1.5 to 2 meters deep so their roots can grow down far enough to anchor the heavy tree and reach hidden water.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa kɛji tɛi ni wa bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli kwɔ mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 he miihia palm tsei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛma tsei wuji anɔ ni amɛyashɛ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ he.

english: How far down under the ground do I need to check for rocks before planting long-term tree crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ akwɛ tɛsaa lɛ shishi kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ dani adu tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You should make sure there are no solid rock barriers for at least 1.5 to 2 meters down. This allows deep-rooted crops like palms to build a sturdy base underground.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni tɛi ni wa ni tsiɔ gbɛ kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 akafee nɔ ko, ni eha tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ato shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some of my heavy farm trees fall over when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Trees often fall over because their roots could not go deep into the ground, usually because they hit solid rock less than 1.5 to 2 meters down. Without deep root penetration, the tree lacks a strong anchor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, tso lɛ tswaa tɛi ni wa ni mli kwɔ fe mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Tso lɛ bɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni mli wa.

english: How deep do the roots of an oil palm tree actually need to go into the ground?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ni mu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: An oil palm tree's root system needs to push down about 1.5 to 2 meters deep into the ground. This deep base supports the heavy weight of the tree above and keeps it standing for many years.
ga: Esa akɛ mu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 mli. Nɛkɛ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ fiɔ tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edamɔ shi afii babaoo.

english: What happens to a tree's growth if its roots hit a hard rock layer underground?
ga: Mɛni baa tso ko dalɛ nɔ kɛji eshishifãi lɛ yatswa tɛ ko ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When roots hit a rock layer too close to the surface, they stop growing downward and spread sideways near the top. This makes the tree weak, easily knocked down by wind, and quick to dry out during dry weather.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ tswa shishitoo tɛ lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ oya, ni kɛ́ hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, egbiɔ oya.

english: Why do palm trees need a deeper base in the soil compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei yɔɔ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmei ahe lɛ?

english: Maize only lives for a few months and has short roots, but a palm tree grows very tall and heavy for decades. The palm needs a base that extends 1.5 to 2 meters deep into the earth to hold its heavy weight.
ga: Abɛi hiɔ shi nyɔji fioo pɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ yɛ kukuji. Shi ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛtsiii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Esa akɛ tso lɛ aná shishitoo ni mli kwɔ mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 koni ekɛfi etsitsi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do deep-rooted trees like palm trees survive during long dry seasons without rain?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Because their main roots reach 1.5 to 2 meters deep into the earth, deep-rooted trees can draw water stored deep underground where the sun cannot easily evaporate it.
ga: Akɛni amɛshishifãi titrii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni hulu lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli lɛ oya.

english: If I clear the rocks off the surface of my land, is that enough for planting palm trees?
ga: Kɛji mijie tɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani enɛ baafee nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ ŋmei tsei?

english: Clearing surface rocks helps, but it is not enough. You must also ensure there are no flat rock slabs hidden 1.5 to 2 meters underground that would block the roots from going deep.
ga: Tɛi lɛ anɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shi eshɛɛɛ he. Esa akɛ okwɛ hu koni tɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 ni baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaya shɔŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly even though the soil on top looks rich and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: Topsoil may look rich, but if a hard rock layer lies just beneath it, the roots cannot go 1.5 to 2 meters deep to reach deep soil water. Once the thin topsoil dries out, the plant suffers.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji tɛ ni mli wa lɛ shishi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aya shi mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 koni amɛyashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ egbi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná amanehulu.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my young cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu kookoo dumɔwui beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide big leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to capture maximum sunlight to manufacture food for root tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil, improving air circulation and preventing fungal leaf diseases that rot the foliage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shishifãi ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa lɛ naa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to weak, slender stems and significantly lower overall harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ eba shi waa.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving inward usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Can I plant cowpea or groundnuts in the same field with my maize, or will they steal food from it?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually share food. They take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant nutrients in the soil, which helps feed the nearby maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun and conserve moisture. If leaves stay curled into the cool evening, it means the plant urgently needs water.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni hulu la akashɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ oya.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or sudden soil dryness. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or heavy shade causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing stems and leafy tops instead of transferring starch down to build thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ batter ɔ kɛ wo mi konɛ e pee yi mi nɛ mi wa.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the middle of my young maize leaves with dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Abɛi baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji gbekɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ emli.

english: This destruction is typical of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ namɔ, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani ŋmãa bibii lɛ afee.

english: Why is it helpful to spread dry grass or plant leaves over the bare dirt around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Spreading dry organic matter—called mulching— acts like a shield over the soil. It traps moisture beneath it during hot days, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from invading your crop beds.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛtsii nii. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akabote oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When soil runs low on nitrogen—the main nutrient plants need for growth—the maize plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ, Abɛi juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha dalɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less harvest every year even though I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops pull natural nutrients out of the earth every season. Without adding compost, manure, or rotating crops like beans that rebuild the soil, the soil gets worn out and cannot nourish new crops properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsakeɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ehee lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or get too much rich food in the soil, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and leaves above ground instead of expanding their tubers below.
ga: Beni adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo eyeɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ bulbs yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a strong yield only in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in weak plants and very small cobs the following year.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside my maize stalks before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: These worms are called stem borers. Moths lay eggs on the maize leaves, and when the eggs hatch, the caterpillars burrow into the stem to feed, which blocks food from reaching the corn cob.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ stem borers. Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi koni amɛtao niyenii. Enɛ haaa niyenii ashɛ ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the base of the stem when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting around the root zone chokes the roots and lets soil fungi invade the stem. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rain drain away from the plant stems.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming fruits during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high heat stresses the tomato plant and dries up the pollen inside the blossoms, causing the flowers to drop off to conserve the plant's water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo koni nu akafite tomato tsei lɛ amli.

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the vines and leaves above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, which signals that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni wain tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my bean crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-bean tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with deep roots that are adapted to grab water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early stops them from stealing food from your beans.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ o-beans lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow differently inside a simple greenhouse compared to out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ shĩa ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ he

english: Greenhouse structures protect crops from extreme heat, heavy downpours, and pests. This creates a controlled environment where plants suffer less stress, growing taller and producing higher yields than those exposed to outdoor weather.
ga: Greenhouse gbɛjianɔtoi buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ baa. kɛ tsei ni naa nɔnyɛɛ fioo lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi amli lɛ

english: Can I build the exact same type of greenhouse anywhere in Ghana and expect the same results?
ga: Ani manyɛ mama ŋmɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ Ghana ni makpa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛ?

english: No, because weather conditions vary across Ghana. A greenhouse design that works well in a cooler, high-altitude area like Aburi might trap too much heat in a hotter region like Tamale, affecting crop growth.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi. Greenhouse he mfonirifeemɔi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ tamɔ Aburi lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ dɔlɛ babaoo mli yɛ hei ni mli edɔ tamɔ Tamale, ni enaa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect crops growing under plastic shade covers compared to crops in an open field?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ plastic shade shishi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe?

english: Plastic covers protect plant foliage and soil from being battered by torrential rains. This prevents soil erosion, stops fertilizer from washing away, and reduces fungal diseases caused by wet leaves.
ga: Plastic ni akɛhaa lɛ buɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni ekaho. ni ebaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baai ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ shi

english: Why should I test a small batch of a new crop variety before planting my entire field with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka tsei srɔtoi heei akuu bibioo ko makwɛ? dani adu kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ hu

english: Testing on a small plot allows you to see how the crop responds to your specific soil type and local weather. It helps you learn if it performs well without risking your entire season's investment.
ga: Kaa ni ooofee yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ haa ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he. Ehaa okaseɔ kɛji eetsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ be muu fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: How long does it usually take to know if a new farming method or structure is truly working for my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani aleɔ kɛji okwaayeli gbɛ loo gbɛjianɔtoo hee ko tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It generally takes at least one full growing season (about 3 to 6 months) to observe crop performance through all stages—from germination and flowering to final harvest—under changing weather conditions.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, eheɔ tso lɛ daalɛ be kome (aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6) dani anyɛɔ akwɛɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli. Kɛjɛ shweremɔ kɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ nɔ kɛyashi naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ lɛ shishi

english: Why are crops doing very well on my neighbor's farm, but the same crop is struggling on my land nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miiye jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ miitswa yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Soil depth, drainage, nutrient levels, and shade can differ significantly even between neighboring farms. Small differences in land conditions alter how crops absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli Kɛ hulutsoo baanyɛ asoro amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ po. Srɔtofeemɔi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat gets too intense, the plant experiences heat stress and drops its blossoms to conserve water and energy rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ naa latsaa he haomɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Yellowing and dropping leaves are signs of water stress or high heat. The plant intentionally discards older leaves to reduce its water needs and prevent the rest of the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji nu he haomɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa he okadi. Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ nii shi ni ekɛtsi tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why are my plants growing lots of thick green leaves but very few crops to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade causes plants to put all their energy into leafy foliage growth rather than shifting energy into flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo baaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ he wami kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii womi nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster during warm weather as long as I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, kɛji akɛ miha amɛ nu lɛ?

english: Warmth speeds up a plant's internal metabolism and food-making process (photosynthesis). As long as the roots have plenty of moisture, heat encourages rapid stem and leaf growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tso lɛ mli nibii ni tsakeɔ kɛ bɔ ni afeɔ niyenii lɛ yaa oya. (Photosynthesis) be fɛɛ be ni shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsei ashishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ daa oya.

english: Maize leaves roll up during high heat to save water. Shrinking their leaf surface area prevents water from evaporating too quickly from the plant into the hot air.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Bɔ ni baa lɛ hiɛ he ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the planting seasons changing so much nowadays compared to when my elders were farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ etsake kwraa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli kɛ akɛto be mli ni minyɛmi nuu onukpa lɛ tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weather patterns and rainfall timing shift over years. Farming requires adapting to changing weather, which means watching current rain patterns each year rather than strictly following old calendar months.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ afii amli. Ehe miihia ni okwaayeli atsake ehe kɛya kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ amrɔ nɛɛ daa afi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ kalanda nyɔji momo lɛ asɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Crops planted too close together compete against each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with many leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the plant spends all its energy growing leafy branches above ground instead of storing food into the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei niji kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small holes appearing on the fresh young leaves of my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ baai bibii heei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in young maize are usually caused by tiny caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hiding inside the center leaf shoot and feeding on the leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves right after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash mud containing tiny fungus spores from the soil onto lower leaves. The wet leaves allow the fungal disease to grow quickly and create dark spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ Baai ni efɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni efee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, drought, or a lack of specific soil nutrients needed to form solid fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii ni wa lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small young pods before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani amɛbaadara kwraa?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra small pods when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all the pods at once, especially during dry spells.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, be mli ni amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha pod muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii shikome lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why do my yam leaves turn yellow and die off long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi be saŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves turn yellow early when excessive water rots the underground tuber, or when tiny microscopic worms in the soil attack the roots and stop water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. aloo beni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu gbɛ koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry up quickly when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young plantain shoots have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out easily under harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade and soil moisture to establish early growth.
ga: Plantain tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and protect itself from drought. As long as the stems remain green and healthy, the plant is alive and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli ni ehe wa lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaakwɛ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three steady, heavy rains that wet the soil deep down. Planting after the very first light drizzle is risky because the dry soil can scorch and destroy your seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or lack of water. When temperatures get too high or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ titri. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why is it bad for my soil when I burn weeds on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛ́ mishã ŋmɔ mli jwɛi dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning clears the land quickly, but it destroys rich organic matter and beneficial soil organisms while drying out the topsoil. Letting slashed weeds decompose naturally feeds the soil and retains moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Mohu ɔ, e kpataa níhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ kɛ níhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ nɛ a he hia a hɛ mi, be mi nɛ e haa zugba a nɔ ɔ ngɛ gĩe. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni afo lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yams struggle to expand in hard, heavy soil or small mounds. Preparing high, loose mounds gives the tubers soft soil to push through easily so they can grow long, thick, and smooth.
ga: Sweet potatoes bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tsii loo gɔji bibii anɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni ooosaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli afee mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ mli. Koni efee kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear from nowhere and eat up my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii je kpo trukaa kɛjɛ he ko ni amɛye mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on the undersides of young maize leaves at night. When these eggs hatch all at once into hungry caterpillars like the fall armyworm, they can consume tender leaves very quickly.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ashishi gbɛkɛ Kɛ́ nɛkɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ fall armyworms. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye baai bibii oya.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in cold, overly damp, and shady conditions. Pruning dense branches and clearing tall weeds lets sunlight in and helps keep the pods dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ tsɔ, kɛ hulutsoo. Nibii ni tsii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: What causes my tomato plant leaves to curl up and turn pale green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually spread by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant sap and transfer viruses, or it can be a reaction to extreme heat and uneven watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ mli ni ehiii lɛ mli baa.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily weakened by microscopic soil worms called nematodes. Planting suckers deep in rich soil and mounding earth around the base helps give the heavy plant strong support.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni akɛ sũ ni abua naa awo shishi lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei ni tsii lɛ náa sɛɛfimɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young maize seedlings turn yellow and stop growing when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Young plants need enough moisture and nutrients in the soil right from day one. If the soil lacks water early on, the seedlings cannot draw up nitrogen, causing their leaves to turn yellow and delaying their growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nitrogen. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce new leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ baai heei beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanted suckers experience root shock when moved. It takes them a week or two to settle into the soil and build new feeder roots before they can support new leaf growth.
ga: Suckers ni atsake amɛ lɛ naa shishifãi ahe shoofeemɔ kɛji ajie amɛ. Eheɔ otsi kome loo enyɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efeɔ shishifãi heei ni yeɔ niyenii dani enyɛɔ eyeɔ ebuaa baai heei ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to apply fertilizer right at the time of planting rather than waiting a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ otsii 2-3 lɛ

english: Crops need immediate food to establish strong roots. If they start off without proper nutrition in their first few days, their growth gets stunted and it takes a long time for them to recover.
ga: Niyenii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji amɛje shishi ni amɛyeee niyenii ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo ni ebaahe be babaoo dani amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings get burnt leaves when I don't plant shade trees next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ náa baai ni shãa lɛ? Ni miduuu shade tso yɛ emasɛi?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunshine. Shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist while its roots settle in.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings wither quickly after I insert them into dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shwieɔ oya beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rely on soil moisture to sprout roots. Without adequate water at planting, the stem dries out faster than it can establish itself.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ biɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaadu nii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ehe ama shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than young roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they face sudden stress, such as irregular watering or nutrient shortages, because they lack the energy needed to feed developing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ amɛmli lɛ. Enɛ jɛɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛha aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen early on, they put all their energy into leafy growth instead of shifting towards flowering and pod production.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo mra lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ e juɛmi maa fɔfɔi kɛ pod peemi nɔ.

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand smoothly. If the soil is too hard or rocky at the start, the tuber struggles to push through and develops unevenly.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛdara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my maize crop if I don't clear the field early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kɛji mijieee he ni miyɔɔ lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive and steal soil water and nutrients. If you do not clear them before planting, they consume the resources your maize needs during its critical first days of growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji otsuuu he dani odu Amɛbaafite nibii ni he hiaa o-ŋmã lɛ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ gbii ni he hiaa waa ni ekɛdaa lɛ amli.

english: You should wait until the rains fall consistently for about a week or two so the soil stays deep-moist, ensuring seeds germinate without drying out in a sudden dry spell.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa otsi kome loo enyɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ trukaa.

english: Why do weeds seem to sprout and grow much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to suck up water and nutrients faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a main food they need to stay healthy, or that excess water in the soil is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Aloo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the plants grow tall with lots of green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdaraa ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant spends its strength growing top leaves rather than expanding its roots underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Hot temperatures, dry winds, or irregular watering stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to conserve energy instead of making fruit.
