ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants slow down and stop producing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants enter a survival state during intense heat and low water, stopping new leaf and fruit growth to preserve moisture until rains return.
ga: Pepper tsei boteɔ wala shihilɛ mli yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ. Ehaa baai kɛ aduawai heei lɛ daalɛ kpaa koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Heavy, waterlogged soil holds excess moisture around the tubers, creating a perfect environment for rot-causing fungi and bacteria.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ bulb lɛ he lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with maize make both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo tsina ŋmãa mli lɛ, ehaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which nourishes the maize, while maize gives structural support to the cowpeas.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa haa tsina ŋmãa lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the same crop in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and lets species-specific pests and diseases build up in the earth.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. kɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa je lɛŋ.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the soil the nourishment your maize needs to turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmei lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the soil so your plants do not dry out quickly in the sun, keeps the soil cool, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ akagbi oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer to my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. If you place dry fertilizer on dry ground without rain or watering, the strong chemical concentrated near the roots can burn the plant and waste your money.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ loo nu bɛ mli. Tsofai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashã ni efite shika.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many leaves when the Harmattan dry wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, the dry air sucks water out of the soil and trees quickly. Cocoa trees drop their leaves to save water and stay alive until the rain returns. Planting shade trees among your cocoa helps trap moisture and protects the leaves.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo lɛ teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rain is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them for too long, preventing air from reaching the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain off so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut down some of the small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi.

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, fight with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers leaves enough food for the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ plantains ni tsii babaoo aba.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the soil, helping your maize grow larger without needing as much expensive store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua oŋmã lɛ ni edara ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow fast and yield big harvests.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Small holes in the center of young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, eating the growing shoot. Checking your farm early and using proper organic or chemical control prevents them from destroying the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen gives crops their healthy green color and strength to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli, amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of green leaves but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmei baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmei baatoo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly like pipes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss through their leaves and protect themselves from burning in the hot sun.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do my plantain suckers stop growing and take much longer to fruit when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni nugbɔ baa shi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need large amounts of water to expand their stems and broad leaves. Without enough moisture, the plant slows down its growth to save water, which delays fruit production.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when tiny insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ha tsei lɛ miihao. Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔii awo mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I leave too many branches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mishi niji babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess branches block sunlight and air from reaching the middle of the tree. Cocoa trees need balanced sunlight to produce energy for flowers and pods to grow.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make the next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil through its roots. This leaves behind natural food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii shwɛɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my land yield smaller yam tubers every time I plant yam on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Yams feed heavily on soil nutrients. Replanting yam on the exact same spot continuously exhausts the soil's fertility and allows soil pests to build up.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ aya nɔ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants wrinkled and twisting upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni etsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are a reaction to tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, causing uneven growth as the leaf expands.
ga: Pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ ji nɔ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa be mli ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight before your crops get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to the young top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ amli koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why does my land produce weaker crops if I plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly in the same place drains those nutrients completely and allows soil-borne pests that target maize to build up.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. The plant drops the unpollinated flowers to conserve energy until temperatures cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Tsi pollination naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their young flowers before small pods appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot afford to nourish, but excessive flower drop is usually a sign that the tree is stressed by dry weather or insect attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in poorly drained soil. The excess water starves the roots of oxygen, allowing fungal diseases to attack and decompose them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua ni amɛfite.

english: Overcrowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of producing heavy fruits or grains, they stretch upward to reach light, resulting in weak stems.
ga: Tsei ni mli eyi tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii aloo wuhi nɛ a he wa. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni niyenii hu baaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal the water, fertilizer, and light your plants need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la koni eha otsei lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, which can also transmit viral diseases to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ashwã tsei amli

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunches start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akutsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Microscopic worms called nematodes or root-boring insects damage the root system underground, leaving the tree without a strong anchor to hold up the heavy weight of the fruit.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni wa ni baaha tso lɛ yibii ni tsii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my stored seed yams are ready to be planted in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seed yams are ready to plant when their natural resting phase ends and you see small green or pale sprouts breaking through the head of the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛji adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be lɛ ba naagbee. ni onaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miitsɔ yitso lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding organic compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize plants free nutrients to grow bigger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and weak roots that burn easily under harsh sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts as a living umbrella, shielding the cocoa until its roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to conserve moisture and energy. Providing steady water and placing dried grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and stops blossom drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he. Nu daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ efɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, which happens when roots sit in poorly drained, soggy soil. The excess water fosters harmful soil germs that rot the roots, leaving the plant unable to drink water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ tara shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa sũ mli helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ anu nu.

english: Why do small insects eat holes through my dried maize grains when I store them in my barn after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli beni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize weevils are attracted to moisture trapped inside stored grain. If maize is not thoroughly dried in the sun before storage or placed in airtight bags, leftover moisture allows weevils to multiply and destroy the harvest.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa abele ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto loo akɛwo vacuum kotoku mli. Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What will happen to my yield if I plant my cassava stems very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of growing fat tubers underground, the plants waste energy growing tall and thin, resulting in a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers act like hungry children stealing water and nutrients from the mother plant. Pruning away all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother tree to focus all its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni tsii ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my yam sprouts right after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit on the surface of the soil with shallow roots ready to absorb the very first rainfall immediately. Yam setts are buried deeper and take several weeks to sprout roots before they start growing above ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Afuɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If pests eat the leaves off my cassava plant, will it affect the cassava roots underground?
ga: Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ye mi ŋmei baai lɛ Ani ebaana ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes. Leaves act as the crop's kitchen, using sunlight to make food that feeds the whole plant. When leaves are destroyed, the plant cannot produce food, which stops the roots underground from growing large and fleshy.
ga: Hɛɛ. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni akɛfeɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ kpata Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii. Enɛ haaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛfee loo.

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and turn yellow when they get too much direct sunlight and lose water faster than their roots can drink. Providing shade crops like plantains protects them until their root systems grow deeper.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ amɛhe. ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plant turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing happens when the soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls available nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to nourish the fresh growing leaves at the top.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ baa kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the central growing leaf fold during the day, eating the leaves from the inside and leaving behind its droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: If I cut off the bushy branches of my cassava plants, will the tubers underground grow larger?
ga: Kɛ mifo ŋmei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, Ani ŋmei lɛ baafee wuji?

english: No, removing the leaves will reduce tuber size. Cassava leaves act like food factories using sunlight to make energy, which is then stored underground in the roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha yitso lɛ dalɛ aba shi. Cassava baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ he, ni ekɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ ni akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture light and stay clear of soil diseases. When vines stay shaded on the ground, the plant wastes energy and produces smaller yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná la ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Kɛ wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or severe dry spells. To save its own life, the plant sheds its flowers instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa. Bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves crinkling up and rolling into tiny tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee tsɔji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems near the soil surface. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, making it easy for strong winds to uproot the tree unless it is supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ ejaaa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa ni efo tsei. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my crops help them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a protective blanket. It blocks hot sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and prevents groundwater from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots with the help of beneficial soil bacteria. When the plant rots after harvest, it leaves behind natural plant food for the next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ayebuamɔ nɔ. Kɛ tsei fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant seeds that I have kept in my storehouse for more than three years?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto nitoohe ko nɔ ni fe afii etɛ?

english: Seeds lose their ability to sprout over time and expire after a maximum of three years, so planting very old seeds will lead to poor germination and empty fields.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nɔ ni fe afii etɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni etsɛ waa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni he ko hu akafee shwɛm.

english: Do crop seeds really expire like packaged food from the shop?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ diɛŋtsɛ tamɔ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Yes, seeds are living things that slowly lose their strength and die over time, with most crop seeds reaching their maximum shelf life within three years.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni fiofio lɛ, amɛhewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui babaoo hiɔ shi afii etɛ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why did half of the seeds I planted last season fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ fã ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds naturally age and expire; if you used seeds that were kept for too many seasons, many of them may have already died while in storage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ tsu nii lɛ, Ekolɛ dumɔwui babaoo egbo beni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How often do I need to replace my saved seeds with new ones?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mikɛ dumɔwui heei ato dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ najiaŋ?

english: You should replace your seed stock at least every three years, because seeds lose their planting quality and expire after that period.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsake odumɔwui lɛ daa afii etɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ bɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and spice seeds stop growing if I keep them until the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ mi-spice dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji mikɛto kɛyashi afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Spice seeds lose their viability much faster than standard food crops, so they cannot be stored for long periods before planting.
ga: Spice dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ oya fe niyenii ni aduɔ daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ amɛ ato be kakadaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Can I store my spice seeds the same way I store my corn seeds for long periods?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma dumɔwui ato bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui toɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, spice seeds go bad much quicker than grain seeds and must be planted shortly after harvest rather than kept in long storage.
ga: Dabi, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmaa, ni esa akɛ adu yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛto be kakadaŋŋ lɛ

english: Do all types of crop seeds stay good for planting for the exact same amount of time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli?

english: No, different crops have different lifespans; spice seeds spoil very quickly, while major grain seeds can last up to three years under good conditions.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ wala be srɔtoi. Spice dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi afii etɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli.

english: Is it important for me to always secure fresh seeds for my main food crops every season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ dumɔwui heei anɔ kɛha miniyenii ni mikɛduɔ nii titri lɛ daa be?

english: Yes, securing fresh, unexpired seeds for your important crops ensures that your main harvest gets a strong start without crop failure.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui heei ni etsɛko lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛha onibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni okpamɔ titri lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I am buying in the market are too old to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ madu?

english: You should check the age or test a small sample in damp paper; seeds older than three years have likely expired and will not grow well.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ afii ni mɔ lɛ eye lɛ loo oka nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko okwɛ. Kɛ wolo ni mli efɔ Dumɔwui ni eye fe afii 3 lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I bother getting new seeds when I can just use whatever old seeds are left in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ naagbai babaoo amli koni mana dumɔwui heei lɛ? Mɛɛ be manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui momo ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii?

english: Old seeds lose their energy and die after three years, so buying or securing fresh seeds guarantees that your effort in land preparation won't be wasted.
ga: Dumɔwui momo lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ afii etɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ooohe loo obua naa lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mli lɛ efeŋ yaka.

english: Officer, why do the leaves on my cassava plant fall off during the dry season, and is the plant dying?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni tso lɛ miigbo lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to save water. The plant is not dead; it stays dormant while storing energy underground in its roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahereɔ nu. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaahi shi ni ekɛ ehewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers, but the blossoms drop off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi egbeeɔ shi dani edara ni ewoɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. This stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to shed its flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa koni ekaye omanye. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔse amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops seem to suffer and wilt if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu ni amɛgboɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by hot dry days that dry out the topsoil quickly. If sustained rains haven't fully set in, young roots dry up in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbi ni mli edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture while cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ latsaa be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and much smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to stake our yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground using stakes improves sun exposure and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need for green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this food deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does my land yield less food when I plant maize on the exact same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Repeatedly planting it in the same spot drains those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ kwraa. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to grow aggressively. Their seeds sit naturally in the soil and react instantly to water and sunlight, absorbing soil nutrients much faster than domestic crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛdara waa. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nu kɛ hulu la ba amɛnɔ. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia dumɔwui.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop soft burnt spots when left out under heavy sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ náa he ko ni shãa fioo kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Direct intense sunlight bakes exposed fruit surfaces, causing sunscald. Crops need adequate leafy coverage to shade developing fruits from hot afternoon sun rays.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ni ebaashã aduawai lɛ hiɛ. Tsei lɛ hia baai ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ afee shade kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What is the main difference between planting local crop seeds and foreign seeds imported into Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa Ghana lɛ ateŋ?

english: Foreign crop varieties are often bred for higher yields or faster growth, but local seeds are naturally adapted to Ghana's soil and weather. Foreign varieties usually require extra care, specific fertilizers, and extra pest control to produce well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi koni amɛwo yibii babaoo loo amɛdara oya. Shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa Ghana shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I know if imported seeds I buy at the local market will grow well on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Imported seeds need to be suitable for your local rainfall and temperature. Before buying, check if agricultural officers have certified the variety for your region, and ask about its specific soil and water requirements.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Dani obaahe lɛ, kwɛmɔ kɛji okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tsofai srɔtoi lɛ ji nɔ ni sa okpokpaa lɛ nɔ. ni obi shikpɔŋ kɛ nu pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ he sane.

english: If I buy crop seeds coming from neighboring countries like Nigeria, will they grow easily in Ghana?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi tamɔ Nigeria lɛ mli. Ani amɛdumɔ waaa yɛ Ghana?

english: Crops from neighboring West African countries often adapt easily to Ghana because of similar climate and soil conditions, but they still require proper land preparation, weed control, and correct nutrient management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ Ghana mli oya yɛ amɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ lolo. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛwoo ni ja

english: Is it better for a small-scale farmer like me to plant local seeds or switch to high-yielding foreign varieties?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ baadu maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui loo amɛbaatsake kɛya maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ?

english: Local seeds are reliable, low-cost, and withstand harsh weather better, but they give moderate yields. Foreign varieties can yield much more food, but only if you have the budget for chemicals, fertilizers, and extra labor.
ga: Anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ akutsoŋ dumɔwui anɔ jogbaŋŋ, amɛjara waaa, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa. Shi ehaa yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ. Maŋsɛɛ henɔi lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii babaoo aba. Shi kɛji akɛ oyɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu tsofai, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsumɔ kroko he nii pɛ.

english: Why do foreign crop varieties usually require more labor and work on the farm than local ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli tsei lɛ?

english: Foreign crop varieties are often less tough against local weeds and insect pests. They need strict planting distance, frequent weeding, regular monitoring, and timely application of farm inputs to reach full growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ jɛmɛ jwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Esa akɛ amɛná he ni amɛduɔ lɛ he jɛkɛmɔ ni mli wa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ shii abɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ daa kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ be naa koni anyɛ ana dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: When is the best time to start applying farm chemicals and fertilizers to my newly planted crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔ mli tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi tsei heei ni midu lɛ anɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ?

english: Young crops need 2 to 3 weeks to establish strong roots after planting before you apply fertilizer. Chemical sprays for pests should only be used when you see early signs of insect damage or as a preventive measure during pest season.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 dani amɛná shishifãi ni wa beni amɛdu amɛ sɛɛ dani amɛwo amɛmli. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii pɛ kɛji ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi lɛ efite loo akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ kooloi lɛ anaa yɛ kooloi lɛ amli be mli.

english: Do imported foreign crop varieties always require more chemical sprays than our local crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ biɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo fe wɔmaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, in many cases foreign crops lack natural resistance to local insects and plant diseases found in Ghana. Because of this, they often depend on regular pesticide sprays to stay healthy and productive.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ shihilɛi babaoo amli lɛ, maŋsɛɛ tsei bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ maŋbii amli kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni anaa yɛ Ghana lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ daa lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my newly planted crops are growing healthily in the first few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Healthy young crops show bright green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady leaf formation. If the leaves turn yellow, look pale, or stop growing, it means the plant lacks nutrients, needs water, or is suffering from pest damage.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. tso lɛ shishi ni wa kɛ baai po Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛkpa dalɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu he miihia lɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall leaves and stems but producing very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baa kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops usually grow tall with little fruit when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or lack enough direct sunlight. The plant spends all its energy on vegetative leaf growth instead of developing strong flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ bɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds affect the growth and yield of my young crop plants?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for light, soil moisture, and nutrients. If weeds are left unchecked early in the planting season, your crop's growth will be stunted, leading to a poor harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi lɛ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra Tsoi lɛ adalɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the ground since I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ejaakɛ anaaa amɛ?

english: Cassava usually matures between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is getting ready when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off, leaving the stem woody and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miisaa amɛhe beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ha tso lɛ tso lɛ afee tso ni efee shiŋŋ.

english: Groundnut plants naturally push their fertilized flowers into the ground because the nuts grow and mature inside the dark soil rather than on the branches above ground.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi ni awo mli fɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any pods start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry weather or heavy shade, or when tiny pests like mirids feed on the flower stems before the pods can form.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi loo hulutsoo ni naa wa miigba amɛnaa. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which helps them build strong green leaves, or that water is sitting around their roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji feɔ. Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Ni okwɛ shwilafo?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular or the soil dried out too much while the fruit was growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejaaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ fe nine beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ ji nɔ ni haa enɛ baa.

english: My plantain plant has produced many small shoots around it; should I leave all of them to grow together?
ga: Mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe. Ani esa akɛ mashi amɛ fɛɛ koni amɛfee ekome kɛdara?

english: You should cut away most of the extra shoots and leave only one or two strong ones. Too many shoots will fight for the same soil food and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tsofɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants when they start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb toward the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la koni amɛha niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots work together with helpful natural soil microbes to trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my vegetable bed when the plants are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small root systems and easily get overwhelmed by aggressive weeds, which steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your plants need to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni jwɛi baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya. Enɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What actually happens to my cocoa trees when I apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo mli?

english: Fertilizer acts as direct food for cocoa trees, supplying essential minerals like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that strengthen root systems, encourage flowering, and help produce bigger, heavier pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛha cacao tsei lɛ. Ehaa shika tsuru nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe hewalɛ Ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛtsiii.

english: How do I know if my soil needs special cocoa fertilizer or if it is already good enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko loo ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow slowly, have pale leaves, or produce very few flowers and small pods, it means the soil has run out of nutrients and requires specialized cocoa fertilizer to boost yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛbɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko awo mli koni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Will applying too much fertilizer to my cocoa trees cause any harm?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli fe nine lɛ kɛ naagba ko baaba?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots, cause the leaf edges to dry up, and even kill the plant because the chemicals become too strong for the roots to absorb safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. dry the leaf edges Ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ po ejaakɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛre shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it harmful if my farm chickens are running around and scratching under my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jo foi kɛmiibɔle amɛhe? ni mikɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi shwieɔ shi

english: While chickens eat harmful farm pests, their sharp claws can damage shallow feeder roots near the surface, and large amounts of fresh droppings can burn young roots.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi yeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara moŋ, shi amɛnaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite niyenii ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ shishifãi. Ni ŋmeii heei babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Can I use fresh chicken manure directly on my young crops instead of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee atsu nii yɛ tsei bibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is extremely strong and generates high heat as it breaks down, which can burn young plant roots; it must be dried and aged before placing it near your crops.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa, ni kɛ́ efite lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ babaoo baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ agbi ni etsa dani akɛma oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Do chickens roaming in my vegetable garden do more good or more harm to my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi ni nyiɛɔ mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ loo amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Chickens help by eating destructive caterpillars and weeds, but they can cause damage if they scratch up shallow seeds or peck at low-hanging leaves and soft stems.
ga: Kooloi yeɔ amɛbuaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ kɛ jwɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite nii kɛji amɛfolɔ dumɔwui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli. loo okɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ abɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop when the plant suffers from too much direct sunlight, lack of soil moisture, or a lack of basic plant nutrients in the ground.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers that drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa flowers shed naturally if the tree lacks water, lacks essential nutrients during flowering, or if tiny insects called midges are not available to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baashwie shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen.

english: Why are some of my growing cocoa pods turning black and rotting directly on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions when cocoa trees are untrimmed and do not get enough sunlight and airflow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Beni afooo kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛnáaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from around my cocoa trees before putting fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu kookoo tsei dani mawo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Weeds grow fast and will quickly absorb the fertilizer and water intended for your cocoa trees, leaving your main crops starved even after you apply food to the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ okɛ niyenii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start followed by weeks of heat. If you plant too early, the soil will dry up and kill the tender seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so the seeds get continuous moisture to grow.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi ni ekpata dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahiɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa.

english: You must make sure the tiny leaf buds on the cassava stem are pointing upward towards the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots will struggle to turn around and grow, resulting in weak plants and very small cassava roots.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni okwɛ koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ Yɛ ŋmei tso ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe ni ebaawa akɛ amɛaada. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa baa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts on the same plot before planting maize next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ mɛi akɛ amɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani amɛdu ŋmei afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that pull natural food (nitrogen) out of the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural food remains in the soil to feed the maize you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmei ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants have very sensitive leaf skins and weak roots. Direct, hot sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil before they can drink water, which is why they need shade trees or plantains nearby to shield them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ. Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani enyɛ enu nu. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe lɛ.

english: When tomato plants get too hot or don't get enough water, they experience severe stress. To save their own lives, the plants drop their flowers so they don't expend energy growing fruits until conditions get better.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ baaha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ ni naa wa. Bɔni afee ni amɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala No sɛɛ lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ aduawai kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot, helping the plant convert sunlight into large, healthy yam tubers below the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many young shoots grow around one plantain tree, they fight each other for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, which ensures you get big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Amɛbaawuu amɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign of tiny, almost invisible insects called aphids or mites sucking the juice from under the leaves. Spraying them early with neem water or insect soap helps uncurl new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji kooloi bibii ahe okadi. Atsɛɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nɔ ni anaaa lɛ akɛ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Ni akɛ neem nu loo kooloi amli samla baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ agbo.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow around my crops reduce my harvest yield at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Weeds act like thief plants on your farm. They grow much faster than your crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow big fruits and grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai kɛ ŋmaa wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale light-green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale or yellow leaves mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main food for growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the rich green color and helps the plant produce large cobs.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko he miihia ŋmãa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná su ni mli kwɔ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: What will happen to my cocoa pods if I delay spraying them with pest control chemicals?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ?

english: Delaying chemical spraying allows fungal diseases like black pod and pests like mirids to spread quickly, causing the pods to rot, turn black, and ruin the beans inside before harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛbaagbe naa lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirid lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pods lɛ ni fiteɔ. tsɔ ediŋŋ ni ofite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow and drop off when insects attack them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua amɛ lɛ?

english: Insects suck the essential sap and nutrients out of the leaves, damaging the plant's ability to make food. This causes the leaves to lose their green color, wither, and fall off.
ga: Kplukai nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. ni fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. egbo ni egbee shi

english: How do I know if the chemical spray I applied to my crops is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will see dead pests on the ground or leaves, the spread of leaf spots or rotting will stop, and your crops will start producing fresh, healthy green shoots.
ga: Obaana kooloi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ loo baai lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo fitemɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baakpa. Ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Is it safe to spray my crops with pest chemicals when rain is about to fall?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ?

english: No, heavy rain will wash the chemical off the leaves before the plant or pests can absorb it, leaving your crops unprotected and wasting your chemical inputs.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abuuu onibii ahe ni tsofai ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Why did my entire patch of crops dry up and die so suddenly as if they were burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ gĩ trukaa ni amɛgboi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden crop death usually happens when severe root-rot fungal diseases or stem-boring pests cut off the plant's internal water supply, causing the whole plant to collapse rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso gbele trukaa baa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, shishifãi ni fiteɔ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bote tso lɛ shishi waa, ni efo nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi oya

english: Why are my cassava plants staying very short and failing to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ wala be kukuoo kwraa ni ewooo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Stunted growth happens when crops lack key nutrients in the soil or are attacked by pests early in their life, preventing them from storing energy in their root tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraaa oya lɛ baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ tsei lɛ amli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ato hewalɛ yɛ shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young crops look like they are burning when the sun shines directly on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young or tender crops easily get scorched under hot sunlight because their roots are not deep enough yet to pull up water as fast as the hot sun evaporates it from their leaves.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii loo amɛdarako. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ amli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛya ŋwɛi oya tamɔ bɔ ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale green even though I planted them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops turn pale green or yellow when they lack nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their deep green color and strength to grow thick leaves.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa su eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa kɛ baai ni mli wa, ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops when I leave the farm unattended?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ beni mishiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that aggressively steal available water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛjuɔ nu ni yɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off off before they turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a sudden lack of essential nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli trukaa

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains alongside them creates a living shade canopy that protects the cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. ni ajieɔ tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is missing nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow leaves and stalks. Applying chicken manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and supports bigger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai kɛ tsei lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ toi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their root systems compete with each other for space, soil nutrients, and moisture. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every cassava stalk has enough soil area to develop large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ He ni akɛaaha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei tso naa shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: How does the fall armyworm cause so much damage to my corn leaves?
ga: Te fall armyworm lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fall armyworms crawl inside the central funnel (whorl) of the corn plant where new growth happens and feed on the soft, young leaf tissues. Because they destroy the leaves responsible for producing the plant's food, the corn struggles to produce healthy ears.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli he ni ŋmãa hee miida lɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ baai ni feɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa abɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ekwɛ̃ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant my yam setts on raised mounds instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds create soft, loose soil that makes it easy for yam tubers to expand deep into the ground. Mounds also improve drainage so heavy rains do not sit around the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Gɔji hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When tomato plants face extreme heat and a lack of water, they experience stress and drop their flowers to preserve their own energy. Providing regular water and partial shade helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ he lɛ, Tomatoi kɛ haomɔ baakpe ni amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my land improve the corn I grow there next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. When you plant corn afterwards, the corn uses that trapped nitrogen to grow faster and produce a better harvest without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo yibii kpakpai ni ehe ehiaaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop yields to drop so sharply if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the moisture and nourishment in the soil go into growing your crops instead of wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ koni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ koo mli tsei najiaŋ.

english: Why do certified hybrid maize seeds yield more than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to combine strong traits like drought tolerance, disease resistance, and high yield. Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose these special characteristics over generations and tend to produce smaller, uneven crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni akɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ hɔmɔ tsuishitoo afata he. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. ni esumɔɔ ni ekɛ yibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee aba.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains kuu lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Plantain is ready to harvest when the fingers become plump and lose their sharp, angular ridges, turning smooth and rounded. The small dead flowers at the tips of the fruits will also rub off easily, even while the skin remains green.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni amɛniji lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli lɛ. Ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fɔfɔi bibii ni egboi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anaagbee lɛ hu shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po.

english: How is it possible for me to harvest crops twice on my one acre of land in a single year?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: In regions with two rainy seasons, you can plant a crop at the start of the major rains, harvest it, and then immediately plant a fast-growing second crop when the minor rains begin.
ga: Yɛ kpokpaa ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ bei enyɔ nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpeteŋkpele ko shishijee mli, okpa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni daa oya lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko je shishi pɛ.

english: What is the difference between the major rainy season and the minor rainy season for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ teŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The major season brings longer and heavier rainfall ideal for main crops, while the minor season has shorter rainfall best suited for quick-maturing crops.
ga: Be titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli wa ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni daa oya lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Late-planted crops miss the peak rains when they are flowering, which causes the plants to produce smaller grains and lower total yield.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ naaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ dumɔwui bibii ni ehaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why can farmers in other parts of Ghana plant twice a year while I can only plant once in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana hei krokomɛi lɛ feɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ adu shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Yɛ be mli ni manyɛ madu nii shikome pɛ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Ghana has different rainfall zones; southern forested regions get two rainy seasons a year, whereas northern savannah regions only receive one main rainy season.
ga: Ghana yɛ hei srɔtoi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ. Kooi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli, yɛ be mli ni kooyigbɛ savanna lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri kome pɛ.

english: Which crops should I choose if my area only gets one short rainy season each year?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala kɛji akɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku pɛ afi kome?

english: You should choose early-maturing varieties of crops like cowpeas, millet, or short-duration maize that can fully ripen before the short rains stop.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and start drying up as soon as the rains pause for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi pɛ?

english: Crop roots need constant soil moisture to drink nutrients from the ground; without rain, the leaves lose water quickly and the plant shuts down to protect itself.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Ni tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: How can I get more food out of my small plot of land without buying extra farmland?
