ga: Manyɛ maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee enɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ kroko?

english: By utilizing both rainy seasons to plant twice a year, or by intercropping legumes with grains, you can double your harvest on the same piece of land.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be muu lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni okɛ dumɔwui baadu lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ oná yibiiwoo lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: If I plant crops twice a year on the same soil, won't my land lose its fertilizing power?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ sɛɛ foŋ?

english: Growing crops continuously can drain soil nutrients, but rotating heavy feeders like maize with leguminous crops like beans naturally restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi niyenii agboi tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know the exact right time after the first rain to put my seeds into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked deep enough into the soil so seeds have continuous moisture to sprout, rather than planting after the very first light drizzle.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se.

english: Should I clear my farm immediately after my first harvest if I want to plant a second crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni madu tso ni ji enyɔ

english: Yes, clearing right after harvest removes pest breeding sites and allows you to prepare the seedbed early enough to catch the start of the next rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni osaa odumɔwui ashishi oya bɔ ni sa koni onine ashɛ nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Sir, why did my neighbor get a huge harvest this year while my own crops barely produced anything?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná ŋmaa babaoo afi nɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo nɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: High yields come from combining good quality seeds, proper plant spacing, and keeping the soil nourished. Even when weather conditions are tough, well-managed crops are stronger and produce much more grain.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ mli baa. He ni sa ni ka tsei ateŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii po. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu he wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why is clearing and loosening the soil so important before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ ajie sũ lɛ mli ni ajie lɛ dani akɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil makes it easy for young plant roots to spread, breathe, and drink water deep underground, which gives the crop a strong foundation to survive and grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmu ni amɛnu nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei naa shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops dry up and stop growing so fast whenever the rains delay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Plants rely on water to dissolve soil nutrients and carry them up to the leaves. Without rain or soil moisture, the plant starves and dries out to protect itself from dying.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ nu nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli. Kɛji nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaagbi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rain comes and goes unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa ni enɛɔ lɛ?

english: It is best to plant after the soil has received a deep, soaking rain rather than the first light drizzle. This ensures there is enough moisture stored underground to support seed germination.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni mli edɔ sɛɛ moŋ fe klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do young plants wilt easily under strong sunshine, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsĩ naa?

english: Young seedlings lose water quickly through their soft leaves in intense heat. Covering the soil around them with dry grass or mulch keeps the root area cool and saves water.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Mulching around Hay loo mulch ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I pay more for certified store-bought seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo nyɔmɔ babaoo koni mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ shwapo mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to grow uniformly, resist diseases, withstand dry spells better, and yield significantly more food than old seeds saved over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa, helai akamɔ amɛ, ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa niyenii babaoo kwraa fe dumɔwui momo ni ato yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does rice seem to need so much water and care compared to crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo kɛ ekwɛmɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice has shallow roots and soft leaves that require constant soil moisture to build grains, whereas cassava stores food in thick underground roots that can survive long dry periods.
ga: Omɔ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu daa koni efee dumɔwui. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei toɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli tse ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ amli.

english: Sir, why do my crops look yellowish and small if I do not apply fertilizer?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops take up nutrients from the soil as they grow. Over time, the soil gets exhausted, and plants show hunger by turning yellow and staying small until new nutrients are added.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni niyenii heei baa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for limited sunlight, root space, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that yield very little.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce fewer and smaller grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha midumɔwui lɛ miiwo dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops. When weeds share the field, your crops starve and cannot put enough energy into growing big grains.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ja he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do people in my village say that the cocoa trees will bring heavy rain soon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ etsɛŋ ni kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa baaba lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees don't actually create the rain, but their natural cycle of flowering and pod growth aligns with the arrival of the rainy season in Ghana. When cocoa trees start budding, it is a natural sign that humid weather and heavy seasonal downpours are close behind.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ haaa nugbɔ nɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Shi adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa Ghana lɛ kpãa gbee. Beni kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be lɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miibɛŋkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods start turning black when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ diŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain increases humidity and leaves constant moisture on the pods, which creates the perfect condition for Black Pod disease (a fungal infection) to spread. Pruning your trees to let sunlight and air pass through helps pods dry faster and prevents the disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eshiɔ hulutsoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. (Fungal infection) Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ oya ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: What steps should I take on my farm before the heavy rains start coming?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Before heavy rains arrive, you should clear weeds and open drainage gutters so standing water can flow off your land. You should also prune tall shade trees to prevent falling branches from damaging young crops during heavy storms.
ga: Dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaba Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni ogbele nu tsɔji lɛ koni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ajɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ koni tsei niji ni egbee shi lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: Is heavy rain always good for my cocoa trees and crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi kɛha mikoo tsei kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be?

english: Rain is necessary for crops to grow, but too much heavy rain without enough sunlight can cause soil erosion, root rot, and fungal diseases. Crops need a healthy balance of both rainwater and direct sunlight to produce well.
ga: Nugbɔ he hia kɛha tsei adalɛ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hela aba. Nugbɔ kɛ hulu la fɛɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I keep heavy rainwater from washing away the good soil on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can plant cover crops like legumes or build soil ridges across sloping land. These barriers slow down running water, allowing it to soak into the earth instead of carrying your fertile topsoil away.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii. Aloo obaanyɛ oma shikpɔŋ ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Gbɛtsii nibii nɛɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ blɛoo. Ha nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ooofɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, you should avoid applying fertilizer right before heavy rain because the rushing water will wash the nutrients away before the plant roots can soak them up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: When is the best time to plant young cocoa seedlings relative to the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui bibii kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he?

english: It is best to plant young seedlings right at the beginning of the rainy season. This allows their roots to settle deeply into moist soil so they grow strong enough to withstand heavy storms and future dry spells.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui bibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ ahum ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni baa wɔsɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Will heavy rain knock the blossoms off my crops before they turn into fruits?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha mifɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai?

english: Yes, heavy rain coupled with strong winds can knock delicate flowers off your crops, reducing your yield. Planting shade trees or windbreaks around your farm helps block strong winds and dampens the force of heavy rainfall.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ atswa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔnei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa ni eye ebua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow when water sits on my field after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain sits on your field without draining, it suffocates the roots by cutting off air. Without oxygen, roots begin to rot and cannot feed the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: When heavy rain falls on your yard without drainage It suffocates the roots by cutting off air. If there is no oxygen The roots will begin to rot and be unable to provide food to the plant. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do weeds grow so fast right after heavy rains start, and do they harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Weeds grow quickly after rain because they absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear them early in the rainy season, they will steal the light, food, and water meant for your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji otsuuu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Amɛbaaju kane, niyenii, kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves the nutrients they need to turn green and produce strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family. Their roots have special nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, acting as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant in that field next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ fãji krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ ŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space underground to grow large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli tse baakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving or planting shade trees acts like an umbrella, keeping the seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes small holes and dark dirt in the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni muji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl into the central leaves (the funnel) to eat the young plant tissue, so checking your farm early allows you to treat them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋ (cone) koni amɛ ye tso bibii lɛ ahe fãji. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and crowd out my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaoɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very aggressive roots that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than young crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly and block sunlight from reaching your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni boteɔ mɔ mli waa. Enɛ baajie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, usually from extreme heat, dry soil followed by heavy watering, or a lack of potassium in the soil during the flowering period.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nu ni mli wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots holding up a very heavy stalk. If you allow too many suckers (shoots) to grow from one stand, or if tiny root worms damage the root base, the stem loses its grip in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ tso ko ni tsii waa lɛ he. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shidaamɔ kome mli, Aloo kɛji shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni enyɛŋ emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the main rains settle in. If seeds sprout during that brief wet period, the young shoots will wither and dry up when the dry days return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi kɛji gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: Why is it bad practice to grow maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani be mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow crops on a sloped hill, or will the rain wash all my soil and fertilizer away?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ edɔ nɔ? Aloo ani nugbɔ lɛ baaho mishikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: You can grow crops on sloped land, but heavy rain can easily wash away fertile topsoil and fertilizer. Planting across the slope or creating soil barriers slows down rainwater and keeps nutrients right where your crop roots need them.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ oya. Dumɔ ni oootsɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi he ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ he hiaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is the soil at the bottom of my sloped land darker and richer than the soil at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ nii fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes away loose, nutrient-rich topsoil and decaying leaves from the top of the hill and deposits them at the bottom. This naturally makes the lower land deeper, darker, and more fertile over time.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ baai ni egboi kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni ebuaa amɛnaa yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli kwɔ, ewoɔ duŋ, ni ewoɔ nii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it better to make soil ridges across a sloped farm rather than straight down the hill?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ aaama ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ waa lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya gɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Making ridges across the slope acts like small walls that hold rainwater and stop it from running wild. If you make ridges straight down the hill, rain will flow like a stream between them, washing away your seeds and roots.
ga: Kɛ́ aha ŋshɔ lɛ jo foi kɛfo ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ gbogbo bibioo ko. He ko ni abaabua nugbɔ nu lɛ naa ni atsĩ enaa koni ekaho basabasa. Kɛji ofee ŋshɔkpɔ ni ja Nugbɔ hoɔ tamɔ faa ni hoɔ yɛ gɔji ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ ateŋ. Efɔɔ dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: If my land is bumpy and uneven, do I need to level it before planting my crops?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Ani ehe miihia ni mafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani madu tsei?

english: Leveling uneven land helps rainwater spread out equally so no part of your farm gets flooded while another stays dry. However, scraping off too much topsoil can expose hard, infertile dirt underneath, so adding manure after leveling helps restore crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ ni oooha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ jaa pɛpɛɛpɛ, bɔni afee ni nu akaho oŋmɔ lɛ fã kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekroko lɛ kã he egbi. Shi kɛlɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashi muji ni wa ni nyɛɛɛ afɔ nii yɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he beni ajie lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Does digging deep into hard soil before planting really help my crop roots grow better?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mifoɔ mli shɔŋŋ dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Digging loosens tightly packed soil so roots can push deep down to find underground water and plant food. Soft, dug soil also lets air enter the ground, which roots need to stay healthy and support a big harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛdu niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ko.

english: How does clearing old tree stumps and big stones from my farm help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii momoi kɛ tɛi wuji ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Removing stumps and big rocks leaves open space for crop roots to branch out freely without hitting barriers. It also prevents old tree stumps from sprouting back up and stealing light, water, and soil nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ tɛi wuji lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ajie niji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni enaaa gbɛtsii nii ko nɔ hewalɛ. Etsiɔ tsei momo hu anaa koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛju la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops on the higher part of my farm dry up faster than the ones in the low area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downhill because of gravity, so moisture leaves elevated ground quickly. Higher areas are also exposed to more sun and wind, which dries out the topsoil much faster.
ga: Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ shĩɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ oya. Hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya kwraa.

english: What happens to my crops when heavy rain leaves standing water in the flat parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu damɔ shi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits in a field for too long, it cuts off air to the soil and smothers the roots. Without air, the roots begin to rot, turning crop leaves yellow and causing the plant to stunt or die.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ. Ehaa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: Can cassava grow well on sloped land where water does not collect?
ga: Ani ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni nu bɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Cassava grows very well on gentle slopes because its underground tubers rot easily if left in soaked soil. The slope ensures extra rainwater drains away quickly, keeping the cassava roots healthy.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔŋji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ eshishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Slopes haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa cassava shishifãi lɛ waa

english: Why do crops grow very tall in one corner of my farm but stay short and weak in another corner?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Shi akɛ afee kuku ni egbɔjɔ yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Soil quality and moisture change from spot to spot on the same farm due to how water flows and where rich topsoil settles. Spots with thinner soil or poor water flow produce weaker crops unless you give those areas extra manure or fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome kɛyaa he kroko yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Nu ni hoɔ kɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, egbeeɔ shi. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseee loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata nakai hei lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger plants like plantains because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbiɔ dani enyɛɔ efeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture as much sunlight as possible, which gives the plant the energy it needs to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all the plants undernourished.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the key food crop plants need to stay green and produce healthy corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of ground every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every season without giving the soil time to recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does adding animal manure and rotten leaves to my land help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egboi fata mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Animal manure and decayed leaves feed the soil with natural nutrients and help the earth hold onto rainwater longer during dry periods.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa je lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in the soil without draining away properly, which suffocates the roots and allows rot-causing fungi to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa.

english: Why do small worms appear inside the leaves of my young maize right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on the tender new leaves that sprout after the rains begin, and these eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars, such as fall armyworms, that feed on the soft heart of the plant.
ga: Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. ni yeɔ tso lɛ tsui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Why do wild weeds in my field cause my crops to produce less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to grow, effectively starving your plants and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi.

english: You should wait until the ground stays moist for several days after the first major rains, ensuring seeds do not sprout and then dry up during a sudden break in the rainfall.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii komɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has to the young leaves at the top, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very wet to very dry. Extreme heat damages the pollen, so the plant drops the unpollinated flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa kɛtee nɔ ni egbi waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing trees like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni afee umbrella ahaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but end up with tiny roots underwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ nu shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is heavily shaded, the cassava plant spends all its energy building leaves and stems up top instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ shishifãi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do tiny worms keep hiding right inside the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central leaf funnel because it provides soft, tender young leaves to eat while keeping them hidden from birds and protected from the hot sun.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhaa baa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛteeɔ okpoi ahe, ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning yellow and the vines dying off after several months of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tso lɛ miiho yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni ekɛdara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a natural sign that your yam has fully matured. When the leaves and vines wither, it means the plant has finished transferring all its food from above ground into the tuber below, indicating it is ready for harvest.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ egbɔ. Beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gboɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ejie eniyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Etsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why should I soak my pepper seeds in clean water overnight before planting them in nursery beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ pepper dumɔwui awo nu ni mli tse mli nyɔɔŋ kome dani mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have tough outer coats. Soaking them softens the outer shell and tells the seed inside it is time to wake up, allowing them to sprout much faster and more evenly in your nursery.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ehaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ekɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ o-nursery lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my young garden eggs look weak and stunted even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop plants and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your garden eggs. They also host insect pests that can attack your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmeii yɛ obɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Amɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atutua onibii hu jɛɛhe.

english: Heavy clay soil holds too much water and prevents air from reaching the roots. When water sits around cassava tubers for too long without draining, oxygen is cut off and rot-causing organisms attack the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ haa nu babaoo hiɔ shi, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Beni nu ebɔle he lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Ni nibii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants start producing flowers so quickly when a short dry spell begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi oya kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Cowpea plants naturally react to dry conditions by speeding up their life cycle. When they sense a lack of water, they hurry to produce flowers and seed pods to ensure their offspring survive before the ground completely dries up.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ tsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ amɛshihilɛ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛ amɛnu he akɛ nu efo amɛmli lɛ Amɛbaafee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji oya koni amɛkwɛ akɛ seshibii lɛ baahi shi dani shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why are the lower fronds on my oil palm tree turning brown and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: As palm trees grow, their older fronds naturally age, dry out, and turn brown. Removing these dead fronds through regular pruning helps the tree direct its energy and nutrients toward growing fresh leaves and bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ da lɛ, baai ni eda lɛ daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni egboi nɛɛ kɛtsɔ tso ni afoɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei kɛ aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: What will happen to my palm trees if I leave the dead fronds hanging on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi baai ni egboi yɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving old, dead fronds on the tree creates a hiding place for pests like beetles and traps moisture that causes fungal diseases. Trimming them away keeps the trunk clean and reduces the risk of infection.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli, ni emɔɔ nu ni kɛ ŋmeii helai baa lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he atse ni ebaaha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I cut off dying branches or fronds without damaging the main trunk of my tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ tsei niji loo baai ni miigboi lɛ ni mifiteee tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ?

english: Use a sharp cutlass or pruning chisel to cut the leaf stem cleanly close to the trunk, taking care not to gouge or slice into the main stem, as deep trunk wounds let in rot and destructive insects.
ga: Kɛ kakla ni naa wa loo chisel afolɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ tso lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okafo loo okafo tso lɛ mli tso titri lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pilamɔi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ fitemɔ aba.

english: What should I do with the dead palm fronds after I cut them down from the tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmei tsei ni egboi lɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Gather the cut fronds and move them away from the base of the trees. Stacking them neatly between crop rows allows them to rot safely into compost without sheltering pests right next to the tree trunks.
ga: Bua baai ni afo lɛ anaa ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgboiɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa

english: How can I tell if a leaf on my tree is dying of old age or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigboi yɛ dalɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Leaves dying of old age usually turn yellow and brown slowly from the tips downward at the very bottom of the tree, while leaf diseases often create strange spots, sudden rotting, or affect younger leaves higher up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni gboiɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ asarasu fiofio. Kɛjɛ tso lɛ naagbee kɛyashi shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baa. Trukaa fitemɔ loo ni enaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ

english: Is it bad to leave rotting plant parts lying on the ground near my tree trunks?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ aaashi tso lɛ fãi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving decaying stems or fruit close to the base attracts dangerous pests like palm weevils and rhinoceros beetles, which lay eggs in the rotting matter and then attack the healthy tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei loo aduawai ni egboi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaagbala kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ ŋmeii ni ji palm weevils kɛ rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ nibii ni fiteɔ mli ni amɛtutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can diseases spread from one tree to another through the cutlass I use for pruning?
ga: Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dade ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, if you cut a sick tree and then cut a healthy one, germs on your cutlass blade can transfer the disease. It is good practice to clean your blade with fire or disinfectant after cutting diseased parts.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ofo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ofo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Muawai ni yɔɔ otsɔnei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã. Eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ akɛ la loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai atsumɔ tsɔne lɛ he beni afo hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for sick or dying plant parts?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji tso lɛ fãi komɛi hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛgboi?

english: Checking your field at least once every two weeks allows you to spot yellowing leaves, pests, or rot early so you can trim infected parts before the problem spreads to the rest of your crop.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa otsii Enyɔ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo baai ni miifite lɛ mra. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ofolɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to clear the ground directly under my crop canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie he ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the space under the canopy makes it easier to spot fallen diseased leaves, prevents climbing weeds from choking the lower branches, and ensures fertilizer gets straight to the crop's roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana baai ni hela emɔ amɛ. Tsi jwɛi ni kwɔɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Should I trim off a branch as soon as I see it starting to rot, or wait until it dies completely?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ mli kɛji mina akɛ ebɔi fitemɔ pɛ loo mamɛ ni tso lɛ nine lɛ agbo kwraa?

english: You should cut off rotting branches immediately. Waiting allows the rot or fungus to travel deeper into the main stem, which can eventually kill the entire tree.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛmɔ baaha ŋmei lɛ agbo loo ŋmei lɛ aya mli shɔŋŋ kɛya tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbo yɛ naagbee.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the center of lower maize leaves usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni etsɔɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no plantains or big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi be mli ni cacao tsei loo tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight; plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the cocoa establishes root strength.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers under the soil.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: When soil stays soaked in stagnant water, air cannot reach the roots, causing the roots to drown and making them easy targets for rot fungi in the wet dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even if the ground still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, leaves lose water to the dry air faster than the roots can suck it out of the ground, so the plant temporarily wilts to protect itself until the air cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ aya oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Extreme midday heat or sudden dry spells cause tomato plants stress, which makes them drop their blossoms to save water and energy instead of trying to feed a growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Having too many young sucker shoots causes them to fight the main plant for water and fertilizer, leaving you with smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa plantain tso bibioo ko.

english: Why are the top leaf shoots on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from the soft leaves or spreading a plant virus as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ baai bibii amli nu lɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa.

english: Why do my crops produce very small yields when I leave weeds growing around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds are strong thieves that steal water, sunlight, and manure meant for your crops, leaving the main plants starved of energy to form full grains or roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni he wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Enɛ haa tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee dumɔwui loo shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do pawpaw trees start growing on my land when I did not plant any seeds there?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni papaya tso ko bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Akɛni miduuu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw seeds are frequently carried and dropped across farmland by birds, bats, or small animals that eat the sweet fruit. When the seeds land on moist, fertile soil, they naturally germinate and grow on their own.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okpoi, ŋmeii, loo kooloi bibii shwieɔ pawpaw dumɔwui lɛ. ni yeɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ni amɛshiɔ amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni baa nii anɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my pawpaw trees taking so long to produce any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pawpaws require abundant sunlight, steady water, and nutrient-rich soil to bear fruit. Additionally, male pawpaw trees only produce flowers and never grow fruit, so you need female or hermaphrodite trees for fruit production.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo, nu ni yɔɔ dioo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛfata he lɛ, pawpaw tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi pɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ tsei ni ji yei loo hermaphrodite lɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo yibii.

english: Why do young pawpaw fruits drop off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young fruits usually fall off if the tree lacks water during dry spells, if the flowers were not properly pollinated, or if the tree is carrying more fruits than its roots can supply with nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pawpaw plant turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate overwatering, poor soil drainage, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Pawpaw roots rot easily in waterlogged soil, causing the lower leaves to drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ awo amɛ nu babaoo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli Pawpaw shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. ha baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ agbo

english: What is the white, sticky substance covering my pawpaw leaves and fruits?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa mibaai kɛ miyibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That white powder-like substance is caused by mealybugs, tiny sap-sucking pests that weaken the tree. You can control them early by spraying the plant with a mild mixture of soapy water or neem leaf extract.
ga: Nɔ ko ni yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda ji nɔ ni mealybugs feɔ. ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem baa mli nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many years can a single pawpaw tree produce fruits before it becomes useless?
ga: Afii enyiɛ papaya tso kome baanyɛ awo yibii dani ebatsɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa?

english: A pawpaw tree produces its heaviest and best yields for about 3 to 5 years. After this period, fruit production declines and the tree grows too tall to harvest safely.
ga: Pawpaw tso lɛ woɔ eyibii ni tsii fe fɛɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ. Yibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi ni tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akpa amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I feed extra or ripe pawpaw fruits to my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ paw paw aduawai loo aduawai ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Yes, ripe pawpaw fruits are rich in vitamins, sugar, and hydration, making them an excellent supplementary feed for animals like pigs, poultry, and tortoises.
ga: Hɛɛ, papaya aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ vitamini, sugar kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi tamɔ tsinai, kooloi, kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi.

english: Is it safe to plant vegetables underneath my growing pawpaw trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu aduawai yɛ mi-pawpaw tso ni miida lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, you can intercrop light vegetables under young pawpaws. However, as the pawpaw leaves spread and create heavy shade, you should give them space so they do not block sunlight from the lower crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ pawpaw lɛ shishi, shi kɛlɛ, be mli ni pawpaw baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni tsii baa lɛ. Esa akɛ oha lɛ gbɛ koni ekatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell when a pawpaw fruit is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni paw paw aduawai lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A pawpaw is ready to pick when the skin turns light green and shows small yellow or orange streaks near the bottom tip. It will continue ripening fully after being harvested.
ga: Pawpaws lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ehewolo lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ bibii ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ Ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I keep harvested pawpaws fresh long enough to sell them at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-paw paw ni akpa lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvest pawpaws when they just start showing yellow patches, handle them carefully to avoid bruising the skin, and store them in a cool, dry, shaded place away from direct sunlight.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tsitsii lɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi kɛkɛ lɛ. Okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni akafite hewolo lɛ. Ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni hulu la akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need crop medicine or fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees show visible signs when they lack nutrients, such as slow growth, yellowing leaves, or small pods. Applying the right booster or fertilizer restores missing soil nutrients, helping the tree grow thicker foliage and produce healthier pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie okadii ni anaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa, tamɔ amɛdalɛ blɛoo, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa baai ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What actually happens inside my mango tree when I apply a liquid booster to it?
ga: Mɛni baa mi mango tso lɛ mli kɛ mikɛ nɔ ko ni haa nu lɛ yaa hiɛ tsu nii yɛ nɔ?

english: Liquid boosters feed plant nutrients directly through the leaves or roots, speeding up the tree's natural food-making process. This helps mango trees develop stronger leaves, blossom faster, and hold onto young fruits without dropping them early.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai loo amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii feemɔ lɛ yaa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa mango tso lɛ ni enáa baai ni mli wa. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ aduawai bibii ahe ni egbeee shi oya

english: How do I know if a liquid plant booster I bought for my crops is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni haa tsei lɛ daraa ni miheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Within a few weeks of application, a effective booster causes noticeable changes like vibrant dark green leaves, fresh shoots, and quicker flowering. If the crop remains dull or stunted, the product may be ineffective or applied incorrectly.
ga: Yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli beni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ lɛ, tsofa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa tsakemɔi ni kadiɔ mɔ baa tamɔ baai ni kpɛɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii heei kɛ fɔfɔi ni baa oya. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tee nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ Ekolɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtsuuu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time of day to spray liquid medicine on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa ni ji nu yɛ cacao tsei anɔ?

english: Liquid inputs are best applied early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is mild. During these cooler hours, the plant's leaf pores are open to absorb the medicine, and heat will not evaporate the liquid before it works.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nu awo mli leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulu la lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe waa koni amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ. Ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ haŋ nu lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani ebɔi nitsumɔ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves mean the tree is experiencing nutrient stress, pest damage, or too much heat. Inspecting the leaves for tiny insects and providing balanced soil nutrients helps the cocoa regain its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. aloo dɔlɛ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ amli kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ mli, ni okɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ja ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua kookoo lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli.

english: How does shade affect the way my young cocoa trees grow during their first year?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ he yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily in direct sunlight. Temporary shade trees reduce water loss and heat stress, allowing the young cocoa to establish strong roots before growing under full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa dani edaa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi.

english: Flower shedding happens when trees face stress from drought, poor soil fertility, or pest activity. Keeping the soil nourished and providing adequate shade helps the tree retain its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai. Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni sa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: What causes my mango trees to produce plenty of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Poor fruit set in mango trees usually happens because of nutrient shortages during flowering, pest attacks, or heavy rains washing pollen away. Nutrient boosters applied before flowering help flowers turn into solid fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibii ni ehiii ni baa mango tsei amli lɛ baa yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ laajeɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwaa.

english: How long should I expect my newly planted cocoa seedlings to take before they start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ baahe dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years with good care, shade, and nutrition, while older traditional cocoa varieties can take 4 to 5 years to start producing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ hulutsoo, ni amɛye niyenii kpakpa. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani aje feemɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees stay small instead of growing big and plump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ ji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Small pods indicate that the tree is short on soil nutrients, lacking sufficient water, or carrying more pods than its leaves can support. Pruning excess branches and feeding the tree properly helps pods grow to full size.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Aloo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ fe bɔ ni baai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do some farmers mix wood ash or chemical powder with their seeds before putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tso mli sũ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ amɛdumɔwui amli lɛ futuɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛduɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ?

english: Treating seeds with wood ash or special protective powder keeps insects, birds, and soil diseases from eating or rotting the seeds before they get a chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo powda krɛdɛɛ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii, okpoi, kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye loo amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I soak my hard maize seeds in water before planting them in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni wa awo nu mli dani mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soaking seeds softens their hard outer coat and signals to the seed that moisture is present, helping them sprout much faster and more evenly once planted in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ehaa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli waa, ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ nu yɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to start my pepper seeds in a small nursery bed instead of planting them directly in the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper seeds are very tiny and delicate; raising them in a protected nursery bed allows you to protect the young sprouts from harsh rain, heat, and pests until they grow strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tsei akwɛmɔhei ni abuɔ he lɛ, ebaaha obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, dɔlɛ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu yɛ he fɛɛ he. Shishifãi babaoo haaa tso lɛ amu ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plantains or taller trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the air around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ plantains loo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi kɛ baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, cools the soil, and stops unwanted weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: If cassava plants are placed too close together, their leaves fight for sunlight and their roots fight for soil food, resulting in tall plants with very small, thin tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaai lɛ kɛ hulu lɛ baawu ni eshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baawu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots can soak up moisture before the midday heat arrives, which would otherwise evaporate the water before the crop can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, nu lɛ baatsɔ lasu dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anu.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden drought, extreme midday heat, or when there are no insects like bees around to move pollen between the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hɔmɔ ni ba trukaa lɛ kpe amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant pepper on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific plant food from the soil and allows pests and diseases that love peppers to build up in the dirt, making future harvests poorer.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli nikpamɔi lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-baby corn tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛfee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water. By rolling up, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight and wind to conserve moisture until it cools down.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ Tsei lɛ baa amɛbai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to get small holes and look chewed?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ bu bibii ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre?

english: Small holes are usually made by crop pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves. Sprinkling wood ash or using neem leaf extract spray can naturally deter these insects from eating your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem tso mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaye otsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants light shade can save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa pods dry up—a condition known as cherelle wilt—when the tree carries more pods than it can feed, or during severe dry spells and pest attacks. Proper pruning and soil feeding help reduce this pod loss.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ—shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilting—beni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye nii. aloo yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni laajeɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my cabbage plant stay loose and leafy instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ etse ehe ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, face high heat, or get irregular watering. Balanced nutrients and steady soil moisture encourage the inner leaves to wrap tightly.
ga: Cabbage lɛ ehiɛɛɛ yitso kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mligbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs daylight to make food for its underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and keeps them away from rot and pests on the soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees close to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings shade and cool soil during their first years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal food, water, and light quicker than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from starving your cassava tubers of necessary soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ la oya fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough moisture to plant seeds after the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of wet soil into a ball in your hand and poke it gently. If it holds its shape but crumbles easily under light pressure, it has the right mix of water and air for seeds to sprout without rotting.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ eko mli yɛ bɔɔlu mli yɛ onine mli ni okɛwo mli blɛoo. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli shi efoɔ oya yɛ nɔnyɛɛ fioo ko shishi lɛ, no lɛ eyɛ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni efutu ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field with no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and lose moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a protective canopy that mimics the natural forest, sheltering tender seedlings until their roots mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛlaajeɔ nu oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shade ni kaseɔ adebɔɔ mli koo lɛ aba. Ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why do crops growing directly under big mature trees sometimes look weak and yield very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Big trees have large, established root systems that swallow up most of the water and soil nutrients around them. Their thick leaf canopy also blocks sunlight, leaving lower crops with too little light and food to thrive.
ga: Tsei wuji yɛ shishifãi wuji ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tsei babaoo Tso lɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ náa la kɛ niyenii fioo tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Each crop draws specific food nutrients out of the earth. When you plant the same crop year after year, it continuously drains those specific soil nutrients without giving the soil a chance to rest or replenish.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, Eyaa nɔ ekɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hegbɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant cassava right after harvesting a heavy crop of maize on the same soil, why does the cassava perform poorly?
ga: Kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmãa toi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ?

english: Maize is a greedy feeder that pulls a lot of nutrients out of the topsoil. When cassava follows immediately without soil restoration or fertilizer, it struggles because the previous crop already consumed the essential soil food.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmei nyiɛɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa ejaakɛ tsei ni eho lɛ eye niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ momo.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry out so quickly after I clear away all the natural bush and trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya beni mijie adebɔɔ mli tsei bibii kɛ tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Trees and wild plants drop leaf litter that rots and creates a organic blanket over the soil. This leaf blanket traps soil moisture and keeps the earth soft; removing all cover leaves the bare soil exposed to direct sun and baking heat.
ga: Tsei kɛ koo mli tsei shĩɔ baai ni egboi yɛ amɛsɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ baai ni akɛfee tsɔne nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɛ́ ajie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niyenii ni ashãa lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I save seeds from my best and biggest maize cobs, will they always produce the same big cobs next season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ Ani amɛbaawo ŋmãa wuji nɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Crops pass traits to their offspring like animals do. While seeds from a good cob carry strong mother plant traits, wind and insects bring pollen from neighboring weak plants, which can cause some offspring to produce smaller cobs.
ga: Taakɛ kooloi ji lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛsui lɛ haa amɛbii. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmeii kpakpai amli lɛ yɛ fɔlɔ tso ni he wa lɛ sui moŋ, Shi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii woɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ amli ŋmeii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha seshibii komɛi afɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are my cassava stems producing tiny roots even though I took the planting cuttings from a high-yielding parent stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Kɛji mifo tso ko ni ji nyɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nine po?

english: Good parent genetics give a crop potential, but final yield depends on current conditions. If the new soil is compacted, infected with invisible ground pests, or lacking food, even high-quality cuttings will produce small roots.
ga: Fɔlɔi a-fɔmɔ su kpakpa baaha oná nyɛmɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii. Shi naagbee nɔ ni anáa lɛ damɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni anaaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo niyenii bɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ po baanyɛ ajie shishifãi bibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, seedlings compete for light, water, and soil space. The plants spend all their energy racing upward to reach sunlight instead of building strong stems and plump cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting plantain and cassava together in a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akwɛ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ shikpɔji heei anɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping plants with different root depths and growth speeds allows them to share land efficiently. Cassava feeds from upper soil while plantain roots go deeper, maximizing field space without competing directly for the same nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjaraa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Cassava naa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa he ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves show that the crop lacks nitrogen. When soil food is low, the plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young top leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my oil palm fruit bunches get scorched and damaged during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm yibii lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight can burn young, delicate palm fruits before they develop a tough outer skin, reducing the quality and quantity of oil you will harvest.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso yibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani efee kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji mu ni obaakpa lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ ebɔ ni baa shi.

english: Can intense sunlight ruin my palm fruits while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-palm yibii lɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, severe heat from the sun can dry out tender young palm fruits, stopping their growth and causing them to drop early or become poor quality.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tso yibii bibii lɛ agbi. Ekpaa dalɛ ni ehaa ŋmei yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi mra loo ehiii kwraa.

english: Is it helpful to cover my growing palm fruit bunches with mats or woven leaves?
