ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba he akɛ mikɛ tsɔji loo baai ni akpɛ lɛ baaha mi-palm tsei ni miida lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, placing a protective cover like a woven mat over young bunches acts as a shield against direct sun, keeping the developing fruit safe from severe sunburn.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ tsɔne ni akpɛ́ ni akɛwo tsei niji bibii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai ni miida lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa he.

english: How does placing a mat over my developing crops help them produce better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: A mat creates a cool micro-climate around tender young fruits, preventing sun damage so the crop can direct its energy into growing full, healthy produce.
ga: Mat lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ baa aduawai bibii lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu lɛ akafite amɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ afee nibii ni yeɔ emuu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How long should I keep protective covers over my palm fruit bunches before uncovering them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maha tsei akui lɛ anɔ dani magbele amɛ?

english: You should generally leave protective covers on for about two months while the fruits are young and sensitive, giving them enough time to grow strong.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ahi nɔ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ ji gbekɛbii lolo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ. Enɛ haa enáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa hewalɛ.

english: Why should I remove shade covers from my fruit bit by bit instead of taking them off all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooojie fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Removing the cover gradually helps the fruit slowly adapt to increasing light and heat, preventing sudden sun shock that could scorch the skin.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ fiofio Ekɛ ehe woɔ la kɛ dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli. Buu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni baa trukaa ni baanyɛ aha hulu lɛ ashã bo lɛ he.

english: What happens if I expose young shaded crops to full sunlight too suddenly?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ mi tsei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli trukaa?

english: Exposing young fruits to intense direct sunlight all at once can shock and burn them, undoing the protection you provided earlier.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso yibii bibii lɛ wo hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli Shikome pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe afee shoo ni eshã amɛ. Enɛ baafo hebuu ni okɛha tsutsu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my covered palm fruits are ready for full sunlight exposure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-palm yibii ni aha nɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: After around two months under cover, the fruits grow firmer, change color, and show signs of maturity, indicating they can now withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha nɔ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, yibii lɛ baafee shiŋŋ, ebaatsake ehiɛ su ni ebaajie okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ enyɛɔ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Will heat damage from the sun affect the quality of palm oil I get from my fruits?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli baa lɛ baaná ŋmei fɔ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, fruits damaged by sun scorch produce less oil and lower quality oil compared to fruits protected during their early development.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni hulu lɛ efite lɛ haaa mu babaoo aba, ni amɛmli fɔ lɛ hu baa shi kɛ akɛto aduawai ni abuɔ he yɛ shishijee lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my covered fruits are developing properly without taking off the whole cover?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso yibii ni midu lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni mijieee nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can uncover small portions step by step to check if the fruits look full, plump, and free from dark, burnt patches on the outer skin.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbele fã bibioo ko Step by step check koni ona kɛji aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shãa diŋ ko bɛ ehe yɛ kponɔgbɛ.

english: How do the small flowers on my cocoa tree actually turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from flower to flower. When a flower gets pollinated, it stays attached to the tree trunk or branch and gradually swells over several months into a cocoa pod.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Ekpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi loo nine lɛ he ni efoɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a tiny fraction get pollinated by insects. Flowers that aren't pollinated within a couple of days wither and fall off naturally to save the tree's energy.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi, ni no baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: What is hand pollination, and why should I try it on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka pollination makwɛ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small brush or forceps. It helps nature along, ensuring many more flowers successfully develop into pods and increasing your overall harvest.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh bibioo loo pliers nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa adebɔɔ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ni esumɔɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi babaoo babaoo yeɔ omanye ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are some of my young, tiny cocoa pods turning black and shrinking before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ dani eda lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It is usually the tree's natural way of shedding extra pods it cannot feed, but extreme heat, lack of water, or bad soil nutrients can make it worse.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry ni shwieɔ shi. Bei pii lɛ, eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni enyɛŋ eye, shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha ehiɛ afee shoo fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from intense sun and drying winds until their roots are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are completely ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Watch the color of the pod skin. Pods that start green will turn bright yellow when ripe, while reddish or purple pods will turn orange-yellow, indicating the beans inside are fully formed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni pod lɛ hiɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. The red or purple pods will change to orange-yellow. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ebɔi feemɔ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to cut off unwanted shoots and extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ yitsei ni ataooo kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning lets fresh air and sunlight reach inside the tree canopy, which stops humidity from building up and causing diseases. It also directs the tree's food toward pod production instead of useless leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa ni ekɛ hela baa. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ hu gbɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn dark brown and rot during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly humid conditions. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and removing infected pods helps protect healthy trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are hungry for nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi cacao tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow, or if the tree stops making flowers despite good weather, the soil lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer to boost tree health.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa baai lɛ bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Aloo kɛji tso lɛ kpa fɔfɔi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi moŋ, no lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves and young shoots on my cocoa trees looking dry and scorched as if burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛhe edɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by insect pests like mirids (capsids) that suck sap from young branches and pods. Using recommended organic or chemical sprays at the right time controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni shwieɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Organic loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baakudɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli akpɔlɔi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure gives the plant the nourishment it needs to turn green and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants harvest and decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil, naturally fertilizing it for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa tsei ni amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaye abua ni awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo aba nɔ. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: What is making holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ bu ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying organic neem extracts or approved chemicals protects the crop before the growing point is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall worm ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli tsofa ni ji organic loo tsofa ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil pathogen that blocks the internal tubes transporting water inside the plant, causing it to dry out despite moist ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Ha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ po.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots from my plantain plant instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ dumɔwu ko mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni eda kwraa?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to compete for water and nutrients, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one main stem, one medium sucker, and one small shoot per stand ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Nikpamɔ tso titri kome pɛ Sucker kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ tso bibioo kome yɛ shidaamɔ fɛɛ shidaamɔ mli. Enɛ baaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why is it best for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to soak up moisture before the heat of the day causes water to evaporate. Afternoon watering in hot sun can stress the roots and scorch wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa efoɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha baai ni efɔ lɛ ashã.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my farm during the first four weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first month is when young crops build their root systems. Removing weeds early stops them from stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during the crop's most critical growth stage.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ ji be mli ni tso bibioo lɛ maa eshishifãi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips, your soil is likely short on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their health.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tight like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up to protect the plant from losing too much water in intense heat. By reducing the leaf surface exposed to the sun, the plant conserves soil moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baahiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted with yellowish patches instead of smooth and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni kɛbaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry weather to save water. Leaves evaporate moisture into the air, so shedding some leaves helps the tree keep enough water inside its stem and roots to survive the dry spell.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fã ko ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtoɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra branches allows air and sunlight to dry out the tree canopy, stopping the wet rot from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. When rain softens the topsoil and a heavy fruit bunch weighs down the plant, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ tsii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why do I need to clear the leaves around my yam vines and tie them to wooden tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai abɔle sweet potato wain tso ko he ni mikɛfi tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need tall sticks so their leaves can spread out and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ niji ni kɛlɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my land better for growing maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in root nodules. When these plants die, the stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely hot or when water levels jump suddenly from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant retain its blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ mli shwie shi trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my seeds sprout much faster when planted right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ adu amɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dry seeds are dormant until water softens their outer shell and activates the living plant inside. Planting in moist soil right after early rains gives seeds the exact water and warm soil temperature they need to germinate fast.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehi mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when it rains heavily for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, it cuts off oxygen to the plant, causing soft rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni efo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ. kɛ gangrene baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Should I plant my plantain suckers right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, planting plantain suckers at the start of the rainy season allows their root systems to establish firmly with plenty of soil moisture before the hot, dry season arrives.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in the dry soil and respond instantly to the first moisture. Clearing weeds early protects young crop sprouts from losing sunlight and nutrients to weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ba. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe koni hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa jwɛi lɛ akafite amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry spells as a natural defense mechanism to save water. As soon as the rains return, the plant will shoot out fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the weather gets windy and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during wind and heavy rain. Using strong wooden Y-sticks to prop up fruiting stems keeps the trees standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa ni tamɔ Y tsu nii ni akɛfi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: What causes cassava tubers to turn woody and tough instead of smooth when boiled for fufu?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ahoo amɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil long past its maturity date or exposing it to severe dry weather makes the tubers fibrous and hard, reducing the starch quality needed for making good fufu.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛho be ni esa akɛ ekwɛ lɛ he loo okɛwo shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni amɛhe wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ashikiŋsha ni he hiaa kɛha fɛ̃i kpakpa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I know that my yam tubers under the ground are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: When the yam leaves and vines begin to dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season, it shows the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber and is ready for harvesting.
ga: Beni sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa, ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Is it helpful to heap dry leaves and grass around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Ani eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ mabua baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi abɔle mi plantains lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, this is called mulching. Placing dry organic matter around plantain stems keeps the soil moist, reduces heat on roots, and stops weeds from growing around the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo Plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ shi ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller when I plant it on the exact same farm plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing cassava continuously on the same soil consumes specific nutrients like potassium without giving the soil time to recover. Rotating crops or applying organic manure restores soil power for better yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, ni ahaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do harmful insects appear on my crops right after the new green leaves come out in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Insects are naturally attracted to fresh, tender leaves that shoot up after the first rains because they are soft and rich in sap. Checking under leaves regularly helps you catch and remove pests before they spread.
ga: Kooloi bibii sumɔɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ mliki babaoo Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni ojie amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving plenty of space and time for the cassava to spread its roots and mature later in the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ náa he ko kɛ be babaoo ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni edaa yɛ afi lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Rain alone isn't enough if the soil lacks nutrients, so adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer can help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ pɛ faaa kɛji niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away the top layer of my soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ?

english: You can protect your land by leaving crop leftovers on the ground, planting cover crops like beans, or building small dirt ridges across sloped land. These methods slow down rainwater so it doesn't carry away your fertile soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo afee ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ amli Gbɛi nɛɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɛɛ sũ ni baa nii lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow and green in patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling with patchy yellow spots is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by local extension agents is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or attack by tiny pests like thrips. Watering your plants regularly and keeping pests away will help the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ trukaa hulutsoo be, latsaa ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten spots on the bottom while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants do not get a steady supply of water, making it hard for them to absorb calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps prevent these black spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three good, steady rains rather than planting after the very first light shower. This ensures the soil holds enough moisture so young seeds do not dry out and die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui bibii lɛ egbiɛɛ ni amɛgboii.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops end up fighting for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong stems and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do tiny bugs attack and ruin my maize grains after I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii No hewɔ lɛ, etutua ni ekpãtã mi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo tsu lɛ mli sɛɛ.

english: Weevils and other pests thrive when stored grain still contains moisture or is kept in open sacks. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is hard and storing it in clean, airtight sacks or bins keeps these insects out.
ga: Moths kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli edɔ lolo loo akɛto kotokui ni agbele mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni akɛto kotokui loo ŋmãa ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ohe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why does an agricultural officer need to inspect and map my farm before I plant cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ he mfoniri dani amɛdu kookoo lɛ?

english: Mapping helps measure your land accurately, identify proper soil and drainage areas, and plan the correct spacing so you know exactly how many seedlings to plant for the best harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ he mfonirifeemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni esusuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ. Ni too gbɛ ni sa ni okɛbaadu lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni ole dumɔwui enyiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni esa akɛ odu koni oná kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Cocoa trees need deep, fertile soil that drains water easily and does not stay flooded. An area with good natural shade trees and reliable rainfall is ideal for cocoa.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni nu afuaa lɛ he miihia kokoo tsei. Hei ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ji hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my newly planted cocoa seedlings dying even after the officer said they would do well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso ni midu ehee lɛ gbo beni onukpai lɛ kɛɛ ebaahi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings often die due to transplant shock, direct sunlight without enough shade, lack of rainfall, or root damage that occurred while moving them from the nursery to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ he shoofeemɔ hewɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa, loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni baa beni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa plants thrive while others right next to them in the same farm fail to survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereee lɛ? Okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi.

english: Differences in local soil moisture, uneven shade cover, hidden pests, or slight root damage during planting can cause some cocoa plants to die while neighboring ones stay healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ srɔtoi uneven shade hidden pests Aloo, shishifãi bibii ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei komɛi agboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What signs show that my cocoa seedling is struggling and might not survive?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni ekolɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi?

english: Yellowing leaves, wilting stems, dry brown leaves, and a complete lack of new green shoots are key warnings that your seedling is not getting enough water, shade, or soil nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei ni egbo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi Ni ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ kwraa lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ enaaa nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of year for me to plant my cocoa seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings in Ghana is at the beginning of the major rainy season (around May or June) so the plants get plenty of water to establish strong roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ Ghana ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli. (aaafee May loo June mli) koni tsei lɛ aná nu babaoo koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when planting them on surveyed land?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa seedlings should usually be planted 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) apart to prevent the roots and foliage from competing for sun, water, and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ mitai 3 x 3 (naji 10 x naji 10) koni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Where can I get high-quality cocoa seedlings that are guaranteed to survive well in Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana kookoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana?

english: You can get strong, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings directly from official government nurseries managed by the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) or approved agricultural officers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ ŋmɔji ni Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ loo okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: You can protect young cocoa by planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them, placing dry leaves around the base (mulching) to hold soil moisture, and providing shade.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni ooodu yɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai ni egbi lɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (mulch) koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ni eha hulutsoo.

english: What should I do immediately after planting my cocoa seedlings to help them settle into the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Gently press the soil around the stem to remove air pockets, ensure the seedling is watered if the soil is dry, and confirm that there is shade protecting it from harsh sunlight.
ga: Nyɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ blɛoo koni ojie kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ hulutsoo be ko yɛ ni baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close makes them compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin trees, fewer pods, and a higher risk of diseases spreading between branches.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ŋmeii lɛ faaa, ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ aniji ateŋ lɛ hu feɔ oshara babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees to get extra food while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni maná niyenii krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: It is best to avoid cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots are very aggressive and steal water and nutrients. Plantains or cocoyams are better because they provide shade without suffocating the cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tapioka ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Plantain loo cocoa hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo be ni ehaaa cocoa lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping to the ground without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by intense sun, drought, or lack of soil nutrients. Providing shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is missing essential food nutrients like nitrogen or potassium. Applying the right cocoa fertilizer helps restore the green color and tree strength.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off good branches from my cocoa trees when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso nine kpakpa lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach all branches. This reduces dampness that breeds diseases and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ niji fɛɛ niji ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo aya ŋmɔtɔ ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This rot is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp areas. Weeding your farm and pruning branches helps air dry the pods faster so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya. Fuji lɛ edaaa.

english: Why am I seeing small dark spots and blister marks on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ ahe tsei kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: These spots are caused by pests called mirids or akate that suck the sap out of the tree tissue. If left untreated, they can kill young shoots, so spraying with approved treatment is necessary.
ga: Kooloi awuiyelɔi ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo akate, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli lɛ kɛ hetsemɔi nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbe ŋmeii bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pluck my cocoa pods from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their color completely changes from green to deep yellow, or from red to bright orange. Plucking them green gives poor quality beans, while waiting too long causes beans to sprout inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ etsuru kwraa nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmɔji lɛ, ebaaha kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii aba. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why must I cover my wet cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days instead of putting them straight in the sun to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ haa plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ehi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Fermenting wet beans under leaves creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for. Drying them immediately leaves the beans bitter, purple, and low in market value.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni edɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛjara waaa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: My cocoa farm is over thirty years old and produces very few pods now, so can I make it produce heavily again?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ eye fe afii 30 ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ bianɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ ofee babaoo. Ani manyɛ mafee ekoŋŋ?

english: Old cocoa trees naturally drop in pod production over time. You can revive the farm by cutting back old stems to sprout fresh shoots, grafting high-yield branches, or gradually replanting with improved cocoa varieties.
ga: Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ amli baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei momo ni ooofolɔ koni ekwɛ̃ tsei heei lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli loo fiofio ni akɛ kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baadu ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are wilting because they need water or because they have a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbo ejaakɛ nu he miihia amɛ loo hela ko yɛ amɛhe?

english: If your tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun but recover by the next morning, they are just thirsty. However, if the leaves stay wilted and limp even after heavy watering or overnight, it is usually a sign of bacterial wilt or root disease in the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Shi amɛhe wa amɛ enɔ jetsɛremɔ. Kuma miiye amɛ kɛkɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ nu babaoo loo nyɔɔŋ kome po sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ egbo loo shishifãi hela yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing tiny holes and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Tiny holes and yellowing on young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like fall armyworms or stem borers feeding on the leaves. Inspecting the central whorl of the plant early helps you catch these insects before they damage the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni baa ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ baa. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot, giving roots water for the day. Afternoon watering leaves foliage wet overnight, which encourages fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni shishifãi lɛ aná nu yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: How can I keep the soil around my crops wet for longer during the dry season?
ga: Mafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground and keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing any young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks. Providing shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the tree retain its flowers so they can develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shade kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall with big leaves but not producing any flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ fɔfɔi loo pepper lɛ?

english: When pepper plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or not enough sunlight, they put all their energy into leaf and stem growth instead of flowering. Balancing your soil nutrients and ensuring full sunlight will encourage fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni aaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after several months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni mikɛdu lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and balanced nutrients to expand. If the soil is hard and compacted, or if the plants are crowded too close together, the roots cannot swell properly to form large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ja jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant groundnuts together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is a great practice. Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize and improves your overall harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpaa lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water accumulates around the roots due to poor soil drainage, or when microscopic soil worms called nematodes bore into the tubers, letting fungal rot inside.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbo yɛ mli.

english: What causes the top layer of soil in my farm to become hard like concrete after rain?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard and crusty when heavy rain hits bare ground that lacks organic matter. Adding manure or compost breaks up the hard soil structure, allowing rain and air to penetrate down to the crop roots easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shi oya kɛyaa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop branches keep snapping when the fruits grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miniji niji lɛ yaa nɔ efoɔ lɛ? Beni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: As seeds absorb water, fruits become big and heavy. Without wooden props to support the extra weight, branches will bend and break before you can harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ Yibii lɛ baafee agbo ni etsii. Kɛji tsei ni akɛfiɔ muji ni fa lɛ sɛɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ aniji lɛ baakɔ ni amɛbaakumɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: What should I do when my heavy fruiting plants start bending down to the soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ tso ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ bɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: You should support them with wooden stakes or poles. Propping them up prevents the heavy fruit from pulling the plant down to the ground and breaking the stem.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso loo tso afi esɛɛ. Kɛ́ ofi esɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tso lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni amɛkumɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Is it okay to leave heavy fruit crops to grow without any wooden support?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii akwɛ̃ ni yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ he?

english: No, if you do not support heavy crops with wood, the heavy weight of the water-filled seeds and fruit will cause the branches to fall to the ground and snap.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ okɛ tso fiii ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii sɛɛ. Dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛkumɔ.

english: How does placing wooden sticks under my crops help save my yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafiteɔ?

english: Wooden supports carry the heavy weight of growing fruits, preventing stems from breaking under pressure and keeping the harvest off the bare ground.
ga: Tso ni akɛfee shishitoo lɛ baaye abua aduawai ni miida lɛ ni tsii lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi. kɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni agbele naa lɛ kponɔ

english: Why is it dangerous if my heavy fruits touch the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji mi yibii ni tsii lɛ ta shikpɔŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: When stems break from heavy fruit and lie on the ground, the crop becomes vulnerable to rot, soil pests, and disease before it matures.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ fã kɛjɛ aduawai ni tsii mli ni ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaafite. Kplukai ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ helai dani eda kwraa

english: What causes the seeds inside growing fruits to expand and get so heavy over time?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efeɔ tsiimɔ waa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: As fruits mature, the seeds inside continuously absorb water. This absorption causes the seeds and fruit to swell, making them significantly larger and heavier.
ga: Beni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu be fɛɛ be. Nɛkɛ shwiemɔ nɛɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni kadiɔ mɔ ni edaa ni etsiiɔ.

english: Why do my fruits become much heavier as they get closer to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyibii lɛ miitsii waa beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, the seeds absorb water continuously, causing the crop to gain size and weight as it develops on the branch.
ga: Beni be hoɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmɔɔ nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii yaa hiɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How does water intake affect the physical growth of my crop's seeds?
ga: Te nu ni anuɔ lɛ saa mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ agbɔmɔtsoŋ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water taken up by the plant is absorbed by the seeds inside the fruit, causing them to expand in size and increase the total weight carried by the stem.
ga: Nu ni tso lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmli shwereɔ ni ehaa tsɔne lɛ mli muji fɛɛ ni tsɔne lɛ woɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my tree crops take several years before showing any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi akpo lɛ?

english: Certain tree crops require a long establishment period to build a strong structure. It can take up to 9 years for some crop varieties to mature enough to start flowering.
ga: Tsei komɛi biɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛfee tsɔne ni mli wa. Tsei komɛi baanyɛ ahé afii 9 dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛje fɔfɔii ashishi.

english: Is it normal if my tree crop has not produced flowers after four years of planting?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ wooo fɔfɔi yɛ afii ejwɛ ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, long-term tree crops grow in stages over time. Reaching 4 years is just part of the maturation process, as some trees take up to 9 years to begin flowering.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, afii 4 ni mɔ ko yeɔ lɛ ji tsɔsemɔ nifeemɔ lɛ fã ko kɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei komɛi heɔ afii 9 dani amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi.

english: Why should I bother planting my crops in neat straight lines using a string instead of just scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya haomɔ ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ kɛtsɔ kpã nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ dumɔwui ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every seed gets enough space, water, and sunlight to grow strong. It also makes weeding much easier and prevents you from wasting expensive seeds by overcrowding them.
ga: Dumɔwu ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa gbɛ, nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa, ni ehaaa ofite dumɔwui ni jara wa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ooodu fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: How does marking out straight rows before planting help me when it is time to clear weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi tɛ̃ɛ dani midu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi waa kɛ́ ebashɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Straight lines leave clear, open pathways between your crops. This allows you to walk through and hoe out weeds quickly without accidentally cutting down your young crop seedlings.
ga: Linei ni ja lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni agbele naa yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ mli oya ni otsaa jwɛi ni okɛ otsei bibii lɛ efooo yɛ oshara mli.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in a much smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do some of my tall crops need sticks or stakes to support them while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ niji loo tsei akwɛ mi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ekomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Sticks provide physical support to keep heavy or tall plants upright. This keeps the fruits and leaves off the damp ground, prevents stems from snapping during strong winds, and protects the crop from soil rot.
ga: Tsoi haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ haa tsei ni tsii loo amɛkwɔ lɛ koni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai kɛ baai lɛ akabote he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my corn plants sometimes fall over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Corn plants fall over when the soil around their roots becomes too soft or if they lack sufficient support at the base. Giving them support or mounding soil around their stems keeps them stable during storms.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ebɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ loo muji babaoo ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: How can I stop wasting so many seeds every time I plant a new plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa dumɔwui babaoo ni mifiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu saatso hee lɛ?

english: Instead of throwing seeds by hand, measure exact distances and place seeds carefully along marked lines. This ensures almost every seed matures into a healthy plant without any being wasted.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ onine aaashɛrɛ dumɔwui lɛ Susumɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni akadi lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni fiteɔ.

english: Will planting fewer seeds in a direct line really produce a bigger harvest than scattering a lot of seeds everywhere?
ga: Ani dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, because well-spaced plants receive maximum food and light, allowing them to produce larger and healthier grains or fruits compared to many crowded plants that remain small.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛ woɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto tsei pii ahe lɛ, amɛji bibii lolo.

english: Is it better to plant my rice in structured rows or broadcast the seeds over the mud?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu omɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo aaadu dumɔwui yɛ muji mli?

english: Planting rice in structured rows gives air and light access to the base of every stalk, reduces seed loss, and makes it easier to manage water and weeds, leading to higher yields.
ga: Omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la shɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso shishi. Ehaa dumɔwui ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu kɛ jwɛi akwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo Ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: What is the benefit of planting my crops along furrows in the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Furrows help channel water directly toward the roots of your crops during dry weather while protecting topsoil and young seeds from washing away during heavy downpours.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu yaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho amɛ.

english: How do I know if my growing crops are getting enough sunlight and air movement in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni miduɔ lɛ miiná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your plants have deep green leaves and strong stems without bending toward each other, they are getting good sunlight and airflow—which is achieved by leaving clear gaps between planting rows.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishi ni wa ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Etsɔɔ akɛ nakai tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni aaashi yɛ dumɔwui akui lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do my crops actually absorb the chemical medicine when I spray it onto their leaves?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amli kɛ́ mikɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ?

english: Leaves have tiny, invisible pores called stomata that act like small mouths. When you spray liquid fertilizer or systemic pesticide, the plant absorbs the liquid through these pores and circulates it through its sap to protect or feed the entire plant.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ nɔ ni anaaa lɛ akɛ stomata, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ bibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa Tso lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli ni etsɔɔ mli nu lɛ mli koni ekɛbu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he loo ekɛye nii.

english: If my maize leaves are turning yellow, should I apply fertilizer to the soil or spray liquid medicine directly on the leaves?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mikɛ nu afɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean a nutrient deficiency or root issue. Applying fertilizer to moist soil feeds the roots for long-term growth, while spraying liquid nutrients directly onto leaves gives the plant a quick temporary boost if the roots are struggling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo shishifã he naagba. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ koni amɛdara be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aya hiɛ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together in my sprayer tank to treat weeds and insects at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ afutu mli yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛgbe jwɛi kɛ kooloi bibii yɛ be kome mli?

english: You must be very careful, because mixing certain chemicals can cause a chemical reaction that destroys their effectiveness, burns your crops, or clogs your sprayer. Always check the chemical label or ask an extension officer before combining inputs.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ waa. Ejaakɛ tsofai komɛi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni fiteɔ bɔ ni nitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba. shã oŋmɔshi nibii loo oha tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ atsĩ Be fɛɛ be lɛ kwɛmɔ tsofa ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ loo bi extension nitsulɔi lɛ dani okɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afata he.

english: Why should I destroy tiny insect eggs on my crop leaves if the eggs themselves are not eating my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpãtã kooloi bibii akutsei lɛ ahiɛ lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeee mitsei lɛ?

english: Even though insect eggs do not eat leaves, they hatch into hungry caterpillars or larvae within a few days. Destroying the eggs early stops a large pest population from hatching and destroying your farm before you even notice them.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi akui yeee baai moŋ, Shi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Okpɔŋɔi ni akumɔ mra Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo lɛ naa koni amɛkafɔ ni amɛfite oŋmɔ lɛ dani oyɔse po.

english: How can tiny germs that I cannot see with my eyes cause my whole field of cassava to rot?
ga: tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni hiŋmɛi enaaa lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ agbo?

english: Crop diseases caused by fungi or bacteria spread through microscopic spores carried by wind, rain, or farm tools. Once inside a plant, these tiny germs multiply rapidly, blocking the plant's water pipes and causing leaves or roots to rot.
ga: Tse helai ni fungi loo bacteria kɛbaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ spores bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo okwaayeli nibii kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. kɛji ebote tso lɛ mli helai bibii Enɛɛmɛi miigbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛtsɔ tsei amli nu paipii ni etsiɔ naa ni ehaa baai loo shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do pests keep destroying my crops even after I spray and kill all the adult bugs I can see?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa eshwie kooloi bibii ni eda ni minaa lɛ fɛɛ anɔ ni migbe amɛ moŋ?

english: Adult bugs often lay eggs in the soil or under leaves before they die. When those eggs hatch days later, a new batch of pests emerges. To break the cycle, you need to spray at the correct intervals and clear weeds where eggs and young pests hide.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni eda lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ sũ loo baai ashishi dani amɛgboiɔ. Beni nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii akuu hee ko eba. Bɔni afee ni ofo sɛɛkuu lɛ mli lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni okɛ jwɛi awo hei ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up or droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the harsh sun, stopping water from evaporating too quickly until the cooler evening arrives.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ abɔle tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ baa shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehaa edɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: If a disease attacks my tomato plant, can the plant cure itself and yield good fruit, or must I uproot it?
ga: Kɛji hela ba mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ Ani tomato tsei lɛ baanyɛ atsa amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai? Aloo esa akɛ mafolɔ mli?

english: Plants can recover from mild leaf spots if treated early with proper care. However, if a severe virus or stem wilt infects the plant, it cannot cure itself and should be uprooted immediately to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ mra. Shi, kɛji akɛ hela ko loo stem wilt ni naa wa ko ba tso lɛ nɔ, Enyɛŋ etsa ehe Ni esa akɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying chemical medicine on my vegetables before it is safe to harvest and cook them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ewo aduawai amli sɛɛ dani manyɛ akpa amɛ ni ahoo amɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Every crop chemical has a required Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) printed on the label, usually between 3 to 14 days. Waiting this full period allows the chemical to break down naturally so the crop becomes safe for people to eat.
ga: Esa akɛ tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ aná nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii (PHI) awo nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ. Kɛ́ mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eyiɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni eha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine I am buying from the local market is safe and authentic?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni eji anɔkwale?

english: Always buy crop chemicals from registered agro-dealers in sealed containers with official approval labels, expiry dates, and clear usage instructions. Avoid buying unlabelled chemicals sold in loose plastic bottles.
ga: Hemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli. Eyɛ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ akɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ, gbi ni ebaagbe naa kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni aŋmalako nɔ ko ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ plastic tsinsii ni mli tse mli lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia nearby to shield them, intense sun dries out their delicate leaves, causing them to scorch and drop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be loo glicidia ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, amɛbaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the leaves their dark green color and energy back.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná su ni mli kwɔ ni ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and stop the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus they spread. The insects suck the sap from new leaves, damaging the plant's tissues and causing leaves to twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kplukai nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ. efiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil water levels swing between too dry and too wet. This stress prevents pollination, causing the plant to shed the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Groundnuts have a unique way of reproducing: once the flower is pollinated above ground, it forms a peg that bends downward and buries itself in the dirt, where the pod safe grows into a nut underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa: kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ebaafee tamɔ ŋtayaa ko ni ekoto shi ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Pods ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the surface. When the heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the top becomes heavy, making it easy for wind to uproot them unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi ku we nɛ e kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa ni ejie shishifãi lɛ. ja tso fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in waterlogged soil for too long, oxygen is cut off, causing fungi to multiply and rot the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, afoɔ Oxygen lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam vines produce broad leaves that act like solar panels. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward sunlight, allowing the vine to make maximum food and send energy down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes straight through the heart leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central growing shoot of maize plants. Treating the crop early protects the growing tip so the plant can continue developing normally.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebuɔ tso lɛ naji ahe koni tso lɛ aya nɔ eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field leave the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, that natural food remains in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nakai adebɔɔ niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I plant them in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade during their early years because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shade and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: If I plant my cocoa trees closer together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting trees too close together actually lowers your yield. Overcrowded trees fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, and dense foliage traps humidity that causes fungal diseases to spread fast.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ fiteɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Does it matter if I drop or crack my cocoa pods on the ground while harvesting?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji mikɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko shwie shikpɔŋ loo mifo mli beni mikpaa nii lɛ?

english: Yes, cracked or damaged pods rot quickly and attract insects that ruin the beans inside. Dropping pods on the bare soil also exposes them to dirt and fungal spores that can infect the rest of your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ekumɔ loo efite lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, no hu haa muji kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ atswa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ aná hela.

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their skin changes color completely—usually turning bright yellow or orange, depending on the variety. Leaving pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to start germinating, which ruins their value.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhiɛ etsake su kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. ni haa ejara baa shi lɛ

english: Why should I cut off the thin shoots growing out from the bottom trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk where the pods grow. Removing them forces the tree to direct all its strength into making heavy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni pod lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ lɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to trim branches so sunlight touches the ground under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pruning lets air and sunlight flow through the canopy, which dries out damp leaves and prevents humidity. Fungal diseases thrive in damp, dark trees, so keeping the canopy open keeps the trees healthy.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha baai ni mli efɔ lɛ agbi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Fungal helai shwereɔ yɛ tsei ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe ewo duŋ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ha ŋwɛitsu lɛ agbele koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet conditions. You can reduce it by picking infected pods off the tree immediately and keeping weeds low so moisture doesn't collect.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Obaanyɛ oba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya lɛ nɔ. ni ajie jwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees drying up and showing tiny insect bite marks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ egbi ni kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like mirids (capsids) that suck sap from young shoots and leaves. Spraying approved treatments at the recommended times of year stops them before they destroy your whole crop.
