ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni atsɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa enɛɛmɛi kpaa dani amɛfiteɔ onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why can't I just take fresh cocoa beans straight out of the pod and dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ maŋɔ kookoo ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fresh beans must be fermented under banana leaves for about six days before drying. Fermentation kills the seed germ, stops sprouting, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Esa akɛ atswa ŋmeii heei yɛ banana baai shishi aaafee gbii enumɔ dani amɛgbi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ekpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni mli wa kɛ su ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: How long will my cocoa tree keep producing good pod yields after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii kpakpai beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: With good soil care, pruning, and weed control, a cocoa tree can produce high yields for 25 to 30 years or more, providing long-term income for your family.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cocoa tsei baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. ni haa oweku lɛ náa shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why does rice need so much water to grow compared to other crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in very wet soil because water helps them absorb nutrients efficiently while naturally blocking weeds from growing around them.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ naa. adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa tso

english: Why does my rice crop produce empty or light grains when there is a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko loo amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice needs continuous moisture when forming its flower and filling grains; without enough water, the plant cannot transfer nutrients into the seed head.
ga: Omɔ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ ewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmaa lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ awo dumɔwu lɛ yitso mli.

english: Can I grow rice on high, dry land where water does not collect?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni egbi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu ato nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant specific upland rice varieties that are bred to grow on dry land relying only on regular rainfall, unlike lowland rice which needs flooded fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa ni he hiaa nu afua lɛ he.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land can hold enough water for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaadu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Squeeze a handful of moist soil into a ball; if it holds together firmly like clay, it retains water well, but if it falls apart easily like sand, water will drain away too fast.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛ́ ekpɛtɛ ehe kpɛŋŋ tamɔ sũ lɛ, enyɛɔ emɔɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji efo oya tamɔ ŋã lɛ, nu lɛ baaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when the weather stays dry for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When the soil dries out, crop roots lose the ability to draw up essential plant food like nitrogen, causing the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛjie tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ ehiɛ su eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if rain stops completely for two weeks right after planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa kwraa otsii enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young plants will stall in growth and roll up their leaves to save moisture, and without water, their young root systems cannot expand to keep them alive.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baakpa amɛdalɛ ni amɛbaabɔle amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni kɛji nu bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli koni ehi shi.

english: How does digging small dirt mounds or bunds around my farm help my crops during rain shortages?
ga: Muji bibioo ko loo muji ni abua naa. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ mli tsɔne lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Bunds act as low walls that trap rainwater inside your field, giving the water time to sink deep into the soil where crop roots can reach it during dry days.
ga: Bund tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni yɔɔ shishi ni ŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ naa be ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he yɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: How can covering the ground around my crops with dry grass help them survive hot days?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which shades the dirt from direct sunlight and stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: What is the best time of day to hand-water my crops during a water shortage?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni nu faaa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives plants time to soak up moisture before the hot afternoon sun can evaporate it away.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to germinate when I plant them in dry soil during a warm month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seeds need constant moisture to soften their hard outer shells and trigger growth; if dry soil steals that moisture, the seed remains asleep or dies.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ awa ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ ejuɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baawɔ loo amɛbaagboi.

english: How many years will it take for my new coconut trees to start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties can start producing fruit in about 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties usually take between 6 to 8 years before you see your first harvest.
ga: Dwarf ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ fɔɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani ona oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave big spaces between my coconut seedlings when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ agbo yɛ ŋmeii tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need plenty of room because their roots spread far and wide, and their leaves need maximum sunlight. Spacing them about 7 to 8 meters apart prevents them from fighting each other for nutrients, water, and light.
ga: He ko babaoo he miihia ŋmei tsei ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni amɛbaai lɛ he hiaa hulu la fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 8 yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye niyenii, nu kɛ la he akaŋshii.

english: How do I pick good coconut seedlings that will give me high yield in the future?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso kpakpa ni baawo yibii babaoo wɔsɛɛ?

english: Choose seedlings that are 6 to 12 months old with thick stems, dark green healthy leaves, and quick germination traits from a certified nursery. Avoid thin, pale, or weak-looking sprouts.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni eye nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 12 ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse. Baai lɛ ahe wa, eŋɔli diŋŋ. ni eyɛ sui ni haa kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ni tamɔ nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Do coconut trees only grow along the coast, or can I plant them inland on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋshɔ lɛ naa pɛ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ loo manyɛ madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: While coconuts are common near beaches, they grow well inland as long as the soil drains water easily, gets good rainfall, and receives full sunlight throughout the day.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ afɔɔ ŋshɔnaa ŋmeii anaa moŋ, shi ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo. nine shɛɔ nugbɔ kpakpa nɔ ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: What type of soil is best for growing healthy coconut trees?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Coconuts thrive best in deep, loose, sandy-loam soils. They do not like heavy clay soils where water stands for days, because standing water rots their roots.
ga: Kokooi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛsumɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii, ni nu hiɔ mli gbii babaoo lɛ. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Can I grow crops like cassava or maize under my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tso bibioo ko shishi?

english: Yes, while the coconut trees are young and small, you can intercrop them with short-term crops like cassava, maize, or legumes. This helps you earn income from the land before the trees start producing nuts.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ji gbekɛ ni eyɛ bibioo moŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa adu lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi.

english: Will planting food crops between my coconut trees take away all the nutrients from the soil?
ga: Ani niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: As long as you leave enough clear space right around the base of the young coconut trees and apply manure or fertilizer, intercropping actually helps keep weeds down and improves the soil.
ga: Shii abɔ ni obaashi he ko yɛ ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ shishi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ baaye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young coconut trees turning yellow and dropping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the tree lacks key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that it is going through dry stress during long heat spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my coconut trees dropping off before fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ akokoo tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Coconut flowers drop early mainly due to severe dry weather, poor soil fertility, or attacks by small sucking insects that damage the delicate blossoms.
ga: Kokoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii Aloo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ.

english: What is making big holes in the leaves of my coconut trees and how does it hurt the crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo baa lɛ mli lɛ baa? Ni te eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Those holes are caused by the Rhinoceros Beetle, which bores into the growing center of the tree. It damages young fronds before they open and can stunt or kill the tree if left untreated.
ga: Rhinoceros ŋmeii ni boteɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu lɛ. Efiteɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How long should I expect my vegetable crops to grow before they start producing full-sized produce?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃ dani amɛje ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ shishi?

english: Most vegetable crops take several weeks to mature. For instance, crops like peppers or tomatoes often require around 18 to 20 weeks of vegetative growth before they reach their peak phase for producing high-quality, full-sized fruits.
ga: Aduawai babaoo heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii 18 kɛyashi 20 ni tsei lɛ adara dani eshɛɔ yibii ni dalɛ fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why aren't my garden egg plants growing major fruits during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo eyibii titrii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops spend their initial weeks building a strong root system and leaves. Major fruit growth only begins after the plant matures to the proper age, so patience is necessary while it reaches that stage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ dani amɛdaraa. Koni ama shishifã kɛ baa gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa Yibii titri lɛ dalɛ jeɔ shishi beni tso lɛ eshɛ afii ni sa lɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsuishitoo he miihia kɛ́ eba nakai fã lɛ he.

english: Why is my cassava crop taking many months before the underground tubers start swelling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava focuses its early energy on leaf and stem growth. The tubers only begin to rapidly swell and reach their peak size in the later stages of the crop's growth cycle.
ga: Cassava kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ mra. Tubers lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfuɔ oya ni amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do young pepper fruits stay very small for a while before suddenly becoming big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yibii bibii lɛ hiɔ shi bibii be fioo dani amɛdaraa trukaa lɛ?

english: Young fruits go through an initial establishment phase where internal cells form. Once this phase passes, the fruit enters a rapid expansion period where it expands significantly toward its full peak size.
ga: Yibii bibii tsɔɔ shishijee gbɛ ko mli ni mligbɛ wala yibii lɛ feɔ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ be nɛɛ ho lɛ, aduawai lɛ boteɔ be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo kɛyashɛɔ elɛɛmɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my maize cobs have reached their peak size for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-abɛi lɛ eshɛ ŋmaakpamɔ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Maize cobs reach their maximum size and quality when the silks dry out completely and turn dark brown, and the kernels inside are fully formed and firm.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhilɛ-kɛhamɔ ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ he beni siliki ŋmeii lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni eye emuu ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it normal for young watermelons to look tiny at first and then grow rapidly in size later?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ watermelon bibii baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii yɛ shishijee mli? Ni ani ebaada oya yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, watermelon growth starts slowly while the fruit develops internally, followed by a sudden growth surge where the fruit expands dramatically until it reaches full maturity.
ga: Hɛɛ, watermelon dalɛ jeɔ shishi fiofio. Beni aduawai lɛ daa yɛ mli lɛ Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya. he ni aduawai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ waa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa kwraa lɛ

english: Will I lose yield if I harvest my crops early when the fruits are still small?
ga: Ani yibiiwoo lɛ baafite kɛji mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra be mli ni eyɛ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting early prevents crops from reaching their peak weight and size. Allowing the crop to complete its natural growing period ensures maximum yield and profit.
ga: Hɛɛ, kpamɔ mra. Ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekashɛ etsitsinɔnii kɛ elɛɛmɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛnáa amɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni aná yibii babaoo kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo.

english: What happens to the size of my fruits if the crop does not get enough water while swelling?
ga: Mɛni baa mi aduawai lɛ adalɛ nɔ kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni efuu lɛ?

english: Water is critical during the fruit expansion stage. A lack of moisture when fruits are growing will stunt their growth, leaving you with small, undersized produce.
ga: Nu he hiaa yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nu bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ, ebaaha egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa onáa yibii bibioo, bibioo.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so my crops grow to their maximum size?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛdara kɛyashɛ he ni amɛdara fe fɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied early in the growth cycle to build strong plants, followed by targeted feeding right before the flowering and fruiting stage to support rapid fruit expansion.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli koni ekɛfee tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ dani fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ baa koni eye ebua yibii lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ oya.

english: Is it true that if my crop flowers very early, it means I will get a bigger harvest sooner?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ oya waa? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ maná nibii babaoo oya?

english: No, early flowering does not mean a bigger harvest. If a plant flowers before it is mature enough, it lacks the strength to grow large fruits, resulting in smaller overall yields.
ga: Dabi, fɔfɔi ni baa mra lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo. Kɛji tso lɛ fɔ fɔfɔi dani eda kwraa lɛ, ebaanaŋ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ aduawai wuji ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ, nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning brown in the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shield them from the sun while their roots establish.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa lɛ.

english: Which suckers should I cut away from my plantain plants to make sure I get big fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ mi plantain tso lɛ mli koni maná aduawai babaoo?

english: You should remove thin, leafy water suckers and leave only one or two strong sword suckers alongside the main mother plant so the soil nutrients go directly into fruit production.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie nu mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya aduawai afeemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants have ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying early with recommended treatments stops the pests before they eat the center growing point of the maize plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ mra lɛ ji tsofafeemɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kpaa dani amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize grow mold and spoil quickly after I store it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni efiteɔ beni mikɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in bags if it is bagged before it is fully dried. High moisture inside the grain creates a damp environment where mold and insects multiply rapidly.
ga: Abele fiteɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baagbɛ amɛshwã oya lɛ

english: When should I put fertilizer on my maize field so that it works best for the crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer twice: a small starter application about two weeks after planting when leaves appear, and a second application when the maize reaches knee height.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ: Okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fioo awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ tsitsi nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Select mature stems from healthy plants that are 8 to 18 months old, making sure to avoid stems that are dried out, insect-damaged, or too soft.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ amli, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni egbi lɛ ahe. Afiteɔ kooloi bibii. loo eyɛ blɛoo tsɔ

english: Groundnuts work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds compete with your crops for space, sunshine, water, and soil nutrients, taking food away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni oooŋɔ kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ fɔmɔ nii lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my newly transplanted pepper seedlings need so much more water than my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo fe mi-tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tiny, shallow roots that cannot reach deep groundwater yet, making them dry out and die very quickly under the hot sun if their soil isn't kept constantly wet.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my young crops too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mitsei bibii lɛ loo mihaaa amɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellowing leaves and soft, muddy soil usually mean you are giving them too much water, while droopy leaves that feel dry and crisp mean the plant is thirsty and needs more moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ooha lɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi ni nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni ehe miihia ni ená ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why is it better to pour water directly around the stem of my crop instead of splashing it over all the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu kɛbɔle he lɛ? mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Yɛ nu ni oooshwie baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Plants drink water through their roots in the soil, and leaving wet water on leaves under warm weather can invite crop diseases and leaf spots.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Ni nu ni mli efɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ baai anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants look weak and droopy right after I move them from the nursery bed into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you move young plants, their tender roots get disturbed and temporarily lose the ability to drink water properly, causing a short period of stress called transplant shock.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi tso bibioo ko Amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ.

english: What time of day is best for me to transfer my young seedlings into the main farm field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Late afternoon or early evening is the best time because the cooler air gives the seedlings all night to rest and recover without strong midday sun burning them.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛhe waaa gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shãaa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to cover my nursery bed with palm fronds before my young seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu ŋmei tsei dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Palm fronds act as a shield that protects delicate young seeds from direct heavy rainfall washing them away and intense sunshine drying out the topsoil.
ga: Palm baai tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shwieɔ amɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ he.

english: Should I put chemical fertilizer into the soil on the exact day I plant my new seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afata he yɛ gbi ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ nɔ?

english: No, it is better to wait a week or two until the roots settle, because strong fertilizer applied immediately can burn the delicate roots of fresh seedlings.
ga: Dabi, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aaahi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui heei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds away from my young cassava plants as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ amli kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal the water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil before your young cassava gets strong enough to feed itself.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani o-yucca bibioo lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ ehe.

english: When planted too close, maize crops fight each other for sunlight and soil food, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi baatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I lay dry grass or leaves on the soil around the base of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil, keeping it cool, trapping moisture so it doesn't dry out fast in the sun, and blocking weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Digging for gold washes mud and toxic chemicals into your soil. This chokes the roots of your crops, stopping them from drinking water and taking in nutrients to stay green and healthy.
ga: Shika tsuru ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ muji kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee bibioo. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkanu nu ni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi akɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why won't my maize grow on parts of my land where the top layer of dirt was scraped away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni ajie muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top layer of dirt, called topsoil, holds almost all the food and natural manure plants need to grow. Without it, crop roots are trapped in deep, hard subsoil that lacks nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akɛ topsoil. Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ ateŋ babaoo toɔ. Eji ebɛ kulɛ, tsei ashishifãi baakã shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni mli kwɔ, ni wa, ni niyenii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops refuse to root deeply in areas where heavy earth-moving machines have passed through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpooɔ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi yɛ hei ni tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery squashes the dirt so tightly together that it turns hard like concrete. Soft, young crop roots cannot push through hard soil to reach water deep underground.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ muji lɛ nɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa tamɔ kɔnkrit. Tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees dry up when thick dust from land clearing settles on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ egbi yɛ be mli ni sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ amɛhe ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves need sunlight and fresh air to make food for the plant. Thick dust acts like a blanket over the leaves, blocking sunlight and clogging the tiny breathing holes of the plant.
ga: Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he hiaa baai koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Muji ni mli tse lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa baai lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni etsiɔ tso lɛ mumɔ bu bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well when I water them with muddy river water from nearby digging sites?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ shika tsuru jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ wo amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Muddy water contains thick silt that coats root tips and seals the soil surface, preventing air and clean water from reaching the plant roots.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli sũ ni mli edɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he tse kɛ nu naa koni ekashɛ tso shishifãi ahe.

english: Why does water collect and rot my cassava crops whenever nearby land is cleared and dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni efiteɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be ni abaakumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ajie lɛ?

english: Digging deep pits and clearing trees destroys the land's natural water drainage. Rainwater gets trapped on your farm, leaving cassava roots soaked in standing water until they rot.
ga: Bu ni mli kwɔ ni atsaa kɛ tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ nu ni ekpɛtɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he Okɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ awo nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaagboi.

english: Is there a crop or tree I can plant around my farm boundaries to protect my land from illegal intruders?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ jɛmɛ? Ani miŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛbuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Planting permanent crops like oil palm, cocoa, or dense citrus trees marks your land boundary clearly and creates a natural barrier that shows the land is actively owned and protected.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa tamɔ oil palm, cocoa loo citrus tsei ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ kadiɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ faŋŋ. ni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbogbo ni tsɔɔ akɛ abuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔyeli kɛ hebuu akɛ nɔ ko ni he hiaa waa.

english: Can I plant anything on land that was dug up and left damaged to make the soil good for crops again?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ ni ashi lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ?

english: Planting cover crops like velvet bean or cowpea helps restore damaged land. Their leaves cover the bare ground to prevent washing, and their roots trap nitrogen to make the soil fertile again.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ velvet beans loo cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Amɛbaai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ koni nu lɛ akaho. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ekoŋŋ.

english: If toxic chemical waste from gold digging gets into my soil, will it affect the food I harvest?
ga: Kɛ tsofai fɔji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaana niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, crop roots suck up dirty water from polluted soil, passing harmful chemicals into tubers like yam and cassava, which can make the harvest unsafe to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei shishifãi shwieɔ nu ni mli ewo muji kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui amaje ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmaa lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii.

english: How can working with an agricultural extension officer help protect my crops from land destroyers?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ lɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Agricultural officers can inspect your farm, officially document your healthy crop growth, and connect you with local authorities to defend your land against illegal destruction.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi baanyɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni ekɛ bo kɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ abɔ koni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. The plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to fuel new growth at the top, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-composted manure will help restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha dalɛ hee aba yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same field help my next crop grow better without adding extra fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi fataaa he?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that gather nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot in the field, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei ko ni buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli bibii amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers in the dry season before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers to conserve water and protect themselves when stressed by excessive heat and direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade trees like plantains and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfee pods.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting under the ground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare main stem, and the soil surrounding the stem starts to swell and crack from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efuɔ ni ejaraa kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow forces them to compete with the mother plant for nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one small replacement sucker ensures all energy goes into producing large fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ yibii titri kome pɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I train them onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food through photosynthesis. It also keeps the leaves dry and away from damp soil diseases, directing more energy into growing big tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Ehaa tsei feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu mli egbiɔ ni helai kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa akɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes the central leaves of my young maize plants to look chewed up with dark dust inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ sũ ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides inside the central leaf whorl to eat fresh foliage. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract directly into the central funnel early in the morning helps destroy the pests.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai heei. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from young leaves and spread viruses. Spraying the underside of leaves with soapy water or neem oil controls these insects and stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch during the continuous rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a soil fungus that multiplies in high humidity, heavy shade, and excessive moisture. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air circulate through the canopy keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, ni hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ nɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry up and become sterile, which prevents pollination and causes the unfertilized flowers to fall off. Mulching the soil with dried grass keeps the roots cool and helps the plant retain flowers during hot periods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ akafee nɔ ko, ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mulching ni egbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a large crop one year but very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees experience natural yield cycles. A heavy harvest drains the tree's stored nutrients, so it spends the following season rebuilding its energy in its branches and leaves before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni efeɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo. Nikpamɔ ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ eheɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani eniji kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ehee dani ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree drop off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction are pollinated by tiny insects called midge flies. Flowers that are not pollinated, or that the tree cannot support due to limited water and nutrients, naturally fall off.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ pollin lɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ midge ŋmeii. Anyɛɛɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi loo tsei ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Excessive shade and poor drainage make it easier for the fungus to jump from the soil or neighboring trees onto your pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shade babaoo kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha efee mlɛo aha ŋmei lɛ akɛ ebaatu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Too much trapped water suffocates the roots, making it impossible for the tree to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni emɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is completely mature and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Mature pods change color: green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting them at full maturity ensures the beans inside are fully developed in size and weight.
ga: Pods ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ su: pods eŋɔli tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daraa yɛ dalɛ kɛ mujiwoo mli.

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the seeds inside to begin germinating or growing roots, which ruins the beans for sale. Overripe pods are also more likely to attract pests and rot.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛná shishifãi. Enɛ baafite ŋmeii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Shedding leaves is a cocoa tree's natural defense mechanism against drought. By dropping leaves, the tree reduces water evaporation through its foliage, helping it survive until rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do insects seem to damage my young cocoa pods more during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pests like mirids (capsids) breed heavily right after rainy periods when new foliage and young pods grow. They attack during these specific growth windows because young pods have soft skins that are easy to pierce for sap.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ fɔɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei komɛi asɛɛ. Kɛ baai heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dara lɛ Amɛtutuaa yɛ nɛkɛ dalɛ samfɛji pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ amli ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ewaaa akɛ aaatsɔ mli koni ana nu.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees yielding smaller pods than when the farm was young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal sap transport slows down, and the surrounding soil becomes depleted of nutrients. Older trees require pruning or soil enrichment to maintain good pod size.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, emli nu lɛ ni ekɛyaa lɛ baa shi. ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei ni edara lɛ ahe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ loo atsake amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛpod lɛ dalɛ ni sa mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if I want more pods to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji krokomɛi kɛji miisumɔ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches that steal water and nutrients from the main trunk. Opening up the tree leaves room for sunlight and airflow, which reduces dampness and encourages more flower production.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele tsei lɛ anaa lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa fɔfɔi babaoo baa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow primarily due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen acts like food that leaves need to stay green and produce good corn, so adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni ehe hiaa ni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa kpakpa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmei ni tsuɔ waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong stems and big produce.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist for their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long, hot dry spell. Seeds that sprout after this single rain will quickly dry up and die before the full rainy season actually sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry leaves help them survive heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. This stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps crop roots cool during dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that crawls deep inside the center of young maize plants to eat soft new leaves, which slows down the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical pest killers when my crops are full of flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals during flowering kills useful insects like bees and tiny midges. These insects carry pollen from flower to flower, which is necessary for crops to form fruits, pods, and seeds.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. Kooloi bibii nɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Amɛ he hia koni ŋmɔshi nibii afee aduawai, pods, kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why do the flowers on my vegetable plants drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Crop flowers drop off without making fruit when plants experience extreme heat stress, lack sufficient water, or when there are no friendly insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tso lɛ fɔfɔi baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni feɔ naanyo bɛ he fɛɛ he. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stalk, and when the ground directly around the base of the plant starts cracking open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tso lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ. Ni beni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out in direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make plenty of food, which travels down to make big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛbaa lɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stalks down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants undergo a natural process called geocarpy. After the flowers are pollinated above ground, the stem elongates into a 'peg' and burrows into the soil so the pods can develop and mature safely underground away from heat and direct sunlight.
ga: Peanut tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ geocarpy lɛ mli. Beni atswa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ‘pins’ ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are some of my harvested groundnut shells completely empty inside when I open them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ migbele ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ, nɔ ko bɛ mli kwraa lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, commonly called 'pops,' usually happen when the soil lacks sufficient calcium or moisture while the pod is forming. Without enough calcium, the plant forms the outer shell but fails to develop the seed inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni afɔɔ amɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ ‘pea pods’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ. Kɛji calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee mligbɛ dumɔwui.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are ready to harvest without pulling up my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mijieee he ni miyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli?

english: You can check maturity by observing the leaves turning yellow and shedding. Dig up two or three sample plants across the farm and scratch the inside of the pods; if the inner pod lining is dark brown or black, the crop is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli abɔ he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant groundnuts on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Replanting groundnuts in the same field continuously allows soil-borne diseases (like leaf spot and collar rot) and pests to build up in the soil. Rotating groundnuts with cereal crops like maize breaks the pest cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa (tamɔ baa mli ŋmeii kɛ kɔla mli ŋmeii) kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Rotating peanuts with cereal crops like corn stops the pest cycle and helps keep the soil healthy.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start producing pods, and at what age does production reach its peak?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii? Ni mɛɛ afii amli nibii ni anáa lɛ baashɛ he ni fe fɛɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties begin bearing pods around 2 to 3 years after planting. Production gradually increases and reaches its peak yield when the trees are between 10 and 15 years old, after which old trees may need rehabilitation.
ga: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties begin to produce pods approximately 2 to 3 years after planting. Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ yaa nɔ fiofio. It increases and reaches its peak when the tree is between 10 and 15 years old. After that time, old trees may need to be rejuvenated.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field where I am setting up new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-plantains lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui heei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch in direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leafy shade to shelter the young cocoa, while also providing food and cash income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hottest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to defend against extreme heat and drought. Closing the leaf surface reduces water loss through evaporation, helping the plant conserve moisture until temperatures drop.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ agbe baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when exposed to environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do weeds stop growing fast once my cowpea crop spreads across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kpaɔ oya beni mi-cowpea lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea spreads wide to form a thick, low canopy. This dense layer of leaves shades the ground, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds in the soil so they cannot germinate or grow.
ga: Cowpea gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo aahu kɛyashiɔ efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kuku ni mli wa. Nɛkɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ loo eda.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining very small and thin even though the leaves above ground look very bushy and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛkwɔ waa moŋ, shi.

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and branches instead of sending nutrients down to swell the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Plants use all of their energy to grow taller leaves and branches. Instead, nutrients are sent down to allow the tubers to expand.

english: When maize turns yellow starting from the bottom leaves, it is usually hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves the limited food it has to the newest growth at the top, leaving the older leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: When corn turns yellow from the lower leaves Often hungry for nitrogen The plant moves the limited food to the newest growth above. Ha baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on the same land before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that grab plant food (nitrogen) directly out of the air and feed it into the dirt. When you harvest groundnuts, they leave that rich plant food behind in the soil, which helps your maize grow strong without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii Eshiɔ nakai tso niyenii ni jara wa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Dropping leaves is a survival trick cocoa trees use when water is scarce. Leaves lose moisture into the dry air, so the tree sheds them to lock in whatever water is left inside its trunk until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala ni cacao tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ nu faaa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ yaafo koni amɛhiɛ nu ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛtsei lɛ amli lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat can make the pollen inside tomato flowers dry out and die before it can form a fruit. When the flower realizes it cannot produce a tomato, it sheds the flower to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi ni egbo dani ewo yibii. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ le akɛ enyɛŋ ewo tomato Ebaashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my plantain stand fall over so easily after a storm, even when the stem does not break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ko sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ efoko po?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots that stay close to the top of the soil. When the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, and wet soil allows the shallow roots to get pulled right out of the ground during high winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaye abua shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli

english: Why do my corn stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the corn plants fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch as high as they can to catch sunlight, leaving them with no leftover energy to build big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Abɛi tsei wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee shɔŋŋ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛná hewalɛ ko kwraa ni amɛkɛbaatswa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛ tsei kakadaji ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei amli koni makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves using sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which results in much bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da kwraa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, aggressive root systems that suck up water and fertilizer much faster than cultivated crops can. If weeds are present when you apply fertilizer, they will eat the food first and outgrow your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaaye klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are small worms suddenly eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. The adult moths lay hundreds of eggs on young maize leaves right as the season starts, and the tiny caterpillars crawl straight into the central whorl of the leaf because it is tender and easy to eat.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Kpɔŋɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmeii baai bibii anɔ kɛji be lɛ je shishi pɛ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Efoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rains flood the soil for days, water fills all the air gaps, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Do plantain trees actually get sick with diseases like other crops, or do they just die on their own?
ga: Ani plantains baanyɛ aná hela diɛŋtsɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi loo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgboiɔ?

english: Plantains do get diseases and pest attacks, such as fungal leaf spots and root worms. When a plantain looks weak or dies early, it is usually suffering from a pest or disease problem rather than natural aging.
ga: Helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ plantains tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shishifã mli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ plantains tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egboi oya Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe naagbai yeɔ amɛ awui moŋ fe adebɔɔ mli dalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and dropping before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean your plantain is stressed, often due to lack of soil nutrients, poor watering, or fungal disease. Clearing competing weeds and adding animal manure around the base helps the plant stay healthy and green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-plantain lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. nu ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ hela Jiemɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ aya hiɛ. Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: How do weeds growing close to the base of my plantain trees hurt my harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from the roots of your plantain. If weeds overgrow the base, the plantain cannot feed properly, resulting in small bunches or complete crop failure.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ Plantains nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa kuu bibioo ko. loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my crops to get a good yield?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Weeds should be cleared regularly, especially during the early stages after planting. Keeping the area around the plant base clean every few weeks prevents weeds from choking young roots and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa. Titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tso fɛɛ shishitoo he tse. Otsii fioo komɛi baatsi jwɛi lɛ naa koni ekafo shishifãi bibii lɛ amli ni eju tso lɛ mli niyenii.

english: Is it true that I can just plant my plantain suckers and leave them until harvest time?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni mashi kɛyashi kpamɔ be?

english: No, plantains require continuous care to produce well. Neglecting your field right after planting allows weeds and pests to overwhelm the young plants, leading to poor growth and very low yields.
ga: Dabi, plantains biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kunim. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers in a bush that hasn't been properly cleared?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ jwɛi ni ajieee mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Planting in an uncleared field forces young plantains to fight heavy weed cover for sunlight and nutrients right away. Clearing the land thoroughly before planting gives root suckers the best chance to establish strong growth.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui bibii anɔ koni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni nuɔ nii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my plantain stalks remaining very thin and refusing to produce big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tse waa ni amɛkpooɔ akɛ amɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Thin stalks and small bunches usually happen when the plantain's roots are choked by dense weeds, damaged by soil pests, or lacking food from poor quality soil.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tseee kɛ ŋmeii bibii Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ jwɛi ni mli ewo muji ehà plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo niyenii ni bɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ efite

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests after I farm on the same piece of land for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nii lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without breaks or nourishment tires out the soil by consuming all its natural food. Tired soil lacks the nutrients needed to support heavy crop growth until it is rested or given nutrients.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii fɛɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ nɔ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii lɛ akwɛmɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni anáa hejɔɔmɔ loo niyenii.

english: How can I revive tired farm soil so my plantains can grow big bunches again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ koni mi plantains lɛ akwɛ̃ jwɛi wuji ekoŋŋ?

english: You can revive tired soil by applying compost or animal manure, practicing crop rotation, or leaving the land to rest for a season so organic matter can naturally build back up.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni etɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ Aloo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be kome bɔni afee ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anyɛ ama amɛhe shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Should I leave cut weeds and plant leaves on the ground around my plantain stems after clearing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni madu baai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? Ani mi plantain tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cut weeds and plant waste as organic mulch around the base protects the soil from drying out under the sun and slowly rots down to feed fresh nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni ashiɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi akɛ organic mulch ni ebɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii heei aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture, acting as a natural umbrella while the cocoa tree establishes its root system.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni cacao tso lɛ maa eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Raising the leaves off the ground allows them to catch more sunlight to make food, while also keeping the leaves dry and away from soil-borne diseases, which leads to bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhooɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ kpaaa gbee. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism for cassava during dry periods. By losing its leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration, preserving water in the stem and root until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala yɛ ŋmei be mli. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaje ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbuɔ nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my maize crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely hardy and rest in the topsoil ready to germinate instantly at the first drop of rain. Early clearing gives your planted crops a fair start to get sunlight and nutrients before weeds overcrowd them.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa onibii ni odu lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli dani jwɛi lɛ feɔ tsɔ.

english: What happens if I plant three or four corn seeds together in one small hole instead of spacing them out?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo ko mli? Bu kome moŋ fe ni amɛaajɛ amɛhe

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot causes the young plants to fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and small or incomplete corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help the maize I plan to plant next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food stored in their root nodules. When the plants decay, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei lɛ fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green pepper plants curling upward and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso eŋɔli lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses spread by them. These insects drain nutrients from the young leaves, causing them to distort and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ srɔtoi ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: What causes tiny holes and saw-dust-like powder inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides inside the young leaf funnel (the whorl) to feed on the tender growing tip of the maize plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli (whorls) koni amɛye ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Blossom End Rot. It is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering patterns where the soil dries out completely between waterings.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Blossom End Rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to plant vegetables without using expensive testing equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai ni mikɛ kaa nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hands, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and contains signs of living organisms like earthworms and decaying leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli ni wala he okadii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting plantain or shade trees alongside cocoa gives them shelter and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
