ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ toi bibii waa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room and food to grow thick stalks and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the funnel of young maize plants. Checking your fields early and applying recommended control methods like neem extracts or approved sprays can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ he tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for too long in poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the specific nutrients that crop uses without giving the soil time to recover. Rotating different crops, such as alternating maize with beans or groundnuts, helps restore soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hoɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to water my tomato plants early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning prepares the plant for the heat of the day. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly before roots can soak it up, and wet leaves under direct heat can easily get scorched or diseased.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni esaa tso lɛ kɛha gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni baai ni efɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo hela aba amɛ oya.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are adapted to absorb water and soil food much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and nutrients away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. When vines trail on the shaded ground, they produce smaller tuber yields and are more exposed to diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ wain tsei nyiɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: It is best to wait until rains become steady rather than planting after the very first rain. Planting after two or three good rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to sprout without drying out during sudden dry spells.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees during their early years to protect their delicate leaves and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can be weakened by underground pests like nematodes or stem borers. Supporting the fruiting stems with strong wooden props and keeping the soil healthy prevents the heavy stems from uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Fi yibiiwoo tsei lɛ asɛɛ kɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei ni tsii lɛ akaje shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs high amounts of nitrogen to grow green and strong, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni efee hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How can I keep my soil moist for longer during the hot dry spells between rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dried grass, leaves, or crop residues—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛwoɔ ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: What is causing small green caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center (funnel) of maize plants. Checking crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or ash mixtures into the funnel saves the young crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ he (channel) lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo ashwishwɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nibii bibii ni adu lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing sticky yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and sticky spots are common symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, often spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ enɛ amɛshwãa. Kasava henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with very small or missing ears. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi náa toi bibii waa loo toi ni bɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes for their vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and protecting leaves from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Maintaining consistent soil moisture through regular watering and mulching helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants do not like harsh, direct sunlight because their roots are small and cannot absorb water fast enough to cool the leaves. Planting plantains or shade trees beside young cocoa gives them living umbrellas that keep the ground cool and protect the leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ akashã.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily as soon as the heavy fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep woody roots like big timber trees; their roots stay close to the top of the soil. When the heavy fruit bunch forms, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds or soft wet soil can pull the roots out unless you prop the stem up with sturdy wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei wuji. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ni tsii fee Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ. Ja okɛ tso ni wa wo tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight and stretch upwards as fast as possible to beat their neighbors. Because all their energy goes into growing tall to catch light, they do not have enough energy left over to develop thick stems or produce fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim. Yɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ amɛdara koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee tsei ni mli tse loo amɛwo yibii.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow from the tip down the center, it means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize uses to build green leaves. To protect its new growth, the maize plant takes nitrogen from its oldest leaves at the bottom and sends it to the young leaves at the top.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ebaai eŋɔlii lɛ. koni ekɛtsi dalɛ hee naa Abɛi tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpea on my land make the maize I plant next season grow so much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea and other leguminous plants have special bumps on their roots that trap natural plant food from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea crop finishes and its roots decay in the ground, that trapped food stays behind to feed the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ayɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsina ŋmeii agbe naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do many of the tiny green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ babaoo etsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani amɛdara lɛ.

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt, and it happens when the cocoa tree realizes it has produced more pods than it can afford to feed with available water and nutrients. The tree deliberately stops feeding the extra tiny pods so it can focus its energy on successfully ripening the remaining healthy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt ni ebaa beni cacao tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ aye abua lɛ. Tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekpa ŋmeii bibii lɛ niyenii. fã ni eshwɛ lɛ koni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime heat gets too intense or when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to wet. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower so it cannot fertilize, causing the plant to drop the useless flowers to conserve moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛŋ ewo fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How does the cassava plant know when to swell its roots underground instead of growing more leaves on top?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ko leɔ be ni esa akɛ ekwɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ baai babaoo?

english: Cassava leaves manufacture food from sunlight and send the extra food down to store in the root tubers. When the plant reaches a few months old and gets good sunlight, it naturally shifts energy from making upper leaves to pumping nutrients down into the ground to expand the roots.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛto. Beni tsei lɛ eye nyɔji fioo ni amɛnáa hulu la kpakpa. Etsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ afeemɔ mli kɛyaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. As these pests suck the sap out of the young leaf tissues, the leaves grow unevenly and twist upward.
ga: Leaf curling on pepper plants is often caused by small sucking pests such as thrips or aphids hiding on the underside of the leaves. or by viruses carried by insects This is because these pests suck the sap from young leaf tissue. No sɛɛ lɛ, baai lɛ daaa ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops turn pale green and stop growing whenever wild weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni koo mli jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems and grow faster than farm crops, so they steal the plant food, water, and sunlight before your crop can get them. Starved of light and soil nutrients, your crop loses its green color and stops expanding.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anine shɛɔ nɔ. yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and grow, and when soil nutrients run low, the plant moves what little it has to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. ni kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing water stress and encouraging soil fungi that rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa nu mli haomɔ baa ni ewoɔ ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why must I place wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy efficiently. Staking keeps leaves exposed to light and away from damp ground diseases, leading to larger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ la he ni helai kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense mid-day heat, pepper leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing too much water.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite.

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to shed their blossoms to conserve energy rather than feed growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaaye aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every season if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land each year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets plant-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating crops helps restore soil balance and reduces pest problems.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Crowded crops compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. When planted too close, no single plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy ears.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Kɛji adu lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ahaaa tso ko nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha etoi lɛ ayi obɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean seeds fail to sprout and rot in the ground when planted during continuous rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ kwɛɛɛ ni egbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds require oxygen in the soil alongside moisture to germinate. Excess water fills all air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the seeds and causing them to decay.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛfata ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is my pepper crop producing lots of tall green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Applying too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer encourages plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of shifting into the flowering and fruiting stage.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ wo mli babaoo lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebote fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets sick, why does the sickness spread to my neighbor's plants so fast?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko hela mɔ Mɛni hewɔ hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa mikutsoŋnyo tsei lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Crop sicknesses are often carried by tiny insects like whiteflies or by the wind. When plants are healthy and close together, insects easily jump from one plant to another, carrying the disease across farms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai baa. Kɛ tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ewaaa akɛ kooloi shwieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. ni amɛkɛ helai baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do some of my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiho fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they are under severe stress, usually caused by extreme heat, lack of water, or pests attacking the stem, which makes the plant save its energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛyɛ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: When you plant too closely, your crops start fighting underground for the same food and water, and fighting above ground for sunlight, leaving all of them hungry and small.
ga: Kɛji odu ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi tawuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛha niyenii kɛ nu hu. ni amɛwu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la Ha tsei lɛ fɛɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛfee bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like human babies and burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow fast and provide living shade and moisture to protect the cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to your land, so they are much aggressive at stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil before your food crops can get them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ basabasa waa yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli dani oniyenii tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn all the bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and friendly insects in the top layer of the soil that naturally feed your crops, leaving your soil dry, hard, and poor over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ, ewaa, ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my farm weeks before the main rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mli ni masaa mihe kɛha Okwaafoi Otsi lɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba?

english: Early preparation allows the dry soil to loosen up and absorb the very first rains, and gives old plant materials time to rot into rich natural fertilizer before you plant your seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni ha tso mli nibii momo lɛ be ni amɛfite akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs, while allowing pests and diseases that love that specific crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving a few large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a soft shade canopy that protects the seedlings while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji fioo komɛi ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the leaves at the top?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It feeds on the young, tender center of the maize plant (the whorl), and the dark powder is its waste. Catching it early and applying approved organic or chemical control protects your crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Eyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. (Fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ) kɛ powda ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji jwɛi. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Does leaving weeds around my cassava plants really harm them, or do they just share the land?
ga: jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ oshara diɛŋtsɛ loo eji he ni ejaa kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. They also hide harmful pests and diseases, so clearing weeds early allows your cassava plants to grow bigger roots much faster.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai hu teeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha o-cassava tso lɛ atsɔ shishifãi wuji oya kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is running out of essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Adding animal manure, compost, or appropriate fertilizers restores the soil's richness and turns the leaves healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to plant beans on my land next season instead of planting maize on the same spot again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up pests. Beans and groundnuts put vital nitrogen back into the dirt naturally, which refreshes the land for the next crop.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Beans kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I measure the distance between my crop seeds instead of just scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he ni midumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Proper spacing ensures that every single plant gets enough room, sunlight, water, and soil food without competing with its neighbors, leading to stronger stems and higher harvest yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ abɔ akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛkpaa yibii babaoo.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell that can scorch and kill newly germinated seeds under the ground. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays consistently moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do you recommend that I cut off some of the side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming extra side branches (suckers) helps the tomato plant direct its power and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ esɛɛ (shishifãi) ​​ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready to be dug up for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ akumɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ koni akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop, and the ground around the base of the main stem will start to crack open as the tubers expand below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ he lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of insects and rot even when I tie them tightly in bags inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ kooloi bibii ni amɛmiifite eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ ewo kotokui amli shiŋŋ yɛ tsu lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Grains rot and attract insects if they are not dried completely before being stored. Trapped moisture inside the grain creates mold and encourages hidden insect eggs to hatch, so drying the grain thoroughly in the sun first is essential.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baafite ni ebaagbala kooloi kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ewoɔ koolooi akuji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe hia ni agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What are these green and brown caterpillars eating my maize leaves overnight, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yeɔ mi ŋmei baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome nɛɛ ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: Those are likely fall armyworms. They are moth larvae that hatch in large numbers and eat very fast, usually hiding inside the young leaves of the maize plant during the heat of the day to escape sunlight.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji enɛɛmɛi. Amɛji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ babaoo ni amɛyeɔ nii oya waa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛjo hulu lɛ naa foi.

english: Why do armyworms attack my crops heavily right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The warm, moist weather after early rains creates perfect conditions for adult armyworm moths to fly across farms and lay hundreds of eggs on fresh, soft green crop leaves.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ha shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ba kɛha ŋmeii lɛ, ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ foɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Which crops on my farm are armyworms most likely to destroy if I do not protect them?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ asraafoi amli ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ waa kɛji mibuuu amɛhe?

english: Armyworms prefer cereal crops like maize, sorghum, rice, and millet because of their succulent leaf funnels, though they can feed on grasses and other crops if cereal leaves are not available.
ga: Cutworms sumɔɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ amɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyeɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi moŋ, shi Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛji obɛ ŋmaa baai.

english: Should I spray chemicals on my crops before I see pests, or wait until insects appear on the farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani mana tsɛŋemɔ helai loo mamɛ kɛyashi tsɛŋemɔ helai baaje kpo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Preventive action and early treatment work best. Once armyworms grow large and hide deep inside the plant's leaves, chemicals become much harder to reach them and are far less effective.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei lɛ daa ni ekɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ, Tsofai ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa waa ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I check my young maize plants to know if armyworms are starting to hide inside them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli koni mana kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii miibɔi amɛhe teemɔ yɛ mli?

english: Look inside the central funnel of young plants for small pin-holes in the leaves or dark, sawdust-like droppings, which are signs that small caterpillars are already feeding inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. koni ana pinhole bibioo ko Yɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii amli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miitao niyenii yɛ mli momo.

english: Is there any natural way to keep armyworms off my farm without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Intercropping maize with legumes, clearing weeds around the field early, or dropping a little clean dry sand or wood ash directly into the plant funnels can suffocate young armyworms before they cause damage.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii adumɔ Jwɛi ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Aloo ŋã ni egbi fioo loo tso sũ ni he tse ashwie dumɔ ŋtayaa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛfite nii.

english: How do I choose the right chemical at the store to keep armyworms away from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofai ni sa yɛ shwapo lɛ mli koni armyworms akabote miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Always ask for pesticides specifically approved for fall armyworms, check that the package is sealed with an official registration number, and consult an extension officer to avoid buying counterfeit products.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobi tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛha fall worms. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ nɔmba ni aŋmalaa awoɔ wolo nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ agba sane koni amɛkahe nibii ni ji amalei.

english: Why does spraying pesticide directly on top of maize leaves sometimes fail to stop armyworms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the center funnel of the plant. If you only spray the outer leaves, the chemical will not touch the insects; you must direct the spray nozzle straight down into the leaf funnel.
ga: Armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ afɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ, tsofai lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ ekpeŋ. Osumɔɔ ni okɛ nozzle lɛ afɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does the chemical pesticide I used last year no longer work against armyworms on my farm this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests can build resistance if you use the exact same chemical repeatedly. Switching between different approved chemical classes prevents armyworms from becoming immune to the spray.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ hela lɛ. Tsofai srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ tsakemɔ baatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will spraying strong chemical pesticides damage my young crops or stop them from producing good yields?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ loo ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo yibii kpakpai?

english: If mixed at the correct recommended dosage, pesticides will not harm your crops. However, applying chemicals that are too concentrated can burn the crop leaves and stunt plant growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yeŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofa ko ni mli wa tsɔ ni akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni etsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early growth phase.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other so I can get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Crowded plants grow weak and yield less, while proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce a heavy crop.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight, which feeds the tuber growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and allowing the plant to get maximum sunlight for bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ afite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hulu la babaoo kɛha ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning from excess water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji niyeli bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are often caused by pests like the fall armyworm hiding inside the leaves. They can quickly ruin young plants if not managed early using recommended pest controls or safe farm practices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fallworms, ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ bu ni baa ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite tsei bibii oya kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why are the branches of my cocoa trees swelling and dropping their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso lɛ niji lɛ efuu ni baai lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Swollen branches and leaf loss are signs of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees cannot transport nutrients properly and usually must be removed to protect surrounding trees.
ga: Niji ni efuu kɛ baai ni elaaje lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya jogbaŋŋ. ni bei pii lɛ esa akɛ ajie koni akɛbu tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer right before heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Heavy downpours wash away fertilizer before plant roots can absorb it, wasting your money and washing nutrients into nearby streams. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during light rain or clear weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest since the roots grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, the soil around the main stem begins to crack from expanding roots, and the crop reaches its variety's maturity age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ fɔmɔ afii ni ji ŋmei henɔ lɛ fɔmɔ he lɛ he.

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to start properly before sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting in dry soil before steady rains begin can cause seeds to dry out and die in hot soil. Waiting for regular rainfall ensures the ground stays moist enough for seeds to sprout and establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, providing necessary shade and conserving soil moisture while young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: How close can I plant my plantain suckers to my other crops without harming them?
ga: Te manyɛ madu plantain dumɔwui lɛ mabɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe tɛŋŋ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Plantains need about 2 to 3 meters of space between each other. If planted too close to other crops, their large leaves block sunlight and their shallow roots steal water and nutrients needed by nearby plants.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 2 kɛyashi 3 kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ. Baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: How long does it take from planting a plantain sucker to harvesting the fruit bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ aduawai akuu ko ni akpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: In Ghana, a plantain plant usually takes between 11 to 15 months to produce a harvestable bunch, depending on the rainfall, soil fertility, and the variety planted.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ nugbɔshikpɔŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have short, shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil. As the heavy bunch grows on top, the plant becomes top-heavy and requires wooden props for support.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ kuku ni ŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ tso afi sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain turning yellow and drying up from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is often caused by leaf spot diseases or a shortage of nutrients like potassium in the soil. It can also happen during dry spells when the plant tries to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ baa ji baa mli hela loo niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli hu beni tsei miitao ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes and soft rotting inside my plantain stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? ni egbo fioo Yɛ mi plantain tso lɛ mli

english: These holes are caused by plantain stem borers or weevils. Their larvae burrow inside the stem to feed, which weakens the plant stem and prevents food and water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni stem borers loo plantain ŋmeii kɛbaa. Amɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa niyenii kɛ nu shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to dig up plantain suckers from my neighbor's old farm to plant on my new field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo dumɔwui kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: It can be risky because suckers from old farms often carry hidden diseases or root pests. It is safer to clean and treat suckers in hot water or source certified disease-free suckers.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, tsei ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ yɛ helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oootsumɔ suckers lɛ ahe ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo suckers jɛɛhe ni atsɔɔ akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after I cut down the fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni mifo aduawai akui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem naturally produces fruit only once in its life. After fruiting, that stem dies off and gives room to new side shoots (suckers) growing around its base to continue the harvest.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli plantain tso lɛ shishifã lɛ woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ eshihilɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ wo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, egboɔ ni ehaa gbɛ ehaa ŋmeii heei (ŋmeii) ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. cones koni amɛya nɔ amɛkpa nii

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or crops are planted too closely, the plant uses all its energy to grow stem and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning purple or reddish during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple loo etsuru yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Purple leaves usually mean the young maize plant is unable to absorb phosphorus from cold or waterlogged soil, which temporarily slows down root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmãa tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ ajie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How does putting dried cow dung or poultry manure around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Tsina ŋmei ni egbi loo kooloi ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts like rich food for your soil. Just like good food keeps a human body strong and healthy, manure slowly releases essential nutrients into the ground, making the soil rich and helping your crops absorb water and food easily.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa haa adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ he wa ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ baafee fiofio Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are 'hungry' for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. Feeding the soil with fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives them the food they need to turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ ‘hɔmɔ’ miiye amɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy branches but very small cassava tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi cassava shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much leaf-growing food (nitrogen) but lacks root-growing food (potassium), the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of expanding its underground roots into large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii babaoo ni baahã baai lɛ akwɛ̃ (nitrogen) shi niyenii bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ (potassium) lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ɔ baai wuji. Mohu ɔ, e gblɛɛɔ sisi sisi nɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ mi kɛ peeɔ bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural defense to avoid losing too much water. It is the plant's way of resting and protecting itself until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tso lɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe ni ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Flowers drop when plants get stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil food. Keeping the soil evenly moist and feeding the plant helps the blossoms stay attached and develop into healthy peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni oha tsei lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn black and soft at the bottom before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or steady water while the fruit is growing. Regular watering and adding lime or organic manure to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How can I stop caterpillars and worms from chewing holes in my crop leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye bu yɛ mitsei lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: Insects eat leaves to survive, but they weaken your plants. Spraying natural organic extracts like neem water or approved crop protection products coats the leaves and stops the pests from eating your harvest.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baai koni amɛhi wala mli. Shi ehaa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli tamɔ neem nu loo tsei ahebuu nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Ebaaha baai lɛ ahe ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: How can I protect my cocoa pods from turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease spreads easily in wet, shady conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight in and applying protective sprays acts like a shield that keeps fungal rot away from your pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la babaoo abote mli ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ afɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akaje ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How does spreading dry grass or palm fronds on top of the soil protect my crops from dry weather?
ga: Te jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass on top of the soil is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that shields the ground from hot sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping water inside so your crops do not dry out quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni onibii akagbi oya.

english: Why is it safer for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same farm instead of planting only one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ?

english: Planting different crops together acts as a natural insurance policy for your farm. If bad weather or a pest destroys one crop, the other crop can still survive and provide food and income for your family.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ Kɛfata he lɛ, amɛji adebɔɔ mli inshuɔrans kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko hiɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛha oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops look burnt after I spray them with strong liquid mixtures in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: When heavy liquids or unrefined plant juices sit on leaves under the strong Ghanaian sun, they can trap heat or draw moisture out of the plant tissue, causing leaf burn. Spraying in the cool morning or diluting the mixture prevents this scorch.
ga: Beni nu ni tsii loo tso mli nu ni he tseee lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi lɛ. Amɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dɔlɛ loo amɛ gbala fɛ̃i kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ baanyɛ ashã. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shãa akashɛ ohe.

english: Can pouring raw plant extracts directly onto my leaves cause them to dry up and die?
ga: Ani tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ mibaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi?

english: Yes, raw extracts and thick plant juices are often too concentrated for delicate leaf skin. Without diluting them properly in clean water first, the intense strength of the extract will burn the leaf surfaces.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ tsei amli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ feɔ nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ kɛha baa lɛ hiɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ amli babaoo lɛ baaha baa lɛ hiɛ ashã kɛji akɛ akɛwooo nu ni mli tse mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How can I safely use aloe vera gel on my crops without damaging the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ aloe vera gel lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni mifiteee baai lɛ?

english: Aloe vera gel must be mixed and thoroughly rinsed in clean water so that no thick, sticky residue remains on the leaf skin. Washing it out properly into water makes a safe mixture that won't burn your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ aloe vera gel lɛ afutu mli ni afɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli tse mli bɔni afee ni nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi akashwɛ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni shãŋ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is sticky plant sap dangerous if left sitting on crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji oshara kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso baai anɔ lɛ?

english: Sticky sap blocks the tiny breathing pores on the leaf and traps heat from the sun. If not washed off, this sap bakes onto the leaf, turning it yellow or brown.
ga: Latex ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baatsi mumɔ bu bibii lɛ anaa. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ mli Kɛji afɔɔɔ he lɛ Akɛ latex nɛɛ shãa baai lɛ anɔ. Ha efee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: If I accidentally put too much natural liquid treatment on my crops, will rinsing them with clean water save them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nu ni mli tse baafɔ he lɛ baaye abua amɛ?

english: Yes, rinsing the leaves immediately with plenty of clean water washes away excess concentrated liquid and dilutes remaining residues, stopping the burning process before permanent damage occurs.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo shwie baai lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie nu ni mli ewo muji ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni ekɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi Koni ekpa la ni tsoɔ lɛ dani ekɛ naagbai ni baahi shi daa aba.

english: Is it safe to leave thick, undiluted herbal juices on crop leaves in hot weather?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi tsofa-kɛ-ŋma nu ni akɛwooo mli lɛ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: No, leaving thick natural juices on leaves under direct sunlight creates a hot film that scorches the plant. It is always best to wash or rinse thick remedies into clear water before applying.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa sini ni mli edɔ ni shãa tso lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ loo okɛ nu ni mli tse awo mli dani okɛtsu nii.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to dilute botanical mixtures with plenty of water before spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ nu babaoo awo tsei amli nibii amli dani wɔkɛshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Water weakens harsh concentrated chemicals and thick plant saps so they are gentle on the crop while still providing protection against pests or diseases without burning the leaves.
ga: Nu haa tsofai ni mli wa kɛ tso mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai anaa ni ekɛ baa shãaa.

english: How does rinsing plant extracts completely in water protect sensitive crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei amli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu tsei ni he yɔɔ oya lɛ ahe?

english: Rinsing releases the beneficial compounds into the liquid while preventing solid, heavy bits of sap from sticking directly onto the foliage and causing localized sun scorch.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ he lɛ, ejieɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛyaa nu lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ naa koni ekamɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ekɛ hulutsoo baa hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi

english: What should I do immediately if my leaves start turning brown right after applying a liquid extract?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ mibaai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: You should take clean water and shower or pour it over the leaves straight away to rinse off all leftover residue completely before the sun causes further damage.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu ni mli tse loo afɔse ashwie baai lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekɛjie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ dani hulu lɛ afite lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use clean water to wash down my plants after applying a thick organic solution?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tsei lɛ ahe beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: Yes, giving the leaves a gentle rinse with clear water after applying a remedy removes excessive surface buildup while allowing the beneficial properties to absorb safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse tsu baai lɛ ahe blɛoo beni okɛwo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nibii ni fa fe nine ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How long does maize usually take to reach full maturity before harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ dani akpaa?

english: Maize typically takes about 110 days to reach full physiological maturity in the field before it is ready to be harvested and properly dried.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa heɔ aaafee gbii 110 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil so quickly after I bring it into my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn spoils quickly when pests break into the grain inside your storage room and moisture causes it to rot, preventing it from lasting long.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bote ŋmaa ni yɔɔ onitoohe lɛ mli. ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can insects attack my crops while I am transporting them from the farm to my home?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ atutua miŋmɔshi nibii beni mikɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa mishia lɛ?

english: Yes, pests can infest and break down harvested crops during transport from the field to your home, starting the destruction before the grain is even stored.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atswa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa oshia lɛ. Hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi dani akɛ dumɔwui lɛ po toɔ.

english: How do farm pests and animals manage to destroy my stored maize inside the house?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi nyɛɔ amɛfiteɔ ŋmãa ni ato yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If storage spaces are not well protected, pests and roaming animals enter to feed on and break up the grain, leading to severe post-harvest loss.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abuuu he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ nibii ni laajeɔ waa baa.

english: What steps can I take to make my harvested corn last much longer in storage?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: To extend storage life, reduce the moisture in your corn through thorough drying and secure your storage space against insects and animals.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ekɛ be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni oooha egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oha he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ afee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: Why do I still need to dry my maize after taking it off the farm if it looks mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmãa lɛ lolo beni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni eda kwraa?

english: Even mature maize contains high moisture levels at harvest. Continued drying is necessary to remove this moisture so mold and pests do not destroy the grain.
ga: Abɛi ni eda po yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛji akpa. Ehe miihia ni agbi be fɛɛ be koni ajie nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: What should I do if the weather is damp and rainy when my crop is ready for drying?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ miinɛ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaagbi lɛ?

english: During damp end-of-season weather, you must continue drying the grain whenever possible or use a crop dryer to bring the moisture level down safely.
ga: Yɛ be lɛ naagbee be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ oya nɔ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ebaahi. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛgbiɔ tsei lɛ atsu nii ni okɛba hulutsoo be lɛ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it possible to dry my harvested maize if there is no strong sunshine available?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ agbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa bɛ?

english: Yes, you can use mechanical grain dryers to dry your maize effectively when wet weather prevents traditional sun drying.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ ŋmaa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbi o-ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulutsoo ŋmaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ naa.

english: Why does high moisture at the end of the harvest season affect my grain quality?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ saa miŋmaa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Damp conditions keep grain moisture high, creating an ideal environment for pests and rot to destroy the corn while it sits in storage.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo baa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Can using a crop dryer give me the same drying result as drying my maize under the sun?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbi tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ náa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, a mechanical dryer effectively removes moisture from your grain just like the sun, making it a reliable option during wet or damp harvest seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛgbiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmaa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ tamɔ bɔ ni hulu la jieɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei ni hulu enyɔ shi loo hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young trees until they are strong enough to tolerate fuller sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which the plant needs to build strong green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plant will restore its healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo kooloi amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many lush green leaves but failing to produce any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas grow too many leaves and very few pods when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants receive too much shade. Reducing nitrogen fertilizer and growing them in open sunlight signals the plant to stop growing leaves and start producing flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season becomes very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects around them and cannot drain away, starving the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain downhill, keeping the tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist using grass mulch protects the roots from heat and helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaabu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a strong wind comes during fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold up the heavy weight of a full bunch of fruit against strong winds. Proping up the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden stakes gives the plant extra support to carry the heavy bunch to harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai ni eyi obɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ wo ŋmei loo tso tso ni wa mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye abua lɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to sun and prevents them from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop four or five maize seeds into one hole so I get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli bɔni afee ni maná ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the roots to fight each other for water, nutrients, and space, resulting in small, weak stalks with tiny cobs. Planting only one or two seeds per hole gives each plant enough space and food to produce large ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, niyenii kɛ he ko he, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Dumɔwu kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients out of the young leaves. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil solution or an appropriate insecticide gets rid of the insects so clean new leaves can grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei ni he tse lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cabbage plants spreading out wide instead of forming hard, tight heads in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni wa ni mli edɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when temperatures are too high or when they lack consistent water during their middle growth stage. Watering regularly and keeping the soil cool with mulch encourages the inner leaves to curl tightly together into a solid head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Nu ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ muji awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ekome ni efee bulb ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants require partial shade to survive because their young leaves cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ baai bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Lifting the leaves helps the plant make food efficiently, which results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa niyenii feɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy green growth. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and supports crop development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.
