english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas can trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil and provides extra nutrients for the maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii krokomɛi fataa he.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests build up. Rotating maize with crops like beans or peppers keeps the soil balanced and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, airless soil for long periods. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry enough to remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool, conserves water, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillar droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest whose caterpillars feed inside the growing center of maize plants. Early detection and applying targeted organic or chemical remedies directly into the leaf funnels can save the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni eŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni ana mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot and dry or when the plant receives inconsistent water, causing extreme stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme midday heat helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Enɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when their root systems are weak, often damaged by underground pests like root nematodes or weevils, or because too many suckers were left attached to the mother plant. Pruning extra suckers and keeping roots healthy anchors the plant securely.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo weevils fiteɔ amɛ. aloo akɛni ŋmeii babaoo ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he hewɔ lɛ Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni akɛha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when planted in an open field without tall crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains near them provides shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent rot and helps the plant produce food to build large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafite ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni efee niyenii ni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK gives the plant the essential food it needs to stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay after harvest, they leave that rich nutrient behind in the soil for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nakai niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I drop fertilizer right next to the seed when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Raw fertilizer is very strong and can burn delicate seeds before they sprout. It is better to place fertilizer a short distance away from the plant roots so they can absorb it safely without damage.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo bɔni afee ni enyɛ etsɔ mli shweshweeshwe ni efiteee.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and nutrients in the ground. This competition results in tall, thin stems with very small, thin tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa.

english: Why does planting egusi melon between my main crops stop weeds from taking over my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Egusi melon ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haaa jwɛi akaye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Egusi melon grows broad leaves that spread quickly over the soil surface, blocking sunlight from reaching the ground. Without sunlight, weed seeds cannot germinate and grow easily.
ga: Egusi melon lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui hu nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara mlɛo.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, usually caused by uneven watering that prevents the plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps stop this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide or neem oil helps destroy the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell of hot weather. If seeds sprout and then face hot dry ground, the seedlings will dry up and die before the real rainy season establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛyashɛ hei ni egbi ni edɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains or shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight and dry air. Fast-growing plantains or shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and humid so the delicate cocoa roots can survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Tsei bibii ni daa oya loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my adult cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the forest trees surrounding them become too dense and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees require heavy shade, mature cocoa trees need balanced sunlight to produce flowers and feed growing pods. Excessive shade traps moisture, encouraging black pod disease and reducing fruit yields.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii po he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Shi hulu la ni sa he miihia kookoo tso ni eda lɛ koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi ni eha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa black pod hela lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip on lower leaves is a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left up to the top leaves and growing corn ear, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ toi ni miida lɛ amli. Shi shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with plenty of green leaves but yield very tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves and thick stems above ground instead of sending sugars down to build large cassava roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu sugars kɛya shi ni ekɛfee ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpea or groundnuts on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants drop leaves or decay, that trapped nitrogen feeds the soil and helps the maize grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gbee shi loo amɛgboi Trapped nitrogen lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tightly and turn brown during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmatta be ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during harsh, dry winds to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve internal water so the main stem stays alive until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ emli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures combined with dry soil stress the pepper plant, causing it to drop its flowers as a defense mechanism to save water and energy rather than trying to feed growing peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ laajeɔ akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my maize stalks break or fall flat on the ground whenever strong rainstorms pass through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni ahum ni naa wa baatsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are too shallow, when crops are planted too close together, or when the soil lacks potassium, which is essential for building strong, woody stems.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni he hiaa kɛha tso shishi ni wa maa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam setts rot inside the mound before they can sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in soil that is too wet or when cut surfaces are not allowed to dry or treated with wood ash. Open wounds invite soil fungi and bacteria that destroy the tuber before it roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ loo kɛ́ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni nɔ ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi loo akɛ tso sũ tsu nii. Pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ nine.

english: Why do my crops grow much greener and taller near old termite mounds than on the rest of my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛkwɔ kɛbɔleɔ termite gɔŋ momo lɛ he fe miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Termites gather organic matter, clay, and subsoil minerals to build their mounds, making the surrounding soil much higher in essential nutrients and far better at retaining moisture than nearby bare earth.
ga: Termites buaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, shikpɔŋ, kɛ shika tsuru ni yɔɔ sũ shishi lɛ anaa koni ekɛfee gɔji, ni no haa sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he hiaa waa, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ fe sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and wither when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade trees or plantain plants around them during their first two years to protect their young leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni akɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I plant suckers with broad leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ

english: Broad-leafed suckers (water suckers) are weakly attached to the main plant and lack stored energy. For big bunches, you should plant sword suckers, which have narrow, blade-like leaves and strong, thick bases filled with stored food.
ga: Broadleaf suckers (nu mli nu) lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkpɛtɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni ato. Kɛha kuu agbo ko Esa akɛ Okwɛ klante ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishi ni mli wa ni mli tse ni niyenii ni ato eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Aloo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season fully establishes. Planting too early can cause the seeds to germinate and then dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto wooden tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to maximum sunlight so they can manufacture food for the tuber underground, while keeping the leaves off the damp soil prevents leaf diseases and rotting.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni baa lɛ akaye hela kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut and plant to get a strong crop?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba?

english: The middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem is best because it has well-developed buds that sprout quickly, unlike the woody bottom section which is too hard or the green top section which dries out fast.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tso shishi ni wa tsɔ loo ŋwɛi ni ji eŋɔli ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a viral infection spread by these insects, which steals the plant's nutrients and stunts its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ juɔ tsei amli niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil goes from very dry to very wet, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni midu yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as natural nitrogen fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) protects it from harsh sunlight, keeps the ground cool and moist, stops weeds from growing, and adds rich organic matter to the soil as the dry material breaks down.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he be mli ni nibii ni egbi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii loo nitrogen ŋmeii, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: This black rotting is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering. Giving tomato plants consistent water and adding lime or calcium-rich fertilizer to the soil stops the fruit from rotting.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo o-tomato tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni calcium yɔɔ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off the plant without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack sufficient water. Watering the crops regularly during hot spells helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cowpeas is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking the sap from the underside of the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem extract or an approved insecticide removes the pests and allows normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ cowpea mli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ, ni ebaaha amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves burning and turning brown in the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their foliage is delicate. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa leaves from sun damage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. kɛ fungal infection baa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my crops staying small and weak even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daraaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for plant growth; crops need essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium from the soil. Adding compost or fertilizer feeds the exhausted soil so the plants can grow tall and produce well.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Tsei hia niyenii ni he hia tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔras, kɛ potasiam kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni egbo lɛ niyenii koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, and the heavy weight of a maturing bunch pulls the whole tree down. Propping up the main stem with sturdy bamboo poles supports the plant until the bunch is fully mature.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni ŋmeii ni edara lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds in my farm cause my main crops to give very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ baa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and space they need to develop big fruits and high yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni nu lɛ baaje onibii amli waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting in the barn before the planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Seed yams break dormancy and sprout early if the storage area is too warm and humid. Storing seed yams in a well-ventilated, cool, shaded barn keeps them asleep until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baaya wɔɔhe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya kɛji he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwɔ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I mix chicken droppings into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmei futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is full of essential nutrients like nitrogen that feed the soil, giving crops the energy they need to grow strong leaves and healthy roots.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Is it safe to put fresh manure from my poultry farm straight onto my growing crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ mikooloi akwɛmɔhe lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and generates high heat as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots and kill the crop; it must be left to decompose into cool compost first.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ babaoo baa be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ejɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How does adding decayed plant material and organic matter help my soil hold water for crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Organic matter acts like a sponge underground, trapping moisture in the soil so plant roots can keep drinking even during warm, dry days.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sponji. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu yɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why do plants fed with natural organic manure stay green longer during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii haa amɛ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Organic manure improves the soil's structure and ability to store water, keeping crops hydrated and healthy when rain is scarce.
ga: Organic fertilizers haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nu ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ faaa.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow more slowly when I use organic manure compared to chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Organic manure releases its nutrients gradually over time as soil organisms break it down, providing steady, long-lasting feeding rather than a short, rapid rush.
ga: Organic fertilizer baafee fiofio Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Ehaa onine shɛɔ niyenii nɔ daa kɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee oya yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for making green leaves that the plant pulls from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni tsei gbalaa kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or improper soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How do natural plant-based sprays stop pests from eating my crop leaves?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso nɔ lɛ atsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anaa?

english: Natural sprays made from plants like neem taste bitter or smell strong to pests, driving insects away from leaves without harming the crop or the soil.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ, tamɔ neem lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni teɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe kpaaa baa lɛ he ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ awui.

english: How do I know if an organic input made on the farm is too strong for my young seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo tsɔ kɛha mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: If an organic mixture turns leaf tips brown or causes leaves to curl inward shortly after application, it is too concentrated and needs to be diluted with water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fee ŋmɔtɔ loo eha baai lɛ tsɔ mli beni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu tsɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nu awo mli.

english: How does keeping farm animals together with crop farming help my soil produce higher yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Farm animals turn crop waste into manure, which feeds the soil microbes that release plant food back into the soil, creating a self-sustaining cycle for higher yields.
ga: Koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii ni jieɔ tsei aniyenii kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa he-kɛ-afɔleshaa he sɛɛkuu baa kɛha nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and stop growing whenever heavy rain floods my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe, just like humans do. When floodwater covers the ground for too long, it suffocates the roots, preventing them from taking up food and water, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to stunt.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Taakɛ adesai sumɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Kɛ nu afua lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the topsoil before the plant's roots have a chance to drink it in. Applying fertilizer when heavy rain is coming wastes your money and leaves your crops hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ, eheɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: What is an 'improved seed variety', and why should I buy it instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ’ ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved seeds are bred by agricultural scientists to withstand local droughts, resist common crop diseases, and produce much bigger harvests compared to traditional seeds saved season after season.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi baadu dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ naa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo fe tsutsu dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ be mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: How does keeping written farm records help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Writing down your planting dates, fertilizer amounts, and harvest yields helps you remember what worked best in past seasons, spot repeating pest outbreaks early, and know exactly when to give your crops care.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmala gbi ni adu lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ, kɛ yibii ni akpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaiɔ nɔ ni tsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shii abɔ lɛ mra ni ole be ni esa akɛ otsa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are a sign that your crop is under attack by small insects like whiteflies, or that the soil lacks key nutrients. The plant curls its leaves because it cannot produce food efficiently.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji etutua onibii lɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titri Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. Large canopy trees act like natural umbrellas; without them, the harsh sun dries out the soil and scorches the young cocoa leaves before the plant can mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei agbo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Kɛ amɛbɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa kookoo baai bibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ daa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to develop strong stems and produce heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baawuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baawo yibii babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in large numbers in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: During the dry season, wild plants dry up, so insects migrate to your farm looking for moisture and food. The hot weather also causes insect eggs to hatch faster, leading to larger pest populations.
ga: Yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii fãa kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyatao fɛ̃i kɛ niyenii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi awɔlɔi fɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get eaten by insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miifite ni kooloi miiye lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If grains are not dried completely before storage, trapped moisture creates mold and attracts insects. Keeping grains dry and storing them in airtight bags keeps moisture out and suffocates any insects trying to eat your harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. Kɛ́ oha oŋmaa lɛ mli egbi ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli, ni ebaaha kooloi ni miitao amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii kɛha tso lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and leafy but do not produce many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Balancing nitrogen with fertilizers that contain phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to produce more flowers and tomatoes.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai amli moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ to he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ tomato babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground if I do not harvest them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers begin to rot in the ground when left past their maturity stage or during heavy rains because fungi and soil bacteria attack the waterlogged roots. Harvesting between 8 to 12 months prevents this rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji ashi amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the trees without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun, heat, lack of shade, or attacks from insects like mirids. Providing shade trees and protecting the cocoa from pests helps the flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, dɔlɛ, hulutsoo be ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni tswaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha kookoo ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain plant. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers helps the main plant produce a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, moist ground, exposing them to light and preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Shi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kane yɔɔ ni otsi baa hela ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai kɛ aduawai adalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster after rain than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have wild, aggressive roots that grab rainwater and soil nutrients instantly. Clearing weeds early stops them from robbing your main crop of the water and food it needs to grow.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to sow your seeds after the soil has received two or three heavy, continuous rains. This ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture so your seeds do not dry out and die shortly after sprouting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant groundnuts together in the same plot as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fata he kɛdu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and naturally put it into the soil, which feeds the maize crop. Mixing groundnuts with maize keeps the soil rich and allows you to harvest two different crops from one piece of land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni no haa ŋmei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei futu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my maize crops growing tall and strong in one part of my field, but staying short and weak in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eyɛ kuku lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil fertility is rarely the same across an entire farm. Some areas may have poorer drainage, less organic matter, or lower nutrient levels, which prevents crops in those spots from growing properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efɔɔɔ kaa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Ekolɛ hei komɛi bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa kwraa. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa Enɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai hei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing a lot of healthy green leaves but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy developing leaves above ground rather than storing nutrients in the root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ woɔ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during wet, humid weather. It attacks the pods when excess water and shade stay trapped in the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Ebaatutua pod lɛ beni nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ efo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Root rot happens when water sits around the tubers for too long due to heavy rains or poor soil drainage, allowing fungal infections to decay the roots in waterlogged soil.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ebɔle he. Tubers lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines curling up and showing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and spotted leaves are often caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids or a plant virus they spread. These insects weaken the vine by draining its nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ haa wain tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They wilt temporarily to preserve moisture and usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures are too high or air is too dry. Heat stress prevents pollination from taking place, so the plant sheds the unproductive blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms once the fruit bunch appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni aduawai akui jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches. If they are not supported with wooden stakes or if tiny soil pests damage their roots, strong winds can easily pull them down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso ko fioo ko pɛ fiɔ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpata eshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛba shi mlɛo.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds wake up instantly with rain and consume water and soil nutrients much more aggressively than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii waa fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Keeping the field free of weeds and spraying recommended pest control products helps keep leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ jwɛi akafee he ni jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ, ni akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa akɛ akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, heavily shaded conditions. Pruning dense tree branches to let in sunlight and air, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods early helps protect the harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu nibii ni adu lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark waste inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf whorl of the maize plant. Checking your crop regularly and applying targeted control measures into the leaf funnel early prevents severe crop damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ awo baai lɛ amli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady watering during dry spells and avoiding over-fertilization encourages the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe babaoo lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akawo yibii.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing very small fruits even though the plant itself looks big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa lɛ? Ni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da?

english: Small fruits usually happen when too many sucker shoots grow around the main plant, taking away water and nutrients. Pruning away excess suckers—leaving just one or two shoots—allows the main plant to direct its energy into producing a large bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he, ni no haa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight, which fuels tuber growth underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp soil, protecting the plant from foliage diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa lɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ baa helai ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plant turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage will help restore leaf health and boost yields.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long, cutting off air to the roots and encouraging rot fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely during heavy rainy seasons.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the middle of the day or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ gbi mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering at mid-day causes much of the water to evaporate in the heat before reaching the roots, and water droplets left on hot leaves can cause leaf stress.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la yɛ latsaa be mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before heavy rains fall?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: It is better not to apply fertilizer right before heavy downpours, as rain will wash the nutrients away before roots can take them in. Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, or during light showers.
ga: Esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. loo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or high heat. Keeping shade trees around and maintaining moist soil helps the cocoa tree retain its flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo la ni mli edɔ waa Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding balanced fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Seeds buried too deep use up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil. They may run out of energy and die underground or emerge as very weak plants that struggle to survive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli. Amɛhewalɛ baanyɛ afite ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛbatsɔmɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ waa ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves, but produces tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of root tubers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage energy to move down into the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni eya shi kɛya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb upright so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. When vines lie flat on the ground, leaves rot easily and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ bulbs bibii babaoo.

english: Extreme heat forces pepper plants to drop flowers to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Mulching the soil and providing light shade helps keep the plants cool enough to hold flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ chili tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Mulching kɛ shade yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by insect-borne viruses, whiteflies, or sudden heat and dry spells. Protecting young plants with nets and keeping the soil evenly moist helps prevent curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ kooloi amli kɛbaa, ŋmeii yɛŋ, loo dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi bu tsei bibii ahe, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔji ewo mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or husks is called mulching. It keeps the sun from drying out the soil, prevents weed growth, keeps crop roots cool, and slowly decays into rich natural soil food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the stems of my small crop seedlings rot and fall over right at ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii Mine lɛ ashishifãi lɛ egbo ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in overly wet soil with poor airflow. Avoid overwatering young seeds and give seedlings space so air can circulate around the base of the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ dumɔwui bibii amli fe nine lɛ he ni oha dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle tso lɛ shishi.

english: When I cut cassava stems to plant, how do I know which end should go into the ground?
ga: Kɛji oofolɔ ŋmei tsei kɛha dumɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male naagbee ni esa akɛ atswa shikpɔŋ?

english: Look at the small buds or 'eyes' where the leaves used to grow; those buds must point upwards toward the sky, otherwise the stem is upside down and will produce weak shoots and few tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, tso lɛ yitso lɛ baatsɔ ehe ni ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi baaje kpo.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting them on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋmei niji amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cassava about 1 meter apart gives the tubers enough underground space to expand fully without competing with neighboring roots for water and food.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ fɛɛ he. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ abɔ he akaŋ

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its lower leaves during dry spells to conserve water; as long as the top leaves stay green, the plant is surviving and will resume normal growth when the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Shii abɔ ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ. Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaaku esɛɛ ebakwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You will often see visible cracks forming in the soil right around the base of the stem, which happens when the subterranean tubers swell up and push the soil outward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ obaana ŋmeii ni anaa ni miifee yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fũu ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtee kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if heavy water collects on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ muji bua ehe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe, so waterlogged land suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to easily cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my young maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against heat—it reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why does weed grass grow so much faster than my food crops during the first few weeks after land clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-forage tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛjie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, wild root systems adapted to pull nutrients and water out of the soil faster than domestic crops, which is why early weeding is necessary to protect young crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛjie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Ehe miihia ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow taller and greener when I plant cowpeas or beans together with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ du tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and sharing nutrients with neighboring crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither when I clear away every single big shade tree on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigbo lɛ? Beni mikɛ hulutsoo tso agbo fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants act like human infants that burn easily under harsh sunlight; larger shade trees protect them from intense heat and keep soil moisture steady.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ adesai abifabii, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the leaves to make more food that gets stored down in the tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni akɛtoɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective canopy that shields the young cocoa leaves and keeps the soil cool and moist while the trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni tso lɛ maa shi lɛ.

english: Cassava stem cuttings have small growth buds or 'eyes' where leaves used to grow. These buds must always point upward toward the sky so that the green shoots can grow straight toward sunlight while roots develop properly underneath.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ yɛ hei ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or root damage from heavy waterlogging. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant recover its green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ efite kɛjɛ nu ni fa babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams signal maturity when their green vines and leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up naturally. This shows that the plant has finished transferring its nutrients down into the underground tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛji wain tso lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ kpa dalɛ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ni ekɛyaa tuber ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do caterpillars like Fall Armyworm attack my maize crops more heavily during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ tutuaa mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm and dry weather helps Fall Armyworms reproduce and grow much faster. At the same time, heat stress weakens young maize plants, making their leaves easier for pests to consume.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa Fall Armyworms lɛ fɔɔ bii ni amɛdaraa oya. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Heat stress haa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why should I remove the small extra stems growing out from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni jɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ

english: Pinching off side shoots (suckers) helps tomato plants direct their water and soil nutrients toward developing large, healthy fruits rather than wasting energy on growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient shortages. The plant sheds blossoms to conserve energy and survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni amɛdalɛ shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do my garden egg plants droop in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot afternoon weather, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Covering the soil around the roots with dry grass mulch keeps the ground cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply in the soil. As the fruit bunch grows large and heavy, the top becomes top-heavy and needs a sturdy wooden prop for physical support.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da ni etsii lɛ Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baafee tsiimɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni aná tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does cassava become hard and woody if left in the farm for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ lɛ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ tso lɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass full maturity, they start converting stored starches into tough plant fibers to support aging stems. Harvesting on time ensures the tubers remain soft and suitable for cooking.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaabɔi ŋmei ni ato lɛ tsakemɔ ewo tso mli ŋmei ni mli wa mli koni ekɛfi ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi bɔdɔɔ ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees swelling and the leaves turning yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efuu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: This is often a sign of a viral infection like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease. Fertilizers help feed plants, but they cannot cure a virus. The swelling and yellowing happen because the virus is disrupting how nutrients move through the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛ mli ba, tamɔ kookoo tsei ni efuu. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii. Shi enyɛŋ etsa hela lɛ. Fuumɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa ejaakɛ hela lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has a viral disease instead of just damage from insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hela ko? Jeee nibii ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible holes, eaten leaves, or clear bugs on the plant that disappear when sprayed. Viral diseases cause internal damage like swollen stems, patchy leaf colors, and slow death that spraying chemicals cannot fix.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa buji ni anaa lɛ shwieɔ shi. baai loo kooloi ni ayeɔ lɛ faŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni laajeɔ kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ Helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu kɛ baa lɛ su ni etse ehe banee. kɛ gbele ni baa blɛoo ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing very small, deformed pods even though the trees are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii waa ni ehiii kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tso lɛ eda kwraa moŋ?

english: When a tree is infected with a viral disease, the virus steals the plant's energy. This prevents the pods from growing to their normal size and cuts down your overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji tso ko hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ Virus lɛ juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛyashɛ bɔ ni sa, ni ehaa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: I sprayed my sick cocoa trees with strong chemicals, so why are they still dying?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwieɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ amɛgboiɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays only kill pests on the outside or fungal infections. They cannot destroy viruses inside the plant's system. Once a tree has a viral disease, chemical sprays will not work.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kponɔgbɛ kooloi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai pɛ. Enyɛɛɛ ekpata helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ Kɛji hela ko emɔ tso ko nɔ Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crop diseases have no chemical cure available at the agrochemical shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofai tsuuu tsei ahe helai komɛi ahe nii yɛ okwaayeli tsofafeemɔ hei lɛ?

english: Plant viruses live deep inside the plant's living cells. Any chemical strong enough to kill the virus inside the tree would also kill the tree itself, which is why there is no chemical cure for plant viruses.
ga: Tso mli helai hiɔ tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli tɔ̃ɔ, ni tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbe helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hu baagbe tso lɛ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsaa helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ bɛ tsei amli.

english: Why should I ask an agricultural extension officer to examine my sick cocoa trees before buying sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni ekwɛ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli dani mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Buying chemicals without knowing the exact problem wastes your money. An extension officer can identify if your crops have a viral disease where chemicals won't work, saving you from spending money on useless treatments.
ga: Tsofai ni ooohe ni oleee naagba pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ofite shika. Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ ana kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haaa ofite shika yɛ helatsamɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why am I being advised to cut down and uproot my cocoa trees instead of just trimming the sick branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ awo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso lɛ ni mijie lɛ moŋ fe ni mafolɔ niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: A viral disease lives throughout the entire tree, including its roots. Trimming branches leaves the virus alive in the trunk and roots, so complete uprooting is the only way to destroy the disease entirely.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ fata he. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa helatsɛ lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpataa hela lɛ hiɛ kwraa.

english: Can a single sick cocoa tree really ruin my entire farm if I leave it standing?
ga: Ani cacao tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji miŋmɛɛ he?

english: Yes. Tiny insects like mealybugs feed on the sick tree, pick up the virus, and crawl or blow onto healthy neighbor trees, quickly spreading the disease across your entire farm.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kplukai bibii tamɔ mealybugs yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ, amɛheɔ hela lɛ, ni amɛkpãa loo amɛfoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ. koni helai agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya

english: If I uproot an infected cocoa tree, can I plant a new young seedling in the exact same hole immediately?
ga: Kɛji mijie kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwu hee yɛ bu kome mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait and clear out all old roots first. Tiny insects carrying the virus can live on remaining roots in the soil and quickly infect your new seedling.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni ofɔ shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ he klɛŋklɛŋ. Kplukai bibii ni hiɛ hela lɛ baanyɛ ahi shishifãi ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ ni amɛwo odumɔwui heei lɛ oya.

english: How does uprooting diseased cocoa trees on my land help protect neighboring cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Pests carrying plant viruses move easily from farm to farm. By removing infected trees from your land, you destroy the source of infection, stopping the disease from jumping to your neighbors' crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hiɛ tsei ahe helai lɛ baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli mlɛo. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaakpãtã he ni hela lɛ jɛ lɛ hiɛ. ni ekpaa helai ni shwieɔ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip often mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow leafy parts. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha baai lɛ fãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist, usually right after a good rain or during early growth stages. Applying fertilizer during dry spells can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer because plants need water to absorb nutrients.
