ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ loo yɛ be mli ni edara oya lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu he hiaa tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to insect attacks or extreme heat combined with lack of water. Spraying an approved crop pesticide and keeping the soil evenly moist will help the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ nu ni bɛ fataa he lɛ baa fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing small green worms to eat the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Yeɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft center leaves of young maize. Identifying them early and applying the recommended chemical or biological spray stops them before they destroy the growing point of the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Ni ooona amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite hei ni onibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use the same chemical spray to treat black spots on my leaves and rotting in my roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛtsa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shishifãi ni egbo lɛ?

english: No, different crop problems require different treatments. Leaf spots are usually caused by airborne fungi and need leaf-applied fungicides, while root rot is caused by soil moisture issues or root pests. You need to treat the specific problem with the right chemical.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai srɔtoi biɔ tsamɔi srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ mli tsɔi baa, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ awo baa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he naagbai loo shishifãi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni sa atsa naagba pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize too close forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. This leads to thin stalks and small or empty corn cobs. Giving each seed enough space allows every plant to grow strong and produce large cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: If my planted cassava stem cuttings look dry, how do I know if I should replace them?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei niji ni adu lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji esa akɛ okɛ oŋmei lɛ atsake?

english: Cassava stem cuttings usually sprout leaves within 2 to 3 weeks if there is moisture in the soil. If you scrape the skin gently and see green underneath, it is alive; if it is dark brown and dry all the way through, it should be replaced with a fresh stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ baa baa yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli kɛji ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ hewolo lɛ shwie shi blɛoo ni ona eŋɔli yɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ wala mli lolo Kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi be fɛɛ be lɛ, esa akɛ atsake tso lɛ shishi.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight on its leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and exposes maximum leaf area to the sun.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitso ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa canopy develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ kookoo bibii adumɔ. Ebaaha hulutsoo be aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔlɔ baaje shishi.

english: Will growing cassava and maize on the same piece of land reduce my yields?
ga: Ani ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes up the space after the maize is harvested. As long as they are spaced correctly, both crops can give good yields without harming each other.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja. Tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai ni amɛyeee amɛhe awui.

english: How do I know which chemical is safe to spray on my farm so I don't destroy my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite minibii lɛ.

english: Approved chemicals have clear instructions showing which crops they protect without causing harm. Safe chemicals kill specific pests or weeds while leaving your main crop healthy, whereas using the wrong chemical can burn crop leaves and reduce your harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ tsei ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbu he ni amɛyeee mɔ awui. Tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii loo jwɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ be mli ni ehaa onibii titri lɛ hiɔ shi lolo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni eha onibii ni oooha lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it better to spray chemicals on my crops early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi fe tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛshwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli.

english: In the hot afternoon, strong sunlight causes chemicals to evaporate quickly before plants absorb them, and heat mixed with chemicals can scorch leaves. Early morning spraying allows crops to absorb protective treatments safely when temperatures are cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni dɔlɛ ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ shweshweeshwe kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Can I use the same weed chemical on both my pepper farm and my cassava farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ mi-pepper kɛ cassava ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli?

english: No, different crops tolerate chemicals differently. Broad-leaf crops like peppers can be killed by weedkillers intended for cassava or maize fields, so each crop requires specific products designed not to harm it.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi kpɛɔ tsofai srɔtoi anaa. Abaanyɛ agbe tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛha ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso henɔ fɛɛ tso henɔ biɔ ni akɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni afee koni akaye mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants rolling up tight during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a survival defense mechanism where the maize plant reduces its surface area to stop losing moisture to extreme heat. Once temperatures cool down or rain falls, the leaves unfold again.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛha wala. Abɛi tso lɛ baa ehiɛ shi koni ekɛkpa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi loo nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɛ ashwã ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience stress from extreme heat, prolonged drought, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil moist and nourished helps flowers stay attached to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ aduawai ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil has too much water, which suffocates the plant roots and prevents them from taking up food. It can also be a sign that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii. Ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do the stems of my tomato plants turn black and rot when the rain is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates damp soil and high moisture in the air, which causes fungal diseases like late blight to attack stems and leaves. Proper farm drainage and timely protective sprays help keep plants safe during rainy seasons.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight lɛ tutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Okwaafoi amli nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the plants grow tall with plenty of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa waa lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo moŋ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow under dense shade, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and big leaves instead of sending energy underground to expand their tubers.
ga: Beni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and fall over easily when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds close together forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of developing thick, sturdy stalks.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená tso ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die so quickly if I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out and burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my harvested corn get ruined by bugs and mold when I leave it piled up in an open area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ beni mishiɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested corn holds hidden moisture inside the cobs. If left piled in humid or open spaces, mold grows quickly and weevils are attracted to the moist grain; it needs to be properly dried in the sun and stored in sealed bags or a clean crib.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ loo he ko ni agbele naa lɛ, Mold lɛ daa oya ni ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni he tse mli.

english: How do I tell if my harvested corn is dry enough to store safely without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee?

english: You can test corn dryness by pressing your thumbnail into a kernel; if the kernel is hard and leaves no mark, or if the grains rattle crisply when shaken together, it is dry enough for safe long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni o-corn lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ o-thumbnail lɛ ni ooonyɛ okɛwo kernel lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛshiii okadii Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ hosoɔ ni amɛkpokpoɔ kɛji akpokpo jogbaŋŋ. Ebaagbi bɔ ni sa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into tight tubes during the middle of the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant hides its surface from the direct hot sun to save water until the cooler afternoon.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei lɛ baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe koni nu akafite kɛyashi shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send what little food it has left to the fresh leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do some of my corn plants grow very tall but fail to produce any cobs at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ miida shi ewooo ŋmeii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Corn plants fail to make cobs when they are planted too close together or lack food during flowering, forcing them to spend all their energy competing for sunlight instead of making ears.
ga: Abɛi tsei nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo niyenii bɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛshiɔ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛtoii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four corn seeds together in the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ ŋmãa bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded into one hole, their roots fight each other for the same limited soil nutrients and water, resulting in weak, thin stalks that produce small cobs.
ga: Beni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ebɔ he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni faaa ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I apply my fertilizer in two stages instead of putting all of it in the soil on planting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ 2-step fertilizer awo mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Young seeds only need a small amount of food to sprout. If you put all the fertilizer at planting, rain washes most of it away before the plant grows big enough to use it.
ga: Niyenii fioo pɛ he hiaa dumɔwui bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: Many modern high-yielding seeds lose their strength after one season. Replanting harvested grains produces weak, uneven plants with smaller yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be kome sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ aba, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my corn leaves have large holes with powdery dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bulɛi wuji kɛ sũ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leafy center of the corn plant during the day and eats the young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli lɛ. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when there is plenty of rain in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients in the soil, effectively starving your corn plants even when water is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei, ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, o-corn tsei lɛ baaye hɔmɔ yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyɛ nu babaoo moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or mixing decomposed animal manure into the soil gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛfutuɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: Small caterpillars and beetles eat holes in leaves to feed themselves. You can protect your vegetables by spraying natural neem seed water early in the morning or using recommended insecticides before the pests multiply.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli koni amɛye niyenii. Obaanyɛ obu o-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui amli nu ni oooshwie nɔ leebi loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii dani kooloi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows the underground roots to expand into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by severe heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing dry grass around the plant base as mulch keeps the roots cool and helps flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ni okɛ jwɛi awo tso lɛ shishi, ejaakɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why is burning dried weeds on my farmland bad for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning weeds destroys good bugs in the dirt and burns away organic food that crops need. Leaving cleared weeds to rot into the soil naturally feeds the land and keeps moisture in the ground during dry periods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ kpataaa kooloi bibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ, ni eshãa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aná niyenii ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a mold that spreads quickly in damp, shaded environments. Pruning heavy cocoa branches lets sunlight in and helps dry out the trees, stopping the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni tsii lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni egbi. Etsiɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully dry and ready to harvest for storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa koni akɛto?

english: Maize is ready for long-term storage when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn dry and brown, and the grain feels hard when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dara. Cob lɛ egbi ni eyɛ asarasu. ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine ŋmei miimɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing thin and crooked instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji mlɛo ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to expand smoothly. Hard or stony ground forces tubers to squeeze into small spaces, causing them to grow crooked; making high, soft mounds gives tubers space to grow big.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi nyɛɔ yitso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa he bibioo ko, ni ehaa ekpokpoɔ; Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni afee lɛ haa bulbs lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take food directly from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that help neighboring maize grow bigger while keeping weeds down.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii jieɔ amɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like giant umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi wuji. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will naturally sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like straws during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest hours to hide their surface from the sun, which slows down water loss and helps the plant survive high heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛtee hulu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without making fruit when the air gets too hot or when the soil lacks moisture, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading wood ash around my pepper plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ tso sũ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Wood ash contains important nutrients like potassium and reduces acidity in the soil, making it easier for pepper plants to soak up water and nutrients from the ground.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium yɛ tso mli ashwishwɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa pepper tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking holds the leaves up high to catch maximum sun, which allows the vine to grow larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai ni hulu la tsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing only male flowers and no fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palms produce male flowers when they are stressed by drought or lack proper fertilizer. When the tree feels well-watered and nourished, it will start producing female flowers that turn into fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ hɔmɔ kpe loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa bɛ. Kɛji akɛ aha tso lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ ni aha lɛ niyenii Ebaabɔi fɔfɔi yei ni baatsɔ aduawai akui.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the undersides of leaves, which can spread sicknesses that stunt fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni haaa aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ ashwã

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sun into the farm, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean the plant is getting too much direct sunlight or is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Providing temporary shade using crops like plantains and applying recommended fertilizers will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn completely black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, cool, and dark conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to allow sunlight and airflow, along with removing affected pods immediately, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the small flower blossoms on my cocoa trees to dry up and drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ bibii? Ani fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Blossom drop is often caused by insect pests like mirids (capsids) that suck sap from delicate flowers, or by severe water stress during dry spells. Managing farm shade and applying safe pest treatments at the start of flowering helps pods form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni nuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee bei amli lɛ baaye abua ni pods lɛ afee.

english: Why is it bad for me to harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe cocoa beans inside green pods do not have enough developed sugars. Harvesting them early leads to poor fermentation, flat chocolate flavor, and lower bean weight, which reduces the price buyers will pay for your crop.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni edako ni yɔɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli mli lɛ bɛ sugars ni etsɔ hiɛ bɔ ni sa. mra be mli kpamɔ Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ tsokolate ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni bean weight decreased Enɛ haa jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright heat. Fast-growing plantains act like living umbrellas that shield young cocoa from harsh sunlight while providing your family with food and extra income while waiting for the cocoa to produce.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ parasol ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni afee kookoo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without big ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ toi wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops end up fighting for the same sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving every seed proper spacing ensures the stems grow thick and produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa baa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rich soil is usually dark in color, smells earthy, crumbles easily in your hand when moist, and allows plant roots to grow deep without hitting hard rock layers. It also holds moisture well several days after it rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ. Efiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni enaaa tɛ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni mi hu midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Crops pull food nutrients out of the ground each time they grow. Over time, the soil gets tired and exhausted unless you restore its strength using compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii ni okɛwo mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread by planting infected stems. Planting improved, disease-resistant stem varieties provided by extension services keeps the crop healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ hiɛɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Adumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛtsɔ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsumɔi anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly even when there is light rain during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Light rains during hot periods evaporate off the soil surface before reaching the deep roots. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) holds water in the soil much longer.
ga: Drizzle yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha onibii ahe (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa amɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a harmful pest that feeds on young maize shoots. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or putting clean sand or ash into the center whorl of the plant can help destroy them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo okɛ ŋã loo sũ ni he tse fata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efite amɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, lacks sufficient water, or suffers from pest attacks. Watering your plants regularly during dry spells and controlling sucking insects will help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nu lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch easily under direct, hot sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or fast-growing shade trees planted nearby to shield them until their roots and branches mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni shwereɔ oya ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi eshishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ baadara.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry up the topsoil and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil stays consistently moist for young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa, ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ oomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha shishifãi bibii.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing food, sunlight, and moisture from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii, hulu la kɛ nu ni jɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year if I plant the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly. Rotating different crops, especially legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, helps naturally restore nutrients to the soil.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Titri lɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better to buy fresh certified seeds every season or use seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi? Aloo okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Certified seeds are specially treated and bred to produce higher yields and resist local diseases better. Seeds saved from past harvests gradually lose their vigor, resulting in smaller yields over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. hewalɛ ni baa shi Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves begin turning yellow and shedding. You can carefully dig up one plant to check if the tubers are thick enough before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome he nii koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in a hot, damp space. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn on raised wooden racks stops rot from developing and spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ Too sweet potatoes ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ. Ehaa fitemɔ baa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my farm land stop producing good cocoa yields after many years of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ ekpa kookoo yibiiwoo kpakpai yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, cocoa trees draw continuous nutrients from the soil. If you do not replenish the ground with compost, organic manure, or proper fertilizers, the soil becomes depleted and tired, leading to poor crop growth.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Cacao tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, humus, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: How can I tell if my soil has lost its power to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: If your crop leaves start turning yellow, plants remain stunted, or your harvest size drops significantly despite getting good rainfall, it means your soil is running dangerously low on essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo okpamɔ lɛ dalɛ eba shi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. No tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ oshara nɔ.

english: What can I plant on my land to make tired soil fertile again?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Planting leguminous crops like beans, groundnuts, or cover crops helps take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring the land's strength for future planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: Why do some crops like cocoa take years to harvest, while crops like maize produce in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ kookoo, heɔ afii babaoo dani akpaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that invests its early years into building strong roots and branches for long-term production, whereas maize is an annual crop designed to complete its entire life cycle in one short season.
ga: Cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ daa ni akɛwo mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. koni akɛfee shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa kɛha nitsumɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Abele ji daa afi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni egbe ewala be fɛɛ naa yɛ be kukuoo kome mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as dry spells, low soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Keeping the soil moist and controlling pests prevents flower drop.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow reduces the humidity that the fungus needs to survive.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ aba shi.

english: How does shade from bigger trees affect the way my cocoa crops grow?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight, but mature trees need balanced light to produce pods. Too much shade reduces yield, while too little sun causes heat stress.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia la ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Shade babaoo baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la fioo pɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa.

english: Is it good practice to plant food crops like cassava together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baadu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with food crops like plantain or cassava provides shade for your young cocoa plants while giving your family food and quick income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo bibii ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava duɔ. Ebaaha okokoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa weku lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛnáa shika oya yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I grow other crops on my farm instead of focusing only on cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ baama kookoo nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Relying on a single cash crop leaves you vulnerable if market prices fall or diseases hit your farm. Diversifying with food crops or vegetables gives you steady income and food security throughout the year.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ bo woɔ oshara mli kɛji jara nɔ jara ba shi loo hela ba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Niyenii ni aduɔ loo aduawai srɔtoi ni ooofee lɛ haa onáa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does the amount of crop harvest I get change so much from one year to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ?

english: Harvest amounts change due to variations in rainfall patterns, changing pest populations, weather conditions, and declining soil fertility. Regular soil maintenance and proper pruning help make your yields more consistent.
ga: Nikpamɔ falɛ tsakeɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi sɔrɔtoi ahewɔ. Tsakemɔi yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ mli, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa onibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are my harvested tomatoes turning soft and rotting so quickly before I can get them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly because heat and trapped moisture cause small bacteria and fungi to break down the fruit's skin. Keeping harvested tomatoes in a cool, shady spot with good airflow stops heat from building up and prevents rapid rotting.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ la ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa helai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ fiteɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baatsi dɔlɛ naa koni ekafee nɔ ni fiteɔ oya.

english: How should I store my harvested tomatoes if the market buyers do not show up on time?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tomato ni mikpa lɛ ato tɛŋŋ? Kɛji jara nɔ hɔlɔ lɛ ebaaa yɛ be naa

english: Store your tomatoes in shallow, well-ventilated crates under a cool shade rather than in deep piles or closed plastic bags. Piling them too deep traps heat and crushes the bottom fruits, which makes the whole batch spoil very fast.
ga: Kɛ tomato awo adekai ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ shishi Moŋ lɛ, too tomatoi yɛ ŋtayaai ni mli kwɔlɔ amli loo yɛ plastic kotokui ni aŋã mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ ahi shi ni ebaakumɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsɔne muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ oya waa.

english: At what stage should I pick my tomatoes from the plant so they do not spoil on the road?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mafo tomato kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ koni ekafite yɛ gbɛ nɔ?

english: Pick your tomatoes when they just start turning light pink or orange rather than full red. They will safely continue ripening on their way to the market without becoming too soft or bruised during transport.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomatoi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse yɛ red ni yeɔ emuu lɛ najiaŋ. Amɛbaatsa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ loo lɛ efeee bɔdɔɔ tsɔ loo ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔ beni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Can I pack fully ripe red tomatoes together with green tomatoes in the same basket?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tomato tsuru ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ tomato eŋɔli awo tsɛnsi kome mli?

english: It is best to separate them because fully ripe tomatoes release a natural gas that forces nearby green tomatoes to ripen and soften too quickly. Separating them keeps the crop fresh for longer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara tomatoi lɛ amli ejaakɛ tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyɛɔ tomatoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee blɛoo oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala amɛmli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to transport tomatoes in ventilated wooden crates instead of plastic sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ tomato baawo tso adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli fe plastic kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Ventilated crates allow cool air to pass through and protect the fruit from being squeezed. Plastic sacks trap heat and squash the tomatoes together, which causes fast bruising and decay.
ga: Krɛtii ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaaa akamɔ aduawai lɛ amli. Plastic kotokui lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli ni amɛshwieɔ tomatoi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants need wooden sticks to hold them off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛbaamɔ tomato lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato vines are weak and get heavy with fruit. Tying them to wooden sticks keeps the leaves and fruits off the damp soil, preventing ground pests and fungal diseases from rotting the crop.
ga: Tomato wain tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ fĩ tso he lɛ, ehaaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Should I pour water directly over the leaves and fruits of my tomato plants or at the base?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse nu yɛ tomato baai kɛ aduawai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: Always water at the base of the plant near the roots. Wetting the leaves and fruits directly creates a moist surface that encourages fungal diseases and fruit rot under the warm sun.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, shwiemɔ nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ aduawai lɛ amli fitemɔ he hewalɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open after a heavy rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry plant gets sudden heavy rain, the fruit absorbs water too quickly and expands faster than its skin can stretch. Harvesting mature tomatoes just before heavy rains helps avoid split and spoiled fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ni egbi lɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa lɛ Yibii lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Tomato ni ekwɛ̃ ni ajieɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ haaa aduawai lɛ mli agbala ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my green tomatoes get flat, dark spots at the bottom while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by 'blossom end rot,' which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb nutrients properly.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ ‘Blossom tip rot,’ ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo aha amɛ nu be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛbaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral sicknesses or by the plant lacking water. Protecting young plants from insects and keeping them watered prevents this stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. loo kɛjɛ tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ amli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ haomɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When cassava stakes are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows them to capture full sunlight and direct energy into swelling big underground roots instead of stretching upward.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ekɛ ehewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi wuji ni efuu lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ ehe kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why should I wait for a heavy rain to soak the ground before planting my maize seeds instead of planting after the first light shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A light shower only wets the surface, which dries out quickly in the sun and can cause sprouted seeds to die. Waiting for a deep soak ensures the soil holds enough moisture down deep for young roots to establish successfully.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ agbo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ aye omanye.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp wet soil, which prevents rot and helps the leaves capture maximum light.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni enine ashɛ hulu ni fa nɔ koni ekɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa egbo, ni ehaa baai lɛ náa la babaoo.

english: Pruning lower branches opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can circulate. This keeps the trunk dry, prevents fungal pod rot diseases, and encourages the tree to produce bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji

english: Extreme heat and inconsistent watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy. Giving plants steady moisture at the root level and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool and preserves the blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away nitrogen or drown roots in waterlogged soil, preventing the plant from taking up food. Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which can be fixed once the soil drains and fertilizer is applied.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen loo ekɛ shishifãi awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow vegetables without spending money on a lab test?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ laboratori mli kaa he?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds water like a wrung-out sponge, and contains living creatures like earthworms, which show that the soil is full of natural nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ nu tamɔ sponji ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli Ni bɔɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds always sprout and grow so much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to your soil, so they react instantly to moisture. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing light, water, and soil nutrients from your slow-starting crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, amɛfeɔ amɛnii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni jeɔ shishi blɛoo lɛ amli.

english: What is the white powder appearing on my pepper leaves, and why are they curling up?
ga: Mɛni ji powda yɛŋ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew that thrives in warm, humid weather. Spacing your plants apart to improve airflow helps keep the leaves dry and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ atse tsei amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshwɛ tso ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛ su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize crop so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when given in two stages: apply a small amount about two weeks after planting when roots appear, and apply the rest when the plants reach knee-height right before they start flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛha yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Akɛwoɔ mli fioo fioo aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ eje kpo lɛ. Ni okɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ afata he beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe dani ebɔi fɔmɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a cleared open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava planted around them to block direct heat and keep the soil cool while they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, wet air. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and wind into your farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them in heavy clay or poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine eshwɛ yɛ he. amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden poles or planting them deeper in rich soil prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi loo okɛdu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if small pests damage the blooms. Regular watering and mulching the base helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by fungal or bacterial diseases living in the ground that destroy roots. Rotating your pepper crops with maize or cassava helps clean the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Pepper tsei ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow very small and produce small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo kwraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy thieves that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small worms inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the growing centers of young maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and using approved organic or recommended crop sprays helps stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fresh and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ efee ehee ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Ripe and fresh cocoa pods change color from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. When you tap a ripe pod, it makes a hollow sound because the seeds inside have detached from the pod wall.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃, ni ehee lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ atswa ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaafee gbee ni mli ewo muji ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejie ehe kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ gbogbo lɛ he.

english: Why is it so physically difficult to harvest cocoa pods that grow high up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods grow along the main trunk and high branches. Cutting high pods requires using long poles with sharp hooks, which take significant physical strength and balance to cut cleanly without damaging the tree.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ kɛ eniji ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni aaafolɔ pods kakadaŋŋ lɛ biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmei ni mli wa yɔɔ mli. Enɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa babaoo koni enyɛ efo tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: What tools can help women or smaller farmers harvest cocoa pods more easily?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii baanyɛ aye abua yei loo okwaafoi bibii ni amɛkpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ mlɛo?

english: Using lightweight telescopic harvesting poles and sharp gooseneck hooks makes harvesting much easier, allowing farmers to cut pods high on the tree without excessive heavy lifting or climbing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni tsiimɔ waaa kɛ gooseneck hook ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfoɔ tsei amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni amɛwooo nɔ loo amɛkwɔɔɛɛ nɔ tsɔ.

english: How do I know if the cocoa beans inside a harvested pod are still fresh and good?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ yɛ ehee lolo ni ehi?

english: Fresh cocoa beans are tightly packed inside the pod and covered in a sweet, moist white pulp. If the pulp looks dark, dry, or slimy, the pod is overripe or damaged and the quality will be low.
ga: Akɛ kookoo yibii heei woɔ ŋmeii amli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni edɔ haa nɔ. Kɛji loo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ediŋŋ, egbi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ fe nine loo efite ni ehilɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do I need to be careful not to tear the branch when cutting off a cocoa pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔkwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni wɔkakumɔ tsei aniji kɛ́ wɔmiifolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods grow from tiny spots on the tree called flower cushions. Tearing the stem damages this cushion, which stops the tree from ever producing flowers or pods at that spot again.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Yɛ tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower cushions lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ otsi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaafite kushɛŋ nɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii krokomɛi yɛ nakai beaŋ.

english: Why is it important to have an experienced farmer inspect my farm before harvest starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaafonyo ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani ekpa nii lɛ?

english: An experienced farmer or extension officer can accurately spot which pods are fully ripe across the farm, ensuring you do not waste time or ruin crop quality by picking unripe pods.
ga: Okwaafonyo loo ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baanyɛ atsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofiteɔ be loo ofiteŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eshɛko ni ohalaa lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa if I accidentally harvest pods that are not fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cocoa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ oshara kpata ŋmeii ni eshɛko kwraa lɛ?

english: Unripe pods have low sugar content in their white pulp, which prevents proper fermentation. This leaves the final cocoa beans tasting bitter and flat, leading to lower prices from buyers.
ga: Pods ni edako lɛ yɛ sugar fioo yɛ loo yɛŋ lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa naa Enɛ haa naagbee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ jara baa shi.

english: Why does harvesting cocoa require special technique rather than just pulling the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ ŋaai krɛdɛɛi moŋ fe ni aaagbala aduawai lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting requires precise cutting close to the pod using sharp blades. Pulling or twisting pods snaps the delicate flower cushions off the trunk, permanently reducing future harvests.
ga: Nikpamɔ biɔ ni afo pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ pod lɛ he kɛtsɔ dade ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala loo atsake ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔii akutsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ajɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afeɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: How many days can fresh cocoa pods stay on the ground after harvesting before I must break them open?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ, gbii enyiɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ehe baahia ni akumɔ amɛ?

english: Harvested pods should ideally be cracked open within 2 to 5 days. Keeping pods whole for a few days helps sweeten the beans, but waiting longer than a week causes beans to spoil or germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ mli agbala mli yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 5 mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ehi shi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. Shi kɛ́ omɛ fe otsi kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I check if a harvested cocoa pod has disease before I open it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji hela yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni mikpa lɛ amli dani magbele?

english: A diseased pod often shows dark brown or black patches, feels unusually light or soft, and lacks the firm, bright skin of a healthy, fresh pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pods ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ. Henumɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo bɔdɔɔ ni bɛ hewolo ni mli wa, ni kpɛɔ ni ji pods heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy, or that too much water around the roots is stopping them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ baai. loo nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ tsiɔ lɛ gbɛ koni ekamu.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot or when they lack water, which stresses the plant and prevents the flowers from forming fruits.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu faaa yɛ emli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall and leafy but not producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of flowering and producing peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in intense heat to shrink their surface area, which helps the plant reduce water loss so it can survive the hottest part of the day.
ga: Ha ni curl lɛ mli adɔ koni ehiɛ he lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa tree branches have sticky white spots and curling leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Sticky white spots are caused by mealybugs, tiny insects that suck the sap out of your cocoa tree and can spread harmful viral diseases across your farm.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔɔ Mealybugs ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni shwieɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛbaa. ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers developing strange swollen bumps and rotting quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ jieɔ fuumɔ kɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kpo oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Swollen bumps are caused by tiny worms in the soil called nematodes that bore into the yam skin, opening paths for rot and bacteria to enter.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni boteɔ sweet potato hewolo mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ baa. Enɛ gbeleɔ gbɛ kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ koni amɛbote mli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels crumbly in your hands, holds moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms and decaying leaves that feed your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ enine mli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ ni akɛbaahã onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it safe for me to spray chemical medicine on my cabbage a few days before I harvest and sell it at the market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ kaabe nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: No, spraying chemicals close to harvest leaves dangerous poisons on the crop that can make consumers sick; you must wait the required days stated on the chemical container before harvesting.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ nikpamɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ hela amɔ amɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi gbi ni atsɔɔ yɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ dani okpa.

english: Cassava roots start to spoil almost immediately after harvest because exposure to air causes rapid chemical breakdown, so they must be eaten, sold, or processed quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, kɛ́ tsofai lɛ bote kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ afite oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aye, ahɔ̃ɔ, loo atsu he nii oya.

english: How can I prevent my stored maize from growing mold that makes my family and animals sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ ni ekɛ hela aba miweku lɛ kɛ kooloi lɛ anɔ?

english: Mold grows when grains are stored while still wet; drying your maize thoroughly in the sun on clean sheets until the grains are hard and dry stops dangerous mold poisons from growing.
ga: Mold daa kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ saatso ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree has the Swollen Shoot disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-koko tso lɛ mli ŋmeii efuu?

english: Swollen Shoot disease causes the leaves of cocoa trees to show red vein patterns or yellow patches, and you will notice unusual swollen bumps or thick swellings on the young stems and branches.
ga: Bud swollen hela lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ baai lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii tsuru loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Ni obaana fũu ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ loo fũu ni mli wa yɛ tsei akutsei kɛ tsei aniji bibii anɔ.

english: Why do the stems and branches of some of my cocoa trees look abnormally thick and swollen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmli edɔ ni amɛfuu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Abnormal swelling on cocoa stems is a physical reaction of the tree to the Swollen Shoot virus, which disrupts the natural flow of nutrients inside the plant.
ga: Fuumɔ ni ejaaa ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa yɛ Swollen Shoot hela lɛ he, ni no tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Can I spray chemical medicine to cure a cocoa tree that already has Swollen Shoot disease?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ anɔ?

english: No, Swollen Shoot is caused by a virus for which there is currently no chemical cure; the only way to stop it from spreading to healthy trees is to completely cut down the infected tree.
ga: Dabi, hela ko ni tsofa ko bɛ ni tsaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fuumɔ lɛ ba. Gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli ji ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kwraa.

english: How does Swollen Shoot move from one cocoa tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te Swollen Shoot lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ ejɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The virus is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs, which suck sap from infected trees and carry the disease to neighboring healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Koolooi bibii gbɛɔ helai amli. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. ni shwieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting down infected trees instead of just trimming off the bad branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni abaajie tsei niji ni ehiii lɛ?

english: Once a tree catches the Swollen Shoot virus, the infection lives in the entire system, including the roots, so trimming branches will not stop the rest of the tree from spreading the virus.
ga: Kɛ tso ko mɔ Swollen Shoot hela lɛ, hela lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ fata he No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haŋ hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: Has the Swollen Shoot disease always been in Ghana, or when did it start affecting our cocoa?
ga: Ani Bud Swollen hela lɛ yɛ Ghana be fɛɛ be loo ebɔi wɔ kookoo lɛ he hewalɛ?

english: Swollen Shoot disease is not new; it was first officially recognized in cocoa farms in Ghana around the year 1938 and has been a major focus of cocoa health programs ever since.
ga: Hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ jeee nɔ hee. Akpɛlɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana aaafee afi 1938 mli, ni eji nɔ titri ni kookoo hewalɛnamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ kɛjɛ nakai beaŋ kɛbaa nɛɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant new cocoa seedlings right away on land where old trees died from Swollen Shoot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei momoi egboi yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahewɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to wait and ensure all infected roots and host plants are completely removed first, because leftover roots can harbour mealybugs that will infect your new young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni okwɛ akɛ ajie shishifãi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ mealybugs ni baaha o-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ aná hela.

english: Why is it recommended to plant a row of crops like oil palm or citrus around the border of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mu loo citrus ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ he lɛ? Mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ husui
