english: Planting non-cocoa trees around your farm creates a physical barrier that stops mealybugs carrying the Swollen Shoot virus from crawling in from neighboring farms.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni ooodu yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaha gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko aba ni tsiɔ mealybugs ni hiɛ Swollen Shoot hela lɛ naa koni amɛkajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli aba.

english: How many years after planting should I expect my young cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually begin producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years if they are properly shaded, watered, and protected from disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ ahã amɛ hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ nu ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods dry up and turn dark before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Pods can stop growing and die early when the tree is weakened by diseases like Swollen Shoot or fungal infections, which cut off the food and water supply to the growing pods.
ga: Pods lɛ baanyɛ akpa dalɛ ni amɛgboi oya kɛji helai tamɔ crown swelling loo fungal infection ha tso lɛ gbɔjɔ. ni ŋmɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the soil cool and moist, acting as a natural umbrella while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ maa shi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is fertile enough for planting maize without paying for expensive lab tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni miwooo laboratori mli kaai ni jara wa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: Healthy, fertile soil usually looks dark, holds moisture well, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms or decaying leaf litter. If the soil is pale, hard, or sandy, it lacks nutrients and will need organic manure or compost mixed in before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ duŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni fiteɔ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ewa, loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ atsu nii dani adu.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he kome.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to build thick, strong stalks and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso lɛ mli tso ni mli wa ni mli wa. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress and inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist around the roots during flowering prevents the plant from getting stressed and losing its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná haomɔ ni efɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up, turn yellow, and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Curled, yellowing leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting helps protect your crop from this virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: If I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my cassava, will the beans steal food from the cassava plants?
ga: Kɛ midu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, Ani ŋmei lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, legumes like cowpeas and beans actually add nutrients to the soil by pulling nitrogen from the air and trapping it in their roots. When grown together, beans feed the surrounding soil and help the cassava grow better.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people cut off some of the leafy side branches on tomato plants instead of letting everything grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ tomato tsei aniji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Removing small side shoots (suckers) forces the plant to send its energy, food, and water straight into growing big, juicy fruits rather than wasting resources on unnecessary leaf growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ, niyenii, kɛ nu tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni mli edɔ ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ baa ni he ehiaaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my yam seeds at the very beginning of the rainy season rather than later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting early allows yam roots to settle deep into the warm soil so the vine can capture maximum sunlight over a longer period, resulting in much larger tubers at harvest time.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my crop seedlings after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with hardy root systems that allow them to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from shading your seedlings and taking away their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni amɛkajie niyenii.

english: Are there simple tools available locally in Ghana that can help me harvest cassava without breaking the roots in dry soil?
ga: Dɛŋdadei ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ. Ani maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhe ko yɛ Ghana ni baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa ŋmei ni efiteee shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, manual cassava harvesters and leverage lifting tools made locally in Ghana allow you to grip the base of the stem and lift the entire root bundle cleanly out of hard soil without snapping or damaging the tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛkpaa ŋmei kɛ lever lifter ni afee yɛ Ghana lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ ni owóɔ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ. ni efoŋ loo efiteee yitso lɛ

english: Leaves turn yellow when the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea early in the plant's life helps it regain its deep green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ eshihilɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ ebatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-fertilized helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight without protection. They need shade from plantain leaves or larger forest trees to keep them cool and protect soil moisture while their roots are growing.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantain baai loo koo mli tsei wuji amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Will my cassava tubers grow bigger if I plant the stem cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ baadara kɛji midu tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: No, planting cassava too close together causes plants to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to small roots. Spacing stem cuttings properly gives each plant enough room to form large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa shishifãi bibii baa. Tso lɛ yitso ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the cool temperature lets the roots absorb moisture. Watering during afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate quickly before plants can use it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa oya dani tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: How does adding dried plant leaves and animal manure into my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ahe baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic materials like dead leaves and animal manure rot into compost, which acts like a sponge to trap moisture in the soil while slowly feeding essential nutrients to your crops over time.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛmɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: What causes small holes to appear inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Eje kpo yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the fresh foliage. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays into the funnel early stops them from destroying the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsɔnei lɛ amli mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil. Regular weeding ensures that your main crops get all the food and light they need to stay strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops inside a greenhouse produce better yields than those I plant in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses shield crops from harsh weather, excessive heat, and insect pests while maintaining consistent warmth and moisture, allowing crops like tomatoes and peppers to grow continuously without stress.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. hulutsoo ni fe nine kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Yaa nɔ eda ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my crops curl their leaves and drop flowers when the dry harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi beni Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds dry out the air and soil rapidly, making plants lose water faster than their roots can drink. Leaf curling and flower dropping are natural self-defense reactions to prevent the plant from drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: What happens to my crops if the major season rains start late this year?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi yɛ afi nɛɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: When major season rains are delayed, seeds planted too early may dry up in the soil or produce weak plants. You should wait for steady rains before planting or switch to short-duration seed varieties.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi loo eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani odu loo otsake kɛya dumɔwui henɔi ni yeɔ be kukuoo nɔ.

english: Why are my corn crops dying even though I planted them around the usual time of year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miigbo lɛ? Mɛni miduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli?

english: Planting dates depend on actual rainfall patterns rather than just calendar months. If rains are delayed, planting at the traditional time leaves crops stranded in dry soil during critical early growth.
ga: Dumɔ gbi damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ nɔ. Jeee kalanda nyɔŋ kome pɛ Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Dumɔ yɛ bei ni sa mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: What is the difference between the major season and the minor season for growing crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ be wuji kɛ be bibii ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ?

english: The major season provides the main, longer period of heavy rainfall best for high-yielding crops, while the minor season brings shorter rains suitable for quick-maturing crops.
ga: Be titri lɛ ji be titri ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ. Ehi kɛha tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli, ni enɛ hi kɛha tsei ni daa oya.

english: Can I still plant maize if the major season rains do not arrive early?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ mra yɛ prime time lɛ mli lɛ, ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa lolo?

english: Yes, but you must adjust your schedule to wait until steady rains fall, or switch to early-maturing maize varieties that need less time and water to produce full yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ otsake obe he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli koni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaya nɔ anɛ. Aloo tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmãa henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni biɔ be kɛ nu fioo dani eshɛ ŋmãa ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does maize seem to grow better in forest areas compared to drier regions during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ fe hei ni nu bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Forest zones naturally retain more soil moisture, have denser tree cover, and experience more reliable localized rain, helping water-sensitive crops like maize survive erratic weather.
ga: Kooi amli hei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. ni ana nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu sumɔɔ waa, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ mli.

english: Why is a farm in a neighboring district getting good rain while my farm is suffering from no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ kpokpai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainfall in Ghana can be very localized depending on nearby trees, land shape, and forest belts, causing one district to receive good showers while nearby areas remain dry.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ anɛ yɛ Ghana yɛ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Edamɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ koo lɛ mli linei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kpokpaa kome naa nugbɔ kpakpa yɛ be mli ni hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli egbi.

english: How does the region where my farm is located affect how my corn handles a lack of rain?
ga: Te kpokpaa ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-ŋmã lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ he nii eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Different regions have distinct soil types and vegetation cover; farms in forest belts retain underground moisture much longer during dry spells compared to open grassland areas.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei srɔtoi. Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kooi amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, kɛ akɛto jwɛi shikpɔji ni agbele naa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my corn need so much water during its early growing stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young corn plants rely heavily on consistent moisture to build deep roots and thick stems; without water early on, the plant stays stunted and cannot form healthy cobs later.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse. Kɛji nu bɛ kɛjɛ shishijee Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What can I do to protect soil moisture on my farm when the rain stops after planting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching), which shades the ground, keeps the soil cool, and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi (mulch) aha onibii ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture to plant corn during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a few inches deep into a ball; if it holds its shape without immediately crumbling, there is enough moisture to germinate seeds safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ inchi fioo komɛi amli kɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni efoŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: This usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen, an important food for plants. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the young top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant maize in the exact same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and encourages soil pests to build up. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ewoɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in cool, very wet, and dark conditions. Trimming extra tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm, keeping humidity low and stopping the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ waa, kɛ duŋ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsoi ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Keep humidity low and stop rotting.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look wrinkled like dry paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ wolo ni egbi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from underneath the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Sprays made from neem seeds can help keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Spray ni akɛ neem dumɔwui fee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny waste that looks like sawdust inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl of your plant. They chew through the leaves before they unfold, which can stunt the plant if not caught and treated early.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo otso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ he okadi. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ ni atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater collects and sits in the soil around the tubers for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off harmlessly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tuber lɛ he lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko baaa mɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain shoots dry out and stop growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ekpaa shweremɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot reach underground water far below the surface. Covering the ground around the stem with dry grass or leaves traps soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it bad for me to spray water directly onto my tomato leaves late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ tomato baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: When leaves stay wet overnight without sunlight to dry them off, fungus and bacteria easily grow on the damp leaf surface, causing black spots and leaves to rot.
ga: Beni baai lɛ edɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni hulu la bɛ mli koni amɛgbi. Fungi kɛ bacteria daa oya yɛ baa ni mli efɔ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ baai ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛha amɛhi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines grow slowly and look weak when I do not provide stakes for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miida blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ? Akɛni misaaa tso lɛ hewɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the vines up toward the sun, allowing the leaves to capture full sunlight and grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kpɛtɛ wain tso lɛ he koni ekwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni eha bulb lɛ agbo.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive. Without shade trees or plantain plants to protect them, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves and dries up soil moisture faster than their roots can absorb it.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni baabu he lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ebaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and cool conditions. Clearing excessive leaves and weeds allows sunlight and fresh air to flow through the farm, drying out moisture and reducing rot.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ jɛmɛ ejɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Baai kɛ jwɛi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the central vein usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or decomposed animal manure restores the leaf color and boosts crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli gbɛkɛ kome?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner funnel of maize plants. They hide deep inside during the daytime, so applying organic or approved chemical treatments directly into the plant funnel early in the morning or late evening works best.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli gbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does it matter whether I plant my cassava stems straight up or slanted in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei ni ja loo yɛ koŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree slant causes tubers to form close to the soil surface, making harvesting easier. Planting them straight upright makes tubers grow deeper into the ground, which requires much more strength to dig out.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo Kɛ́ adu shi jaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha bulbs lɛ adara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni biɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to create energy for root growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the leaves to capture maximum sunlight for bigger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa Ni oye obua baa lɛ ni ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni bulbs lɛ adara.

english: Why do elders say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. They pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny root nodules. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land exposes weed seeds buried in the topsoil to sunlight and moisture, which triggers them to germinate rapidly. Covering the bare soil with mulch or leaf litter blocks light and stops weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko loo baai sũ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi la naa ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants don't get enough water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Extra shoots (suckers) steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing all but one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant has enough energy to grow large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine (tso lɛ) juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why does my cassava look good on the outside, but turn out hard or rubbery when I cook it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ ahoo lɛ, ani ebaafee nɔ ni wa loo ebaafee tamɔ rɔba?

english: Visual appearance on the outside does not show the internal starch quality. Different cassava varieties have different cooking traits—some are rich in starch and boil soft quickly, while others are better suited for processing into gari or flour.
ga: Bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hi ha. Kasava henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni ahoɔ nii ahaa. Ekomɛi amli ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli, ni abaanyɛ ahoo amɛ koni amɛfee blɛoo oya. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ ni akɛfeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why does my cassava become lumpy when I cook it without adding enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mihoo ni mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa fataaa he lɛ?

english: Cassava starch requires a sufficient amount of water and heat to expand and bond smoothly. Without enough water during preparation, the starch cooks unevenly, creating dry, hard lumps.
ga: Tapioca starch lɛ biɔ nu kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ be mli ni asaa he lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaho yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbi ni wa baa.

english: Why do some cassava varieties need extra water to cook soft while others cook soft with very little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi biɔ nu babaoo kɛha ŋmeii ni ahoɔ lɛ blɛoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ nu fioo ko pɛ ahoo ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi fioo lɛ?

english: Varieties with high dry-matter content absorb a lot of water during boiling to break down the starch, requiring extra water in the pot, whereas varieties with higher natural moisture soften easily on their own.
ga: Henɔi ni nibii ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni ahoɔ lɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ nu kroko awo tsɛnsi lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ baafee mlɛo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How can I test my harvested cassava roots to know if they will cook well before taking them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa lɛ makwɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?

english: You can cut a small sample root near the stem; a fresh root that boils well will appear milky-white, clean, and firm inside, without dark vascular lines or dry fibers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo shishifã lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ. Shishifãi heei ni ahoo jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ futafuta tamɔ mliki, amɛhe tse, ni amɛmli wa. Là fãji ni tsuɔ loo tsɔji ni egbi bɛ mli.

english: Is it important for me to separate damaged cassava roots from good ones right after harvesting?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matse ŋmei shishifãi ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, sorting damaged roots immediately is essential because bruised or cut cassava spoils rapidly due to air exposure and can speed up deterioration in neighboring healthy roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie shishifãi ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni atswa loo afo lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ afite oya.

english: Why does cassava harvested from my farm cook well during the rainy season but stay hard when harvested in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Shi ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ akpa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Water availability directly affects root moisture and starch structure. During dry periods, cassava roots lose internal water and build more fiber, making them harder to cook soft.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ lɛ saa shishifãi lɛ amli nu kɛ starch lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ fiber babaoo. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo nii blɛoo.

english: How can I know which cassava stem cuttings to plant if I want cassava that boils quickly for quick family meals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso ni esa akɛ madu kɛji miitao ŋmei ni shãa oya kɛha weku niyenii?

english: You should ask your extension officer for sweet cassava varieties recommended for fresh boiling, which have high starch quality and low cyanide levels compared to bitter processing varieties.
ga: Esa akɛ obi extension officer lɛ yɛ cassava henɔi ni ŋɔɔ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ afee dãa hee lɛ he. Eyɛ ashikishaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ cyanide ni falɛ faaa kɛ akɛto ashikiŋshai ni afee amɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Does adding cold water while my cassava is already boiling on the fire affect how it turns out?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛbaafata he be mli ni tapioka lɛ miiho lɛ baaná nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, adding cold water suddenly drops the temperature in the pot, which shocks the cassava starch and can leave the center of the root hard.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsɛnsi lɛ mli la lɛ aba shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tapioca ŋmei lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ebaanyɛ eha shishigbɛ lɛ afee shiŋŋ.

english: Can the soil quality on my farm affect whether my cassava cooks soft or rubbery?
ga: Ani bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ baanyɛ aná mi-cassava lɛ ni ahoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ rɔba?

english: Yes, soils rich in organic matter and potassium help cassava build soft-cooking starch, whereas poor soils deficient in key nutrients produce rubbery, fibrous roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cassava starch ni ahoo lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni niyenii titrii bɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why does cassava spoil and lose its good taste within just two days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots undergo rapid natural breakdown as soon as they are detached from the living plant, meaning they must be eaten, processed, or properly stored right after harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ amɛtse amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ aye amɛ, atsu he nii, loo akɛto he jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akpa amɛ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees taking so many years before they produce fruits for palm nut soup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛha palm nut soup lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their first 3 to 4 years building strong root systems and trunks to support heavy fruit bunches later. Clearing weeds around them and applying proper fertilizer early on helps them grow faster so they can start fruiting sooner.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni baaye abua sɛɛ mli aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara oya koni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi mra.

english: Planting crops too close together actually reduces your total yield. When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small or poor-quality fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi woɔ yibii bibii loo nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and look tired during the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ amɛ ni amɛkpokpo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much moisture. It is a natural self-defense mechanism to survive heat, and the leaves usually stretch back out once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ dɔlɛ mli. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct, bright sunlight to grow strong stems. Under heavy shade, the plant wastes its energy stretching upward to search for light, which makes the stalk weak and prone to falling over before producing good cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni etso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi dani amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for healthy growth. The plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left and sends it to the young leaves at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ekɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does wild grass make my crops grow so slowly even when rain is falling regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds and wild grass have aggressive roots that consume the plant food and fertilizer in the soil before your main crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients and water go directly to feeding your crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yeɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu fɛɛ baa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground when heavy rains flood the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without draining away, it suffocates the roots and causes them to rot under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or too much rain at once. Keeping the moisture in the soil steady helps the flowers stay on the stem and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Removing extra side branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on weak leaves and stems. This forces the tomato plant to channel its food and water straight into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ amligbalamɔ nɔ lɛ, otsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu amaje tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my stored seed grains start spoiling or sprouting inside the sack before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli dani shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Stored seeds spoil or sprout early when they still contain trapped moisture or are kept in humid places. Thoroughly sun-drying seeds before bagging them keeps them dormant and healthy until you are ready to plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya kɛji amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo akɛto ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ oogbi dumɔwui lɛ dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkatsi amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: How can I know if the seeds I buy at the market will actually give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Good seeds are uniform in size, clean, free from insect holes, and certified by agricultural officers. Improved seed varieties are specially bred to withstand common crop diseases and harsh weather, yielding much more food than untraced seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, amɛhe tse, ni ŋmeii bu bɛ mli. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ Afee dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo baa fe dumɔwui ni atsuuu he nii ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do some improved maize seeds survive dry spells better than the seeds I saved from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ dumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Improved maize seeds are bred with strong roots and drought-tolerant traits. This helps the plant pull deep water from the soil and slow down water loss through its leaves during hot periods.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are signs of cassava mosaic disease, spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents the virus from damaging your crop and stopping root growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni helai nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ekpa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Clearing excess branches and weeds lets airflow and sunlight in, keeping the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Niji kɛ jwɛi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow greener and bigger when I plant cowpeas in the soil first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ agbo kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this stored nitrogen, which makes leaves greener and stalks stronger without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni ato. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eshishifãi lɛ hu waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small and loose even when I water them daily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages need rich soil nutrients, especially nitrogen and phosphorus, to build dense, heavy heads. Water alone is not enough; adding compost or manure provides the food the plant needs to form tight heads.
ga: Cabbage he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni akɛfeɔ yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsii Nu pɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee bulbs ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant maize in straight rows instead of scattering seeds across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows gives every crop equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. It also reduces the labor required for weeding and harvesting, making farm work much faster and less tiring.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa amɛnáa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa nitsumɔ ni he hiaa kɛha jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu baa shi. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ yaa oya ni ehaaa nijiaŋ aje wui kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants get leaf spots and rot when their branches rest on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ tsɔi ni egboɔ kɛ́ eniji lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Soil contains natural fungi and moisture that easily transfer onto leaves when they touch the ground. Tying tomatoes to upright wooden stakes keeps leaves dry and elevated away from soil diseases.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ oya kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tomato fĩ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛkwɔ kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit forms when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy and water. Providing light shade or mulching around the roots keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Ehaa hulutsoo loo ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam mounds dry out so fast after planting during the sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato pile lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji adu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture rapidly to the sun through evaporation. Covering your yam mounds with dry grass or leaves (mulching) shades the soil, trapping moisture beneath so the seed yam can sprout smoothly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha sweet potato ni ato lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishi koni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why am I not seeing any pests on my maize during the sunny part of the day, even though my crops are clearly being eaten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ mi-abele lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ eka shi faŋŋ akɛ ayeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ moŋ.

english: Pests dislike heat and bright light. As the sun comes up around 8 o'clock in the morning, they move deep into the middle funnel of the corn stalk to hide, making them invisible during the day.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ te shi aaafee 8 a.m. lɛ, amɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli koni amɛyatee amɛhe. Enɛ haaa ana amɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Where do pests go when the sun gets hot on my corn farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa kɛji hulu lɛ miitso yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When sunlight becomes strong in the morning, pests retreat deep into the center leaves of the maize plant where it is shaded, cool, and protected.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ tso waa leebi lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ hulutsoo, amɛhe jɔɔ ni abuɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How do pests react to daylight versus evening on a maize farm?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ helai feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkpɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ gbɛkɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: During bright daylight, pests hide deep inside the crop center to escape the sun, but in the evening they move out toward the surface leaves to feed.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, la kpɛɔ waa. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛjo hulu lɛ naa foi. Shi kɛ́ shɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, amɛfãa kɛyaa kɛbaa koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply pest treatments to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Evening is the best time to act against pests because they emerge from deep inside the corn leaves as daylight fades, making them vulnerable to treatment.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be mli ni amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaatsa amɛ.

english: Why is spraying pest control in the morning around 8 o'clock ineffective on my corn field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi aaafee 8 a.m. lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: By 8 AM, bright sunlight forces pests deep into the core of the corn plant where sprays cannot reach or touch them.
ga: Beni shɛɔ 8:00 a.m. lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsirɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛyaa ŋmãa tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni spray lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he loo eta he lɛ

english: Why does my extension officer tell me to treat my crops in the evening instead of daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu tsei gbɛkɛ mli moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: If pests enter or feed during the day, they remain hidden inside the plant until evening; treating in the evening targets them right when they come out.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ bote mli loo amɛye niyenii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaahi shi yɛ tsei amli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Gbi gbɛkɛ helatsamɔi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ beni amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: If I inspect my farm at midday and see no bugs on the leaves, does that mean my maize crop is safe?
ga: Kɛji mikwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shwane mli ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ mi-abele lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: No, an empty-looking plant during midday can still be heavily infested because pests hide deep inside the center funnel of the corn during hot daytime hours.
ga: Dabi, tso ni tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ mli lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the center leaves of my maize getting damaged when I cannot see any insects on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ efite lɛ? He ni anyɛɛɛ ana kooloi yɛ kpo nɔ?

english: Pests nest and feed deep inside the center whorl of the corn plant during the sunny hours, destroying inner leaves while staying hidden from sight.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ amɛshĩa ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpatamɔ mligbɛ baai lɛ ahiɛ, ni okɛ amɛ ato koni mɛi akakwɛ amɛ.

english: Why is it difficult to catch or spot crop-destroying animals on my farm during normal working hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mamɔ loo mana koolooi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nitsumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests are active when light is low; during daytime working hours, they burrow deep inside the plant structure where sunlight cannot reach them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛ́ la fioo pɛ yɔɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli nitsumɔ be mli lɛ Amɛfoɔ tsei amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why is morning time around 8 AM a bad time to go looking for pests on my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ 8:00 a.m. ji be ni ehiii ni esa akɛ mayatao tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Around 8 AM, the sun triggers pests to go deep into the middle of the corn plants, making it almost impossible to detect them during a morning walk.
ga: Aaafee ŋmɛji 8:00 a.m. lɛ, hulu lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛyashɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa eshwɛ fioo ni abaanyɛ ana amɛ yɛ leebi nyiɛmɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients in the soil or are getting too much standing water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back their healthy green color so they can produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ ni nitrogen niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eye amɛ loo amɛná nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni anyɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting cowpeas will make my soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special crops that have tiny helpful bacteria in their roots. These bacteria take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Muawai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood the soil and leave standing water, the roots suffocate and drown, which causes fungal rot to set in quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha nu lɛ ekã shi. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under the harsh direct sun. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaada waa.

english: Why should I train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ?

english: Yam leaves need to reach as much sunlight as possible to make food for the plant. Staking gets the leaves off the ground and spreads them out, which gives the plant energy to grow bigger, heavier tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ená shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: If too many small sucker shoots grow around one main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from the mother plant. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only the strongest one, ensuring your main plant produces a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ Too babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, niji ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ awo niji babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their tiny flowers before any cocoa pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baabɔi feemɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack. Providing light shade, keeping soil covered with mulch, and controlling sap-sucking pests helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi tutuaa hulutsoo ni kpɛɔ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting in the afternoon heat even though the soil still feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni migbooo lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During the hottest part of the day, pepper leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, and it usually recovers by evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack and split open right as they are turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛtsɔ tsuru lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden heavy watering or rainfall after a long dry spell. The inside of the fruit fills up with water and grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Tomatoi baatswa kɛ nu ni naa wa trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni eho lɛ sɛɛ. Nu eyi aduawai lɛ amli obɔ, ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Why does watering my vegetable farm in the late evening work better than watering at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu yɛ ŋtayaai abɔɔ lɛ mli gbɛkɛ mli? Ani ehi fe nu ni ashwieɔ yɛ shwane mli?

english: Watering in the hot sun causes much of the water to evaporate straight into the air before reaching the roots. Evening watering gives the soil and roots all night to soak up moisture deeply without heat stealing it away.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni hulutsoo lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or are getting flooded with too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and promotes healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ ni baanyɛ atsɔ nu afua mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, right after a light rain. If the ground is completely dry, the fertilizer cannot dissolve to reach the roots, while heavy rain immediately after application can wash the fertilizer away from your field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp conditions during the rainy season. Pruning heavy shade tree branches to let in light and harvesting ripe pods frequently helps prevent the fungus from destroying your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ ni oookpa koni la abote mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni oookpa shii abɔ lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Flower dropping usually happens when heat becomes too intense, watering is irregular, or the plant lacks nutrients like calcium. Maintaining a consistent watering schedule and using mulch to keep the soil cool helps the plants hold onto their flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ mli daa, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same farm plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during peak heat to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation. This is a natural defense, but if the leaves fail to uncurl by the cooler evening, it means your crop is suffering from severe drought stress and needs water.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieee shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ hu? No tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa miikpe ni nu he miihia amɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. You can test maturity by carefully digging up one plant to check if the roots are thick, firm, and full of starch before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka ehewalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso ko ni oootsa jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli eyi, amɛmli eyi, ni starch eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Dani abaakpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why should I expect some crop loss every harvest season even if I care for my farm well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite daa afi? ŋmaakpamɔ be Eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ

english: Natural factors like unpredictable weather patterns, minor pest damage, and handling losses during harvest mean almost no farm achieves a 100 percent yield. Expecting a small loss of around 10 to 30 percent is normal in farming, though good field hygiene minimizes these losses.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nibii ni elaaje lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmɔ ko bɛ ni woɔ yibii oha mlijaa 100. Nibii bibii ni baafite ni ji oha mlijaa 10 kɛyashi 30 ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ okwaayeli mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ nibii ni laajeɔ nɛɛ baa shi moŋ, shi.

english: How can joining a local farmers' group help me get government support and good seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ dumɔwui kpakpai?

english: Agricultural extension officers and government programs distribute subsidized fertilizers, improved seed varieties, and training mainly through registered farmer cooperatives. Being part of a recognized local group makes it easier to receive these inputs and expert advice on your farm.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ maŋ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi jaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake kɛ tsɔsemɔ titri kɛtsɔ okwaafoi akui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kuu ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ mli ni oyɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ obaaná saji nɛɛ kɛ ŋaawoi ni he esa ni kɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their small leaves lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Planting shade crops like plantains around them provides a living canopy that keeps them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Yɛ baai bibii lɛ ahewɔ Efiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni baaha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots underneath stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic waste, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and branches on top instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ nii babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji wuji yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize are a clear sign of nitrogen hunger. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to stay alive, showing that the soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye mɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni eji ŋmaa bibioo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for soil nutrients and water while their leaves fight for sunlight. Giving each crop enough space ensures every plant gets what it needs to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot on the stem during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity, which helps a micro-fungus spread rapidly over the pods and cause black pod disease. Pruning tree branches lets sunlight and breeze in to dry the pods and prevent rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo ni anaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmei lɛ mli fɛɛ oya ni ekɛ black pod hela baa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why does my plantain stem die after it finishes producing a bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo aduawai babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once. After harvesting, that main stem naturally dies so its energy can pass to the young sucker shoots growing around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie hewalɛ kɛya ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start shooting out green sprouts even while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock. After resting for a few months in storage, warm air and time trigger them to wake up and sprout in preparation for the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa yɛ mli. Beni ejɔɔ ehe yɛ nitoohe lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ be woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves or spreading a plant virus, causing the leaves to twist and stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever producing fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extremely hot temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making them sterile. When the flowers cannot be fertilized, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. and render sterile Beni fɔfɔi ko nyɛɛɛ afee fɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil microbes to pull natural nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot withstand intense, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the extreme sun causes the seedlings to lose moisture faster than their roots can drink, burning the leaves and killing the plant.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulu la babaoo bɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha baai ashã ni efite tsei.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the stems of my young cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi yucca tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young cassava for sunlight, soil nutrients, and groundwater. Clearing weeds ensures the cassava roots have full access to soil nourishment and don't get choked out early in their growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli yɛ shishijee bei ni edara lɛ amli

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is missing nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient needed to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni afee baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe dry heat or lack of soil water. The plant drops its blossoms to save its own life until moisture and temperature conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpe. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe kɛyashi hulutsoo kɛ latsaa baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Cabbage heads split when there is a sudden abundance of water—such as heavy rain after a dry period. The inside of the cabbage absorbs the water and expands faster than the outer leaves can stretch, causing the head to burst.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji nu babaoo ba trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Kaabaji lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni no haa yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: How come my okra plants grow very tall with big leaves but bear very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji shi pods fioo?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage rather than producing flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ashishifãi.

english: Why should I keep space between my tomato plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ abɔ he kroko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing plants allows sunlight and fresh air to flow freely around the leaves and stems. When tomatoes are crowded, moisture gets trapped between leaves, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases quickly spread from plant to plant.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe kɛji tomatoi lɛ eyi obɔ. Fɛ̃i boteɔ baai lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the soil when I plant them during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water in the soil starves the stems of oxygen and encourages soil fungi to attack the fresh cut ends, causing the stem to decay before it can sprout roots.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaawo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii ni afo ehee lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ fiteɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests if I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws specific nutrients out of the ground every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot wears out the soil's strength, whereas rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ Cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by waterlogging in heavy soils or microscopic pests like nematodes that wound the tuber, allowing destructive soil bacteria and fungi to enter and feed on the yam.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ sweet potato mli lɛ jɛɔ nu ni tsii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ nematodes, ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ehaa muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ sweet potato lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?
