english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient found in healthy soil or fertilizers that gives leaves their dark green color and helps produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji feɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the ground and improves harvest yields for the next crop planted there.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them from intense heat until they grow mature and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch sunlight, which allows the plant to produce the energy needed to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juice from the leaves, or passing along a plant virus that stunts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo tsei amli helai ni haa amɛdalɛ kpaɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do weeds in my field reduce my crop harvest even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the moisture, fertilizer, and soil nutrients meant for your plants, leaving the crops starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when the plant doesn't get enough water, causing it stress so it saves energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa ni no haa hewalɛ baa shi yɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I buy fresh seeds from the agricultural store instead of planting seeds saved from my last hybrid maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapo mli? Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, midu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee hybrid ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give high yields only in the first harvest. Seeds saved from that crop lose their special vigor, leading to uneven growth and much smaller yields the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and turn brown when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi tsei ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rainy season starts again, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth and dark green color. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔji lɛ ahewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ebua ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Beni okpaa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ baakã sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply solid fertilizer when my farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa fataaa he beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants cannot absorb dry fertilizer directly through their roots. The soil needs moisture to dissolve the fertilizer into a liquid form that the roots can drink up without getting burned by concentrated chemicals.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ atsɔ nu ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu ni tsofai ni mli ewo muji lɛ shãaa lɛ.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around a main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) dara kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain panicles ni dara ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves into maximum sunlight and keep them off the wet ground. This increased sunlight helps the plant make more food, leading to larger tubers, while keeping leaves away from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baawo tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ. Hulu la ni fa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do small holes appear in the leaves of my young maize plants early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ leebi?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are often caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which come out to feed on soft leaves during the cool night and early morning hours before hiding from the heat of the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa dani amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local soil conditions and have strong seed reserves in the ground. They are built to absorb water and soil nutrients instantly, allowing them to outpace domestic crop seeds.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ shia ŋmaa nɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop yield less harvest when I plant it in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the specific soil nutrients maize relies on and allows maize-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that plot over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abɛi lɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ baafite. ni eha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it safe for me to feed fresh cocoyam leaves directly to my farm stock?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ kookoo baai heei aha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh cocoyam leaves contain raw calcium oxalate crystals that cause irritation and itchiness in the mouth and gut. Wilting, drying, or cooking the leaves breaks down these compounds, making them safer and more digestible for livestock or farm stock.
ga: Kookoo baai heei lɛ amli calcium oxalate kristalo ni ŋmɔŋ ni haa mɔ mli fuɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa daaŋ kɛ fɔmɔ kotoku mli. Kɛ́ egbo, egbi, loo ehoo lɛ, efiteɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa kooloi loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi yeɔ niyenii.

english: Should I peel or boil cocoyam tubers before using them as feed on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli dani mikɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, preparing cocoyam tubers by peeling or heating reduces raw chemicals that cause throat irritation and stomach upset, ensuring your animals digest the energy-rich starch without health problems.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo shishifãi ni asaa he kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni ajieɔ loo ni akɛwoɔ la mli lɛ haa tsofai ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baanyɛ aha tsitsi lɛ mli afuu ni eha musu lɛ mli afuu lɛ baa shi. Ehaa okooloi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni haa hewalɛ babaoo lɛ mli ni helai ahe naagbai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do some cocoyam varieties cause a scratchy feeling when eaten, while others do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi komɛi haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛ́ aye lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi nuuu he lɛ?

english: Cocoyam varieties differ in their levels of microscopic calcium oxalate crystals. Red or wilder varieties generally contain higher levels of these itchy crystals than standard cultivated green cocoyam, requiring more heat or drying before consumption.
ga: Cocoyam henɔi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni calcium oxalate kristalo ni anaaa lɛ fa ha lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kristalo ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni yɔɔ tsuru loo koo mli lɛ yɛ mli fe kookoo eŋɔli ni akwɛɔ daa lɛ. ni biɔ ni atswa loo agbi dani aye

english: Why do I see clear water droplets dripping from the tips of my crop leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa nu ni mli tse ni miiho kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ?

english: This natural behavior is called guttation. During cool nights when humidity is high, plant roots absorb water faster than the leaves can evaporate it, forcing pure excess water out through small pores at the leaf edges.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ rumination. yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Tso shishifãi shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. kɛ nu ni atsuu he ni fa fe nine lɛ ni enyɛɔ enɔ koni etsɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli kɛje kpo

english: How can I tell if water on my crop leaves is natural morning dew or a sign of plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli leebi ŋmɔtɔ loo eji tso hela he okadi?

english: Morning dew sits as round droplets on top of leaves and dries quickly in the sun. Disease signs appear inside or under the leaf tissue, turning parts of the leaf soft, dark, mushy, or translucent.
ga: Leebi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ nu ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai anɔ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Hela lɛ he okadii jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ mli loo eshishi. Ehaa baa lɛ fãi komɛi feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I harvest outer leaves from my growing cocoyam plants without killing the main crop under the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa cacao tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ni mifiteee tso titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, you can harvest mature outer leaves periodically, provided you leave at least three healthy main leaves in the center so the plant can continue capturing sunlight to grow its underground tuber.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa kponɔgbɛ baai ni eda lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛ hoo lɛ, shi baai titrii etɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ koni tso lɛ aya nɔ aná hulu la koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my soil is too wet for growing cocoyam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ akɛ manyɛ makwɛ kookoo?

english: While cocoyam loves moisture, soil that remains waterlogged causes root rot, leading to soft stems, yellowing leaves, and stunted tubers. Healthy soil should feel damp but allow excess water to drain away.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ lolo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ bulbs ni egbɔjɔ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ shi eha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: What causes crop stems near the ground to suddenly turn soft, watery, and rot?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ashishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, nu, ni amɛgboɔ?

english: Soft, watery stems are usually caused by bacterial soft rot or fungal pathogens thrive in overly wet, poorly drained soil. Damaged roots in waterlogged conditions allow these organisms to enter and break down the stem tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Shishifãi ni efite yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: What kind of soil conditions give the best yields for cocoyam crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ haa anáa kookoo ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoyam grows best in loose, rich, loamy soils that retain moisture without staying completely flooded. High organic matter content gives the roots space to expand into heavy, healthy corms.
ga: Cocoyam daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ kwraa Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ mli he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli alɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: How does poor land drainage affect the overall health of leafy crops?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Poor drainage suffocates root systems by driving out air from the soil. Without oxygen, roots stop absorbing nutrients properly, causing leaves to turn pale, wilt, and drop prematurely.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: How can I test my maize seeds at home to know if they will sprout before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ makwɛ yɛ shia koni mana kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Take ten seeds and wrap them in a wet cloth for three days; if eight or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and good for full planting.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui nyɔŋma awo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii etɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii ekpaa loo nɔ ni fe nakai Odumɔwui lɛ baafee hewalɛ ni hi kɛha tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Should I try planting a new crop variety across my whole farm right away, or test it on a small piece of land first?
ga: Esa akɛ maka ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Aloo kaa he bibioo ko okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Always test a new crop variety on a small trial patch first to see how it grows in your local soil and climate before spending money on your whole field.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kaa tso hee ko okwɛ yɛ kaa he bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni edaa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Dani obaafite shika yɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them too weak to produce large fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa agbo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their blossoms without forming any pods during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages flower pollen, causing the plant to drop blossoms to save water and energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee fɛ̃i ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even when it rains every few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ daa gbii fioo komɛi po lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter or high sand content cannot trap water, letting rainfall drain away deeply before plant roots can drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ loo ŋã babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. Ha nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow much better when I plant them near cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ cowpea masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and storing it in their roots, which helps neighboring plants grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting from lack of water or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni bɛ loo hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Thirsty plants wilt during hot afternoons and recover overnight, whereas diseased plants stay wilted, turn yellow, or show spots regardless of watering.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baagbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛbaatsa amɛhe nyɔɔŋ kome mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baagbi. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ejie ŋmɔlɔ kpo ekɔɔɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he

english: Why do tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling protects the plant from burning in strong sunlight, but yellowing often signals heat stress or a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do young crop seedlings die quickly when weeds are left growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii gboiɔ oya kɛ́ jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and weak stems, so fast-growing weeds easily steal their sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize crop turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The crop moves available nutrients to its top growing leaves to survive, leaving the lower leaves starving.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Tsei kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisting up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and pale cassava leaves are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The disease stops the plant from making food efficiently, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni etsake ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baaná ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly dry up and die while the leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in green pepper plants is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease blocks the water channels inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper plant and causing it to collapse rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili tsei ni eŋɔli lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa nu ashɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni ehaa efoɔ oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates heavily. High heat damages the pollen, so the plant sheds the flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are my yam vines growing so thick and leafy, but the yams underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi yam lɛ ji nɔ ko bibioo kwraa?

english: Yam vines grow heavy leaf foliage when soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium. Nitrogen builds green leaves above ground, while potassium is needed to swell the root tuber below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni tsii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ feɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni potassium he hiaa koni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli alɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees drop their young fruit bunches before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii akui dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms drop young fruit bunches when they face severe water stress during dry spells or suffer from potassium deficiency. The palm drops its fruits to save water and keep the main tree alive.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii akui kɛji akɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa kpe yɛ hɔmɔ loo potassium ni faaa lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my crop help feed the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food. Leaving these roots in the soil naturally enriches it for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ nodes yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ ashi nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems adapted to grab soil nutrients and water immediately. Cultivated crops take longer to establish roots and can easily be overcrowded if weeds are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsakeɔ ehe kɛyaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsei ni adu lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi aba, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛyi obɔ kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ mra.

english: Why are my garden vegetables remaining weak and stunted even though I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from soil pockets to absorb nutrients. Overwatering fills up all soil air pockets and washes essential nutrients deeper into the ground, starving the plant roots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ buji amli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food they need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the topsoil or leaves the roots waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ loo eha shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When you plant maize after them, the maize uses that natural plant food to produce bigger stalks and ears.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji kɛ toi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the midday sun, their leaves burn and lose water faster than their roots can drink it.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulutsoo be lɛ naa lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why does the soil around my vegetable plants dry out and crack so fast after I water it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ ni egbɛɔ oya beni mikɛ nu wo amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil left exposed to the hot sun loses water quickly through evaporation. Covering the earth around your plants with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shades the soil and keeps the moisture trapped longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ashi yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil gets too dry. When the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and wither even when there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: When cassava sits in waterlogged soil for too long, its roots begin to rot underground. Once the roots decay, they can no longer suck up water for the plant, causing the leaves to wilt even in wet conditions.
ga: Beni ŋmei hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu amɛha tsei lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ po mli.

english: Why are my planted yam seed tubers taking so long to sprout out of the soil mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period after harvest called dormancy. If planted before this resting state ends, or if the soil mound is too hot and dry, the tuber stays dormant until conditions trigger it to grow.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji akɛ adu dani nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni bɛ shihilɛ mli nɛɛ ba naagbee. aloo kɛji gɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi Yitso lɛ baakã he ahi shi shiŋŋ. kɛyashi shihilɛi baawo lɛ hewalɛ ni eda.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies that damages leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbalaa baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid weather, or by sap-sucking insects like capsids that puncture the pod and damage its tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni efiteɔ fãji lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my maize growing so poorly in areas where small weeds with pink flowers are present?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni jwɛi bibii ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Those plants with pink flowers are likely Striga, also known as witchweed. Striga attaches its roots directly to your maize roots underground, stealing water and nutrients meant for your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ tso ni yɔɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ witchweed. Striga kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ o-corn shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. koni oju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants get burned easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like large shade umbrellas, protecting the delicate cocoa seedlings and keeping the soil cool while they grow.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves out in the sun to make food. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows maximum sunlight reach and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe babaoo, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. When soil lacks nutrients, the plant moves what little food it has to its top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abele bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when we get heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows water-loving fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi. ni eha ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ atutua ni ekɛ tuber rot aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and become small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juice from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. The damaged leaves cannot grow normally and shrink into tight curls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛshwie shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat or water stress stops the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: If too many small shoots grow around one plantain stand, they fight with the main mother plant for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Ekɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ baawu koni ená nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why is it better for me to transplant my vegetable seedlings late in the afternoon instead of at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ adu shwane mli moŋ fe shwane?

english: Moving seedlings in the middle of the day exposes them to hot sun when their roots cannot soak up water yet, causing severe wilting. Transplanting in the cool afternoon gives them all night to rest and adapt.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa amɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa baa. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shwane ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ haa amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɔ shi gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops remain small and weak when weeds grow close to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛhe waaa beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; their roots grow faster and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops before your crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer helps the plants regain their green color and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee dumɔwui akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees often shed flowers when stressed by extreme sun, drought, or insect pests like mirids (akate). Providing light shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects allows flowers to develop into mature pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (akata) lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is typically caused by a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and using disease-resistant seed varieties stops the spread and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ni akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baakpa gbɛfaŋnɔ ni eha tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during high winds before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stem with strong bamboo or wooden stakes helps the plant hold the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ etsiimɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants are vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to catch more light, resulting in much larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa la babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji babaoo baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in slow-draining soil. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle properly before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Sowing seeds into dry soil or right after a single light rain can cause seeds to dry out or germinate poorly. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures the soil holds enough moisture for young roots to establish.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo amɛkwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers on very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause pepper plants to drop flowers to save energy and protect themselves. Watering early in the morning and placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and helps flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Nu leebi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi yɛ jɛmɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds regularly keeps all the available plant food focused on growing your crops quickly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ onibii ni oookwɛ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant all my crop seeds very close together in one small spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves all the plants weak, thin, and prone to poor yields or disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai loo helai baa amɛnɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainfall dates keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Yɛ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry out, while waiting too long misses the best growing window. You should plant right after the soil receives enough steady rainfall to stay consistently moist for several days.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi. Shi kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ oshɛɛɛ dalɛ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Esa akɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects like midges to transfer pollen between flowers. If there are no beneficial insects around, or if heavy rain or harsh chemicals wipe them out, the unpollinated flowers simply drop off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii hia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo tsofai ni mli wa tsumɔ he. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛkɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and crowded conditions. Pruning excessive shade trees and weeding helps sunlight and air dry out the pods, preventing the rot from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, so adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore leaf health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear out extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drain water and food away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one strong sucker ensures the mother plant has enough energy to produce heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine loo suckers lɛ hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo kɛjɛ mli ni ashi sucker ni mli wa kome pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee panicles ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain small and thin when harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand. If the soil is too hard, compacted, or poor in nutrients, the roots cannot grow thick and plump underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛmli alɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my farm develop more crop diseases when the trees create thick shade over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ahe helai babaoo yɔɔ be mli ni tsei feɔ hulutsoo ni tsii kɛhaa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Thick shade blocks sunlight and traps moisture near the crops. Dark, humid conditions make it very easy for fungal diseases and rot to attack leaves and fruits.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize alongside my young cocoa trees without damaging them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with crops like plantain or maize helps protect the young cocoa seedlings from direct burning sunlight while providing food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo ŋmei du kookoo tsei bibii lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the soil around my plants help them stay healthy during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root zone cool, and prevents direct hot sunlight from drying out the earth.
ga: Hay ni aduɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nutrients like nitrogen, which acts as food for crop growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant what it needs to make fresh green leaves and grow healthy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tsei adalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdu ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops instead of letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? mi tso bibioo Moŋ lɛ, ha amɛfee ekome kɛdara.

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and space they need to grow strong and yield a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the roots of my yam vines rot when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, well-drained soil with air pockets to breathe and expand. When water stands on the field for too long, it chokes the roots by cutting off air, allowing rot organisms in the soil to attack the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni etsɔɔ nɔ emuɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ nu damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaagbe shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves curl up and roll inward during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a cocoa tree's natural defense to protect itself from losing too much moisture in severe heat. Planting shade trees like plantain or shade-providing forest trees reduces direct sun exposure and keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni ekɛbuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow tall and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava stems stretch tall and skinny because they are competing with neighboring plants for sunlight. Giving each cassava stem enough space allows it to spread out, capture full sunlight, and direct its energy into growing large underground roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ aha cassava tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha egbɛ eshwa. Naa hulu la ni fa ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they get stressed by sudden dry soil, intense heat, or pest damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist using organic mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers until young tomatoes form.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic mulch tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tomato bibii baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fresh peppers after I pick the first batch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ beni mifo mi klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants pause production when soil nutrients run low or when overripe peppers are left on the branches for too long. Harvesting ripe peppers promptly and feeding the soil with compost encourages the plant to keep producing new blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ ashi pepper ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ otsi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi heei.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully matured underground and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts signal maturity above ground when their leaves turn yellow and begin to drop. You can confirm by pulling up one plant to check; if the insides of the pod shells have turned a dark brownish color, the crop is mature.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ tso kome ni oootsi kɛya ŋwɛi koni okwɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Blackened cocoa pods are typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp and overly shady farms. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunshine and airflow through the farm, drying out the moisture that helps the fungus spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need sufficient soil moisture and warm conditions to break out of dormancy and shoot new roots. If planted in dry soil or cut improperly at the base, the sucker will pause its growth until proper moisture returns.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ koni amɛje shihilɛ ni amɛwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwo shishifãi heei. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo kɛji akɛ afolɔko shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Suckers lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that heavy rain has waterlogged the soil and prevented the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, ni no haa nu ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are placed too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf vegetation above ground rather than swelling its tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo akɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my field help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Large shade trees act like umbrellas that protect fragile seedlings from getting heat-scorched and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ waa he ni ehaa sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right after they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni ebɔi yibiiwoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily be damaged by tiny soil pests like nematodes or stem borers, leaving the plant too weak to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why is it important for me to lift and stake my yam vines off the ground using sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tso nɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground into direct sunlight so they can feed the plant better, while also preventing wet leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I water my vegetable farm during the middle of the day when the sun is hottest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: No, watering during the intense midday heat causes most water to evaporate quickly before roots can drink it, and cool water drops left on hot leaves can stress the plant.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli ejɔ ni shwieɔ baa ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding in the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Akɛtee gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest that eats soft inner leaves and can destroy the plant's growing point if not caught early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli, ni ebaanyɛ efite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off before any peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to drop flowers instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my developing tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly between wet and dry.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ.

english: Why does rain wash away the topsoil on my hilly farm land, and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rainwater flowing down slopes carries away the nutrient-rich topsoil, leaving hard ground behind. Planting crops across the slope or using mounds helps slow down water runoff and keeps essential soil nutrients near the plant roots.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ yaa. Shi shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ yɛ sɛɛ Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ loo gɔji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crops grow much better in some parts of my farm plot than in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil quality, moisture levels, and sunlight vary across a single piece of land. Areas with deeper soil or better moisture retention nourish crop roots better, leading to faster and healthier growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, hulutsoo kɛ hulu la lɛ baasoro amɛhe yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni sũ ni mli kwɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa mɔ daa oya ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why does water gather around my crops and cause their roots to rot after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil traps water instead of letting it drain. Planting on raised soil beds creates channels that guide excess water away, preventing roots from drowning and rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeeha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛi ni kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yaa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote nu mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores green leaves and active growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither so quickly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops lose water rapidly through their leaves in high heat before their roots are deep enough to reach soil moisture. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and conserves moisture.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check if pests are damaging my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji ŋmeii miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Checking crops two to three times a week allows you to spot tiny pests or holes in leaves early. Finding pests early lets you remove them or treat the plants before the damage spreads across the entire field.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ amɛ loo ohereɔ tsei lɛ ayiwala dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shia lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take nearly a full year before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require several months to build up strong root systems and thick stems to support heavy fruit clusters. Continuous water and organic matter feed the plant so it can store enough energy to flower.
ga: Plantains he miihia nyɔji babaoo dani ená shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni baaye abua aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ. Nu ni yaa nɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato kɛha fɔfɔi.

english: How can I make sure my cassava farm produces big roots so I have enough for my household and extra to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji? No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shia nitsumɔ ni ekomɛi yɛ lolo ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Giving cassava plants enough space when planting allows roots room to expand without competing for nutrients. Early weeding in the first three months gives roots maximum access to light and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ oha o-cassava tsei lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdu lɛ, ehaa amɛgbɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa la kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last season's maize harvest yield smaller cobs when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛji midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from improved crop varieties lose their strength in the next generation. Using fresh certified seeds each planting season ensures high yields, strong stems, and better resistance to disease.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii yɛ shweremɔ be fɛɛ be mli lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba, shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ, ni helai hu nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if the soil stays flooded and drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very big leaves but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build large tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni efee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my groundnut plant flower above the ground if the nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers bloom in the open air to attract sunlight and insects for pollination. Once fertilized, the plant sends down long stems called 'pegs' that push into the soil where the nuts form.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ koni ekɛgbala hulu la kɛ kooloi kɛba koni amɛfee pollination. Kɛji akɛ awo mli lɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet seasons when rain droplets splash fungal spores from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie tsɛŋemɔ hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ,

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my yam farm produce bent and strangely shaped yams that are hard to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potato ni ebɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ ni ekpamɔ wa lɛ?

english: Yams become misshapen when the soil underneath them is hard, stony, or compacted, making it difficult for the tuber to push straight down into the earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture before I plant my cowpeas?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa dani madu tsina ŋmei?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a few inches deep. If it forms a loose ball without dripping water or crumbling immediately to dust, it has good moisture for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo komɛi. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni etse ehe ni nu shwieɔ shi loo efolɔ etsɔ sũ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaná hulutsoo kpakpa kɛha dalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells, which prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when roots are shallow due to hard soil, poor nutrients, or when stem borer insects weaken the inside of the stalk.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa hewɔ. niyenii ni ehiii Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli fã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong green growth. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, or the soil may simply be tired and need manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year. It also gives pests and diseases that love cassava a permanent home to multiply in your farm.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu. Honey, cassava yɛ shia ni baahi shi daa kɛha shweremɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden sticks to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni enine ashɛ bulbs wuji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber using their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into direct sunlight, helping the plant catch full light to manufacture more food for a bigger harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa la ni fa babaoo koni amɛwo niyenii babaoo kɛha kpamɔ babaoo.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread near the top of the soil rather than going deep. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the bunches grow heavy, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the mud.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ shɔŋŋ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni jwɛi lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ muji lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or dry, or if insects do not visit to shake the flowers to spread pollen. Extreme heat stresses the plant, making it drop flowers to save water and survival energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii baaa lɛ, shwiemɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni egbɛ pollen lɛ eshwã. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Gbalamɔ fɔfɔii koni okɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Young cocoa pods drop off in a natural process called cherelle wilt when the tree feels it has more pods than it can feed. It discards extra young pods so it can concentrate its energy and water on fully ripening the remaining ones.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherel wilting lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye lɛ Eshɛrɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwieɔ koni enyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ atsu ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe nii kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants start twisting and curling up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. As they suck the plant juices, the leaves deform and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. beni ekɛ tsei nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when rain sits on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves stagnant water on the farm, the roots suffocate from lack of air and wet soil fungi attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds around my young crops before applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Tsei bibii dani awoɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal crop food, water, and sunlight. If you do not clear them first, the weeds will drink up the fertilizer before your crops get a chance to use it.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ niyenii, tsei, nu kɛ hulu la kɛji ojieee amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Jwɛi lɛ baanu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do crop seeds germinate faster when I plant them in soft, moist soil instead of hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Moisture tells the seed inside its shell that it is safe to wake up and start growing, while soft soil lets the tender root push down easily and allows the tiny green shoot to break through into the sunlight.
ga: Fɛ̃i lɛ kɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ amɛbaate shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi mlɛo. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Baanyɛ abote hulu la mli

english: How do I know if a new piece of land is good enough for growing maize before I clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ dani mafo mli?

english: Look at the wild plants already growing there; land covered with thick green bush and loose dark soil usually has good fertility, while dry, hard, gravelly soil will struggle to feed maize.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsei eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ehà nɔ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, hard kɛ gravel baaná naagbai yɛ ŋmãa kwɛmɔ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground in the farm plot I cleared near the valley?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni mifo mli yɛ jɔɔ ko masɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots drown, so low-lying land with clay or poor drainage holds water and destroys the tubers during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. No hewɔ lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli ni efiteɔ bulb lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellow V-shapes on lower leaves mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient it needs to build green leaves and grow big cobs.
ga: V ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ nikpamɔ be mli?

english: Giving yams too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to build thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee yitso ni mli wa

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, which stops pollination and causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve water.
