ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa pollination lɛ kpaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, making them grow tall and weak instead of putting energy into cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ.

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the soil by pulling nitrogen from the air into their roots, which releases extra nutrients into the soil that help your maize grow better.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii krokomɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct hot sun, so fast-growing plantains provide broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of the maize plant during the day and chew on the soft young leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛi amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: The first rain is often a early false rain followed by dry weeks, which causes newly sprouted seeds to dry out and die before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji amale nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra ni otsi ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly even though my soil looks dark and rich to my eyes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mihiŋmɛii ahiɛ moŋ?

english: Dark soil doesn't always mean rich soil. Soil can look healthy on the surface but lack essential invisible nutrients, have high acidity, or harbor root diseases that only specialized soil testing or expert examination can detect.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ hiɛ shi ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaaa. Acid ni mli wa waa Aloo eji shishifãi ahe helai ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa krɛdɛɛ loo ŋaalɔi akwɛmɔ pɛ baanyɛ ana.

english: How can I know what nutrients my farm soil is missing before I buy expensive fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: You cannot tell exact nutrient levels just by looking at the dirt. Having an extension officer collect soil samples for laboratory testing reveals precisely which nutrients are lacking so you only spend money on the right fertilizers.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ muji ni okwɛɔ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ. Kɛ́ aha mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii anaa koni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ laboratori mli lɛ, ebaajie niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteɔ shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ pɛ he.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect their roots, but severe leaf loss can also be a sign of pest attacks like spider mites or severe nutrient shortages.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Shi baa ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ ŋmeii, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa lɛ eba.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small, incomplete cobs with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii ni yeee emuu ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Incomplete maize cobs usually happen when hot weather or drought stresses the plant during its flowering stage, preventing proper pollination, or when the soil lacks enough nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni edako lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow big leaves instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of developing strong stems and high crop yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni miyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in humid, shady conditions. It requires pruning trees for airflow and applying specific fungicide treatments rather than just clearing weeds.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ehe miihia ni afo tsei koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni akɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie jwɛi kɛkɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Simply watering the plant won't fix it; the insects must be identified and treated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ pɛ haŋ naagba lɛ aba naagbee. Esa akɛ ayoo kooloi bibii ni atsa amɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and dry up early before the tubers are big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi oya dani bulbs lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam vines is often caused by invisible pests in the soil, like nematodes, or root fungal wilts that destroy the root system before the tuber finishes growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya.

english: Why is it good for my main crop when I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground and helping neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist so it can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ hu haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs, leading to a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced maize.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi fe ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Curling and yellow leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps protect your field from this sickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why do new shoots keep sprouting around the base of my plantain tree, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: Those shoots are called suckers, which the plant uses to reproduce. If you leave all of them, they will steal water and food from the main plant; cutting them back to leave only one or two strong suckers ensures large, healthy bunches of plantain.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii, ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛji oshɛrɛ amɛ fɛɛ oshwie lɛ Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofo lɛ sɛɛ koni eshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantains akuu agbo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves toward the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, allows them to catch maximum sunlight, and helps the plant grow bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy and weak in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to leave the leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The plant wilts to protect itself and conserve moisture, usually bouncing back once the heat drops in the evening.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu jeɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: What makes the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow at the tips and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better when I plant groundnuts on the field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the dirt. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural fertilizer left behind in the soil.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop growth so much even when my plants are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ awui waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi momo moŋ.

english: Underneath the soil, weed roots are very aggressive and quickly steal water and nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds leaves all the food in the ground available for your crops to feed on.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, jwɛi shishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the day temperatures get too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when bees aren't around to pollinate them. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛfee pollination lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Small holes and ragged leaf edges are usually caused by armyworms eating the growing shoots, while yellow leaves mean the plant is stressed or lacking nitrogen nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni etse lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao loo nitrogen niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping, and the soil at the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why is it better to place fertilizer near the base of my crops instead of scattering it across the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your crop absorbs most of the nutrients directly before heavy rain washes them away or weeds steal them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo jwɛi lɛ juɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil during the flowering period.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Should I start planting my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady, because the first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry up and kill newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Maize removes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but legumes like cowpea and groundnut take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more during the first few weeks after planting than later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ fe sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are small and weak, so early weeds easily steal the limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients the crop needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni jeɔ shishi mra lɛ juɔ hulu la fioo, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ oya.

english: How do I pick the best seed yams to ensure I get a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Select medium-sized, firm, and healthy tubers from healthy plants that show no signs of rots, holes, or disease spots, as strong seed tubers produce early, vigorous sprouts.
ga: Halamɔ bulbs ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ejieee ŋmɔtɔ, bu, loo helai ahe okadi ko kpo lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha obɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, whereas afternoon watering causes rapid evaporation and can scorch warm leaves.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use my regular bush-trimming shears to cut ripe cocoa pods off the tree?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ daa lɛ atsu nii kɛfo kookoo ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: While general trimming shears like secateurs work well for cutting foliage, harvesting cocoa requires extra care. Using proper cocoa knives or specialized shears helps you make clean cuts without tearing the tree bark or damaging the flower cushion.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tsei ahe daa tamɔ Secateur lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛfoɔ baai moŋ, shi kookoo ni akɛtoɔ lɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Kɛ́ okɛ kookoo ŋmei ni sa loo sɛkɛs krɛdɛɛ ko tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ofolɔ tso lɛ he tse ni ogbalaaa tso lɛ shishi loo ofiteee fɔfɔi lɛ akushin lɛ.

english: Why is it important to keep my harvesting blades sharp when working in the cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ootsu nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: A sharp blade makes a quick, clean cut through the pod stalk without pulling or twisting the stem. Dull blades force you to yank the pod, which damages the trunk surface and exposes the tree to pests and diseases.
ga: Blades ni yɔɔ oya haa anyɛɔ afoɔ stem pods lɛ oya, ni amɛhe tseɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ogbala loo otsi tso lɛ shishi Lade ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ baaha otsi ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Enɛ baafite tso lɛ shishi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Where exactly on the pod stem should I make the cut when harvesting cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ pod tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo kɛji mikpa kookoo?

english: You should cut the stalk close to the cocoa pod itself, leaving a small piece of the stem attached to the tree. Cutting right at the pod base protects the flower cushion on the trunk where future cocoa pods will grow.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo tso lɛ he ni obɛŋkɛ kookoo tso lɛ he, ni oshi tso bibioo ko ni akpɛtɛ tso lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi akushin ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni kookoo tso lɛ baajɛ mli akwɛ wɔsɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: What happens to my cocoa tree if I yank or twist a pod off instead of cutting it cleanly?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji migbala loo mitsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yanking a pod tears the flower cushion off the main trunk. Once a flower cushion is destroyed, that spot on the tree can never produce cocoa flowers or pods again, lowering your total yield over time.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie pod lɛ, etseɔ fɔfɔi lɛ akushin lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ akpata fɔfɔii a-pillow lɛ hiɛ Nakai he ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haŋ kookoo fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii aba dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: If small young pods are growing right next to a ripe pod, how do I cut the big pod safely?
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo ŋmeii wuji shweshweeshwe?

english: You must carefully slice the ripe pod's stalk right where it joins the fruit using a sharp edge. Careful, close cuts prevent your tool from slicing into neighboring young pods or breaking the shared cushion base.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ afo ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishifã lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ obɛŋkɛ ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi odɛŋdade lɛ naa koni ekafolɔ ewo ŋmeii bibii amli. ni bɛŋkɛ loo eha kushɛŋ shishitoo ni aja lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to trim back bushes around our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ jwɛi ni bɔle kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Trimming surrounding bushes removes overgrown weeds that block air and sunlight. Good airflow keeps the farm dry and prevents fungal diseases, like black pod, from spreading to your developing pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni afoɔ Ebaajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Will cutting unnecessary stems and extra branches hurt my cocoa tree's growth?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa kɛ niji krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni abaafo lɛ baaná kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, light pruning helps the tree direct its nutrients into growing healthy pods rather than feeding excess leaves. It also creates a clean canopy that makes harvesting mature pods easier without damaging main branches.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afolɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa tso lɛ mli tsei ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha foliar niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni he tse hu feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni efiteee tsei lɛ aniji titrii lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the thick tree trunk instead of on the thin branch tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei niji bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are heavy fruit that need strong support. Growing on the main trunk and thick canopy branches allows the tree to carry heavy pods safely without the stems snapping under the weight.
ga: Cocoa pods ji aduawai ni tsii ni biɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni mli wa. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii shweshweeshwe ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ fãaa kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is ready for harvesting without damaging the stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ ni mifiteee amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Ripe pods change color completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or red to orange. When full color change happens, the pod stalk is mature, making it easier to slice close to the pod base cleanly.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su kwraa—bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo red kɛyashi orange Kɛji atsake sui lɛ fɛɛ Pod lɛ shishifã lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaafolɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ pod lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What is a flower cushion, and why is it so important for my cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji fɔfɔi pilɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A flower cushion is the small raised bump on the cocoa trunk where flowers sprout and turn into pods season after season. Protecting these cushions during harvesting ensures your tree continues producing pods for many years.
ga: Fɔfɔi akushin ji ŋmeii bibii. Atsɔse lɛ yɛ kookoo tso nɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛ́ obu kushɛnii nɛɛ ahe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ehaa otso lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and start wilting even when the sun is not extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ tsɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of water to carry nutrients from the soil up to their leaves. When the soil becomes dry, the plant closes its leaves to save water, which stops its growth and causes wilting.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛbaai lɛ koni nu akafite. Enɛ haa ekpaa dalɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Is spending money to set up an irrigation system on my farm really worth it?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ akɛ mafite shika yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, because even though irrigation costs money upfront, it allows you to grow crops during dry periods when market prices are highest, turning a higher profit overall.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ heɔ shika kɛtsɔɔ hiɛ moŋ, shi ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii hu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, be mli ni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni fa babaoo

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops so they grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because less water evaporates in the cool air, allowing the roots to absorb most of it.
ga: Nu ni oooha lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu fioo pɛ baaho yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Can I still grow and harvest vegetables during the long dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Ani nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha adu aduawai lolo ni akpa?

english: Yes, by using simple irrigation methods like bucket drip systems or water pumps, you can supply water to your crops year-round without waiting for rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ baagi mli nu ni hoɔ loo nu pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni omɛɛɛɛ nugbɔ.

english: How can I keep my farm producing crops continuously throughout the year instead of just once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ, shi jeee shikome pɛ?

english: Combining a reliable water source with crop rotation allows you to plant and harvest continuously through both the wet and dry seasons, keeping your land productive all year.
ga: Nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa nɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa nii yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do vegetables that get extra water during dry spells produce bigger fruits than rain-fed crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni náa nu babaoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ woɔ yibii wuji fe tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Constant water allows plants to continuously absorb soil nutrients without stress, resulting in larger, heavier, and healthier produce.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ daa lɛ haa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni da, ni tsii, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before turning into fruits during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy when they experience water stress, but keeping the soil moist through regular watering keeps the flowers healthy so they set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji amɛkɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Shi kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooshwie nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Too little water makes leaves turn yellow, curl, and wilt, while too much water turns the soil soggy, rots the roots, and causes leaves to drop off.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, amɛkpãtã, ni amɛbaagboi, yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbo.

english: How does watering my crops regularly help make farming a reliable full-time job for me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa okwaayeli feɔ be fɛɛ nitsumɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛhaa mi?

english: Regular watering guarantees consistent monthly harvests and income, turning farming from a seasonal gamble into a steady, profitable business year-round.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ haa anáa ŋmaa kɛ shika daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ okwaayeli kɛjɛ be mli asɔshwɛmɔ mli kɛya jarayeli ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What simple watering method can I use if I do not have enough money for big irrigation machines?
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Mɛɛ nɔ manyɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛji mibɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaahe nu shwiemɔ tsɔne agbo?

english: Drip irrigation using raised water tanks and simple plastic hoses directs water straight to the roots, saving water and keeping costs low for small farms.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni awo nɔ kɛ plastic paipi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ nu lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ nu ato ni oha shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ akafee bibioo kɛha ŋmɔji bibii.

english: If stray goats or cattle eat the leaves off my young maize plants, will the crops grow back or are they ruined?
ga: Kɛji too loo tsina ni elaaje lɛ ye mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ, Ani ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ loo ebaafite?

english: If the central growing point inside the stem core is not damaged, maize can grow new leaves and recover. However, if the animals eat the plant down to the ground level where the stem tip is, the crop will die and must be replanted.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni tso lɛ dalɛ yɔɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Abɛi baanyɛ akwɛ baai heei ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ jwɛi lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagboi ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I plant a living fence around my farm to keep hungry animals away from my main crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu gbogbo ni hiɛ ka yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he koni kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ akashɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe?

english: You can plant dense, fast-growing plants like Jatropha, thorny bushes, or cassava closely together along your farm boundary. These plants form a thick physical wall that deters livestock while protecting your main crops from being trampled or eaten.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ jatropha, thornbush loo cassava ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ feɔ gbogbo ni mli wa ni haa kooloi anijiaŋ jeɔ wui yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ hu ahe koni akanyiɛ nɔ loo aye.

english: Is there a crop I can plant on my farm border that animals naturally dislike eating?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa ni kooloi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Yes, crops like hot chili peppers, ginger, and lemongrass naturally repel livestock because of their sharp smell, burning taste, or rough texture. Planting a boundary row of hot peppers creates a natural barrier that animals will avoid.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ chili, ginger kɛ lemongrass shwieɔ kooloi yɛ amɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa, shãa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hewɔ. Peppers ni mli edɔ lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa. lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kpo

english: Why do farm animals avoid eating leaves on some cassava varieties while heavily eating others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ahe baai lɛ yeli he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ekrokomɛi babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally produce bitter defense chemicals (cyanide compounds) to protect themselves from pests and animals. 'Bitter' cassava varieties have high chemical levels that stop animals from eating them, while 'sweet' cassava has lower defenses and gets eaten easily.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ feɔ tsofai ni tsiɔ ŋmɔlɔ naa. (Cyanide compound) lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Tsofai babaoo yɛ ŋmei henɔi ni ‘bitter’ lɛ amli ni haaa kooloi aye ŋmei lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni ‘ŋɔɔ’ lɛ ebuuu mɔ he tsɔ, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ayeɔ.

english: What happens to my underground yam and sweet potato tubers if heavy animals walk all over my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ? Kɛji kooloi ni tsii nyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Heavy animals pack the soil tightly, removing the air spaces that roots need to breathe. Compacted soil forces developing yam and sweet potato tubers to become small, twisted, or stop growing completely because they cannot push through hard earth.
ga: Koolooi ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha sweet potatoes kɛ tubers lɛ afee bibii, amɛtsake, loo amɛkpa dalɛ kwraa ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli.

english: Can I safely grow vegetables directly behind my house where I keep goats and chickens?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ he ni mikwɛɔ tooi kɛ kooloi yɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, but you must protect the plants with a barrier because free-roaming animals will eat young crop shoots. Additionally, while animal manure makes great fertilizer, you must let it rot and dry first so it does not burn the delicate vegetable roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ gbɛtsii nii abu tso lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi ashishifãi haa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai moŋ, shi ehe miihia ni oha egbo ni egbi klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni ekashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and turn brown during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves curl as a defense behavior to lose less water when the weather is extremely hot and dry. You can protect cocoa crops from heat stress by leaving taller shade trees on the farm to block direct sunlight.
ga: Cocoa leaf curling ji subaŋ ko ni tsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Obaanyɛ obu cocoa tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni oooshi lɛ nɔ. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees easily fall over when animals lean on them or strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have a deep taproot; their roots spread out shallowly in the topsoil. Because the plant carries a heavy fruit bunch at the top, even slight pressure from animals or strong wind can pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you prop the stem with a wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo ejaakɛ tso lɛ yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Nɔnyɛɛ fioo ko ni jɛɔ kooloi adɛŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa po baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. nyɛɔ eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stay greener than my cultivated crops during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔŋ fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have evolved deep roots and strong survival features to grow aggressively in poor conditions. Cultivated crops are bred to put their energy into producing food, so they need human help with weeding and water to compete successfully.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ wala yibiiwoo sui ni mli wa ni baaha amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Akwɛɔ tsei ni aduɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, adesai aye abua tsei nɛɛ yɛ jwɛi kɛ nu mli koni amɛye omanye yɛ akaŋshii mli.

english: What fast-growing crop can I plant on a cleared plot to prevent weeds and bush from taking over?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ koni jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii akaye nɔ?

english: You can plant cover crops like cowpea or mucuna (velvet bean). These crops spread rapidly across the ground like a carpet, blocking sunlight from weed seeds, improving soil fertility, and keeping the field ready for your primary crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo mucilagina. (Velvet beans) Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tamɔ kapɛti. Tsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to cut down and uproot some of our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi ni wɔjie amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees get infected with viruses, there is no chemical cure. Cutting down and uprooting infected trees is necessary to destroy the virus completely and protect healthy neighboring trees from getting infected.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ kookoo tsei lɛ Tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsa hela nɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni ajie amɛ koni akɛkpata hela lɛ hiɛ kwraa, ni atsĩ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa koni hela lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Is it possible to heal a cocoa tree once a virus gets inside it?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ abu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛji hela ko ebote mli pɛ?

english: No, once a virus enters a cocoa tree, it spreads inside the living parts of the plant and cannot be cured. The only way to save the rest of the farm is to remove the sick tree.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ hela lɛ bote kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ Egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ fãi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ. Gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahereɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala ji ni ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why isn't trimming the sick branches of a cocoa tree enough to cure it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni akɛtsaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once mealybugs deposit a virus into a tree, the disease enters the whole plant system. Cutting off branches leaves the virus in the trunk and roots, allowing it to continue spreading.
ga: Beni mealybugs lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ woɔ tsei anɔ lɛ Hela lɛ boteɔ tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ. Niji ni afoɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa hela lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: If I cut down a diseased cocoa tree, do I really need to pull out the roots as well?
ga: Kɛ́ ofo kookoo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni ofomɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, uprooting is essential because the virus stays active in any living parts left behind. Removing the roots ensures mealybugs cannot feed on remaining live tissue and spread the disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ hela lɛ yaa nɔ etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ wala mli nibii ni ashi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie shishifãi lɛ, ehaa mealybugs lɛ yeɔ fãji ni eshwɛ ni hiɛ ka lɛ ni amɛkagbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa.

english: What are mealybugs, and why are they dangerous to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii? Ni mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Mealybugs are tiny insects that attach to cocoa trees. They are dangerous because they act as carriers, depositing harmful viruses directly into the cocoa tree while feeding.
ga: Mealybugs ji kooloi bibii. ni kpɛtɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛhe yɛ oshara ejaakɛ amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ mɛi ni hiɛɔ nii. Amɛkɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui woɔ cacao tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: How do small insects like mealybugs get onto my cocoa trees in the first place?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ bashɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Mealybugs are often carried from tree to tree by flying insects or vectors that move around the farm, transferring mealybugs onto healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ loo ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ woɔ Mealybugs kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ koni amɛkɛ aphids lɛ aya kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can flying insects harm my cocoa farm if they do not eat the cocoa pods?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni foɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ awui amɛha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛyeee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Even if flying insects do not eat your pods, they carry mealybugs on their bodies. When they land on your cocoa trees, they transfer the mealybugs, which then transmit viruses into the trees.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ yeŋ o-pods lɛ. Shi ehiɛɔ ŋmeii hu. Kɛ egbee o-cacao tso lɛ nɔ Ebaajie mealybug lɛ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli.

english: How does a viral disease move from one cocoa tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helai ni jɛɔ cacao tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The disease moves when flying insects transport mealybugs from infected trees to healthy ones. The mealybugs then attach to the new tree and deposit the virus into it.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ kɛ mealybugs lɛ jɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛtee tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Mealybugs lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ tsei heei ahe ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Will leaving just one diseased cocoa tree on my farm really affect my healthy trees?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi kookoo tso kome pɛ ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaana mitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, leaving even one sick tree allows mealybugs and flying insects to pick up the virus from that tree and transfer it to your surrounding healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi tso kome po ni hela mɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa mealybugs kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i lɛ jieɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ nakai tso lɛ mli ni amɛkɛyaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: How does a virus actually enter the inside of a cocoa tree?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ cacao tsei amli?

english: A virus enters the cocoa tree when mealybugs feed on the plant tissue and deposit the viral disease into the parts of the tree where the disease takes root.
ga: Virus lɛ boteɔ kookoo tsei amli beni mealybugs yeɔ tsei amli fãji ni ekɛ virus hela woɔ tso lɛ fã ni hela lɛ shishijee yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin stems and produce very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei bibii waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is strong direct sunlight on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out quickly under direct sun. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crops right as the main rainy season is ending?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: Young plants need steady moisture in their first few weeks to build strong roots. Planting near the end of the rains leaves crops stranded in dry soil before they can mature.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged and drowning the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho.

english: Why does my soil produce a smaller harvest if I plant cassava in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year, and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my farm reduce the amount of food my crops produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving the main plants weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small worms to eat holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the soft growing center of corn plants to feed before the plant can produce cobs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii dani tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested high-yield crops lose their strength and disease resistance over generations, resulting in weaker plants and lower yield compared to fresh, certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I keep different crop varieties separate after harvest instead of mixing them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ aaafutu lɛ

english: Mixing crop varieties together causes them to spoil unevenly during storage and lowers their selling price, as market buyers pay more for clean, uniform grains.
ga: Tsei ni afɔɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afite yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni ajie jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ shi Enɛ ji akɛ, esa akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ awo nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha ŋmaa ni he tse ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers underground are fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to swell and crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why does my cocoa crop take several years before it starts giving me pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that needs three to five years to build a strong trunk and deep root system to support fruit production before it begins flowering and fruiting regularly.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani ená shishifã ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua ni ewo yibii dani ebɔi fɔmɔ kɛ yibiiwoo daa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that lose water quickly in direct sun, which is why they need fast-growing shade plants like plantain to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to trim or prune branches from my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ loo afolɔ kookoo tso ni miida lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches, allowing light and air to move through the tree. This reduces dampness that causes disease and helps the tree direct its energy into producing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do black spots spread over my cocoa pods when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Rainy weather brings high humidity and moisture, which causes a fungal infection called Black Pod disease to develop and spread rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ baa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why are the branches of my cocoa trees swelling and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ efu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swollen branches and yellowing leaves are signs of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, a serious disease spread by mealybug insects that weakens and eventually kills the tree.
ga: Niji ni efuu kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: Why are my plantain leaves drying up before the bunch of plantain fully matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Early drying of leaves is usually caused by leaf spot diseases or a lack of soil nutrients and water, which prevents the plant from feeding the developing fruit bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ahe hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ agbiɔ oya. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii aha aduawai niji ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving space and sunlight for the cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ he ko kɛ hulu la ni ashiɔ koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if the seeds were old or damaged by pests during storage, or if soil insects ate the seeds before germination.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my land give me smaller harvests if I plant cassava on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously without resting the land or adding fertilizer drains key nutrients from the soil, leaving fewer resources for new plants to grow well.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ daa ni akɛ sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii titrii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii fioo pɛ ashiɔ koni tsei heei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds growing around my yam plants cause the tubers to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi sweet potato tsei lɛ haa amɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients directly from the soil, leaving the yam vines with fewer resources to produce large tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɛ nibii babaoo ni ekɛbaafee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the best time of day to water my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best because temperatures are cooler, allowing the soil to absorb water deeply instead of losing it to heat evaporation.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi loo shwane ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaafite dɔlɛ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ

english: What will happen to my plants if I do not water them after applying fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu efɔɔɔ amɛ nɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely absorb it. Without water, concentrated fertilizer sits against the roots and burns them, causing the plant to wilt and dry up.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baakpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaashã amɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to wait too long after the rains start before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mamɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting early with the first good rains gives seeds time to establish deep roots while moisture is steady; planting late means crops may run out of water before maturity when the rainy season ends.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi daa. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu baanyɛ afite tsei lɛ dani amɛdara yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: When is the right time for me to start clearing weeds from my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ?

english: Weeding should be done when your crops are still young seedlings because weeds compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during the crop's early growth stage.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwui bibii lolo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even when the soil has enough moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that your crop is hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen. While water keeps the plant alive, adding manure or fertilizer provides the food required for leaves to stay dark green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia onibii lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ nu haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi moŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: How far away from the plant stem should I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Place fertilizer in a small ring or hole about a hand-width away from the main stem; putting it directly against the stem can scorch the crop, while putting it too far prevents the roots from reaching it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii loo buji amli. Aaafee tso tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akashɛ he ko.

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient shortages, shedding the blossom to conserve energy rather than trying to support a developing fruit.
ga: Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is a natural protective reaction where the plant reduces its leaf area exposed to the sun to prevent excess water from evaporating out of its leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu nifeemɔ. Tso lɛ baaha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akajɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, seedlings compete for sunlight and stretch upward as fast as possible, resulting in weak, skinny stems that break easily in wind.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaagbala amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ, egbɛɔ oya.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up; rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally require filtered sunlight to thrive. Direct, harsh sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly, causing the leaves to dry up and the seedling to die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulu la ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya. Ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during the dry harmattan season even after a good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture directly out of plant leaves and exposed soil. Covering the bare ground around your plants with mulch or crop leaves keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛkɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. tso ni jwɛi loo tso baai yɔɔ nɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce tiny pods that turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani edara

english: This is often cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot afford to feed due to lack of nutrients, or it is caused by fungal rot when there is too much shade and dampness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji cherel ŋmei. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo fungal rot ji nɔ ni kɛbaa beni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees yield far less fruit now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal systems slow down and become less efficient at pulling nutrients from the soil to form pods, requiring side-pruning or replanting.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baa shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Enɛ biɔ ni afolɔ niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ loo adu eheei.

english: How does heavy rain during the flowering season affect my cocoa harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa mi-kookoo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains knock delicate flowers off the branches and prevent insects from pollinating them, resulting in fewer flowers turning into healthy pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa kooloi bibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ayibɔ baa shi kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why did the store-bought fertilizer I used fail to improve my cocoa tree leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa mi-kookoo baai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer during dry spells or on degraded, overly acidic soil prevents the crop from absorbing the nutrients effectively.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo shikpɔŋ ni efite ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are turning yellow from nutrient lack or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa loo hela hewɔ?

english: Nutrient deficiency usually causes an even yellowing across many leaves, starting with older leaves, while diseases leave irregular spots, patches, or sudden rotting on specific shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baai babaoo feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai momoi anɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, helai srɔtoi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ trukaa baa baa lɛ ekomɛi anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa shoots curling up and turning dark brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by small sap-sucking insects called mirids (capsids) that bite tender green shoots and inject toxins, causing the leaves and stem tissues to dry out and die.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (capsids), ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛkɛ tsofai fɔji woɔ amɛmli lɛ. Ehaa baa kɛ tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava directly next to my young cocoa trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots aggressively suck up soil nutrients and water, which starves young cocoa plants; crops like plantains are better companions because they provide gentle shade without stealing as many nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ waa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo tsei bibii. Tsei tamɔ plantains ji nanemɛi kpakpai ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo blɛoo ni amɛjuuu niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do cocoa pods near the ground rot much faster than pods higher up on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Raindrops bouncing off the soil splash fungal spores directly onto low-hanging pods, and high moisture near the ground creates a damp zone where rot thrives.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni baanyɛ afite lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's primary food for healthy green growth, or when water accumulates too long around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. aloo kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when there is too much water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water on the field without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and soil bacteria cause them to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ma shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin without producing many peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ pepper babaoo baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants stretch tall and thin when they are shaded and searching for sunlight, spending all their energy on growing tall stems rather than producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛmiitao hulu la. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei kakadaji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the rain season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground stays consistently damp after two or three strong rains, rather than planting immediately after the very first rain which might be followed by a hot dry stretch that burns seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi asɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni ekolɛ la ni mli egbi ni haa dumɔwui lɛ ashãa lɛ baanyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Staking holds tomato stems off the ground, keeping leaves and fruits away from wet soil pests and diseases while letting air and sunlight flow freely through the plant.
ga: Staking hiɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akashɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya.

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground and helping nearby maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛɔ waa.

english: Why should I weed my farm while my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak, shallow roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for soil food, water, and light, so clearing weeds early gives your main crop a strong start.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni ená niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ la mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I prepare a natural liquid from neem leaves to protect my vegetables from insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee adebɔɔ mli nu ko kɛjɛ neem baai amli koni mikɛbu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Crushing bitter neem leaves in water and spraying the mixture on your vegetable leaves acts as a natural repellent that repels leaf-chewing caterpillars and beetles without expensive chemicals.
ga: Neem baai ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli ni akɛfutuɔ tsofai lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why does hybrid maize seed produce a bigger harvest than seeds saved from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ mitsutsu ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum vigor, disease resistance, and uniform growth, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: How can I prevent insects from damaging my maize after I harvest and dry it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋma lɛ beni akpa ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ensure the maize grains are thoroughly sun-dried until hard before storing them off the damp ground in airtight bags or sealed storage bins that keep insects and moisture out.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛto he ko ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ yɛ vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ŋtayaai ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli koni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii kɛ nu mli.

english: My father farmed this land for decades, but now my crops won't grow well on it. What is happening to the soil?
ga: Mitsɛ tsu okwaa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ midumɔ nii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ. Mɛni ba sũ lɛ nɔ?

english: Over many years of continuous farming, crops draw out essential nutrients from the ground. If the land is not given time to rest or enriched with compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and loses its ability to support healthy plant growth.
ga: Yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awooo mli lɛ, ebaafite ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Is it possible to plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same land where old cocoa trees died out?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kookoo tsei momoi gboi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Replanting on old cocoa land can be difficult because the previous trees may have left behind soil-borne diseases and completely depleted the soil nutrients. The land usually needs clearing, soil treatment, and a period of crop rotation or fallowing before new cocoa will grow successfully.
ga: Kookoo momo ni aaadu ekoŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa ejaakɛ ekolɛ tsei ni eho lɛ eshi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ, ni eha sũ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ efite. Bei pii lɛ, ehe baahia ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, atsu he nii, ni akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli dani kookoo hee baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing so slowly even though I clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ Nɔ ni Mijie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense sunlight and harsh weather. If they do not have enough overhead shade from plantains or shade trees, sunlight stresses the leaves and slows down their overall growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe. Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli loo tso lɛ haaa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. Hulu la lɛ baaha baai lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni ebaaha amɛdalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to conserve water. Providing temporary shade crops and maintaining organic mulch around the root base helps retain soil moisture and prevents this leaf drop.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛbu nu he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛhaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: My cocoa trees produce flowers, but many of the small pods turn black and dry up before growing big. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi, shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: This is often caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod or a natural tree process called cherelle wilt where the plant discards extra fruit it cannot feed. Proper pruning to allow air flow and applying approved fungicides help keep pods healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod loo adebɔɔ mli tso nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine ni enyɛɛɛ eye lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains on the same land when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ́ aje kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa plants from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm to feed my family while I wait for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ko teŋ koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a very heavy feeder that aggressively competes with young cocoa for underground water and soil nutrients. It is better to plant plantains or cocoyams instead, as they share resources better and provide the necessary shade.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ cocoa bibii yeɔ akaŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantain loo kookoo moŋ. Ejaakɛ amɛjaa nibii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa.

english: Why do tiny insects attack the fresh green shoots of my cocoa trees and make the leaves curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ ni amɛmiiha baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: These insects are usually mirids (capsids), which feed on the sap of young cocoa shoots and release a poison that causes the stems to dry out. Spraying recommended pest control treatments at the right times of year keeps these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji mirids (capsids), ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ tsofa ko ni haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ lɛ kpo. Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted crops, and how does this hurt my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than domesticated crops. If you don't clear them early, they choke your crops, steal their food, and lower your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛji ojieee amɛ mra lɛ, Amɛbaatsi oŋmɔshinii lɛ anaa. jumɔ eniyenii lɛ ni okɛ nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa crops so that I do not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii koni mikafite shika?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, usually at the beginning or middle of the rainy season. Applying fertilizer during dry periods prevents the roots from taking up nutrients and can burn the roots of the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee loo teŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food for plant growth. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the younger top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my cowpea flowers more than the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ fe baai lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers are full of sweet nectar and nutrients, which attract insects like thrips and pod borers. Insects target the flowers because they are soft and nutrient-rich, but protecting them is essential because damage to flowers prevents bean pods from forming.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Kplukai kwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Shi ehe ni abuɔ he lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ haaa ŋmeii afee ŋmeii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves to save water and survive hot, dry conditions. By getting rid of its leaves, the plant stops water from escaping through leaf pores, and it will quickly sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam plant grow long vines and leaves for weeks before any yam grows underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni ewoɔ baai otsii komɛi dani sweet potato lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: The yam plant uses its long vines and leaves like solar panels to trap sunlight and make food. Only after building a strong foliage system can the plant send that extra food down into the soil to swell up into a heavy yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ wain tsei kɛ baai kakadaji tamɔ hulu la tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. Beni ato baa gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa shishi pɛ kɛkɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni fa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the sunny months?
