ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have very tender leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to stay cool and retain moisture in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ashishifãi amli. Bɔni afee ni fɛ̃i ahi shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily once the heavy fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the top of the soil. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top becomes too weighted for the shallow roots to hold, so farmers need to support the stem with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ we nɛ e kɛ zugba ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsii tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ he lɛ aye abua.

english: Why does my young oil palm tree produce flowers for a long time before giving me solid fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso bibioo lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi be kakadaŋŋ dani ehaa mi yibii ni wa lɛ?

english: Young oil palms produce separate male and female flowers. In their first few years, the tree mostly produces male flowers or small undeveloped female bunches until it becomes mature enough to produce large, healthy oil palm bunches.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baawo fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei babaoo woɔ fɔfɔi hii loo fɔfɔi bibii yei. ni eshɛko he lolo Kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee mu tsei wuji ni mli wa.

english: Groundnut flowers open above ground to be pollinated, but the actual nuts grow underground. After pollination, the stems bend down and push into the soil so the nuts can safely develop away from heat and pests.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛha pollination aba, shi nut lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. after pollination Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, poor watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. nu ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin lɛ ni bɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they carry. As the pests feed on the soft leaves, they cause the new foliage to grow distorted and twisted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Beni kooloi ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ Amɛbaahã baai heei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why did my planted pepper seeds fail to sprout even after I watered the seedbed every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni mikɛ nu efɔ dumɔwui lɛ atsu lɛ nɔ daa gbi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds can fail to sprout if planted too deeply in the soil, if the soil is packed too tightly, or if seeds were stored in damp, hot places before planting. Planting small seeds shallowly in soft, moist soil allows oxygen and warmth to reach them so they can germinate.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa yɔɔ dani adu. Dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ dɔlɛ shɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and produce less every time I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same heavy nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the land depleted and allowing maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility because legumes naturally add nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. shikpɔŋ nɔ he ni efiteɔ ni eha ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ kooloi lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under harsh, direct sunlight because heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the surrounding air and soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during rainstorms just when the fruit bunches are growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not hold deeply into the ground, making them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo props prevents the trees from snapping or falling under heavy wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ tsii kɛji ewo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign of nitrogen deficiency, which is the key food crop plants use to make healthy leaves. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure supplies nitrogen to the soil and restores the deep green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná nitrogen ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku esɛɛ efee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and rot when heavy rainwater sits in my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize roots need air in the soil to breathe and take up nutrients. When land stays flooded, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen, causing the stems to rot and the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy stems above ground but tiny thin roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it spends its energy growing leaves and stems instead of roots. Giving cassava proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourages the plant to store food in big underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmei lɛ he jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yam sets taken from tubers that have soft rot or dry brown spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato kits ni ajie kɛjɛ tubers ni miifite loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tubers with rot carry fungal or bacterial diseases hidden inside their flesh. Planting infected yam sets transfers those diseases directly into your soil, causing the young tuber to decay before it can produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Tubers ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná fungal loo bacteria helai ni yɔɔ loo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, nakai helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: What causes ragged holes in my maize leaves and small brown dust inside the center of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa kɛ sũ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the soft leaf funnel of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf solution directly into the funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers dry up and drop off when temperatures get excessively hot or when plants suffer from dry soil. Watering tomato plants regularly at the roots and providing light shade during peak midday heat keeps the flowers healthy so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tomato tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni aduawai anyɛ afee.

english: Why do some of my crops take up to seven months to fully mature before I can complete the main harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ nyɔji kpawo dani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ?

english: Different crops have unique biological growth cycles. Long-term crops spend their first three to four months developing a strong root system and leaves, while the remaining months are used to produce heavy fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa. Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa baa. yɛ be mli ni akɛ nyɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ woɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa ni tsii.

english: Can I get any harvest or income from my seven-month crop around the third or fourth month?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa loo maná shika kɛjɛ nyɔji kpawo mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, depending on the crop, early weed control, pruning, or intercropping with short-season vegetables allows you to make early sales or yields mid-way through the main crop's growth cycle.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Mra be mli jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ akwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ Aloo, be kukuoo mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ dalɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow very slowly during the first three months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the early months, plants focus most of their energy underground building deep root networks. Once roots are established, above-ground stem and leaf growth speeds up rapidly.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji komɛi lɛ amli lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni abɔ shishifãi lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei kɛ baai lɛ daa oya.

english: Why does rain in our farming area seem to come twice a year roughly every six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ wɔ okwaayeli hei lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli, aaafee daa nyɔji 6 lɛ?

english: Many farming regions in Ghana experience a bimodal rainfall pattern, meaning there are two distinct rainy seasons spaced about six months apart, which dictates your major and minor planting times.
ga: Okwaafoi akutsei babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ naa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee nyɔji 6, ni no tsɔɔ be ni okɛbaadu nii klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting right at the start of the six-month rain cycle help my young crops?
ga: Te tsei ni sa ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei bibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting at the very beginning of the rains ensures young seeds get steady moisture when their roots are small, helping them grow strong enough to endure the drier months ahead.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ po kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ darako. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi yɛ nyɔji fioo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: What happens to my long-term crops if the six-month rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nyɔji enumɔ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Early stoppage of rain causes water stress, which can shrink seed size or cause flowers to drop. Using soil covers like mulch helps trap residual moisture in the ground for your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ni akpaa mra ni kɛ nu he haomɔ baa Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ aba shi loo eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If rainfall only comes every six months, should I plant short-duration or long-duration crops?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa nyɔji 6 lɛ, ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kuku loo be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Short-duration crops (3 to 4 months) are safer if rains are short, while long-duration crops (up to 7 months) yield more if planted early enough to capture the full rainy period.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli (nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ (ni shɛɔ nyɔji 7) lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu mra bɔ ni sa koni anyɛ aná nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does soil hold water to keep my crops alive between rain cycles?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ ehiɛɔ nu mli koni eha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli?

english: Soil containing organic matter like decomposed leaves acts like a natural sponge, storing rainwater deep underground so crops can keep drinking even during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ Tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji Toɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anu nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po.

english: How can I combine short and long crops so I do not wait seven full months before getting any money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji ekome bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni mamɛ nyɔji kpawo muu lɛ fɛɛ dani awo mi nyɔmɔ?

english: You can intercrop fast-maturing crops like maize or beans that harvest in three months alongside longer crops, giving you food and cash while your main crop matures.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 3 mli kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ fe no. Koni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do deep-rooted crops survive dry periods better than shallow-rooted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops with long root systems can reach water buried deep in the soil profile long after surface rain has dried up, whereas shallow roots quickly dry out.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi kakadaŋŋ yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ aná nu ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baagbi oya.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps bring back the green color and speeds up growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ená baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of green leaves but produce very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, bean and cowpea plants focus all their energy on making big leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so they need less fertilizer to produce good pods.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ Bean kɛ cowpea tsei lɛ hu kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai wuji ni amɛbaafee yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ he hiaa koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungal organism that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and heavy shade. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni mli wa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers curling up and looking weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and stunted plantain leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like nematodes or banana weevils attacking the roots underground. When the roots are damaged, the plant cannot drink enough water or take in food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana weevils ni tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ plantain baai ni ebɔle ehe ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ anu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛye niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target young maize plants because the tender center leaves are easy to eat. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the whorl helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yeli waaa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground whenever there is heavy rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain stays trapped in the soil without draining away, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing rot fungi to attack them underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ekpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efooo. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji rot fungus lɛ baanyɛ atutua amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my pepper crop drop its leaves suddenly after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden leaf drop in peppers after rain happens when waterlogged soil chokes the root system, causing shock to the plant. Planting on raised beds helps excess water drain away quickly so roots stay healthy.
ga: Pepper ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yaa shoofeemɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy without paying for expensive laboratory tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni miwooo laboratori mli kaai ni jara wa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hands, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or decayed plant matter, which shows it has good natural life to feed crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ nine mi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni miifite lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ayelikɛbuamɔ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences intense heat stress or irregular watering during flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, twisted, and bumpy instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers twist and deform when they hit hard, stony, or tightly packed soil while growing downward. Planting yams in deep, loose, soft mounds or ridges gives the tubers space to stretch out smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ beni adu lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ŋmeii amli lɛ, ebaaha tuber lɛ he lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dying suddenly even though the leaves were green just last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ gbo trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo otsi kome ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden dying, often caused by root rot or swollen shoot disease, happens when hidden viruses or fungi attack the tree's internal water pipes underground. It looks like a mysterious spell, but it is actually a biological infection in the root system.
ga: gbele trukaa Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo loo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ kɛbaa. Ebaa kɛ́ hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutua tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli nu paipii lɛ. Etamɔ teemɔŋ shɛɛ sane ko, shi eji nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips in a V-shape is a clear sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is an essential plant food that helps crops stay green and grow strong stems.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V su mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu waa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites living under the leaf. They suck the plant juice out, causing the leaf to twist and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, ni no haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do my yam vines grow so many big green leaves without forming large tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi babaoo ni efeee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii agboi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo tsɔ. Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ starch ato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava taste bitter and make people sick during long dry seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ŋɔɔ ni ehaa mɛi yeɔ hela yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally produces a protective defense chemical called cyanide when it gets stressed by dry weather or poor soil. Fermenting, soaking, or boiling the cassava properly removes this bitterness and makes it safe to eat.
ga: Cassava feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ cyanide kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hao lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei wo mli jogbaŋŋ, okɛwo nu mli, loo okɛwo mli lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ ni ebaaha efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. The plant gets stressed and discards its flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto nu he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why does that purple-flowered weed always make my sorghum and maize stunt and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa mi-sorghum kɛ mi-corn lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: That weed is called Striga (or witchweed). Its roots attach directly to your crop's roots underground like a parasite, stealing all the water and nutrients before the crop can use them.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi lɛ akɛ Striga (loo abɛi jwɛi). Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ dani tsei kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do groundnut flowers grow above ground but the nuts develop inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnut plants open their flowers above ground for pollination. Once pollinated, the plant sends long pegs growing downward to push the developing seed underground where it is protected from heat and sun.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee pollination. Kɛji akɛ pollination wo tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la he

english: Why are the fruit bunches on my oil palm trees turning black and rotting before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Oil palm flowers need tiny beneficial insects called weevils to carry pollen from male flowers to female flowers. If there are no insects around to pollinate, the fruit bunch cannot grow and will dry up.
ga: Mu tso fɔfɔi biɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmei. Koni ekɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli lɛ aya fɔfɔi yei amli. Kɛji kooloi ni baawo pollination bɛ lɛ Yibii akui lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and the swollen swollen branches appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni niji ni efuu lɛ miije kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and swollen stems are key signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). It is a viral infection spread by tiny insects called mealybugs, which weakens the tree and eventually stops it from producing pods.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni efuu lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud virus hela (CSSVD) lɛ eba. Eji hela ko ni jɛɔ muawai bibii amli kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaaa efee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather and high humidity. Excessive shade and poor water drainage allow the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod through splashing rainwater.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i, kɛ latsaa shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tiny, young cocoa pods turning brown and dropping off the tree before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ batsɔ blɔfo ni egbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ agbo.

english: Young cocoa pods drop off (a process called cherelle wilt) either naturally when the tree has more pods than it can feed, or due to stress caused by drought, pest attacks, or disease affecting the tree's nutrient supply.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ baagbee shi. (Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt) Taakɛ eji lɛ, tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. aloo yɛ haomɔ ni hɔmɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo hela ni saa tso lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers ask us to cut down diseased cocoa trees instead of giving us medicine to spray on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni wɔɔha amɛ tsofa ni amɛkɛwo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Certain viral diseases, like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, live inside the tree's sap and have no cure. Cutting down infected trees and nearby healthy-looking contact trees is the only proven way to destroy the virus and prevent it from killing the rest of your farm.
ga: Helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli ni amɛbɛ tsabaa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpataa hela lɛ hiɛ ni atsĩɔ enaa koni ekagbe oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What simple everyday practices can I do on my farm to prevent crop diseases from starting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo daa gbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei ahe helai akaje shishi?

english: Keeping your farm weeded, pruning shade branches to allow sunlight and airflow, regularly harvesting ripe pods, and immediately removing diseased pods from the farm will prevent pests and fungi from breeding.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shia tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Kpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa. Ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafɔ.

english: How long do I need to wait before planting new cocoa seedlings on land where infected trees were cut down?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should clear out all old roots and wait a few months to ensure any remaining virus dies off. When you replant, use disease-resistant hybrid seedlings recommended by extension officers to keep the new farm safe.
ga: Esa akɛ ofɔ shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ ahe ni omɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ helai ni eshwɛ lɛ egbo. Beni oduɔ ekoŋŋ Kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ atsu nii koni oŋmɔ hee lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Can diseases on my neighbor's farm cross over to infect my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mikookoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, crop diseases travel easily between farms through wind, rain splashes, insects carrying viruses, shared pruning tools, and even on the boots or clothing of farm workers walking between properties.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai fãa gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii ni hiɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ni ajaa kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔji ateŋ lɛ atadei loo atadei po anɔ.

english: Why do ants crawling on my cocoa trees make crop diseases spread faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ?

english: Ants protect and move around mealybugs, which are tiny sap-sucking insects that carry the swollen shoot virus. By farming these mealybugs for food, ants indirectly carry the disease from sick trees to healthy ones.
ga: Akpɔlɔi buɔ mealybugs, ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe ni amɛyaa amɛhe. ni ji shoot virus ni efuu lɛ he tsɔne Kɛtsɔ mealybugs nɛɛ ni akwɛɔ koni aye niyenii lɛ nɔ. Akpɔlɔi kɛ helai yaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa farm yielding far fewer pods this year even though my trees still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo pods fioo ko kwraa yɛ afi nɛɛ mli lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, mi-cacao tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo.

english: A hidden drop in yield usually means the soil is exhausted of nutrients, insect pests are damaging invisible flower buds, or the trees are in the early stages of a disease before visible leaf symptoms appear.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ teemɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miifite fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ ni anaaa. aloo tso lɛ yɛ hela lɛ shishijee mli dani baai lɛ ahe okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: How can agricultural extension officers assist me if a sudden disease outbreak hits my cocoa farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji hela ko ba trukaa yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers can visit your farm to correctly identify the disease, guide you on government support programs, assist with cut-out protocols, and provide access to disease-tolerant hybrid seedlings and safe chemicals.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ ayasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyoo helai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Wo bo ŋaa yɛ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ahe. Ye obua yɛ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli ni oha gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa dumɔwui ni akɛfee tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni helai kɛ tsofai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How do I select the right plantain suckers to make sure my new farm grows well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa koni miŋmɔ hee lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers,' which have narrow, blade-like leaves and strong, thick bases. Avoid suckers with wide leaves or any visible spots, holes, or rot at the bottom.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ loo ni anaa ŋmeii, bu, loo ŋmeii ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What is the proper way to handle and clean plantain suckers before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ plantain tsei ahe nii ni atsumɔ he dani aduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Before planting, trim off old roots and peel away any dark or damaged outer layers on the bulb to inspect for pests. Letting them dry briefly or dipping them in clean water mixed with wood ash helps prevent fungal infections.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, gbee shishifãi momoi lɛ ni ojie kponɔgbɛ fãi ni yɔɔ duŋ loo ni efite lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ bulb lɛ nɔ lɛ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha egbi minitii fioo komɛi loo okɛwo nu ni mli tse ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Can a diseased plantain sucker pass illness to my new soil and other plants?
ga: Ani plantain suckers ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie hela kɛya mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ kɛ tsei krokomɛi anɔ?

english: Yes, planting material is the main way diseases and underground pests spread. Using infected suckers carries rot directly into your clean land, ruining the new crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ titri ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbo tɛ̃ɛ kɛya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei

english: Why do the stems and roots of my plantain trees rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Rotting is usually caused by excess water sitting around the root zone, combined with soil fungal or bacterial infections. Good soil drainage and healthy planting material prevent waterlogging and decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔle shishifã lɛ he, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo hela ko ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain crop is dying from a disease or just bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ miigbe mi-plantain lɛ?

english: Diseased plants often show yellowing leaves even during rainy seasons, soft or foul-smelling stems, black spots, or roots that break off easily underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ baai ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eŋɔɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmeii diji, loo shishifãi ni fãa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Should I completely dig up and remove a plantain plant if it starts to rot?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ni majie plantain lɛ kɛji ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: Yes, you should carefully uproot and destroy diseased plants away from your field. Leaving them in the farm allows the infection to spread through the soil to neighboring healthy plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hela lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain or strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, but if pests like nematodes destroy the root system, the plant loses its grip on the soil. Supporting plants with wooden stakes and keeping roots pest-free keeps them standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni aha shishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: What type of soil do plantain roots need to stay healthy and avoid rotting?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ he hiaa ni plantain shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkafite?

english: Plantain roots thrive in loose, fertile soil rich in organic matter that drains water easily. Heavy clay soil that traps water will suffocate the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep dying after producing only one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ yaa nɔ egboɔ lɛ? Beni afee plantains ŋmɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ?

english: While an individual stem dies after fruiting, healthy roots should continuously sprout new suckers to take its place. Total plant death after one harvest means the root system was damaged by pests, disease, or poor soil.
ga: yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gboɔ beni ewo yibii sɛɛ. Esa akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni baaye amɛ najiaŋ. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni gboɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: How many years should a plantain farm stay healthy and produce fruit if managed well?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ plantain ŋmɔ ko ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: With clean planting material, fertile soil, and disease control, a plantain farm can continuously yield harvests for 3 to 5 years or longer through its regenerating suckers.
ga: kɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ Plantain ŋmɔji baanyɛ afee nibii ni yaa nɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛtsɔ suckers ni atsake amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so it doesn't get ruined by pests before the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite lɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba?

english: You can dry your maize properly until the grains are hard, then treat them with approved grain protectants or store them in airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) to keep insects out and preserve the grain for months.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbi o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ amɛhe nii loo akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli koni kooloi akabote mli ni akɛto dumɔwui lɛ ahe nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. Leaving it in the ground too long, especially during heavy rains, makes the tubers woody, watery, or prone to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni aaashi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei, nu loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya.

english: Always dry crops on a clean tarpaulin or a raised platform off the ground. Drying directly on soil exposes your harvest to dirt, ground moisture, fungal spores, and insects, which cause mold and quick spoilage.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbi yɛ tarp loo kpoku ni he tse nɔ ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ afee muji. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Mold kɛ kooloi bibii, ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ oya baa.

english: What green crops can I plant on my farm specifically to feed my goats during the dry season when wild grass dies?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei eŋɔli manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha mitooi lɛ niyenii, titri lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: You can plant drought-resistant leguminous shrubs like Gliricidia or fodder grasses like Elephant grass. They stay green longer into the dry season and provide high-protein feed when regular pasture dries up.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ glicidia loo jwɛi ni akɛyeɔ niyenii tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi. Amɛbaahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni amɛhaa niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein beni kooloi alɛɛhei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ mli egbi.

english: Can I safely feed leftover crop waste like cassava peels and cowpea vines to my animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mikooloi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsei lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, but fresh cassava peels must be dried thoroughly in the sun first to remove natural toxins. Cowpea vines can be fed fresh or dried into hay to provide valuable protein during feed shortages.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ agbi ŋmeii heei yɛ hulutsoo be mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni ejie tsofai fɔji kɛjɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Abaanyɛ akwɛ cowpea wain tsei lɛ ehee loo agbi amɛ akɛ jwɛi koni ekɛ protein ni he hiaa aha yɛ be mli ni niyenii faaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and yield small tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need light, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. Planting them too close forces them to compete with each other for these limited resources, resulting in thin stems and low yields.
ga: Tsei hia la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nibii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow from the bottom up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure early in the growth stage helps keep leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: How can I keep my soil moist and protect my vegetables when rain stops for weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo?

english: You can apply mulch—covering the bare soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves. Mulch traps soil moisture, lowers root temperature, and slows down water evaporation during hot dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. tsei ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Mulch baaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ha shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha nu lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Can I just save and replant seeds from my last maize harvest, or should I buy certified seeds every season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu ekoŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ daa afi?

english: While you can replant saved seeds, certified hybrid seeds yield much more because they are bred for vigor and disease resistance. Saved seeds from hybrids lose these traits, leading to lower yields in the next season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ejaakɛ atsɔse amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrids mli lɛ laajeɔ sui nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or soil fungal diseases that block the water tubes inside the plant. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like maize or cassava helps break the disease cycle in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsɔɔmɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: What is drip irrigation, and how does it help my cocoa trees during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi? kɛ bɔ ni aaafee aye abua kookoo tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Drip irrigation uses thin pipes to deliver water drop-by-drop straight to the roots of your cocoa trees. This keeps the soil moist through dry weather without wasting water through evaporation in the hot sun.
ga: Drip nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ paipi bibioo ko tsuɔ nii. Koni okɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ o-cocoa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni nu lɛ efiteee kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and stop making pods when there is a water shortage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛkpaa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, cocoa trees go into survival mode and drop their leaves to conserve moisture. Without enough soil water, the tree cannot feed new flowers or grow pods.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Cacao tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo fɔfɔi heei loo ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to clear old concrete structures and obstacles off the ground before laying irrigation pipes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie kɔnkrit tsũi momoi kɛ nibii ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akɛ nu shwiemɔ paipii awo mli lɛ?

english: Irrigation pipes need flat, clear ground to lay straight so water can flow evenly. Concrete or heavy rubbish can bend, block, or puncture the pipes, stopping water from reaching all your cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ paipii lɛ aná nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse koni ekɛma shi tɛ̃ɛ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɔnkrit loo jwɛi ni tsii baanyɛ abɔle, atsĩ, loo atswa paipii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ abote kookoo tso lɛ mli kwraa.

english: How does setting up a central water station help distribute water to every part of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu mlijaa he ko ni ato yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ajaa nu kɛyaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei fɛɛ?

english: A central water station pushes water through connected pipes directly to every corner of your farm, making sure every tree gets its share without you needing to carry heavy water buckets.
ga: Nu he ko ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ kɛ nu baa kɛtsɔɔ paipii ni akɛtsa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa egbɛfaŋnɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu baagi agbo aya he fɛɛ he.

english: Will giving my cocoa trees steady water during dry months increase the size of my harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha mi-cocoa tsei lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, steady water prevents drought stress, allowing the cocoa tree to continually produce healthy flowers and fill cocoa pods with larger, heavier beans throughout the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni anáa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni eyaa nɔ ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii awo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it better to store water in large open tanks or pump it directly through drip pipes to my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu lɛ ato nu agbo ko ni agbele naa mli loo matsɔ paipi ni hoɔ nu mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Direct drip pumping is often better because open storage tanks can lose a lot of water to heat evaporation and can run empty fast during severe droughts, whereas piped drip systems use water efficiently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nutoohei ni agbele naa lɛ baanyɛ afite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eho oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Yɛ be mli ni paipii ni akɛ nu shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa tree roots are getting enough water beneath the ground surface?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo shishifãi lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: You can dig a small hole near the base of the tree; if the soil a few inches down crumbles like dry dust in your hand, the roots are thirsty and need direct watering.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko. Ebaanyɛ ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ba shi inchi fioo lɛ efoɔ tamɔ sũ ni egbi yɛ onine mli. Kuma baaye shishifãi lɛ ni ehe baahia ni awo amɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is relying only on natural rainfall becoming risky for cocoa farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ji oshara kɛha Ghana kookoo okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Rains are becoming less predictable with longer dry spells. Relying only on rain leaves trees vulnerable to water shortages, which stunts pod growth and lowers your cocoa yield.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba be mli ni nugbɔ be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli ni nu faaa yɛ oshara mli lɛ pɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha pod lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni ebaaha o-cocoa lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is watering cocoa trees near their roots better than spraying water all over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha kookoo tso lɛ nu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ fe ni ooowo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nu lɛ?

english: Spraying water causes much of it to evaporate in the heat or feed unwanted weeds. Placing water right at the root zone ensures only your cocoa tree drinks it.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu babaoo atsɔ la kɛji akɛ edɔ loo aha jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ niyenii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa cacao tso lɛ pɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why is flat ground space so important when installing a farm watering system?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ he hiaa beni akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Water flows best on level ground. Flat ground allows irrigation lines to maintain steady water pressure so that trees at the far end of your farm get as much water as trees near the source.
ga: Nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu lɛ mli tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ aná nu babaoo tamɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛɛhe lɛ.

english: Can my cocoa trees keep producing high yields forever, or will their output naturally drop as they get older?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛya naanɔ? Aloo yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees reach their peak production period between 10 and 20 years of age. After this period, their yields naturally begin to decline due to aging branches, soil depletion, and higher vulnerability to diseases.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛ shweremɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 teŋ. Yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Yibiiwoo lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tsei niji lɛ daraa lɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ ni amɛyɔɔ helai ahe oshara babaoo mli

english: How do I know when an old cocoa farm is past its prime and needs to be replanted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko eho ehiɛyaa he ni ehe miihia ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: When trees grow very tall, yield fewer pods even with fertilizer, and show frequent disease signs like swollen shoots or constant black pod, the farm is aging out and requires rehabilitation or replanting.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da waa lɛ Pod yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ awo lɛ fɔ po. ni ejieɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu loo ŋmeii diji lɛ ahe okadii be fɛɛ be. Okwaafoi lɛ hu egbɔ ni ehe miihia ni asaa loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my newly planted cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them and keep the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How long does a new hybrid cocoa seedling take from planting until it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Is it safe to plant food crops like cassava and plantain alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ emasɛi? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Yes, intercropping with food crops is beneficial early on because plantains provide necessary shade, while crops like cassava generate quick food and income for your family while waiting for cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔi yɛ niyenii tsei ni akɛ niyenii tsei duɔ mra lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei ji niyenii kɛ shika ni oweku lɛ náa oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I consider planting other cash crops alongside cocoa instead of growing only cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu shika ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni mikɛbaafata kookoo he lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu kookoo pɛ

english: Growing multiple crops protects your family's income if cocoa yields decline due to unpredictable weather or disease, while also keeping the soil healthier through varied plant nutrition.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oweku lɛ shika he kɛji akɛ kookoo ni anáa lɛ ba shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei amli niyenii srɔtoi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce lower crop yields now compared to when I first cleared the land years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ be ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Continuous farming over many years removes essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus from the soil. Without organic matter or fertilizer to replace them, the soil becomes tired and less productive.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: What causes my cocoa trees to drop their flowers before the pods can form?
ga: Mɛni haa mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ?

english: Flowering loss usually happens when trees experience stress from long dry spells, extreme heat, severe nutrient shortages in the soil, or damage from sucking pests like capsids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo nɔ ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids ni amɛnuɔ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot while hanging on the tree during rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet weather and spreads quickly when there is poor air movement or excessive shade on the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do older, bushy cocoa farms suffer more from diseases than newly planted ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai yeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji momoi ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi babaoo fe ŋmɔji ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older and form thick, overgrown canopies, they trap humidity and block sunlight, creating an ideal damp environment for fungi and insect pests to breed.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ, Amɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their leaves from harsh sunlight and heat stress. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, intense sunlight scorches the young plants and dries out the soil before their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã tsei bibii ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ mli aba.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves is a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen runs low, the plant draws whatever nitrogen is left out of its older bottom leaves to feed new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni baa heei ahi nɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction the stem nodes point when I plant my cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmei nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf nodes pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new buds to grow downwards first, delaying plant growth and drastically reducing tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves. These insects also spread plant viruses that stunt leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ hu gbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ baa kɛ aduawai adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Staking raises yam leaves into the sunlight so the plant can absorb light and manufacture food to grow larger tubers underground. Leaving vines on the damp ground exposes leaves to fungal rots and shade from weeds.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ la ni ekɛ niyenii aba koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbo ni ebaaha jwɛi lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during the flowering stage helps keep the soil moist and encourages flowers to form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli baa lɛ mli. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ he hewalɛ yɛ tomato mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts fix natural nitrogen gas from the air into the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, providing free fertilizer to the maize plants growing alongside them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce tall bushes with big leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei kakadaji ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excess rain, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing stems and foliage instead of storing starch in the root tubers. Excessive shading also prevents tubers from expanding.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ, shading ni fe nine hu tsiɔ bulb lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to shield themselves from direct sun and reduce water loss through their pores during hot, dry hours. It is a protective signal that the crop is conserving internal moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi. Eji okadi ni tsiɔ hela naa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry granular fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ji granular lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb the nutrients. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots or sit unused on the ground until rain washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni akɛwooo mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baafɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to stay green and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or compost can help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks keep falling over when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ fioo ko miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over easily if they are planted too close together, if the soil is too shallow for deep roots, or if stem borer insects have eaten away the inside of the stalk near the ground.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ nyɛɛɛ atswa Aloo kɛji kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and sensitive leaves that burn in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted next to them to keep the soil moist and block harsh sun until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets in sunlight and air, which stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a symptom of Cassava Mosaic Disease. This disease is spread by tiny whiteflies that move from infected plants to healthy ones.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava produces natural defensive chemicals that turn bitter when the plant experiences stress, such as long dry spells or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Cassava feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when they do not get enough water regularly, or when there is a lack of essential nutrients like calcium in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ daa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do caterpillars only come out to eat my cabbage leaves at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ pɛ koni amɛbaye mi-cabbage baai lɛ?

english: Many caterpillars hide under the soil or leaf debris during the day to protect themselves from the hot sun and birds, coming out at night when it is cool and moist to feed.
ga: Kplukai babaoo kɛ amɛhe tee shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ baai amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛtsuɔ nii waa gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why does rain water sit on top of my land for days instead of sinking into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Water sits on top of the ground when the soil is tightly packed or heavy with clay. Adding decomposed leaves or organic manure loosens the soil so water can sink in.
ga: Nu kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni nu lɛ abote mli.

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, feels moist, crumbles easily in your hands, and contains visible life like earthworms, which help break down nutrients for plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Feeling moisturised Egbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ eyɛ nine mli Nibii ni anaa hu yɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbalaa niyenii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops start rotting in the ground whenever we get heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely soaked with water for long periods, crop roots cannot get air and begin to drown and decay, which causes waterlogging and rots root crops like cassava and vegetables.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Tse lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni ebɔi nu mli shwiemɔ kɛ fitemɔ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does heavy rainwater wash away the top layer of my soil and pull out my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ mitsei bibii lɛ?

english: Fast-flowing rainwater creates surface runoff that easily carries away loose topsoil and fertile nutrients, unearthing small crop seedlings that have shallow roots.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ feɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ oya. Amɛyana tsei bibii ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: How does making high soil mounds or ridges protect my crops during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Raising soil into ridges or mounds lifts root systems above standing water, allows excess rainwater to drain away naturally, and prevents plant roots from suffocating in soggy soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to dig water channels across my farm before the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nubu ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Digging drainage channels gives excessive rainwater a designated pathway to flow off your land safely without flooding your crops or destroying the farm structure.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ ni ooofo lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni etsɔ nɔ efo kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeee nɔ loo efiteee ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are my crops failing even when I plant them at the exact same time my parents used to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikpa shi eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ be kome too mli ni mifɔlɔi du lɛ moŋ?

english: Weather patterns are changing, bringing unpredictable rainy and dry seasons, which means traditional planting calendars can lead to crops being damaged by early droughts or unexpected floods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. Enɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, blema dumɔ kalandai baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afite kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni baa mra loo nu afua ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do strong rainstorms easily knock down my tall maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahum ni naa wa waa lɛ shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ anɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall softens the soil around the base of plants while high winds push against tall leaves, pulling shallow root systems right out of the wet ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ, baai lɛ Gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ he ni nu lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground breaks the impact of falling raindrops so they do not wash away soil, while also trapping soil moisture and cooling crop roots on hot days.
ga: Mulching haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, efɔɔɔ sũ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it safer for me to plant different crops together on one farm instead of planting only one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ?

english: Mixing different crops reduces risk because some plants handle heavy rains or pests better than others, ensuring you still harvest food even if one crop fails.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ haa oshara baa shi ejaakɛ tsei komɛi nyɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ obaakpa niyenii lolo kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome po fite.

english: Why do leaf spots and diseases spread so fast on my plants right after continuous rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ahe tsɔi kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Excess moisture and damp weather create an easy environment for fungal spores to hatch and spread quickly across wet crop leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha fungal spores lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ amli oya.

english: Why does fertilizer seem to lose its power when heavy rain falls right after I put it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the topsoil into water streams before plant roots have enough time to absorb the food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn is dry enough to grind into flour without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli ashikishaŋ ni efiteee?

english: Dry corn makes a sharp cracking sound when you bite a kernel or hit it with a stone. If corn is too wet when you mill it, the flour will trap moisture, grow mold quickly, and spoil within a few days.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi lɛ feɔ gbee ni naa wa waa kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔ loo okɛ tɛ ko tswa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ beni ashɛreɔ lɛ Ashikishaŋ lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fungus daa oya ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Why do some of my maize grains turn into a fine flour easily when milled, while others stay gritty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi tsɔɔ powda kpakpa mli oya kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi ji gazelle lolo lɛ.

english: Different varieties of maize have different seed structures. Softer corn varieties break down easily into fine powder, while harder varieties resist grinding and produce coarser grains used for different traditional meals.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi. Abele henɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efeɔ powda kpakpa. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni wa lɛ teɔ shi woɔ shwiemɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema niyenii srɔtoi amli lɛ.

english: Can I mix different colors or types of corn together before taking them to the mill?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa sui srɔtoi loo ŋmãa henɔi afutu? Ani abaanyɛ afutu amɛ dani akɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can mix them if you are preparing general animal feed, but for human food, mixing hard and soft grains causes uneven milling, leaving some parts powdery and others coarse.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afutu kɛji oosaa kooloi aniyenii fɛɛ. Shi kɛha adesa niyenii Dumɔwui ni wa kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa aba. Ha fãi komɛi afee powder ni fãi komɛi hu afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it more profitable for me to sell my maize as raw dried grains or process it into flour first?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ he akɛ aaahɔɔ ŋmãa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi loo aaafee lɛ ashikishaŋ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Grinding maize into flour adds value so you can sell it at a higher price to local kitchens and bakeries, but you must account for milling costs and use airtight packaging so the flour stays fresh.
ga: Abele ni oootsɔ ashikishaŋ mli lɛ haa ejara yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ oha maŋ lɛ mli ŋtayaai kɛ aboloofeemɔ hei kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ. Shi esa akɛ osusu shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he ni okɛ vacuum packaging atsu nii koni ashikishaŋ lɛ akafee ehee.

english: Why does my stored corn flour sometimes turn yellow or develop a sour smell after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mi-cornstarch ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sour smells and color changes happen when moisture is present in the grain before grinding. Bacteria and mold feed on that hidden water inside the flour, causing it to ferment and spoil.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli dani ashɛre lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ su tsakemɔ baa. Muawai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ ashikishaŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do my corn grains shrink and show tiny holes while drying on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shrinkage is normal as water leaves the grain during drying, but small holes mean pest insects like weevils are eating your corn from the inside, which reduces the total flour yield when milled.
ga: Shrinkage ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa akɛ nu shĩɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ, shi bu bibii tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii miiye ŋmaa lɛ kɛmiijɛ emli. Enɛ baaha starch ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ aba shi kɛ́ ashɛre.

english: How can I protect my dried corn from insects before I take it to be ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi adɛŋ dani mafolɔ mli?

english: You can store clean, well-dried corn in airtight hermetic bags or treat it with approved food-grade grain dust to keep insects out without making the future flour unsafe to eat.
