ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni he tse ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ ŋmãa sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii koni kooloi akabote mli ni eha wɔsɛɛ be mli ashikiŋsha akafee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn brown and dry up on their own in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize reaches full maturity, the plant naturally stops sending water to the leaves and focuses on drying out the cobs, indicating that the grain is ready to be harvested.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaakpa nu ni ekɛmajeɔ ebaa lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmãa lɛ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why should I weigh my harvested corn instead of just counting the number of bags I fill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ he moŋ fe ni makane kotokui enyiɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ?

english: Bags vary in size and packing tightness, so counting bags can trick you. Weighing your harvest gives you an exact measurement to calculate your profit and ensures buyers pay you fairly per kilogram.
ga: Baagi lɛ dalɛ kɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, kotokui ni akaneɔ lɛ baanyɛ alaka bo. Kɛ́ osusu nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa onáa susumɔ ni ja ni okɛbuɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni onáa lɛ he akɔntaa. Ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ náa hekɛnɔfɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiwo bo jara ni sa kɛha kilogram kome.

english: Why is it important for me to write down how much seed and fertilizer I used this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni miŋmala dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ?

english: Keeping written records helps you compare what you spent against the total weight of crop you harvest, showing you clearly if your farm made a profit and how to plan for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nɔ ni ofite lɛ toɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okpa lɛ ahe. Etsɔɔ bo faŋŋ kɛji sɛɛnamɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he. Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ ato gbɛjianɔ aha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil quickly. Keeping tall canopy trees or planting shade crops like plantains protects the young seedlings from severe heat until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients before I plant my next batch of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu mi-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your soil is pale and hard, or if previous crops had stunted growth and yellowing leaves, the soil is low in nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer restores essential food into the soil so your maize can grow tall and produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni o-abele lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ wala shihilɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when it rained earlier in the week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ otsi lɛ shishijee mli moŋ?

english: In intense sun, crops lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the dry surface soil. Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture for much longer.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) aha onibii ahe koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants with very small fruits or cobs. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow fully and yield a much larger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, shishifãi ahe he, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-free, resistant cassava varieties prevents the virus from damaging your crop leaves, ensuring healthy tuber development underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai bɛ mli ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akabote otsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest produce weaker plants than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can carry hidden diseases from the previous season and gradually lose their vigor over time. Certified seeds are specially bred and treated to resist common local diseases, survive dry weather better, and grow uniformly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa fiofio. Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehi akɛ ooohi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. ni amɛdara daa

english: How do weeds lower my harvest if they are just growing on the sides of my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressive, stealing water, soil fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early during the crop's first few weeks gives your plants the food and space they need to grow strong and high-yielding.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to cut off extra stems and bottom leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishi baai lɛ?

english: Trimming useless extra shoots (suckers) directs the plant's food and energy straight into developing large, healthy tomatoes instead of wasting energy on growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni he ehiaaa ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ koni ená tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops so they do not rot in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Crops show natural signs of maturity, such as lower leaves turning yellow and drying up, stalks hardening, or fruits changing to their final mature color. Harvesting too early or too late makes crops prone to spoiling quickly after picking.
ga: Tso lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ he okadii akpo, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi, shishifãi ni wa, loo aduawai ni tsɔɔ amɛnaagbee su ni egbɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso ni miida lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and build leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it continuously in the same place drains those specific nutrients completely and allows pests and soil diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil richer for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special root structures that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ

english: Why should I place fertilizer right next to my crops instead of scattering it everywhere on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near crop roots ensures the plant gets to absorb the nutrients directly, rather than wasting expensive fertilizer on weeds or allowing it to wash away in heavy rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ loo oha amɛho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves and center whorl of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest whose caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of the maize plant to feed on young leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and hard instead of swelling into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ ni amɛfuu ni amɛdara lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand when the soil is too hard and compacted, or when the soil lacks potassium, which is the key nutrient responsible for root and tuber enlargement.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni ji niyenii titri ni haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly because of extreme heat or erratic watering, which stresses the plant and prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating and forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: You should wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains so there is enough deep ground moisture to sprout the seeds and keep them growing through short dry spells.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii 2-3 ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted over centuries to survive harsh local conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow strong fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu He ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai loo bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli koni amɛkaho?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a moderate rain, but not when the field is flooded. Covering the fertilizer lightly with soil prevents heavy rain and direct heat from destroying or washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi jeee beni nu eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekafite loo efo lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole patterns in the centers of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. They hide deep inside the center of the maize plant where the tender leaves grow and eat them from the inside.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ baa nɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui mli tɔ̃ɔ he ni baai bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap, or spreading a plant virus that causes the leaves to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo tsei amli helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa

english: How can I stop my cassava roots from rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Cassava rots mainly when water collects around the roots in heavy soil without draining away. Planting cassava on top of raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain off, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from forming seeds, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do some farmers plant maize and cassava together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize and cassava together helps you maximize your land and harvest at different times. Maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving space and light for the cassava to mature later without wasting effort.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ohaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni okpaa ŋmãa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko kɛ la koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli ni okɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ efiteee.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing into fruits when I grow them alongside other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani edaa ni ewoɔ aduawai beni midu lɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they feel stressed, often caused by competing with nearby crops for light, extreme heat, or inconsistent water and soil nutrients.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ akaŋshii kɛha la, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my crops after the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rain is consistent and the soil stays moist for a few days. Planting too early after just one light rain can burn your seeds if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer or spray my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because cool temperatures allow the plant to absorb nutrients safely without the hot midday sun scorching the leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he shweshweeshwe ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shãaa baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell early on if my growing maize crop is healthy and will give a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male enɛ mra? Ani mi-abele ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy maize has dark green, broad leaves and thick stems. If the leaves turn yellow or start curling, the plant is telling you it lacks nutrients, water, or is under attack by pests.
ga: Abɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikɛɛ bo akɛ niyenii, nu, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves but producing small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Cassava plants stretch tall when they are planted too close together or don't get direct sunlight, using all their energy on leaf growth instead of building tubers underground.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɛ amɛhe. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii

english: Yam rot happens when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, creating wet conditions that allow soil pests and disease fungi to enter and destroy the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni haa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds every season instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ daa be mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved seeds are bred to resist local diseases, tolerate drought, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over time and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni sa mli ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are extension officers telling us not to plant tomatoes in the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly builds up tomato-specific pests and diseases in the soil and depletes the nutrients tomatoes need, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ kɛ tomato he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tomato lɛ baa shi Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings right after I clear and plant the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil and sprout immediately when exposed to sunlight and water, growing rapidly to steal food and water from your young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nu shɛ enɔ. Edaa oya koni eju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ odumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my crops grow better than planting on an open farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a structure covered with clear plastic or mesh that creates a protected environment for plants. It guards high-value crops like tomatoes and peppers against heavy rains, scorching sun, and pests, allowing you to harvest healthy vegetables all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ he ko ni abuɔ he. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa kɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for growth. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the air gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get consistent water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers. Providing light shade and keeping the soil evenly moist helps preserve the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with thin stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too close, they shade one another and compete for sunlight. The plants stretch upward quickly to reach the light, resulting in tall, weak stems that break easily and produce fewer fruits.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe oya koni eshɛ kane lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baakumɔ oya ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up naturally during hot afternoons to save water and protect themselves from drying out. If they unroll in the cool evening, the crop is fine, but if they stay rolled up in the morning, the field needs urgent watering.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ nu akafite ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni egbi lɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ mli gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi, shi kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli lolo leebi lɛ. Ehe miihia ni awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice from young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do the small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads in cool, damp, shade-heavy conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air into the cocoa farm helps prevent the fungus from damaging the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ waa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ mli?

english: Ragged holes and green droppings mean Fall Armyworm caterpillars are hiding and feeding inside the central leaf funnel of your maize. They feed during the cool early morning or evening to avoid direct sunshine and birds.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe ni amɛmiiye nii yɛ o-corn lɛ baai lɛ amli. Amɛtaoɔ niyenii leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ koni hulu la kɛ okpoi akashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava crop is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking. You can carefully dig up one plant to confirm that the tubers are thick and firm before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome he nii koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ bulbs lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so the roots can take them in. If you apply fertilizer to dry soil under hot sun, the concentrated chemicals can burn the roots and kill the plants.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: Why can't I just scatter my cocoa seeds randomly on my land like we used to do in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ magbɛ kookoo ŋmeii ashwã mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Planting in measured rows with proper spacing ensures every cocoa tree gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, leading to healthier trees and much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kookoo tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and burn easily in full sunlight; planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural cover and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aaadu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree through pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive shoots and overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to pass through the tree, which stops fungal diseases from breeding and helps the plant put energy into growing big cocoa pods.
ga: Tsoi lɛ afolɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wooo yibii kɛ tsei niji ni mli ewo wu fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ woɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Does leaving tall weeds around my cocoa trees protect the soil or harm my crop?
ga: ŋmɛɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ he Ani cacao tsei buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Weeds steal vital water and nutrients away from your cocoa trees and provide hiding places for harmful pests, so keeping the base of your trees clean helps your crop thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ náa he ko ni amɛhiɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha otso lɛ shishi he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is tired and needs added nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ niyenii krokomɛi awo mli?

english: When soil loses its richness, cocoa leaves often turn pale or yellow, trees stop growing actively, and pod yields drop significantly; applying compost or recommended fertilizer restores the missing nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ kpa dalɛ. ni pod yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are mature enough to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease caused by excess moisture in bushy or overcrowded farms; clearing weeds, pruning excess branches, and removing infected pods keeps the farm dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ loo mɛi ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ mli baa. jwɛi ni ajieɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: What is causing the young shoots on my cocoa trees to turn brown and look like they were burnt by fire?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ?

english: This damage is caused by capsid insects that bite and suck sap from young leaves and stems; spraying approved treatments at the correct time of year protects your trees from this destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji capsid kooloi ni ŋmɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ he.

english: My cocoa trees produce many tiny flowers, but why do most of them fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects called midges to pollinate them so pods can form; if the farm is too dry or sprayed heavily with harsh chemicals, those midges die off and unpollinated flowers drop.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ midges akɛ pollinators koni amɛfee pods. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa efɔ nɔ lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baagboi ni fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do modern hybrid cocoa trees start bearing fruit much faster than the traditional trees on old farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa fe blema cacao tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees are specifically bred to grow faster and resist common stress, allowing them to produce pods in about 2 to 3 years compared to older varieties that take up to 5 years.
ga: Atsɔse cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛte shi amɛwo haomɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli, kɛ akɛto ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ ni baanyɛ ahé afii enumɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green or half-ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lolo loo amɛshɛ fã lɛ?

english: Harvesting unripe cocoa pods results in small, flat beans that weigh less and cannot ferment properly, leading to poor quality cocoa that buyers will reject.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni edako ni akpaa lɛ haa kokoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsiimɔ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight when they are small because their leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains around them provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ darako ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting during the major rainy season?
ga: Kɛji oodu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ abɔ he shɔŋŋ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures each stalk gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce large cobs without choking neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa ni ato lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75 ni tsei ateŋ lɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 40, ni ehaa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmãa wuji ni ekɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crops are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves stay green and feed the growing grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ebaaha dumɔwui ni miida lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Is it better to burn my cleared bush or leave the cut grass to rot on my farm before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ loo abaaha jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu?

english: Leaving cut brush to decompose naturally creates mulch that protects topsoil from heavy rains, keeps the soil cool and moist, and slowly releases essential nutrients back into your farmland.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi brɔshi ni afo lɛ koni egbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How do I stop armyworms from destroying the leaves of my young maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi cutworms lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Inspect your maize early in the morning when armyworms are active. You can hand-pick them on small farms or spray approved insecticides directly into the center funnel of the young plants where the worms hide.
ga: Kwɛmɔ o-corn lɛ mli leebi beni cutworms lɛ miitsu nii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ onine atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ he ni kooloi lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black spots are usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in humid weather. Pruning extra tree branches improves airflow to dry out moisture, and removing infected pods keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Black spot ji Black Pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to produce fruit after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need strong roots to establish quickly. Trimming old roots and peeling the corm clean before planting, along with adding organic manure to the planting hole, helps them grow faster and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe miihia shishifãi ni wa koni amɛma shi oya. Kpɔ̃ɔ shishifãi momoi lɛ ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ dani odu. Kɛfata he lɛ, akɛ organic fertilizer woɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between overly dry and overly wet. Regular watering and mulching around the roots help stabilize moisture levels.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ daa Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa.

english: How can I tell the exact time my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures high bean quality and good fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa bean lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my heavy rainfalls crush my young vegetable seedlings, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ mi aduawai bibii lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Heavy raindrops hit tender plants with strong force, which breaks weak stems and washes away soil. Covering your seedbed with a sloped thatch or mesh screen breaks the heavy drops into a fine mist while still letting sunlight through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tswa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ gbálaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛ sũ lɛ hoɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo ŋwɛi ŋta ni etse ehe lɛ ha odumɔwui saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni mli wa aba. Efeɔ afua kpakpa yɛ be mli ni ehaa hulu la lɛ tsɔɔ mli lolo.

english: Why is it important to leave open sides on my seedling nursery shed instead of closing it completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná fã ko ni agbele yɛ mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekpa kwraa?

english: Open sides allow cool air to flow continuously through the nursery, preventing trapped heat from scorching young plants while helping stem tissue grow stronger against breezes.
ga: Fãi ni agbele lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Etsiɔ la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekashã tsei bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get black spots and rot when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, air cannot flow between the leaves. Moisture from rain or dew gets trapped on the leaves for too long, creating damp conditions where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ baai lɛ ateŋ. Nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How does placing fine insect netting over my cabbage crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fine netting acts as a physical wall that stops moths and beetles from landing on leaves to lay eggs, keeping destructive caterpillars off your crops without needing chemical sprays.
ga: Mesh kpakpa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ji ladybugs lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee baai anɔ koni amɛwo amɛwui. Tsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi fe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Morning watering gives plants moisture for the hot day, and the daytime breeze quickly dries excess water off the leaves. Watering at night leaves foliage wet in the dark, inviting fungal diseases and pests.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa nu yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ duŋ mli. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy when I store it inside a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still holds moisture. In an enclosed room without breeze, heat and moisture build up, creating the perfect environment for mold and fungi to ruin the grain.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaaa lɛ mli Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo baabua amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite ŋmaa lɛ.

english: How can I keep flies and bugs away from my hot peppers while drying them in the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛmiigbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering drying peppers with a thin, breathable mesh wire or net allows hot air and sunlight to pass through while preventing flies and insects from laying eggs on the fruit.
ga: Akɛ waya loo ŋshɔŋloo bibioo ko baaha chili ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni tsiɔ amɛnaa koni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should the roof of my grain drying shed have a steep slant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ etse lɛ?

english: A steep slant forces heavy rainwater to drain off immediately rather than pooling on top, preventing leaks from dripping into your drying crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee nɔ ko yɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote onibii ni egbi lɛ amli.

english: When standing rainwater collects around roots, it cuts off their oxygen supply and smothers them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well inside my plastic shade house during the hottest months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi plastic greenhouses lɛ amli yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plastic sheets trap heat like an oven. If there are no open mesh vents to let hot air escape and cool breezes enter, high temperatures stress the plants and cause their blossoms to drop off.
ga: Plastic tsɔji mɔɔ dɔlɛ tamɔ flɔnɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsɔnei ni agbeleɔ ni akɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ baa lɛ bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little food it has to the new leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as long dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination from small insects. Providing shade trees and organic compost helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Niyenii nibii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ pollin. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and top-heavy leaves, making them easy to push over in strong winds. Supporting them with wooden stakes and planting them in deep, rich soil gives them better stability.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa wɔ kɛya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ ni aduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii amli lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my stored seed yams starting to sprout before the rain even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ dani nugbɔ po bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their sleeping state after a few months as warm weather begins. Storing your harvested yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn away from direct sunlight slows down premature sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe shihilɛ lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ o-sweet potato ni okpa lɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ekɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing big green leaves but not producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages tomato plants to spend all their energy growing thick leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Switching to a balanced fertilizer rich in phosphorus helps the plant produce more tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaaha o-tomato tsei lɛ afite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baai ni mli tse. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai adumɔ najiaŋ lɛ Kɛ́ otsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo tomato babaoo.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop leaves and roots decay in the soil, they feed the soil with natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not right before a heavy downpour. Burying or covering the fertilizer lightly with soil next to the plant stem prevents the rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, shi jeee dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ fu loo okɛ sũ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo yɛ tso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ̃ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, poorly drained soils during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of young maize plants to eat the tender leaf tissue. Applying approved biopesticides or organic neem spray early in the morning reaches them before they damage the growing point.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii leebi maŋkpa. Esa akɛ awo mli dani efite he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread viruses. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with neem oil or mild soap water controls these insects and keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi. Ekudɔɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my vegetable crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of plastic or glass that protects crops from extreme weather, direct heavy rains, and pests. It creates a controlled environment where delicate vegetables like tomatoes and peppers can grow faster, stay healthier, and produce higher yields all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo glase fee ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ehaa shihilɛ ni akudɔ lɛ baa. he ni aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Does a greenhouse need to be very large before it can be useful on my farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afee wuji waa dani amɛhe aba sɛɛnamɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, a greenhouse does not need to be big to be effective. Even a small, simple structure built to fit your available land can successfully shield high-value seedlings and crops from harsh weather and pests.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni greenhouse lɛ afee agbo dani enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsũi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ama koni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ momo lɛ akpã gbee lɛ po baanyɛ abu dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Can I grow delicate vegetables in the open field during heavy rainy seasons without any cover?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli ni nɔ ko bɛ he?

english: You can grow crops in the open field, but heavy rain can wash away soil nutrients, damage blossoms, and cause fungal diseases. Simple covered structures or greenhouses help control moisture and protect delicate plants from water stress.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, efite fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ tsũ yiteŋ loo tsũ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu he haomɔ he.

english: Why are crop seeds like cabbage or tomato so small, yet they grow into large plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui tamɔ kaabe loo tomato daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei wuji lɛ?

english: Tiny seeds contain concentrated genetic information and energy reserves needed to sprout. Once placed in moist, nutrient-rich soil, the seed unlocks its growth capability, using sunlight and soil nutrients to rapidly build a full-sized plant.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe saji babaoo kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbeleɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii tsuɔ nii koni amɛfee tsei ni dara oya lɛ naa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together to get an abundant farm, will they produce more?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Ani dumɔwui babaoo baaje kpo?

english: Planting too closely often reduces your total usable yield. When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, weak crops rather than a healthy, abundant harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, o ma ná ní kpami babauu nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: How can I tell if my soil has the strength to support a high crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertile soil is typically rich in organic matter, dark in color, and retains moisture without getting waterlogged. Healthy soil allows plant roots to easily draw nutrients, leading to deep green leaves and strong fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ, ehiɛ su ji ediŋŋ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ aduawai ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers in clusters, but some drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ? Shi tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomatoes form flowers in clusters to maximize pollination opportunities. Flowers often drop without making fruit when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients like calcium during flowering.
ga: Tomatoi fɔ̃ɔ yɛ kui amli koni ekɛha pollination hegbɛi lɛ aya hiɛ. Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ amɛmli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why are my pepper fruits smaller when the plant produces a huge quantity of them at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ feɔ bibioo beni tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: A plant has a limited supply of water and nutrients to share among its fruits. When it produces a large abundance of peppers at once, it divides its energy among all of them, resulting in smaller individual sizes unless given additional fertilizer and water.
ga: Tsei bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaajara aduawai lɛ amli. Kɛji ejie chili babaoo yɛ be kome mli Ebaajara hewalɛ yɛ chili ŋmeii fɛɛ ateŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. ja amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu krokomɛi

english: Why do some cassava varieties yield many small tubers in a cluster while others produce a few large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo yɛ kui amli. Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi haa yitsei wuji enyɔ loo etɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different genetic traits for yield distribution. Some varieties direct their energy to form a higher abundance of small-to-medium tubers in a cluster, while others direct their nutrients into growing fewer, larger tubers.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi kɛha amɛ yibiiwoo mlijaa. Henɔi komɛi kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee bulb bibii kɛyashi teŋgbɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ kui amli. Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ koni amɛfee bulb bibii kɛyashi wuji ni daaa fioo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look small and pale even though I planted them during the right season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe tseee eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ moŋ? Adu yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Stunted or pale crop growth usually indicates a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, poor soil drainage, or root damage from pests. Adding compost or the right fertilizer restores the soil's capability to feed the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni edaaa ni egbɔjɔ loo amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ. aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite shishifãi lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye abua otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from bigger plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from harsh sunlight. Without shade, intense heat burns the young leaves and dries out the moisture the cocoa plant needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei adɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Why do I see tiny caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the growing center of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves, which weakens the plant early if not controlled.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ oya kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant carry calcium to developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛna ŋmɔlɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in flooded soil. Excess water fills the air spaces in heavy or flat soil, suffocating the roots and allowing fungi to rot them underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally restores soil fertility that heavy-feeding crops like maize used up.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did my maize produce tall leaves but very small cobs after I added fertilizer late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ baai kakadaji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer too late encourages the plant to grow green leaves instead of feeding the ears. Fertilizer must be applied early in the plant's life so it has nutrients ready when forming cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni eeeha toi lɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ mli mra bɔni afee ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahi shi beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔi shibaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough for crops without using expensive testing tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kaa nibii ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbly to the touch, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and contains earthworms, which show that organic matter is present.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during heavy wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: When too many suckers (shoots) grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for root space and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves stronger roots to anchor the main tree.
ga: Beni suckers (tso) babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tso lɛ tsei afomɔ kroko baaha shishifãi ni mli wa aba tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass around the base of pepper plants during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool under hot sun, and prevents weeds from growing around your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in the storage barn before I am ready to sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani mifee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally sprout when exposed to warmth, light, and humidity. Storing yams in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn signals to the tuber to stay asleep longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ, la, kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ewɔ be babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to shelter them, the harsh heat burns their leaves and dries up the moisture they need to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ dumɔwui bɛ ni baaha amɛhe lɛ, la ni naa wa lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ agbi.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by stemborers or fall armyworms. These caterpillars eat the soft central leaves and bore into the stem, which prevents the maize plant from getting nutrients to form strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers loo fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa amɛfeɔ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaf. They suck out the plant's sap and can pass on diseases that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni haaa baai lɛ adara lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but only produce small, thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are given excess nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing thick upper leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei lɛ baato hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground toward the sun. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy through photosynthesis, which flows down into the ground to build bigger yam tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛ naa hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of balance in soil nutrients. Without stable water and mild temperatures, the flowers cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni ehiii. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi.

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, steal water, food, and light from the main plantain tree. Removing extra suckers leaves enough strength for the main tree to grow a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots collect nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps food crops like maize grow better.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ buaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs animal manure before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia kooloi ashishifã dani adu?

english: If your soil feels very sandy, loses water quickly, or looks light in color, it lacks organic matter. Adding animal manure helps the soil hold onto water and provides steady food for growing crops.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eji ŋã waa Nu ni laajeɔ oya loo ehiɛ su ni mli tseee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often heats up dry soil without soaking deep enough. If a long dry patch follows that first rain, seeds get trapped in hot, damp soil and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ he ko ni egbi kakadaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of ragged holes with small droppings inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that burrows into the leaf funnel during the day to feed on tender growth, which weakens the plant before it can produce ears.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ baai amli lasu ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye gbekɛbii bibii ni dara lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ dani enáa toi.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. It prevents the plant from producing food efficiently, resulting in stunted growth and smaller cassava roots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa fioo, ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the tips and dying off in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This yellowing indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow plenty of leafy green branches but produce almost no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ niji kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko kwraa bɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Adding phosphorus and potassium helps trigger blooming and fruiting instead of just green leaves.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Fosfɔs kɛ potassium ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ moŋ fe baai eŋɔli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and fall over easily when I plant three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the stalks stretch tall and thin to reach light, leaving them too weak to support heavy winds or ears.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eshɛɔ la lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishitso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo toi.

english: Why do my yam vines yield larger tubers when I train them up on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight to manufacture food, while also keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal leaf spot diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha amɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni fungal leaf spot hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my newly transplanted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaf shade and retain soil moisture, creating a cool microclimate that protects cocoa seedlings during their tender first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to save water. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to direct heat, the plant slows down water loss through evaporation during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahiɛ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomato fruits turning dark brown, sunken, and leathery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, efo mli, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants experience uneven watering or a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is rapidly forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔ tomato tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be loo calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai miiba oya lɛ.

english: Groundnuts have a unique growth habit called 'pegging.' Once the above-ground flower is pollinated, the stem grows downward and pushes into the moist soil so the actual nut can develop safely underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ dalɛ su krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘fixation’ kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie amɛhe. Tso lɛ tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni anɔkwa ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash nutrients out of the soil, so applying fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid burning cleared bush on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?
