english: Burning destroys the natural topsoil and kills beneficial organisms that feed your crops. Leaving cleared vegetation to decay into mulch naturally enriches the soil and keeps it moist for longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa shade and soil moisture during its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to plant my crop seeds in straight rows instead of spreading them randomly?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ trukaa?

english: Planting in straight rows gives every plant enough space to receive sunlight and nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my tomato leaves and stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-tomato lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes are usually made by pest insects, such as caterpillars or beetles, feeding on the plant. Clearing surrounding weeds where pests hide and applying organic or recommended sprays protects your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. He ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu onibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by hot temperatures, dry soil, or low nutrients. Regular watering and placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and helps flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to accumulate in the field. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or beans naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to resist common local diseases and withstand dry spells. Saved seeds gradually lose their strength over generations, leading to lower crop yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni amɛte shi amɛwo hɔmɔ shihilɛi. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ fiofio yɛ wala be fɛɛ mli Ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching crop roots and encourages fungal diseases to rot the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds lower the amount of food my crops yield at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ náa kɛji akpa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and ground nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the energy they need to produce large tubers, grains, or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji, dumɔwui, loo aduawai.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen from the soil or their roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving farm drainage helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛaawo mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much fertilizer. Regular watering during hot periods helps the plants hold onto their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their delicate leaves from harsh sunlight and heat. Without shade from bigger trees or plantains, the sun scorches the leaves and dries out the roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji loo plantains lɛ ahe hulutsoo bɛ lɛ Hulu la baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away and keeps the tubers safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that cannot support heavy weight against strong winds. Supporting the stalk with a strong wooden prop pole helps hold the tree up until the bunch is fully ripe.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ nibii ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that bakes the topsoil. If seeds sprout and the soil dries up, the tender roots die, so it is safer to wait until the rains are regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wood instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes to get maximum sunlight on their leaves. The leaves use sunlight to make food, which travels down to create larger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and produce smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Because weeds grow fast, they starve your main crop of the food it needs to develop strong stems and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya No hewɔ lɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni amɛná ŋmeii kɛ yibii ni wa lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When these plants die and decay, they leave behind rich, natural plant food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛfite lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a long dry season only wets the top layer of dirt while the deeper soil remains hot and dry. Seeds need steady moisture to sprout, so planting too early causes the seeds to dry out and die before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he edɔ ni egbi. Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aje shishi.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room to swell and form big, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it, or the soil has run out of nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize eats up a lot of food from the dirt and leaves the soil weak. Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab clean nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, refreshing your field for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ sũ babaoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen ni he tse kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the dirt quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa muji agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce smaller yields than new seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are specially bred in laboratories to give high yields and resist diseases. Seeds saved from your own farm lose those strong traits in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai akamɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ baafite nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my yam mounds need to be high and made of loose soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ afee nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni efee sũ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing down into the earth. High mounds with soft, loose soil allow the roots to grow long and thick without hitting hard dirt that stops them from expanding.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ amɛshwiemɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ nɔ.

english: If a tomato plant has too many branches, it wastes its strength growing leaves instead of fruit. Trimming extra shoots forces the plant to send all its water and food straight into making larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji o-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji babaoo Ebaaha baai ni miida lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi yɛ aduawai lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛha tomatoi lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant soya beans on the same farm alongside my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu soybeans yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Soya beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This feeds the corn plants naturally, helping them grow stronger and reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Soybeans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa, ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant corn on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting corn continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that attack corn to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does leaving the stems and leaves of soya beans in the field after harvest help my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybean tsei kɛ baai ni mishiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soya bean stems and leaves decompose in the ground, they turn into natural compost that returns rich organic nutrients and nitrogen back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Kɛji soybean tsei kɛ baai lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your corn is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots and preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and look droopy in the afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves from losing too much moisture until the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛgboiɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my soya bean plants without making any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Soya bean plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water during flowering, or missing nutrients in the soil, which prevents the plant from having enough energy to form seed pods.
ga: Soybean tsei lɛ baafite amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa miipiŋ amɛ. Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee dumɔwui akutsei.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to fight for light instead of using their energy to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds grow aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly away from your crops, effectively starving your main plants even if weather conditions are good.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi po.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my soya beans so they do not split open on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa soybeans? Koni soybean dumɔwui akagbala yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Soya beans are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and fall off, the pods turn light brown, and the seeds inside make a dry rattling sound when you shake the pod.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Pods lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ gbee ni miigbi kɛji otsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop dark mold inside storage bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-nitoohe kotokui lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mold grows when corn is put into bags before it has completely dried under the sun. The trapped moisture creates a warm, wet environment that allows destructive fungi to spread through the grains.
ga: Muji baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa wo kotokui amli dani ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mimasɛi lɛ? Cocoa dumɔwui ni adu ehee?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry up and die. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: I found small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize, why is this happening?
ga: Miyana ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ amli. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks the growing point of maize plants. They target healthy young leaves to feed, and treating them early with an approved pesticide protects the plant before it gets destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Amɛkwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛhaa niyenii. kɛ amɛ tsamɔ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ebuɔ tsei ahe dani efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, showing that your soil needs compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. It stops the leaves from making food properly, which reduces tuber size, so removing infected plants helps save the rest of your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Ehaa baai lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ dalɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any tomatoes when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination. To save water and energy, the plant sheds its flowers; providing root mulch and watering regularly during hot weather helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to keep seeds from my maize harvest to plant next season or buy new packaged seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni akɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwoɔ paketii amli?

english: Commercial packaged seeds (hybrids) are specifically bred to yield high harvests and resist pests and dry spells. Replanting seeds from your previous harvest often leads to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli (hybrid) lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hulutsoo be. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to seize nutrients and water quickly. Clearing them during the first three to four weeks is crucial so they do not steal food and light from your young crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛjie niyenii kɛ nu oya. Ehe miihia ni ajie amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll upward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from losing water to heat. It shrinks the leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun to preserve moisture inside the stem.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ kɛyaa dɔlɛ mli lɛ he. Ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of small holes and powder when stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Insects called weevils bore into stored maize to lay eggs and feed on the grain, especially if the maize was not dried completely before storage. Proper drying and using airtight storage bags prevents them from attacking your grain.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmãa ni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Kɛ́ ogbi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatutua odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my farm water channels get full of mud and dry weeds, and why must I clean them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ muji kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ mli daa lɛ?

english: Water channels get blocked by mud, leaves, and weeds brought by heavy rain. Cleaning them out regularly keeps water flowing smoothly to your crops' roots, which stops water from collecting in one spot and drowning your plants.
ga: Muji, baai kɛ jwɛi ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛbaa lɛ etsĩ nu gbɛi lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ otsu he nii daa lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ he kome ni ekɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Why does my drip irrigation hose stop giving water to my vegetable crops after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-drip irrigation paipi lɛ kpaɔ nu ni ekɛhaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: The small holes in drip hoses get blocked by dirt, river sand, or algae in the water. Flushing clean water through the pipes and wiping the small holes keeps them clear so all your crops get an equal amount of water.
ga: Muji, faa mli ŋã, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ etsĩ buji bibii ni yɔɔ paipi ni hoɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Nu ni mli tse ni oootsɔ paipii lɛ mli ni otsumɔ buji bibii lɛ amli lɛ baaha paipii lɛ mli atse bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: How do well-cleaned drainage ditches protect my maize during heavy rainy seasons in Ghana?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-ŋmãa lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Clear drainage ditches quickly carry excess rain away from your field. If debris blocks these ditches, rain collects in the farm, rotting crop roots and washing away the rich topsoil your crops need to grow.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni mli tse lɛ baajie nugbɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ oya kɛjɛ oyale mli. Kɛji sũ ni efite lɛ tsi nɛkɛ nubui nɛɛ anaa lɛ Nugbɔ baabua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. tsei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni he hiaa ni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I clear dead plants and weeds from around the stems of my crops instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Dead leaves and weeds lying close to crop stems trap damp air and act as hiding places for insects and fungus. Clearing this trash allows air and sunlight to reach the base of your plants, keeping them dry and healthy.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ashwieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ha tso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers ask us to burn or bury rotten cocoa pods far from the farm instead of leaving them under the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ biɔ ni ashã loo afu kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ, moŋ fe ni amɛaashi amɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Rotten pods carry black pod disease spores that can easily jump to healthy pods through rain splashes. Removing and destroying the bad pods breaks the disease cycle and stops it from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Pod ni egbo lɛ yɛ black pod hela he tsɛŋemɔ helai, ni baanyɛ atsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ atsɔ pods ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ oya. Pods gbohii ni ajieɔ kɛfiteɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaaa gbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and causes maize pests to build up in the field. Switching to crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil food and reduces pests.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: What happens if I leave my farmland completely empty without planting anything during the short dry season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miduuu nɔ ko yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli?

english: Leaving soil completely bare exposes it to hot sun and harsh winds, which dry out the ground and destroy good nutrients. Planting cover crops like cowpea protects the dirt and adds natural food back into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ, ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaafite niyenii kpakpai. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ muji he ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers let a portion of their land rest for a season instead of farming all of it at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi haa amɛshikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi jɔɔ amɛhe be kome lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu okwaayeli fɛɛ shikome lɛ

english: Soil gets exhausted when crops are grown on it without end. Letting land rest gives wild plants and natural soil microbes time to rebuild natural fertility so the soil produces better yields when you plant on it again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi beni ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ ni naagbee bɛ he lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa koo mli tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛsaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii lɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛ́ odu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why must I wash my knapsack sprayer with clean water immediately after spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical residues dry up and harden inside the nozzle and tank, causing blockages and damaging the rubber seals. Washing it right after use ensures the sprayer lasts long and works properly during the next planting season.
ga: Tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ewaa yɛ nozzle lɛ kɛ tanki lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɔne lɛ tsiɔ ehe ni efiteɔ rɔba ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha o-sprayer lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do farming groups share big tools like motorized tillers or water pumps between neighboring communities instead of keeping them in one village forever?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli kui jaa nibii wuji tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu pɔmpii yɛ akutsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ehi akrowa kome mli kɛya naanɔ

english: Expensive machines stay in good working condition when they are used regularly and maintained properly by trained groups. Sharing equipment across neighboring villages ensures the tools are actively used where needed without sitting unused in a shed.
ga: Tsɔnei ni jara wa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kuu ko ni atsɔse amɛ kɛtsu nii daa ni amɛkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli ni ajaa lɛ haa anáa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Abaakɛtsu nii be mli ni ehe miihia ni ataaaa tsũ lɛ mli ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly after I burn the bush to clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ beni mishã jwɛi koni mikɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and micro-organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops, leaving the ground dry, weak, and unable to hold water for healthy root growth.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is there a safe way to clear my land for planting without burning the bushes?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni ashãaa jwɛi?

english: Yes, you can slash the weeds and spread them across your field as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, slows down water loss, and decays into natural plant food for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ogbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔji amli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does uncontrolled bush burning in my community affect my farm even if my own field did not catch fire?
ga: Te koo ni ashãa yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ, kɛji akɛ la etswaaa miŋmɔji lɛ po?

english: Widespread fire strips the land of plant cover across large areas, which heats up the air, destroys natural soil moisture, and reduces the local humidity your crops rely on to stay green.
ga: La lɛ gbɛ eshwa tsei agbo ko nɔ, ni eha he ko agbo ko nɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ Efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ nɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does the soil on my farmland dry out so quickly now even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Without forest trees to block direct sunlight and hold moisture in the ground, the hot sun evaporates rainwater from bare soil long before your crop roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛji koo mli tsei bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee la be kakadaŋŋ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why are my crops wilting faster during short dry spells than they used to in past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Fe bei fɛɛ ni eho yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli.

english: The overall loss of forest trees in the area has lowered underground water levels and reduced natural humidity, leaving your plants with no moisture reserve when the rains pause.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni elaaje yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ eha shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ eba shi, ni adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ hu eba shi. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: How does losing trees in our community cause changes in when the rains fall on my crops?
ga: Te tsei ni laajeɔ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Trees release moisture into the atmosphere through their leaves to help form local rain clouds, so removing forest cover disrupts regular rainfall patterns that your crops depend on.
ga: Tsei jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua ni ekɛ nugbɔ atatui ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ afee. No hewɔ lɛ, koo mli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni oŋmɔshi nibii damɔ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do big trees near my farmland help my crops survive hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Trees act as natural shields that lower ground temperature, block scorching sun rays, and create a cooler climate around your crops so they do not heat-stress.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi. Tsi hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni otsi ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: What can I do on my farm to protect my crops from heavy winds and bad weather?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ahe?

english: Planting rows of trees along the borders of your farm creates natural windbreaks that prevent strong storms from snapping your crop stems and blowing away healthy topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ahum ni naa wa naa lɛ naa koni ekafo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsei lɛ amli ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afɔ.

english: Will keeping shade trees on my farm steal food and water away from my crops?
ga: Ani shading ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: If spaced correctly, deep-rooted trees bring underground nutrients and water up to the surface layer where your shallow-rooted food crops can easily reach them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ lɛ ja Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii kɛ nu baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni niyenii tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he mlɛo lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crop fields from accidental bushfires coming from nearby lands?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ koo mli la ni jɛɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ he yɛ oshara mli?

english: You can clear wide strips of land around your farm boundaries or plant green, fire-resistant barriers like cassava or fresh grass to stop advancing flames from reaching your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie hei wuji. Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe Aloo dumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni la nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Enɛ baatsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa onibii amli.

english: How can I tell the difference between a plantain plant and a banana plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ plantains kɛ banana tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Plantain plants are generally taller with thicker stems and produce larger, starchier fruits that are usually cooked before eating. Banana plants are usually shorter, produce sweeter fruits, and can be eaten raw when ripe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ starch ni bei pii lɛ ahoɔ dani ayeɔ. Bei pii lɛ, banana tsei lɛ feɔ kuku. Yibii lɛ ŋɔɔ fe no. ni abaanyɛ aye lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji ahoo

english: What are the common local plantain varieties I can grow in Ghana, and how are they different?
ga: Mɛni ji maŋ lɛ mli plantain henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ ni manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ amɛsoro amɛhe?

english: The main varieties include Apentu, Apem, and Yeretia. Apentu produces large, thick fingers but fewer per bunch; Apem produces many smaller fingers on a big bunch; and Yeretia produces medium-sized fingers that mature relatively quickly.
ga: Apentu, Apem kɛ Yeretia ji henɔi titrii. Apentu woɔ niji agboi ni mli tse shi fioo pɛ yɛ kuu kome mli. Apem jieɔ niji bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ. Ni yerethia lɛ woɔ nanetsitsii ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo ni daa oya.

english: When is the right time of the year for me to plant plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: The best time to plant plantains is at the start of the major rainy season, usually around April to May in Ghana, so the young plants get plenty of water to establish strong roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛyashi May mli yɛ Ghana. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baaná nu babaoo koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: How long does it take from the day I plant plantain until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ plantain kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa eyibii lɛ?

english: It generally takes between 12 to 15 months from planting a fresh plantain sucker to harvesting a fully matured bunch of plantains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa plantain tsei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why does my young plantain plant take such a long time to start growing fast after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani midumɔwui bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have a difficult early growth stage because the sucker first spends several months building a strong underground root system before it starts shooting out thick leaves rapidly above ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ dalɛ be ni wa yɛ shishijee mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baahe nyɔji babaoo dani amɛto shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi. dani ebɔi baai ni mli tse ni jeɔ kpo oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jiemɔ

english: What does a healthy young plantain plant look like when it is growing well?
ga: Te plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ?

english: A healthy plantain plant has thick, deep-green leaves, a strong upright stem, and new leaves unrolling steadily from the middle without yellowing or leaf curling.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni mli tse, eŋɔli diŋŋ. Tso lɛ damɔ shi ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Ni baai heei baaje kpo be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛfeee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does it take so long for my plantain plant to start bearing fruit after it grows tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain plant must produce around 30 to 40 large leaves to store enough food energy before it can trigger flowering and support a heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ plantains lɛ awo baai agboi 30 kɛyashi 40 koni amɛkɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii.

english: How can I tell that my plantain plant is about to bring out a fruit bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain lɛ miibawo yibii?

english: You will notice the top leaves becoming shorter and growing closer together in a cluster, followed by a large reddish-purple flower bud emerging from the very center of the crown.
ga: Obaayɔse akɛ afee ŋwɛi baai lɛ kuku ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kui amli. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji magenta ŋmeii wuji ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ akɔɔble lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: What can I do to help my plantain grow faster during its slow early stage?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni eye ebua mi plantains lɛ ni amɛdara oya yɛ be mli ni mijeɔ shishi blɛoo lɛ?

english: You can clear weeds around the base, apply decomposed manure or compost around the plant, and ensure the soil remains moist during dry spells to support early root development.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo afata he, ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara mra.

english: How do I know that a bunch of plantain on my farm is mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: The plantain fingers will lose their sharp angular edges and become plump and rounded, and the dark flower tips at the ends of the fingers will easily dry up and break off.
ga: Ring finger lɛ laajeɔ e-angular edge ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni yɔɔ niji ahe lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ egbi ni efoɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown in the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia to shield them, intense heat dehydrates the plant and scorches the tender foliage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei amli nu sɛɛ foɔ ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during windstorms even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by microscopic soil pests called nematodes or banana root weevils. When pests weaken the roots under the ground, the heavy plant loses its anchor and easily tips over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi ŋmeii baanyɛ afite. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Tsei ni tsii lɛ laajeɔ amɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ oya ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why does my maize grow plenty of tall green leaves but end up with empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ebatsɔ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs a lot of water right when it produces silks and tassels. If dry spells happen during this flowering stage, pollen grains dry out before fertilizing the cob, resulting in missing or underdeveloped kernels.
ga: Abɛi biɔ nu babaoo kɛ́ afee siliki kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Pollen lɛ gbiɔ dani ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ loo amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed carries only a tiny package of stored energy to start growing. If planted too deep, the shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight, causing it to die underground.
ga: Hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ Tsoi lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe waa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help the maize grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown together, cowpeas release this nitrogen into the soil, feeding the maize crop like a natural fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen gas mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu Cowpeas yɛ he kome lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava bushes curling up and turning yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies. The flies feed on the plant sap and infect it with a virus that stunts root growth and lowers overall yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ tsei amli nu ni hela ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ daalɛ kpaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start shooting out sprouts even when kept in a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go dormant after harvest, but after a few months, internal biological signals trigger them to wake up and sprout as they prepare for the next rain and planting season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yaa wɔɔhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ amli okadii woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ be mli ni amɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when day or night temperatures get too hot, or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. The plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for survival instead of producing fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa shwane loo gbɛkɛ. aloo beni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ trukaa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die within days after heavy rainwater sits around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ebɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. Stagnant water suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases like root rot, causing the plant to suddenly collapse.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa.

english: Why do my crops grow lush green leaves but produce very little fruit when I use too much nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: High amounts of nitrogen signal the plant to focus almost entirely on vegetative growth like stems and leaves. This delays the plant's shift into flowering and fruiting, reducing your harvest.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ, tamɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai, ni no haa tso lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do improved seed varieties from agricultural researchers grow so much faster and bigger than my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi lɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni amɛfee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Scientific research breeds seeds specifically for high vigor and fast growth. These improved varieties absorb water and soil nutrients much more efficiently, allowing the plant to develop quickly and achieve larger sizes in a shorter period.
ga: Jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ fɔɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ oya. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei daraa oya ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do scientists develop fast-growing crops for farmers to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jeŋ nilelɔi miifee tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni okwaafoi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fast-growing crops mature early, which helps farmers harvest before harsh dry seasons begin or before major pest outbreaks occur. They also produce food faster to help meet family and community nutritional needs.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa baa loo dani tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa. Amɛfeɔ niyenii hu oya koni eye ebua ni atsu niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii ni wekui kɛ akutsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do my crops need chemical fertilizers if the soil already has natural nutrients?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he hiaa mi tsei lɛ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii momo?

english: Soil loses its strength over time through continuous farming. Chemical fertilizers give crops a concentrated boost of essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, helping them grow rapidly and produce larger yields than worn-out soil can provide.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ.

english: Can using too much chemical fertilizer on my field actually harm my crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, over-applying fertilizers can 'burn' the roots of your crops, stunt their growth, or spoil the soil balance. Crops only require specific, recommended amounts of nutrients to grow healthily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ‘ashã’ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi, ni etsĩ dalɛ naa. aloo efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ja lɛ Tsei biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do nutrients added to the soil help my crops grow bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji?

english: Plants use soil nutrients as food to build leaves, stems, and fruits. Adequate nutrition gives the plant the energy it needs to grow strong foliage and feed larger, heavier fruits during the harvest season.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛ baa, ashishifãi, kɛ aduawai akwɛ̃. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛye aduawai wuji ni tsii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Does food grown with chemical fertilizers have good nutritional value for human consumption?
ga: Ani niyenii ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ duɔ lɛ hi kɛha adesai niyenii?

english: Yes, plants convert soil chemicals into natural vitamins, proteins, and carbohydrates. When fertilizers are applied correctly according to guidelines, the harvested food is nutritious and safe to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tsakeɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli vitamini, protein, kɛ carbohydrates. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ anaa Niyenii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Can natural plant extracts protect my crops from insect pests as effectively as store-bought chemicals?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsofai ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Natural solutions like neem leaf sprays contain natural bitter compounds that keep pests away safely. While they may work a bit slower than synthetic chemicals, natural practices protect your crops without harming beneficial soil organisms.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni mli edɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sɛɛ foɔ shweshweeshwe. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nii blɛoo fioo fe tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi moŋ. Shi adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni eyeee nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ awui.

english: Is it possible to combine natural soil treatments with chemical fertilizers to get a better harvest?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afata he koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, mixing natural compost with controlled amounts of chemical fertilizer improves soil structure while giving crops immediate nutrients. Natural matter holds moisture in the soil, helping the crops absorb the added fertilizer better.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ hu aná niyenii kpakpai. Adebɔɔ mli nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my maize stalks grow very tall quickly, does that automatically mean I will get a big harvest?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ dara oya waa Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not always. Rapid tall growth can mean the plant is stretching for sunlight or receiving too much leaf-building nutrient like nitrogen. Without balanced nutrients for ear development, a tall plant might still produce small cobs.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yaa hiɛ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikpa ehe koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ awo mli loo enine shɛɔ niyenii ni haa baai feɔ baa lɛ babaoo nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛji akɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha toi lɛ dalɛ bɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ awo ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow very fast at first but then stop growing before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpaa dalɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plants use up early nutrients primarily to grow stems and leaves. If the soil lacks specific flowering and fruiting nutrients as the crop matures, the overall growth stalls before fruits can develop.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii kpakpai tsuɔ nii mra titri kɛha tso lɛ yitso kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo, titri lɛ be mli ni tsei miida lɛ Dalɛ fɛɛ kpaa dani yibiiwoo baanyɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your crops are missing nutrients like nitrogen, or they are being attacked by pests or fungal diseases. Adding compost or the right fertilizer, and clearing weeds early, helps the plants stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua lɛ. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cassava plants to wilt even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cassava tsei lɛ miigbo? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Wilting during rainy periods usually points to root rot or bacterial infections inside the plant that block water flow. Removing infected plants immediately prevents the disease from spreading through the soil to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo loo hela ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni miitsi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread faster on my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in warm, damp environments. Rainwater splashes fungal spores from the soil onto lower leaves, and high humidity helps the disease grow and spread quickly across wet plant foliage.
ga: Fungi yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Ni hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa hela lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why is it important to space my crops properly when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso lɛ awo he ni sa kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Leaving proper space between plants ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. Good airflow between plants also keeps leaves dry, preventing fungal diseases from taking hold.
ga: Shi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ he yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating different crops breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can planting two different crops together help protect my farm from pests?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Yes, growing complementary crops together, such as legumes alongside cereals, confuses insect pests, attracts beneficial insects that eat farm pests, and improves overall soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ nibii ni akɛfataa he tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmaa masɛi. Ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afutu. Egbalaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛnamɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if the seed maize or stem cuttings I want to plant are healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy seeds look clean, full, and unblemished, while good stem cuttings come from strong parent plants with no dark spots or insect damage. Planting certified seeds ensures your crops start life disease-free.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse, amɛye emuu, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. yɛ be mli ni niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jɛɔ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. Ebɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aje wala shishi ni hela bɛ mli.

english: How do weeds cause my crops to get sick or produce poor yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hela loo amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from your crops, making them weak. Weakened plants cannot fight off sicknesses easily, and weeds can also harbor harmful insects that spread diseases to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ha egbɔjɔ Tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ awuu ashi helai mlɛo. Ni jwɛi baanyɛ ahi kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ agbala helai kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me when disease breaks out on my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ hela ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers visit farms to inspect damaged crops, identify specific pests or diseases, and teach you safe, practical methods to treat and protect your fields before you lose your harvest.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi yaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai pɔtɛɛ ni etsɔɔ bo gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe ni obu he dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot or get moldy so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains mold when they are stored while still wet or kept in dark rooms without airflow. Properly drying your harvested crops in the sun before storing them in clean, sealed containers prevents mold and spoilage.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto be mli ni edɔ loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi dani akɛwo tsɛnsii ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ fitemɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize seeds sprout well in some parts of my farm but fail completely in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Seeds need a warm, moist, and well-aerated soil environment to sprout. In areas where the soil is too hard, compacted, or waterlogged, the seeds suffocated and cannot breathe, while areas with loose, fertile soil retain just enough moisture for healthy germination.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the seed I receive from the cooperative is good quality before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni minine shɛ nɔ kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe nine lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani adu?

english: Good quality seeds are clean, whole, uniform in size, free from insect holes or mold, and certified by agricultural inspectors. You can also test them by placing a sample in water—seeds that sink are usually healthy and full, while light, damaged seeds will float.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni he tse, ni ji dumɔwui muu fɛɛ lɛ dalɛ yaa nɔ daa. Ebɛ ŋmeii bu loo ŋmeii. Okwaayeli he nilelɔi etsɔɔ akɛ Obaanyɛ oka lɛ okwɛ hu kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni okɛaawo nu mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyi obɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni efite fioo lɛ baaho.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival strategy to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and protects its underground roots until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni ebu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme midday heat, lack of regular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Too much nitrogen causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of keeping flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabua fɔfɔii anaa koni ewo yibii

english: What causes my maize stalks to fall over easily whenever a strong storm passes through?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ahum wulu ko tswa kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over (a condition called lodging) when roots are planted too shallowly, plants are spaced too closely together, or the soil lacks potassium. Strong roots and thick stems require proper planting depth and balanced soil nutrients to hold the plant firmly.
ga: ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy) kɛ́ adu shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. loo shikpɔŋ ni potassium bɛ mli Shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse biɔ dumɔ ni mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cereal crops grow taller and greener after I plant cowpeas or beans on the land the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji beni midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land with free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: How do I know when my soil is exhausted and needs a rest or extra manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni maná hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli?

english: Exhausted soil becomes hard, light in color, washes away easily during rains, and produces weak, pale yellow crops even when there is enough rain. When you notice crops growing slowly despite good rainfall, the soil lacks key nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ oya. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Kɛji ona tsei ni miida blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves in the morning even though I do not see insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli leebi be mli ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm feed inside the tender central leaf whorl during the cooler night hours or early morning and hide deep within the plant during the hot afternoon sun to protect themselves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ amli. ni amɛtee amɛtee tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are my tomato roots swelling up into ugly lumps instead of growing straight down into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lumpy tomato roots are caused by microscopic soil worms called root-knot nematodes. These tiny pests enter the root tissue and block the plant from taking up water and nutrients, causing stunted growth above ground.
ga: Kpluka bibioo ko ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ root-knot nematode lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishifãi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in high humidity, shade, and excessive wetness. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores onto low pods, and dense tree branches trap the moisture that allows the disease to grow.
ga: Hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo, hulutsoo be, kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores nɔ yɛ pods ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba lɛ.

english: Is it better for my soil to clear my land using a machine tractor or by hand with a cutlass?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ trakta loo nine ni akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Clearing by hand with a cutlass leaves the topsoil rich and undisturbed, but takes much more time and labor. Using a heavy tractor clears the land very quickly, but it can pack the soil down tight like a rock, making it hard for crop roots to breathe and spread.
ga: Nine ni akɛ ŋmei tsuɔ he nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa lɛ naa. Shi eheɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo fe nakai. Trakta agbo ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baajie jɛmɛ oya. Shi ebaanyɛ ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ tɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is flooded with too much standing water, which prevents the roots from drinking up soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and developing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. Tiny white insects called whiteflies suck juice from sick plants and spread the disease to healthy cassava plants as they fly around your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ŋmei bibii yɛŋ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whiteflies lɛ nuɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli beni amɛfoɔ kɛbɔleɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, a lack of water, or when tiny beneficial insects haven't visited to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Amɛsaraaa koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants start rotting when the fruits get heavy and touch the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ tsii ni eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tomato fruits rot easily when they lie on wet soil because damp dirt carries rotting fungi. Tying the branches to wooden sticks keeps the fruits off the ground, dry, and safe.
ga: Tomato yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ejaakɛ muji ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛgbi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why must I wait for the soil to be wet before puting fertilizer near my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for roots to drink it. If you put fertilizer in dry soil under strong heat, it will burn the roots or turn into gas and blow away in the wind.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛtsɔ gas ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa amɛ kɛya.

english: Why do my yams turn out small and thin when I build my mounds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo waa beni mikɛtoɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When mounds are too close, the yam leaves block sunlight from each other, and the underground tubers fight for the same water and soil food, leaving no energy to grow big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋtayaa lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Sweet potatoes lɛ baaha amɛhe afee shade kɛjɛ hulu la he. Ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ hewalɛ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha eda.

english: Why do my cowpea bean plants produce mostly big green leaves but very few bean pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Too much rain causes the plant to spend all its energy making tall branches and lush leaves instead of focusing on producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei niji kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ a juɛmi kɛ ma fɔfɔi kɛ ngmahi nɛ a maa pee ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after clearing the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild survival experts. Their seeds stay hidden in the soil for years and are built to wake up and grow instantly as soon as they get a little sunlight and rain.
ga: Jwɛi ji mɛi ni le bɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ koo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo. ni abɔ lɛ koni ete shi ni eda kɛji enine shɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ fioo nɔ pɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture when it is hot and dry. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the sun and wind, the plant slows down water loss until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ni abaajie lɛ shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: What makes my cabbage plants wilt in the afternoon but look fresh and healthy again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni haa cabbage lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli shi efeɔ ehee ni eyɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the ground, causing temporary wilting. Overnight, as temperatures drop, the roots catch up and replenish the water, making the plant stand upright again.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baate shi ni nu baayi mli obɔ. Ha tso lɛ adamɔ shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ

english: Why does my cassava crop start dropping its bottom leaves when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during dry spells to protect itself. Dropping leaves reduces the amount of water the plant needs to stay alive, allowing it to save moisture and keep energy in its underground roots until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu ehe he. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my tomato crops are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu babaoo?

english: If tomatoes lack water, their leaves wilt, turn yellow at the tips, and flowers drop off. If they get too much water, the leaves may turn yellow and feel soft, roots can rot from lack of air in the soil, and the fruit can split open.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tomato mli lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi ni amɛyitsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni onu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo. Shishifãi baanyɛ agbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. ni aduawai lɛ baanyɛ atswa.

english: Is it better for my crop health if I pour water directly on the soil near the stem or sprinkle it over the leaves?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ kɛji mikɛ nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Pouring water on the soil near the root zone is much better because roots absorb the water. Wetting the leaves unnecessarily can encourage fungal diseases and causes water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots.
