ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni oooha nu lɛ hi kwraa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ nu ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ ni eha nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow even when I bucket-water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering too heavily every day can drown the plant roots by pushing out the oxygen in the soil. Without air, roots cannot breathe or take up nutrients properly, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine daa gbi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhe niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How does digging a simple water hole near my farm help my vegetables grow better during the dry season?
ga: Nubu ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsaa Te ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A water hole provides a reliable supply of water when the rains stop. Regular watering prevents crop growth from stalling, stops flowers from falling off, and keeps vegetables growing healthy despite heat stress.
ga: Nubui ji nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃. Kpaa fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my okro plants stop producing new flowers when the weather becomes very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei feemɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil put stress on the okro plant, forcing it to save its remaining energy just to survive rather than spending energy on producing new flowers and pods. Regular watering reduces this stress so flowering can resume.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa odum tso lɛ nɔ. ni nyɛɔ enɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ato koni ehi shi kɛkɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ tso ehehi. Nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa haomɔ baa shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi.

english: How does spreading dry grass or dry leaves around my crop stems help keep moisture in the soil?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts as a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from heating the soil. This slows down water evaporation, keeps the root zone cool, and helps the soil stay moist longer between waterings.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli adɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ teŋ

english: Why do my watermelon fruits crack open right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons usually split open when they receive a sudden large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs the water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the rind to burst.
ga: Watermelon lɛ fɔɔ tswamɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. gbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn quickly under direct sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to draw extra water. Planting fast-growing companion crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu babaoo. Hefatalɔi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant restore its green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water sits around the roots for too long, cutting off oxygen and allowing underground fungi to multiply. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves wither and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly during dry winds. Placing a layer of dried grass or leaves around the base of the plant (mulching) traps moisture in the soil and shields the roots from extreme heat.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaabu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting during cooler windows helps the flowers set into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ samflɛ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot strips away specific nutrients and allows maize-eating pests to build up in the soil. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas replenishes soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for food production. Staking also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni dalɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from young leaves. Using organic sprays like neem leaf extract early on helps clear these insects before they damage the plant permanently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ kwraa.

english: Why should I mix dried animal manure into my soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture longer and slowly releasing essential nutrients that feed your crops over a long period.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ fiofio. yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Why do my young maize stalks have holes in the leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the growing center of the plant. Checking your field early and applying ash or recommended biological treatments directly into the plant whorls controls the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni naa niyenii yɛ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ sũ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: The first rain after a dry spell is often followed by a hot dry period before the main rainy season truly begins. If you sow too early, seeds will sprout but then dry up and die under the hot sun due to a lack of continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be ko ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ toi bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together in the same spot, their roots fight each other underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunshine from one another. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread and grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa ŋmeii wuji ni wa.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight or dry winds. They require fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or shade trees to act as natural umbrellas until their branches grow strong enough to endure full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look dead in the hot afternoon but stand upright again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ete shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: During peak heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can drink it from the dirt, so the plant droops to protect itself from losing more water. Once the air cools down at night, roots catch up and refill the stem and leaves with water.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gboɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baafata tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people say that growing groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have helpful tiny nodules on their roots that capture invisible food (nitrogen) from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that extra food stays in the dirt to feed whatever crop you plant next, such as maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ shishifãi ni mɔɔ niyenii ni anaaa (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni okpaa lɛ Nakai niyenii kroko lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni adu lɛ niyenii. nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow down the center while the edges stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishigbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing inside the leaves is a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its rich green color and build strong leaves.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ eŋmɔŋ ni mli wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Lifting yam vines onto wooden stakes lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and fresh air, while keeping them away from damp soil diseases. Sunlight powers the leaves to send energy down to make the underground tubers grow bigger.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ aba mli babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje shi koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Extreme heat and water stress make the plant shed its flowers to save energy to keep the main vine alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni wain tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are there ragged holes and sticky waste inside the center whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and sticky dark droppings mean Fall Armyworm caterpillars have crawled into the central funnel of the plant to feed on fresh young leaves. Checking the farm early allows you to remove them before they destroy the growing tip of the corn.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmɔtɔi lɛ etsɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni darako lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ yitsei lɛ.

english: How do I know my cassava roots are ready to harvest if I cannot see them under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a woodier main stem. To be completely sure, carefully scrape away dirt from one mature plant to check if the root tubers are long, thick, and firm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbɔ kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ eshwɛ, ni ji tso babaoo. to be sure Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie muji ni yɔɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ koni ona shishifãi ni kɛlɛ, ni mli wa, ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a sickness or just need water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ?

english: Plants that lack water usually perk up in the cool early morning or evening after watering, whereas plants suffering from a disease remain wilted, develop leaf spots, or show unusual color changes regardless of water.
ga: Tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ, amɛfeɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ, loo amɛjieɔ amɛhe su tsakemɔi ni ejaaa kpo ekɔɔɔ he eko nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right chemical or medicine when my crops get sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofa loo tsofa ni sa kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Different plant sicknesses require specific treatments; for example, fungicides only cure fungal spots, while insecticides kill bugs. You should show a freshly damaged leaf to an extension officer to identify the exact cause before spending money on chemicals.
ga: Tsoi ahe helai babaoo biɔ tsamɔ krɛdɛɛ ko, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ baatsa hei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi baanyɛ agbe kooloi. Esa akɛ ajie baai heei ni efite lɛ atsɔɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni amɛna nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa dani amɛfite shika yɛ tsofai ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives leaves their dark green color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by inconsistent watering while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender stems and shallow roots that cannot pull water fast enough to replace what the strong sun evaporates from their leaves, causing them to dry out and die.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛye nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ efo kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and split during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbalaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves lose water quickly in dry winds due to their large size; the plant naturally lets its outer leaves dry up to save water for its main stem and root system.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli yɛ amɛdalɛ hewɔ. Tsei haa kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni akɛto nu he kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds reduce my yield even when my crops are bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ da fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that secretly steal fertilizer, water, and soil nutrients underground before your main crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli yɛ teemɔŋ dani tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How does planting cassava very close to my other crops affect how they grow?
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe Te minɔ lɛ saa dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava develops dense roots and wide leaf branches that block sunlight and rob neighboring smaller crops of moisture and soil nutrients.
ga: Cassava woɔ shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it; applying it to dry soil can burn and damage the plant roots instead of helping them grow.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and allows pests to build up in the soil. Alternating your maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmãa ekoŋŋ ni efo ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs manure or organic soil booster?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: If your crops grow slowly, stems remain thin, and leaves look pale green or yellow instead of deep green, your soil lacks nutrients. Adding compost or well-rotted animal manure improves soil structure and feeds your crops naturally.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo. ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts between my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside other crops, groundnuts act as natural fertilizer, feeding the surrounding plants and improving future crop yields.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Peanuts baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ niyenii ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ wɔsɛɛ

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the plant. Checking your crops early and applying recommended biological treatments or simple neem leaf extract can stop them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting, curling, and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellowing cassava leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. You can protect your farm by planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings.
ga: Kasava baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kasava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmei ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves under severe heat and dry conditions to keep from losing too much water. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains and placing dry grass mulch around root zones protects young cocoa trees from intense sun damage.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ shishi koni nu babaoo akaje mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shishifã lɛ buɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stand, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Leaving only one strong follower shoot ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ ajie sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni he wa lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee kuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten spots on the bottom end before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rotten spots on the bottom of tomatoes are known as blossom-end rot. This happens when the soil lacks calcium or when water supply is irregular, preventing the plant from distributing nutrients evenly to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aja niyenii mli hewalɛ eha aduawai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to train my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall wooden stakes so their leaves can spread out and absorb maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to grow large, healthy tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛhe hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the initial rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the ground has been thoroughly soaked by two or three steady rains before planting. Sowing after the very first light rain risks having seeds dry up if a short dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu nii. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba.

english: Where can I get good quality seeds that are guaranteed to give me a big harvest in my district?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ akɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can visit your District Agriculture Office, where extension officers provide certified, high-yielding seed varieties designed to perform well in your local climate and soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli. Afee amɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy seeds from the agriculture office instead of just planting seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds provided by the agriculture office are certified improved varieties bred for high yield, disease resistance, and uniform growth, whereas saved seeds often lose vigor and produce significantly smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛdaraa daa. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Will the seeds provided by the agriculture officer really produce more crops than local seeds?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛhaa lɛ baawo yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, certified seeds from agricultural offices are scientifically selected and tested to ensure high germination rates and maximum yield potential when given proper care.
ga: Hɛɛ, ahala dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does it mean when agricultural officers say a crop can produce 10 to 13 tons per hectare?
ga: Beni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii tɔn 10 kɛyashi 13 yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ. Mɛni etsɔɔ?

english: It means that on a piece of land measuring one hectare (about 2.5 acres), properly grown plants using improved seeds can yield a total harvest weight between 10,000 and 13,000 kilograms.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji hectare 1 (aaafee acre 2.5) nɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ du jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 10,000 kɛyashi 13,000.

english: How much harvest should I realistically expect if I use improved crop varieties on my farm?
ga: Nikpamɔ enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: With improved seed varieties and recommended farming practices, crops can achieve high target yields, often reaching between 10 and 13 tons per hectare depending on the specific crop.
ga: kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ shɛɔ tɔn 10 kɛyashi 13 yɛ hectare kome mli. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How big is a hectare of land, and why is it important to know my farm size?
ga: Te hectare kome da ha tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni male bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ da ha lɛ?

english: A hectare is a land measurement equal to 100 meters by 100 meters (roughly 2.5 acres). Knowing your farm size helps you correctly calculate how much seed, fertilizer, and labor you need to reach expected harvest yields.
ga: Hectare ji shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji mitai 100 x mitai 100 (aaafee acre 2.5). Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔ ni he baahia koni aná yibiiwoo ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm harvest is performing well compared to national standards?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ shishitoo mlai ahe?

english: You can measure your farm's performance by comparing your total harvest weight per hectare against target yield benchmarks provided by extension officers, such as 10 to 13 tons per hectare for high-yielding varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa lɛ he kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okpa yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ ni okɛtoɔ yibiiwoo he okadii ni shweremɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ eto lɛ he, tamɔ tɔn 10 kɛyashi 13 yɛ hectare kome mli kɛha yibiiwoo srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: How can the District Agriculture Office help me improve my crop production as a farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni mahã miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ akɛ okwaafonyo?

english: The District Agriculture Office supports farmers by supplying improved seed varieties and providing expert advice on land preparation, proper planting methods, pest management, and harvest targets.
ga: Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ekɛhaa amɛ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛha ŋaawoi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he nilelɔi adɛŋ Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ otii.

english: Why do some farmers get small harvests while others get huge harvests from the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi náa yibii fioo ko pɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi Naa nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Differences in yield usually depend on seed quality and farm practices; farmers using certified seeds from official agricultural offices and following proper planting guidelines harvest far more produce per hectare.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibii sɔrɔtoi ni anáa lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kpakpa kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi anɔ. Okwaafoi ni kɛ dumɔwui ni Official Agriculture Office lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛnyiɛɔ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpa yibii babaoo yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: What steps do I need to follow after getting seeds from the agriculture office to achieve high yields?
ga: Beni minine shɛ dumɔwui anɔ kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: To achieve maximum harvest output, you must follow the extension officer's instructions on proper land preparation, correct spacing, timely weed and pest control, and proper harvesting techniques.
ga: Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ kpamɔ yibii babaoo nɔ Esa akɛ onyiɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔ lɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi asɛɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa. jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ he jɛkɛmɔ ni ja yɛ be ni sa mli; kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ gbɛ̀i ni sa

english: What makes high-yielding seed varieties like Ghana Sumatra better than the wild seeds I pick from the bush?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ Sumatran ghana lɛ hi fe koo mli dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High-yielding seed varieties are specially bred by agricultural researchers to grow faster, produce larger and higher-quality yields, stay shorter for easier harvesting, and withstand local diseases far better than wild or unselected seeds.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi ekwɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Feemɔ babaoo ni oná su ni nɔ kwɔ. Ewala be kuku kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa fe helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ fe koo mli dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni ahalaaa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave wide spaces between my seedlings instead of planting as many as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ oshi he ko ni da yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ?

english: Crops require adequate sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce heavy yields. If planted too close together, they fight for these resources and grow tall and thin with very few fruits.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛwo aduawai babaoo. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ Ebaatswa akaŋ yɛ nibii nɛɛ ahe ni ebaada ni ekwɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young crop turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or poor water drainage around the roots. Applying the proper fertilizer and ensuring excess water drains away will help restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli ni akwɛ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I grow cassava or maize between my young tree crops during their first year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term food crops provides quick food and income while your main trees mature. However, keep companion crops at a safe distance from tree stems so they do not block sunlight or steal nutrients from the seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niyenii ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli tsei baadu lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni otso titri lɛ daa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ha tsei ni fata he lɛ ahi he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji koni akatsi hulu la lɛ naa loo akaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away old or dry leaves from my tree crops instead of letting them fall off on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbee shi lɛ?

english: Removing dead or diseased fronds prevents fungal diseases and pests from hiding in the foliage. It also improves air circulation and lets sunlight directly reach the developing flowers and fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the very first flowers on my young trees drop off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ miikwɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Young plants often produce immature or male flowers first as they build up the strength to produce fruit. This is normal plant behavior, and as the plant matures, it will successfully retain and develop full fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii woɔ fɔfɔi bibii loo hii klɛŋklɛŋ beni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Enɛ ji tsei asubaŋ ni yaa nɔ daa. ni kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ aduawai akuu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha eya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops stop producing new fruit during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry air and low soil moisture force plants to conserve water and energy. Their growth naturally slows down, but proper mulching and watering can help keep them healthy until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Dalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do tall weeds growing near the base of my crop stem hurt my harvest later on?
ga: Te jwɛi kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water directly from crop roots. They also hold excess moisture against the plant stem, which creates a habitat for harmful insects and fungal rot.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Emɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ naa shihilɛhe.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and prepare my land before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he gbɛjianɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Preparing your field before the rains allow seedlings to be planted at the very start of the rainy season. This gives root systems maximum time to grow deep and strong before the next dry period.
ga: He ni asaa he lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be babaoo ni amɛkɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa dani hɔmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: How do I tell if my crops are suffering from a disease or just lacking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii loo nu efo mli?

english: Lack of water causes the whole plant to wilt during hot afternoons and revive slightly at night. A disease usually creates specific spots, rot, mold, or deformed leaves and fruits that do not change regardless of the time of day.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe waaa fioo gbɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo baai kɛ aduawai ni efite ni tsakeee ekɔɔɔ he eko gbi lɛ mli be.

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male pawpaw trees only produce pollen to fertilize female trees, so their flowers naturally drop off without ever turning into fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Pawpaw tsei hii lɛ woɔ pollen pɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei yei lɛ feɔ ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsakeee amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the first flowers on my watermelon vines fall off without forming any small melons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee melon bibii lɛ?

english: Watermelon vines produce separate male and female flowers on the same plant. The first flowers to appear are usually male flowers meant to attract bees, so they naturally fall off after releasing pollen.
ga: Watermelon wain tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi klɛŋklɛŋ ni jeɔ kpo lɛ ji fɔfɔi hii ni gbalaa ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie pollen lɛ, ebaagbee shi yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Should I cut down the non-bearing trees in my farm that only produce pollen, or do they serve a purpose?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei ni wooo yibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni woɔ yibii pɛ lɛ? Aloo ani yiŋtoo ko yɛ nakai tsei lɛ ahe?

english: You should leave a small number of male trees on your farm because female trees require their pollen to set fruit. Removing all male trees can cause female trees to fail to produce crop yields.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi tsei hii fioo komɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei yei ahe miihia pollen koni amɛwo yibii. Tsei hii fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei yei anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Can I tell whether a nursery seedling will be male or female just by looking at the seed or young leaves?
ga: Kwɛmɔ dumɔwui loo baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ, ani amɛji hii loo yei?

english: For most crops like pawpaw or nutmeg, you cannot determine the sex of the plant by looking at young leaves or seeds. The gender usually only becomes visible once the plant produces its first set of flowers.
ga: Kɛha tsei babaoo, tamɔ paw paw loo nutmeg Onyɛŋ otsɔɔ bɔ ni tso ko ji nuu loo yoo kɛtsɔ ebaai bibii loo edumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, anaa bɔlɛnamɔ pɛ kɛji tso lɛ wo eklɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why does my maize plant have tassels at the top and silk on the side instead of just one flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ siliki yɛ esɛɛ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize carries both male and female flower parts on the same plant. The tassel at the top drops male pollen, while the silk on the cob catches that pollen to form individual grains of corn.
ga: Abɛi ji fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei ahe fãi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ. Tasel ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ stamens. yɛ be mli ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ ŋmei ŋmeii aŋkroaŋkroi.

english: Flowers drop when they are not pollinated by insects, or when the plant experiences stress from high heat or dry soil, causing it to shed flowers it cannot feed.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aye.

english: My cassava plants have started producing small flowers on top, does this mean the tubers are ready for harvest?
ga: Mi-cassava tso lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi bibii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Flowering is simply a natural part of cassava growth and does not indicate tuber maturity. You should determine harvest time based on the crop's age in months and stem thickness rather than flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔii ni shwereɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli fã kome pɛ ni haa ŋmei daa. ni etsɔɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa amɛhaa. Esa akɛ okwɛ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye yɛ nyɔji amli kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔ ha lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from a very sweet pawpaw fruit, will all the new trees produce sweet fruit too?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ paw paw yibii ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Ani tsei heei fɛɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ hu?

english: Not necessarily. Seeds inside a single fruit carry mixed traits from parent plants, so seedlings will vary—some may be male, some female, and some may yield fruit with different sweetness levels.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso yibii kome mli lɛ ji fɔlɔ tso lɛ fã ko. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ srɔtoi. Ekolɛ kooloi srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi ji hii. some bitches Ni henɔi komɛi baanyɛ awo aduawai ni ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli srɔtoi.

english: Why do extension officers advise us not to save and replant seeds from hybrid crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkabua dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ anaa ni wɔdu lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong yields in the first generation, but seeds saved from that harvest break down in the next season, resulting in uneven growth, mixed traits, and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baafite yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, sui ni efutu, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: How can I tell if an oil palm fruit bunch is ripe without cutting into the bunch to check?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei tso yibii ko ekwɛ̃ ni ofolɔɔɔ mli bibii koni okwɛ mli?

english: You do not need to cut open the bunch to check maturity. Look at the base of the tree—when 2 to 5 loose orange palm fruits naturally drop to the ground, the entire bunch is ripe for harvest.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofolɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko koni okwɛ kɛji eshɛ. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Kɛji akɛ 2 kɛyashi 5 ni ji orange dates lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, no lɛ, ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baakwɛ koni akpa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key food plant roots need. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of topsoil, so adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei shishifãi Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmei fata The base lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when the bright sun comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong direct sunlight because their root systems cannot suck up water fast enough. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides living shade and cool air to protect the cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ abu kookoo lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are small worms creating ragged holes right in the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii feɔ bu ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive caterpillars that hide in the growing center of the corn plant. Dropping a pinch of clean dry ash mixed with sand or an approved organic spray into the funnel smothers the pests and stops them from eating the heart of your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni mli tse ni egbi ni akɛ ŋã loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ fioo ko shwie tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsui lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them in heavy clay soil. Building high soil mounds or ridges before planting gives excess rainwater a channel to drain away, keeping the roots surrounded by moist air rather than stagnant water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi lɛ, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee dani aduɔ nii lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe nu ni damɔ shi.

english: Why do farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots collect free nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When these plants grow beside or before maize, they enrich the soil with natural fertilizer, saving you money while keeping your corn healthy.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ buaa nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei nɛɛ dara yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo dani ŋmãa aba lɛ Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa okɛ shika baa shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa o-corn lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp around the roots and mulching with dry grass keeps the roots cool, helping the flowers stay on the plant long enough to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Shishifã lɛ he lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo nɔ koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut long bamboo stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture energy, which travels down to swell the tuber underground; without stakes, the vines lie on damp ground, rot easily, and produce tiny tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa tuber lɛ shwieɔ shi. Wein tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, egboɔ oya ni ewoɔ bulbs bibii. ni tso bɛ he

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaf undersides and spreading leaf-curl viruses. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or boiled neem seed extract kills these pests and allows healthy new leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem dumɔwui ni ahoo lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai heei ni mli wa lɛ shwereɔ

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over in strong wind just when the fruits are growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots that cannot anchor the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch against strong winds. Proping up the main stem with a sturdy wooden Y-stake placed under the fruit stalk supports the weight and keeps the plant upright until full harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii waa lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y ni akɛwo tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashishi lɛ fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni tsii lɛ ni eye ebua ni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa tso lɛ yibii lɛ kwraa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing huge, loose leaves but no hard round head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai wuji shi yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo bɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages develop loose open leaves when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth or suffer in hot weather. Reducing nitrogen application once the plant has established foliage encourages it to start wrapping its inner leaves tightly into a firm head.
ga: Cabbage feɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni agbeleɔ kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ sɛɛ loo enaa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔtsemɔ beni tsei jeɔ baai shishi lɛ Enɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ebɔi emli baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bulb ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I see ants on my cocoa trees all the time, even when it is not the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ jeee kpamɔ be ji no moŋ?

english: Ants stay on cocoa trees year-round because they feed on the sweet substances produced by small insects like mealybugs. Because these insects live on the tree continually, ants will remain present throughout the year unless actively controlled.
ga: Akpɔlɔi hiɔ cacao tsei anɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ nibii ni ŋɔɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ feɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii hiɔ shi yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. ja akudɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Are the ants on my cocoa trees actually damaging the crop, or are they harmless?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo amɛyeee mɔ awui?

english: While ants may not eat the cocoa pod directly, they protect and spread mealybugs, which carry the deadly Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. Controlling ants helps protect your trees from severe disease and crop loss.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeŋ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ, shi etsĩɔ mealybugs lɛ naa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. ni ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ Kokoo Swollen Shoot Virus ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. Ant nɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do ants keep coming back to my cocoa farm even after I clear all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Weeding helps keep the farm clean, but ants often build their nests inside the cocoa tree bark, pod husks, or deep in the soil around the tree roots. They rely on the cocoa trees themselves for food, so weed control alone will not eliminate them.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii maa amɛtsui yɛ kookoo tsei ahe tsɔi amli, pod ŋmɔji amli, loo yɛ sũ ni mli kwɔ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛhaa niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ayeɔ lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ ajie amɛ kɛya.

english: How often should I walk through my cocoa farm to check for pest problems like ants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ?

english: You should walk through your farm regularly throughout the entire year. Constant monitoring allows you to spot ant activity early before they build large colonies and spread diseases across your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa onaa ŋmeii anifeemɔi mra. Dani amɛbaafee ŋmɔji wuji ni amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What signs should I look out for when checking my cocoa trees for ant infestation?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ beni mikwɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli koni mana kɛji ŋmeii emɔ amɛ?

english: Look for visible trails of ants climbing up the main trunk, soil or debris tubes built along branches, and small white cotton-like spots (mealybugs) on young pods and shoots that ants usually cluster around.
ga: Taomɔ gbɛi ni anaa ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kwɔɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ tsei niji amli lɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ (mealybugs) yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa lɛ anɔ.

english: Is pest control on a cocoa farm something I only need to do during the main harvest season?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ji nɔ ko ni ehe hiaa ni mafee yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli pɛ?

english: No, pest management must be a continuous, year-round activity. Pests like ants remain active in all seasons, so stopping control efforts after harvest allows pest populations to rebuild quickly.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ afee afi muu lɛ fɛɛ nitsumɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii, yaa nɔ amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akudɔ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Can having too many ants on my cocoa trees reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmeii babaoo ni miyɔɔ yɛ cacao tso nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, high ant populations help spread sap-sucking insects that weaken the tree, stunt young pod growth, and cause flower drops, which leads to fewer healthy pods at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii babaoo yeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Etsiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ adalɛ naa. ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Do young cocoa plants need to be checked for ants as much as older trees?
ga: Ani cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, young cocoa trees need constant checking because they are more fragile. Ants and the insects they transport can easily stunt the growth of a young tree or kill sensitive new shoots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli daa ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa kwraa. Aŋkroaŋkroi kɛ kooloi bibii ni amɛkɛyaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ afee mlɛo loo amɛfite ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What is the general advice from officers regarding ant management on cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋaawoo ni onukpai lɛ kɛhaa yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ he yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ he?

english: Agricultural guidelines recommend continuous, year-round monitoring and routine control of ant populations on your farm rather than waiting until the trees show signs of damage.
ga: Okwaayeli nifeemɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ daa ni akudɔ amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, mɛ nɛ tso ɔ nɛ tsɔɔ kaa e puɛ.

english: If I see ants on only a few trees in my farm, should I treat just those trees or check the whole farm?
ga: Kɛji mina ŋmeii yɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani Esa akɛ makwɛ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ loo makwɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: You should inspect the entire farm. Ants move easily between adjacent trees through canopy foliage and root systems, so a small ant presence in one spot often means they are spreading nearby.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Ants nyiɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ He kome lɛ bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiigbɛ amɛshwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions. Excessive rain and high humidity help the fungal spores splash from the soil onto the pods, causing them to rot if the farm is not well-weeded or pruned to let in sunlight and air.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ajieee jwɛi kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo afolɔɔɔ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of producing fruits when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat causes heat stress in tomatoes, which damages the pollen and prevents proper pollination. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ ni ehaaa pollen lɛ afee nɔ ni sa. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip and moving down the center of older maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant is moving stored nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer top growth because the soil lacks enough nutrients.
ga: Abɛi ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei miitsi nitrogen ni ato kɛmiijɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy stems above ground but small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, or when planted in overly shaded areas, cassava plants put all their energy into leafy top growth instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ Yɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants yield smaller bunches when many suckers are left growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many suckers around one mother plant compete for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the plant to send maximum nutrients into developing a large bunch.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ ni ebɔle he. Tso kome ni ji nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to direct sunlight for photosynthesis and prevents leaves from touching damp soil, which reduces fungal infections and leads to larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and helps heavy feeders like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees require plantain plants to be grown next to them in their early years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ plantain tsei ahe lɛ? Cocoa tsei yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade to cool the young cocoa seedlings and keep the surrounding soil moist until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli jɔɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea flowers falling off before any pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny insect pests called flower thrips feed on the delicate parts of cowpea blossoms early in the morning, causing the flowers to dry up and fall off before pod formation can begin.
ga: ŋmeii bibii Ale amɛ akɛ flower thrips, ni amɛyeɔ cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ leebi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to become weak and stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal applied fertilizer nutrients and groundwater faster than young crops can absorb them, effectively starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya fe bɔ ni tsei bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain waterlogs the soil, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu afua ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when humidity is high. Clearing weeds, pruning extra shade branches, and removing infected pods helps keep the air dry around the tree to stop the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. weeding Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo titri lɛ afolɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaye ebua kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tsei ni agbi koni helai akpa

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or mites sucking the sap from tender leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the crop early or planting pest-resistant varieties helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Aloo tsei srɔtoi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I see small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoots of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋma lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the growing point of the plant. They eat the young leaves before they unfold, which slows down growth unless treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ ahe hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ja atsa lɛ oya.

english: Plantain trees fall easily when invisible pests like microscopic root nematodes or stem borers eat away the underground roots. Without a strong root anchor, the tree cannot support the weight of its heavy leaves and fruit bunches.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shishifã ni mli wa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atere baai kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ahe muji.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or inconsistent watering. When the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops flowers to conserve its energy and water.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants waste energy growing tall to reach the light instead of using that energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu ŋmeii wuji lɛ

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil stays soaked for too long or carries fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for the next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my stored seed yams starting to sprout in the barn long before the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Stored yams sprout when temperatures rise or light hits them inside the barn. Keeping your seed yams in a well-ventilated, shaded, and cool storage area keeps them resting until planting time.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kane tswa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ dumɔ be lɛ shɛɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the root zone or leaves the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why do my groundnut pods end up empty inside with no nuts when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ mli efee efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops', happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are developing underground. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting gives the plants the calcium needed to fill out the seeds.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'pops' lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛwo amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays around them for too long or when fungal diseases in the soil attack the plant. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua tso lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting early in the barn before the planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ mra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when they feel heat and high moisture in the air, which tricks the tuber into thinking rainy season has started. Keeping your storage barn well-ventilated, cool, and shaded delays this sprouting so the seeds stay fresh until planting time.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Enɛ haa atomo lɛ susuɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ bote mli jogbaŋŋ, eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi ehee kɛyashiɔ dumɔ be mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot dry weather or attacked by sap-sucking insects like mirids. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot support with water and food to protect itself from dying.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua amɛ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ato nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do my tall plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the wind is not strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because their root system is naturally shallow, and tiny soil pests called nematodes often chew the roots away. Supporting the trees with wooden props and controlling soil pests keeps the plants firmly anchored.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii Bei pii lɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni akudɔɔ sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning crusty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that carry viruses, or by intense sun heat causing water loss. Providing light shade and controlling sucking insects early protects the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni haa nu fiteɔ lɛ mli Mra be mli hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms as soon as the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms during extreme heat to conserve water and energy so the main stem does not dry out. Mulching the base of the plant with dry grass keeps the soil cool and helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni dɔɔ waa koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ akagbi Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea flowers before the pods can even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet scents and nectar that attract pests like thrips and pod borers seeking food. Spraying neem water or recommended bio-pesticides right as the first buds open protects the blossoms so pods can develop.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers ni niyenii he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ bio-insecticide lɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbele pɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my lowland rice plants stay short and yellowish instead of growing tall in the flooded field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young rice seedlings stunt when water in the field is kept too deep early on, preventing oxygen from reaching the roots. Lowering the water level so roots can breathe allows the rice to absorb nutrients and grow tall.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ akɛ nu to ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ nyɛɛɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ajie nu lɛ shi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ, ni ebaaha elɛɛmɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear the weeds around my rubber trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Ehe miihia ni midu rɔbɔt tsei daa.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water and fertilizer from the soil that your rubber trees need to grow strong. Clearing them neatly ensures your trees get all the nutrients and makes it easy for you to walk around to harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ejuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa o-roba tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa enine shɛɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ. ni eye ebua bo ni oya he fɛɛ he koni okpa nii lɛ mlɛo

english: Does removing bush and grass from around my trees help them yield more crop?
ga: Ani tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, when you clear the bush around tree crops, the roots don't have to fight for moisture in the ground. This allows the trees to easily suck up water and nutrients, which boosts their overall production.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ojie tsei bibii ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ehe ebahiaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to weed the farm before collecting latex from rubber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abua latɛs ni jɛ rɔbɔt tsei amli lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Clearing around the trees prevents dirt, leaves, and insects from falling into your collection cups. Clean rubber latex brings a better price at the market than dirty latex.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tso lɛ, ebaatsi muji, baai, kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkagbee o-collection cup lɛ mli. Latex ni he tse lɛ jara hi fe latex ni he tseee.

english: How do rubber trees draw up water and make the liquid sap that is collected?
ga: Te rɔba tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ nu ni amɛbuaa naa lɛ?
