english: Rubber trees use their deep roots like drinking straws to pull water and nutrients from the soil up into the trunk. The tree mixes this water with nutrients to form a milky liquid called latex or sap.
ga: Rɔba tsei kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ futuɔ nu nɛɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni efeɔ nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ni atsɛɔ lɛ latex loo sap.

english: What time of day do rubber trees produce and move the most sap?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛ rɔbɔt yaa babaoo?

english: Rubber trees draw up water and move sap mostly during the cool early morning hours. Tapping the trees early in the morning yields more liquid because the heat of the afternoon sun slows down the sap flow.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ babaoo yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ otswa tso lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ shwane lɛ baaha mliki lɛ atsɔ blɛoo.

english: How does water travel from the underground roots all the way up into the trunk of a tree?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli kɛyaa tso shishi?

english: Inside the trunk are tiny tubes, like small pipes. As leaves lose moisture to the air, it creates a natural suction that pulls water from the roots straight up through these trunk pipes.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ, tsɔne bibioo ko yɛ ni tamɔ paipi bibioo ko. Kɛji baai lɛ fite ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nu ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ baa. kɛtsɔ tsɔne paipii nɛɛ anɔ

english: How do I cut a rubber tree to get the sap out without killing the tree?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afo rɔbɔt tso ko koni emli nu lɛ ajɛ mli ni egbeee tso lɛ?

english: You make a thin, shallow shave on the bark using a special tapping knife. This opens the tiny sap channels without reaching the deep wood inside, allowing the sap to drop out safely while the tree continues growing.
ga: Okɛ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko shwieɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe ni efee bibioo ni ekɔɔɔ he eko. Enɛ baagbele mliki gbɛi bibii lɛ. ni eyaaa tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Enɛ haa nu lɛ joɔ foi shweshweeshwe be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: How do farmers in Ghana make money from growing rubber trees?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnáa shika kɛtsɔ rɔba tsei ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Farmers collect the milky sap in cups attached to the trees, allow it to set into liquid or solid blocks, and then sell it to processing companies that use it to make tires, boots, and other items.
ga: Okwaafoi buaa mliki mli nu lɛ anaa yɛ kɔɔpoi ni akɛkpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ amli. Ha ni efee nu loo nɔ ko ni wa. No sɛɛ lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii ni akɛfeɔ rɔba, bɔɔtu kɛ nibii krokomɛi.

english: Can rubber trees grow well in my region in Ghana?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Rubber trees thrive in warm, high-rainfall regions of Ghana, such as the Western Region. They need deep soil and plenty of rainwater to produce liquid sap continuously.
ga: Rɔba tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Ghana, tamɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛ nugbɔ babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛná mliki ni ji nu ni yaa nɔ.

english: How many years must I wait after planting a rubber tree before it is ready to produce sap for sale?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔdu rɔbɔt tsei wɔgbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani wɔfee rɔbɔt ni wɔkɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 6 to 7 years to grow thick enough bark before you can start tapping them safely for sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛhewolo lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa dani obaanyɛ oje amɛtswamɔ shishi shweshweeshwe koni onine ashɛ amɛmli nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees, keeping the soil moist and protecting them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes in that soil helps the maize green up and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my corn leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm pests. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments before they burrow deep into the plant stalk protects your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii dani amɛbote tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do people say I shouldn't burn all the weeds and bushes on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich topsoil nutrients and beneficial soil insects, while leaving the ground dry. Clearing weeds without burning preserves soil moisture and organic food for your crop roots.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ ni ashãaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with beans or peanuts restores nutrients and starves pest populations.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water collects around them without draining away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away so the tubers stay dry enough to grow well.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots coming out from the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots causes them to fight for food and water, leading to small plantain bunches. Leaving only one main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures larger fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo baaha amɛye niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni kɛ plantain tsei bibii baa Ashiɔ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso yibii ni mli wa kome loo enyɔ koni ekwɛ akɛ ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why are the stems on my cocoa trees swelling up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a symptom of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus disease, carried by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees stop producing healthy pods and must be removed to prevent spreading the disease to healthy cocoa.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ lɛ mealybug tsɔne. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baakpa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ. ni esa akɛ ajie koni hela akagbɛ ashwã kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant cowpeas together with their main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, acting like natural fertilizer for nearby crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do small beetles appear inside my stored grain bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ midumɔwui kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils hatch from eggs hidden in grain that wasn't dried completely before bagging. Drying harvested grain thoroughly in the sun and using sealed bags prevents insect infestations.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmaa ni egbiko kwraa lolo dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli kɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: If I plant oil palm trees on my land today, how many years do I have to wait before I can start harvesting the fruits?
ga: Kɛji midu mu tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabɔi nikpamɔ?

english: Oil palm trees usually take about 3 to 4 years after field planting to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches, after which they can produce for up to 25 to 30 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu mu tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, eheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. No sɛɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee lɛ kɛyashi afii 25 kɛyashi 30.

english: Can I plant cassava or vegetables in the empty spaces between my young oil palm trees during the first year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ he ni yɔɔ mu tsei ateŋ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can plant short-term crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between young oil palm trees during their first two years to get income and food while keeping weeds away, as long as you do not plant too close to the young palm stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. yɛ mu tsei ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni ená shika kɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ. Shii abɔ ni oduuu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso bibioo lɛ tsɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the lower dead or yellowing leaves from my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ baai ni egboi loo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning old or dead leaves frees up nutrients for the tree to produce bigger fruit bunches, keeps the tree trunk clean, and makes it much easier to spot and harvest ripe fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ baai ni egbɔ loo ni egboi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite koni ekɛfee aduawai akui wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei akutsei lɛ ahe tseɔ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaana aduawai ni ekwɛ ni akpa.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I leave cleared grass to rot on the farm instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miha jwɛi ni he tse fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: When you leave cleared grass to rot naturally on the soil, it acts as mulch that retains soil moisture, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and slowly adds natural nutrients back into the land.
ga: Kɛ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, Ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to weak, tall plants with smaller fruits or lower yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii loo amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: Pale yellow leaves on corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that the roots are waterlogged from heavy rain, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so that rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, or early in the morning when rain is expected to be mild, but avoid applying it right before heavy downpours that can carry it away from the roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Aloo leebi beni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ fioo lɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Weeds are native to the area and have very strong root systems that absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to grow aggressively as soon as moisture arrives.
ga: Jwɛi nɛɛ jɛ jɛmɛ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa waa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ha amɛdara oya kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bashɛ shi pɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during the long dry season without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers during severe dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water and protect the main tree from drying out until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni abuɔ tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do small insects like aphids multiply and attack my crop leaves mostly during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids fɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ amɛtutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather helps insects reproduce much faster, while drought stresses the plant, making its sap richer and easier for insects to feed on.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hɔmɔ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa latex lɛ fa babaoo, ni ehaa ŋmeii yeɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks Nitrogen. The plant naturally pulls Nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai bibii lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural trick to save water. By curling its leaves, it reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and traps moisture inside.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap, or by a virus carried by those insects that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry spells to protect themselves from losing too much water. Adding shade trees and mulching helps keep moisture in the soil to prevent this.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni ekɛtsi enɛ naa.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or poor pollination. Consistent watering helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛgbiɔ loo pollination ni ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing lots of leafy green vines but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ wain tsei babaoo ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, cowpea plants spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers. They need balanced nutrients to switch to making pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja he miihia amɛ koni amɛtsɔ pods.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big open leaves without forming a hard round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa agboi ni agbele naa ni efeee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when the weather is too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer early on.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ ajie yitso kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni anáa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mra

english: Look at the small buds or 'eyes' along the stem where leaves used to grow. These buds must point upward toward the sky so the shoots can sprout easily.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe ni tsutsu lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Ehe miihia ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ adara mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem fight for the same food and water in the soil, which makes the main tree produce smaller, lighter bunches of plantains.
ga: Plantains ni ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle amɛhe Plantain kome pɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ feɔ fãji bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantains next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain yɛ kookoo dumɔwu ni adu ehee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural sunshades while the young cocoa trees build strength.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Beni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ maa ehewalɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much standing water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost and improving farm drainage can help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aha nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmɔ mli su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the middle of my young maize leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmãa ni atse yɛ ŋmãa bibioo ko teŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ shishi? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: This is usually caused by the fall armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central funnel of the plant. You can manage them early by applying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides directly into the funnel of each affected plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall flukes, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsu he nii mra. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees dry out easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through your farm, along with removing infected pods immediately, helps stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant a cassava stem cutting into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or buds along the stem and make sure they are pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down makes it difficult for shoots to grow properly and reduces your total harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃, ni no haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it really necessary to place wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso ko ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch full sunlight and make energy for the plant. Yams that are properly staked develop much larger tubers underground than those left crawling on the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. Sweet potatoes ni adu jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa fe nɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he amanehulu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants early in the morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots can absorb moisture before the sun gets hot. Watering in the hot sun causes most water to evaporate quickly and can stress the plant leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa.

english: This practice, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight, slows down water evaporation, prevents weeds from taking over, and enriches the soil as the organic material rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fite

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them first enriches the ground naturally, giving the next crop of maize essential nutrients for strong growth.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: I noticed tiny caterpillars eating the leaves inside the tops of my young maize plants. Why is this happening and will it destroy my crop?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko. Ye baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ enɛ yaa nɔ lɛ ni ani ebaafite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the growing center of maize plants. If left untreated, they destroy the leaves and prevent the plant from forming healthy corn ears, so early treatment with recommended pest controls or neem extracts is necessary.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Efiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ awo ŋmãa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaawoo loo neem mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni esa akɛ afee.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or tomato in the exact same patch of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ he ni mikpa tomato lɛ yɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Planted in the same spot, crops from the same family suffer from accumulated soil diseases and pests left behind by the previous harvest. Rotating with unrelated crops like maize or beans breaks the pest cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ naa shikpɔŋ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ ahe amanehulu. Nibii ni aduɔ ni kɛ amɛhe bɛ wekukpaa, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe. Efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight and dry heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture needed for survival.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ latsaa ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my crops help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or crop leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground so water does not evaporate quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the dirt instead of growing roots and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot when they are planted upside down, buried in waterlogged soil, or cut from old, diseased stems. Always select mature, healthy stems and plant them with the buds pointing upward in well-drained soil.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ loo afo kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni he wa be fɛɛ be. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die shortly after I move them from the nursery bed to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee miŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved into hot sun with damaged roots. Moving seedlings late in the afternoon or on cloudy days, along with watering them immediately, helps them recover smoothly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ transplant shock he kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛshishifãi efite. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ Kɛfata nu ni akɛhaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil a few weeks after planting when roots are ready to absorb it. Avoid applying fertilizer during heavy downpours or on dry ground right before heavy rain to prevent it from washing off.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he koni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ he.

english: People say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil richer for my next crop—how does that work?
ga: Akɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ—te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas directly from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen acts as natural manure for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and mushy before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom end rot, happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil swings between very dry and very soaked.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ miihoso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming out around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Special ni jeɔ kpo kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ ajieɔ.

english: Leaving too many suckers around a plantain tree forces them all to fight for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves strength for the main plant to yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ashiɔ ŋmeii lɛ abɔleɔ Plantain babaoo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ehe baahia ni tsei nɛɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛ niji agboi ni tsii awo.

english: What does it mean when extension officers say there is a late onset of rains for our area?
ga: Kɛ́ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A late onset means the main rainy season will start later in the year than normal. Instead of planting at your usual month, you must hold off until regular, steady rains begin so your seeds do not dry up in the ground.
ga: Shishijee ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baaje shishi yɛ afi lɛ mli sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ nyɔŋ ni sa mli lɛ Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ anɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa nɔ daa nɔ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I know if the rainy season has truly started or if it is just a temporary rain shower?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo eji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko kɛkɛ?

english: A proper season start means heavy rain wets the soil several inches deep for consecutive days. A temporary shower only wets the top surface of the dirt and quickly dries out under the hot sun.
ga: Be lɛ shishijee kpakpa tsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɛɔ inchii babaoo gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Be kukuoo mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ baaha muji lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How does a delay in rainfall impact crops planted in the southern part of Ghana?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Delayed rains shorten the total time crops have to grow before the dry season returns. This can cause crops to produce lower yields unless you use fast-growing seed varieties.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha be ni he hiaa koni akɛdu nii lɛ afee kuku dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aku esɛɛ aba. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi ja okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni daa oya tsu nii.

english: Why does rain fall in a nearby town like Bonsu while my farm in a neighboring area stays dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Bonsu maŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Rainfall in Ghana varies from place to place due to local trees, hills, and wind patterns. Forested areas or elevated land often pull rain clouds sooner than surrounding open or cleared areas.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ tsei, gɔji, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ. Hei ni kooi yɔɔ loo hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ fɔɔ nugbɔ atatui ni nɛɔ oya fe hei ni agbele loo hei ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: What happens to my seed if I plant it in dry soil before the delayed rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo?

english: Seeds planted in dry ground can get scorched by intense heat, eaten by insects and birds, or rot if they receive only a light rain that isn't enough to keep them growing.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ashã yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Kplukai kɛ okpoi yeɔ lɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ egbo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo. pɛ, ni faaa kɛha dalɛ

english: Should I change the type of crop seeds I buy if the rainy season arrives late?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba sɛɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ matsake tso dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, when rains are late, it is best to plant early-maturing or drought-tolerant seed varieties so the crop can ripen completely before the rains stop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Why do my crops look weak even after we receive a small amount of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ wɔnine shɛɛɛ nugbɔ fioo nɔ moŋ?

english: Light rains only soak the top surface of the dirt, but crop roots grow deeper underground where the soil stays dry until heavy, continuous rains fall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ atsɔ mli. Shi tsei ashishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he agbi kɛyashi be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaya nɔ nɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm soil from losing moisture while waiting for regular rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your plants with dry grass or plant leaves, which is called mulching. This shades the soil from the sun and stops moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Is it safe for me to apply chemical fertilizer on my crops when the rains are delayed?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: No, applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn your plants' roots. Fertilizer needs plenty of water in the soil to dissolve safely so the plant can feed without getting damaged.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Nu babaoo he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aha amɛ niyenii ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: What will happen to my corn if the rains stop too early at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra tsɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: If rains end early, crops like corn cannot get enough water to fill out their cobs, leading to small, light grains and a smaller harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba naagbee mra lɛ Dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa nyɛŋ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: What exactly is fertilizer, and why do my crops need it to grow well?
ga: Mɛni tuuntu ji ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mitsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is essentially food for your plants. Just like human beings need good food to grow strong and stay healthy, crops need nutrients from fertilizer to develop strong stems, lush green leaves, and produce a high yield.
ga: Fertilizer ji niyenii titri kɛha otsei lɛ. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa adesai koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛná tsei ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Can I use manure from my farm animals as food for my crops instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii atsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure is a rich natural food for plants that feeds your crops and improves the soil structure, but it should be dried or decomposed first so it does not overheat and burn the roots of your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ji niyenii ni jara wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Shi esa akɛ agbi loo efite klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ ji koni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine ni okɛshã otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and lacks enough nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ mli?

english: Tired soil often produces crops with light green or yellow leaves, thin stems, and poor yields. If your soil feels hard, pale, or dry, it usually lacks the natural plant food needed to sustain good growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egbi lɛ, no lɛ ebɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and wilting when there is no drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni hɔmɔ bɛ lɛ?

english: When leaves turn yellow and wilt without a drought, it usually means your crop is sick from a plant disease, affected by root-damaging pests, or suffering from a lack of essential plant food in the soil.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi ni amɛgbiko lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emɔ tsei ahela. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ náa enɔ hewalɛ loo tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he piŋmɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my crop leaves, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects eat leaves because leaves are the engine room where plants make their food using sunlight. When insects destroy the leaves, the plant starves and cannot grow big leaves, fruits, or grains.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baai ejaakɛ baai ji tsɔne tsuji ni tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ mli. Beni kooloi bibii fiteɔ baai Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni enyɛŋ ewo baai wuji, aduawai, loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do my young crops dry up or burn when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛshãa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops have tender roots that cannot reach deep into the soil to draw enough water. Under hot direct sun, they lose moisture faster than their small roots can drink, causing them to dry up.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ejie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii. nɔ ni anuɔ lɛ eko lɛ, ha egbi.

english: When you plant seeds too close together, the crops fight each other for limited plant food, water, and sunlight, resulting in crowded, tall, and weak plants that yield very little.
ga: Kɛ́ odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei wuɔ koni amɛná tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la fioo ko. Enɛ haa tsei ni mli tse, ni kwɔlɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops produce less harvest when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific plant food that crop loves from the soil and allows pests and sicknesses that target that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving your crops of the food you provided.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni okɛhaa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can too much rainfall harm my crops when plants need water to survive?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ be mli ni nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, which causes the roots to rot and the plant to die.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ minyɛɛɛ mamu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them directly in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to protect their delicate leaves from burning. Without plantains or shade trees nearby to block intense sunlight, the heat dries them out faster than their small roots can drink water.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. Kɛji tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbi oya. amɛteŋ ni baanyɛ anu nu

english: Why do my pepper plants under big trees produce long stems and leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pɛpɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ tsitsi kakadaŋŋ kɛ baai shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to generate the energy required for flowering and fruiting. In deep shade, the plant spends all its energy stretching high to reach light instead of producing fruit.
ga: Hulu la he miihia pepper tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛgbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená la moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings grow long, thin, and weak if I keep them under a thick thatch shade for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ daraa, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ mikɛ amɛ wo jwɛi ni mli edɔ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch rapidly upward searching for sunlight when it is too dark. If kept under dense shade, they become tall and fragile, making them weak and likely to break when transplanted into the main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baajie amɛhe oya koni amɛyatao hulu la kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ akɛto hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ebaafee kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni kɛ́ ajie amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛkumɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to apply fertilizer to my maize at specific weeks rather than just anytime I buy it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele lɛ mli yɛ otsii komɛi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he be fɛɛ be ni obaahe lɛ

english: Maize needs heavy nutrients at key growth moments, such as when it reaches knee-height and when it produces tassels. Applying fertilizer outside these periods means the plant cannot use it effectively, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Abɛi biɔ niyenii ni tsii yɛ be mli ni edalɛ he hiaa waa, tamɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ enaji ahe kɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni enyɛ ekɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Eji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika fitemɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ?

english: Rain provides water, but plants also need nutrients from the soil to stay green. Yellow leaves often mean the soil is exhausted of nitrogen, showing that the plant is starving despite receiving enough rain.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tsei yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow giant green leaves but give me small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? kɛha mi beni akpaa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground rather than storing food in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I miss watering them for a few days right when flowers start showing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ha amɛ gbii fioo komɛi beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most delicate stage for tomatoes. Missing water during this period causes severe heat stress, making the flowers drop off before setting fruit, which drastically reduces your total yield.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ kɛha tomato. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: How can a short dry spell during the tassel stage destroy my entire maize harvest?
ga: be kuku ni mli egbi Yɛ tassel be lɛ mli lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ makpãtã mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: During tasseling, maize relies on water to move pollen and form kernels. If water fails during this short window, the ears remain empty or poorly filled, ruining your expected harvest.
ga: yɛ be mli ni abuaa naa lɛ Abele kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ koni ekɛ pollen lɛ aya ni ekɛfee dumɔwui. Kɛji nu hoɔ yɛ be kukuoo nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ baakã he ahi shi efolo loo ekɛ ehe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ. Efiteɔ yibiiwoo ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: If I delay spraying my farm for fall armyworm for just three days, can it ruin my whole field?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛha cutworms lɛ to sɛɛ gbii etɛ pɛ lɛ, Ani ebaakpata miŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Yes, pests like fall armyworms reproduce fast and eat aggressively. A delay of just a few days allows them to multiply and destroy the central growing tips of young plants, making recovery impossible.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ nii waa. Gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni akɛbaakpa sɛɛ lɛ baaha amɛshwere ni amɛfite tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ. ni ehaa enyɛŋ ehi shi ekoŋŋ

english: Do my crops stop growing at night, or are they still active when the sun goes down?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ gbɛkɛ loo amɛtsuɔ nii lolo kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi?

english: Crops gather energy from sunlight during the day, but at night they use that stored energy to build roots, stems, and fruits. They are constantly active, which is why healthy night conditions and moist soil matter.
ga: Tsei buaa hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli yɛ gbi mli. Shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtswaa shishifãi, tsei ashishifãi, kɛ aduawai. Amɛmiitsu nii be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni gbɛkɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant food needed for growth. It can also happen when the soil stays flooded with water for too long, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What causes small holes in my cassava leaves, and how will it affect my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmei baa nɔ Ni te ebaaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Small holes in leaves are caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating them. When leaves get damaged, the plant cannot catch enough sunlight to make food, which results in smaller cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Beni baai lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomato seeds too close to each other in the bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso nɔ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing lets fresh air pass between plants, which keeps leaves dry and prevents damp diseases from spreading.
ga: Beni tomato tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa helai ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does my crop field dry out so fast even when rain fell just two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it has too much sand or lacks organic material. Adding dry leaves, compost, or well-rotted animal manure acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold rainwater for a much longer time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ ŋã babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be babaoo.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they are under severe heat stress, lack sufficient water, or are missing key nutrients like potassium in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ latsaa he haomɔ shishi. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do experienced farmers advice me to plant beans alongside my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans belong to a plant family that traps air floating in the ground and converts it into free soil fertilizer. This extra food helps nearby corn grow stronger and improves soil quality naturally.
ga: Beans fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni akɛfataa he nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it bad if I keep planting cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Yes, growing cassava on the same spot continuously exhausts the soil's specific nutrients and allows pests or soil diseases that attack cassava to build up, resulting in smaller harvests over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tutuaa ŋmei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa yibii bibii baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I sowed fail to come out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ejeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the soil, eaten by underground insects, sowed in soil that is too dry, or if the seed was stored badly and died before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ lɛ Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ etooo jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani adu.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs extra food before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii kroko dani madu?

english: If your land looks pale or turns hard like concrete when dry, or if your previous crops produced weak stems and pale leaves, the soil is low on nutrients and needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse loo ewa tamɔ kɔnkrit kɛji egbi loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ tsei ni etse kɛ baai bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my harvested onions rot so quickly after I pick them from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sabalai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Onions spoil easily if they are harvested while the soil is wet or if they are not left to dry in an airy, shaded spot for a few days to harden their outer skins before storage.
ga: Sabala fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni egbi yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi koni ehewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli awa dani akɛto.

english: Why are many farmers in Ghana starting to grow cashew instead of sticking only to cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miibɔi cashew ŋmeii dumɔ yɛ kookoo pɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees are much more resistant to drought and warm weather than cocoa trees. They require fewer expensive chemical sprays and can still give good yields in areas where changing weather patterns are making cocoa farming difficult.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli babaoo fe cacao tsei. Amɛbiɔ tsofai ni jara waaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii kpakpai hu yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ nɔ ni wa lɛ.

english: Can cashew trees survive in dry, poor soil where my cocoa trees are struggling to grow?
ga: Ani cashew tso ko baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ehiii ni mi-cocoa tso lɛ miitao ni eda lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cashew trees have deep taproots that reach underground water easily. They are very tough plants that can thrive in poorer, drier soils where traditional crops like cocoa dry up and die.
ga: Hɛɛ, cashew tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he mlɛo. Amɛji tsei ni wa waa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ohia emɔ nɔ ni egbi nɔ. Kusum nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting a cashew tree before I can harvest my first nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ adu cashew tso lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani akpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cashew trees grow fairly quickly and usually start producing their first small batch of nuts within 3 years of planting, reaching their full harvest production when they are around 7 to 10 years old.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ daa oya ni bei pii lɛ amɛjeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii bibii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ, ni akpaa amɛ kwraa beni amɛye aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 10 lɛ.

english: Why do young cashew plants need full sunlight while young cocoa trees need shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ he hiaa cashew tsei lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Cashew is a sun-loving plant that uses direct sunlight to build strong stems and deep roots. Young cocoa trees, on the other hand, have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun, so cocoa needs shade trees to protect it.
ga: Cashews ji tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo aná tsei ni haa ehe hulutsoo koni ebu ehe.

english: Do cashew trees need to be sprayed with chemicals as often as cocoa trees to protect them from pests?
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai afɔ cashew tsei anɔ shii abɔ tamɔ Kɛ kookoo tsei ahe koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: No, cashew trees generally suffer from fewer destructive insect pests than cocoa. While they still need monitoring for bugs and fungal diseases, they require far less frequent and less costly chemical spraying.
ga: Dabi, cashew tsei lɛ fɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fioo fe kookoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ lolo kɛha kooloi kɛ ŋmeii helai moŋ. Shi amɛbiɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ shii abɔ ni amɛjara waaa.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize between my young cashew trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Yɛ cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when cashew seedlings are still small, you can safely intercrop maize, groundnuts, or legumes to earn food and extra income before the cashew canopy spreads out.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli lɛ, cashew tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii kɛ shika kroko dani ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: If I want to replace an old cocoa farm with cashew, do I need to clear out all the old cocoa roots first?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni matsake kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko mafee cashew ŋmeii. Ani esa akɛ majie kookoo shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yes, it is best to remove old, dead, or diseased cocoa stumps and roots. Clearing them prevents fungal root diseases from lingering in the soil and attacking your new cashew seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie kookoo tsei kɛ shishifãi ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etutua o-cashew tso hee lɛ.

english: How do I know when cashews are ripe and ready to be harvested from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cashew ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Unlike cocoa pods which you harvest from the tree trunk, cashews are fully ripe when the fruit turns bright yellow or red and the nut falls naturally to the ground on its own.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni okpaa kɛjɛɔ tso shishi lɛ he. Cashews lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsuru ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do cashew flowers drop off when there is unexpected rain during the flowering season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers are delicate, and heavy rains or high humidity can wash away pollen or encourage fungal diseases like anthracnose, which damages the flowers and prevents nuts from forming.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ mlɛo. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo ewo ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ anthracnose, ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ni ehaaa ŋmeii afee lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Will a cashew tree keep producing nuts every year, or does it die off after a few harvests?
ga: Ani cashew tso lɛ baaya nɔ awo ŋmeii afi fɛɛ afi loo ebaagbo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: A cashew tree is a long-term investment. If you weed and prune it properly, a single cashew tree can reliably produce nuts every dry season for 30 to 40 years or more.
ga: Cashew tsei ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji okɛ jwɛi shwie shi ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Cashew tso kome pɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Can I grow tall timber trees on the same farm alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei kakadaji yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ kookoo tsei ahe?

english: Yes, growing timber trees with cocoa creates a beneficial agroforestry system. The tall timber trees provide natural shade that protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight, retains soil moisture, and gives you valuable timber in the future.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo dumɔwui feɔ agroforestry gbɛjianɔtoi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha bo tsei ni jara wa wɔsɛɛ

english: Why do young cocoa plants need shade crops like plantain when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains beni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain provides temporary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ama shi lɛ.

english: How do shade trees help my farm survive during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli

english: Shade trees block strong dry winds, reduce the temperature on your farm, and slow down soil water evaporation, helping your cocoa and other crops stay hydrated through dry periods.
ga: Tsei lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa, ni amɛgbiɔ waa. Ha hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni oha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi O-hiɔ shi yɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is the correct way to prepare my land before starting a new farm for the season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni matsɔ nɔ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mije ŋmɔ hee shishi kɛha be lɛ?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing weeds, removing diseased plant debris, loosening hard soil so root systems can spread easily, and ensuring good drainage so water does not sit and rot crop roots.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Tso mli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo Ni akwɛ koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni nu akafee ekome ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I space my crops properly instead of planting them close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato he ni mikɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and resources to grow strong and produce a bigger total harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ená yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: How many years does a newly planted cocoa tree usually take before it starts bearing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties common in Ghana usually begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed. Flower drop occurs due to natural self-thinning, insufficient insect pollination, water stress, or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Kplukai ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. nu mli haomɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do the leaves on my crops start turning yellow after prolonged heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can cause waterlogging in the soil, which cuts off air to the roots. Without oxygen, the roots cannot take up essential nutrients like nitrogen, making the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its richness and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of poor soil fertility include slow plant growth, thin stems, pale or yellowing leaves, and reduced harvest size compared to previous years.
ga: Okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ ekomɛi ji tsei adalɛ blɛoo, tsei bibii, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ ba shi kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it dangerous to let tall weeds grow around my young crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal light, water, and nutrients from them. Tall weeds also harbor destructive insects and plant diseases that can kill young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ hu ji nɔ ni kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are very tender. Too much sun scorches the leaves and dries out the soil, so planting shade plants like plantains protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ baai lɛ darako kwraa. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce many flowers, but many fall off due to lack of water, heat stress, or poor pollination by tiny insects called midges. Keeping soil moist and preserving natural shade helps more flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbee shi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. heat stress Loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ feɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehiɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ babaoo.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen, which the plant needs to build strong green leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and grow bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baadara.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves but giving me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi lɛ? Dani aduawai lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or plantain weevils eat away the roots and inner stem underground, weakening the plant's hold in the soil until the weight of the fruit or a gentle breeze knocks it down.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo plantain ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii. Ha tso lɛ mli ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee mlɛo kɛyashi tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiimɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ ko baatswa. baatswa tsei ashwie shi

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and densely shaded air. Pruning excess cocoa branches lets sunlight in and air circulate, drying out the pods so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he. Gbimɔ ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmeii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil. It is usually caused by irregular watering, where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli eyi kɛ muji yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the deep heart of the plant to feed on new leaves. The dirt you see inside is the waste left behind by the worm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei. Muji ni onaa yɛ mli lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the heavy tuber below. Keeping vines off the damp ground also protects the leaves from rot and fungal infections.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ tee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do tiny young cocoa pods turn shriveled and dark while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Toɔ ni amɛfeɔ diŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. The tree intentionally sacrifices extra small pods it cannot feed so that it has enough water and strength to grow the remaining pods to full size.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Tso lɛ tsɔ hiɛ ekɛ pod bibioo ko sha afɔle. ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii Enɛ ji koni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa trees when I want them to grow and bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ? Be ni misumɔɔ ni eda ni ewo yibii?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so the cocoa tree can focus its energy on sprouting fresh new twigs and healthy leaves, which helps the tree flourish and bear more fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha kookoo tso lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ahi niji heei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How does trimming my old cocoa trees help them produce pods again?
ga: Te mi-cacao tso momo lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Trimming or pruning stimulates and revitalizes old cocoa trees, causing them to shoot out new branches and fresh foliage that bring the tree back to life and restore fruit production.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni ehaa amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ niji heei kɛ baai heei ni haa tso lɛ baa wala mli ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the main advantage of pruning my cocoa farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ he?

english: Pruning has a double benefit: it revitalizes the cocoa tree by helping it grow new twigs, and it gives the tree healthy leaf coverage needed to support a good yield of cocoa pods.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi enyɔ yɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ he: Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ niji heei ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ lɛ haa ehe waa ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai ni mli wa ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa

english: Why are fresh green leaves so important for my cocoa tree's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ he hiaa yɛ mi-cacao ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: New leaves feed the cocoa tree and give it energy. When a cocoa tree gets fresh leaves, it grows bushier and becomes strong enough to carry and nourish fruit.
ga: Baai heei lɛ haa cacao tso lɛ niyenii ni ehaa hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná baai heei Ebaatsɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ emɔ aduawai amli ni eha amɛ niyenii.

english: What does it mean when my cocoa tree starts shooting out new twigs after I prune it?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tso ko ni ji niji heei lɛ?

english: Sprouting new twigs is a sign that the cocoa tree is revitalizing itself, growing new fruiting wood that will eventually support new cocoa flowers and pods.
ga: Niji heei ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ miifee ehe ehee. Amɛduɔ aduawai tsei heei ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaaye amɛbua kookoo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are healthy enough to support a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: A healthy, revitalized cocoa tree will actively produce new branches, twigs, and a thick canopy of leaves, showing it has the strength to bear fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfee ehee lɛ woɔ niji, tsei niji, kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Can proper management make an old, weak cocoa tree produce like a young one again?
ga: Ani nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ awo yibii ekoŋŋ tamɔ tsei bibii?

english: Yes, proper management and pruning revitalize tired cocoa trees, prompting them to grow fresh branches and leaves so they can bear fruit again like younger trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaye abua ni eha kookoo tsei ni etɔ amɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Wo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo tsei niji kɛ baai heei koni amɛwo yibii ekoŋŋ tamɔ tsei bibii.

english: Why does a cocoa tree need to become bushy before it can yield plenty of pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ cacao tso ko aná jwɛi dani ebaanyɛ ewo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: A bushy canopy filled with healthy new leaves means the tree is making enough food and energy to sustain a heavy load of developing cocoa pods.
ga: Kpo lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miiwo niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua kookoo ŋmeii babaoo ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa trees that stopped bearing fruit to start fruiting again?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni ekpa yibiiwoo lɛ woɔ yibii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Good field management and strategic pruning revive the tree, encouraging it to produce new leaves and twigs which are essential for fruiting.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ niyenii. Ekanyaa baai kɛ niji heei ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Will cutting back cocoa branches cause any harm to my farm's production?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaná miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: When done correctly, cutting back branches does not harm the farm; instead, it stimulates the cocoa tree to grow back stronger with fresh branches that improve future harvests.
ga: Kɛji afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Pruning lɛ yeee ŋmɔ lɛ awui. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ cacao tsei ɔmɛ he wami konɛ a ná nimli ehehi nɛ ma ha nɛ hwɔɔ se ɔ, ní kpami ɔ maa hi saminya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food they need from the soil to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What good does putting animal manure on my field do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔji ahe lɛ yɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Animal manure acts like a slow-release food for the soil, helping it hold water longer during dry spells and providing vital nutrients that make crops grow healthy.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa sũ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei daa waa lɛ haa
