english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under hot direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to make food, which helps the yam tubers under the ground grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛhoo nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adara ni amɛtsii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath, sucking the juice out of the leaves and spreading plant sicknesses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo amɛshishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms, which are caterpillars that hide inside the plant funnel during the day and eat the fresh leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai heei gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry periods without enough water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be trukaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of leaves but very few pods when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much water and rain causes cowpeas to put all their energy into growing green leaves instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nu kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa cowpea fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ baai eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and sunlight, stealing the food your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the main leaves start turning yellow and dropping off the stem, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even though I am giving them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crop is missing a key food called nitrogen. When soil lacks good nutrients or gets waterlogged, the roots cannot feed properly, causing the leaves to turn pale yellow instead of deep green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ bɛ onibii amli. Beni niyenii kpakpa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce many flowers but most of them drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tso ko yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off easily if the tree lacks water during flowering, if pests like thrips attack the blossom, or if hot dry winds dry them out. Protecting the flowers from pests and ensuring proper moisture helps the fruits stay attached.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Aloo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ha egbi Fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni anaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are suffering from insect attacks or a disease in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii etutua mi-pepper tso lɛ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ hela ko?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible holes, chewed edges, or tiny bugs under the leaves. Soil diseases usually cause the whole plant to suddenly wilt, turn yellow from the bottom stems upward, or rot right at the soil level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni anaa, ŋmeii ni ŋmɔɔ, loo ŋmeii bibii baa baai lɛ ashishi. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. loo ni efiteɔ kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my crops wilt so fast during the dry harmattan season compared to other times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni nu egbi lɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi lɛ mli bei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan air acts like a sponge, pulling water out of leaf pores much faster than roots can draw it up. Covering the soil around the crop base with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and preserves soil water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farm yield less crop when I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific food nutrients that crop relies on. Changing crops every season—especially planting beans or groundnuts—allows the soil to rest and rebuild its natural strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ ekwɛɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ajɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa be Titri lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni etswaa ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Big shade trees protect them from direct heat and create a cool, humid climate that young cocoa needs to grow strong in its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. ni eha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be aba. Esa akɛ kookoo bibioo lɛ adara waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tuber rot happens when rainwater sits in the soil for too long without draining away, suffocating the roots. Planting on raised dirt mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the cassava roots.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows roots and leaves to spread out and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why do tree crops take several years to bear fruit while vegetables yield in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kɛ tsei aheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii, yɛ be mli ni aduawai woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo ko pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables are quick-growing crops that spend all their energy making fast leaves and seeds before dying. Tree crops spend their first few years building strong trunks and deep roots so they have enough strength to bear fruit for decades.
ga: Aduawai ji tsei ni daa oya ni kɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai kɛ dumɔwui oya dani amɛgboi. Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Koni ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without making tomatoes when the afternoon sunshine gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteee tomato lɛ beni shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high afternoon temperatures can ruin the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from forming fruit. Watering early in the morning and using light shade netting during peak heat keeps the flowers cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ afite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaaa enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii Nu ni awoɔ lɛ leebi kɛ shade netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller plants, like plantain or forest trees, to hold moisture in the soil and protect the young plants while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When maize plants are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow thick stalks and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to save water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Keeping soil moisture steady and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni ahiɛɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ naa mawo gɔŋ mli dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil so their tubers can expand easily without running into hard ground. Mounds also keep the roots from rotting in waterlogged soil during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛkaho kɛya shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Gɔji lɛ hu tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already settled in the soil and adapted to local conditions, allowing them to absorb rainwater instantly. Planting crops promptly and clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to establish before weeds take over.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔ oya kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛma shi dani jwɛi lɛ abaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer to waterlogged or flowing soil causes the nutrients to wash away into gutters and streams before the roots can absorb them, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nu ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant peppers on the exact same piece of land where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mifo mibɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Peppers and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil pests and diseases. Rotating with a different crop family, like beans or maize, breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Peppers kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii jɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛgbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ Enɛ haa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize and small caterpillars hidden in the center fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni etse. Akɛtee teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the leaf whorl to eat tender young growth. Early detection and applying appropriate control measures protect the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ baai amli koni eye tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni ana mra Ni gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ he.

english: How do I decide how much land to clear for planting cassava this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mafo kɛha ŋmei yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ he?

english: It is best to start with a farm size you can easily clear, weed, and manage with your available money and labor. Taking care of a smaller piece of land properly yields far more food than planting a huge area that gets overgrown with weeds because you ran out of resources.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobɔi kɛ ŋmɔ dalɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛ shika kɛ nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ lɛ ajie, ajie jwɛi, ni okwɛ nɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔkwɛmɔ Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ, ebaawo yibii babaoo fe shikpɔŋ wulu ni jwɛi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ni ooodu ejaakɛ onibii lɛ faaa.

english: If my first cocoa yield is successful, how should I plan to expand my farm for the next season?
ga: Kɛji mi klɛŋklɛŋ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ye omanye Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafee gbɛjianɔ koni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli alɛɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Expand gradually by reinvesting a portion of your profits into quality seedlings and fertilizer rather than trying to double your field size overnight. Scaling up step-by-step ensures you maintain good care and shade for new young trees without overstretching your energy or savings.
ga: Gbalamɔ mli fiofio kɛtsɔ sɛɛnamɔi lɛ fã ko ni okɛaawo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ofee oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ shii enyɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ, shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei heei ni darako lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ohaa amɛhe hulutsoo. ni efiteee hewalɛ loo shika babaoo ni ekɛto

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are turning yellow because of a disease or because the soil lacks food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela hewɔ loo akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the center in a V-shape usually means the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer. If the yellowing appears as random spots, stripes, or twisted leaves, it is more likely a viral or fungal disease that needs immediate treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔi je kpo trukaa, yɛ ŋmɔtɔi amli, loo yɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ ekolɛ eji hela ko ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli loo ŋmɔtɔ mli baa ni biɔ ni atsa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What should I do as soon as I notice strange white spots on my tomato leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? Yɛ tomato baai anɔ?

english: Act quickly by removing and destroying the affected leaves away from your farm, as white spots often mean a fungal infection like powdery mildew. Reporting and treating plant sickness early prevents the disease from spreading to the rest of your healthy crop.
ga: Feemɔ oya kɛtsɔ baai ni ena hela lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ofite lɛ nɔ. Akɛni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ powdery mildew eba hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni abɔ tsofai ahe helai mra ni atsa amɛ. Ye obua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to weed my field within the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a clean environment to establish strong roots and grow rapidly without stress.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shihilɛ ni mli tse ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdara oya ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge inside the soil by improving its structure and organic content. This allows the soil to trap and hold onto rainwater much longer, keeping your crops nourished and hydrated during hot dry periods.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ egbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa eyaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ ni ehiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kpakpa kɛ nu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving your plants consistent water and light shade during very hot weather helps them retain their blossoms and set healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam vines staying short and bushy instead of climbing up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ fe ni eeekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to catch sunlight and build energy for tuber growth. If they lack strong tall stakes to climb, or if pests are attacking their root system, the vines remain short and produce very small yam tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha amɛ tuber lɛ dalɛ. Kɛji amɛbɛ tso ko ni kɛlɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɔ, loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa eshishifãi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi kuku ni ebaawo sweet potato ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do certified seeds buy from an agricultural shop produce better yields than seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapo ko mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local Ghanaian pests, tolerate dry spells, and produce uniform, high yields. Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength over generations, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo Ghana maŋbii awuiyelɔi lɛ. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni fa babaoo Dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil. Without nitrogen, the leaves cannot produce enough green pigment to process sunlight into plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ hu nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulu la lɛ afee tsei aniyenii.

english: Is it beneficial for my farm if I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like groundnuts or beans together with maize helps the soil because legumes capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding in the center whorls of my maize and eating holes through the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on tender leaves inside the plant funnel. Catching them early in the season is critical to prevent them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: No baafee Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei akui amli lɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɔmɔ amɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers usually fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When temperatures get too high or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees close to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants sunburn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary living shade and keep the air moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ hulu lɛ shãa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves towards direct sunlight to manufacture energy. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, reducing fungal diseases and helping the plant produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many suckers compete with the mother plant for nutrients and water. Pruning extra suckers ensures that all the plant's energy goes into producing one large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni afoɔ lɛ kɛfataa he lɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ plantains akui wuji ni he wa.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout, but the hot, dry soil afterward will wither the tender roots before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ lɛ bɔi diŋ kɛ fitemɔ beni mifo mli gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not store well once removed from the moist ground because air entering the cuts triggers rapid decay. You should harvest cassava only when you are ready to process or consume it immediately.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ etooo amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni boteɔ he ni afo lɛ mli lɛ baaha efite oya. Esa akɛ okpa ŋmei pɛ kɛji ofee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo oye amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry material (mulching) prevents the hot sun from drying out the soil quickly, keeps the root area cool, and stops weed seeds from receiving light to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Is it fine if I plant my yam seed setts in February instead of December or January?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji mi du mi sweet potato dumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ Oflɔŋ mli moŋ fe Alemle loo Aharabata?

english: Yes, planting in February is common in many parts of Ghana as the rainy season approaches. However, you must make sure the soil has enough moisture or that rain starts soon so the seed tubers do not dry out under the hot sun.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ yɛ February mli ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Ghana hei babaoo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ, shi kɛlɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, etsɛŋ ni nugbɔ baanɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ akagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some farmers plant their yams in December before the rains even start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ December mli, dani nugbɔ po nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Planting early in December allows the yam seed to rest in the cool mound underground and break its natural dormancy, so it sprouts immediately when the early rains arrive.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ December shishijee gbɛ lɛ haa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ, ni efiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover my newly planted yam mounds with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi aha sweet potato ni adu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the tops of your mounds with dry leaves, known as mulching, protects the buried yam seeds from scorching soil heat and keeps moisture in the ground until the main rains come.
ga: Atsɛɔ gɔŋ ko yiteŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baabu sweet potato dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa

english: How does lifting my yam vines onto wooden stakes help the tubers underground grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni miwóɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-tubers lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Staking exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and food. This food is stored underground, causing the yam tuber to swell and grow large.
ga: Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo. Akɛ niyenii nɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa sweet potato yibii lɛ fuɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Does the yam tuber continue growing bigger after the leaves on the vine start dying?
ga: Ani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baaya nɔ ada beni baai ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔi gboimɔ sɛɛ?

english: No, once the leaves turn yellow and dry up, the plant stops making food. At this point, the tuber stops growing in size and simply rests in the soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Tso lɛ baakpa nihoomɔ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Tubers lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni amɛbaajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep down in the mound do I need to plant my seed yams?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Seed yams should be planted about 10 to 15 centimeters deep inside the mound. This keeps them safe from heat stress while giving the roots and tubers enough loose soil to push downward.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ shi.

english: How can I know that my yams are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni adu sweet potatoes ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell yams are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely, showing that the plant has finished transferring all its nutrients into the underground tuber.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ sweet potato ko egbɔ kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Can I harvest the main yam tuber early and still leave the plant to grow seed yams?
ga: Minyɛ mikpa sweet potato ŋmeii titrii lɛ mra. Ni ani obaanyɛ oshi tso lɛ lolo koni oyadu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yes, with certain yam varieties, you can carefully remove the mature main tuber early in the season while keeping the roots intact; the vine will then grow smaller secondary tubers that you can use as seeds for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi. Obaanyɛ ojie ŋmeii titrii ni eda lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. yɛ be mli ni ohiɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lolo lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, wain tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii ni ji enyɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What happens if I leave mature yams in the soil for too long after the vines dry up?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmeii momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If mature yams stay underground too long during wet weather, they can rot or attract pests like beetles and rodents that will eat the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ da lɛ, ebaahi shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo amɛgbala kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baaye ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Which part of a harvested yam tuber is best to cut and use as seed for my next planting?
ga: Mɛɛ sweet potato tuber ni akpaa lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ afo ni akɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The head portion (the top part connected to the stem) sprouts the fastest and produces the strongest vines, though the middle and tail pieces can also sprout if cut and cured properly.
ga: Yitso lɛ (ŋwɛigbɛ he ni tso lɛ tso lɛ tsaa lɛ) daa oya fe fɛɛ ni ekɛ wain tso ni mli wa fe fɛɛ baa. Teŋgbɛ kɛ sɛɛ fãi lɛ po baanyɛ adara kɛji akɛ afolɔ ni atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and stay alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will shoot out fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my neighbours plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ duɔ tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ amɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer for the maize, helping it grow stronger while giving you two crops from the same land.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Ye obua ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛ he kome.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping the insects away early and ensuring proper soil moisture helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ He ni ajieɔ kooloi kɛyaa he kroko mra Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the air gets too hot, when the soil drops too low on water, or when too much chemical fertilizer is used. Giving the plants steady water and light shade during high heat keeps the flowers on the stem.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbee shi kɛtee nu fioo tsɔ mli loo kɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn reddish-purple instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ red-purple yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking phosphorus or the soil is too cold and waterlogged for the roots to feed properly. As the soil dries and warms up, the plant usually recovers its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ni edɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Tsei lɛ naa amɛ su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is there a black powdery layer covering the leaves of my citrus tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda diŋ ko ni haa mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Small sap-sucking insects leave a sticky liquid on citrus leaves, and a harmless black fungus called sooty mold grows on top of it. Controlling the insects with soap water or organic spray stops the sticky liquid and clears the leaves.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ shĩɔ nu ni mli tse yɛ citrus baai lɛ anɔ. Ni ŋmei diŋ ko ni bɛ awui ni atsɛɔ lɛ sooty mold lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ye kooloi anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akpa ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe atse.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die off completely when harvest time comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ egbi kwraa ni egbo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die back above ground when the tubers underground have fully matured and stored enough energy. The yellowing and drying of the leaves is a natural clock telling you the yam is ready to be harvested.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛto hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni kɛɔ bo akɛ sweet potatoes eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa saplings burning and turning brown at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shã ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or banana trees around them protects their delicate leaves from burning until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Banana tso lɛ baabu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after heavy rains flooded my land right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi mimaŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much water, air cannot reach the buried seeds, causing them to rot before they can sprout. Heavy rain can also create a hard upper crust of dirt that blocks seeds from breaking through.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afee muji yɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ nɔ ni haaa dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why did my vegetable stems turn brown and wither after I put fertilizer right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmasɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated chemical fertilizer touching a plant stem acts like salt and draws moisture out of the plant roots, burning them. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem in ring shapes.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni eshãa amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ he inchii fioo komɛi be fɛɛ be.

english: Leaves turn yellow and curl when the crop is sending a distress signal. It usually means the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, is getting flooded or scorched by sun, or is being attacked by tiny pests or viruses.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ yelikɛbuamɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hulu la ni shwieɔ mɔ nɔ loo eshãa lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baatutua lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look wilted and lifeless during hot afternoons even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants sweat out water faster through their leaves than their roots can drink from the ground. Drooping is the crop's natural way of protecting itself by shrinking its leaf area exposed to direct sunlight until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ latsaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ahe hei ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni efoɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my young maize leaves, and will it destroy my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni ani amɛbaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding on tender shoots. If left untreated, the insects eat away the leaf surface the plant needs to absorb sunlight, resulting in weak growth and smaller corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ cutworms, ni egbee shi ni eye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ, kooloi yeɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ aná hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: What does NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer actually do when I put it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ NPK 15-15-15 ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: NPK provides three main foods crops need to thrive: Nitrogen builds green leaves, Phosphorus builds strong roots, and Potassium helps the crop fight off diseases and form big grains or fruits.
ga: NPK haa niyenii titrii etɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara: Nitrogen feɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji loo aduawai.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when crops are actively growing—typically 2 to 3 weeks after seeds sprout when young roots can reach it, and again just before flowering when the plant needs extra energy to produce fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ beni tsei lɛ miida waa, bei pii lɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi bibii lɛ ebashɛ shi lɛ. Ni okɛfata he ekoŋŋ dani ewo fɔfɔi beni tso lɛ he miihia hewalɛ kroko koni ewo yibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains act as living umbrellas, creating cool shade and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What will happen to my cassava yield if I plant the sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This starves the plants, leading to thin stems and very small tubers compared to well-spaced crops.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii waa kɛ akɛto tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start sowing seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rainy season settles with two or three heavy, soaking rains. Sowing after just one light shower tricks the seed into sprouting, only for the young roots to die in dry soil when rains pause.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shishifãi bibii pɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme midday heat, prolonged dry spells, or lack of soil food. The plant sheds flowers to save its own life when conditions are too harsh to nourish fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala beni shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I give my field plenty of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops sometimes turn yellow and wilt right after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops get stressed when chemicals are mixed too strong or sprayed under the hot afternoon sun. Chemical burn happens when the leaves absorb concentrated liquid too quickly, so it is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening using the correct measurement.
ga: Tsei lɛ haoɔ kɛji akɛ tsofai futu mli waa tsɔ loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsofa shãa baa kɛji baai lɛ shwie nu ni mli eyi obɔ oya tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ susumɔi ni ja atsu nii ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Is it safe to spray chemical medicine on my crops while they are flowering?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Spraying during flowering can kill or chase away bees and insects that help turn flowers into fruits. It is better to wait until flowering finishes or spray late in the day when pollinating insects are no longer active.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe loo ashwie ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ aduawai lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi fɔfɔii lɛ baagbe naa loo oooshwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni pollinators lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How long must I wait after spraying pest medicine before I can harvest my crops to sell at the market?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie shi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ makpã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Every farm chemical has a required waiting period, usually between 3 to 14 days depending on the product. Harvesting too soon leaves chemical residues on the produce that can make consumers sick and degrade crop quality.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ be ni akɛmɛɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ nibii ni adu lɛ amli ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ he ajɔ amɛ ni efite nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Why is my farm land producing less harvest today than it did when our elders farmed it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe be mli ni wɔ onukpai lɛ ŋmɔ nɔ afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous planting on the same piece of land without leaving it to rest or adding organic matter drains the soil of its natural food. Over time, heavy rain washes away the rich topsoil, making the ground weaker than in past generations.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ashiuuu lɛ loo akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, ebaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ fe yinɔi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use animal manure and decayed leaves instead of buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi kɛ baai ni egboi atsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni jara wa lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, animal manure and compost add rich nutrients and help the soil hold water much better than chemical fertilizers alone. While organic matter takes longer to show results, it builds long-term soil strength without damaging the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii babaoo fataa he ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ pɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ejieɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ kpo moŋ. Shi emaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and feel sticky during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are caused by tiny pests like mealybugs or whiteflies that multiply in dry weather. They hide under the leaves to drink the plant's sap and leave a sugary waste that turns dark and attracts mold.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. ni fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded areas. Pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm, which stops the fungus from growing and destroying healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ada ni efite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from lack of water or from a pest attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua amɛ?

english: Drought causes entire leaves to roll up or droop during the hot afternoon and recover by night. Pest attacks usually leave clear physical marks like tiny holes, spotty discoloration, or sticky substances on individual leaves.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe feɔ shoo gbɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ bu bibii, su ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi. yɛ baa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds properly gives each plant enough space to build thick stems and produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do weeds grow back faster when I cut them with a cutlass compared to when I use weedkiller spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya kɛ́ mikɛ dade shwie amɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Cutting weeds with a cutlass leaves their roots alive underground, allowing them to sprout new leaves quickly. Certain weedkillers travel down into the roots to kill the whole plant, though relying only on chemicals can affect soil health over time.
ga: Jwɛi ni akɛ kakla shwieɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei heei oya. Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛgbe tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii pɛ po baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some new rice seeds produce far more bags per acre than the traditional seeds I have always planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei No hewɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ kotokui babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe blema ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to produce more grain heads per plant, resist local diseases, and use soil nutrients much more efficiently than older, uncertified seeds.
ga: Atsɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ dumɔwui ayitsei babaoo aba tso fɛɛ tso nɔ. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui momo ni bɛ he odaseyeli.

english: Why are my rice plants growing very tall with lush green leaves, but producing very few grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ dumɔwui fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage with low grain output usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or lacks phosphorus, causing the plant to put its energy into growing leaves instead of flowering and setting grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe tsei ni fa fe nine kɛ dumɔwui ni faaa lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo phosphorus bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Why do the seeds I save from a high-yielding harvest produce smaller yields when I plant them again the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni midu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yielding crop varieties are hybrids whose superior traits fade after the first generation, meaning saved seeds lose their vigor and produce weaker plants compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo ji tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ yɔɔ mli ni sɛɛ foɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my seeds closer together on my one acre of land, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ acre kome nɔ lɛ, ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, weak stalks and a smaller overall harvest than if they were properly spaced.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Ni ŋmaa lɛ faaa fe kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my field yield fewer bags of crops every year even though I am using the exact same farming methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? He ni mikɛ okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, causing the land to tire out unless you rotate crops or add compost and manure.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ efite. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why is standing water important for my rice crops during the early stages of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ lolo yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Maintaining shallow standing water smothers competing weeds, keeps the soil moist, and protects the young rice roots from extreme heat so the plants can grow quickly.
ga: nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni obu omɔ shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he Koni tsei lɛ adara oya

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer at different times instead of putting all of it in the ground when I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Crops feed differently as they grow; early fertilizer builds strong roots and stems, while later applications supply the necessary energy for the plant to form heavy, full grains.
ga: Akɛ niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa baa. yɛ be mli ni sɛɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo dumɔwui ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties remain healthy during an insect outbreak while neighboring farms get destroyed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii baa lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties have built-in natural defenses, such as tougher stalks or leaves that insects dislike, allowing them to resist pests that attack standard crop varieties.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe, tamɔ tsei loo baai ni mli wa ni kooloi sumɔɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei srɔtoi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing during short dry spells even if I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpa shweremɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ miha amɛ nu fioo po.

english: Light watering only wets the top layer of soil, encouraging roots to stay shallow where they burn easily; deep watering pushes roots deeper down to access cooler, hidden moisture.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ hei ni amɛshãa oya lɛ. Nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛshɛ fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ he.

english: How can I be sure a new crop variety will grow well in my local soil before I invest my money in it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mimaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ mishika awo mli?

english: You can verify if the seed is certified for your specific region, consult your local agricultural extension officer, or test the new variety on a small portion of your farm before planting your entire field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji akɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ahe odaseyeli kɛha okpokpaa pɔtɛɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. aloo aka ŋmeii heei akwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã bibioo ko mli dani adu jɛmɛ fɛɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong stalks. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the growth stage helps fix this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni edara lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cowpea root systems have tiny round bumps on them, and are they harming my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Those small bumps are called root nodules and they are actually very good for your crop. They contain beneficial bacteria that convert nitrogen gas from the air into plant food, which fertilizes both your cowpeas and the soil for future crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ root nodules, ni yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni tsakeɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ewoɔ tsei aniyenii mli lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsinabii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rains during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in soaked soil because standing water starves the roots of oxygen, allowing fungal diseases to grow. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root system.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa wala yibii lɛ anáa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits split open while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitswa be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs split when a dry spell is followed by sudden heavy watering or rainfall. The plant absorbs water quickly, forcing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than its skin can stretch. Giving your plants steady, regular water prevents this.
ga: Abɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ tswaa kɛ́ nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa trukaa lɛ nyiɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nu oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden dry soil conditions. Watering your plants consistently at the root level during hot spells helps save the flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na dɔlɛ haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa shihilɛi. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of small flowers, but only a few of them turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many unused flowers because they rely on tiny insects called midges for pollination. Dry winds, lack of humidity, or low midge populations prevent pollination, causing unfertilized flowers to fall off.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni akɛtsuuu nii ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ pollination gnats, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo gbɔmɛi ayibɔ ni faaa. Tsi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to cut away extra suckers from around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-plantain tso titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo plantain tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall and slender with only a few pods at the very top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Okra plants grow tall and thin when planted too close together because they are competing for sunlight. Giving your okra plants enough space between rows allows light to reach all sides, encouraging them to branch out and produce more pods.
ga: Rosella tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Ha okra tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ateŋ koni la ashɛ he fɛɛ he. Wo okra tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niji ajie ehe kpo ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Yam vines need their leaves lifted toward the sun to make food efficiently, which is what expands the tuber underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp soil, reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ji shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa helai baa shi

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning thick and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on leaf juices. Spraying early with recommended insecticidal soap or neem oil protects the leaves and keeps the plant growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key food plant leaves need to stay green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Treating the crop early for small pests stops the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Koni ana kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baakpa baa ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotting at the bottom before they get red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛmiitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi waa, ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves. Sunlight gives the plant energy to build large, heavy tubers underground; without stakes, leaves stay shaded and produce smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baaná hulutsoo ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii.

english: Should I cut away the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for water and food, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only the main stem, one medium follower, and one small shoot gives you the biggest fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ tso titri lɛ pɛ. Follower kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ tso bibioo kome baaha oná yibii ni da fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass on top of the soil around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the earth too fast, keeps soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can pull natural food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it into the ground. This feeds the soil and helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger without extra fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni akɛ ŋmãa kroko fataaa he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same patch of ground where I just harvested peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he ni mifo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and feed on the same nutrients while attracting the same ground diseases. Planting them back-to-back lets pests and diseases build up in the soil.
ga: Tomato kɛ pepper yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome shi amɛgbalaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. Look for signs like the lower leaves falling off naturally and visible cracks forming in the soil right around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Taomɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmeii ni anaa ni eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot feed, but excessive flower drop happens when there is a dry spell, insect attacks on young flowers, or a lack of small midges (tiny insects) to pollinate them.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko yɛ. Kplukai komɛi yɛ ni tutuaa fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. aloo kooloi bibii (kooloi bibii) ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why should I cover my harvested produce in containers instead of touching them directly with my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-fruits kɛ aduawai ni mikpa lɛ awo tsɛnsii amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ miniji baata he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Bare hands carry moisture and tiny germs that cause rot when transferred to fresh crops. Keeping produce in covered containers protects it from dust, bacteria, and pests, helping it stay clean and fresh for market.
ga: Niji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai bibii. No haa egboɔ kɛ́ ajie kɛtee tsei heei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni adu lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu he kɛjɛ sũ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe tseɔ ni efeɔ ehee kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn dark inside just a few days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living plant parts that quickly react to air once removed from the soil. This natural reaction causes internal discoloration and spoilage within 48 hours unless the roots are processed or kept submerged in water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji tso lɛ fãi ni hiɛ ka ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsuɔ nii oya kɛji ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa mligbɛ su lɛ tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli ja atsu shishifãi lɛ ahe nii loo akɛwo nu mli.

english: Why is it important to keep my stored maize covered tightly in containers in the shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ato nibii ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Open storage allows humid air and insects to reach the grain. Keeping maize tightly covered prevents moisture from causing mold and stops storage pests from laying eggs in the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ ni agbele naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ oha ŋmãa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee ŋmãa, ni ebaaha ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ akawo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do market buyers offer me a very low price for my peppers even when they look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ haa mi-peppers lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ peppers lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Buyers check for firmness, moisture levels, and soft spots. If peppers are bruised during harvest or stored in heat, they soften quickly and ruin food preparation, which lowers their market price.
ga: Mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ha lɛ Moisture levels kɛ hei ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya ni efiteɔ hesaamɔ. Enɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and rot fast instead of ripening slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni akpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ fiofio lɛ?

english: Plantains release ethylene gas as they ripen. Rough handling, direct sunlight, or storing them in tight, hot spaces causes them to produce extra gas, making them ripen too quickly and spoil.
ga: Kɛ́ ahoɔ tsei lɛ, amɛjieɔ ethylene gas. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, loo akɛto he ko ni mli wa ni mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaha gas lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the crop lacks nitrogen nutrients from the soil or that waterlogged roots cannot breathe properly to absorb food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu koni amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, shady conditions and destroys the cocoa beans inside the pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft black spots at the bottom before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ shishigbɛ dani edɔ kwraa?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to irregular watering during fruit formation.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds end up full of small holes after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay eggs inside the pods in the field or in storage. As the young insects grow, they eat their way out of the seed, leaving hollow holes.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ pods amli yɛ ŋmɔji amli loo he ni akɛ nibii toɔ. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii dara lɛ Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of straight and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, stony, or compacted soil underground. Soil needs to be loose and deep to allow the tuber to expand straight downward.
ga: Sweet potato lɛ yitso tsɔ beni etswa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. tɛi loo ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees during their first few years to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes tall, weak stems and very small or empty cobs instead of a healthy harvest.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Mi lɛ yɛ baa ko mli

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. These caterpillars feed on young maize leaves and central shoots, which stops the plant from growing properly if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing it for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my crops still need fertilizer even if my farm soil looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: Dark soil shows rich organic matter, but specific heavy-feeding plants like maize still require high amounts of key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that dark soil alone may not supply in sufficient quantities.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ jieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kpo. Shi titri lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, biɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo lolo. Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ pɛ faaa yɛ bɔ ni sa mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which is stored underground as tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ tuber Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?
