english: Cassava plants signal maturity around 9 to 12 months when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young cassava crop even if the soil has plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young cassava plants and steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, preventing the young cassava roots from expanding properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni no haa ŋmei shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some plantain suckers grow into strong plants quickly while others stay weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Sword suckers with narrow leaves and a large underground base have strong food reserves and grow fast, whereas water suckers with broad leaves have weak bases and grow slowly.
ga: Nɛkɛ sucker ni baai lɛ mli tseee kɛ shishitoo agbo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nɛɛ yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni ekɛtoɔ ni edaa oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ yɛ shishitoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get brown patches and curl up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like blight. Rain splashing soil onto leaves allows fungal spores to spread and destroy the plant's leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do my crops start wilting and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need a continuous supply of water to take up nutrients from the soil to their leaves. During the dry season, high temperatures cause water to evaporate quickly from both the ground and the plant leaves, causing the crops to lose strength, wilt, and stop growing unless extra water is provided.
ga: Tsei hia nu daa koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya baai lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ja nu kroko fata he.

english: Why does rain fall on farms in nearby communities but skips my own farm entirely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ akutsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shi amɛhoɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rain clouds during dry or transitional seasons are often small and localized, meaning they dump water on small areas before dissipating. Relying only on this unpredictable rainfall makes farming risky, which is why having an independent water source on your farm helps protect your investment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ atatui ni nɛɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be loo tsakemɔ be mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshiɔ nu yɛ he bibioo ko. dani egbɛ eshwa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ pɛ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔɔ lɛ haa okwaayeli feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni nu jɛɛhe ko ni yɔɔ ehe ni oyɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he lɛ.

english: How will buying a water pump actually help my crops grow better during the dry months?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp ni miheɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: A water pump allows you to draw water directly from a nearby river, stream, or borehole to your field whenever it does not rain. This keeps the soil constantly moist so your crops can continue growing, flowering, and bearing fruit even when there is no rainfall.
ga: Nu pɔmp haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu shwieɔ faa, faa loo nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my farm using a pump?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ pɔmp baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: The best times to water your crops are early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Watering during these cooler hours allows the soil to absorb the moisture deep into the root zone before the harsh midday heat can evaporate it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi loo shwane. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani gbi lɛ mli la ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Will investing in a farm pump give me better financial returns during harvest?
ga: Ani shika ni akɛwoɔ pɔmpi ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha shika ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Yes, because irrigating your farm allows you to produce crops during the dry season when most rain-fed farms cannot produce. Harvesting during periods of scarcity means you can sell your produce at much higher market prices.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛshwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ owo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Okwaafoi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ amɛwo nibii. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni nibii faaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough water when the rains stop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: You can dig a few inches into the soil around your crop roots; if the soil is dry and crumbles easily, your plants need water. Plants also show thirst through drooping leaves, yellowing leaf tips, or stunted growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔle he. Tso shishifãi ni ji inchi fioo komɛi Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni efoɔ oya Nu he miihia Otsei lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ ajie kumai he okadii hu kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni egbee shi, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is there a way to keep the soil moist for my crops without watering every day?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni awooo amɛ nu daa gbi?

english: Yes, you can cover the bare ground around your crop roots with dried grass, straw, or dry leaves—a practice called mulching. The mulch acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, reducing evaporation and keeping water in the soil much longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egboi awo otsei lɛ ashishi. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out faster than the soil on other farms after a short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Different soil types hold water differently. Sandy soil has large particles that allow water to drain away very quickly, whereas clay or loamy soil holds moisture much longer. Adding organic compost or farmyard manure to sandy soil helps it trap and hold water like a sponge.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ henɔ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ toɔ nu ehaa. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii wuji ni haa nu hoɔ oya waa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sũ loo sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi tamɔ sponji.

english: Which crops can survive best on my farm when there is very little rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and deep-rooted legumes like cowpeas naturally handle heat and low moisture better than water-hungry crops like tomatoes or maize. They are well-suited for dry periods when water is limited.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni shishifãi mli kwɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmãa baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ tomato loo ŋmãa. Ehi kɛha bei ni nu lɛ mli egbi ni faaa lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, stopping moisture from escaping into the hot air.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can capture sunlight and produce full ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la ni ewo baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava roots if I plant cassava on the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a large amount of food nutrients out of the soil to grow its big tubers. Repeating the crop on the same land drains the soil, so resting the land or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas helps replenish nutrients for future harvests.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni ji enyɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides crucial shade and keeps the air humid while the seedlings mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall without making big cobs if I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room to gather nutrients and produce heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa ni ekɛfee ŋmei ni tsii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the inner leaves of my young maize during warm weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ amli yɛ otsii ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that multiplies quickly in warm weather and targets the tender center leaves of maize. Checking your crops regularly and applying recommended biological or chemical treatments early saves the young shoots.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fɔɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Kwɛmɔ onibii amli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my pepper plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Should I plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular because the first single rain is often followed by a long dry stretch. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then dry up before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants turn soft and dark when rainwater sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water sits on the soil surface for long periods, it drowns the roots and creates wet conditions where harmful soil diseases rot the root system.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa he ni shikpɔŋ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ

english: If I cut off some of the lower branches from my tomato plants, will it hurt my crop yield?
ga: Kɛ mifo tomato tso ko niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ, Ani ebaana bɔ ni miwoɔ nii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves and wild side shoots actually improves your yield because it directs the plant's food supply toward building bigger fruits instead of useless foliage, while also keeping leaves off the damp soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji afeemɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni oookɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni niyenii tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the growing center of the plant. Inspecting the field early helps you spot them before they destroy the crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I leave recommended distances between my cassava cuttings when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Spacing cassava properly ensures that the roots under the ground have enough room to expand into large tubers without competing with neighbor plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kasava ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants drooping and dying even when the ground is full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays waterlogged for too long, plant roots cannot breathe and begin to rot. This root rot stops the plant from taking up water properly, causing it to wilt as if it were dry.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. ni haa egbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight the main tree for light and nutrients. Keeping only one main shoot and one small follower ensures the tree puts its energy into producing large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ awuu koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei titri kome pɛ kɛ esɛɛnyiɛlɔ bibioo kome pɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite hewalɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my field when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop seedlings and steal essential water, light, and nutrients. Clearing them early prevents young crops from becoming stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ akafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable beds with dry leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun rays. This keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture so you do not have to water as often.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ.

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to grow downward easily. Hard or stony soil stops the roots from expanding smoothly, so forming high mounds or ridges gives them soft earth to grow big and straight.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ adara ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the corn plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Corn needs plenty of nitrogen to grow healthy and green, so adding balanced fertilizer like NPK or well-decayed manure around the stems helps restore their color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same farm make my maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt. When planted together, the groundnuts naturally fertilize the soil for the maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu Peanuts yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during the heavy rains. Pruning extra branches to allow sunlight and airflow through your farm helps dry out the trees and prevent the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kpojiemɔ kroko ni fata he koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by them. Spraying the underside of the leaves with neem oil mixture or an approved insecticide protects the leaves from being damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ efutu baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do tiny insects start attacking my cowpea pods as soon as the flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ shishi amɛtutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and soft young pods produce sweet juices that attract pod-boring insects. Protecting your crop requires applying recommended pest treatments right at the start of flowering before the insects lay eggs inside the pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni gbalaa kooloi ni hiɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ooobu lɛ biɔ ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ayeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Dani kooloo lɛ baawo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away, suffocating the roots and attracting fungal diseases. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni efooo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be weakened by underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Staking mature trees with sturdy bamboo poles and planting clean suckers keeps the roots strong against wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fĩɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulching helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulching ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. The sunlight allows the vine to manufacture food that goes down into the ground to build big, heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing very big leaves but failing to form a hard head in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form firm heads if they get too much nitrogen late in their growth or if the weather is too hot. Giving them balanced feed early on and growing them during cooler months encourages the leaves to wrap tightly into a head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa blɛoo lɛ loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni ahaa amɛ mra kɛ dalɛ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baawo baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ yitso lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to stay green. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the energy it needs to build healthy green leaves and big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo mli loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo baai ŋmɔji ni mli wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts on my farm help the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. When you harvest them, that trapped plant food stays in the soil to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni okpaa lɛ Tse niyenii ni akɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: What is eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended pesticides or neem oil extracts directly into the leaf whorls stops them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant sap and spreading diseases. Spraying the plants with neem leaf juice or suitable insecticides controls these bugs and allows normal leaves to grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua baa ni sa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantain or cassava act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can reach full sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛhe tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da kwraa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong rains when they are carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep, and heavy bunches make the tree top-heavy and easy for wind to push over. Supporting the stems with bamboo poles or strong wooden Y-sticks prevents them from snapping or uprooting before the fruit ripens.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ nɔ ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ ewoɔ lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee dani aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around them because roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and planting heat-resistant tomato varieties helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tomato henɔi ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ adumɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Watermelons crack open when heavy rains arrive suddenly after a dry period, causing the fruit to soak up water and expand faster than its skin can stretch. Watering your crop evenly throughout the dry season prevents this sudden cracking.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ nu ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni eshishifã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbala trukaa.

english: Why do I need to apply fertilizer to my maize crop at different stages instead of putting it all in the soil on the day I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ gbi ni miduɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need different types and amounts of food as they grow, just like growing children. Applying fertilizer in stages ensures young plants get what they need for early root development, while later applications support cob growth without wasting fertilizer.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛji amɛmiida. Taakɛ gbekɛ ni miida lɛ ji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ náa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua cob lɛ ni eda ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afiteee.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain plant, they compete for water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce a big, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii dara kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need direct sunlight to produce food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from ground fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again and grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop leaves during severe drought to protect themselves from losing water through their leaves. Once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh leaves and continue building tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ baai heei ni efee bulbs.

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees provides a cool shelter that keeps the soil moist and protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ haa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my ripening tomato fruits split open right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miikwɛ̃ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden surge of water after a dry spell, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin can stretch. Regular, even watering prevents this cracking.
ga: Tomatoi baatswa kɛji amɛná nu ni fa trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nu ni oooha lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akatse nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ.

english: Curled, distorted leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids that suck the juices out of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading viruses that stop the plant from bearing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbɛɔ helai ni haaa tsei awo yibii lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and will aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer when the plant is young gives it the strength to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni sa fata he beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my land for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aye ehe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil, making the earth richer for crops like maize or cassava planted next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa je lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get easily scorched by full sunlight. Big trees act like umbrellas that shade the young cocoa, keeping the soil damp and protecting the leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei wuji lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baadara ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them because they cannot breathe flooded soil. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets dry suddenly. Giving the plants consistent water at their roots and keeping the soil covered with grass mulch keeps them cool enough to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ egbi trukaa. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects hiding under the leaves and sucking the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or natural neem tree liquid helps drive those pests away so new leaves grow flat.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ mra Nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni jɛ neem tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ashwie nakai kooloi lɛ kɛya. koni ekɛfee baai heei lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I wait to clear weeds until after they have grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛji mimɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii kɛyashi ebaada lɛ?

english: Weeds steal food, water, and sunlight from your crops while they are small and struggling to grow. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks gives your crops a strong start so they can produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ kpamɔ wulu ko shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground, so a heavy bunch makes the tree top-heavy. Placing strong, tall wooden sticks under the stem to support the weight keeps the tree upright until the plantains are ready to harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsɔne ni akɛfiɔ lɛ ni tsii waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee nɔ ni tsii. Tso kakadaŋŋ ni wa ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛfi etsitsinɔnii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do I need to clear vines and put tall wooden sticks for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie wain tsei lɛ ni mikɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ awo mli koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves away from damp ground where diseases spread easily.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing very large leaves but refusing to form a tight, round head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai wuji waa shi eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni yitso ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo ahi teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather is too warm or if they get too much nitrogen food all at once. Planting them during cooler periods and watering them regularly helps the leaves fold inward properly.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ ebɔŋ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha lɛ yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ, ni ashwieɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe kɛya mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding well-rotted chicken manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season gives the crop the energy it needs to grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: How does adding animal manure to my field help my crops survive when the rains stop early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It holds onto water from the rains much longer, giving your crop roots access to moisture even during unexpected dry spells.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehiɛɔ nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe nakai. Enɛ haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa nu yɛ hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ po amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and full yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big green leaves on top but small tuber roots inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of root growth. Crops need balanced nutrients and loose, well-tilled soil so the tubers can expand properly underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ he miihia tsei. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear inside the heart of my young maize plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on young maize leaves right as the season starts, and these hatch into worms like Fall Armyworm. Checking the central leaves early allows you to catch and manage them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni be lɛ je shishi Ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or viruses they spread. Controlling these pests early prevents them from stunt-ing your plants and stopping fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ mites loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee mɛi ni egbɔjɔ ni amɛbaakpa aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why does sorghum stay green and survive on my farm during dry periods while my maize wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deeper roots and leaf features that lock in water, making it naturally resistant to heat and dry conditions compared to maize, which needs more consistent moisture.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni emɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni biɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers on top but the nuts mature under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant grows long stalks called 'pegs' that push themselves down into the soil, where the nuts safely form away from hot sun and surface pests.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ewo ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ 'pegs' ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe jɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it bad to burn the weeds and grass on my farm before making yam ridges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani adu sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial earthworms and burns away organic matter that feeds the soil. Leaving cleared grass to decompose enriches the soil structure, helping yams grow larger tubers.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni ekwɛɔ yitsei wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to pull up enough water. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to shield them from the sun until they are established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he kɛyashi amɛbaatswa amɛhe shi.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves droop and look weak in the afternoon heat even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbɔjɔɔɔ moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Under strong afternoon heat, plants lose water into the air through their leaves faster than roots can pull it from the ground. The plant temporarily droops to conserve moisture and will usually bounce back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Heavy rains often wash away nitrogen, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen lɛ shwiemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cowpea crop have plenty of thick green leaves but almost no seed pods growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni dumɔwui ŋmɔji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Alternatively, tiny pests might be eating the flower buds before they can develop into pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the crop early with insecticidal soap or neem oil helps protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani ebafeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or attacks from sucking insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ adɛŋ Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without draining away, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Ehaa shihilɛi ni sa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my swamp rice crop grow much better when there is standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa beni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers competing weeds that would otherwise steal light and nutrients from the rice, while creating the flooded environment that swamp rice roots prefer for nutrient absorption.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni baanyɛ aju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baa ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for the leaves to manufacture food, which feeds the growing underground tuber. Vines left on the ground are also more vulnerable to soil diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni baai lɛ afee niyenii. ni haa niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ Wein tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil. Underground root pests, like banana weevils or nematodes, can also destroy roots and make the plant top-heavy and weak.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo nematodes Ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ ni eha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings will not sprout if they are planted upside down, if the stem cuttings used were dry and old, or if the soil is too hard and dry for the young roots to push through.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii ji niji ni egbi kɛ niji ni egbɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key food plant uses to stay green and strong. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii tsei titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and produce less food if I plant maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planted in the same spot every season, maize eats the exact same soil nutrients over and over until the ground becomes empty. Planting beans or groundnuts in between seasons puts good food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi, ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shii abɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ be mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii kpakpa baa. Ku osɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Covering soil with dried grass, called mulching, acts like a shade cloth for the earth. It keeps the hot sun from drying out water in the soil, keeps roots cool, and stops weeds from stealing plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ mama ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the top leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide in the soft center leaves of maize where it is cool. They eat the growing tips, which damages the plant's ability to produce healthy corn cobs later.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii baai bibii amli yɛ hei ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they feel too hot or do not get enough water. When the plant gets stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy so the main stem stays alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji edɔ amɛ tsɔ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ tsei lɛ miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he koni eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam leaves need lots of sunlight to make food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the earth so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all end up weak with small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot sun wastes water because the heat evaporates it into the air before roots can drink it. Cool morning or evening watering allows water to sink deep into the soil where roots can draw it in slowly.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ nu ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nu ni oooha yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baaha nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu fiofio lɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage leaves turning yellow and dropping off before they form a firm head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages are heavy feeders that require plenty of nitrogen and consistent moisture. Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks key nutrients or that the plants are experiencing water stress.
ga: Cabbage ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ.

english: Is it safe for people to eat leafy vegetables like cabbage directly from my farm without cooking them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ gbɔmɛi baaye aduawai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kaabe kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mihooo?

english: Raw vegetables offer high nutritional value, but they must be washed thoroughly with clean water before eating to remove farm dirt, bacteria, and any chemical residues from pest treatments.
ga: Aduawai ni ahoko lɛ yɛ hewalɛ waa. Shi esa akɛ akɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ he jogbaŋŋ dani aye. Koni ajie ŋmɔ mli muji, helatsɛmɛi kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young fruit trees drop their flowers and small fruits before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miifɔlɔi kɛ amɛyibii bibii lɛ miifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruit drop usually happens when a tree is stressed by hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like potassium during the early fruiting stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ yɛ yibiiwoo shishijee bei amli.

english: What can I do to make my pineapples and watermelons taste sweeter for fruit juice production?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni anana kɛ watermelon afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha juis feemɔ?

english: Fruits build up natural sugars through full sunlight exposure, properly timed watering, and adequate potassium in the soil as they ripen.
ga: Yibii buaa sugar naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Nu taakɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I mix animal dung into the farm soil instead of using only chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu ŋmɔ mli sũ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Animal dung builds organic matter in the soil, helping it hold water longer and feeding the crop slowly over time, whereas chemical fertilizers only provide quick nutrients without improving the soil structure.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi feɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya pɛ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my traditional crop varieties giving lower yields compared to how they used to perform years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishijee tsei srɔtoi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Over time, planting the same crop repeatedly on the same land drains the soil of specific nutrients, causing yields to drop unless organic matter or crop rotation is restored.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. ja aku sɛɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from a plant disease or if they just lack plant food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tsei ahe hela loo tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: A lack of plant food usually causes even yellowing or pale color across entire leaves, while diseases often cause dark spots, irregular patches, or leaf curling on specific parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa baa muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ŋmeii diji, ŋmeii, loo baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa tso lɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ.

english: Why do my green vegetable plants go straight to flower and seed instead of producing big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei eŋɔli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo baai wuji lɛ?

english: This behavior is called 'bolting,' which happens when plants get stressed by high temperatures or dry periods, forcing them to produce seeds early to reproduce before dying.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ ‘bolting’ ni ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo dumɔwui oya bɔni afee ni amɛfɔ dani amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops wither during the heat of the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu wo mli leebi?

english: High daytime heat causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can absorb it from the soil. Placing grass or dry leaves around the base of the plants keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during dry spells than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather speeds up insect breeding cycles, and plants become weaker from water stress, making it easier for pests to feed on them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii oya. ni tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii

english: How should I prepare a small piece of land before I put my crops in the ground?
ga: Esa akɛ osaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. Dani abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, te afeɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: To prepare a small plot, clear away weeds and bushes, dig up the soil to loosen it so plant roots can grow easily, and break up large dirt clumps to make a smooth bed for seeds.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko he saamɔ mli Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni oha egbɔjɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. ni agbala sũi wuji amli koni afee dumɔwui ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: My farmland holds a lot of water right now; can I still grow crops on it?
ga: Miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo amrɔ nɛɛ. Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ nɔ lolo?

english: Yes, waterlogged land can grow crops, but you should make raised soil mounds or beds so the plant roots do not rot, or grow crops like vegetables and rice that handle wet conditions well.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi esa akɛ ofee gɔŋ loo saatso ni awo nɔ koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akafite. Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmãa ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I keep my crops alive when my wet land starts to dry out in the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi beni mihei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can trap moisture in the soil by covering the ground around plants with dry leaves or straw (mulching), and use small channels to collect remaining groundwater for watering.
ga: Obaanyɛ omɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) baawo mli lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii atsu nii. Koni abua shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni eshwɛ lɛ naa koni akɛshwie nɔ.

english: Can I plant my crops at any time of the year, or is there a specific season I must follow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu tsei yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Aloo ani bei komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: Most crops need to be planted at specific times, usually at the start of the rains, so they get enough moisture to build strong roots before dry weather sets in.
ga: Ehe miihia ni adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nugbɔ lɛ shishijee. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Is animal manure good for my land, and how does it help my crops grow?
ga: Ani kooloi ashikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural plant food and helps the ground hold water longer, which makes crops grow stronger and produce better yields.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Should I put animal manure on my farm before planting or after my seeds have sprouted?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu loo beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to mix animal manure into the soil a few weeks before planting so it breaks down and enriches the dirt without burning tender young plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani adu. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eshãaa tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I cut parts of my growing crops to feed my chickens without killing the plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii ni migbeee tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, you can trim lower leaves or leafy shoots of certain forage crops to feed poultry, as long as you leave the main stem and top leaves intact so the plant keeps growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ ekomɛi ashishi baai loo amɛshishifãi koni okɛha kooloi niyenii. Shii abɔ ni obaashi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni tso lɛ aya nɔ eda.

english: What care do my crop sprouts need as soon as they emerge from the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ he hiaa mi tso dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Newly sprouted crops need protection from weeds that steal sunlight and water, as well as light soil stirring around them to help air reach their young roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ahe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni juɔ hulu la kɛ nu lɛ ahe. Tamɔ diatomaceous shikpɔŋ ni atswaa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ. Koni eye ebua kɔɔyɔɔ ni eshɛ shishifãi ni darako lolo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds sprout faster than others on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli

english: Seeds sprout at different speeds depending on how deep they were planted, how much water that spot received, and the natural differences in seed strength.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ bɔ ni adu lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ nɔ. nu abɔ ni anáa kɛ adebɔɔ mli srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ mli.

english: How can I get the best yield from a small plot of land if space is limited?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ana sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? Kɛji akɛ he ko faaa?

english: You can maximize a small plot by enriching the soil with manure, keeping proper distance between plants, and choosing fast-growing crops that can be harvested multiple times.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibioo ko dalɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi shi. Ni halamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni abaanyɛ akpa shii abɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can test your farm by carefully digging up one plant to check if the tubers have reached a good size before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ oka oŋmɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooofo mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dalɛ sa dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does cassava seem to grow and survive even in dry or poor soil on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a very hardy crop with deep root systems that store water and nutrients effectively. This allows it to withstand long dry spells and poor soils where other sensitive crops would die.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni wa waa ni eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enyɛɔ edamɔ bei ni nu bɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagboi yɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sun. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees to shield them from excessive heat and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How should I select the best cassava stem cuttings to plant on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always cut stems from healthy, mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from leaf disease. Choose thick, woody stems from the middle portion of the plant with visible buds for the best germination.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni bɛ ŋmeii ahe hela ko lɛ amli. Halamɔ tso tso ni mli tse. Kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmeii ni anaa kɛha shweremɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava with young cocoa is common because the cassava provides vital shade to the young cocoa trees while yielding food early. However, space them well so the fast-growing cassava does not completely choke the cocoa plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei haa ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmei mra. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ akatsi kookoo tso lɛ naa tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start turning dark and spoiling just a few days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifee diŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots rapidly lose moisture and react with oxygen in the air, causing internal spoilage within 48 to 72 hours. To avoid loss, process or sell your cassava immediately after digging it up.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Ha mligbɛ fitemɔ aba yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli koni akafite. Okɛ o-cassava lɛ atsu nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ogbe naa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has the right soil for growing cocoa successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ ni yeɔ omanye?

english: Cocoa trees thrive in deep, dark, well-drained soil rich in organic material that holds moisture without getting flooded. If water stays pooled on your field for days after heavy rains, cocoa roots will rot.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu afua baaa mli. Kɛji nu tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ Cocoa shishifãi baanyɛ agbo.

english: Curled and discolored leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant varieties is the best way to protect your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛhe su tsakeɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Heavy flower drop can also happen if the tree lacks water, fertilizer, or suffers from pest damage.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ pollin lɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji nu, ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ.

english: Why should I buy improved cassava varieties instead of using the traditional stems from my old farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ moŋ fe blema ŋmeii ni jɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties developed by agricultural scientists grow faster, resist common local diseases better, and yield significantly larger roots per acre compared to older, unimproved traditional varieties.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni fa babaoo yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ ni asaaa lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn dry and brown, the silks at the top of the cob turn dark brown, and the kernels become hard when pressed with a fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ nineshi ŋmei mimɔ nɔ.

english: How many months does it take for improved cassava varieties to mature after planting?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduɔ ŋmei?

english: Improved cassava varieties in Ghana typically take 9 to 12 months to mature, which is faster than traditional varieties that can take up to 15 to 18 months.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛshwereɔ. Enɛ yaa oya fe blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni baanyɛ ahé nyɔji 15 kɛyashi 18 lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?
