english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and plant nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from one another, resulting in weak plants and lower yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Dropping leaves during a dry spell is cassava's natural way of saving water to survive drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves.
ga: Baai ni ashiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei.

english: My tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into fruit. What is happening?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii. meni ba?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off without forming fruit when temperatures are too high, when the soil lacks enough water, or when there are no bees and insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ. shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and misshapen instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil or high mounds to expand smoothly. If the soil is hard, compact, or filled with rocks, the tubers cannot grow straight and become stunted or deformed.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Tubers lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ loo amɛhe efee shoo.

english: Why do my maize plants stay pale green or yellow even after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away nitrogen from the soil, which is the nutrient responsible for making leaves dark green and strong. Adding fertilizer or compost will restore their health.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agricultural office yield more than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and bred to resist common local diseases, withstand weather changes, and grow uniformly, whereas saved seeds lose vigor and yield potential over time.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni edaa daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do crops like tomatoes and yams need wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ sweet potato he hiaa tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Certain crops have weak stems that cannot support heavy fruits or vines on their own. Staking lifts the plant off the moist ground, which prevents fruit rot, reduces pest attacks, and helps leaves catch more sunlight to grow bigger fruits.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ aduawai wuji loo wain tsei anɔ. Staking woɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akafite. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo koni eha aduawai lɛ adara.

english: When is the best time for me to start staking my crops in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to stake early, usually when the crops are young or just starting to send out vines. Staking early prevents you from accidentally damaging the plant's roots later when they spread deep into the soil.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ ohe awo mli mra. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ loo ebɔi wain tsei shwiemɔ kɛkɛ. Ni ooohi shi mra Ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ oshara mli yɛ sɛɛ mli beni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the high afternoon heat even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it usually bounces back once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of green leaves but fail to produce fruits or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo aduawai loo aduawai ko lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen makes the plant focus all its energy on growing long stems and leaves instead of flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why do young crops require so much more attention and care in their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In their first year, plants have small, shallow root systems that cannot search deep underground for water or nutrients. They are weak and easily choked by weeds or dried out by the sun until their roots are established.
ga: Yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, tsei yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ atao nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi loo hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ oya kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed the nutrients away. It can also happen if the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden heavy rainfall. It can also happen if there are no bees or insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants that produce smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are getting burned by too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: Sun-scorched plants will have leaf tips that turn brown, yellow, or dry like paper. The leaves may also curl inward to hide from direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni hulu lɛ shã amɛ lɛ baaná baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔŋ, loo egbi tamɔ wolo. Baai lɛ baanyɛ abɔle amɛhe kɛya mli koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do root crops like cassava sometimes grow short and twisted underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ yucca lɛ hiɔ shi kuku ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Roots grow twisted or shallow when the soil is too hard and compact for them to push through. Loosening the soil deep down before planting gives the roots room to expand long and straight.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi loo amɛhe ekɔɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ebote mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor's maize turn dark green just a few days after applying fertilizer, but mine takes weeks to show any change?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni awo mli ŋmãa lɛ? Shi minɔ lɛ he otsii babaoo dani ena tsakemɔ?

english: Quick-acting chemical fertilizers dissolve fast in soil water and give plants an immediate boost of nitrogen, whereas organic manure or slow-release fertilizers take time to break down before roots can drink up the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii oya lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nu mli oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa nitrogen ni amɛyeɔ lɛ babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ni tsuɔ nii blɛoo lɛ he miihia be dani shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: What are those liquid chemical boosters sold in the shop, and do they replace regular bag fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapoi amli? Ni ani ebaaye baagi mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli daa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Liquid boosters sprayed on leaves give plants a quick dose of micronutrients for fast recovery, but they do not replace ground fertilizers, which feed the main root system required to produce heavy yields.
ga: Nu ni yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii bibii ni he hiaa oya koni amɛhe wa oya. Shi ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shishifãi titrii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ ayeee najiaŋ.

english: How do my crops actually feed on fertilizer, and why can't they grow big using only rainfall and normal soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ tsei kɛ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ folo pɛ tsuuu nii kɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Crops pull minerals dissolved in ground water through their roots to build leaves and fruits; continuous farming exhausts soil nutrients over time, so fertilizer refills the soil with essential plant food.
ga: Tsei jieɔ shika tsuru ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ koni amɛfee baai kɛ aduawai. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyiɔ kɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die easily in heavy heat while cassava plants on the same land stay fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji ehee lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are delicate crops with shallow roots and soft leaves that lose water rapidly in intense heat, whereas cassava has deep roots and tough leaves designed to store moisture during hot weather.
ga: Tomato ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji edɔ waa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni afee koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray my pepper farm with protective chemicals every few weeks even when I do not see any insects on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ afɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa otsii fioo komɛi? Eyɛ mli akɛ anaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ.

english: Regular preventative spraying protects tender young growth before microscopic pests or fungal spores can attach, keeping the crop healthy before visible damage appears.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa daa lɛ baabu tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ he dani tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ he. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ dani nɔ ni anaa ni efite lɛ aba.

english: Why did the leaves of my young crops burn and turn brown after I sprayed them with pesticide on a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals in strong midday heat causes liquid drops to evaporate quickly, leaving behind concentrated chemical residues that scorch tender leaf tissues.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Eshiɔ tsofa ni eshwɛ ni shãa baa bibii lɛ ahe fãji.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take several years to bear pods while my maize crop produces food in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops like cocoa focus their first few years on building strong trunks and deep root networks for long-term survival, while seasonal crops like maize are programmed to mature, seed, and complete their lifecycle quickly.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo kwɛɔ tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛha wala be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, atoɔ be mli nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛwo dumɔwui, ni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya.

english: Why do some of my farm crops produce lots of big leaves but fail to give me good fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa shi amɛhaaa mi yibii loo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen causes them to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems, leaving no energy to develop flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ehaa amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni baaha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my green pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tso ni ji eŋɔli lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of a plant usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or root damage caused by waterlogged soil, which prevents the crop from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ efite. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does crop disease spread so much faster through my field when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ miŋmɔji amli kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting too close traps moisture between leaves and blocks sunlight, creating a warm, damp environment that allows fungal diseases and pests to spread easily from plant to plant.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baagbɛ ashwã tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and strong, so when the soil doesn't have enough, the plant pulls whatever nutrients it has left from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the fresh growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa tsei heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps make my farm soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have small bumps on their roots that host friendly bacteria. These bacteria take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil, which feeds the next crop you plant in that same spot.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni ji he ni helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ hiɔ Nɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot survive intense direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains beside them creates a canopy of shade that lowers the heat and keeps the air humid, giving the young cocoa time to grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. ni ejieɔ tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛdaraa waa.

english: Tightly curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. It can also be a sign of a plant virus spread by these same insects, which prevents the leaf from expanding normally.
ga: Baai ni ekpɛtɛ shi shiŋŋ lɛ ji kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ he okadi. Ebaanyɛ efee tso mli hela ko ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers very small even though the plant leaves grew very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given too much leaf-building fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ ŋmei babaoo wo mli koni ekɛha baai lɛ aya hiɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Every extra sucker that grows from the root competes with the main plantain stem for food, water, and sunlight. Removing the smaller suckers allows the mother tree to direct all its energy into growing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi krokomɛi fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii lɛ, ehaa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering—like going from very dry soil to flooded soil. Keeping the moisture in the soil steady helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do the roots of my crops start rotting when rainwater sits on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to stay alive. When water covers the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the ground, effectively drowning the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔji anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do I need to put up tall wood stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then sent down into the ground to build a much larger, thicker yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm crawls inside the funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on the tender young leaves before they unfold, leaving holes and frass behind as it eats.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo. Amɛshiɔ bu kɛ tsei bibii yɛ amɛsɛɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight while they are small. Without larger trees or crops like plantain to provide shade, the hot sun scorches the tender leaves and dries out the soil before the cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Kɛji tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo aba lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani kookoo lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ ni ashiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender growth, which can destroy the crop if not addressed early with proper remedies or approved sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra. kɛ tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ.

english: Does it matter which way I point a cassava stem cutting when sticking it into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ni mikɛduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, you should plant cassava stems with the tiny buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting a stem upside down forces the shoots to bend around to grow upward, resulting in weak plants and a lower harvest of tuber roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni oootsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni amɛdara. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my chemical fertilizer on dry soil during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so the plant roots can soak it up. Applying fertilizer on hot, dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer through evaporation or wind.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the bottom of my crops help them during a dry spell?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around plants with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective cover that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping your crops stay hydrated.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leafy growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baa ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting yam tubers instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abua sũ lɛ naa awo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ mli dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil so the tubers can expand easily into large, smooth shapes. Mounds also prevent rainwater from pooling around the roots, which stops the yams from rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu ni baa lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or too much water. Maintaining consistent soil moisture helps the plant retain its blossoms so fruit can grow.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side shoots growing in the corners of my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato niji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Removing those extra side shoots, called suckers, keeps the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This directs more nutrients toward producing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo aba koni ekɛwo tomato aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the very next step I should take on my farm right after planting my shade trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ?

english: After planting your shade trees, the next step is to mark out your field with pegs and prepare your land for planting temporary shade crops like plantains or transplanting your cocoa seedlings once the weather is favorable.
ga: Beni adu tsei koni ekɛha hulutsoo lɛ sɛɛ Nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ji ni okɛ ŋtayaai awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni asaa he ni aduɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tsei, tamɔ plantains, loo aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛ gbɛ.

english: Is it really possible to get my new cocoa farm properly established within just one year?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ama mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ afi kome pɛ mli?

english: Yes, if you properly clear the land, plant fast-growing shade crops early, use healthy hybrid cocoa seedlings, and manage weeds, your cocoa farm can be fully established within a single year.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ shade tsei ni daa oya lɛ mra. Kɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ atsu nii. kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ O-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ baaje shishi kwraa yɛ afi kome mli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is well-established after its first year of planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A well-established first-year farm will have a high seedling survival rate, healthy green leaves, strong trunk stems, and a good mix of shade trees protecting the young plants from extreme heat.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ afi ŋmɔji ni ato ama shi lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi babaoo. Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, tsei ashishifãi ni wa, kɛ tsei ni haa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is it necessary for me to plant shade trees before or alongside my young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ dani mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ loo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under the strong sun. Shade trees act as a natural shield, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa plants can grow without drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How do shade trees affect the way my young cocoa plants grow in their early months?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ saa mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees reduce heat stress on young cocoa, allowing them to focus energy on growing strong roots and fresh leaves instead of struggling to survive under harsh direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai heei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ohi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa seedlings if I plant them in direct sun without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei haaa mihe ajɔ?

english: Without shade trees, direct sun will scorch the leaves of your young cocoa plants, turn them yellow, dry out the soil, and cause many of the seedlings to die before they mature.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã kookoo baai bibii lɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwui babaoo gboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do you recommend permanent shade trees instead of just using plantains for shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ he ŋaawoo haa yɛ plantains ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains provide quick temporary shade for the first two years, but permanent shade trees protect your mature cocoa long-term against heavy winds, soil degradation, and extreme dry seasons.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Shi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ baabu o-cocoo ni eda lɛ he yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or cocoyam together with my young cocoa during the first year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cocoa kɛ baby cocoa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, intercropping with food crops like plantain or cocoyam gives your young cocoa quick temporary shade, protects the soil, and provides you with food and income while the cocoa grows.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo cocoa duɔ lɛ baaha o-cocoa bibioo lɛ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko oya, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni eha niyenii kɛ shika aba be mli ni cocoa lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How long after planting shade trees should I put my cocoa seedlings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei agbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ akɛ kookoo dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ?

english: You can plant your cocoa seedlings at the same time or shortly after setting up your temporary shade crops, as long as the major rainy season has started and the soil is sufficiently wet.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ be kome too mli loo yɛ be kukuoo mli tsei ni odu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ eje shishi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ bɔ ni sa lolo lɛ.

english: How can I help my young cocoa plants survive their very first dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can help young cocoa survive the dry season by leaving enough shade trees standing, mulching around the base of the cocoa stems to retain moisture, and clearing weeds that steal soil water.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ni oooshi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ abɔle kookoo tso lɛ shishi koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. ni ajie jwɛi ni juɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for green growth, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil and cannot absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii adara Aloo shishifãi lɛ ekã shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water trapped in heavy soil cuts off oxygen to cassava roots, causing fungal diseases that make the tubers rot. Planting on mounds or raised ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does covering the dry soil around my crops with dry palm fronds or grass keep them green during warm dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching lɛ egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? Mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi lɛ duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with grass or fronds acts as mulch, shading the earth from direct heat so water in the soil evaporates much slower, keeping roots cool and hydrated.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ blɛoo waa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most drop off without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: A cocoa tree drops flowers it cannot feed when it lacks adequate soil moisture, nutrients, or pollination by tiny insects, shedding extra blooms to protect its overall health.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ayeee amɛ niyenii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu, niyenii, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ amɛhe, ni no haa fɔfɔi krokomɛi baa ni buɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ he.

english: Why should I pinch off the small side shoots growing out of my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato nine lɛ mli lɛ

english: Removing extra side branches prevents the tomato plant from wasting energy on foliage, forcing it to direct its water and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi o-tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi akudɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni tomatoi ni miida lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, stretching tall to reach light instead of building strong stems and thick fruit.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni la abote mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni mli tse.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds in the first few weeks after planting rather than waiting until the crops are big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small, weak roots that easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for water and nutrients; early weeding lets seedlings build a strong base.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa jwɛi ni daa oya koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛmaa shishitoo ni wa.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates between too dry and too wet while the fruit forms.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my cabbage farm more heavily when I plant cabbage on the same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tutuaa mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ cabbage yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously gives crop-specific pests a constant source of food, allowing pest populations to multiply in the soil and surrounding bushes year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ daa. Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: What is a demonstration farm, and how can visiting one help me improve my own crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ nɛɛ saramɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ?

english: A demonstration farm is a small teaching field where officers show new seed varieties and planting methods. Visiting one lets you see how crops behave under proper care so you can copy the successful techniques on your own farm.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ ji tsɔɔmɔ he bibioo ko. Nitsulɔi lɛ baajie dumɔwui srɔtoi heei akpo. kɛ bɔ ni aduɔ nii ahaa Saramɔ ko baaha ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okase ŋaai ni yeɔ omanye lɛ yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should we set up a small farm at our local school alongside our main commercial fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔto ŋmɔji bibii shishi lɛ? yɛ maŋ lɛ mli skul ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ jarayeli he titri lɛ masɛi lɛ.

english: A school farm acts as a practical learning plot for children to understand crop care while also growing fresh food to feed students or sell for extra school funds.
ga: Skul ŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nikasemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii kɛhaa gbekɛbii. Nuu ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ shishi Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛduɔ niyenii heei ni amɛkɛhaa nikaselɔi loo amɛhɔ̃ɔ akɛ skul shikatoohe krɛdɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to save water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the harsh sun so it doesn't dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their rich green color and strength, so adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and thin with weak stems that fall over easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when seeds are planted too close together. The plants stretch upward to compete for sunlight, but because they lack space and nutrients, their stems stay thin and weak.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei lɛ shwie amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Shi yɛ he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ mli tso lɛ mli etsii ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui abɔle he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows makes sure each crop gets equal sun, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why should I test a new crop seed on a small plot before planting my whole field with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Testing on a small plot lets you observe how the crop behaves in your local soil and rain without risking your entire livelihood if the crop fails or gets eaten by pests.
ga: Kaa yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo nɔ Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi amli. Ni okɛ oshihilɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ye amɛ

english: How do I transition my farming from just feeding my family to selling at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake okwaayeli kɛjɛ miweku lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ nɔ kɛya jara nɔ jarayeli nɔ?

english: To sell commercially, you need to expand your planting area, use proper spacing and fertilizers to boost yields, and plan your harvest so you have extra high-quality produce beyond what your home consumes.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli mli Ehe miihia ni ogbɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ. ni oto okpamɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni eha bo nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo fe nɔ ni oshia lɛ yeɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize is dry enough to harvest and take to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Maize is ready for the grain market when the outer leaves turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels are so hard that your thumbnail cannot leave a mark on them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa jarayeli beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa waa akɛ oshishifa lɛ nyɛŋ ashi okadi ko yɛ nɔ.

english: How do I divide my maize harvest between home use and selling to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ aja mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli yɛ shia ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ateŋ?

english: First, calculate and set aside enough dry grain to feed your household until the next harvest, then pack and sell the remaining surplus at the market to generate cash income.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, buu ŋmaa ni egbi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaahã oshia lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ he akɔntaa ni okɛto he. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ shika ni eshwɛ lɛ mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ koni aná shika.

english: Officer, why is the bottom of my cassava stem turning dark brown and soft?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishi bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is usually root rot, which happens when water settles around the roots in poorly drained soil. Creating ridges or mounds helps drain excess water away so the stem and roots stay healthy.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ eji shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela Enɛ baa kɛji nu bɔle shishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛjegbɛ loo gɔŋ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Koni tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning white as if white flour was sprinkled on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee eyɛŋ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfɔ powda yɛŋ amɛshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: That white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which often happens in humid weather. Clearing nearby weeds to improve air flow around the plants and spraying a recommended fungicide helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Nakai nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ, ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: If I see one sick plant in the middle of my healthy crops, should I pull it out right away?
ga: Kɛ mina tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ teŋ lɛ, Ani Esa akɛ Matsi mihe kɛjɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you should remove and destroy that sick plant immediately. Pests and diseases can easily spread from one infected plant to all surrounding healthy crops through wind, rain splash, or insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie tso ni hela mɔ lɛ ni okpãtã ehiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo kooloi bibii anɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark brown and spoil during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, dark, wet conditions. Pruning extra shade trees and clearing infected pods from the farm helps keep your cocoa pods healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ fɔ́ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni oookpa ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small green insects cluster tightly under the leaves of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ebua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those insects are aphids, which suck the sap from crop leaves and cause them to curl and weaken. You can manage them by spraying a neem seed extract mixture or a approved insect spray.
ga: Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ ji aphids, ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei baai amli lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo. Obaanyɛ otsa amɛ kɛtsɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu ni akɛfutu mli loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and produce small ears when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ toi bibii kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded together, they fight for the same water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Plant only two seeds per hole at the recommended distance so each plant grows strong and produces large ears.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔ dumɔwui enyɔ pɛ yɛ bu kome mli yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso ada waa ni ehiɛ toi wuji.

english: Why does leaving wild grass around my yam mounds slow down the growth of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni ashiɔ lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi sweet potato pile lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo.

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal the water and soil nutrients meant for your yams. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes directly into growing big yam tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know if a new piece of land is suitable for growing tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko hi kɛha tomato ŋmɔ?

english: Good soil for tomatoes should be dark, loose, and crumbly so water drains through easily without creating mud, and the field should receive full sunshine throughout the day.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha tomato lɛ afee ediŋŋ, ni egbɛ eshwa, ni egbɛ eshwa bɔni afee ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya ni ekɛ muji akafee. Ni esa akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over at the base and die right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is known as 'damping off,' caused by fungi in soil that is kept too wet. To prevent it, avoid overwatering your nursery beds and ensure the seeds get plenty of fresh air and sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni efɔ tsɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji koni akatsɔ o-nursery bed lɛ nɔ nu fe nine. Ni kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What can I do with all the rice husks left behind after I mill my harvested rice?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ beni mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rice husks can be reused as mulch to keep moisture in your soil, mixed into compost to enrich the land, or even burned into ash to provide natural potassium nutrients for future crops.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔi atsu nii ekoŋŋ akɛ mulch koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo ashãa lɛ po ni etsɔɔ sũ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli potassium ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my rice crop need so much standing water compared to my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are adapted to grow in flooded conditions, which helps keep weeds from growing and ensures the plants get the high, steady moisture level they need to absorb soil nutrients efficiently.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa ni yaa nɔ daa ni he hiaa koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which plants need to make food; applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea can help bring the healthy green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, usually around 9 to 12 months after planting, but digging up one test plant to check tuber size is the best way to be sure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Shi tso ni akaa mɔ akwɛɔ koni ana bulb lɛ dalɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa nɔmimaa.

english: Why do experts advise me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field as my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi kɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your corn and improves overall soil health.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the centers of my corn leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which thrive in warm, damp weather; catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil protects the central growing leaf of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid corn ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields for only one generation; planting seeds saved from that harvest will result in weak plants with significantly smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ adumɔ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why are many of the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli fãi babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers, but high flower drop happens due to water stress, lack of insect pollinators, or disease, which can be improved by pruning shade trees to balance light and humidity.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi babaoo yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Pollinators loo hela ni bɛ, ni abaanyɛ aha eya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni afolɔ mli koni la kɛ hulutsoo afee ekome lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass or plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai aha he ni gbɛ yɔɔ ni ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the earth, prevents weeds from sprouting, and slowly rots into rich food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite fiofio ni etsɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly drooping and wilting in the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil sickness that blocks water flow inside the plant stem; infected plants should be removed immediately so it does not spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei akutsei amli lɛ naa Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm that will still give me food if the rains fail this year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha maná niyenii lolo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpea, sorghum, and millet are naturally tough against dry weather. Cassava stores food safely underground for months, while cowpea and millet have deep roots and fast growing cycles that allow them to produce grain even with very little rain.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Cassava kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo. Shi cowpea kɛ millet lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, ni amɛdaraa oya ni haa amɛwoɔ dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainfall keeps changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ tsakeɔ daa afi hewɔ lɛ

english: Instead of planting after the very first rain—which can be a false start—wait until the rain soaks the soil down to your hand's depth and rains become regular. You can also use early-maturing seed varieties that require fewer weeks of rain to yield.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha sũ lɛ ashɛ oniji amli shɔŋŋ. ni nugbɔ baanɛ tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra, ni biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe otsii komɛi dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba lɛ hu atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it, or the soil itself may be worn out.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ afite.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans (legumes) with maize is very good. Beans grab nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps your land fertile without relying completely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii (legumes) ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under strong sun and hot winds. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted next to them to block the harsh heat and trap moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots get choked without air. Damp, waterlogged soil attracts underground fungi and bacteria that attack and decay the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi amli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani akpaa amɛ.

english: Yam is a vine that makes its food through sunlight hitting its leaves. Staking lifts the vine off the wet ground so it gets maximum sunlight to grow bigger tubers, while keeping the leaves away from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni hoɔ amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tswaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing small worms to hide deep inside the funnels of my maize plants and eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms. Night-flying moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the center funnel of the plant where it is cool and soft to feed on the growing tip.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni foɔ gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. ni mli ejɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo ni akɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern packaged seeds are hybrids bred for special yield power in the first generation only. If you save seeds from that harvest, the next generation loses that strength, resulting in weak plants and small cobs.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome koni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji ohere dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: How can I protect my stored grains from insects without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can use airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) or clean plastic drums. By sealing the grains tightly, you choke out the oxygen that insects need to live, keeping your grain safe for months naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ vacuum ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo plastic baagi ni mli tse atsu nii. Kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni oootsi naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Obaahã kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa kooloi bibii ahi shi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa oŋmaa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ adebɔɔ naa nyɔji babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves, or the soil has too much water drowning the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know whether my farm soil needs organic chicken manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia tsina loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Organic manure improves light or sandy soil so it can hold water and nutrients longer, while chemical fertilizer provides a fast, concentrated boost of specific nutrients when crops are growing quickly.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ sũ ni mli tse loo sũ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya kɛ́ tsei miida oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun, so fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas to keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade koni eha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do many farmers in my village plant cassava and maize together on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early for quick food, while cassava grows slowly underneath and matures months later, allowing you to get two harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa mra koni aye niyenii oya. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before setting any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, hot drying winds, or irregular water supply during the flowering period.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Once cassava passes its maturity period, the plant stops storing food in the roots and starts turning the soft starch into tough woody fiber to support its long-term survival.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsɔ dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni ebɔi ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsakemɔ ewo tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli koni eye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten spots at the bottom while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow so slowly even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your field, aggressively stealing sunlight, space, water, and soil food away from your crops before your plants have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oyale mli. Ejuɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani otsei lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strong traits in the second generation, resulting in smaller cobs, weaker stalks, and lower yields compared to buying fresh certified seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii, ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam rot in storage usually starts when small cuts or wounds created during harvest let fungal germs enter the tuber, especially if the barn is hot and poorly ventilated.
ga: Sweet potato nitoo mli fitemɔ jeɔ shishi kɛji pilamɔi bibii ba yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. ni ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ boteɔ yitso lɛ mli Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli la bɛ jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact best time to plant my crop seeds during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Planting right after the first major, steady rains—when the soil is moist but not waterlogged—ensures seeds get enough water to germinate without rotting or washing away.
ga: Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ daa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee loo amɛshwieee amɛhe.

english: Is it better to plant vegetable seeds directly on the main field or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Tiny seeds like lettuce and pepper do best when nursed in a protected nursery bed first, as this gives them extra care until they grow strong enough to survive transplanting to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii tamɔ lettuce kɛ pepper tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abuɔ he lɛ amli. Enɛ baabi kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What can I apply to my soil to make my leafy crops grow very green and fast?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii koni mi tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya waa?

english: Nitrogen-rich fertilizers, such as well-decomposed poultry manure or urea, supply the essential nutrients that make leaves dark green, broad, and quick-growing.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo urea ni nyɛɔ efiteɔ waa. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli, amɛlɛɔ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too wet or too dry, which stops the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daraaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need nutrients in the soil as well as sunlight to grow; watering alone isn't enough if the soil lacks organic matter or manure to feed the plant.
ga: Tsei hia niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la koni amɛdara. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaahã tso lɛ niyenii.

english: What key items and materials do I need to gather before I start planting vegetables on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii kɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ mabua naa dani mabɔi aduawai adumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You will need good quality seeds, organic manure or fertilizer, watering tools, nursery soil or trays, and basic equipment like a hoe and cutlass to prepare the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ he baahia bo. Manure loo organic fertilizer, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli, shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shishijee nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kuku ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plants grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too tightly, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food, causing them to stretch upwards thin instead of growing full and strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: What will happen to my young vegetables if the rains stop for a few weeks right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-baby vegetables lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Unplanned dry spells cause severe water stress, making young plants wilt, stunt, or flower too early, which is why manual watering or mulching the soil is needed to protect them.
ga: Nu mli hɔmɔ ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi oya tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ niji awo nu loo ŋmɔtɔ awo tso lɛ nɔ koni akɛbu tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Do leafy crops like lettuce need full direct sunlight all day in hot weather?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ lettuce he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: While crops need light to grow, intense afternoon sun in hot seasons can burn tender leaves or cause wilting, so light shade during the hottest hours helps them thrive.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ la he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ, shi hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbɔjɔ baai bibii, no hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛshwere.

english: How can I tell the perfect time to harvest my lettuce before it spoils on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa lettuce dani efite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Lettuce is ready to harvest when the center feels firm and leaves are full, but before a tall flowering stem shoots up from the middle, which makes the leaves bitter.
ga: Lettuce efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji teŋgbɛ lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni baai lɛ eyi obɔ. Shi jeee dani fɔfɔi tso kakadaŋŋ ko je kpo kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plants produce chlorophyll, turning them healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. Ha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plants helps prevent blossom drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot withstand direct hot sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside the cocoa provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil to protect the young plants.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni amɛkwɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava roots thin and small even though the leaves on top are leafy and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ ŋwɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are crowded, the crop uses all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of swelling tubers below. Proper plant spacing and balanced nutrients direct energy into root growth.
ga: Beni ŋmei shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shishi. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars suddenly appear and eat my cabbage leaves after a rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ trukaa lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on the undersides of cabbage leaves, and warm, humid weather after rain causes those eggs to hatch all at once. Inspecting the leaves early and removing the egg clusters prevents caterpillars from destroying the crop.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi woɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabii baai lɛ ashishi. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ haa nakai wuji lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni ojie ŋmeii akui lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat to reduce water loss from the plant. If the leaves stay curled even in the cool morning, it may indicate a lack of soil moisture or tiny sap-sucking insects like mites under the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli po lɛ Enɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: How do I know if my processed cassava gari is good enough quality for buyers to accept and transport to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava ni mifee lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛya jara nɔ?

english: Traders reject damp or poorly processed gari because it spoils easily in transit. High-quality gari comes from fully matured cassava that is properly fermented and thoroughly roasted until dry, crisp, and uniform in color.
ga: Jarayelɔi kpooɔ Gari ni mli efɔ loo ni atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ejaakɛ efiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Gari ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ni eda ni ashã lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ashãa jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbiɔ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ su fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny black insects destroy my stored maize inside the barn after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji fiteɔ ŋmãa ni ato yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils hatch from eggs laid inside maize kernels that were not completely dried before storage. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly until the grains are hard before storing them in sealed bags keeps pests away.
