ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ amli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Can I save seeds from fresh tomatoes I bought at the market to plant on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato hee ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Most market tomatoes come from hybrid seeds, meaning seeds saved from them will produce weak plants with low yields. Buying certified seeds from an agri-dealer ensures your crop grows uniform, strong, and disease-resistant.
ga: Tomatoi ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo faaa. Kɛ́ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni amɛná hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground if I leave them after the leaves dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ nɔ beni baai lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and dry up, the tuber has fully matured and stopped growing. Leaving mature tubers in damp ground allows soil pests and fungi to enter and rot the crop before harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni amɛkpa dalɛ. Kɛ́ ashi bulbs ni edara lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii abote mli ni eha tso lɛ agbo dani akpa.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is an essential plant food responsible for keeping leaves green and healthy so the plant can grow big corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When these plants decay, that stored nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for the next crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, harsh sunlight because their roots are not deep enough yet. Tall shade trees act like umbrellas that protect the delicate leaves from burning and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing all the plants to stay small and weak.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller plantain bunches if I leave all the suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ plantain tso bibioo ko nɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra suckers act like competing mouths to feed, stealing water and plant food from the main stem. Removing most suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ niyenii, nu jumɔ kɛ niyenii ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my fertilizer fail to help my crops if I apply it on dry soil during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can soak it up. On dry soil in hot weather, chemical fertilizers can burn the plant roots or evaporate into the air before the plant receives any benefit.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ yɛ nɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ ana sɛɛnamɔ ko.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil fills up air spaces, suffocating the roots and creating a wet environment where soil fungi thrive and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young corn and chew holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the funnel of the corn plant to feed on soft new leaves, which weakens the plant before it can form ears.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ dani eda ni etsɔ toi.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering, as a way to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. Taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kɛha nu kɛ wala ni akɛbaatsu nii.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and soft leaves that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight or dry winds. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from heat and preserves moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit heavy bunches are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya nɛkɛ be mli ni yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems while the fruit bunch adds weight to the top. Strong winds can easily uproot them unless you dig deeper planting holes and use bamboo poles as props to support the weight of the heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa. yɛ be mli ni aduawai akui kɛ mujiwoo baa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Ja otsa dumɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ. Ni okɛ ŋmei tsei atsu nii akɛ nibii ni akɛfiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ muji lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to absorb nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and yield healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the ground and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates and sits around them, cutting off air supply to the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ afo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create energy for tuber growth under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, preventing leaf diseases and maximizing the sunlight the plant receives to produce big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi baa helai anaa ni oha hulu la ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant sap, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Spraying neem seed extract or recommended organic insecticidal soap helps control these pests so new growth comes out healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Neem dumɔwui amli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ. koni dalɛ hee lɛ abaje kpo kɛ hewalɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is poor pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and ensuring good airflow between plants helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni pollination lɛ ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch woɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Weed seeds stay dormant in the soil for long periods and are naturally adapted to sprout rapidly at the slightest moisture. Clearing weeds early before planting gives your crops a head start so they do not have to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsakeɔ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the bare ground around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minibii ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective shade layer. It keeps the soil cool under direct heat, stops soil water from evaporating quickly, and blocks sunlight so weed seeds cannot easily sprout.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaaa hulu la lɛ akashɛ he, no hewɔ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster after natural rain falls compared to when I pour water on them myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ nu haa mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe lɛ he.

english: Rainwater contains natural nitrogen absorbed from the air, which acts like a free boost of fertilizer for your crops. Rain also falls evenly over the entire field and cools down the air, helping the plants absorb nutrients better than bucket watering.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa onibii ahe ni aheee nɔ ko. Nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young crops dry up and die when the weather becomes too hot in the middle of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water very quickly in direct heat. Without strong shade or deep roots to pull water from deep in the soil, the intense sun causes them to dry out and collapse.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbi ni amɛkumɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to cut or harvest my crops so they don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Koni tsei lɛ akafite

english: Most crops show clear signs when they are ready: maize leaves turn brown and the husks dry out, cassava leaves start yellowing and dropping, and fruits reach full color and firm texture. Harvesting too early means small yields, while waiting too long leaves crops exposed to rots and pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji amɛfee klalo: ŋmãa baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ hu baagbi. Cassava baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni aduawai lɛ yɛ su ni eyi obɔ kɛ loo ni mli wa. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa yibiiwoo baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛmɛɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa.

english: Why do some of the seeds I saved from my previous harvest fail to grow when I plant them next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in damp or warm places can absorb moisture and rot, or lose their living strength before planting time. To keep seeds healthy, dry them thoroughly in the sun and store them in cool, airtight containers away from heat and insects.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni mli ejɔ loo he ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi. loo hewalɛ ni ekɛbaahi shi lɛ baaje mli dani adu koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi be fɛɛ be Ha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi abɔ he.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops now than it did when I first started farming on it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa fe beni mije okwaayeli shishi afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the soil every time they grow. If you plant on the same land repeatedly without adding compost, manure, or giving the soil time to rest, the soil becomes hungry and exhausted, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same farm, or will they destroy each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli loo amɛbaafite amɛhe?

english: You can plant them together if spaced correctly. Maize grows fast and feeds closer to the soil surface, while cassava grows slower and feeds deeper. Because they feed at different levels and mature at different times, they can share the space well without competing.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome kɛji akɛ okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja. Abele daa oya ni ayeɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ nii yɛ hei srɔtoi, ni amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛja he ko jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other underground for food and water, while their leaves fight above ground for sunlight. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow big, strong, and produce full leaves and fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ agbo, ehe awa, ni ewo baai kɛ aduawai ni eyi obɔ.

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help from your crop showing that it lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient found in good soil or fertilizer. It can also happen if the roots are sitting in flooded soil and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bolɔmɔ kɛha yelikɛbuamɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Weeds are wild plants native to the area, so they are naturally tougher and adapted to survive on very little water and poor soil. They quickly swallow up sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your planted crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ jɛmɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu fioo ko pɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni okwɛɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do insects suddenly flood my farm right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain causes plants to put out fresh, tender stems and leaves, which are the favorite food for many insects. The damp weather also creates the perfect environment for insect eggs buried in the soil to hatch all at once.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ feɔ ehee. ni ji niyenii ni kooloi babaoo sumɔɔ waa Shihilɛi ni mli ewo nu lɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi akui ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikome.

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in excess water and high humidity. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods, causing them to turn black and dry up.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo babaoo mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves before they unfold and leaving behind waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai bibii dani amɛgbele ni oshi jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: This yellowing means your soil is short of nitrogen, which is the food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top new leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and smell bad underground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains cause standing water on your field, the roots get waterlogged, drown, and rot due to a lack of air in the soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha nu damɔ shi yɛ oyale mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines. Staking pushes their leaves up high into the sunlight, allowing the plant to capture energy to build larger and heavier tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my healthy-looking plantain trees snap or fall over easily during light winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ?

english: Tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevils eat away the roots under the ground. Without strong roots to anchor the plant in the dirt, the top-heavy plantain tree easily collapses.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Plantains ni yiteŋ tsii lɛ nyɛɔ efoɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat or sudden changes in water levels. If the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu lɛ mli tsakemɔi trukaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck the plant juice, they cause the leaves to wrinkle and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛnuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛbaahã baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do groundnut plants form their nuts under the ground after flowering above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flowers bloom above ground and get pollinated, they grow long stalks called 'pegs.' These pegs bend downward, drill themselves directly into the loose soil, and swell to form the groundnuts.
ga: Beni ŋmeii fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Eyɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pins’. Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi. Ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni efuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ ebafeɔ ŋmei

english: Why is it important for agricultural officers to inspect my cocoa seeds before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ kookoo yibii amli dani amɛdu lɛ?

english: Inspecting seeds before planting ensures you are using healthy, high-quality, and disease-free varieties. This protects your farm from major disease outbreaks and prevents you from wasting time and money on seeds that will not yield well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni oookwɛ mli dani odu lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni hela bɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he. ni etsĩɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite be kɛ shika yɛ dumɔwui ni wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Do my general food crops like maize and cassava need seed inspection like cocoa does?
ga: Niyenii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ ekomɛi ji ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Ani ehe miihia ni akwɛ dumɔwui amli tamɔ kookoo?

english: Yes, all crop seeds and planting materials benefit from inspection. Checking food crop seeds helps ensure they are free from pests and diseases, giving you higher yields and better food security.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baaná sɛɛkwɛmɔ he sɛɛ. Niyenii dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo ni niyenii hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees seem to grow slowly during their first eight months in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ da blɛoo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ekpaa ni ekɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In their first eight months, young trees focus energy on growing strong roots underground to find water and nutrients. Once their root system is firm and established, top leafy growth will speed up.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ekpaa lɛ mli lɛ, tso bibioo lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ shishifãi ni wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe nii koni etao nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛji eshishifãi lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ŋwɛi baai lɛ adalɛ baaya oya.

english: Why are young cocoa seedlings so sensitive when first moved from the nursery into the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa beni ajieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ he ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are used to the cool shade of the nursery. Moving them outdoors exposes them to harsh sunlight, hot winds, and changing soil moisture, which shocks the plant until it gets adjusted.
ga: Akɛ tsei bibii woɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee kpo nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ naa amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsakeɔ ehe.

english: What causes the leaves on my young cocoa tree to start turning yellow or drooping?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛmiigbee shi?

english: Yellow or drooping leaves are a sign of stress, which can be caused by lack of water, too much harsh sunlight, poor soil nutrients, or early insect damage.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ enɛ aba. Hulu la babaoo Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I plant them and leave them for months without visiting my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ ni mishi amɛ nyɔji babaoo ni miyasaraaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If you leave trees unmonitored, weeds will choke them, pests and diseases can destroy them unnoticed, and drought can kill them before you realize there is a problem.
ga: Kɛji oshi otso lɛ ni otsuuu he nii lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa. Kplukai srɔtoi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai Ebaanyɛ efite tsei ni mɔ ko mɔ ko yɔseee. Ni hɔmɔ baanyɛ agbe tsei nɛɛ dani ole akɛ naagba ko yɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on my young crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: You should walk through your farm at least once or twice a week. Regular visits allow you to spot early signs of disease, insect infestation, or weed growth before they destroy your crop.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo jwɛi ni miida lɛ ahe okadii mra dani amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: What should I do if an inspector or extension officer finds a disease on my young cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii amli loo mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii amli lɛ na hela yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Follow the officer's advice immediately, which may include cutting away affected leaves, applying recommended treatments, or removing heavily infected plants to protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ agbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ asɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni baanyɛ afata enɛ he ji baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafolɔ. Okɛ tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii. Aloo jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ koni obu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How can government agricultural extension officers help me on my crop farm?
ga: Te nɔyeli okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers bring scientific knowledge directly to your community. They help inspect your crops for disease, teach proper planting methods, and show you recommended ways to care for your soil and seeds.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ kɛ jeŋ nilee baa akutso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ye obua ni okwɛ otsei lɛ amli kɛji helai yɛ amɛmli. Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛi kpakpai ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii ni otsɔɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ oshikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ.

english: Where can I find certified seeds and planting materials for my farm in Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui kɛ dumɔ nibii ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: You can obtain approved and certified seeds through local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA) offices, COCOBOD seed production units, or registered seed dealers in your region.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni awo he odaseyeli kɛtsɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA) nitsumɔhe lɛ, COCOBOD dumɔwui afeemɔ kuu loo dumɔwui ajalɔ ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I suddenly see so many insects crawling on my farm ground when the rains start around October?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni miihoso yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ October mli lɛ?

english: Rain softens the soil and provides moisture, which signals buried insect eggs to hatch and dormant pests to emerge from the ground all at once between October and March.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ baafɔ. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni wɔɔ Amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli yɛ October kɛ March teŋ.

english: Which months of the year should I prepare the most for large insect swarms on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ esa akɛ masaa mihe jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The period from October through March is usually the peak time for insect outbreaks because the weather and moisture levels create perfect conditions for them to multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, October kɛyashi March ji be ni kooloi bibii yeɔ helai babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni kooloi bibii lɛ afɔ.

english: Why do insects appear in such terrifyingly large numbers all at the exact same time on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miije kpo yɛ yibɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ nɛkɛ mli shikome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Insects synchronize their hatching with rainfall patterns so that their young have plenty of moist soil and fresh green crops to feed on as soon as they emerge.
ga: Koolooi kɛ wɔji fɔmɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛjianɔtoi tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa amɛbii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ.

english: How can I protect my young crops when swarms of insects land on my soil during the wet season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛ́ kooloi bibii babaoo ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: You can clear weeds around your farm before the rains start, use protective netting over tender seedlings, or apply recommended sprays early in the morning when ground insects are most active.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ Kɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii leebi be mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ.

english: Will my crops survive if a huge swarm of ground pests lands on my farm all at once?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo baye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikome?

english: Yes, if caught early. Healthy crops can recover from minor insect feeding, but large swarms require quick action like clearing crop residues or applying targeted pest control to prevent total damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ amɔmɔ lɛ oya lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kɛjɛ kooloi fioo ni ayeɔ amɛ lɛ mli. Shi tsinai akui wuji biɔ nifeemɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Aloo okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii koni akafite kwraa.

english: What signs should I look for on my farm right before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛɛ okadi esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi?

english: Look for cracks in the soil where pests hide, small egg clusters under dry leaves, and early crawling bugs near the soil surface as soon as the first rain hits.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. Akpɔlɔi akui bibii ni yɔɔ baai ni egbi shishi kɛ kooloi ni shwereɔ yɛ shishijee bei amli. Ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ

english: Does turning over my soil before October help reduce the number of bugs that appear later?
ga: Ani kɛ́ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ dani October aba lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni baa sɛɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, plowing or tilling the soil exposes buried insect eggs and larvae to the hot sun and birds, killing them before they can hatch when the rains begin.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa kooloi bibii kɛ amɛmli ŋmeii ni afu amɛ lɛ naa hulu kɛ okpoi amli dɔlɛ. Gbemɔ amɛ dani amɛfɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: Why do many insects stay on the ground surface instead of climbing onto my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɔ mitsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Many young insects need the moisture and warmth of the soil surface during the early rainy months before they grow strong enough to climb up and feed on plant leaves.
ga: Kplukai bibii babaoo he miihia amɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shishijee lɛ amli. Dani amɛbaada ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛye tsei ahe baai lɛ,.

english: Is there a simple way to keep ground-crawling insects away from my crops without spending a lot of money?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ maha kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akaje miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii?

english: Sprinkling dry wood ash or spraying homemade neem leaf extract around the base of your crops creates a protective barrier that repels crawling pests during rainy months.
ga: Tso mli sũ ni egbi ni oooshwie nɔ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni afee yɛ shia lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ obɔle Otso lɛ shishi Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni shwieɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Does heavy rain make my crops weaker against insect attacks?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtutuaa mi?

english: Rain actually makes crops grow stronger, but because the wet weather also causes thousands of insect eggs to hatch at once, the sudden swarm can overwhelm young plants if not managed.
ga: Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, nugbɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ waa. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi bibii akpei abɔ fɔɔ shikome. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aye tsei bibii anɔ kunim kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves, especially starting from the bottom of the stalk, usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build strong leaves and green growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni wa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baa lɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in direct sun without cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mibɛ he ko ni amɛhiɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and dry out quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides the damp, sheltered environment seedlings need to build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná he ko ni mli ejɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I tell underground crops like cassava are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishifã ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ eshwɛ ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni gbɛ eshwa eshishi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Keeping the farm free of weeds and using insect traps helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni akɛ kooloi bibii atsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no bees or wind to help pollinate the flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaye abua ni fɔfɔii lɛ afee aduawai.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots coming out around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ he lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: When a plantain tree produces too many young shoots (suckers), they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the main plant and one strong replacement, resulting in larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui wo ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso titri lɛ kɛ tso ni he wa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to lift and stake my yam vines on tall poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni mikɛma tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps vines off the wet ground, which prevents leaf rot and allows maximum light exposure.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa wain tsei ahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite, ni ebaaha la aba mli babaoo.

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb moisture before heat builds up. Hot afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can shock plant leaves with extreme temperature changes.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ akpokpo kɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi wuji.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant them immediately after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need both water and air in the soil to sprout. When the ground is completely waterlogged, air is trapped out, causing seeds to suffocate and rot before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests or soil diseases targeted at that crop to build up in number. Rotating with legumes like beans restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai babaoo anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tso lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern when the crop lacks nitrogen food in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their dark green color back so they can produce big ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ekɛfee toi wuji.

english: Hot midday sun causes tomato plants to lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the warm soil. As the air cools down in the evening, the plant recovers, but putting straw mulch around the base keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ. Shi jwɛi ni akɛhaa shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillar droppings in the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii afɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miteŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the soft center whorl of the plant to feed away from sunlight. Early spraying of recommended biopesticides or applying neem leaf extract directly into the leaf funnel destroys the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye hulu la lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get a larger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together forces them to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall thin stems with tiny roots. Giving each plant proper distance lets the roots spread out into thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, yucca ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the cowpea plant dies and rots, that trapped nitrogen feeds the next crop like natural fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruits. Keeping the soil damp and avoiding excessive urea keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ ha tso lɛ hao, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ urea babaoo he lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he.

english: Why did my planted seeds rot in the ground after a sudden heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need both moisture and oxygen from air pockets in the soil to sprout. When heavy rain leaves standing water, it drowns the seeds by cutting off their oxygen, causing soil fungi to rot them before they can emerge.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ha nu lɛ ahi shi. Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do weeds steal strength from my young crops so quickly during the early rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mitsei bibii lɛ amli oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have aggressive roots that drink up water and fertilizer much faster than young crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks gives your crop full access to food so it can grow tall enough to shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni baanu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei bibii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Enɛ baaha eda ni ekwɛ jwɛi heei anɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs and vegetables grow faster during dry season irrigation than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In the dry season, crops receive continuous bright sunshine without long cloudy days, allowing them to turn light into plant food continuously as long as irrigation supplies steady water to their roots.
ga: Yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii naa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni atatu bɛ mli gbii. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ la amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii be fɛɛ be, kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my previous maize harvest give me smaller yields than certified seeds bought in a sealed bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time and often inherit hidden diseases or undesirable mixed traits from surrounding farm pollen. Certified seeds are specially produced in controlled fields to ensure every plant grows strong, uniform, and high-yielding.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛnáa helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo sui ni esaaa ni akɛfee ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ gboshinii. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ yɛ hei ni akudɔɔ koni tso fɛɛ tso ada jogbaŋŋ. Yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective shield that blocks harsh sun and traps moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, awo amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ baa, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant to eat early shoots, which weakens the plant before it can grow maize ears.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli koni amɛye ŋmãa bibii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ dani ŋmãa toi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize reduce my maize harvest?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baaha mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: No, planting legumes like beans alongside maize actually helps the maize. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had thin light-green or yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produced small harvests, your soil is exhausted and needs compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo okɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ aba Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why is my maize producing thin stalks and tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ toi bibii kɛ́ adu lɛ babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Crops spaced too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room to feed well and build strong stems with full maize ears.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛfee tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ

english: Yam plants store energy in their tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. When the vines climb tall sticks into full light, the leaves produce more food, resulting in much larger underground yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ bulbs lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ niji lɛ anɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni sa koni enine ashɛ la ni fa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away, usually in heavy clay soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni efooo. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I keep my vegetable soil moist during the hot Harmattan season when there is no rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-vegetable shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ Harmatton hulutsoo be mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the earth and traps water in the root area for much longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekagbi, ni ebaaha nu ahi shishifã lɛ he be babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh weather and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogging around the roots from heavy rainfall, which prevents the plant from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in soil rich in leafy organic matter without enough potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha cassava nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baai amli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ nɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agbo lɛ ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛ tsei ewo mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally need to climb high to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Exposing more leaves to sunlight gives the plant the energy it needs to build large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo hulu la babaoo mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when the soil dries out suddenly. Extreme heat and water stress prevent successful pollination, causing the plant to shed its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects that distorts normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil for your maize crop while covering the ground to stop weeds from spreading.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni okɛ mulching woɔ mli koni jwɛi lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is causing ragged holes and dry powder inside the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni etsilɛ kɛ powda ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This pattern of damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center funnel of the maize plant. The dry powder you see is the waste material left behind by the caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Powda ni egbi ni onaa lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves (known as mulching) traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, ekatsɔ la oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly onto dry soil around my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plants can absorb it safely. Placing fertilizer on dry soil can concentratedly burn the delicate roots and damage the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni nu atsɔ mli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua ni ekwɛ̃.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods before they rot?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ diji dani amɛgboiɔ?

english: Black spots are caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds, trimming extra branches to let air in, and removing infected pods helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. weeding Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding poultry manure or appropriate fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad if I plant cassava on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Ani ejaaa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Yes, growing cassava in the same spot repeatedly drains all the specific nutrients from the soil, leading to smaller harvests over time. Rotating your land with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps rebuild the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaajie niyenii ni yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ama ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early using neem oil solutions or proper pest management stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the soil gets too dry or when daytime temperatures become extremely hot. Regular watering and keeping the soil covered with organic mulch helps the plant retain its blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa efɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open on the vine right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miitswa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when a plant receives a sudden flush of heavy water after a long dry spell. The inside of the tomato expands faster than its skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tomatoi lɛ ni fãa.

english: Why should I space my maize plants far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fe bɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sun, rain, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing thin and twisted instead of fat and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ mli tse ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams become misshapen when the soil underneath is too hard, rocky, or compacted for the tuber to push through easily. Building high, soft mounds of loose soil allows the yams to grow fat and smooth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato lɛ feɔ fɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to conserve water and survive heat. The plant isn't dead; once the rainy season returns, it will shoot up fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ, ebaakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune my cocoa trees after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ mli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches and suckers that steal nutrients from the main trunk. It allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and encourages the tree to channel its energy into producing healthy pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni ataooo ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ awo ŋmeii ni mli wa amli.

english: Will trimming off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt its growth?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha eda?

english: No, careful trimming actually helps the tree grow stronger. By cutting away weak or misplaced shoots, you force the tree to direct its food and water to the main stem and flower spots, resulting in a healthier tree and better harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akwɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ mli awa. Tso lɛ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni bɛ he ni sa lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu gbɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ hei ni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ, ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does cutting back side shoots encourage more pods to grow on the main trunk?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ afolɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni pods babaoo daa yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ?

english: When you trim side shoots (suckers), the plant stops wasting energy on leaf growth and focuses that energy lower down on the trunk, where flower cushions form and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛji ofolɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, tso lɛ kpa hewalɛ fitemɔ yɛ baa dalɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ ama shi kɛyashɛ tso lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni fɔfɔi akutsei lɛ feɔ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: What is the 'Nkrumah' cocoa variety, and why do farmers talk about it?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Nkrumah’ kookoo henɔ lɛ ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi miiwie he lɛ?

english: Nkrumah cocoa is a fast-bearing hybrid variety popular in Ghana. It is known for growing lower to the ground and producing pods early in its lifespan, often bearing fruit right around the lower trunk and base.
ga: Nkrumah kookoo ji kookoo henɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii oya ni ale waa yɛ Ghana. Ale akɛ edaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ewoɔ yibii mra yɛ ewala be lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Is it normal to see cocoa pods growing right at the bottom base of the tree trunk near the soil?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ ooona kookoo ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, certain high-yielding cocoa varieties naturally produce flower cushions and pods near the base of the trunk. Proper care and clear spacing around the base help these low pods mature safely without touching damp soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo henɔi komɛi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔii akutsei kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ nɛɛ daa shweshweeshwe ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he.

english: What steps should I take once I notice the very first pods forming near the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi feemɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi?

english: Once pods start forming near the base, keep the area around the trunk clear of weeds and excess shoots. Managing surrounding growth ensures sunlight reaches the lower trunk while keeping pest crawling pathways away from the young pods.
ga: Beni pods lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ Ha he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ahi shi. Ha tsei lɛ amli jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine akafee nɔ ko. Nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ lɛ akashɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why does cocoa farming require so much continuous labor compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a sensitive tree crop that requires active management like regular weeding, shade control, and pruning. Without consistent effort, the tree spends energy fighting off pests and growing wild branches instead of producing high yields.
ga: Cocoa ji jwɛi tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ ashiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛbɔɔɔ mɔdɛŋ be fɛɛ be. Yɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ najiaŋ

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees yielding heavily while mine on the same soil have very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Soil is only part of the equation. Trees that are regularly pruned and properly managed channel their nutrients into fruit production, whereas unmanaged trees waste energy growing excess foliage, leading to low yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ji equation lɛ fã kome pɛ. Tsei ni afolɔ amɛ daa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha niyenii ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi

english: How can I ensure that the effort I put into my young cocoa farm gives me the maximum possible harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mɔdɛŋ ni mikɛwo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: To get maximum results, combine good field clearing with strict canopy management. Planting high-yield varieties and consistently pruning shoots ensures every tree reaches its full pod-bearing potential.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ Okɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa kpakpa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa afata he. Tso sɔrɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shɛɔ e-pod-bearing nyɛmɔ lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my cocoa tree is channeling its energy into pods rather than just growing tall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miitsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛmiiya ŋmeii lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ?

english: A tree focusing on fruit production will develop thick stem growth and early flower cushions along the lower and middle trunk. If a tree is only growing tall with thin branches and lots of leaves, it usually means it needs pruning.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai afeemɔ nɔ lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ fɔfɔii ni baajɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ, eyɛ niji bibii kɛ baai babaoo pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afolɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, so applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted at an angle instead of flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps the roots grow deeper and spread out evenly in the soil, which leads to stronger plants and bigger, healthier tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps feed the maize plants growing alongside them.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hottest part of the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting. Placing straw or leaves as mulch around the stem keeps the root zone cool and moist.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Jwɛi loo baai ni akɛhaa he lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms always gather inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target the central whorl of young maize because the leaves there are soft, tender, and easy for them to chew, while providing shelter from heat and rain.
ga: Meatworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, abifao ŋmãa baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Ehaa aboɔ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa kɛ nugbɔ hu he.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are damaged by black pod disease or just scorched by the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ black pod hela efite mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ loo hulutsoo kɛkɛ?

english: Black pod disease causes dark brown spots that spread rapidly across the whole pod and turn soft with white fungus, whereas sun damage creates dry, hard spots only on the side facing direct sunlight.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ pod lɛ mli fɛɛ baa, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa hei ni egbi ni wa baa yɛ fã ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whiteflies that spread viral diseases, or by heavy heat stress. Managing sucking insects early helps prevent this curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa loo kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ curling naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground if I delay harvesting them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa nii yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills the spaces in the soil with water and drives out oxygen, causing the soil to suffocate the roots and encouraging rot-causing fungi to attack the yams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops before applying fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that will steal the fertilizer nutrients before your crops can absorb them, so clearing weeds first ensures your crop gets the full benefit of the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe sɛɛ kwraa.

english: Why is it important for me to check for an official regulator's approval label on pesticides before buying them for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ he wolo lɛ nɔ dani mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Regulatory bodies check pesticides to ensure they effectively kill target pests without destroying your crops, harming your soil, or leaving dangerous chemical residues on the food you produce.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kwɛɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛgbe kooloi ni ataoɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ofiteee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ awui loo oshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ niyenii ni ofeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green so the plant can make food and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that attack maize to stay in the field. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or beans helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be Bei lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas focus on growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas produce their own nitrogen from the air, so adding extra fertilizer often hurts pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsina ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ náa pod feemɔ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves when water is scarce to protect themselves from losing moisture. Once the rain starts again, the plant uses energy stored in its roots to grow fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji nu faaa koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ.

english: Why do crop seeds sprout much faster when I sow them right after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?
