english: Seeds stay asleep until water softens their outer shell and Signals them to grow. Moist soil provides the exact water and cool environment a seed needs to break open and push roots down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eda. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa nu kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛgbala ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛtsake yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Hard or stony soil prevents yam tubers from expanding smoothly into the ground. Building high, loose mounds of topsoil allows the tubers room to stretch freely and grow big and straight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and looking squeezed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying with neem leaf extract or mild soapy water keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Extreme sun heat or dry soil causes stress, making tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy. Giving the plants regular water during flowering keeps the flowers attached so they can grow into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Ha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool air they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why must I remove weeds from my farm even when my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, plant food, and space from crop roots beneath the soil regardless of their height. Keeping the farm clean leaves all the soil's water and nutrients for your crops to yield better.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni amɛkwɔ ha. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly like straws during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during peak afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural way of trapping moisture when the sun is very strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛji hulu la lɛ mli wa waa.

english: If I get access to an irrigation scheme, why is it bad to water my crops at midday when the sun is high?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ hegbɛ kɛya nu shwiemɔ nitsumɔi amli Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu shwane mli beni hulu lɛ teɔ shi lɛ?

english: Watering crops in midday heat causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can soak it up. Drops left on leaves can also magnify sunlight and burn the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni eshã tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water sits on my farm for too many days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the field without draining, the roots get suffocated and start to decay.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha ŋmãa ŋmɔji anɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my rice crop turning yellow while the top leaves are still bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older lower leaves to keep its new upper leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight for sunlight and stretch upward instead of branching out. The plant spends all its energy growing tall instead of making flowers and peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ ni ehaa esɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ niji ni eeetswa lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any tomatoes during dry hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out the pollen inside tomato flowers. Without good pollen, the flowers cannot form fruits and the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollen kpakpa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my onion leaves fall over and dry up on their own when the bulbs get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbiɔ kɛji onion lɛ miida lɛ?

english: When an onion bulb finishes growing, the neck naturally loses its strength and collapses. This is the plant's signal that it has moved all its nutrients into the bulb and is ready to be harvested.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sabolai lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tsitsi lɛ hewalɛ baaje edɛŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaagbee shi. Enɛ ji tso lɛ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do white powdery spots spread over my okra leaves when the morning weather is foggy and damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mi okra baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Leebi lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo afua ni edɔ.

english: High moisture in the air combined with warm temperatures creates the perfect conditions for powdery mildew, a fungal disease that feeds on plant leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha powdery mildew. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai

english: Why do armyworms like to hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of young maize has tender, moisture-rich leaves that are easy for worms to eat, while also hiding them from hot sunlight and birds.
ga: Abɛi abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛtee hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my field even after I cut it down to the soil line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo lɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that store food. Cutting the top only removes the leaves, leaving the underground roots alive and ready to shoot back up.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni akɛtoɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ baai lɛ pɛ. Ashiɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛhiɛ kã ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow and looking weak before the corn even forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ dani abele lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for plants. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its strength and produce healthy ears of corn.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ewo ŋmãa toi ni mli wa.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my harvest get smaller each time?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil, leading to soil exhaustion. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and keeps it healthy for future crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these resources first, leaving your crops starving and unable to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Amɛbaaju nibii nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they are exposed to full direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh sun and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my hot pepper plants curl up and stop growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses, draining the crop's energy. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or safe pest control prevents these insects from damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbeɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before it is time for me to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Root rot in cassava happens when heavy soil holds too much water around the roots or when soil fungi infect the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni tsii hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are small worms eating the tender leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the main growing point of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended neem-based treatments or pesticides protects the leaves so the plant can continue to grow.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa hei titri ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daa yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii ni neem loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ aya nɔ eda.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and preventing fungal diseases from spreading on wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When too many suckers grow at once, they compete with the main plantain tree for water and food. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, allowing the main stem to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida shikome lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛkɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains babaoo.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps cool the plant so the flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it important for me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily get scorched by strong sun. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves, acting like living umbrellas that provide the shade and moist soil environment cocoa needs in its early years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nutrients away, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and food-producing again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee niyenii.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the main stem near the ground will swell and crack as the tubers underneath grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni tso titri ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafu ni egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to get maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. It also keeps the leaves dry and off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil extract or recommended insecticides stops these pests from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for the maize I will plant next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the ground. When the crop leaves and roots decay, that stored nitrogen remains behind to feed future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛye wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Is it better for my garden eggs and tomato plants if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tomato tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the hot sun causes it to evaporate. Afternoon watering wastes water and can cause heat stress on wet plant stems.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ aba tsei ahe tsei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What type of plantain sucker should I select from my old farm when I want to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker esa akɛ mahala kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli kɛ́ miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmɔ hee?

english: Choose 'maiden suckers' which have spear-shaped leaves and thick bases. They establish roots quickly and grow stronger than suckers that already have wide, flat leaves, which struggle more after transplanting.
ga: Halamɔ ‘bamboo shoots’ ni yɔɔ baai ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishi ni mli tse. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛdaraa waa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ momo lɛ. ni baabɔ mɔdɛŋ babaoo yɛ be mli ni ajie lɛ awo mli lɛ sɛɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any green tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving your plants consistent moisture and mulching around the roots helps hold the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ mli fũ daa ni okɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I prevent small dark insects from eating holes into my harvested maize kernels in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ akashɛ mihe? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack maize when it retains too much moisture. Drying your harvested corn on the cob until the seeds are rock hard before shelling and storing them in airtight, sealed bags keeps insects out and suffocates any hidden pests.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji ehiɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee tamɔ tɛ dani ajie lɛ ni akɛwo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbe amɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully matured and ready to harvest for making flour?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛha ashikishaŋ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels become hard to the touch. Letting the crop mature fully on the stalk ensures the grains are dry enough to mill into fine flour for local foods like kenkey.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni ewa akɛ aaata dumɔwui lɛ ahe Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tso lɛ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, egbiɔ ŋmaa lɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli ashikishaŋ kpakpa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii, tamɔ kenkey ŋmãa.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves during peak heat to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation. It is a natural stress response showing that the crop needs extra soil moisture to grow properly.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli haomɔ hetoo ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kroko koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn stalks turn yellow before the cobs have finished growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the maize plant lacks key soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, or is getting too little water. Adding organic manure or fertilizer early in the growing process helps the plant stay green and nourish the cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ Organic fertilizer loo organic fertilizer ni akɛfataa he mra Yɛ dumɔ nitsumɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes small holes to appear in my young maize leaves, and will it stop my cobs from growing?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa abifao lɛ baai lɛ amli, ni ani ebaatsi mi-ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃?

english: Small holes in leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the plant. If left untreated, these insects damage the plant's leaves, leaving it too weak to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni egbee shi ni eye tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ tsei ahe baai. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ efee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to spoil just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are removed from the soil, exposure to air causes rapid chemical reactions that rot the root within 48 hours. To prevent waste, harvested cassava should be processed or dried into flour immediately.
ga: Beni ajieɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofa ko ni yɔɔ oya ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli lɛ baa. Bɔni afee ni akafite lɛ, esa akɛ atsu ŋmei ni akpa lɛ he nii loo agbi lɛ ni efee ashikishaŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I grow wheat in Ghana to make bread flour, or should I use cassava instead?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmaa yɛ Ghana koni mikɛfee blodoo ashikiŋsha? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei atsu nii moŋ?

english: Wheat requires cold weather to grow well and does not thrive in Ghana's warm climate. Instead, farmers can grow cassava, which thrives locally and can be processed into high-quality cassava flour to substitute for wheat flour in baking.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ he miihia ŋmaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Okwaafoi baanyɛ adu ŋmei, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ afee ŋmei ashikiŋsha ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛye ŋmaa ashikishaŋ najiaŋ yɛ niyenii shãa mli.

english: How does sun-drying help process cassava into usable baking flour?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei feɔ ashikishaŋ ni ashã ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii?

english: Sun-drying removes the moisture from cassava roots, stopping mold growth and breaking down natural plant toxins. Once completely dried, the root can be easily ground into fine flour that stays safe to eat for months.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ ni efiteɔ tsei amli tsofai fɔji lɛ. Kɛji egbi kwraa lɛ, abaanyɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ hu ni afee lɛ powda kpakpa. Amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛtoɔ ni ayeɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does my harvested grain rot or get insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyɛ kooloi amli be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain rots or attracts pests if it is stored while still carrying moisture from the field. Drying your grains thoroughly under the sun until they are completely hard prevents mold and insects from destroying your yield after the agricultural process is done.
ga: Ŋmãa fiteɔ loo egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ lolo. Kɛ́ ogbala odumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni agbe okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ naa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I plant maize on the same piece of land every season, why does my yield drop?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ eba shi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen, and planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally for future harvests.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. kɛ dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do some food crops take only three months to produce food while root crops take almost a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi heɔ nyɔji etɛ pɛ dani amɛwoɔ niyenii yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ŋmɔshi nibii heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi lɛ?

english: Different crops have different growth behaviors programmed in them. Grain crops like maize focus energy on fast surface seeds in a few months, whereas root crops like cassava need many months to store starch deep underground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ dalɛ subaŋ gbɛjianɔtoi srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ni jeɔ kpo oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkɛ ŋmeii lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni aduko dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa creates living umbrellas that shade the young seedlings and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow before the cobs form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure gives the crop the energy it needs to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am burying cassava stems into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the green buds or nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to bend unnaturally underground, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain plant for water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to yield a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains babaoo.

english: Placing fertilizer right against a crop's stem causes chemical burns to the stem tissue and root system. Placing fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away allows the outer roots to safely drink in the nutrients.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi anɔ lɛ haa tsofa shãa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli He ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of maize leaves to eat the growing tip. Spraying early with recommended bio-pesticides or targeted neem extracts helps clear the pest before it destroys the stalk.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ afɔse mra. Aloo, neem mli nu lɛ baaye abua ni egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat waves, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent watering and using balanced nutrients helps flowers turn into healthy tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high enough to catch maximum sunlight, which powers root growth and makes underground tubers grow large. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa koni hulu la ashɛ enɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by microscopic sucking insects like thrips or mites that spread viruses. Controlling these tiny insects early using soapy water or neem oil protects the foliage and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii ahe nitsumɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo chili ŋmeii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for the next crop season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that trap nitrogen from the air and convert it into soil nutrients. When harvested, they leave behind enriched soil that acts as natural fertilizer for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa lɛ, eshiɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn bright yellow faster when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ mihe lɛ?

english: Strong sunlight and high temperatures speed up the natural ripening process of cocoa pods. However, if the sun hits the pods too intensely without enough shade, they can ripen prematurely before the beans inside fully develop.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya. Shi, kɛji hulu lɛ tswa ŋmeii lɛ waa tsɔ ni hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Beans baanyɛ akwɛ̃ mra dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pod is truly ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ he diɛŋtsɛ akɛ abaakpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin color changes fully—usually turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety. If you gently tap the pod, it should also make a slightly hollow sound indicating the beans have detached from the inner wall.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo nɔ su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. E da si ngɛ slɔɔtoslɔɔto ɔmɛ a nɔ Ke o ta pod ɔ he bɔɔ ko ɔ, e sa nɛ e pee kaa nɔ́ ko nɛ e ngɛ hɛ mi nyami hulɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ejɛ mligbɛ gbogbo lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green and unripe?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lolo ni amɛshɛko?

english: Unripe cocoa beans lack the necessary sugars needed for proper fermentation. If you harvest them too early, the beans will fail to ferment, resulting in a flat, bitter flavor and poor quality beans that buyers may reject.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni edarako lɛ bɛ sugar ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ lɛ Beans lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baa shi ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpoo lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I yank or pull cocoa pods directly off the tree stem with my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ minine gbalaa loo mikɛgbalaa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yanking pods off damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk where future pods grow. Using a sharp sickle or cutlass to make a clean cut leaves the flower cushion healthy for next season's crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ, efiteɔ fɔfɔii akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ baajɛ mli aba lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni naa wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ Nɔ ni ooofolɔ mli lɛ baaha fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What preparations should I make on my farm before the harvesting season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ hesaamɔi esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before harvesting begins, you should clear weeds around your trees, prune dead branches, clean and sharpen your cutting tools, and set up a clean, dry area for fermenting and drying your beans.
ga: Dani kpamɔ lɛ baaje shishi Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ofolɔ niji ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ. Tsumɔ nibii ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ ahe ni okɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni afee he ko ni he tse ni egbi ni akɛbaawo ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛgbi.

english: Why should I remove black or rotten cocoa pods from my trees if I cannot sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ediŋŋ loo ni egbo lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Leaving diseased or rotten pods on the tree allows fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread to healthy pods via rain drops and insects. Removing and burying them protects the rest of your yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni efite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kooloi bibii anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie ni ofu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat stress. Planting adequate shade trees helps keep the soil moist and reduces heavy leaf loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa baai babaoo ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to cover fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves after opening the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ plantain baai aha kookoo ŋmeii heei ahe beni agbele ŋmeii lɛ anaa lɛ?

english: Covering freshly extracted cocoa beans with plantain leaves traps the heat needed for fermentation. Proper fermentation destroys the bean germ, removes bitterness, and develops the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha kookoo yibii ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: How long should I leave my harvested cocoa pods before breaking them open?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni mikpa lɛ dani magbele amɛ?

english: It is best to break cocoa pods within two to four days after harvesting. Waiting too long can cause the beans inside to start germinating or rotting, which ruins their commercial value.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookumɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo ejwɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. ni fiteɔ jarayeli sɛɛnamɔi lɛ

english: Why do I need to spread my cocoa beans out in the sun to dry right after fermentation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-kokoo yibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes moisture from the fermented beans, stopping the fermentation process and preventing mold growth. Drying them completely ensures the beans can be stored and transported safely without spoiling.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔfi yibii ni edɔ lɛ amli. Ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ nifeemɔ lɛ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ egbi kwraa lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii lɛ toɔ ni akɛyaa shweshweeshwe ni efiteee.

english: Why should I avoid burning the cleared weeds on my field before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashãa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Burning weeds destroys useful organic matter that feeds the soil and holds moisture. When you leave cleared weeds to rot into the soil or turn them under, they act as natural food for your crops and help the soil stay moist during dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli lɛ. Beni ohaa jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo oshiɔ amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field help the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the season ends, this extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your next crop naturally, saving you money on fertilizer.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ be lɛ ba naagbee Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shika toɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo he.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai ni wa aba. Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but produce tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is shaded by tall trees, it uses all its energy to grow top leaves instead of storing food underground. Planting cassava in open sunlight and avoiding excess nitrogen encourages the plant to form fat, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo eyɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ ni ajie nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ, ni mli wa.

english: Why should I plant my crop seeds with wide spacing instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mabɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the dirt, resulting in thin stems and poor harvests. Giving each plant proper space allows it to spread roots and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny waste behind?
ga: Te eji tɛŋŋ akɛ maye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni mashi jwɛi fioo ko yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the funnel of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended sprays or clean wood ash into the center leaves helps stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei akutsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo tso sũ ni he tse ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather. Pruning extra shade trees to let in sun, clearing weeds, and picking off infected pods keeps the cocoa farm dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kroko lɛ afolɔ koni hulu la aba, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni ebaaha helai aba shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over easily at the base when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ eshishi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often damaged by small worms called nematodes or stem borers eating the root base inside the ground. Using clean suckers for new planting and keeping soil rich with compost strengthens the roots so the heavy plant stays upright.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers ni yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ plantain shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui heei amli, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ. koni tsei ni tsii lɛ anyɛ adamɔ shi jaŋŋ

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough rain water for me to start planting my seeds safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui aje shishi shweshweeshwe?

english: Dig down a hand's depth and squeeze a ball of soil; if it holds its shape comfortably without dripping water or falling apart into dust, there is enough moisture for seeds to sprout without rotting or drying out.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli ni okɛ muji lɛ ajie. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli mlɛo Nu ko bɛ ni hoɔ loo efoɔ kɛfeɔ sũ. Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo loo amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering. Mulching your field to keep soil dampness steady and adding lime or powdered eggshells to the soil prevents this rotting.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime loo powder ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni enɛ akafite.

english: Is it better for me to clear my whole farm at once or prepare it in small bits before planting cassava?
ga: Esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo asaa he bibii bibii. Dani abaadu ŋmei?

english: Preparing land in smaller, manageable sections allows you to plant on time without letting weeds regain control of cleared areas before you get the chance to plant your cassava cuttings.
ga: He ni asaa he yɛ he bibioo ko ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli ni jwɛi lɛ kuuu amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛkudɔ he ni ajie lɛ lɛ dani oná hegbɛ oduɔ ŋmei niji.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing so thin and falling over easily in the wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of developing thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a natural umbrella that protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa lɛ baa.

english: How often do I need to hand-water my maize crop if the rains stop early?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mikɛ minine afɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: Maize needs steady moisture when forming ears. Watering deeply two to three times a week during dry spells keeps the soil moist enough for the kernels to fill up completely.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ eefee toi. Kɛ́ afɔ nu shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ayi.

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce the area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from drying out during high heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo bei amli ni egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crop plants help them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and gradually breaks down into food for the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya ni efite fiofio akɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of leafy green branches but very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ niji kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi tomato fioo pɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which encourages the plant to use all its energy growing leaves rather than producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do weeds sprout and spread much faster than my crop seeds after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in the dirt for a long time, sprouting instantly when sunlight and rain hit the exposed soil, whereas cultivated crop seeds take longer to wake up and root.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: What causes deep holes inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the tender growing center of the corn plant during the day to feed on the fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida blɛoo lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and soft if I delay harvesting them after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛji mikɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ ni akpa lɛ?

english: When rain returns after a dry spell, the mature cassava plant draws stored energy from its tubers to grow new leaves, leaving the roots watery and fibrous inside.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni ato kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛkɛfee baai heei. Shi shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ tsɔji yɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade and holds soil moisture, protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to endure the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout and instead rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi edaaa ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings rot if they are cut from young, soft parts of the plant instead of mature wood, or if planted upside down. For good sprouting, use mature stems cut cleanly and plant them with the node buds pointing upward into well-drained soil.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli yɛ tso ni eda lɛ najiaŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ tsei ni he tse ni eda lɛ atsu nii ni odu ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to give my yam vines sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ maha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf rot and maximizing the energy sent down to build bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa hewalɛ ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient or that water is sitting around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK and ensuring proper soil drainage will help the leaves turn green so the plant can make food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he ni akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During extreme heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and protect themselves, usually recovering once the afternoon temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air temperature becomes too hot or when the plant experiences sudden changes between drought and heavy watering. These stress conditions prevent successful pollination, causing the flowers to shed.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni tsei naa tsakemɔi trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ waa lɛ teŋ lɛ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ shihilɛi nɛɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔii amli pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize feeds the soil naturally, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he loo yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves over the soil around my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, stops weeds from taking over, and prevents heavy rains from washing away nutrient-rich topsoil.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha nɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust-like waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged leaves and internal waste are key signs of Fall Armyworm infestation. These caterpillars hide inside the plant's growing point and feed quickly, requiring early application of recommended insecticides or neem extract to protect the crop yield.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela lɛ eba. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ daa yɛ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ nii oya. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii mra. Koni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why should I remove small shoots growing around my main plantain stem instead of leaving them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ plantain tsei wuji lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ fɛɛ oshwie lɛ

english: Leaving too many side shoots (suckers) forces the mother plantain stem to share its water and food with all of them, leading to smaller bunches. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong successors, ensuring large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehe bahia ni plantain tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii yɛ amɛ fɛɛ ateŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa, ni no baaha aduawai agbo ni tsii aba.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block direct heat and keep moisture in the soil while they establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni akɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli be mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is the best one for me to plant on my new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers—the ones with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base—are best. They have strong energy reserves and grow into healthier, higher-yielding plantain trees compared to broad-leafed suckers.
ga: Klante ŋmeii—ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse lɛ—ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft growing center of maize leaves. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf funnel helps protect your crop yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward sunlight and away from humid soil. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy to grow large tubers underground, while keeping leaves off wet ground prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulb agboi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ be mli ni baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How do I select the right cassava stem to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso ni abaafo ni adu koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose mature, healthy stems from the middle section of a harvested plant—about thumb-thickness with clear, undamaged bud nodes. Avoid dry, woody bases or soft green tips because they sprout weakly.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso ni akpa lɛ teŋgbɛ—ni tamɔ tsitsi ni mli tse, ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shishitoo ni egbi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants face extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium during flowering. Keeping soil evenly moist and mulched helps protect the flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Managing insects early prevents leaf distortion and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Mra be mli kooloi akwɛmɔ Ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu kɛ dalɛ ni baa shi lɛ naa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi nakai nɔŋŋ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ, ehaa nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: If previous crops had pale yellow leaves, grew slowly, or produced thin stalks and small harvests, your soil is depleted. Adding well-rotted animal manure or organic compost restores life and nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo, loo amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛkpaa nii fioo Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koolooi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni wala kɛ niyenii kpakpai aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if I give my plants enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa mitsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively underground for soil nutrients, root space, and moisture that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures all applied water and fertilizer go directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shi waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná sũ mli niyenii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food crop plants need for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Mulching around the base and keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the plant from shedding its flowers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: What causes small holes and brown powder inside the leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common caterpillar pest in Ghana. The brown powder is their waste, and applying recommended treatments or neem extract early in the morning can help control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Pauda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji jwɛi. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato leaves curl up to reduce water loss when the sun is very hot. It is the plant's natural defense against heat, and providing steady moisture early in the morning helps lower the plant's stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha be fɛɛ be leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ anɔ haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas on the land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting cowpeas after maize naturally restores soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi cowpea lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Cowpeas ni aaadu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable beds help my plants?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi-vegetable ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, prevents weeds from growing, holds moisture in the ground during hot days, and cools the roots of your crops.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwaa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni ehaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How will I know that my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Should I cut away the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, you should remove extra suckers so that only the main stem and one small follower remain. If too many suckers grow together, they steal food and water from each other, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ bibioo kome pɛ ahi shi. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why should I wait to plant my seeds instead of planting right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ koni madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba dani odu.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. It spreads quickly through rain splashes and untrimmed branches.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ mli Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the branches of my young cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ niji efuu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swelling in the stems and leaf discoloration are classic symptoms of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. It is spread by tiny mealybug insects and weakens the tree's ability to transport food.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni efuu kɛ baai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela lɛ he okadii ni ale waa. Mealybugs bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛ niyenii yaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods growing into strange, twisted shapes instead of normal pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ni efite yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ daa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Deformed pods usually occur when insects bite and feed on very young pods, or when severe fungal stress affects the pod tissue while it is still developing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni efite lɛ baa kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ ŋmeii bibii waa ni amɛye amɛ. aloo be mli ni fungal haomɔ ni naa wa saa pod tissue lɛ he yɛ be mli ni edara lolo lɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without ever forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a few percent become pods. Flowers drop if the tree is short on water or nutrients, or if there aren't enough tiny midges around to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ tsɔɔ pods. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Aloo bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during hot, dry winds is a survival mechanism. The cocoa tree sheds leaves to stop losing moisture through transpiration when water in the soil is scarce.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ naa kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: What causes the dark patches on my cocoa pods and the blasted, dry leaves at the top of my trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ kɛ baai ni efite ni egbi ni yɔɔ tsei ayiteŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by mirids (capsids), which are sap-sucking pests. Their toxic bites destroy leaf canopy and leave dark spots on young pods, reducing overall farm yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ nu lɛ. Amɛ tsofa fɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ shishi ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii fɛɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide the needed canopy shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive growth so the tree can send its water and energy directly into making healthy pods. It also opens the canopy to let sunlight and air pass through, reducing disease.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ dalɛ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛma ŋmeii ni wa. Egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ hu naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, ni no haa helai ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye kookoo tso ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of nutrient deficiency include pale or yellow leaves, weak flowering, and small, lightweight pods even when rainfall is adequate.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa lɛ ahe ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ ahe waaa. Ni ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa, eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ baashɛ he moŋ.

english: Pods are ready when their skin changes fully from green or red to a solid yellow or orange. Harvesting too early results in poor quality beans, while waiting too long causes beans to germinate inside.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo kɛji hewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa kɔfi yibii ni ehiii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them alone in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikome too midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a canopy shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after I harvest my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ko ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nutrients in the soil, leaving it exhausted. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa egbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn yellow during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and intense heat cause water to evaporate rapidly from soil and leaves. Without sufficient water in the soil, crop roots cannot absorb nutrients, leading to yellowing leaves and delayed growth.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa ni naa wa haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest, and why do the tubers rot if I leave them underground during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgboiɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving tubers in waterlogged soil during heavy rain starves the roots of air, causing fungal decay and tuber rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tuber ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it wrong for me to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baawo ŋmãa tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem causes 'chemical burn' on tender plant tissues due to high salt concentration. Fertilizer should be buried a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely reach out and draw in the nutrients.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ haa ‘Chemical burn’ baa tso lɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmei babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he inchi fioo ko pɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii.
