english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruits when I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yibii bibii yɛ be mli ni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces crops to compete for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets adequate light and nourishment to develop thick stems, healthy foliage, and large fruits.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse, baai ni wa, kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear the land and make mounds or ridges before planting yams or sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jɛmɛ ni afee gɔji loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Mounds create loose, topsoil-rich conditions that allow root tubers to expand easily without hard soil resistance. Ridges also improve soil drainage, preventing root rot during heavy rains while keeping essential moisture near the surface.
ga: Gɔji lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ yibii ni haa shishifãi lɛ amli tsei lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nyɛŋ ashi amɛ. Ridges hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize crop look like ragged holes have been eaten through them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant funnel. Inspecting crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps kill the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni agbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I collect seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again during the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuaa dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ naa ni maduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give high yields only in the first generation. Replanting saved hybrid seeds results in low yield, non-uniform crop growth, and reduced resistance to local pests and diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi. Tsei lɛ adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni ehaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai.

english: Why does putting dry grass or cocoa pods around the base of my pepper plants keep them healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ji jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Covering soil with organic materials is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents sunlight from evaporating moisture, stops weeds from growing, and decomposes into rich plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Kpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to produce high yields for one generation. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the new plants lose those strong parent traits, resulting in uneven growth and much smaller yields.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei laajeɔ nakai fɔlɔ sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and dry out easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as umbrellas and protect their tender leaves while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing them ensures the main plant gets all the food it needs to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-pattern from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing lots of green leaves but failing to produce flower pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Over-fertilizing can prevent cowpeas from setting pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ cowpea naa koni ekafee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines on wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kakadaji ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to sunlight while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ, kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Heavy, waterlogged soil suffocates the roots and creates ideal conditions for rot fungi to attack.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to discard the bloom.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa, ni no haa tso lɛ wooo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense response to conserve moisture. By rolling its leaves inward, the pepper plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to prevent water loss.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛbuɔ he koni akɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni nu akaje mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and excess moisture. Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops suffer much less insect damage when grown inside a net structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-aduawai lɛ fiteee kwraa kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ trellis mli lɛ?

english: The fine netting acts as a physical barrier that keeps destructive flying insects like whiteflies, moths, and beetles away from your plants, preventing them from eating leaves and laying eggs.
ga: Mesh kpakpa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni fɔ̃ɔ ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ahe. Enɛ haaa amɛye baai ni amɛkawo ŋmeii.

english: Why do plant leaves develop white powder or mold spots when packed tightly inside a net house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ powda yɛŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛji akɛ amɛwo trellis shĩa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Enclosed structures hold moisture in the air. When crops are crowded without good airflow, high humidity creates a wet environment where fungal diseases like powdery mildew thrive.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: Why do crops grown under shade netting seem to require less frequent watering during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he ehiaaa nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade netting blocks intense direct sunlight and reduces hot winds. This keeps the soil cooler, slowing down water evaporation from the ground and reducing moisture loss from plant leaves.
ga: Shading nets lɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my peppers and tomatoes get pale, burnt spots on their skin when grown in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ mi-tomato lɛ hewolo nɔ shãa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Direct exposure to strong sunlight over-heats the fruit skin, causing 'sunscald' or tissue burn. Protective covers or natural leaf shade block these harsh rays and preserve fruit appearance.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yibii lɛ adɔ fe nine, ni ekɛ ‘hulutsoo’ loo fãji ni shãa lɛ aba. Nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he loo adebɔɔ mli baa he ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ la ni naa wa nɛɛ he, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ahe feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do leafy vegetables like lettuce grow larger leaves under light shade netting than in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ lettuce lɛ woɔ baai wuji yɛ trellis shishi fe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight is slightly reduced by shade, plants expand the surface area of their leaves to capture as much light as possible, resulting in wider, softer leaves.
ga: Beni hulu la lɛ baa shi fioo kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsei lɛɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛmɔ la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow much taller inside a protected net house than outside in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ mi-trellis ni buɔ he lɛ mli fe kponɔgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants naturally reach upward when light is filtered by a net cover. This soft light causes the stems to stretch tall, requiring staking or trellising to support their height.
ga: Tsei baate shi kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ la tsɔ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli. Kane ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Ebiɔ ni akɛ staking loo trellis awo mli koni ekɛfi tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable plants flowering heavily inside a net house but failing to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ mi-trellis lɛ mli shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Fine nets keep out insect pests, but they also block beneficial pollinators like bees. Without insects or strong winds to move pollen between blooms, flowers drop off without setting fruit.
ga: Fine mesh yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Shi etsĩɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii hu anaa. Kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswaaa pollen yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Does growing crops in a warm, covered shelter help them mature faster than outdoor crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shia mli ni ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, a sheltered structure maintains warm, stable temperatures and protects plants from weather stress, allowing them to absorb nutrients continuously and mature earlier.
ga: Hɛɛ, wɔɔhe gbɛjianɔtoo baaha dɔlɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ahi shi daa. ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai daa ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do heavy downpours destroy open-field crops but leave covered crops unharmed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani tsei ni aha nɔ lɛ eyeee awui?

english: Hard rain physically tears delicate leaves, knocks off flowers, and compacts the soil. Protective covers break heavy raindrops into a fine mist, safeguarding the plant's structure.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbálaa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ gbálaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ afua bibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ shishitoo he

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without forming fruit during extremely hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat places severe stress on plants, causing them to shed their flowers to conserve water and survive, which stops them from producing fruit until temperatures cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei afɔse amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haaa tsei awo yibii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: If my crop seedlings arrive at my farm late in the evening after a long journey, should I plant them immediately or wait until daybreak?
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ bashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛkɛ mli yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Ani esa akɛ madu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mamɛ kɛyashi jetsɛremɔ?

english: It is best to leave them in a shaded, cool place overnight and plant them early in the morning. Planting at night in the dark can lead to poor soil placement, while planting in the morning allows seedlings to settle into the moist ground before the heat of the afternoon sun arrives.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni odu leebi. Kɛ́ adu nii gbɛkɛ yɛ duŋ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ leebi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ dani shwane hulu lɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young plant seedlings look weak and wilted after being transported in a vehicle for many hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni akɛ amɛ wo tsɔne mli ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During long travel, heat builds up inside vehicles and wind blows away moisture. The seedlings lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, causing their stems and leaves to droop from heat stress.
ga: yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa. Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: What is the best way to keep my cocoa seedlings safe overnight if I cannot plant them on the day they arrive?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mahã mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔɔŋ kome kɛji minyɛɛɛ madu amɛ yɛ gbi ni dumɔwui lɛ baashɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Keep the seedlings upright under a thick tree shade or shelter, protect them from direct wind and goats, and sprinkle a little water on their roots so the soil in their bags stays moist until morning.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ama tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe loo he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shishi. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ tooi ahe. Ni okɛ nu fioo afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi leebi.

english: Should I water my seedlings immediately after they arrive from a hot, long trip?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo dumɔwui lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eba lɛ?

english: Yes, but move them into deep shade first and let them cool down for a short while before giving them a gentle watering. Watering hot plants in direct sun can shock their root systems.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi tsi amɛ kɛya he ko ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni oha amɛhe ajɔɔ minitii fioo komɛi dani okɛ nu awo amɛmli fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ amli yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe afee shoo.

english: What happens to young crops if I plant them under the strong afternoon sun instead of early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi moŋ fe leebi?

english: The harsh afternoon sun bakes the bare topsoil and causes rapid water evaporation from the crop leaves, which can scorch fragile young plants and kill their tender roots before they establish.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni efite amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Can cassava stem cuttings still grow well after spending several days in transit across regions?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni afo lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ gbii babaoo ni akɛtee kpokpai anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems are hardy and store energy inside their stalks. As long as they are kept shaded and dry during transit so they do not dry out completely or rot, they will sprout successfully when planted.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei lɛ amli. Shii abɔ ni akɛ amɛ toɔ shia mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Koni ekagbi loo ekafite. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested vegetables from spoiling when transporting them on a long road trip to distant markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite beni mikɛyaa gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvest early when temperatures are cool, pack the produce in ventilated wooden crates instead of airtight plastic sacks, and cover the load with wet jute bags to keep the temperature down during travel.
ga: Kpamɔ mra be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ Pack nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso adekai amli ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ awo plastic kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ najiaŋ. ni okɛ jute kotoku ni mli efɔ aha nɔ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly after long transportation from the farm to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee jara nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy pressure from tightly packed sacks combined with heat buildup during long travel causes tomatoes to bruise. Bruised fruits release juices that allow soft-rot bacteria to spread rapidly through the entire load.
ga: Nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ kotokui ni awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli kɛ dɔlɛ ni abua naa yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yibii ni etse lɛ jieɔ nu, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe to transport seed yams in an open vehicle during the hot, dry season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui baawo tsɔne ni agbele mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Transporting seed yams in an open truck exposes them to direct sun and dry winds, which dehydrates the tubers and damages their growing buds. Cover them with dry straw or woven mats to shield them from heat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ wo lɔle ni agbele mli lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ baaha nu ajie ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ebaafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsɔji ni akpɛ lɛ aha nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my dried grains survive long travel easily while my leafy greens wilt within a few hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Dried grains have very low moisture content and are dormant, making them resistant to heat. Leafy greens are living tissues filled with water that continuously breathe and lose moisture once cut from the root.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ mli nu faaa kwraa ni amɛhiɛ edɔ. Ehaa ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli Leafy greens ji fãji ni hiɛ ka ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji afo kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from heat stress until their roots become strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Extremely heavy rain packs the soil too tightly and fills all the air gaps with water. Without air in the flooded soil, the seeds drown and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli hei lɛ eyiɔ nu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves wither and droop during the dry season, but the plant stays alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani tso lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo?

english: Plantains slow down their leaf growth and let older leaves dry out during hot weather to conserve water. This is a natural survival habit so the main trunk stays alive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains haa baai lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ su. No hewɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: When too many seeds are planted in one spot, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing allows each stalk to get enough nutrients to grow strong and yield big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning purple or dark red during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ purple loo etsuru ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When cassava leaves turn purple or reddish, it usually means the plant lacks phosphorus in the soil. Phosphorus helps roots grow big and strong, so adding organic compost or phosphate fertilizer helps solve this.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ tsɔ purple loo red Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ phosphorus yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo fɔsfɛt ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ tomato fioo lɛ?

english: Giving tomatoes too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing leaves instead of fruit. Switch to fertilizers higher in potassium and phosphorus once they start flowering to encourage fruit growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tomato lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium kɛ phosphorus fa yɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji fɔfɔii je shishi ni ekanya aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by insects. Removing damaged leaves and spraying neem oil helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ajie baai ni efite lɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting inside the ground before it is even time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani be po shɛɔ ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot in wet soil is usually caused by fungal or bacterial infections spreading in flooded soil or through damaged seed yams. Planting in high, well-drained mounds prevents water from collecting around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli loo kɛtsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni efite lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my garden egg flowers keep falling off the stem without turning into vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat, dry soil, or lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na amanehulu yɛ latsaa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall stems above the ground, but only tiny tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi ni kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ mikpa lɛ, ŋmei bibioo ko pɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots cannot swell if the soil is packed too hard or lacks potassium. Loosening the soil into raised mounds or ridges makes it easy for the roots to expand into large tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli kɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil cool and moist, protecting the young cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip and moving down the middle of the lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-composted manure will help the plant regain its green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know which direction to face my cassava stem cuttings when planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ makwɛ yucca niji lɛ ahiɛ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Make sure the tiny buds or nodes on the stem point upward toward the sky. Planting stem cuttings upside down slows down sprouting and leads to poor root development.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ tso ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi nɔ Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to chew holes inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaves (whorl) to feed. Applying approved pest control early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf center helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (rings) koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: The first rain after a dry spell is often followed by several days or weeks of heat without rain. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up due to a lack of continuous moisture. It is best to wait until the rainy season fully settles.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ, gbii loo otsii babaoo ni mli edɔɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ sɛɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli aba shi kwraa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and dark shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and clearing heavy weeds around your cocoa trees helps dry out the farm and stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɔlɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie jwɛi ni tsii ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ. Cacao tsei lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni ekpa helai.

english: Can I put fresh droppings from my chicken coop directly onto my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ kooloi atsu lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is very strong and produces heat, which can burn plant roots and kill them. You should allow the manure to dry out and rot in a pile (compost) for a few weeks before mixing it into your farm soil.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni egbe amɛ. Esa akɛ oha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni egbo yɛ ŋmeii (compost) mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences stress from erratic watering or extreme heat. Maintaining consistent, regular watering prevents flower drop and allows the plant to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa, daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do farmers rub dry wood ash on the cut pieces of yam setts before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ tso sũ ni egbi shwieɔ sweet potato ni afo lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Wood ash acts as a natural protective shield. It dries out the cut surface of the yam sett, preventing soil insects and fungal rot from attacking the seed yam before it sprouts.
ga: Tso sũ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibii. Ehaa sweet potato lɛ hiɛ ni afo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I trim the bottom bulb and cut off the old roots of a plantain sucker before planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shishigbɛ ni mafo sucker tsei lɛ ashishifãi momoi dani madu?

english: Trimming the bulb allows you to inspect and peel off hidden root pests like nematodes and weevil larvae. It also encourages the sucker to shoot fresh, healthy new roots once planted in your field.
ga: Kɛtsɔ yitso ni ooofo lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ ni ojie shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ nematodes kɛ weevil larvae lɛ. Ewoɔ mɛi ni nuɔ nu lɛ hewalɛ hu koni amɛtswa shishifãi heei, ni yɔɔ ehee, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛdu amɛ yɛ oyale mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before the problem spreads to my entire farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Look for early signs like yellowing leaves, swollen stems, unusual spots on pods, or leaves falling off early. Catching these symptoms early allows you to seek help from an officer before the whole farm gets affected.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ baai ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni efuu, hei ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. loo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Omɔ okadii nɛɛ mra Enɛ baaha otao yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ mli dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: Can a sick cocoa tree heal on its own if I give it extra water and care?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ atsa kɛji miha lɛ nu kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko?

english: Minor problems can improve with good care, but severe diseases like viral infections cannot heal on their own. Leaving a severely diseased tree in the ground usually causes the illness to spread to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Abaanyɛ asaa naagbai bibii kɛtsɔ hiɛdɔɔ kpakpa nɔ. Shi helai ni mli wa tamɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ Enyɛŋ etsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What should I do immediately if I notice strange symptoms on my cocoa trees?
ga: Kɛji ona okadi ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You should report the issue to your local extension officer right away, avoid moving plant parts or soil from the affected area, and clean your farm tools so you do not carry the disease to healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he nitsulɔ lɛ he amaniɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãi loo shikpɔŋ ni oootsi kɛjɛ he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ he. Ni otsumɔ oŋmɔ mli nibii ahe koni amɛkɛ helai akabote ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do crops seem to get sick more often during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hela shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal diseases, such as Black Pod, to grow and spread rapidly across leaves, branches, and pods.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ baai, tsei aniji kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ateŋ.

english: Why do government officers insist on cutting down cocoa trees when disease is found on a farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mli onukpai maa nɔ mi akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei beni ana helai yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Certain serious diseases, like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, have no chemical cure and spread quickly. Cutting down infected trees is necessary to create a barrier and save the surrounding healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Helai komɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ bɛ tsofa ni akɛtsaa amɛ, ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya. Ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛfee gbɛtsii nii ko ni akɛbu kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: If my sick cocoa trees are cut down, how long must I wait before planting new ones?
ga: Kɛji afo kookoo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu ekoŋŋ?

english: You generally need to clear all diseased plant material and wait a few months to ensure the pests or viruses in the soil and surrounding area are completely gone before planting fresh, healthy seedlings.
ga: Nɔ titri ni he baahia ni ojie tsei ahe nibii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni mɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ kɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ fɛɛ etee dani odu dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does the government offer support or new seedlings to farmers whose diseased trees are removed?
ga: Ani nɔyeli lɛ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ loo dumɔwui heei haa okwaafoi ni jieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, national cocoa control programs often support farmers by providing technical guidance, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings, and assistance to help restore affected farms after treatment.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ maŋ kookoo nɔkwɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoi yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi kɛtsɔ ŋaawoo ni amɛkɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Kookoo dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa ni asaa ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ helatsamɔ sɛɛ.

english: What information should I share with the cocoa extension officer when they visit my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ saji esa akɛ mikɛ cocoa extension nitsulɔi lɛ agba kɛji amɛbasara miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Tell the officer when you first noticed the problem, which section of the farm is affected, whether neighboring farms have similar issues, and what fertilizers or chemicals you recently used.
ga: Ha nitsulɔi lɛ ale kɛji ona naagba ko klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Mɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fãi enaa he sɛɛ? Ani ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hu yɛ naagbai ni tamɔ nɛkɛ? ni mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai okɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: Can my farm tools spread disease from one crop to another?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: Yes, fungal spores and viruses stick to cutlasses, pruners, and boots. Cleaning your tools with soap or sanitizer after working on sick plants prevents spreading sickness to healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dadei ahe. pruning knife and boots Kɛ́ okɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai tsu odɛŋdadei ahe nii beni ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Will applying more fertilizer cure my cocoa trees if they are already diseased?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni ahere cacao tso lɛ yiwala kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ ehiɛ hela momo?

english: Fertilizer helps healthy trees grow stronger, but it cannot cure a plant that has a viral or destructive disease. Applying fertilizer to a heavily diseased tree will not save it and can be a waste of resources.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa. Shi enyɛŋ etsa tsei ni helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli loo helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsei ni helai emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ hereŋ tso lɛ yiwala, ni eji nibii ni afiteɔ.

english: Why do my crops wither so fast during the dry season even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot dry weather, intense sunlight and wind dry out the topsoil fast, causing small amounts of water to evaporate before the crop's roots can pull it in.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu fioo ko shwieɔ shi dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ mli.

english: Why do some crops survive dry season heat while others die very quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya waa lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root structures; crops with deep taproots can pull moisture from deep underground, while crops with shallow roots rely only on surface water that dries up quickly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi srɔtoi. Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my dry season crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo mi tsei ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground acts like an umbrella for the soil, keeping the direct sun from drying out ground moisture and keeping root temperatures cool.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni eha shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How can I tell if the early rains are steady enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ehi shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: A single early rain only wets the surface; you need multiple continuous days of rain so the wetness penetrates deep where root systems can stay moist.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ. Ehe miihia ni nugbɔ anɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni nu lɛ abote he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Is it safer to plant my crops immediately after the very first rain or wait for the rain pattern to stabilize?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo aaamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Waiting for steady rain patterns prevents seeds from germinating after a single rain and then dying if a dry spell follows immediately.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ. ni ebaanyɛ egbo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do newly planted crops need much more attention and care than crops that have been on the field for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu ehee lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni ehi ŋmɔ mli afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak root networks that cannot search deep for food and water, making them fragile until their root systems mature.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ atao niyenii kɛ nu mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why do crops planted several years ago handle harsh sunny weather much better than young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ hulutsoo be he nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Older plants have had years to grow deep root systems that reach underground moisture reserves hidden deep below the dry surface soil.
ga: Tsei ni edara lɛ he miihia afii babaoo dani amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ adara kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I expand my farm to a larger plot this year, why might my crops need more water than they did on my smaller plot?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ tee he ko ni da afi nɛɛ Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: More plants sharing a large field consume soil water faster, and open fields lose moisture quickly to wind and heat across a larger surface area.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni jaa he ko yɛ ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ nu lɛ oya. Ni ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops look yellow and weak during intense sunshine even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants, causing them to close their leaf pores to save water, which temporarily stops them from taking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei tsiɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do my crops suffer more from heat when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crops aggressively compete with each other for limited water and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weaker under intense sun.
ga: planted too close Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why did my crop yield turn out so small this year even though we received some rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ afi nɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainfall is only one part of crop growth. Crops also need food from the ground, so if your soil lacks essential nutrients or fertilizer, the plants cannot form big yields even with good rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ fã kome pɛ. Niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii babaoo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po.

english: Can poor soil cause my crops to fail even if it rains heavily throughout the season?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ po sɛɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain alone cannot replace missing soil nutrients. If the soil is exhausted and lacks proper fertilizer or organic matter, crops will remain small and yield poorly regardless of rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ atsake niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni sa bɛ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii ni amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning yellow even when the soil has enough moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nutrient deficiency, particularly nitrogen, in the soil. It means your plant is starving for nutrients even though it has enough water to drink.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. titri lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otsei lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnuɔ yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: How does fertilizer help my yam plants form bigger tubers underground?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer supplies key nutrients like potassium and phosphorus that strengthen the roots and allow the plant to produce and store food underground, which expands the yam tubers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni baaha sweet potato tubers lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my poor harvest was caused by lack of rain or by bad soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ ni mikpaa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Drought usually causes plants to dry up and wither early, whereas poor soil causes plants to stay small, turn yellow, or produce tiny fruits even while staying green and watered.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haa tsei lɛ gbiɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa tsei feɔ bibii. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ewo aduawai bibii Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni nu yɔɔ mli, moŋ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops look healthier than mine when we both faced the same dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe mi nɔ lɛ, be mli ni wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔmiikpe hulutsoo be kome lɛ?

english: Crops grown in fertile soil with adequate fertilizer develop stronger, deeper root systems. These deep roots help the plant find deep underground moisture and withstand dry periods better.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli kwɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do to get a good crop harvest when the weather and rain are unpredictable?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli?

english: Focusing on soil fertility by adding manure or fertilizer helps crops build strong root systems that make the most of whatever little rain falls during unpredictable seasons.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛŋmɔ ma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. Enɛ kɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my yams yield very large tubers in some years but very small ones in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ naa tubers wuji waa yɛ afii komɛi amli shi amɛnáa bibii waa yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers feed heavily on soil nutrients. If you plant yams in the same field without replenishing the soil nutrients with fertilizer or manure, the soil becomes depleted, leading to smaller harvests in later years.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ odu sweet potatoes yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baafee bibioo yɛ wɔsɛɛ afii amli.

english: Is it really necessary to apply fertilizer to traditional crops like yams in Ghana?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo blema ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, yams extract large amounts of nutrients from the soil to grow big tubers. Adding fertilizer restores worn-out soil and helps produce larger, healthier yams consistently.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does planting yams on the same piece of land every year affect how they grow?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ saa dalɛ he?

english: Yes, growing yams repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients needed for tuber growth, leading to poor yields over time unless you rotate crops or apply fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa yɛ be ni sa mli. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli.

english: How long does standard maize usually take from the day I plant it until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Most common maize varieties in Ghana require roughly four months (90 to 120 days) of continuous care, water, and nutrients to fully mature and yield dry grain.
ga: Abele henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ biɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ daa, ahaa nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni ekwɛ ni ewo ŋmeii ni egbi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt so fast if I stop pumping irrigation water for just a week during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji mikpa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwiemɔ otsi kome pɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes and peppers have shallow roots and need steady moisture throughout their 3- to 4-month growing cycle; stopping water disrupts their flow of nutrients, causing leaves to wilt and flowers to drop.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ehe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi enɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni ekɛdaraa lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nu ni kpaɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni fɔfɔi lɛ hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do fall armyworms cause so much damage to my maize during the first few months of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni ekɛmiida lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young maize plants produce soft, nutrient-rich leaves during their initial growth period, which attracts armyworms; unmanaged pests can destroy the crop before it completes its 4-month lifecycle.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ woɔ baai bibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ beaŋ. ni gbalaa ŋmeii Ŋmeii ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ dani amɛgbe amɛ nyɔji ejwɛ wala be lɛ naa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crop to get the highest yield for my investment?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni maná shika babaoo kɛjɛ mishika ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer is most effective when applied early in the crop's 4-month cycle—once at planting or germination, and again during the rapid growth phase before flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ mli mra, klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii loo beni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni edaa oya dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off during dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during prolonged dry periods as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss and save energy until moisture becomes available again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi ni akɛ hewalɛ toɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and grow mold if I bag them immediately after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops carry high internal moisture; if they are not dried using solar or mechanical powered driers before storage, heat and fungi build up rapidly and ruin the grain.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ mligbɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo. Kɛji akɛ akɛ hulu loo tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii tsuuu nii dani akɛtoɔ. Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa oya ni efiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Overcrowded crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or poorly developed fruits.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii loo ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring crops throughout the season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants designed to rapidly soak up ground water and nutrients, which can starve young crops unless you clear the field early in the season.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya. ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aye hɔmɔ Ja ojie jɛmɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does running power machinery like pumps or processing mills continuously throughout the farming season cost so much money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ shika babaoo ni akɛyaa nɔ atsuɔ tsɔnei ni haa hewalɛ tamɔ pɔmp loo nitsumɔhe ni tsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Powered machinery requires a constant supply of fuel or grid electricity over the 3 to 4 months of crop production, making power and maintenance one of the largest monthly expenses for a modern farm.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ biɔ ni akɛ fuɛl loo sarawa hewalɛ aba be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa srawa hewalɛ kɛ ekwɛmɔ he nyɔmɔwoo feɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ ko mli nyɔmɔwoo ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome.

english: How do I know if the water from my local stream is safe to use for watering my vegetable crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni jɛɔ mimaŋ faa lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii kɛwo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Dirty or contaminated water can spread soil-borne diseases to crops like tomatoes and peppers, causing rot or leaf wilting. Clean, untreated water ensures plants absorb soil nutrients without carrying harmful bacteria that stunt their growth.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ agbala helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgboɔ. Nu ni mli tse ni atsuuu he nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground even when the leaves above look completely healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When farm water pools around roots in poorly drained soil, it suffocates the underground tubers by cutting off oxygen, causing fungal rot before any visible signs appear on the green leaves above.
ga: Beni nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tubers lɛ shwieɔ mumɔ kɛtsɔ oxygen ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fiteɔ dani okadii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants lose leaves under strong heat to protect themselves from losing too much moisture. Providing temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava keeps the surrounding air humid and prevents solar heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni akɛhaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni atsĩ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli baa lɛ naa

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival trick maize uses to reduce leaf surface exposure to direct sunlight and conserve internal water. If the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, however, it means the soil is dangerously dry.
ga: Baa ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la baa shi lɛ shi. ni ato nu he gbɛjianɔ yɛ mli Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ oshara gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my pepper leaves during foggy morning weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ leebi ni afua yɔɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity and cool morning fog create the perfect environment for powdery mildew spores to grow on leaf surfaces, which blocks sunlight and slows down the plant's ability to produce food.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ leebi afua ni mli ejɔ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha powdery mildew spores ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ niyenii.

english: What causes broad ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and how does it slow down crop growth?
ga: Mɛni kɛ pores ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi?

english: Ragged leaf holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the foliage, which reduces the plant's green leaf surface area needed to capture sunlight and convert it into growth energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni emɔ hulu la ni etsake lɛ ewo dalɛ hewalɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato stems suddenly wilt and collapse overnight without any yellowing of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting without leaf yellowing is typically bacterial wilt, where bacteria multiply inside the plant's water-carrying tubes, completely blocking water flow from the roots to the upper branches.
ga: Trukaa ni egboɔ ni baai lɛ efeee ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Muawai lɛ baafa babaoo yɛ tso lɛ nu ni akɛyaa paipii lɛ amli. Etsiɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ naa kwraa.

english: How many suckers should I leave on one plantain plant to get large, heavy bunches?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii enyiɛ yɛ sɛɛ koni maná ŋmeii agbo ni tsii?

english: Leaving only three shoots per stool (one bearing mother, one large follower, and one small infant) stops the plants from competing with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii etɛ pɛ yɛ ŋmeii kome mli (nyɛ kome, sɛɛnyiɛlɔ agbo kome kɛ abifao bibioo kome) lɛ, ehaa tsei kɛ amɛhe wooo akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo babaoo kɛha tsei.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and bushy after applying fertilizer but fail to produce flowers or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi loo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes crops to focus all energy on leaf and stem growth instead of reproductive growth. Crops need balanced phosphorus and potassium to initiate flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, e ji fɔmi blɔ nya tomi ɔ mi wami. Tsei he miihia ni amɛná phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Does lifting yam vines onto tall wooden stakes really make the yam tuber under the ground grow bigger?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ haa sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the leaves to generate more sugars that feed directly into enlarging the underground tuber.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa baai lɛ holeɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ sugar babaoo ni ekɛyeɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize gets too hot and thirsty, it rolls its leaves inward to hide them from direct sunlight. This behavior helps the plant trap moisture inside so it loses less water to the hot air.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kumai miiye lɛ Ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ekɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: When water becomes scarce, cassava drops its older leaves on purpose to reduce the amount of water it needs to survive. The plant goes into a resting state during the drought and will produce fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Cassava shwieɔ baai momoi koni ekɛba nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ shi. Tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ mli mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ebaawo baai eŋɔli heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has tiny roots that pull free nitrogen out of the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize adds natural plant food to the dirt so your crop grows better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi bibii. No gbalaa nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close to each other, why do they grow tall and thin without giving big corn ears?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Mɛni hewɔ ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋmãa toi wuji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of using energy to grow big corn ears, the plants waste all their energy stretching upward just to reach sunlight over their neighbors.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛkwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji Tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It keeps the ground cool, stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water, and prevents unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why must I put tall wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves wide in direct sunlight to manufacture energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp dirt where they could rot and lets them catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli babaoo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baabu tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ muji ni mli ewo fɔ ni baanyɛ afite ni eha hulu la ashɛ enɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a strong rain wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep main roots going far down into the earth; instead, they have shallow roots spreading near the surface. Because heavy fruit bunches make the top very heavy, strong winds easily pull those shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi titrii ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, shi moŋ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Akɛni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Nomɛi jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack nutrients in the soil, or lack tiny midges (insects) to pollinate them. When the tree senses it cannot support full pods, it drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ afee pollination ni bɛ, beni tso lɛ nuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning rather than at mid-day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the soil absorb the moisture before heat sets in. In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates before plant roots can drink it, and hot water droplets left on leaves can burn the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani latsaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava spoil and turn dark inside just two or three days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ egbo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you harvest cassava, detaching the roots creates tiny wounds. The root tries to protect itself by producing natural defence chemicals, but exposed to air, these chemicals cause the tissue inside to turn dark and spoil very quickly.
ga: Beni okpaa ŋmei Shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa pilamɔ bibioo ko baa. Shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ tsofai nɛɛ wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ duŋ ni egboɔ oya waa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dying when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight because their foliage is delicate and burns easily. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living canopy that shields the young trees and keeps the soil moist until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana typically begin bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years before they produce their first yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee ekome yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the lower branches of my young cashew trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning the lower branches of cashew trees forces the plant to direct its nutrients and energy upward. This creates a strong main trunk and a higher canopy, which makes harvesting easier and improves overall nut yield.
ga: Cashew tso niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ aya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso titri ni mli wa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I know which end of the cassava stem to put into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mli kɛ́ midu?

english: When planting cassava stem cuttings, make sure the small leaf buds or nodes are pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the shoots to grow downward first, resulting in weak plants and poor tuber formation.
ga: Kɛji oodu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmei bibii loo ŋmei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ oodu tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber ni ehiii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden poles to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to build up energy and grow big tubers below the ground. Staking the vines holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them off the damp soil, which reduces the risk of leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa la, ni ehaaa eshɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha baa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my plantain crop sprout many small plants around the main trunk, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ tsei bibii babaoo ebɔle tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Plantain plants produce suckers from their base to reproduce. You should cut away most extra suckers—leaving only one or two strong ones—so they do not steal water and nutrients away from the main plant while it is producing a bunch.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ koni amɛfɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baatsi nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the center of lower leaves is a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost will help the leaves stay dark green and support healthy corn cob growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off mainly due to environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper blossom ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I grow maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii tamɔ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for essential resources like soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. If weeds are not cleared early, your crops will be starved of food and grow slowly, leading to small yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛji akɛ atsaaa jwɛi lɛ mra. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii ni sa ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ fiofio. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is a main food plants need to grow. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil, keeping the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: My tomato plants have very bushy green leaves, so why are they not producing any flowers?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ amɛfɔɔɔ fɔfɔi kwraa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing big leaves instead of flowers. To get fruits, the soil needs phosphorus, which encourages the plant to bloom.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia phosphorus, ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather or when small insect pests like mirids attack them. Keeping good shade trees and protecting the trees from sap-sucking insects helps the flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ otsei lɛ wo hulutsoo mli ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Curled yellow leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. A sick plant cannot make enough food, which results in very small cassava roots at harvest time.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi bibii waa baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are my pepper fruits rotting and turning black from the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked all at once. This uneven water stops the plant from absorbing calcium, causing the bottom of the pepper to rot.
