ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, etsɔ nu trukaa. Nu ni ejaaa nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná calcium. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shishi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and thin instead of large and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ mlɛo moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deeply dug soil to push downwards easily. If the soil is hard, clay-heavy, or full of stones, the tuber struggles to expand and becomes twisted and small.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni abaanyɛ akumɔ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni akɛtsi kɛya shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni tsii loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbaafee mɛi ni etse amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I harvested to plant next season, or must I buy fresh seed packets?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei yɛ paketii amli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize will produce weak plants with lower yields in the second season. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures every seed grows into a strong, high-yielding plant that resists local diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ aba ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai

english: What will happen if I plant my plantain suckers very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu plantain tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their large leaves block the sunlight from each other, and their roots fight for nutrients. This causes the trees to grow very tall and thin, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɔlɔɔ waa ni amɛhe tseee, ni no haa amɛfeɔ jwɛi bibii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of leaves during the main rainy season but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Some cowpea varieties rely on shorter daylight hours to start producing flowers. Also, very heavy rains can wash away or damage the delicate flowers before they have a chance to turn into cowpea pods.
ga: Cowpea henɔi komɛi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo be kuku nɔ koni amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi. Kɛfata he lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ loo egbe fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛtsɔ tsina ŋmeii.

english: Why do my okra plants drop their leaves during the dry hot season even when I water them a little bit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu fioo pɛ woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Okra plants shed their leaves in extreme heat to stop losing water through their foliage. Giving them just a little water on top of the soil isn't enough; the roots need deep watering to keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Roselle tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ akpa. Nu fioo ko pɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaaha lɛ faaa. Nu ni mli kwɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if the seeds I buy in the market are approved by the Ministry of Agriculture?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni Ministry of Agriculture lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ?

english: Government-approved seeds come in sealed, official packages with certification tags, batch numbers, and stamps from agricultural authorities to prove they have been tested for good quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ baa yɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli ni amralo lɛ efo mli ni nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ eji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ eji lɛ nɔ, yibɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ stamp ni jɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ dɛŋ lɛ mli koni akɛtsɔɔ akɛ aka amɛ akwɛ akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy seeds from registered extension dealers instead of regular grain sellers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ moŋ fe tso dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Registered dealers sell certified seeds that have high germination rates and pest resistance, whereas regular market grain is meant for eating and may not grow well or carry crop diseases.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛnɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmaa ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni aye ni ekolɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ loo eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai.

english: Where do the new crop varieties that withstand drought actually come from?
ga: Nɛgbɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ jɛɔ?

english: Agricultural research institutes and universities breed and test these specialized crops for years before the Ministry of Agriculture releases them to officers and farmers.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ hei kɛ okwaayeli he univɛsitii baatsu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ ahe nii ni amɛka amɛ amɛkwɛ afii babaoo dani Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baajie amɛ kpo etsɔɔ onukpai kɛ okwaafoi.

english: Can I trust seeds distributed through government farm initiatives to grow well on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mihe afɔ̃ dumɔwui ni ajaa kɛtsɔɔ nɔyeli ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi anɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, government-endorsed seeds undergo trials across different regions to ensure they are compatible with local soils, climate conditions, and local crop diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, aka dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛ yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ. Enɛ ji koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akpã gbee. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ

english: What makes certified cassava cuttings better than the cuttings I collect from my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei ni afo ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hi fe ŋmei ni jɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified cuttings are produced under strict supervision to ensure they are completely free of mosaic virus and bred to yield heavier tubers than random farm cuttings.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmeii ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni ana akɛ mosaic hela ko bɛ mli kwraa. ni afɔ lɛ koni ekɛ yitsei ni tsii fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni afolɔ trukaa lɛ aba.

english: What is seed multiplication, and how does it affect my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui babaoo? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Seed multiplication is the specialized process of growing pure parent seeds under strict controls to produce large quantities of high-quality seeds that yield uniform, strong crops.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni anáa lɛ ji gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nyɛ dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ anɔ yɛ kudɔmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni akɛdumɔwui babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni mli wa lɛ aba.

english: Why do crops grown from my saved maize seeds produce smaller harvests than when I bought fresh seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ wo yibii fioo fe beni mihe dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their hybrid strength and disease resistance over generations, causing plants to grow weaker and produce smaller cobs compared to freshly produced certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite hybrid hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni afee ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why are all the plants from my certified seed bag growing at the exact same height and timing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fɛɛ ni jɛ mi dumɔwui kotokui ni awo he odase lɛ amli lɛ daa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo kɛ sɛɛkpeemɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds come from controlled multiplication programs, meaning they share uniform genetics so every plant matures, flowers, and fruits at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jɛɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akudɔɔ ni akɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ daa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli.

english: Can diseases from this season's sick plants pass to next season's crop if I save seeds from them?
ga: Ani helai ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ to?

english: Yes, many fungi and bacteria live inside the seed itself. Planting seeds saved from infected crops carries the disease directly into your new field, causing premature plant failure.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi babaoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya ohe hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: What causes some seeds to fail to sprout even when I plant them in good soil with enough rain?
ga: Mɛni tsiɔ dumɔwui komɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Uncertified or poorly stored seeds may have dead embryos inside due to age, heat damage, or insect attack, preventing them from germinating regardless of soil or rain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli loo ni akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná fɔmɔ kotokui ni egboi yɛ amɛmli yɛ afii ni amɛye lɛ hewɔ. latsaa ni fiteɔ nii loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ anaa ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees protects the young leaves from scorching, keeps the soil moist, and helps the seedlings establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo shia tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet environments with little air movement. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, which helps dry the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ tsiɔ ehe Dense pruning haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base of the plant helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes and look like they were chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the center of the plant. Checking your field early and putting neem leaf extract, sand, or recommended insecticides into the plant center can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu, ŋã, loo tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛwo ŋaa akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ fata tso lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: How do I know which direction to plant cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You should check the small raised buds on the stem cutting and ensure they are pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the leaves to grow downwards, weakening the plant and drastically reducing tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. ni awó nɔ yɛ tso ni afo lɛ nɔ Ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ atsɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants so the leaves can climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni ejie hulu la lɛ kpo bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tsei ni baai egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot weather, prevents soil from washing away during heavy rain, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain will wash the fertilizer off the surface of the land before the roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after rain or when light showers are expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ loo be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-abele lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that help feed the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why will my crops produce smaller fruits if I plant them very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough resources to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade plants like plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under intense sun. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade and trap moisture in the soil, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛha kookoo ni edako yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is my maize crop growing very tall and weak without producing big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmãa toi wuji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and thin when they are planted too close together. They compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients instead of putting energy into forming large corn ears.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee ŋmãa toi agboi lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen. This happens when soil nutrients are low or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients beyond the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do my crop leaves get covered in dark brown spots after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Brown spots after rain are usually fungal diseases. Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the leaves, and the moist leaf surface helps the disease spread.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ hela. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni baai ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my fresh tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi heei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or a lack of water. The plant drops flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long and prevents air from reaching the roots. Raising soil into mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open or grow into strange shapes instead of smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miijara loo amɛmiida kɛmiiya gbɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack or become misshapen when they hit hard, stony soil as they grow underground, or when sudden heavy rain follows a long dry period.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbala loo amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tswa amɛ beni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves around my crops help them stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minibii ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Dry leaves form a protective layer over the dirt. This layer blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture and keeps the root area cooler.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ muji lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee sũ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and break off before the fruit bunches are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbalaɔ dani aduawai akuu lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves dry prematurely due to fungal leaf diseases like Black Sigatoka or a lack of key nutrients in the soil. Healthy leaves are needed to feed the growing fruit bunch.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fungal baai helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Tsofɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he hia koni eye ebua aduawai akuu ni miida.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that lose water very quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain or cassava nearby shields the seedlings from harsh sun until their roots are deep enough to handle heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ dɔlɛ.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the exact same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is a good practice because beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while giving you two crops from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo. Enɛ haa abele lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick stems and full leaves for maximum harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni eyi obɔ kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid crop harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid plant harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong yields only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields the following season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or organic manure around the roots will help the maize regain its deep green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni eda oya.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied when the soil is moist right after a light rain. Applying it on dry soil can burn the crop roots, while applying it during heavy downpours will wash the plant food away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso shishifãi. Yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ afite lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with dark powdery dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni muji ni tamɔ powder diŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning directly into the leaf funnel kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni naa niyenii yɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long and drowns the roots, suffocating them. Planting your cassava on high soil ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away cleanly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or lack water. Keeping the soil moist continuously and putting dry grass mulch around the base cools the soil and helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i kɛ sũ ni egbi ni akɛwo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already wild and deeply established in the soil, allowing them to absorb nutrients faster than fresh crop seedlings. Clearing weeds within the first three weeks gives your crops the best head start.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni afuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ahe dumɔwui. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Crops show thirst through wilting, yellowing leaves, or stunted growth. Checking the soil depth with your finger—if it feels dry two inches below the surface, your crops need watering, preferably early in the morning or evening to prevent evaporation.
ga: Tsei jieɔ kumai he okadi kpo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ onine akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha. Kɛji enu he akɛ egbi 2 inches yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, no lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo onibii amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ afee lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ko.

english: Planting with the first major rains gives seeds warm soil and steady moisture, allowing them to build strong root systems quickly before heavy rains arrive or dry spells return.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulutsoo be lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why is it important to clear and space out my farm land properly before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni mafee he ko dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing and clearing ensure crops do not fight over nutrients, sunlight, and soil moisture. It also allows air to move freely between plants, which reduces the spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii akayeɔ niyenii, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do crops like tomatoes and garden eggs need wooden sticks to support them as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa tsei ni baaye abua amɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking keeps heavy stems and fruits off the damp ground, preventing rot and soil pests from damaging them. It also helps the plant catch more sunlight for better growth.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ni tsii kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Eyɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akpãtã amɛhiɛ. Ehaa tsei hu naa hulu la babaoo kɛha dalɛ kpakpa.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or overwatering which suffocates the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or compost helps replenish missing soil food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my young seedlings wither and die when exposed to direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young or delicate seedlings have weak root systems and lose moisture rapidly in intense heat. Providing temporary shade using palm fronds or cover crops protects them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛ́ edɔ waa lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei tsei loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaha abu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, soil fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: What is the benefit of using certified improved seeds over seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni asaa he ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified improved seeds are specially bred to tolerate local weather, resist common field pests, and yield more food compared to saved seeds that lose strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anaa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni ehaa niyenii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell when my maize or cassava is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma loo mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready: maize husks turn brown and papery dry, while cassava plants show yellowing lower leaves that drop off as energy stores move into the roots.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji efee klalo: ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ tamɔ wolo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tsei jieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi beni hewalɛ ni ato lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kpo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food crop plants need to make leaves green and healthy, or the ground is soaked with too much trapped water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Aloo nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ babaoo etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does planting my cassava stems very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he kroko lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba?

english: Planting stems too close together causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, which results in thin stems and small cassava tubers instead of big, thick roots.
ga: Tsoi ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to multiply and stay in your farm.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛhiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops water from drying out quickly, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on the farm the exact day I plant my seeds or wait a bit?
ga: Ani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ni okɛbaadu lɛ nɔ loo omɛ fioo?

english: It is best to wait a short time after germination because tiny new seeds do not have roots big enough to soak up fertilizer yet, and strong fertilizer can burn them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ fioo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ dumɔwui heei bibii lɛ Ebɛ shishifãi ni da bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants burn and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that get scorched by full afternoon sunlight, so they need temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwane hulu lɛ shãa amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha amɛhe ahi amɛhe kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara waa.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming up at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Mɛi krɛdɛɛi ni ba yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal food and water from the main mother plant, so removing the weak ones ensures the main plantain tree grows strong and produces a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwu titri lɛ ada waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pruning overcrowded or dead branches lets sunlight and breeze pass through the tree, which stops wet-weather diseases like black pod from spread and helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Niji ni eyi obɔ fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: What causes tiny holes to appear all over the leaves of my corn plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe fɛɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworm that hatch on the leaves and feed on the soft growing parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ bibii ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks steady water, or when the soil doesn't have enough nutrients to support the fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and help keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need for strong growth, or that the soil has become waterlogged from excessive rain, preventing roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my corn leaves and leaving brown powder inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the plant leaves during the day and feed on the crop, which can severely reduce your harvest if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my vegetable roots if rain falls continuously for one week on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsi kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When it rains constantly for a week, air spaces in the soil fill with water, which can suffocate plant roots, lead to root rot, and stop plants from absorbing necessary food from the soil.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsi kome Kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in tall, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack, and a test harvest of one stem shows thick, mature roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Ni tso lɛ yibii kome ni akpaa lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni mli tse ni eda.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants before fruit begins to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant grow stems instead of fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Is it better to burn cleared weeds on my field or leave them on the ground after land clearing?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds to rot on the ground creates mulch that keeps the soil cool, retains moisture, and adds nutrients, whereas burning destroys natural soil organisms and beneficial organic matter.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli wala kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: What causes white powdery dust to appear on the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It spreads when air humidity is high and plants are crowded together without enough airflow between them.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni abua tsei anaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded, typically a few weeks after germination. Applying fertilizer to completely dry soil or during heavy downpours can burn the roots or wash the nutrient investment away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How many days does it usually take for my maize seeds to break through the soil after I plant them?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Under warm Ghanaian weather, healthy maize seeds usually germinate and sprout above the soil in about 3 to 5 days when given proper soil moisture. If the soil is too dry or seeds are planted too deep, sprouting takes longer or fails.
ga: Yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ aaafee gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli kɛji akɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni sa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Ekwɛ̃mɔ baahe be babaoo loo ebaafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do small seeds like tomatoes need to be spread lightly near the soil surface instead of buried deep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui bibii tamɔ tomato fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni aaafu amɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small seeds carry very little stored energy. If buried too deep, the young shoot burns all its energy trying to reach the top; spreading them close to the surface allows them to easily break through within a few days of watering.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, oblahii kɛ oblayei lɛ shãa amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi lɛ. Kɛ́ agbɛ amɛ ashwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛfoɔ mli oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni awo amɛ nu lɛ.

english: Why do some of the pawpaw trees on my farm produce plenty of flowers but never grow any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees have separate sexes. Male trees produce clusters of flowers to supply pollen, but they cannot grow fruit themselves. Only female or hermaphrodite pawpaw trees develop actual fruit once they receive pollen from a male tree.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii akui ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ pollen. Shi enyɛŋ eda kɛjɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe. Pawpaw tsei ni ji yei loo hermaphroditic pɛ baawo yibii diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ amɛná pollen kɛjɛ tso ni ji nuu ko mli.

english: How does pollen move from the top of a maize stalk to make the corncob form grains?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni pollen lɛ jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛyaa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shishi?

english: The tassel at the very top of the maize plant acts as the male part, releasing pollen into the air. The long silks hanging from the cob act as female parts, catching the falling pollen so each grain can develop on the cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nuu lɛ gbɔmɔtso. Kɛtsɔ pollen ni ejieɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ Siliki kakadaŋŋ ko ni fĩɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ yoo lɛ fã. Catch fallen pollen Enɛ haa dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi shwereɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I put my crop seeds in a bucket of water before planting to check if they are good?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ aduawai dumɔwui awo nu baagi mli dani madu koni mana kɛji amɛhi?

english: Yes, floating seeds in water is a simple test. Healthy, solid seeds sink to the bottom because they are full of life, while damaged, hollow, or diseased seeds float to the water surface and should be thrown away.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ ji kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ejaakɛ wala eyi mli obɔ. Dumɔwui ni efite, ni mli ewo bu, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baafo kɛya nu lɛ hiɛ ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to keep nursery beds very wet when sprouting rice seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔha ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i waa kɛ́ wɔmiidu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Rice seeds need constant high moisture on the surface to soften their hard outer shells and trigger germination within 3 days. Keeping the seedbed wet prevents the delicate early shoots from drying out in the heat.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui biɔ ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo aya nɔ yɛ nɔ koni eha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli awa ni ewo shweremɔ he hewalɛ yɛ gbii 3 mli. Kɛ́ oha he ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why do tender young crop sprouts wither so quickly if exposed to hot sun right after emerging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo lɛ?

english: Newly sprouted crops have thin skin and very small roots that cannot pull water fast enough. Shading them with palm leaves for the first few days protects the delicate sprouts from drying out under harsh sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ hewolo ni mli tseee kɛ shishifãi bibii waa ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei ahe hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How soon after my vegetable seeds sprout in the nursery should I transplant them to the main field?
ga: Beni mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, te esa akɛ mikɛwo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli mra tɛŋŋ?

english: Wait until the sprouts grow about 3 to 4 true leaves, usually 2 to 3 weeks after sprouting. Moving them earlier damages fragile new roots, while waiting too long makes the plants stressed and slow to recover.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 baaje kpo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ otsi ohe mra lɛ, ebaafite shishifãi heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni ebaaha ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ oya.

english: Why is it necessary to pull out some sprouts when my seeds germinate too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmeii kɛji amɛdara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds sprout in tight clusters, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Thinning them out leaves room for the strongest sprouts to grow thick stems and deep roots.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee kui ni mli wa lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni afee lɛ mlɛo lɛ haa gbɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ po koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: What is the correct way to hold young sprouts when moving them so I do not destroy them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ tsei bibii ahe nii kɛ́ ajie amɛ? Bɔni afee ni akafite?

english: Always lift sprouts gently by their leaves or the soil ball around the roots, never by the stem. Squeezing the delicate stem crushes the tiny water tubes inside, causing the young plant to die shortly after planting.
ga: Wo tso bibioo lɛ nɔ blɛoo yɛ baai lɛ ahe loo sũ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kaawó nɔ yɛ tso lɛ masɛi. Ni aaatsi tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ yɛ nu paipi bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei bibii gboiɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without nurse crops like plantain or cassava to block the harsh sun, the young leaves lose moisture too fast, turn yellow, and scorch.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ char

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very tiny ears when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ toi bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to compete for light, leaving them weak and unable to develop full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight cups during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during peak afternoon heat is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce its leaf surface area and stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba baa lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the soil long after the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As the dry season progresses, the cassava plant draws on stored starch and moisture in its roots to stay alive. This process converts the soft, starchy root into tough, fibrous wood.
ga: Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni ato kɛ nu ni yɔɔ eshishifãi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ehi shi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ starch lɛ feɔ tso ni wa, ni yɔɔ fiber.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain suckers turn yellow and dry up during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally shed their older, lower leaves during dry, dusty periods to save water and send whatever moisture remains to the new leaves growing at the center.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai ni etsɛ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ kɛ sũ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu nu he ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop turn pale green and stop growing when heavy rains flood the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching crop roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn pale yellow or green.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Amɛkpaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ yeli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without forming fruits during periods of high heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme temperatures dry out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. To conserve water and energy, the stressed plant drops its unfertilized blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he Tsei ni haoɔ lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ shi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages legumes like cowpeas to put all their energy into growing foliage and stems rather than developing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do some of my young watermelons turn black and rot at the tip while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon gbekɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ enaagbee be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rotting at the tip of growing fruits is usually caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering, which prevents proper cell development at the fruit blossom end.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ tso yibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ wala yibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my avocado trees produce thousands of flowers but only end up setting a few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-avocado tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ shi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Avocado flowers have male and female parts that open at different times of the day, so natural flower drop is high unless pollinating insects are active during the short pollination window.
ga: Avocado fɔfɔii yɛ hii kɛ yei ahe fãi ni gbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ja kooloi bibii lɛ tsu nii yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Does the shape of my land affect how well my cocoa crops grow?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, the layout of your land determines how rainwater moves across your farm. Steep or sloped ground loses nutrients and moisture quickly, while flatter land retains topsoil better.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nu baatsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baabu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant my cocoa trees on sloped or hilly land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ gɔŋji loo gɔji anɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant on sloped land, but hills cause rainwater to rush downhill quickly, which can wash away fertile topsoil and damage young cocoa roots if you do not use protective planting methods.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Shi gɔji lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni efite kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛi ni abuɔ he ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii

english: What special methods should I use if I plant my cocoa on a steep hill?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛji midu kookoo yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ?

english: When planting on hills, plant along contour lines (across the slope rather than up and down) or build simple soil barriers to slow down rushing water and keep nutrients on your farm.
ga: Kɛ adu yɛ gɔŋ nɔ Dumɔ yɛ linei lɛ ahe. (otsɔ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni oooya ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ) loo oma shikpɔŋ gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baaha nu lɛ akaho oya ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow well in some parts of my land but struggle in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hei komɛi shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different areas of your farm have varying slopes and soil conditions. Areas where water flows off too quickly or washes soil away will cause your cocoa trees to struggle compared to balanced ground.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ ŋshɔkei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi. Hei ni nu hoɔ oya tsɔ loo efoɔ sũ lɛ baaha cacao tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni ja lɛ ahe.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain falls hard on exposed ground, the force of the water loosens the soil particles and carries the fertile top layer away, especially if the land tilts downward.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hei ni agbele naa lɛ Nu lɛ hewalɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ejieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni baa nii lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi kɛtee shishi.

english: How can I stop rainwater from sweeping away my farmland's topsoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekashwie miŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ sũ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can protect your topsoil by planting cover crops, building small barriers across water paths, and avoiding leaving the farm ground completely bare during rain season.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Feemɔ gbɛtsii nibii bibii yɛ nu gbɛi lɛ anɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni oooshi nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ he.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if the top layer of my soil gets washed away?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ho?

english: The top layer of soil contains the richest plant food and nutrients. If it washes away, your cocoa trees will lose their main source of nourishment, leading to weak growth and lower yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ji he ni tsei aniyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ yɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu ho O-cacao tsei lɛ baafite amɛ niyenii titri ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How can I tell if heavy rain is damaging the land on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miifite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Look out for small channels carved into the ground, exposed roots on your crops, or muddy water collecting at the bottom of slopes after it rains. These are clear signs of soil wash-off.
ga: Taomɔ he ko ni yɔɔ bibioo. akpɛ́ yɛ shikpɔŋ Shishifãi ni jeɔ kpo yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Aloo nu ni mli ewo muji ni buaa ehe naa yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miiho.

english: Why is controlling rainwater so important for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu he nitsumɔ he hiaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ?

english: Managing rainwater keeps it from flowing too quickly across your farm. Controlled water stays in the soil to feed your trees instead of stripping away good dirt and fertilizers.
ga: Nugbɔ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo tsiɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akudɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha otsei lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie muji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ,.

english: Why does rainwater run off my farm so fast instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water runs off quickly if your soil is hard and dry or if your farm is located on a slope. Slowing the water down gives it time to soak deeply into the root zone of your cocoa trees.
ga: Nu baaho oya kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi. Aloo kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ. Nu lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fioo lɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛboteɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains often turn moldy or discolored after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii loo amɛsu tsakeɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains turn moldy and change color when they are harvested before fully drying or are stored while wet. Drying grains thoroughly under the sun until they are hard and low in moisture keeps them clean, bright, and suitable for buyers.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛ su tsakeɔ kɛji akpa dani egbi kwraa loo akɛto be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tseɔ, amɛkpɛɔ ni amɛhiɔ kɛha mɔ ni heɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my maize plants to produce very small ears with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee toi bibii waa kɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Poorly filled cobs usually happen when plants lack enough water during flowering, suffer from low soil fertility, or are planted too close together. Ensuring good soil nutrients and proper planting distance gives each plant the energy to fill every grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eyimɔ obɔbɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi loo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ he naagba ni anaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ dumɔ he ni sa ni akɛduɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small grains instead of a large, healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso bibioo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my stored grains before I take them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmaa ni ato lɛ dani eya jara nɔ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in moist, unprotected grains. Storing thoroughly dried grains in sealed hermetic bags or treating them with approved grain protectants prevents insects from eating holes into your crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni abuuu he lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli. Aloo okɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua ni kooloi akaye bu ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani efee pods lɛ?

english: Cowpeas drop flowers mainly when tiny insect pests like thrips attack the blossoms, or when the plant experiences extreme heat and drought. Applying safe, targeted crop protection at early flowering helps save the buds so pods can grow.
ga: Nɔ titri ni tsina ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ji be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ loo be mli ni tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Why are the leaves of my grain crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant energy, or that water is standing too long at the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving land drainage will restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Aloo nu lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the best time to apply fertilizer to my grain crops for the best output?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmaa tsei lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in split doses: a first application shortly after germination to build strong roots, and a second application right before flowering when the plant needs maximum strength to build grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ: akɛwo mli klɛŋklɛŋ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba. Ni okɛwo mli shii enyɔ nɔ dani fɔfɔi aba be mli ni tsei lɛ he hiaa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛfee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the same field where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil naturally. Rotating them with grain crops like maize restores soil fertility and improves grain yields for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ abele ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant leftover seeds from my previous harvest or buy fresh seeds from an agrodealer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli loo ooohe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds from dealers are specifically bred to resist diseases and produce uniform, high-yielding crops. Leftover grain seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to lower yield and uneven grain quality.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni mɛi ni jaa lɛ ewo he odaseyeli lɛ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni dumɔwui lɛ hu ehiii kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my grain crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ edara ni esa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Grains are fully mature when the leaves and husks turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Ŋmãa lɛ eda kɛji baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ tsɔ asarasu ni amɛgbi kwraa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsɔ otsitsii lɛ anɔ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do international buyers reject my mangoes even when they look big and sweet to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi-mango lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdara ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ mi moŋ?

english: Foreign buyers look for specific export quality standards, such as fruits completely free of insect spots, sap burns, or chemical residues, because strict health laws in their countries prevent imported food from carrying pests or dangerous chemicals.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi taoɔ mlai pɔtɛɛ ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ, tamɔ aduawai ni kooloi bɛ mli. rɔbɔt ni ashã loo tsofai ni eshwɛ Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewalɛnamɔ he mlai ni mli wa ni yɔɔ amɛmaji lɛ amli lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ naa koni ekakɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara aya.

english: Why are some pesticides I buy at the local market not allowed on mangoes I want to sell for export?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ekomɛi atsu nii yɛ mango ni misumɔɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ koni mikɛya maŋsɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Export markets test fruits for chemical residues. Certain strong chemicals stay inside the fruit for a long time and are considered unsafe for consumers abroad, so buyers only accept crops treated with approved, safe chemicals.
ga: Jarayelihei ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ kaa aduawai amɛkwɛɔ kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwɛ. Tsofai komɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hiɔ aduawai lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ, ni abuɔ amɛ akɛ amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni yeɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpɛlɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni aŋmala he odaseyeli ewo mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the government need to inspect my farm before I can sell my fruit outside Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nɔyeli lɛ akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ miyibii lɛ yɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Government officers check farms to ensure your crops do not carry destructive pests or plant diseases. They issue an official health certificate that proves to foreign countries that your fruit is safe to enter their markets.
ga: Nɔyeli mli onukpai lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii loo tsei ahe helai bɛ onibii amli. Amɛhaa maŋ hewalɛnamɔ he woji ni tsɔɔ maŋsɛɛ maji akɛ oyibii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbote amɛjarayelihei lɛ.

english: How does joining a farmer group help me sell my mangoes to foreign markets?
ga: Te okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ mi-mango lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei?

english: Foreign buyers want large quantities of uniform, high-quality fruit that one small farm cannot supply alone. Joining a group allows farmers to combine their harvest, share the cost of export training, and gain recognition from international trade organizations.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo be fɛɛ be. ni ŋmɔ bibioo kome pɛ nyɛŋ aha. Kuu ko mlibotemɔ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛbuaa amɛnibii lɛ anaa. Jaa nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahe tsɔsemɔ he nyɔmɔwoo ni majimaji ateŋ jarayeli gbɛjianɔtoi ekpɛlɛ nɔ

english: Why do buyers pay more money for mango varieties like Keitt instead of my local mangoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ Keitt mangoi lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe mimaŋ mangoi lɛ?

english: Varieties like Keitt have firmer flesh, less stringy fiber, smaller seeds, and a longer shelf life, which makes them survive long travel across oceans without spoiling, making foreign consumers prefer them.
ga: Keitt henɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Less tough fibers ji dumɔwui bibii ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋshɔi amli lɛ mli ni amɛfiteee. Enɛ haa maŋsɛɛ jarayelɔi sumɔɔ nɛkɛ srɔtoi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my mangoes develop soft spots and tiny worms inside just when they are getting ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani eyɛ mli beni ahoo lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by fruit flies that lay invisible eggs under the skin of green mangoes. When the fruit ripens, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the inside, which makes the fruit rot quickly and ruins its sale value.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tso yibii amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ mango eŋɔli hewolo shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ loo lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni efiteɔ jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce plenty of flowers in some years but very few fruits make it to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ afii komɛi amli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains or tiny insects like thrips can damage mango flowers during bloom, preventing them from forming fruit. Poor tree nutrition or dry spells at the wrong time also cause trees to drop young fruits early.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips baanyɛ afite mango fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. ni no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii Tso lɛ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo hulutsoo be ni esaaa mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ afite oya.

english: Does the way I harvest my mangoes really affect whether buyers will take them?
ga: Ani bɔ ni akpaa mango lɛ ahaa lɛ saa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ahe kɛji amɛbaakpɛlɛ nɔ loo amɛkpɛlɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, pulling fruits roughly or letting them drop to the ground causes hidden bruises and causes sap to leak onto the skin, turning it black. Cutting the fruit carefully with a short stem attached stops sap leakage and keeps the skin clean.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni agbalaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Aloo ha egbee shikpɔŋ, ni ekɛ fãji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba ni eha latɛs lɛ atsɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ, ni eha etsɔ ediŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii kukuji tsu nii kɛfo aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi latɛs ni hoɔ lɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni hewolo lɛ he atse.

english: Why should I trim the inner branches of my mature mango trees when they are growing fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mango tso ni eda lɛ mli niji lɛ amli be mli ni mango lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Trimming branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the tree canopy. This dries up excess moisture that fungi need to grow, reducing disease spots on your fruit and helping flowers grow into healthier crops.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi. Ehaa helai ni yɔɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested mangoes turn soft and spoil so quickly before I can reach the buyer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Mangoes generate heat and ripen very fast if left under direct sun after picking. Keeping harvested fruit in cool shade and using ventilated crates prevents heat buildup and keeps the fruit firm longer.
ga: Mango lɛ baadɔ ni ebaakwɛ oya waa kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni akɛ adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater stays on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When standing water stays around roots for too long, it suffocates them by cutting off air. This stagnant water also allows tiny disease-causing germs to grow quickly, which makes the roots rot and leaves turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni ekã shi nɛɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai bibii ni baa mɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni haa helai daa oya Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is the best way to stop rainwater from creating stagnant pools in my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekafee ŋshɔkei yɛ mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Digging small drainage trenches around your field lets excess rainwater flow away naturally. This keeps the soil damp enough for crops without leaving standing pools where plant diseases and pests can breed.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ he bibioo ko ni afoɔ Yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baajɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshiuuu ŋshɔi ni ekã shi ni tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does the soil in low parts of my farm smell bad and kill my pepper plants after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trapped standing water blocks oxygen from reaching the soil. Without air, harmful microscopic organisms multiply and produce a sour smell, creating poisonous conditions that kill the roots of pepper plants.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Oshara nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ babaoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa.

english: How can I protect my young maize seedlings from dying when water collects on low ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo beni nu ebua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Building raised soil beds or mounds lifts the seedlings above the flood line. This prevents stagnant water from submerging the roots and keeps disease-causing organisms in the water away from the young stems.
ga: Saji loo gɔji ni awó nɔ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni awó dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛho nu afua lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ akabote shishifãi lɛ amli, ni nibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ akabote nu lɛ mli lɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei bibii ahe.

english: How does dirty standing water on my land spread sickness to my cassava plants?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Standing water often contains invisible disease-causing germs called pathogens. When water sits around your cassava, these germs enter through small wounds in the roots or stem, causing the whole plant to decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni kɛ helai baa ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ germs lɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Kɛ nu bɔle ŋmei lɛ he Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ boteɔ pilamɔi bibii amli. yɛ shishifã loo shishifã lɛ nɔ Ha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbo.

english: Is it safe for me to use water from a stagnant pond on my farm to water my tomato crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ nubu ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛwo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu?

english: It is risky because stagnant ponds collect plant pathogens over time. Pouring that water directly onto tender crops like tomatoes can transfer disease germs straight to their leaves and roots.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ nubui ni ekã shi lɛ baabua tsei ahe helai anaa yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ afɔse nu yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, tamɔ tomato nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai kɛya baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do crop diseases seem to spread much faster across my farm right after a flood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nu afua ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Floodwaters act like a road for germs, carrying plant pathogens from infected soil or weeds directly to healthy crops across your entire farm in a short time.
ga: Nu afua lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛi kɛha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ tsei ahe helai ni jɛ shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi ni hela emɔ mli lɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: I see many tiny insects breeding in puddles on my farm—can these insects harm my crops?
ga: Mina kooloo bibioo ko ni Many fɔɔ yɛ nu ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Ani nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, standing water acts as a breeding site for many harmful insects. Once adult pests hatch from the water, they bite young crop leaves, suck plant juices, and spread viral diseases from plant to plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ nu lɛ mli. Amɛ ŋmɔɔ baai bibii, amɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu, ni amɛ gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my feet and legs get itchy and infected after I walk through standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaji kɛ minaji ahe shwieɔ shi ni hela mɔɔ mi beni mitsɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Stagnant farm water can hold microscopic parasites and biting water insect larvae. These organisms can penetrate human skin or bite you while you work, leading to skin infections or illnesses like bilharzia.
