ga: Okwaafoi amli nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛ nu mli kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mɔ. Nɛkɛ bɔɔ nii nɛɛ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ loo amɛkɔmɔ bo beni otsuɔ nii lɛ. Ekɛ hewolo nɔ helai loo helai tamɔ bilharzia baa.

english: Can the insects that breed in stagnant water on my farm make both my family and my crops sick?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni fɔɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha miweku muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, stagnant water breeds mosquitoes that carry malaria to your family, while also breeding crop pests like beetles and flies that carry plant viruses directly to your farm crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɛkɛ atiridii aba oweku lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ladybugs kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ tsei amli helai baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have a broad base, short stem, and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. These grow faster and yield larger fruit bunches than suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ 'sword shoot' ni shishi lɛ mli kwɔ, tso kuku kɛ baai ni mli tse, ni tamɔ lance. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ kui wuji fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: You should leave about 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) between plants. This prevents the large leaves from blocking sunlight from each other and gives roots room to feed.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei lɛ abɔ he aaafee mitai 3 x 3 (10 x 10 feet) yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni amɛbaai wuji lɛ akatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii

english: What is the best month to plant plantains in Ghana so they survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ Ghana koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Plant at the start of the major rainy season, usually around April or May. This allows the root system to grow deep enough to survive the drier months later in the year.
ga: Aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April loo May. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli yɛ sɛɛ mli afii lɛ amli.

english: Yes, you should remove extra shoots and keep only 1 main tree and 1 or 2 healthy followers. Keeping too many shoots starves the main tree, resulting in very small bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kome loo enyɔ ahi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii babaoo to he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ daraaa kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain stems bend over or break when the fruits start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and cannot hold the heavy weight of full fruit bunches during strong winds. You need to support the heavy stems with strong, forked wooden poles called props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ aduawai ni akɛwo tsɔne mli ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ props lɛ afi tsɔne ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava and plantains together on the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping plantains with cassava works well during the first year because cassava covers the soil and reduces weeds while the plantains grow tall enough to provide light shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi. Beni tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo lɛ,.

english: How long will it take from the day I plant a sucker until I harvest my first plantain bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It typically takes between 11 and 14 months for a plantain plant to produce mature fruit, depending on rainfall, soil fertility, and the variety you planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 14 dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii kwraa. Edamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow with dark brown patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Sigatoka, a fungal leaf disease common in humid weather. You can manage it by cutting off severely infected leaves and keeping the field weed-free to improve airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Black Sigatoka, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. ni oha jwɛi akafee he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain plants dying off so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miigboi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Older leaves naturally die off as the plant grows, but if many turn yellow at once, the soil may lack nutrients like nitrogen or water, or the roots may be damaged by pests like nematodes.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome hu? Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ŋmeii tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my green plantains from ripening too fast while transporting them to the market in Accra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain eŋɔli lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ beni mikɛyaa jara nɔ yɛ Accra lɛ?

english: Harvest the bunches while they are dark green and fully filled out, handle them gently to avoid bruises, and cover them with fresh banana leaves in the truck to protect them from direct sunlight and heat.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ lolo ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ. Okɛ amɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni akatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛ banana baai heei aha lɔle lɛ he koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are there so many different varieties of cassava, and how do I pick the right one for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific conditions. Some mature faster during short rainy seasons, while others resist common diseases or yield more starch depending on your local soil and rainfall.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anaa. Henɔi komɛi daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ loo amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lɛ, ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know which maize variety is best suited for the weather pattern in my district?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ?

english: Short-duration maize varieties are designed to mature quickly if your area gets brief rainy seasons, whereas long-duration varieties yield more grain if your district receives steady rainfall over a longer period.
ga: Afee ŋmãa henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ koni amɛshwere oya kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ baawo dumɔwui babaoo kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do some of my crops grow roots very deeply into the ground while others stay near the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shishifãi yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Deep roots help plants reach water stored far underground during dry periods and keep the plant anchored, while shallow roots spread out to quickly capture surface rainwater and nutrients from fertilizers.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni emɔ nugbɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ oya.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants rot and die during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, it pushes out oxygen. Without air in the soil, the roots drown, rot, and die from fungal infections.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagboi kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow long and thin instead of big and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee agboi ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Yams grow long and thin when the soil is too hard or compact underneath, forcing the tuber to work harder to push downward rather than expanding outwards in loose, soft soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishi. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii waa koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya kponɔgbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli.

english: During dry periods, plants enter a resting phase or dormant state to conserve water and energy, slowing down active growth above ground until moisture returns.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo wɔɔhe shihilɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Edaa fiofio yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and drop off right before the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Plants drop their leaves to reduce moisture loss through evaporation, which helps the stem and roots survive through dry weather until the next rain.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛba ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kroko mli lɛ.

english: How deep into the soil should I plant my seeds to make sure they grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Seeds should generally be planted at a depth equal to two or three times their thickness. Planting too deep prevents seedlings from reaching sunlight, while planting too shallow exposes them to birds and dry heat.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛmli ŋtayaa lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi lɛ aná la ni amɛgbi.

english: Why does plowing or digging the soil deeply help root crops yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akuɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduɔ shishifãi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Deep soil preparation loosens hard ground, making it easy for roots to grow deeply to absorb hidden moisture and allow root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes to expand fully.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ shɔŋŋ koni amɛŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ koni amɛshwere kwraa.

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil, causing temporary wilting until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their deep green color and strength, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant grow healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ ni yɔɔ onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What makes the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, which is a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air circulate through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to keep your harvest safe.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi eto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops early instead of leaving them until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui kɛjɛ mra Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, light, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the food they need to build strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the stems above ground grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: If cassava plants are given too much nitrogen or planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: How do I know it is safe to plant my maize seed after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil has received two or three steady, deep rains. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a hot dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, their roots fight over water and nutrients in the dirt, resulting in thin plants and smaller yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries out the flower pollen, preventing fruit formation. Covering the soil around the plant with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ aduawai anaa Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same plot where I am establishing young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii miitswa lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade that cools the soil and holds moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to survive direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do maize and cowpeas help each other when I grow them together in the same field?
ga: Te ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the heavy-feeding maize crop while ground cover prevents soil from drying out.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni ahaa lɛ niyenii ni tsii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to save water. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts new leaves and continues growing its tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: Why does my oil palm crop take several years before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi aduawai akui feemɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm spends its early years establishing a deep root network and a sturdy trunk to hold heavy fruit loads later. This long preparation allows the tree to bear fruit continuously for over twenty years.
ga: Palm fɔ lɛ he eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ. Koni afee tsɔne ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa yɔɔ mli kɛha aduawai ni tsii ni abaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli. Nɛkɛ hesaamɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii be fɛɛ be nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ.

english: Cocoa naturally produces flowers and fruit on its trunk so that thick, heavy pods can mature safely supported by strong wood without snapping delicate outer branches.
ga: Cocoa baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii ni mli tse ni tsii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ tsei ni wa anɔ. ni ekuuu kponɔgbɛ tsei niji ni waaa lɛ

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my yam crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems designed to quickly grab water and plant food from poor soil, whereas domesticated crops like yam focus their energy on building underground tubers and need clear ground to establish.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni ejie nu oya ni ekwɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shia tamɔ sweet potato lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tubers ni amɛbaafee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ koni amɛto amɛhe shi.

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same crop family and attract identical soil pests and diseases. Rotating to a different crop like beans starves out these hidden pests before you plant pepper again.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tso kroko nɔ, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ dani odu ŋmei ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing thick leaves and stems but no flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes tomato plants to put all their energy into growing foliage instead of setting flowers. Balancing nutrients encourages the plant to shift its growth toward fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsake kɛjɛ dalɛ mli kɛya yibiiwoo mli.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow during harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Staking the stems with strong wooden poles gives them the extra physical support needed to stay upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni akɛ tsei ni wa fĩɔ amɛhe lɛ haa amɛnáa yelikɛbuamɔ kroko koni amɛhi shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage crops get full of small holes when I plant them during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaabeji lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Moist, rainy weather encourages soft-bodied caterpillars and pests to multiply rapidly on lush cabbage leaves. Planting on raised beds improves air circulation and prevents water logging that attracts foliage-chewing insects.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ babaoo oya yɛ kaabɛji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa nu ni damɔ shi ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ baa lɛ naa.

english: How do I properly prepare my land before planting cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui?

english: Clearing land without burning all the vegetation preserves soil nutrients. Leaving some tall trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain ensures young cocoa plants are protected from harsh sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa tsei fɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi. Tsei kakadaji komɛi ni aaashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Pruning removes dead or crowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to flow through the tree. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and helps the tree put its energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ black pods wuji.

english: How much water do my young cocoa plants need to survive the dry heat?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need regular watering about two to three times a week during dry periods, keeping the soil moist but not waterlogged so the roots do not rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔse kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nu daa shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ shi nu akabote mli No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: How can I protect my crop soil from drying out completely during the Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around the base of your plants with dry leaves or weeds—helps trap moisture in the ground, keeps the roots cool, and protects plants during hot, dry spells.
ga: Mulching—ni ji shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How do I safely mix water and liquid chemicals in my knapsack spraying machine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nu kɛ tsofai ni ji nu afutu tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe?

english: Fill the sprayer tank halfway with clean water first, add the measured chemical, stir gently, and then top it up with the remaining water so the mixture is evenly blended without clogging.
ga: Dani okɛ nu ni mli tse baawo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli fã, Okɛ tsofai ni asusu lɛ afata he, ni okɛfutu mli blɛoo, ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ afata he koni ekɛfutu jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ nɔ ko akatsi.

english: Why is clean water so important when filling up my crop spraying machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mli tse he hiaa beni mikɛ mi-crop sprayer lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Using dirty or muddy water blocks the spraying nozzle, damages the machine's pump, and weakens the chemical mixture so it does not protect your crops properly.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji ni akɛtsiɔ nozzle lɛ naa. ni ekɛ tsɔne lɛ pɔmp lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebuuu onibii ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to use my spraying machine on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the air is cooler and wind is low, which prevents the sprayed water and chemical mixture from evaporating quickly or blowing away.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haaa nu kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akafo oya loo efo kɛya.

english: How do I clean and store my spraying machine after finishing my field work?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ mi-sprayer lɛ he ni mikɛto beni migbe ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ naa lɛ?

english: Flush the tank with clean water two to three times, spray clean water through the hose and nozzle to clear chemical residues, and dry the machine upside down in the shade to prevent rust.
ga: Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tanki lɛ he shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ hose kɛ nozzle lɛ nɔ koni ojie tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ. ni okɛ tsɔne lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ŋmei akafee lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the cocoa tree is stressed from too much direct sunlight, lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or is not getting enough water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eshɛ kookoo tso lɛ he tsɔ. Nibii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack water or nutrients, or when beneficial insects are absent to pollinate them. Maintaining shade trees and keeping soil healthy helps the tree retain flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ afee pollination bɛ Tso lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell when my maize is fully mature and ready to be harvested for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn dry and papery, and a small black spot forms at the base of each kernel. Harvesting at this stage prevents excess moisture from causing mold and rot while in storage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee tamɔ wolo. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Unlike yams, cassava roots do not have a protective outer bark, so they naturally begin to deteriorate within two to three days after harvest. Processing them quickly into gari or flour helps preserve them for much longer periods.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe yɛ kponɔgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ oya lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and providing light shade during the hottest parts of the day helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of a dark green color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf development. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or appropriate fertilizer will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft stems and shallow roots that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it important to keep specific distances between my cassava stems when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ koni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ahi ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each cassava plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, allowing the roots to grow larger and form bigger tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ wuji ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, and how does that affect crop growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Ni te ebaaná tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the maize and helping it grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edaraa waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same patch of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing tomatoes continuously on the same soil allows pests and soil diseases specific to tomatoes to multiply. Rotating your land with unrelated crops like maize or leafy greens breaks pest life cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tomato he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai babaoo aya hiɛ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii baatsake. Efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain suckers are receiving too much water in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When plantain roots sit in waterlogged soil, they suffocate and decay, causing the main leaves to turn soft, yellow, and droop despite having plenty of water around them.
ga: Kɛ plantain shishifãi ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaafo ni ebaagbo. Enɛ haa baai titrii lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe moŋ.

english: What causes fall armyworms to suddenly attack the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ha cutworms lɛ tutua mi-baby corn baai lɛ trukaa?

english: Fall armyworm adult moths fly into fields during the night and lay eggs on young leaf blades. Once the eggs hatch, the caterpillars feed rapidly on the inner leaf whorls, requiring quick treatment to prevent severe crop damage.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ foɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ oya. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ nɔ oya koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa.

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water, it drowns the roots and washes away nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that keeps leaves green and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛshwieɔ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain packs the topsoil tightly into a hard crust or washes the seeds away completely, making it impossible for tiny shoots to break through the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa loo ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa. feemɔ ŋmeii bibii Enyɛŋ ebote ŋwɛi

english: What happens to my cassava if heavy rain leaves water sitting on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. If water covers the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to rot underground and spoil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu ha he lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my pepper leaves after wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: The cool, damp air after heavy rain creates the perfect environment for fungal diseases to multiply on damp leaves, which slows down crop growth if not treated.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ada blɛoo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the trees before turning into pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall and high humidity make the stems weak and encourage fungal diseases like black pod, causing the tree to drop its flowers before they can form pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei akutsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the vine right after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ niji shwereɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpeteŋkpele ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When dry tomato plants suddenly take in a massive amount of rainwater, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei ni egbi lɛ ná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ, Yibii lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: How does heavy rain affect the fertilizer I put around my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rainwater washes fertilizer deep into the ground past the roots where plants cannot reach it, or carries it away off the field entirely, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi ni tsei nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ anɔ. loo akɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika.

english: Why does my field's soil dry out and crack open like stone a few days after rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi ni egbɛ eshwa tamɔ tɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Clay soil swells when wet and shrinks quickly as sunlight bakes the surface. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw helps trap moisture and prevents the soil from cracking.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fũuɔ kɛ́ edɔ, ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, egbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli agbala.

english: Why do I see so many caterpillars eating my maize leaves right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni miiye mi-abele lɛ baai lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: The early rains cause plants to shoot up fresh, soft green leaves, which attracts parent moths to lay hundreds of eggs that quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmei nyɛ lɛ koni ekɛ wɔji ohai abɔ awo ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Is it bad to harvest my corn while it is raining or still wet from rain?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ oookpa ŋmãa be mli ni nugbɔ miinɛ loo edɔ lolo?

english: Yes, harvesting wet corn traps moisture inside the husk, which creates dangerous mold and toxins while the crop sits waiting to be dried or transported.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa be mli ni tsei lɛ miimɛ ni amɛgbi loo akɛ amɛ aya he kroko lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or isn't receiving enough water. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their healthy green color and improves growth.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants have tightly curled leaves and stop growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant's juices, or by viruses spread by these insects that stunt the plant's development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei kpaa dalɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my rice crop turn pale and grow unevenly across different parts of the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ? ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ

english: Rice grows unevenly when the field is not leveled properly, causing water to collect too deep in low spots while leaving higher spots dry and unable to absorb soil nutrients.
ga: Omɔ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ atsakeee omɔ ŋmɔji lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ buaa ehe naa tsɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni anyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cowpeas drop flowers without forming pods when they suffer from high heat, lack of water during the flowering stage, or attack by small pests like thrips that damage the flower buds.
ga: Cowpea baajie fɔfɔii ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji edɔ waa. Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips, ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ tutuaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms before any small tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out suddenly, which stresses the plant and prevents successful pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa.

english: What makes my cassava roots stay very thin and woody instead of swelling into thick tubers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the ground is too hard and compacted for the roots to expand, or if the tubers are harvested too early before the plant has stored enough starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe, ni no baaha shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ dani tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa eto.

english: Yam tubers rot under the ground when water gathers in the soil without proper drainage, or when tiny soil worms called nematodes infect damaged skins on the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ yitso hewolo ni efite lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to dig up my groundnuts so I do not harvest too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii? koni akakpa mra tsɔ

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and dry up, and when you open a few test pods to find the inside lining of the shell has turned dark pink or brown.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele test pods fioo komɛi ni ona akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ etsɔ pinki loo blɔfo ni mli edɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil consumes all specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, reducing your yield over time.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛi lɛ fɛɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes the nearby maize plants while covering the ground to retain soil moisture.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yields now compared to years ago even though I work just as hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eji afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over years of continuous farming without rest or fertilization. Adding organic manure, compost, or allowing the land to lie fallow restores essential plant nutrients to the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni ekɛ ehe ejɔɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the dirt naturally and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ

english: Why do cowpea plants make the soil better for my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that have small nodules on their roots. These roots trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi bibii. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, a vital food for leaf growth. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early will help the plant turn dark green and produce large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea baafata he mra Enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewo toi wuji.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink the leaf surface area exposed to intense sunlight, which prevents water loss. However, if leaves remain curled continuously, it indicates tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or thrips.
ga: Pepper tsei baafo amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha baa lɛ hiɛ afee bibioo kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkpãtã lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ.

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and partial shade during peak sun helps flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ tomato nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, woody roots instead of large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ tsei lɛ? Yɛ yitso agbo najiaŋ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, well-aerated soil to expand. If planted in hard-packed dirt or placed too close together, the roots cannot swell and will compete for space and nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli koni amɛshwere. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ loo akɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ ni amɛbaatswa he kɛ niyenii he akaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava stems rot under the ground when the rainy season gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots drown in standing water because wet soil cuts off their air supply and attracts soil fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi woɔ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ mli ni egbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply in wet soil. As the heavy bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy, requiring wooden support stakes to prevent wind damage.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni ŋmɔ lɛ da kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite nɔ ko.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have holes in them that look like caterpillar damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Checking leaves early and applying biological controls or recommended insecticides early protects the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ahe loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaabu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I buy from the local market fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds bought from open grain markets are often meant for cooking and may be old, heat-damaged, or improperly stored. Certified seeds from registered agro-dealers are specially processed and tested to guarantee high germination rates and healthy crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa jarayeli hei ni agbele naa lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii, ni ekolɛ egbɔ, ni dɔlɛ efiteɔ. loo akɛtoɔ he ni esaaa Atsuɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ahe nii yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if crop seeds brought from neighboring countries like Togo will grow well on my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ tamɔ Togo lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Seeds perform best when planted in soil and climate conditions similar to where they were developed. Before planting a large field with imported seeds, test a small patch first to see if the crop can handle local rainfall, heat, and soil conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tamɔ he ni adu amɛ yɛ lɛ nɔ. dani ooodu ŋmɔji wuji ni dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ Ka shikpɔŋ bibioo ko okwɛ. klɛŋklɛŋ koni ana kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi ahe nii.

english: Why are my young maize plants staying short and turning light green instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing or light green leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an important food for plants. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives the crop the energy it needs to grow tall and dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This leaves you with weak, thin plants and smaller harvests than if you had spaced them properly.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baawo yibii babaoo fe kɛji okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the main rainy season officially begins. If your seeds germinate after that initial rain, the hot sun and dry soil in the following weeks will dry up and kill the young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Hulu ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ otsii ni baa lɛ amli Ebaagbi ni ekpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather as a self-defense mechanism to save water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly because of high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding extreme heat stress helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ titri. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ ni baa lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with appropriate bio-pesticides or insecticides stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa loo kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce thousands of flowers, but only a few pods actually develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, shi fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ shwereɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed, and only flowers pollinated by tiny insects called midges will form pods. Leaving leaf litter on the ground creates a moist breeding area for these helpful midges to improve pod formation.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Ni fɔfɔi pɛ yɔɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midges pɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ pods. Kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ amli jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yams are completely mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams are fully mature when the leaves and vines naturally dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season. Harvesting while the leaves are still green means the tubers haven't reached their full size and weight yet.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bulb lɛ eshɛɛɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii he lolo.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast even after I water them during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: When the weather gets very hot, intense sun and wind cause water to evaporate quickly from the soil surface. Covering the soil with mulch, such as dry grass or leaves, traps moisture in the ground for much longer.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching kɛ jwɛi ni egbo, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo.

english: Why can't I plant my maize in the same month I used to plant it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nyɔŋ ni midu afii komɛi ni eho lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana have shifted over time due to changing climate conditions. Planting based on updated local weather forecasts rather than old calendar dates prevents seeds from drying out during unexpected dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ etsake yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa ni atsake lɛ naa moŋ fe kalanda gbii momo lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa?

english: If crops get too little water, leaves will curl and turn dry or crisp. If they receive too much water, leaves will turn yellow, look limp, and the roots may rot because waterlogged soil starves them of air.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu fioo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaafee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ, ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young vegetable seedlings turning brown and scorching in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves and undeveloped roots that burn easily under full sun. Providing temporary shade with palm fronds protects them until their roots grow deep enough to handle strong sunlight.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni edarako ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ tsei ahe tsei ewo mli lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni naa wa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn light green or yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is flooded. Adding compost or the right fertilizer restores nutrients and brings back healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted too close together produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete directly for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to mature fully and yield larger crops.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does planting cassava or maize on the exact same plot every season reduce my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in that spot. Rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii fata he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Which food crops should I choose if the rains in my district become irregular?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like cassava, sorghum, millet, and cowpeas handle dry stretches much better than water-heavy crops, ensuring you still get a yield even when rainfall is low.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ aŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hei ni nu egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ nibii ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ lolo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ fioo po.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even more during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal stored soil water and nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early leaves more moisture in the ground for your crops to survive dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can a young person start farming successfully on a small plot with limited water access?
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei baaje okwaayeli shishi yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu he aaashɛ?

english: Using smart techniques like drip irrigation, raised garden beds, and heavy mulching allows you to grow high-value vegetables efficiently on tiny plots of land while saving water.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋaa gbɛ̀i tamɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Raised garden bed Kɛ heavy-duty mulching lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ aduawai ni jara wa waa yɛ he bibioo ko jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni okɛ nu lɛ toɔ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Clearing weeds, trimming excess branches to let in sunlight, and quickly removing infected pods will help stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. weeding Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ he Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants filled with tiny holes and green caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli

english: Your maize is likely being attacked by the Fall Armyworm. These caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves and eat the growing leaves, which can greatly reduce your harvest if you do not control them early.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ tutua o-abele lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi kwraa kɛji okuuu nɔ mra.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays or neem oil helps keep the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa loo neem fɔ ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-loving pests to build up. Rotating your crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: This is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, prevents weeds from growing, and eventually breaks down to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbee shi ni amɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and soft if I harvest them right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains arrive after a dry period, the cassava plant uses the starch stored in its roots to rapidly grow new leaves. This process drains energy from the roots, leaving them watery and low in starch.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai heei oya. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa efeɔ nu ni starch faaa yɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows big and produces a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo kooloi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize yield much less than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation only. The seeds collected from that crop lose those special traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests in the second generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant maize and cassava together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and can be harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly over a full year. Intercropping them allows you to get an early grain crop while the cassava takes over the land later, giving you two harvests from one field.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onine shɛɔ dumɔwui anɔ mra yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. It can also happen when the soil is too soaked with water, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does adding dry manure or compost help my cassava grow better than using plain soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Manure and compost act like long-lasting food and a sponge for your soil. They slowly feed nutrients to your crops while helping the soil hold moisture better during dry spells, making tubers grow larger and healthier.
ga: Manɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ sponji kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛbaafee fiofio Amɛbaaha onibii lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in overly damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight reach the crop and removing infected pods quickly will help stop it from spreading.
ga: Fungal tutuamɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or recommended insecticides helps protect your peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-peppers lɛ ahe.

english: How can I stop small caterpillars from chewing holes through my corn leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmei bu lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called Fall Armyworms, hide in the central funnel of the corn plant. Catching them early by inspecting your farm weekly and applying natural sprays like neem oil or approved pest controls directly into the plant funnels stops them from destroying the yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ nɔ daa otsi. ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo dumɔwu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they get stressed, usually by extreme heat, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over easily whenever heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, but they fall over mostly when tiny soil worms (nematodes) damage their root systems or when the fruit bunch becomes too heavy. Propping up the trees with sturdy wooden poles helps keep them standing.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii. (Nematodes) lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Aloo be mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii tsɔ. Tso lɛ he tsei ni wa ni akɛwulaa tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Why are my cabbage heads staying soft and loose instead of forming tight, hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages need consistent water, cool root temperatures, and enough room to grow tightly. If they get inconsistent water, too much heat, or lack sufficient nutrients like phosphorus, the heads will not wrap tightly.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia cabbage. shishifãi ni mli ejɔ ni eyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ nu ni mli edɔɔ fe nine loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, yitso lɛ etswaŋ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting quickly while waiting for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Yams spoil fast if they are injured during harvest or exposed to direct sun and rain. Curing them in a well-ventilated, shaded barn off the ground helps heal small skin wounds and keeps them fresh for a long time.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji amɛ pila yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo amɛ shɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ atsa yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsa pilamɔi bibii. yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: How do I know if my harvested crops meet the standard required for export or long-distance markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ yeɔ shishitoo mlai ni ataoɔ kɛha nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ loo jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: High-quality market crops must be clean, free from pest bites, uniform in size, and harvested at the right maturity stage so they don't spoil in transit. Exporters also look for produce grown with safe chemical levels.
ga: Esa akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe atse. Ebɛ kooloi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Ha elɛɛmɔ afee ekome ni akpa yɛ be ni sa mli bɔni afee ni ekafite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ hu taoɔ nibii ni adu kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf yellowing in young maize usually means the soil is missing nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special friendly bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the cowpea roots rot after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsina shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani oooha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water early on, it spends all its energy building leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo nu babaoo nɔ mra lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the ground and exposes them to the sun, allowing the plant to make enough food to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Staking jieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afuu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a hot open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantain act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs until its roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hot afternoon but bounce back in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil, so they droop to save moisture. When the sun goes down, water loss slows down and the leaves firm up again.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi ni baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like boron and calcium needed to hold the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ boron kɛ calcium ni he hiaa koni akɛhiɛ fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I leave too many sucker shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ susumai komɛi ni amɛkã shi lɛ? Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ fa tsɔ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all compete for the same food, water, and light. Cutting back extra shoots leaves energy for the main plant to produce big bunches.
