ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kome he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji wuji.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites underneath the leaf, or a virus spread by whiteflies. They drink the plant juice and cause new growth to twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo baa mli ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛkɛ dalɛ hee ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot underground instead of sprouting into seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds rot underground if planted too deep or in overly wet, soggy soil. Small seeds have limited energy and will exhaust themselves trying to push through heavy soil before reaching light.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo. ni hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baaho ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsi shikpɔŋ lɛ waa dani eshɛ kane lɛ he

english: Why are so many of the small pods on my cocoa tree dropping off before they reach full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo miiho dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more young pods than they can support. The tree intentionally sheds the extra or weak pods—a process known as cherelle wilt—so it can direct its nutrients toward growing the remaining pods to full maturity.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine loo ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherel wilt. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing harvestable pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years before you can harvest from them.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: How many months does it take for a tiny cocoa pod to grow and mature into a fully ripe pod?
ga: cocoa pods bibii Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani edaa ni ekwɛɔ?

english: Once a flower is pollinated and forms a tiny pod, it takes about 5 to 6 months for the pod to grow to full size and change color to show it is ripe.
ga: Beni fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii bibii. Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwere.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are ripe enough to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kookoo lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: You can tell a pod is ripe by its skin color. Pods that start green will turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow when ripe. Tapping the pod and hearing a hollow sound also shows the seeds inside have loosened.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ pod ko egbɔ kɛtsɔ ehewolo su nɔ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ feɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei kɛji ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ota pod lɛ he ni onu gbee ni mli ewo muji lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbee shi.

english: What happens to my crop if I harvest cocoa pods before they change color and ripen?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii dani amɛtsake amɛhe su ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Unripe cocoa pods do not have enough sugar in their sweet white pulp. If you harvest them early, the beans will not ferment properly, leading to low-quality, bitter beans that buyers will reject.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni edako lɛ bɛ sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛloo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa mra Beans lɛ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni ehiii, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo.

english: Why do my trees seem to produce fewer pods after three or four years of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mitsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pod production drops if the soil loses its nutrients, if trees are overloaded with shade, or if pests and diseases damage the branches. Regular pruning, soil fertilization, and pest control help trees keep producing high yields every year.
ga: Pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo babaoo loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai fiteɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Is the sweet white pulp inside a fresh cocoa pod safe for me to eat?
ga: Ani ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ hee mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maye?

english: Yes, the sweet white coating around the fresh cocoa seeds is completely safe and pleasant to eat. In fact, the sugars in this pulp are essential because they feed the yeast during the pod fermentation process after harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsɔne yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Cocoa yibii heei lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni amɛhe ŋɔɔ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, sugars ni yɔɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ he hiaa waa ejaakɛ amɛhaa yeast lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I plant fresh cocoa seeds directly from a ripe pod to grow new cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei heei kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛdu kookoo tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, fresh seeds can grow into trees, but you must plant them almost immediately after opening the pod. Cocoa seeds lose their ability to germinate within a few days once exposed to air.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui heei baanyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei. Shi ehe miihia ni odu amɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce hundreds of flowers, but only a few pods actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ, shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny insects called midges for pollination. Because these insects are very small and don't visit every flower, only a small fraction of the blossoms get pollinated successfully to become pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ daraaa kwraa, ni amɛyasaraaa fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi. Fɔfɔi lɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ No sɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are some of the pods turning black and shriveling up while still hanging on my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛkã mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Pods turning black on the tree is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and heavy shade. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning your farm to let in sun and air will stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ofolɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaakpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense heat because their leaves and roots are tender. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahewɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa wɔɔhe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning excess branches allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, preventing fungal diseases and directing the plant's energy into producing cocoa pods rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ahelai anaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to leave fallen leaves around the base of my crops instead of sweeping or burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni mafolɔ loo mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving organic matter on the soil acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, holds moisture during hot weather, and slowly breaks down into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my cassava help my farm?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the land for surrounding crops like cassava.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni ebɔle he tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my farm plot?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield larger crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when there is plenty of rain for everything to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshinii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ babaoo miinɛ koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the soil's natural nutrients, sunlight, and root space. Even with heavy rain, your crops will stay small if weeds consume the fertilizer first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi bibii kɛji jwɛi lɛ ye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: High moisture and humidity cause Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast on wet pods. Clearing bushy weeds and pruning extra branches improves airflow to keep pods dry.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be kɛ blackpod hela baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: What causes small dark patches on my young cocoa pods that make them shrivel up early?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anɔ kɛyashi amɛbaagboi oya.

english: Dark spots are often caused by small insects like mirids (capsids) that feed on the sap of young pods. Regular field checks and proper pest control prevent them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kwɛmɔ ni oookwɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers during very hot weather without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni latsaa be mli ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water and stay alive. Providing shade and keeping the soil covered helps cool the plant so flowers can stay on and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ wo hulutsoo mli ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yams need deep, loose, well-drained fertile soil so the tubers can expand easily. If your land has shallow, hard, or stony soil that holds too much water, yam tubers will rot or stay very small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni wa, loo tɛi ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbo loo amɛji bibii waa.

english: Why does corn grow well on land where my yams fail to produce good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-sweet potatoes lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie ŋmãa kpakpai lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Corn has shallow roots and can tolerate a wider variety of soil types, whereas yams need very deep, soft, and fertile soil to build heavy underground tubers.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi ahe gbɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli eyi obɔ waa koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: What are the early signs that my farmland is not suitable for yam cultivation?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ esaaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: If water collects on top of the soil for days after rain, or if the soil turns into hard crusts when dry, the land will choke yam tubers and cause rot.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa beni egbi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: How can I test or tell which crops will do best on my farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka loo male tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can check soil depth, texture, and water drainage after heavy rains; sandy loam soils suit root crops like yams, while clay-heavy soils are better for rice or sugarcane.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, ehiɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes yɔɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: What causes my corn crop to perform poorly even when I plant at the start of the rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli moŋ?

english: Poor corn performance is usually caused by low soil nutrients like nitrogen, sudden dry spells during flowering, or damage from pests like the fall armyworm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa nitsumɔ ni ehiii baa ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni faaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ ŋmãa ni egbiɔ trukaa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yams turn out small and misshapen when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efiteɔ kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: Misshapen or small yams happen when the soil is too hard or compacted, preventing the tuber from pushing smoothly downward as it grows.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni efite loo bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo kɛya shishigbɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why does my corn yield change so much from one year to the next on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni miwoɔ lɛ srɔtoi babaoo kɛjɛɔ afi kome mli kɛyaa afi kroko nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Corn extracts heavy amounts of nutrients from the soil every season; without adding manure, fertilizer, or rotating with legumes, the soil gets weaker each year.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ daa afi.

english: What happens to yams if my farm land holds too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baa sweet potato nɔ kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Excessive water in the soil cuts off air to the roots and causes fungal rots, which quickly destroys the underground tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbáa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii fiteɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ oya dani akpaa.

english: Why should I avoid planting corn on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting corn repeatedly drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and allows corn-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant only corn or mix it with other crops on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikome too makwɛ ŋmãa loo mikɛ ŋmãa krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafata he?

english: Mixing corn with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts improves soil fertility by adding nitrogen, protecting your farm income if one crop fails due to bad weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa futu mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Buu oŋmɔ mli shika ni onáa lɛ he kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the foliage burns, loses moisture rapidly, and curls up to protect the plant from dying.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ Bɔni afee ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, baai lɛ shãa, ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. ni abɔleɔ he koni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekagbo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and why am I finding tiny caterpillars inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli Ni mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii bibii? yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed inside the whorl (the central growing tip) of young maize plants, which weakens the stalk and leaves holes as the leaf expands.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. (Nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ) ni ji ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa buji baa be mli ni baa lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do green aphids gather under the leaves of my pepper plants, causing the leaves to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Aphids suck the sweet sap directly out of the underside of tender leaves. This sap loss causes the leaves to curl, yellow, and deform, while the sticky waste left behind by aphids can attract black mold.
ga: Aphids lɛ nuɔ wuo mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi. Nɛkɛ nu ni laajeɔ nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfiteɔ, yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii diji.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but produce small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium and phosphorus, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding its storage roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium kɛ fɔsfɔs he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi ni ato yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my field's soil is too tired to grow a good yield of maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Tired or depleted soil often causes yellowing on lower leaves, stunted plant growth, and yields hard, crusty soil when dry. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nutrients to exhausted soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni etse loo efite lɛ haa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. ehaa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ egbi. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting four or five maize seeds together in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ ni mikɛaadu yɛ bu kome mli lɛ he?

english: Planting multiple seeds together forces the young plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce very small cobs or no grain at all.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ Dumɔwui ni ajaa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, draw water and food away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant has enough energy to grow big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Enitsumɔ ji ni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch maximum sunlight for tuber development. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and fungal infections.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plants to experience heat stress, which prevents proper pollination of the blossoms. When pollination fails due to high temperatures, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni sa. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs turn into powder and dust inside my storage barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage pests like grain weevils burrow inside dry maize kernels to lay eggs. As the hatching larvae feed inside the grain, they hollow it out, leaving behind empty husks and fine powdery dust.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii baafo ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwui. Beni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ, Amɛbaafo mli. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ sũ bibii.
